Heading: Judge in list of Lalu admirers - Indian Express
Content: The appointment of veteran leader Kalraj Mishra as in-charge of the BJP's election campaign in Uttar Pradesh is being seen as a compromise formula after moves to bring him in as state chief were met with stiff resistance by party president Rajnath Singh, who belongs to Uttar Pradesh. With Uttar Pradesh BJP president Ramapati Ram Tripathi — a Rajnath confidant —  largely seen as a non-performer, L K Advani wanted the party to be resuscitated in the state (which sends 80 seats to the Lok Sabha) well in time, with Kalraj at the helm. However, Rajnath noted that if Tripathi was a disaster, Kalraj's track record in the state had not been shining either, giving the former a new lease of life.

Heading: Virk men work on DGP post - Indian Express
Content: RJD leader Lalu Prasad Yadav's inimitable style has not only wowed supporters and the political class, even senior judges are impressed. At a recent legal seminar on the UPA Government's NREG scheme, which was attended by the Prime Minister, Chief Justice of India, Rural Development Minister and legal fraternity, some of the judges reached out to Rural Development Minister Raghuvansh Prasad Singh praising his work and commitment, while lamenting the lack of media focus on the rural employment programme. A sitting judge of the Supreme Court pulled Singh aside suggesting he use the services of his party leader Lalu for speeches on the subject. "This way, not only more media will come to listen, but you will also get more publicity," the Hon'ble judge is learnt to have counselled Singh.

Heading: Valley red signal on train - Indian Express
Content: Supporters of S S Virk, the controversial former Punjab DGP who was suspended by the SAD-BJP Government, are hopeful he would become the next DGP of Maharashtra since the appointment of A N Roy to the post has been set aside by the Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT). Virk belongs to the Maharashtra cadre. However, with Roy's backers determined to get the Government to challenge the CAT ruling in the state high court, Virk chances are slim.

Heading: In Orissa’s ‘liberated’ zone, two villages take on the Maoists - Indian Express
Content:
Playing with white pieces in the second game of the World Chess Championship, India's Viswanathan Anand took a commanding position against Vladimir Kramnik before finally agreeing to settle for a draw after 32 moves.

Anand pressed Kramnik into a false move and sacrificed a pawn for no gain and raised hopes of a win. Both players made surprising moves and invited complications.

In the end, the draw was a fair result as Anand found himself short of a plan to Kramnik's defensive move.

In an exciting contest, Anand had started with an all out attack and caught Kramnik off guard.

Time trouble

Anand's white retained some advantage when the draw was called, but result is explained by the time situation. Anand was down to only two minutes and 33 seconds while Kramnik had nine minutes and 54 seconds.

Earlier, playing with black and starting with Slav defence, Anand shared points with Kramnik in the first match too. The twelve match series is tied at 1-1 with ten more matches to go.

Heading: Shinde: I'll be happy to see Pawar PM - Indian Express
Content:
Armed with an axe, Rukmani Majhi, 45, of Gatibeda village in Sunabeda wildlife sanctuary area, takes a break from household chores every evening to take position on a "morcha" (a fortified platform), along with other men and women of her village, all armed with traditional weapons like bows and arrows, to watch out for Maoists.

For the first time since 2008, when Maoists set up base in the area, two villages on the Orissa-Chhattisgarh border, Sunabeda and Gatibeda in Nuapada district — a part of the "liberated" zone — have taken up arms against them. The two villages together have a population of around 4,000, mostly belonging to the Chakotia Bhunjia tribe.

While no district administration official or local police would venture into the area earlier, the Central Reserve Police Force's (CRPF) CoBRA and Orissa Police's Special Operations Group (SOG) personnel have been camping in the Sunabeda forest rest house since December.

Officials said the change was due to the successful elections in Chhattisgarh. The Maoists had threatened to disrupt the Chhattisgarh polls. But other than some minor incidents, the elections were conducted successfully. According to officials, after the Chhattisgarh polls, people in the two villages started to stand up to Maoists, refusing them food, shelter or any other help.

"This is the first time that we are seeing such resistance against Maoists anywhere in the country. Not everyone wants to help them, but they were doing so till now out of fear. After the Chhattisgarh elections, we got information that locals were rising against the Maoists. It was a conscious strategy to set up camps there, they have to be protected too," said Dilip Trivedi, DG, CRPF.

"When news of the successful polls reached other states, it was taken as a failure on the part of the Maoists. These two villages started resisting the Maoists and also put up a fight against them with bows and arrows," said a senior officer.

"We had been going to these areas for combing operations, but this is the first time that we have set up a base there. This would not have been possible without local support," said another official.

Since the two villages are located on the border with Chhattisgarh, they have often provided a safe refuge for Maoists in the past. In fact, the top Maoist leadership reportedly conducted their fourth central committee meeting in February last year in a village called Kodinga in Sunabeda area. While there are 50 other Naxal-affected villages in the area, they are yet to put up any resistance.

Trivedi said the Maoists are now being seen as "outsiders", as most of them hail from either Andhra Pradesh or Chhattisgarh. "The villagers don't see any gain in siding with the Maoists. We are hopeful that there will be resistance in other areas too," he said.

"One grouse among the villagers was that Maoists were taking their children away. This has given them enough reason to put up a resistance," said an officer.

For Maoists, Nuapada is strategically important as it is the gateway to western Orissa districts of Bargarh, Sambalpur, Bolangir and Kalahandi. If they can dominate Nuapada, it will be easy for them to build a seamless red corridor in western Orissa that connects Bastar in Chhattisgarh to Saranda in Jharkhand.

"When we first entered the area last month, we found several villages around the sanctuary that were not even on the Survey of India map. The villagers had no option but to support the Maoists," said R Jaykumar, a CRPF commandant in charge of the area.

The CRPF has sent a detailed report to the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) on the new developments. "We have started by deploying a small team there. After reviewing the situation, we will deploy more men," said an officer.

Heading: Thousands spoil durbar debut - Indian Express
Content:
Just days ahead of the AICC session on January 17, where the Congress is expected to make its stand clear on party vice-president Rahul Gandhi's candidature as its prime ministerial candidate, Union Home Minister Sushil Kumar Shinde on Saturday was quoted as saying that he would be "happy" to see NCP president Sharad Pawar as the Prime Minister.

"I would be happy if Sharad Pawar becomes the Prime Minister. He is my political guru, I must admit I entered politics because of Sharad Pawar. He brought me to politics in Maharashtra," Shinde was quoted as saying at an interaction with the media in his constituency, Solapur, in western Maharashtra.

"Everyone has ambition. He has been trying (to become the Prime Minister) since 1992... I believe Pawar has been a victim of Delhi politics... There is no reason for harbouring two views about my support to Pawar as Prime Minister. I have said this many times, even on the national platform," he was quoted as saying.

When contacted by The Sunday Express, Shinde did not deny the remarks, but claimed that he was quoted out of context. "My support to Pawar as Prime Minister was in response to questions asked by mediapersons. It was not as if I was pitching Pawar's candidature. It should be seen in the right perspective and not projected wrongly," he said. "My support will always be for Rahul Gandhi as Prime Minister," he said, asserting his loyalty to party president Sonia Gandhi and Rahul.

In Delhi, AICC general secretary in charge of Maharashtra Mohan Prakash refused to comment, saying he was unaware of the context in which Shinde made the observations. Party spokesperson Meem Afzal claimed Shinde had already denied the remarks, and hence he had nothing to add.

But a senior Congress minister in Maharashtra said, "It does not augur well for the party which is pitching Rahul Gandhi for the post". Some Maharashtra PCC leaders indicated a "ploy" to streamline the party's strained relationship with the NCP. "Shinde is a seasoned Congress leader. He would never make a mistake. There is a definite ploy," said a party leader.

"Shinde's support to Pawar has a hidden political agenda — to mend fences with the NCP in his own constituency," said a senior AICC leader.

The NCP, meanwhile, said Pawar was not in the race for the top job. "We all know Sharad Pawar is the most capable leader to become the Prime Minister. But he is not in the race. The NCP understands its political limitations. The party contests limited seats in the Lok Sabha which makes it difficult to stake claim for the top post. The arithmetic is not in our favour," said party chief spokesperson Nawab Malik.

"Shinde's statement is his personal view. What he meant was that if Pawar becomes the Prime Minister, he would have liked it as he is a leader from Maharashtra. But he also indicated that he would like to go by the party's decision," said MPCC spokesperson Ratnakar Mahajan.

"Shinde's open support to Pawar as PM is to ensure NCP helps him in Solapur. The 2014 Lok Sabha elections will be crucial for Shinde as he faces unrest from farmers in the region," said another MPCC leader. The NCP is known to have some strongholds in his Solapur Lok Sabha seat.

"Moreover, the AICC is already exploring the possibility of picking Shinde as one of the probable candidates for the top post in order to consolidate the Dalit vote bank in its favour. Even if it doesn't declare Shinde as the candidate, it wants to use his No. 2 position at the Centre to retain its Dalit vote bank," he added.

\"Shinde has supported Pawar's candidature as Prime Minister. It was shown on television channels, so how can we deny what appears in public. Moreover, he has spoken extensively on Pawar and not just made a passing remark. However, we don't doubt Shinde's loyalty to Rahul's leadership," said another state Congress leader.

Shinde and Pawar are known to share a close friendship. During the 2009 Maharashtra Assembly elections, Pawar and his daughter Supriya Sule launched the campaign of Shinde's daughter, Pranati, in Solapur Assembly constituency. Pawar also campaigned for Shinde during the Lok Sabha elections.

"Pawar and Shinde have always been friendly despite the Congress and NCP often being at loggerheads," said a senior NCP leader.

Meanwhile, the BJP said Shinde's remarks showed the Congress has accepted that Manmohan Singh's successor will not be from the party. "In a way, Shinde has already conceded that no Congress leader will be the next Prime Minister. He may daydream about who should be the Prime Minister, but the people have already reposed their faith in Narendra Modi's leadership," said BJP spokesperson Prakash Javadekar.

with inputs from Delhi

Heading: Six dud firms to transfer money to Virbhadra, family - Indian Express
Content:
The first of Arvind Kejriwal's planned daily janta durbars collapsed an hour after it started Saturday, after a heaving crowd of over 20,000 people threatened to physically swamp the chief minister and his cabinet colleagues, and the meeting teetered on the edge of disintegrating into complete chaos.

Kejriwal and Urban Development Minister Manish Sisodia were forced to retreat into the secretariat building about an hour after the durbar started at 9 am, leaving the other ministers attempting to hear the people's complaints.

The chief minister said he was in danger of being crushed by the crowd, and announced that the durbar was being suspended until the government was able to plan better and put proper arrangements in place.

Standing on the roof of the reception wing of the secretariat, Kejriwal told the crowd behind police barricades: "I accept that there were problems with the arrangements. I am deeply sorry that we could not listen to all your problems. People climbed on to the chair and table at which I was seated, and I could have been crushed if I had not left... We will come back to you with full arrangements and have another janta durbar in four to five days."

"When the crowd became unmanageable, there were two options before me, either to resort to a lathicharge or to talk to the people. I chose the second option. Next time we will have the janta durbar at a stadium," he said.

The chief minister had announced that the entire cabinet would sit outside the Delhi secretariat every Saturday to listen to the people's grievances, and would attempt to solve the urgent problems on the spot. Every weekday, a minister would receive grievances from the public.

A large proportion of the people who thronged the road outside the Delhi government headquarters were contract workers seeking permanent jobs.

Kejriwal said: "I realise that the maximum grievances are among contractual workers from BSES, Asha workers, teachers. I assure you that we have taken note of your complaints.

"On Monday I will ask all departments for data on the number of contractual staff, and why they cannot be made permanent. They will submit a report in a week, and I will try to take a decision in a month. You have waited for so many years, give me this much time."

He also requested them not to come back at the next janta durbar, so that other complaints could be heard.

The chief minister and six cabinet ministers sat in the open outside the secretariat along with senior officials, as people began handing in their complaints. Health Minister Satyendra Jain, whose mother passed away on Saturday morning, was not present.

Each person was given a slip to confirm the receipt of his complaint. Officials at the help desk said those who had supplied their mobile phone numbers would receive a confirmation SMS. \"All written complaints will be put up on our web site and the status of action taken on the complaint will be constantly updated," an official said.

Barely 15 minutes into the durbar, however, the crowd — Kejriwal said there were 5,000 people against an expected 500, while police sources said at least 20,000 people had turned up — turned unruly. Delhi Police and Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) personnel struggled to manage the crowd, which broke the barricades at some places. The entire stretch of road from ITO to Rajghat was closed, and barricades were erected on the divider so that people could occupy one carriageway.

Some 300-400 police personnel were present outside the secretariat. "There was seating arrangement for 1,000 people outside the secretariat, but a much larger crowd turned up, leading to the chaos," a police officer said.

Several people returned disappointed. "I had come here in the hope of getting relief from my problems. But I was pushed around, and I am leaving after having waited for five hours. I wanted to meet the CM to seek a job for my physically handicapped son. There is no one to look after his needs after I retire," said M S Kaushik.

The BJP accused the AAP of promoting anarchy. "This is definitely promoting anarchy. It is a sign of bad governance," senior BJP leader Harshvardhan said.

Heading: After telling Delhi to sting, AAP wants Lokpal to snoop - Indian Express
Content:
The web of financial transactions between Himachal Pradesh Chief Minister Virbhadra Singh, members of his family and controversial businessman Vakamulla Chandrashekhar involve money transfers from him to the CM and his family via at least five companies that ceased to exist. And, in one case, money moved back and forth between the two sides.

This is revealed in an investigation by The Indian Express based on Registrar of Companies records and bank statements, including the one made public by Leader of Opposition in the Rajya Sabha, Arun Jaitley.

As per that statement, on January 10, 2012, Chandrashekhar received Rs 49.99 lakh in his personal account from Maple Destinations, a company owned by the CM's son and daughter, Vikramaditya Singh and Aprajita Kumari, respectively. The very next day, this amount was transferred to Tarini International, a company of Chandrashekhar's Tarini group. As per RoC records, in the financial year 2011-12, Maple received Rs 49.99 lakh from Tarini Sugar and Distillaries Ltd, another company of the Tarini group.

No one from the CM's family responded to questions from The Indian Express on this transaction and others and involving companies that didn't exist. Chandrashekhar denied any wrongdoing and said he was "open for any investigation at any levels".

Between November 4 and November 21, 2011, Chandrashekhar, as per his bank statement, received inflows into his personal account amounting to Rs 1.6 crore from six companies. During the same period — November 4 to November 29 — a total of Rs 1.75 crore was transferred to the accounts of Chief Minister Virbhadra Singh, wife Pratibha Singh and son Vikramaditya Singh.

Consider the nature of these transactions:

* One of these six companies is Punjab Foods Private Ltd. On November 21, 2011, Punjab Foods deposited Rs 45.5 lakh into Chandrashekhar's account and four days later, Rs 40 lakh from here was transferred to Vikramaditya Singh's account.

Incidentally, six months earlier, on April 18, 2011, Punjab Foods had filed an application before RoC, Chandigarh, to wind up its operations.

That application stated, "Pritpal Singh (director of the company), informed the members the company is not having any business activity for the last 10 years. Further company is having neither any assets nor any liabilities, therefore Easy Exit Scheme 2011 is opted for the closure of the company".

The company was officially wound up on April 20, 2011. Yet, Chandrashekhar's account showed a deposit of Rs 21.50 lakh from Punjab Foods as late as July 24, 2012.

Speaking to The Indian Express on January 2, Chandrashekhar had said he received money from Punjab Foods against agricultural produce he sold.

* On November 4, 2011, Chandrashekhar had a balance of Rs 4.05 lakh in his account. Over the next five days, Rs 92.90 lakh came into it from Kesari Nandan and Co (Rs 17.99 lakh), Shiva Stores (Rs 15.01 lakh), Jai Durga Impex (Rs 12.25 lakh), Laxmi Enterprises (Rs 7.65 lakh), Siddharth International (Rs 26 lakh) and one Suraj Singh (Rs 14 lakh). On November 11, Chandrashekhar transferred Rs 65 lakh, in two transactions, to Virbhadhra Singh's account.

According to the RoC records, Jai Durga Impex, Shiva Stores, Kesari Nandan and Co and Siddharth International all had ceased to exist before any of these transactions.

From Chandrashekhar's account, a transaction of unknown value failed on November 15, due to "insufficient funds".

* Between November 17 and November 21, Chandrashekhar's account received Rs 45.5 lakh from Punjab Foods and Rs 53 lakh from from one "V Chandra Shekhar". Four days later, Rs 71.80 lakh in two instalments of Rs 40 lakh and Rs 31.8 lakh was transferred to CM's son Vikramaditya Singh from Chandrashekhar's account.

Subsequent to this transfer — and some minor transfers not related to the CM's family — Chandrashekhar's account balance became Rs 55.05 lakh on November 25, 2011. On November 29, 2011 two instalments of Rs 25 lakh each were transferred to Pratibha Singh and Virbhadhra Singh.

His balance after these transactions was Rs 4.73 lakh, marginally higher than what it was when the transactions began.

When asked about the transactions with the CM and his family, Chandrashekhar said: "These companies are vendor companies with whom we have had trade relationships. We have done all transactions legitimately through banks. Whether they are doing business still or not, I am not competent to answer as it is purely their business."

Despite telephone calls and text messages Vikramaditya Singh was not available for comment. Jaitley has accused Virbhadra of granting an extension to Venture Energy and Technology, promoted by Chandrashekhar, for executing a hydel project.

Asked about the money received from Maple, Chandrashekhar said: "I and VVikramaditya Singh together wanted to do a construction project in 2010-11. Accordingly, my part contribution of Rs 2 crore was made to Vikram. Since the project did not take off, he returned the money through Maple. Where is the illegality?" He added: "Shri Virbhadraji is a very noble person and worthy of friendship...I am open for any investigation at any levels."

Heading: Delhi businessman overtakes Vadra’s car, booked for rash driving - Indian Express
Content:
After urging citizens to sting corrupt government officials, the AAP government is pushing hard to pass its version of the Jan Lokpal Bill in Delhi. While the process to draft the bill is already underway, Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal has announced that the Bill will be passed in a special Assembly session by February.

"A committee has been formed to draft the law. The committee under the chief secretary will include secretaries of the departments of home, urban development, law, finance and advocate Rahul Mehra," Kejriwal said on Thursday.

"We will all meet at Ramlila Maidan either in the last week of January or first week of February," he said.

The Bill, he said, would be discussed with the "people of Delhi" at Ramlila Maidan for consent.

A Lokayukta will head the new body to combat graft with powers to conduct its own investigations, surveillance and even tap phones.

"As in the AAP's model Jan Lokpal Bill, the head of the body, in this case the Lokayukta, will have powers to tap phones, conduct independent investigations and surveillance against those who face corruption charges," Urban Development Minister Manish Sisodia said.

According to Kejriwal, the Lokayukta would function as an independent body. "Today if I am accused of corruption, there is no independent body which can investigate me but this will happen once the law is drafted," he said.

Heading: Does AP mean Ahmed Patel, asks prosecutor in Italy court; middleman says don’t know - Indian Express
Content:
A Delhi businessman was penalised by traffic police for "rash driving" after his car overtook the cavalcade of Robert Vadra, son-in-law of Congress president Sonia Gandhi.

A police officer, who did not wish to be named, said the car of Saurabh Rastogi, a businessman who lives in Paschim Vihar, was chased and intercepted by police after Vadra's securityman called the police control room and complained that a car had driven past "dangerously".

The officer said Rastogi was headed towards Lajpat Nagar from the Modi Mill flyover in Okhla at the time of the incident.

"Rastogi was in a Maruti Ritz and Vadra's cavalcade was ahead of him. We were told he had been honking continuously. In a bid to overtake the cavalcade, he accelerated and sped past Vadra's car. It was then that a securityman travelling with Vadra made a PCR call. The traffic police were also informed," the officer said.

Rastogi's car was chased by traffic policemen and intercepted near Amar Colony in south-east Delhi. "He was issued a challan for dangerous driving under Section 184 of the Motor Vehicles Act and let off," the officer said.

Heading: PAU sexual harassment case: DSW goes on leave - Indian Express
Content:
Prosecutors in an Italian court Thursday asked the key middleman in the IAF's VVIP chopper deal whether the initials 'AP' in an alleged "budget sheet" for bribes to politicians referred to Ahmed Patel, the political secretary of UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi.

The middleman, Guido Haschke, who has consistently denied bribing Indian officials or politicians, replied that he did not know who or what 'AP' stood for.

As first reported by The Indian Express, Italian prosecutors had last month produced a handwritten document they alleged was a "budget" drawn up by two middlemen — Haschke and Christian Michel — which purportedly lists initials of Indian politicians and designations of bureaucrats and IAF officers who allegedly had to be "handled" to fix the Rs 3,546 crore deal.

The alleged "budget sheet" detailed how kickbacks of 51 million euros would be divided and under the heading "POL" — Haschke has claimed this referred to Indian politicians — there is a reference to "AP" against which "3 million euro" has been listed.

Another amount of 15/16 million euros was listed against "FAM" which is said to be "Family". Haschke has claimed the note was dictated to him by British consultant Michel during one of their meetings in 2008.

On Thursday, Italian prosecutor Eugenio Fusco asked Haschke during a court hearing in Busto Arsizio near Milan whether "AP" in the note was a reference to Ahmed Patel.

In his reply, the middlemen said he did not know what AP meant when he wrote it down. Haschke also denied any bribes were paid for the contract and said that the "budget sheet" was just an imaginary note drawn up and was never acted upon.

He also said the budget sheet was merely bragging by Michel about his Indian contacts and that Haschke tried to disassociate himself from the Briton.

Strongly denying any wrongdoing in the deal, Haschke also claimed to Indian interrogators in the court that no bribes were paid for the contract and that the money he received from AgustaWestland - in excess of 24 million euros - is justified as fees for engineering consultations.

Italian prosecutors also produced another note in court Thursday - a March 2008 fax by Michel to Peter Hulett, said to be the then head of region, govt sales at AgustaWestland's India office. The fax said that among the politicians who would use the choppers once acquired by India would be UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi and her senior advisors, including Ahmed Patel.

However, Sonia is not entitled to use government helicopters. She can use VIP aircraft only when she flies with the PM, President or ministers who are officially entitled to the aircraft. This fax by the British middleman has also been shared by the Italian side with the CBI team that is in Busto Arsizio for the hearing.

Michel has been elusive and no investigative agency has been able to reach him.

Haschke, who is facing a case in Italy for being part of a conspiracy to bribe Indian officials to ensure the AW 101 chopper was picked by the IAF, faced several questions from the Indian side and denied any irregularity.

But the Indian side did not ask Haschke to explain what AP, FAM or any of the other acronyms in the note - "DS", "JS AIR", "AFA", "DG Acquisition", CVC" etc - referred to, source said.

The middleman, who was quizzed about his association with former Air Chief S P Tyagi - named as an accused in the CBI case in the deal - denied that any money had been paid to the retired Indian officer. Haschke, sources said, admitted that he was in regular touch with three cousins of Tyagi who have also been named in the case.

In response to a question from the Indian side, Haschke said he was not aware if any money was paid to S P Tyagi.

The UPA government had come under pressure in connection with the alleged kickbacks last month after The Indian Express report on the budget sheet of the middlemen. The opposition BJP had demanded the government reveal what or who "AP" and "FAM" stand for. The party also said that it wants a detailed discussion in Parliament on "alleged payments to persons close to the ruling establishment" in connection with the controversial chopper deal and has accused the government of "running away from discussions".

The discussion did not take place as the Parliament session was abruptly called off midway.

Heading: Jeev rises to 55th, Randhawa slips to 115 - Indian Express
Content:
The ruling SAD-BJP combine on Monday failed to wrest control over the Kharar Municipal Council (MC) even after winning 10 of the total 15 seats in the general elections held on September 14.

On Monday, a special meeting of the civic body was called to elect the president and vice-presidents of the MC after administering oath of allegiance to the newly elected 15 municipal councillors.

During the meeting, Kharar sub-divisional magistrate (SDM) Rajeev Kumar Gupta, who had convened the MC meeting, sent a notice announcing that the election has been postponed indefinitely as he was not well.

Terming the postponement as "illegal" and "murder of democracy", Congress MLA Balbir Sidhu claimed rift in the ruling SAD-BJP combine to form United Front, comprising the councillors from the SAD-BJP alliance, Congress and Independents.

While seven councillors, including three from the SAD-BJP combine, two from the Congress party and two Independent candidates, reached the meeting venue MC office at 2 pm, seven others of the SAD-BJP combine and a Congress councillor failed to turn up. Kharar Congress MLA Balbir Sidhu, the ex-officio member, and Chamkaur Sahib MLA, Charanjit Singh, who had supported the SAD-BJP combine in the MC polls, were also present at the meeting.

Claiming absolute majority of eight councillors besides his vote in the United Front, Sidhu accused the ruling combine of "abducting" one of the two Congress councillors Sarabjeet Kaur to secure her vote. "Kaur and her husband are missing since Saturday and even their family members don't know about there whereabouts," alleged Sidhu, claiming that as and when she surfaces, she will join the United Front.

Sidhu, without disclosing the name of the presidential candidate of the United Front, added that his group will capture the coveted top posts in the MC as and when elections will be held.

However, Punjab Cooperation Minister Capt Kanwaljit Singh, who had toiled to ensure clean sweep of the SAD-BJP combine in the civic elections, claimed that all the 10 councillors of the ruling alliance stand united and will undoubtedly wrest control over the civic body.

Rubbishing the allegation of "abducting" a Congress councillor, Captain Kanwaljit asked: "How we can join hands with Congress?" Ridiculing Sidhu's claims of forming the United Front, senior Punjab Minister said all such "claims" will fall flat when elections will be held for the top posts.

Chamkaur Sahib MLA Charanjit Singh, whose younger brother Sukhwant Singh and his wife Paramjit Kaur are among the 15 councillors, claimed that besides ten SAD-BJP councillors, three independent councillors were also with the ruling alliance.

However, Kharar SDM could not be contacted for comments.

Journalists denied entry

Local journalists were denied entry to the MC office, which was turned into a fortress. Angry over the police action, the journalists will boycott all official functions in Kharar, said Vishal Nagpal. He said Kharar DSP detained the scribes on the pretext of receiving orders from Mohali Deputy Commissioner Rahul Bhandari, who categorically denied issuing any such orders.

Heading: Hockey tourney from October 16 - Indian Express
Content:
The fourth place finish in the Indian Open, his best show here, pushed Jeev Milkha Singh three places up to 55 as the Indian inched towards a top 50 re-entry in the latest world golf rankings issued today. Jeev, battling through a stiff neck, yesterday posted his best show at the Delhi Golf Course which has been less-than-kind to him in the past.

Though Jeev's 12-under aggregate was still four shots adrift of what eventual winner Liang Weng-Chong totalled, it was enough to see him jump from his previous week's 58th position. The US $ 49,300 he won also helped Jeev consolidate his second place on the Asian Tour Order of Merit, adding to his season's collection which now stands at US $ 589,994. Compatriot Jyoti Randhawa, meanwhile, continues his freefall in the ranking ladder and his tied 57th place finish in the Indian Open, which he had won thrice in the past, saw him slip 11 rungs to126. US-based Arjun Atwal is 230th in the chart, while Indian Masters winner SSP Chowrasia, who failed to make the cut this weekend, is placed 286th.

Heading: Trials for School Nationals from tomorrow - Indian Express
Content: The district police on Tuesday claimed to have busted a gang of robbers with the arrest of five persons identified as Sanju Kumar, Ajay Kumar, both hailing from Kathmandu but living in Amritsar, Nirmal Singh of Main Bazaar, Mustfabad, Rohit Kumar of Akash Vihar and Davinder Sharma of Jawahar Nagar. The police have recovered an axe, a dagger and two sharp-edged weapons from the accused. The accused were arrested from Mustfabad Kotla Basti. A case under sections 399 and 402 of the IPC has been registered at Sadar police station.

Heading: NPS-18 claims girls’ basketball title, boys’ final marred by protest - Indian Express
Content:
The Chandigarh Education Department will hold selection trials for the forthcoming 54th School National Games from October 15. The trials will be held for basketball, hockey, volleyball, kabaddi, lawn tennis, softball, chess, cricket and football. The trials for basketball in the U-14 category for boys and girls will be held at Sports Complex, Sector 46 on October 15 at 10 am while the U-17 trials will be held on October 16 at 10 am. The trials in the U-19 category will be held on October 17 at 10 am. Heading: Mohali track to assist seamers: Daljit - Indian Express
Content:
Defending champions IS Dev Samaj School, Sector 21 left the court before the much anticipated final to hand over the girl's title to New Public School, Sector 18 in the final of the 11th CBSE Cluster XIII Inter-School Basketball Championship for boys and girls held at the New Public School courts on Monday.

The Dev Samaj girls started to warm up for the much but, much to the surprise of the audience, left the court few minutes before the match was about to start.

Meanwhile, Sacred Heart Convent School, Sector 26 got the better of Carmel Convent School, Sector 9 to claim the third place.

In the boy's category, the result of the boys' final has been withheld following New Public School's protest against Sanjeev Rao of SD Public School being over-aged, and thus not eligible to play.

Both the teams unleashed attacking games in the final. SD Public School, after losing two quarters at 10-16, 17-18, bounced back into the game and won the third quarter by 13-7.

Deepak turned the match with three consecutive three-pointer. Amjyot and Sanjeev Rao were the top scorers with 23 points each. Rakesh Verma, CBSE observer, confirmed that he had received a protest from NPS alleging that Sanjeev Rao was not eligible to take part since he was born in 1989. The CBSE authorities in Delhi have been apprised of the situation and the results will be declared after the verification.

Defending their player, the SD Public School authorities said that Rao's date of birth was 1990 according to their records, and is eligible to compete.

Meanwhile, Guru Nanak Public School, Sector 36 snuffed out the challenge of Maharaja Hari Singh Agricultural Collegiate of Jammu by 66-33 to claim the third spot.

Heading: MC frets as Badal seeks building plans of Mall Road - Indian Express
Content:
After the draw at Bangalore, all eyes will be on the 22 yard pitch at the PCA Stadium here, venue of the second Test of the India and Australia series. And going by the chief curator Daljit Singh there is bound to be a smile on Ricky Ponting's face: Seamers and not spinners will have a bigger role.

"This has been an unusual season and we have seen heavy rains in this part of the country. Honestly the pitch and ground preparations have been hampered," Daljit admits, "We are trying our best to have a hard and a dry wicket with consistent bounce." As ever, especially with winters around the corner, the faster bowlers will find movement both on and off the wicket. "We can see the data. The morning sessions are always loaded in favour of seamers while the pitch eases out as the game goes on. We have a few days left and hope the sun shines," Daljit said.

"I think bowlers can exploit the bounce at this wicket resulting in batsmen edging deliveries. Also, there would be no reverse-swing here as we don't have a rough outfield," he added.

The pitch would also keep the Indians engrossed in a debate over the final XI. Will India go in with the two spinner and two pacers theory or drop a spinner for the third pacer? Even though Anil Kumble has picked up two Man of the Match awards, his shoulder injury has hampered his bowling of late. "I feel he enjoys the bounce here and if he is fit he would love to bowl here," Daljit felt.

The Stadium has seen a few drawn games but Daljit is optimistic this time of a result. "The rains have to stay away," he concluded.

Heading: Midnight brawl at vet varsity leaves one injured - Indian Express
Content:
The CM has reportedly asked for a time-bound action against the guilty

The Town Planning wing of the Municipal Corporation is in panic. Reason: Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal has asked for building plans of structures constructed on the Mall Road.

This has been done following a complaint about illegal constructions on the road. With insufficient parking space, the roads are choked with traffic.

With a majority of buildings having inadequate parking or no parking, the Town planning wing has been asked to produce the building plans of the complexes on the road.

The complaint also states violation of building bylaws while constructing the high-rises with most of them having inadequate fire-fighting equipment, no entry or exit route and many other anomalies.

The wing has given the building plans to MC Commissioner G S Ghuman on Saturday and the CM has asked for a time-bound action against the violators.

If action is taken against the building owners on the Mall Road, many other markets in the city will also come in the line of fire. These include Ghumar Mandi, Ferozepur Road buildings,

Model Town market, Satpaul Mittal Roadamong others.

Hemant Batra, Municipal Town Planner, agreed that a few building plans have been submitted to MC Commissioner and added, "I have no idea as for what reason these plans have been taken from us."

Heading: Mischievous Net-savvy youths made things easy for accused, say cops - Indian Express
Content:
CASH AT JUDGE'S DOOR: To evade media, ex-Haryana AAG spends 2 extra hours in jail

After spending more than 50 days behind the bars, former Haryana Additional Advocate General (AAG) Sanjeev Bansal, accused in the cash-at-judge's-door case, was released on bail on Monday. The Court of Special CBI Judge Jagdeep Jain also granted bail to co-accused Prakash Ram and Rajiv Gupta, Bansal's munshi and friend, respectively.

The other two accused — Nirmal Singh, a property dealer, and Ravinder Singh, the alleged kingpin — are still behind the bars. A bail application demanding Ravinder's release was filed in the court on Monday, while that of Nirmal Singh is likely to be filed shortly.

Arguing for Bansal's bail, defence counsel S K Vohra said he had already been in jail for 53 days. He submitted that all documents and relevant material pertaining to the case had already been recovered by the CBI and keeping the accused further in jail would serve no purpose.

The special CBI prosecutor contested the bail applications, submitting that the whereabouts of Jai Parkash, senior munshi of Sanjeev Bansal who was required by the agency for investigation, was still not known. He said the accused should not be granted bail as they might tamper with the evidence and influence the case once released. Showing little conviction in the contentions raised by him, the court allowed the bail applications of the three.

While Bansal and Gupta were directed to furnish bail bonds of Rs 2 lakh each, Parkash Ram furnished a bail bond of Rs 25,000.

High drama prevailed at the Burail Jail late in the evening after the supporters and relatives of Bansal gathered outside to greet him on his release. They tried their best to dodge the lensmen and reporters waiting for Bansal. A number of cars were lined up, waiting for Bansal and the two others. Exactly at 6.50 pm, when Rajiv Gupta and Parkash Ram came out, Bansal's relatives and advocate friends hugged Gupta and covered his face with a piece of cloth, trying to project him as Bansal. "I hope everything was fine inside the jail. Mediapersons are waiting for you, don't talk to them," a supporter could be heard telling Gupta. Within seconds, all the vehicles left the scene.

Around 8.45 pm, when the mediapersons had left, it is learnt Bansal quietly came outside the jail and was taken away by his friends, who were all the while keeping a tab on the mediapersons by visiting the jail after regular intervals.

Heading: 71 more dengue cases confirmed; toll rises to 761 - Indian Express
Content:
Mischievous Internet-savvy youngsters eager to befriend girls and chat with them online — Suryansh, prime accused in the 'web extortion' case, was reportedly always on the lookout for such targets. Posing as a girl, the accused would let himself befriended by such youngsters and then make it rich by blackmailing them after allegedly morphing their photographs and threatening to make them public, the police said.

The cyber crime cell of the Chandigarh Police cracked the case on Sunday, by arresting a couple — Deepak Singh and Puja Negi — who allegedly worked for Suryansh, a resident of Ludhiana, as his messengers.

According to members of the cell, due to his unique email ID — khoonkar_darinda840@yahoo.com — complainant Navkaran Singh fit the profile of a perfect target for the accused who laid a trap for him by posing as 'Shelly' in the Yahoo chatroom.

As their friendship grew after regular chatting, police sources said, Navkaran showed 'Shelly' the pictures of his family. The accused then morphed the pictures, making them obscene, and allegedly started blackmailing him into parting with money and valuables.

"The two never met, but the complainant sent his photographs to the 'girl' through Internet, completely ignorant of the racket," a police officer said.

While Suryaansh is still absconding, a local court sent Deepak and Puja to two days' police custody on Monday. The sources said the accused had an affair with Puja prior to her marriage and that he had blackmailed her the same way into making conversations with Navkaran on the phone, posing as Shelly. The police added that while it was Suryaansh who ran the racket with the help of a fake email ID — shellyjindaal@yahoo.com — he had roped in Puja because he needed a female voice for talking to his target.

According to the police, the accused had managed to rope in Deepak, an employee with a courier firm, too, by blackmailing him.

Navkaran was forced to give away valuables worth over Rs 1 lakh, including a Rado watch, Nokia mobiles and an MP3 player.

"The youngsters should be careful while making friends on the Internet and falling prey to such frauds," a police officer said.

The police managed to contact Suryaansh over phone soon after Puja Negi's arrest on Sunday, but the latter anticipated trouble and threw away his SIM card. The police sources said it being a Sunday they were not able to get the tower locations of the phone number from the cellular service provider immediately. The police are now studying his call details to arrest him.

The police said it was possible that many more youths like Navkaran had fallen prey to the accused.

Heading: DM prohibits disposal of waste in Sidhwan Canal, Buddha Nallah till Dec 10 - Indian Express
Content:
Seventy-one cases of dengue were confirmed by the Health department today, taking yesterday's official toll of 690 cases to 761 in the district.

However, the total tally of dengue cases, including the ones in the suspected cases category (233) and those from other districts but diagnosed in the city (374), has already gone up to 1,368.

With nearly 150 fresh patients of dengue reported at various hospitals of the city today, the number of fresh cases being admitted everyday is also rising steadily.

The Dayanand Medical College and Hospital (DMCH), admitted over a 100 patients today taking the total tally of patients admitted in the hospital to over 900. The Christian Medical College and Hospital (CMCH) also admitted about 22 patients today and the total count at CMCH has reached close to 300.

On the other hand, SPS Apollo Hospitals admitted 11 fresh cases and GTB Hospital admitted 20 cases today.

The total number of cases in both hospitals has reached the 100 mark. MD Oswal Cancer Hospital also registered two fresh cases and the total number of cases reported at the hospital has also touched the 100 mark.

The Sri Rama Charitable Hospital and Ludhiana Mediciti today registered 10 and 4 fresh cases respectively. Both the hospitals have reported a total of about 40 cases each.

Heading: Residents protest erection of cell phone tower - Indian Express
Content:
To keep a check on the pollution level in the city, the District Magistrate (DM) has passed prohibitory orders to ban the disposal of solid waste in the Sidhwan Canal and the Buddha Nallah.

The orders have been passed under Section 144 of the Criminal Procedure Code (CrPC) in the interest of the public. The orders will remain in force till December 10.

The Punjab and Haryana High Court on July 18 last year, had also directed the district administration to keep a check on the disposal of solid waste in the Sidhwan Canal.

While the Buddha Nallah has become a source of pollution due to the discharge of solid in it, the Sidhwan Canal is also being polluted by local industry.

Heading: Rajasthani theme-based township to be set up on 70 acres launched - Indian Express
Content:
Fuelling another debate on the installation of cell phone towers in the residential complexes, the residents of Mission Compound near Kalvary Church are up in arms against a reputed telecom firm.

The residents have written to the chief minister, district administration and the municipal corporation seeking the dismantling of the tower at the earliest, stating potential health hazards caused by radio frequency radiations.

A few residents of Sarabha Nagar, Block I, have also raised a similar question as regards the installation of two cell phone towers in the residential complex, citing studies that link EMF radiations to various health hazards, particularly cancer.

"We do not want this potential health hazard for our children and elders. We are well aware of the fact that a cell phone antenna emits harmful EMF radiations which can cause various health hazards like brain tumour and cancer," said Sumit Malaki, one of the residents of the residential complex whose house is adjacent to the one where the tower has been erected.

The tower has been erected on the rooftop of a house in an area where a cluster of houses is situated in two rows, separated only by 8.5-feet narrow lane. The residents are also concerned that in case of any mishap, the tower may destroy the adjoining houses and cause loss of lives too. The tower has still not been activated so far.

They further said that though the company which is setting up the tower has secured permission from Pradeep Procha on whose rooftop the tower has been installed, it should not be allowed in the larger interest of the residents.

"The person who has given the permission should also keep in mind the welfare of the residents rather than falling for a few thousand rupees promised to him as the rent for the same," complained another resident of the area.

However, Pradeep Procha, said that he would abide by the directions of the authorities as and when he receives them. "I do not have any objection if the authorities order dismantling of the tower. But as long as there is no such order from the government, I do not have any problem with it being erected," Procha said.

The residents said that they were also following the legal approach to the matter and have sought legal help from District Bar Association vice-president HS Narang. On the other hand, when contacted, a representative of the telecom firm said that all the guidelines of TRAI (Telecom Regulatory Authority of India) are adhere to and permission taken from the authorities while erecting a structure.

Heading: One-day workshop on communication skills held - Indian Express
Content:
A 70-acre Rajasthani theme-based township, Rajgadh Estates, was today launched by Bhasin Infrastructures & Developers Private Limited. The township has built-up villas that are in range of Rs 1.28 crore to Rs 2.09 crore. The company has announced bookings from today onwards and five villas have already been booked.

Balraj Bhasin, chairman of the group, said, "Four have been booked by Ludhiana residents and the fifth one by a NRI."

The township, built in red sand-stone, has been planned and landscaped by Singapore-based architects, DLQ.

Bhasin said the township is eco-friendly and they have a rainwater harvesting system and a sewer treatment plant too.

Apart from independent villas, concept-based villas, including Chittaurgarh villas, Hanumangarh Villas and Jaisalmer Villas, are also available.

Heading: Industry-Institute interaction programme held at RIMT - Indian Express
Content:
GGN Institute of Vocational Studies, in collaboration with BJK Institute of English Learning, organised a one-day workshop on communication skills here today. About 100 students pursuing their masters degree under PTU scheme attended the workshop. Gurkanwaljot Kaur, director of BJK Institute of English Learning, said, "English language is omnipresent and its presence cannot be ignored."

An interactive session was organised later in which students were told to ask questions in English to remove their hesitation. Speaking on the occasion, the college coordinator, Manjit Singh Chhabra, said, "The main purpose behind such workshops is to encourage our students to face challenges in life." GGNIVS director Kuldip Singh thanked all present for organising and attending the workshop.

Heading: Employees of mohalla sanitation committees would be regularised soon, promises Badal - Indian Express
Content:
As part of the Industry-Institute Interaction programme, D L Sharma, the director of Vardhman Textiles Limited, Ludhiana, visited the Regional Institute of Management and Technology here today. An alumnus of Harvard Business School, Sharma, who is a member of the CII National Committee on Textiles, did his MBA from the first batch of PAU, Ludhiana and shared his varied experience with the students.

He said in the corporate world, business executives have to face a lot of stress while performing their duties. Only by better time management and adaptability to change, one can cope with it, he said.

Sharma answered the queries of the students, on topics including job opportunities, work environment in corporate world and self-development.

Dr BS Bhatia, the director general of the RIMT, thanked Sharma for the visit. Dr SP Panda, the principal of the institute, was also present.

Heading: Gujarat archaeological dept finds Buddhist monastery in Sabarkantha - Indian Express
Content:
Punjab Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal today called upon the people of Punjab to follow the teachings of Bhagwan Valmik to strengthen the bonds of compassion and brotherhood in the state.

Greeting people at a state-level function to commemorate the Prakash Utsav of Bhagwan Valmik here today, Badal announced that the employees of mohalla sanitation committees would be regularised soon after abolishing these committees in the state.

"Bhagwan Valmiki was the creator of the first epic, the holy Ramayana, that occupies a paramount place in Indian religious literature," said Badal.

Claiming that the SAD-BJP government is committed to the upliftment of the downtrodden, Badal said it is the agony of the fate of our country that 70 per cent of the total population was earning just Rs 20 per day.

Badal said the state government would also provide free education to the poor deserving students upto university level. He also said the local Valmiki Bhawan would be renovated soon.

Among others who addressed the function were Hira Singh Gabria, Minister for Jail and Tourism; Harish Rai Dhanda, Chief Parliamentary Secretary; MP Sharanjit Singh Dhillon and MLA Harish Bedi.

Heading: SSG Hospital to install six new elevators - Indian Express
Content:
In a significant breakthrough confirming the prevalence of Buddhism in ancient western India, the Gujarat State Archaeological Department has excavated an archaeological site, complete with a monastery, in the Vadnagar area of Sabarkantha district, this month.

It was after an extended work of three years involving five field archaeologists that the monastery was unearthed.

Y A Rawat, Director, Gujarat State Archaeological Department, said, "This excavation is an important finding since it establishes that besides caves sighted in Junagadh as well as in other areas of north Gujarat, structural constructions also existed during the 2nd and 4th Century AD."

Referring to another essential aspect of the excavation, Rawat said: "It has been found that a Chinese monk and traveller by the name of Wenshang visited India in 7th Century AD. In his travelogue he had mentioned about 1,000 monks living in 10 monasteries at Vadnagar, which was earlier known as Anandpur during that era."

Rawat said the recently discovered monastery is one of those 10 mentioned by Wenshang, adding that the monastery is situated right within the fortified area of ancient Vadnagar town. "Generally, the monasteries are situated outside human habitation. But the presence of monastery right inside the town shows how keenly Buddhism was followed here," said Rawat.

He said it took over three years to confirm that the structure was indeed a Buddhist monastery, as several alterations were made in the structure in the following years.

The monastery is small and has 12 shelves with small spaces and a single plinth. It is a fortified area, around 16 metres sq in size, and has steps and an open courtyard, he said.

Incidentally, it was way back in 1962 when a team of archaeologists from the M S University (MSU) discovered the ruins of Buddhists stupas during work on a reservoir project in Devnimori village of Sabarkantha district. After a gap of nearly 50 years, a Buddhist monastery has finally been excavated in the fortified area of Vadnagar.

Rawat said the Vadnagar excavation project is an ongoing task taken up by the Gujarat State Archaeological Department. "Within a town planning layout of ancient Vadnagar there have been several inscriptions reflecting Gandhar sculptures, seals, various successors, trade as well as economy. Various findings show the impact of north India and West Asia; it's an ongoing project," he said.

Heading: City traffic lights crave for maintenance - Indian Express
Content:
The Sir Sayajirao General (SSG) Hospital will install six new elevators on its premises. At present, only two of the wards in the hospital boast of elevators. The hospital will now not only construct new elevators, but also replace some of the already existing ones.

The construction of the elevators will cost anywhere between Rs 15 to 17 lakh each. While one of the elevators at the surgical ward and the Operation Theatre (OT) ward will be replaced, the OPD, Trauma Centre and the Gynaecology Ward will get new elevators. At present, these departments do not have any elevator facility.

"Most of the buildings are over two-storey and the step is being taken to provide convenience to the patients," said Dr V T Hathila, in-charge Superintendent of SSG Hospital.

One of the two elevators, which was non-functional in the surgical block, will be replaced while in the other wards, elevators will be constructed.

The construction of the new elevators will start within the next three months. "The proposal has been submitted to the Health Department and the logistics of the project is still under process," said Dr Hathila.

At the Godhra Civil Hospital, elevators have been non-functional for the past one month. As a result, inconvenience to the patients have often led to a physical tussle between the ward boys and the relatives of the patients.

Hauling the patients on stretchers to the respective wards in the three-storey buildings is becoming a nightmare for the ward boys and the class IV workers as most of the relatives turn aggressive on them due to the inconvenience caused as a result of the non-functional elevators.

"Taking patients till the third floor is obviously a stress on us; but it is more of an inconvenience to the patients. With critical cases like fracture or burns, even a little jerk while taking them upstairs causes them a lot of pain," said a class IV worker at the Godhra Civil Hospital.

He said: "The relatives are already under tension and if the patient experiences pain, they get extremely aggravated and sometimes even abuse us physically. We try to maintain as much calm as possible, but things do get out of hand sometimes".

He said the condition at the hospital during Dussehra was not much different. Fourteen cases of burns were admitted to the hospital after a burning effigy of Ravan collapsed. The shortage of staff coupled with non-functional lifts, only added to the chaos, he added. "We have complained to the authorities about the elevator, which has remained shut for the last one month, but we have been told that it will take two months to get it repaired," said a hospital worker.

Hospital officials said that the elevators have been non-functional for the last fortnight. "The lifts are as old as 58 years and they have been non-functional due to construction work. But we will get them repaired as soon as possible," said Dr Mahesh Sagar, Chief District Medical Officer (CDMO), Godhra Civil Hospital.

Heading: Two attempt suicide by consuming insecticide - Indian Express
Content:
At a time when the latest technology in streetlights —Global System for Mobile Communication (GSM) Control — will be lighting up city streets, traffic lights seem to be a neglected lot as they crave for proper maintenance at most junctures in the city. Some areas including the juncture at Banyan Circle in Fatehgunj are in dire need of proper lights, which witness heavy traffic in most parts of the day.

Traffic lights are controlled by the traffic department and are maintained by the Vadodara Municipal Corporation. "There maybe a power cut in that area or some wire might have got disconnected. We have not received any complaint as yet," said PSO Raman Kumar, in-charge of the traffic department, who did not seem to be aware of the situation of the area.

Heading: Govt school teacher, clerk arrested for issuing fake NCC certificates - Indian Express
Content:
In two separate incidents, a woman and a man attempted suicide by consuming insecticide on Monday. According to the police, both persons are recuperating in SSG Hospital.

The Jawahar Nagar police said that Narmada Parmar, a 37-year-old woman and a mother of two, tried to commit suicide by consuming insecticide in a field near Kadodia village. Police said that the reason for attempting suicide is yet to be ascertained. Her husband, Satish, rushed her to the hospital where she was operated upon, the police said.

Meanwhile, 27-year-old Vijay Kharwa, a resident of Pathargate, falling under the jurisdiction of the Navapura police station, went to Charasta market at 8 am and attempted suicide by consuming insecticide. SSG hospital authorities said that Kharwa was critical.

Heading: At Seva Café, pay what you feel like - Indian Express
Content:
The Vadodara police arrested a school teacher and a clerk of a government school for issuing fake NCC certificates to applicants for the post of government primary school teachers.

The police said the accused, teacher Ramsu Charel and clerk Mahendra Patel of Motnath Vidyalay High School, located some 5 km from Vadodara city, used school stamps and stationery to issue fake certificates.

The police recovered 34 fake NCC certificates, two sealed covers of applications, 17 blank letterheads of Girdhar Vidyalay of Padara Masar village and receipts of sent applications from the accused. A case of fraud, cheating and conspiracy under Sections 420, 465, 467, 468, 471, 34 and 120(b) of the Indian Penal Code has been registered against them.

More than 40,000 schools across the state are functioning under a staff crunch after the recruitment drive was stalled following revelations that fake applications had exceeded the genuine ones. The Primary Education Department received more than 1.5 lakh applications for the 10,200 seats at 40,000 schools across the state, and many applicants had attached fake sports certificates along with their degrees and mark sheets to get the additional five points.

A co-curricular activity certificate can fetch an applicant extra five marks.

According to the police, the two accused had issued fake certificates to the applicants who took part in the recruitment drive held at Bodeli and Sankheda in February. At the camp, they themselves contacted the applicants and took anything between Rs 2,000 and 5,000 to help them with the applications, the police said.

A Panigate police officer said: "We are yet to find out the number of applicants to whom the two have provided fake certificates. Preliminary investigations reveal a possible nexus between the accused and the Education Department in the scam".

While the Education Department had earlier registered a complaint against five Ahmedabad-based institutes for issuing fake certificates, this is the first arrest in the case.

In August, the Sports Department filed a complaint against five institutes with the Gandhinagar police on the instructions of the Education Department. But the matter became sub-judice after some applicants, who were disqualified for allegedly producing fake certificates, moved court.

Heading: GU students demonstrate to increase number of ATKT exams - Indian Express
Content:
Seva Café is a cafe with a difference. Even three years later — this homely and unique cafe was opened on October 13, 2005 — it is going strong with its ideology and the concept of "Atithi Devo Bhava—Guest is God" and "Living is Giving."

At Seva Café, the meal is offered as a genuine gift, so to say. At the end of the meal, the guests receive a blank envelop (Seva Café works on the principle of 'pay it forward,' which is very different from modern restaurants). The belief is that as someone else in the past has already paid for your food, so to complete the circle, you can leave as much amount as you desire, in the envelop. Significantly, no one will check how much one pays.

The café is mostly run by volunteers with six or seven paid staff, who provide service at the café because they have full faith in its concept.

The café is situated opposite the Municipal Market on C G Road and is open from Tuesday to Sunday. The first 50 guests are served every evening between 7 and 10 pm. All the profit generated is used for social service projects.

Deepti Shah, a volunteer, told Newsline: "The café's inspiration springs out from an age-old Indian custom which believes in the principle that guests are God (Atithi Devo Bhava). We also try to make sure that they feel at home here."

Raju Thakore, a member of the family that runs Seva Café, said: "In the past three years, I have seen thousands of volunteers and guests coming here. In the later stage, volunteers and other NGOs associated themselves with Seva Café."

Raghu Kulkarni, another family member told Newsline: "Sometime ago a German couple came to Seva Café and got angry when we invited them for prayer before starting the day's operations. They thought we were just offering prayers of one particular religion. But when they came to know about this place and the concept behind Seva Café, their eyes were filled with tears."

Sandeep Vaghela, who mainly explains the concept of Seva Café to guests and volunteers, told Newsline: "We are trying to spread and sustain the traditional Indian concept. We come across several new people everyday and try to share and learn as many things as possible from them."

Incidentally, the concept is not limited to Ahmedabad only. On June 15, 2006 a volunteer group named 'Be the Cause' started Seva Café at Long Beach, California and continued it till March 3, 2007.

The Seva Cafe in Long Beach was operated at the Royal Cup Coffee Shop, which transformed into Seva Café every Saturday from 5.00 to 10.00 pm.

Now on October 26, 2008 the same group is opening a Seva Café at Zephyr's in Long Beach, California where it will be run everyday Sunday from 5.00 to 9.00 pm.

Heading: First success for health dept in battle against sex determination tests - Indian Express
Content:
Around 250 students of 13 engineering colleges, affiliated to Gujarat University (GU) staged a demonstration on Monday. The IInd, IIIrd and IVth year students were demanding an increase in the number of ATKT examinations from the present four to six.

Vice-Chancellor (V-C) Parimal Trivedi said the demands were not up to the mark and asked the students to contact MN Patel, the Dean of Engineering faculty at GU.

Patel told Newsline: "The demands of the students are senseless. If we allow them to keep more ATKTs then the level of education will go down."

He added: "Last year also the students had done a similar thing and then the V-C had increased the number of ATKTs from two to four. This year also they want the number to be increased, which is not possible."

Patel said the students who are weak will always remain so and increasing the number of ATKTs will not be of any help to them.

I have clearly told the V-C that if the number of ATKTs exams are increased then "I will resign from my post."

This year, there are around 1,000 students who have ATKTs in five or more subjects due to which they will be detained for a year.

The students also alleged that both the V-C and the Dean of Engineering faculty are not interested to listen to them and are avoiding them.

Heading: Soon, CNG to power cars, kitchens - Indian Express
Content:
The State Health Department tasted its first success in the fight against sex determination tests after the Supreme Court issued an interim stay on the sale of sonography machines that were sealed after a sting operation at Dr Harshad Thakkar's clinic here.

The Health Department has been waging a long battle against sex determination tests in clinics, commencing with a sting operation in March 2007. The sting ascertained that Dr Thakkar was conducting sex determination tests in his registered 'Genetic Clinic.' Later officials sealed the two sonography machines at the clinic under Section 30 of the Pre-conception and Pre-natal Diagnostic Techniques (PCPNDT) Act.

Illegal pathology labs and sex determination clinics have been a cause of constant trouble for the Health Department. But for the first time, the department has seen a positive impact of the corrective steps taken by it.

Commissioner of Health Amarjit Singh told Newsline: "Last year, a total of 200 labs were booked under the PNDT Act, but there has been no conviction as yet. For the first time now, there is realisation of the seriousness of the issue by the judiciary. Even after the sting operation, the High Court had taken a very lenient view of the matter although the doctor was caught red-handed. It has been difficult to convince the judges on why it is important to prevent the sale of the machines and what was the medical emergency. The Supreme Court's order is a positive development."

While the complaint was filed under the PCPNDT Act, the doctor sought removal of the seals on the sonography machines. In March 2008, the High Court had allowed the doctor to sell the machines. After a prolonged period of filing affidavits, applications, petitions and a further appeal in the Supreme Court, on September 29, passed an order issuing an interim stay on the sale of the machines.

The sting operation

THE Health Department had conducted the sting operation on Hari X-ray and Colour Doppler 4D (live 3D) Sonography Clinic. A pregnant nurse from the Department posed as a domestic servant along with a member of the detective agency, which was engaged for the purpose. Dr Harshad Thakkar was caught red-handed for conducting sex determination tests and accepting Rs 4,000 for the sonography, following which the registration of his Genetic Clinic under the PCPNDT Act was cancelled and the two sonography machines were sealed.

Heading: Farmers shun from submitting memorandum regarding compensation over Nano land - Indian Express
Content:
With CNG filling stations being set up across most major cities in Gujarat, the government has decided to focus on small towns where this clean pollution-free fuel will be made available to vehicle owners.

Accordingly, the state government has directed the Gujarat State Petroleum Corporation (GSPC) to set up 'daughter stations' at small towns to cater to the needs of vehicle owners for the clean, environment-friendly fuel.

"After covering all major cities, the government has now decided to set up CNG filling stations in small towns situated within 35 km radius on both sides of the gas pipeline being laid by the GSPC's sister concern, the Gujarat State Petronet Limited (GSPL)," said Minister of State for Energy Saurabh Patel.

Patel told reporters that the 'daughter stations' to be set up in such towns will be supplied CNG through tankers. As many as 120 CNG stations have already been set in all the major cities across the state, he said. "We have chalked out plans to add 70 more filling stations that will be set up in smaller towns by March 2009," he added.

GSPC Managing Director D Jagatheesa Pandian said that GSPL has already covered 15 of the total 25 districts in Gujarat under its gas grid network. "Work on laying of the gas pipeline covering about 1,400 km stretch has already been completed and we propose to cover the remaining 10 districts under the gas grid network by 2010," he said.

He said work on the gas grid between Vapi in south Gujarat and Mehsana and Himatnagar in north Gujarat and between Rajkot and Morbi up to Jamnagar in Saurashtra has been completed. "Work on covering another 800 km stretch is going on in full swing. We are in the process of issuing tenders for the work on laying of gas pipelines between Limbdi in Surendranagar and Paipavav in Bhavnagar, as also between Morbi and Mundra in Kutch," he said.

Once the entire state is covered under the gas grid network, gas will be made available not only to the industries, but also for domestic use. The GSPC has roped in different agencies, both in the private and the public sectors to supply gas for industrial as well as domestic use in cities and towns where the gas grid is passing through their vicinity.

Heading: New fee structure of SFIs to come after Diwali - Indian Express
Content:
None of the farmers from Khoda, Bhod, Amareli and Modasar villages, who had earlier declared to submit a memorandum to the authorities regarding compensation for the land being transferred to the Tatas for their Nano project in Sanand taluka, turned up on Monday.

Several farmers from these villages had claimed that the 1,100 acres of land being given to the Tatas belonged to their forefathers. Hence, they should be given fair compensation by the state government, they had claimed.

But surprisingly, none of the farmers came to Sanand or to the site of the Nano car project. Ahmedabad District Collector Harit Shukla said he had gone to visit the site on Monday but no farmer turned up to give him any memorandum. Sanand taluka authorities also said that no one had come to give them any kind of memorandum regarding the land.

Shukla said the land belonged to the government for the last 98 years. He said the records available with the government show that it was in the possession of the government since 1911 and hence the question of paying compensation did not arise at all.

Meanwhile, the state unit of the Congress on Monday accused the Narendra Modi government of being secretive about the Nano deal.

Gujarat Pradesh Congress Committee chief Siddharth Patel told media persons that the Congress was not opposed to the deal but wanted the state government to reveal its key features.

"We know that the people of the state will benefit from the project, but what is the need to be so secretive about it. The government must tell the people about it," said Patel.

He said his party has asked for a copy of the agreement, including the rate at which the land was being transferred to the Tatas, incentives being given and the ancillary units to be set up there.

He said as the government was not willing to share information on these issues, the party has filed an RTI application to seek information on the various aspects of the deal.

Heading: 8-month-old raped by ‘mentally ill’ man - Indian Express
Content:
Justice R J Shah (retired) Fees, Admission and NRI Committee on Monday postponed the meeting that was to decide the new fee structure of the Self-Financed Institutes (SFIs) offering Masters in Business Administration (MBA) and Masters in Computer Application (MCA). The new fee structure will now be decided after Diwali.

Around 25 per cent of the architecture institutes have hiked their fee. At present, the Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel Institute of Technology, Vasad, is charging the highest fee.

It has increased its fee from Rs 36,000 to Rs 45,000. D C Patel School of Architecture, Vallabh Vidyanagar has increased its fee from Rs 40,000 to Rs 48,000. At Indubhai Parekh School of Architecture, Rajkot, the fee has risen from Rs 40,000 to Rs 46,000. The students of Sarvajanik Education Society's College of Architecture, Surat, now have to pay Rs 47,000 instead of Rs 41,000.

The five institutes offering Diploma Engineering courses after standard X have increased their fee up to Rs 30,000. The new fee at B S Patel Polytechnic Institute (Ganpat University) and Maharaja Sayajirao Self Finance Engineering is Rs 30,000.

The students at STBS College of Diploma Engineering, Surat, have to pay Rs 28,000, while at the Sigma Institute of Technology & Engineering (Polytechnic), Bakrol, students have to pay Rs 26,000. At the Vivekananda Institute of Engineering the fee now is Rs 20,000.

The fee of Parul Institute of

Hotel Management & Catering Technology, Vadodara is Rs 20,000, at present.

Heading: Woman dies during childbirth, husband alleges negligence by doc - Indian Express
Content:
A mentally ill person allegedly raped an eight-month-old girl child at Dankaria village in Bharuch district on Sunday. According to the Palej police station, the mother of the victim, Tara Shailesh Morji Vasava, is a housemaid who left for work at 9 in the morning, leaving the baby with Suresh Rawal (20) at her home.

According to the police, Tara and her husband, Shailesh Vasava, had provided shelter to the accused as he was sick and was roaming in the area looking for food. Suresh is a resident of Mehsana and had been staying in the village for the past two days, according to the police. The villagers claim that they knew that the accused was mentally challenged, however, they never thought that he could commit such a 'heinous crime'. Tara, a daily wage labourer, had gone for work when the incident occurred.

The incident reportedly took place around 2:30 pm, when Tara returned from work and saw her baby bleeding.

"The victim was taken and allegedly raped at the Tankeria-Sitapod road, which is one-and-half kilometres away from her house," said Deputy Superintendent of Police, B S Ninama.

Minor raped in Pandesara, one arrested

In a shocking incident, a five-year-old girl was allegedly abducted by three youths and later raped near Pandesara area in Surat on Sunday night. The police have arrested one accused and are investigating the case further. The girl's father, a resident of Vadod in Pandesara, lodged a complaint with the Pandesara police against one Satyendra Choudhary and two others, for their alleged involvement in the crime.

The complainant said that his daughter was playing outside the house as there was power cut in the area. Unable to find her, he searched the entire area but failed to find her. After about half-an-hour, Satyendra was spotted leaving the girl on the main door of her house by a few neighbours.

The girl complained of sexual assault and later fell unconscious. Her father, along with the neighbours, went to Satyendra's house and questioned him. Seeing the situation going out of hand, the police was called in, who arrested Satyendra and started investigations.

During interrogation, the accused disclosed that he was standing outside his house when two youths left the minor girl. "Two youths approached me and asked me the way to the girl's house stating that she was found on the main road. When I directed the way to her house, the duo left the girl saying they had some important work," Satyendra claimed.

Investigating officer V N Pateliya said: "We have got primary information confirming rape from NCH doctors. We are interrogating Satyendra to verify his role in the case. We are yet to confirm the number of accused in the case. We are waiting for the girl to regain consciousness as only she can identify the accused, which will provide us leads into the investigation."

Heading: ‘There’s a co-relation between Bahadur Shah and Muslims’ condition in India’ - Indian Express
Content:
The husband of a 27-year-old woman, who died during childbirth at a maternity home in Saraspur on Sunday, has alleged that she died due to negligence on the part of the doctor. Though the Shaherkotda police have registered a case of accidental death, they are waiting for the postmortem report to decide the future course of action in the case.

The deceased has been identified as Yogita Chauhan, a resident of Arvind Mill ni Chali in the Saraspur area. Her husband, Ajit Chauhan (28) — a garment exporter, has accused Dr Bharat Atit of negligence. The doctor runs a maternity home at Desai ni Pol in Saraspur and is the husband of former mayor of Ahmedabad, Maliniben Atit.

According to the police, Yogita was eight months pregnant when she was admitted to Dr Atit's hospital on Saturday night after she complained of stomach pain. Later, the doctor performed a caesarean operation on her. The child died during the operation and Yogita's condition too deteriorated, after which she was referred to the Shardaben Hospital, where she died on Sunday.

Inspector D G Gohil said: "We have registered a case of accidental death and have got the postmortem done. Now, we are waiting for the report. If there is anything which suggests that the woman died due to the negligence of the doctor, we'll register a case against him under provisions of the IPC. We cannot register a case unless we have some medical evidence against him."

Heading: Riot victims to protest delay in release of ex gratia amount - Indian Express
Content:
