I first came to Gujarat in 2001, when fundamentalists in Dangs district burnt some churches. It was an unpleasant sight

His latest acquisition is a book on Maharaja Sir Sayaji Rao of Vadodara. Donning a half-sleeve blue shirt on a bright Monday afternoon, he comes across as a jovial man often seen wandering amid the lost remains of forts and palaces. But William Dalrymple, a historian and a traveller who brought Mughals in a fresh perspective to the world without delving much into historical dates, has been travelling the country for the last 28 years. Newsline caught up with India's very own travelling chronicler, as he flipped a few slides of his journey for a talk show organised by the Association of British Scholars, Vadodara Chapter. Excerpts:

Ques Is this your first visit to Gujarat? Do you see metaphorical reflections of a besieged and helpless Bahadur Shah Zafar who was his own prisoner in an inexorable time warp, in the current state of the Muslim community in places like Gujarat, particularly after the 2002 riots?

I first came to Gujarat in 2001, when fundamentalists in Dangs district burnt some churches. It was an unpleasant sight. I would say there is a direct correlation between the helpless Bahadur Shah Zafar and the current state of the Muslim community in India. In fact, it is not metaphorical. The decline of Muslims started with the siege of the Delhi Sultanate in 1857, which led to the bifurcation of two different schools of thought — one at Deoband and the other at Aligarh. The humiliation of Islam during the siege of 1857 was a repository of what was to come. While Deoband vouched for its pure roots, Aligarh embraced other parallel cultures.

Ques Where would you draw the line between a biography and hagiography? What efforts, conscious or otherwise, did you take to avert The Last Mughal from sliding that way?

I am surprised I have not come across a review describing it as hagiography. Bahadur Shah Zafar was magnificently well-equipped as an inspiration with his utopian ideals and poetry, but ill-suited for the task of leading the rebels from the quandary of siege. The Last Mughal is neither a biography nor a hagiography. Delhi is the principal character among the cast.

Ques Though he has come a long way now from the clichés of snake charmers, magicians, maharajas and other oriental exotica, the archetypal Western reader is still obsessed with an India with a strong sepia tint. How would you reason this?

I think that's what my next novel, tentatively called Nine Lives, tries to bring forth. It is a chronicle of nine individuals who have taken to mysticism in these times. It transcends, what is commonly called Karma in hippy parlance and all other such clichés. That one needs to see how a sadhu lives like I met this one at Goumukh, with whom I spent a week. While talking to him, he came across as an MBA who was selling Kelvinator refrigerators, around 15 years ago or a Devdasi called Ranibai from Hampi, in Karnataka, who was pulled out of the school, driven to prostitution, and ended up as an HIV positive; then also Haridas from Kerala, a Dalit well digger who enjoyed inverting caste structures with exorcism.

Ques What is the one thought upper most in your mind when you think of Gujarat?

Riots. But if I go by what is being most talked about, it's Nano.

Ques Your niece, Alice, is in India and she just published her first book.

We are in the process of setting up our family business here (laughs). She is my first cousin and coincidentally, we are working on similar things. Though we haven't travelled much here.

Heading: Noose to tighten around hospitals holding sex determination tests - Indian Express
Content:
Efforts are on to get over 1,000 riot-affected Muslims from across the state to stage a protest demonstration in New Delhi, against the delay on the Centre's part in releasing additional relief money for them. The amount is estimated to be around Rs 270 crore.

Five months after the Centre announced an additional relief package of more than Rs 330 crore for the victims of the 2002 riots, nothing has changed for around 30,000 Muslims whose property was razed or damaged in the mayhem. They were supposed to receive an additional ex gratia 10 times the amount paid to them earlier.

Yusuf Sheikh, the Vadodara-based convener of the Antrik Visthapit Hak Rakshak Samiti, said: "The protestors will represent the 29,467 registered and the nearly 4,500 unregistered cases of damage to Muslim residential properties during the riots." He said the demonstration will be staged at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi on November 5.

On May 22 this year, the Centre had announced Rs 330 crore additional relief package for the riot victims. This was aimed to bring relief to the victims at par with the measures taken in respect of victims of the anti-Sikh riots of 1984.

The Gujarat government had, however, criticised the decision and called it 'partial'. A day after the relief package was announced, the Gujarat government had termed is as "cheating" and full of "duplicity". In a statement, government spokesperson and Health Minister Jai Narain Vyas had called for a similar package for the anti-Sikh riot victims of 1984 and all other communal riots that had taken place in the country since then. The Gujarat government had also demanded a package on similar lines for the victims of the Akshardham Temple attack of 2003.

The next of the kin of 1,169 people killed in the riots were supposed to receive Rs 3.5 lakh ex gratia in addition to the Rs 1.5 lakh already paid to them by the state government earlier. A sum of Rs 1.25 lakh was to be paid to each of the 2,548 people injured, after deducting the Rs 2, 000 already paid to them by the state government.

For the victims, whose residential property was damaged in the riots, an additional ex gratia of 10 times the amount given by the state government, after excluding the amount already paid by the state, was to be given.

Though ex-gratia for the kin of those killed in the riots and the people who were injured, has already been paid, the state government is yet to receive the money proposed as ex-gratia for those who lost their houses and shops in the riots.

Gujarat State Director for Relief D A Oza said: "Ex gratia for the kin of those killed and the people who were injured in the 2002 riots, was released by the Centre on time. We have even disbursed it among the victims. The money for ex-gratia for those whose property was damaged, however, is yet to be released by the Centre. We had even sent an estimated proposal for this to the Centre, but it is yet to respond."

According to records, of the 29,467 cases of people whose property was damaged during the riots, around 15,000 are from Ahmedabad city and the district alone.

Records also indicate that the state government has already paid Rs 18.137 crore for properties damaged in rural areas in the state and Rs 15.12 crore for those damaged in the urban areas. An additional Rs 270 crore is needed to pay these victims ex-gratia 10 times the amount already given, excluding that which has already been paid.

Heading: Centre encouraging vote bank politics: Modi - Indian Express
Content:
Pre-natal Diagnostic Test (PNDT) committee headed by District Collector Vijay Nehra, while embarking on Beti Bachao Andolan this week, declared to tighten the noose around city-based hospitals encouraging sex determination in Vadodara.

He announced to set up an efficient software system in hospitals to keep a tab on how they deal with pregnant women. Spy cameras will also be set up to keep a check on them.

Addressing mediapersons, Nehra said the PNDT committee is going to be stricter with gynaecologists and ultra sonography services. A meeting with gynecologists will also be held, he said.

Though things are at a preliminary stage at present, more rigorous steps will be taken soon, he said. This year, around Rs 10 lakh will be spent from the MPs' fund to spread the message of 'Save the Girl Child'.

From this week, the district health department will embark on week-long public awareness programmes asking people to come for mass swearing-in ceremonies against female foeticide with female sex ratio dipping drastically and becoming a serious social problem.

Nehra warned, "Female foeticide is a non-bailable offense. It is difficult to nab the offenders without evidence, but the PNDT committee is going to get tough with them."

Jayaben Thakkar, MP from Vadodara, said: "It is interesting that in tribal areas, the female sex ratio is much more than in the urban areas of Vadodara."

Heading: Top brass screen A Wednesday to scuttle convention of low-rung cops - Indian Express
Content:
Chief Minister Narendra Modi has accused the UPA Government at the Centre of "encouraging vote bank politics" and willfully avoiding use of the word "terrorism" in the agenda items of National Integration Council's (NIC) meeting held at New Delhi on Monday.

Addressing the NIC meeting chaired by Prime Minister Manmohan Singh, Modi expressed shock that the issue of terrorism was not mentioned in the agenda, according to a statement issued here on Monday evening by the State Information Bureau, Government of Gujarat.

Although the word "terrorism" was replaced by "extremism" in NIC's agenda, Modi raised the contentious issue saying, "It (the UPA Government) doesn't want to mention terrorism (in the agenda), and doesn't know the difference between terrorism and extremism. The rise of terrorism with educated youth involving in terrorist attacks does not augur well for communal harmony".

He said a national consensus was required to isolate such people, groups and so-called intellectuals supporting these elements in the name of protection of human rights, and demanded a deterrent punishment to keep the youth away from such "indoctrination".

Urging the UPA government to expedite approval of the GUJCOC Bill passed by the Gujarat Assembly to curb terrorist activities in the state, he said: "It is unfortunate that the nation not only lacks determination to strictly deal with terrorism, but also does not have any clear policy and programme to prevent our youth from falling into the trap of indoctrination and joining the terrorist outfits."

He said that his government was keen on maintaining social harmony and peace by focusing on welfare and development of all its citizens.

Modi further said that even after the recent serial blasts in Ahmedabad and the recovery of "live bombs" from Surat, the 5.5 crore people of Gujarat maintained peace and showed great character in fighting terrorism. "During his visit after the bomb blasts, even the Prime Minister had appreciated the great resilience and determination demonstrated by the people of Gujarat," he said.

Highlighting education among the minorities, SC and the ST communities, Modi said that Gujarat was determined to improve its literacy rate and provide easy access to education to all sections of society. "The overall literacy rate of the state is 69.14 per cent. The Sachar Committee has highlighted that the literacy rate among Muslims in Gujarat, at 73.47 per cent, is not only higher than the state average of 69.14 per cent, but also way above the all-India literacy rate of Muslims at 59.01 per cent," he said.

Heading: ’93 Mumbai blasts accused summoned in arms smuggling case - Indian Express
Content:
A special screening of the Hindi movie A Wednesday, by the Mehsana Superintendent of Police for the lower rung personnel of the force, is being seen as an attempt to disrupt the possible convention of the two proposed associations of the latter.

Mehsana Superintendent of Police Raju Bhargav had organised a special show of the movie at a private cinema hall in Mehsana town on Sunday. Bhargav said around 400 policemen of the district had seen the movie.

Incidentally, the same day, leaders of the two proposed associations of the lower rung police officers in Gujarat, the Gujarat State Police Constable Association and Gujarat State ASI/ Head Constable Association, had planned a convention at the Arbuda Bhavan on the Mehsana-Palanpur Highway.

Naresh Brahmbhatt, president of the proposed Gujarat State ASI/Head Constable Association, said: "Despite the fact that we had cancelled the convention due to some reasons and had also issued an intimation for the same, the higher authorities had taken pre-emptive steps to make sure that there was no unplanned meeting of the two associations at the venue. The screening of the movie A Wednesday was held, especially for the policemen of the district."

On his part, Bhargav said that the main reason behind organising the special show was to give policemen some idea on the expectations of the common man from the police in the age of terrorism.

"The show was already over before the proposed time of the convention, which, incidentally, had already been withdrawn," he added.

Elsewhere, Brahmbhatt said the police authorities took pre-emptive steps for the entire day. "The district police authorities had deployed police bandobast at the venue where the convention was earlier planned, from morning till evening, so that we did not hold any impromptu meeting," he said.

Brahmbhatt's claim is also evident in the reply Bhargav gave when asked about the police bandobast at the venue of the convention: "The bandobast was deployed at the spot so that the meeting was not organised without any notice".

The formation of police associations of lower rung officers in the state has seen resistance from higher authorities. The leaders of the proposed associations have now approached the Gujarat High Court for a legal remedy.

Heading: Three students killed in accident - Indian Express
Content:
The Bharuch sessions court has sent summons to the 1993 Mumbai serial blasts accused Mustafa Ahmed Dosa alias Mustafa Majnu to appear for trial in an arms smuggling case.

Dosa was deported from Dubai in March 2003. He was arrested under the Terrorist and Disruptive Activities Act (TADA) along with mafia don Abu Salem and handed over to the Gujarat Police in 2007. At present, he is in Porbandar facing the charges.

"Summons have been sent to Dosa for an arms smuggling case along the Gujarat-Madhya Pradesh border," said a senior police officer from Bharuch. Dosa is accused of having connived with Ibrahim's close aide Chhota Shakeel and one-time Ahmedabad underworld don Abdul Latif in supplying a cache of 35 AK-47 rifles and hand grenades to trigger violence after the Babri Masjid demolition.

According to Bharuch police, Dosa is also accused in another case of landing of arms and explosives in Bharuch.

This case relates to landing of a part of the consignment of RDX and AK-56 rifles meant for use in the 1993 serial blasts, on the coast near Porbandar. Landing of this consignment was also allegedly planned and executed by Dosa.

Heading: ‘Co-op sugar mills to generate power worth Rs 200-cr’ - Indian Express
Content:
Three B.Tech students of CT Institute were killed in an accident on Sunday night, when the motorcycle they were travelling in hit a heavy vehicle on the 66-foot-wide road, near Partapura.

The students were admitted to a nearby hospital, where they succumbed to their injuries. Lambra SHO Harpreet Singh said it was yet to be established how the accident took place.

The deceased were identified as Tushar Vaidya, 20, of Jammu, Sumit Rana of Drant village in Palampur and Ajay Bhandhari of Sainbagh, also in Palampur in Himachal Pradesh.

The SHO said bodies have been handed over to the families after post-mortem. A case has been registered against an unknown person.

Heading: State to Centre: Lift ban on export of non-basmati varieties - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab government has chalked out a plan to generate Rs 200-crore power per annum by setting up co-generation power plants at all the state cooperative sugar mills in the state.

This was disclosed by Co-operation Minister Capt Kanwaljit Singh here today while presiding over a one-day workshop organised by Sugarfed to suggest various ways and means to make the state cooperative sugar mills self-sufficient.

The workshop was attended by the chairmen and board of directors of all the cooperative sugar mills. Singh said the state cooperative mills have the potential of generating 100-120-MW power annually and the state electricity board has offered to purchase it at the rate of Rs 2.86 per unit, thereby creating an additional revenue of more than Rs 200 crore annually, while the existing losses of all these mills were pegged at Rs 77.95 crore.

He said a comprehensive revival plan to convert these mills into mega sugar complexes has also been drafted. Accordingly, the enhancement in the crushing capacity of the mills has become imperative, as now a minimum crushing capacity of 5,000 MT could only make a unit sustainable.

Besides, creation of additional sources of income with special emphasis on diversification and production of ethanol, the state government had agreed in-principle to grant bottling licence to three distilleries of the state co-operative sugar mills and the proposals were being drafted. The minister said Rs 22 crore out of the total pending Rs 37-crore arrear of sugarcane growers would be disbursed within a week.

He said the Co-operative Society Registrar has been directed to constitute a high-level committee of senior officers to streamline the functioning of the co-operative institutions.

Heading: Caught in the Net! - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab government today urged the Union government to immediately lift the ban imposed on the export of all non-basmati varieties and categorise PUSA-1121 as a basmati variety.

In a communication sent by Punjab Food, Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs Minister Adesh Partap Singh Kairon to the Union Minister of Commerce Kamal Nath, it was requested that in view of the ongoing procurement of paddy in the state, the Centre should lift the ban so as to enable the rice millers purchase superior grade 'A' non-basmati varieties. "This step will, on the one hand enable the farmers to get higher prices for their produce, and on the other help the millers to earn valuable foreign exchange for the country. This will give the much-needed impetus to the industrial economy of Punjab in the times of recession," Kairon said.

Heading: Pup Fiction - Indian Express
Content:
Ten new designers focus solely on accessories at the

Delhi Fashion Week

As the capital city gears up for the clash of the fashion weeks— the Delhi Fashion Week and the Wills India Fashion Week that start barely a day apart— fashion watchers can be sure of one thing; to see more holistic work. The fallout of the FDCI has opened the platform to many new young designers, eager to showcase their work, some of it startling in its originality.

For the first time since the inception of Indian fashion, accessories, crucial elements in fashion, will not be neglected. Ten accessory designers are showing for the first time at Delhi Fashion Week, beginning on Tuesday. Bags, scarves, shawls, wrap dresses, jewellery stalls, even blankets dot the venue— Emporio Mall in Vasant Kunj. The look is defined by etching Kalidasa's poetry on silver, weaving sequins in hand weaves of Bengal and using Moroccan designs on a Cashmere shawl. "We received an overwhelming demand from buyers who attended the fashion week last time. Most of the designers showing here are currently exporters," says Geetanjali Kashyap of Fashion Foundation of India. Bangalore-based jewellery designer Deepti Sudhindra who has been in the circuit for nine years, has found her niche by etching Henry David Thoreau's poetry on to silver, transforming a ubiquitous coconut shells into delicate beads, pendants and necklaces and contemporising the 200-year-old filigree craft of Karimnagar artists of Andhra Pradesh. "I take coconut shells and embellish it with silver," explains Sudhindra, 32, who will be showcasing eight different collections. "My look is contemporary but the design element is essentially Indian," says Sudhindra who works on a commission basis.

Turning scarves, shawls and wraps into a heritage label is Kolkata-based

designer Bappaditya Biswas, 36, who founded Bai Lou in 2002. Closely working with weavers of Bengal, Biswas uses Jamdani and double cloth weaving techniques. "We don't believe in embellishments on top of the fabric. Everything is woven in and comes out as a finished product," says Biswas who works with 350 weavers. His collection has stoles in malta silk with geometrical patterns, scarves in a blend of silk and wool in an oyster pink and aqua blue. "Wearing scarves is a recent trend in India and the hand weaving craft of Bengal has got a boost," says Biswas.

But it is Nepal-based fashion designer Yasmine Rana who has given the jaded crafts industry in the neighbouring country a lift, by incorporating traditional Nepalese designs into luxurious loungewear. Rana, of French origin, has been in the field for 25 years. Her collection—lounge wear, chic jackets in shining blue and jade green, cashmere shawls and blankets have a bourgeoisie elegance. "My designs are classy, multi-cultural and bold. I pick-up ideas from my travels, use local designs and natural material," she emphasises.

Among others, Peachy Bawa of Basta will show a range of leather bags, Delhi-based Shilu Kumar of Pashma will exhibit a

collection of scarves and Jyotika Jhalani of the label Janavi will show a trendy line of beach garments, hand bags and high-end wraps in silk and chiffon.

Heading: Plaint against Mona, Bhajji - Indian Express
Content:
Things are looking up for this debutante director of Roadside Romeo

When the news of Yash Raj Films collaborating with Walt Disney for a one-of-its-kind animation film started flashing a year back, there was one thing that intrigued us the most - the director of Roadside Romeo: Jugal Hansraj. The little green-eyed boyed in Masoom, the sweet boy next door in Papa Kehte Hai and the best pal Jignesh in Salaam Namaste, that's all our mini wiki recalled, till it appeared there in black and white, this bow-wow detail of the 'Talented Mr Hansraj'.

"I am an animation film buff," he dimples, as he tick marks all the books, DVDs, toons he has devoured so far. "Pixar, Disney, you name it and I've seen it. I've never missed a single show," he says with pride, placing Ratatouille on the number one favourite slot. This was of course a 'passionate' secret, one that was known to none other than Aditya Chopra, who called Jugal in to write their first animation film. "We toyed with many ideas, wrote scripts but nothing seemed to fall in place till this one day, I was waiting at the traffic signal and saw these dogs playing in the dirt...uncared for, scruffy looking gang, totally mast in a garbage pile, and I instantly knew the characters of my story." So came about Roadside Romeo, and Adi asked Jugal to direct it too! "Two-and-a-half years, 150 people and we are all set to release on October 24."

Roadside Romeo is the story of how Romeo, a pet dog in an affluent household, becomes a stray overnight when the family decides to shift out. Pampered all his life, Romeo feels helpless on the streets till he falls for Laila, a canine beauty, and then fights the local don, Anna Charlie. The voices to the characters have been lent by Saif Ali Khan, Kareena Kapoor and Javed Jaffery respectively.

"I just knew Saif would fit best as Romeo is street-smart and has style. Laila is a diva, and who else would've portrayed her better than Kareena?" says the actor, who was last seen as Sanjeev Mehta in Aaja Nachle. Jaffery was a natural choice for "he is a versatile actor, you give him one option and he'll come up with ten variations! He's perfect for animation." An out-and-out commercial flick, full of dance, song (Saif and Javed sing a hip hop number for it too!) and drama - this is where Jugal's inspiration from Don, Amar Akbar Anthony and the likes comes - he explains how an animation movie differs that from of a regular one. "An animation film is made backwards. The dubbing happens first. Months were spent in getting the expression in each frame right. A retake means seeing the change two days later...it's all paper work, imagination and patience."

Roadside Romeo has kept the director busy and his acting plans, for now, are on hold "till something interesting comes up". And does he have any pets? "Well, now I do." Touché.

Heading: Girl on the go! - Indian Express
Content: A complaint has been filed against cricketer Harbhajan Singh, TV actor Mona Singh, Pak cricketer Wasim Akram, former Miss Universe Sushmita Sen and choreographer of a reality show on 'Colors' channel for allegedly hurting the religious sentiments. Mona and Harbhajan dressed as Ravana and Sita in the show. The complaint was filed by local Shiv Sena leader Sanjeev Sharma under Sections 295-A and 298 of the IPC in the court of Judicial Magistrate (First Class) Preet Mohan Sharma, who has fixed December 23 as the date for recording statement of the complainant.

Heading: Waiting to exhale! - Indian Express
Content:
City's Tishaa Khosla could well be MTV's youth icon for the year

Till last count she had crossed the 12,000 mark and was leading the list. A list that figures bigwigs from Bollywood - Shahid Kapoor, Salman Khan and Ranbir Kapoor to name a few! And Chandigarh's own Tishaa Khosla was way, way ahead and from the huge margins of votes, she seems to be heading towards a win. This time as MTV's Youth Icon for the year. "I never really knew I had been nominated till my friends mentioned it to me," says the 18-year-old who is currently in the spotlight for her book 'Pink or Black' that's already sold 10,000 copies in a month and is on its third reprint! "The feedback that I have got from readers, mostly youngsters, is very flattering," mentioned Tishaa, dressed once again in her favourite two colours.

Since the teen novel, published by Rupa & Co, hit the shelves, this Chandigarh girl who schooled in Sanawar has been featuring in interviews, formal launches and events all across the country. So is she finally feeling celebrity-like? "I don't want to see myself as one," chuckled Tishaa, who is already planning another teen novel. But before that, she's got the MTV Youth Icon 2008 nomination."I never knew I would come so far. Frankly, my icon has been Hollywood actress Audrey Hepburn. Not only was she a good actor but a true humanitarian," spoke Khosla, who is looking to garner support from the city. For the record, past winners include SRK, Anil Ambani and Rahul Dravid.

"I featured on MTV's youth campus show Wassup and have also spoken about my book at various schools and colleges. As for votes for the contest, I am banking on my city," she smiles to say listing out the website's link www.mtvyouthicon.in.com where one can vote for her. And what if she wins, which at the moment seems highly likely, Tishaa answers in all honesty: "To be a youth icon isn't easy. There comes in a lot of responsibility." Given the fact she's still a teenager herself, what are the youngsters of 2008 like? "They are clear in what they want but sometimes lose the focus," tells Tishaa. Clearly, she's stayed on track.

Heading: Celeb watch - Indian Express
Content:
With an aim to beautify the Panchkula bus stand, the Haryana Transport department is all set to construct an entrance gate at the entry point of the bus stand in Sector 5, Panchkula.

While the contract has already been allotted, the work for the same will start in a week's time and will be complete by this November end. To be constructed at a cost of around Rs 4 lakh, the entrance gate will also be one of the sources of income for the department with the provision of displaying of advertisements on the gate.

"This is for the first time that a fabricated entrance gate is coming up. The contract has been given to us and the work for the same will start in a week's time. The entrance gate will be around 107 feet in width and 31 feet in height and would have provision of displaying of advertisements," said Praveen Behal, an official of the Oceano Graphics, which has undertaken the construction work.

Behal added that besides the entrance gate, sheds for the vehicles in the bus stand parking will also be constructed. "For quite some time, this proposal to construct sheds for the vehicles was in the pipeline. The work will definitely be over by November end."

While for the residents, it is good that the bus stand, which was in a bad shape, will be beautified. Seema Malik, a resident of Sector 11, said: "The condition of the bus stand was very bad. Not only was it poorly maintained, there was no shed for the vehicles. The ongoing work will definitely help the commuters who frequently visit."

Heading: Foot loose - Indian Express
Content:
Usha Saboo has sent us a few leaf specimens of chrysanthemums, which have leaf spots and insect injury. I call her an intelligent gardener as she has told us about the movement of tiny red insects that also have a web made at the back of the leaf. The description given is detailed, as the insect she has found is almost microscopic and not usually detected by amateur gardeners. Usha, your plants have been attacked by mites and leaf spot disease. Spray rogor, dissolved at two millilitre to a litre of water. Mix with it bavistin, at one gram to a litre of water. Repeat the spray after a fortnight.

* A friend has offered me helliconia plant that is growing in her garden. Can I plant it now?

Paramjit Kaur, Chandigarh

It's a little late to plant helliconia, as it dies in winter and emerges in spring. If you plant it now it will not be established before the onset of winter and there is chance that you will lose the plant. Wait till spring.

* Should I start applying farmyard manure to my fruit trees? What precaution should I take?

Suraj Kumar, Panchkula

It is still early for applying farmyard manure. Wait till the middle of December. Make sure the manure you procure is well-rotten and add lindane powder, a fistful per plant as safeguard against white ants.

* The new growth of my citrus plants is being eaten by some insect and I find many black ants on the plant. The leaves are shrivelled. What is this due to and how can I check the problem?

Rajinder Kaur, Mohali

The insect in question is lemon butterfly larva and the one that causes leave curling is aphid and leaf miner. Spray rogor, dissolved at one millilitre to a litre of water. Repeat the spray after a fortnight.

Heading: Arms licence of Sukhbir’s wife foxes Gurgaon admn - Indian Express
Content:
Diwali Dil Se!

MY FM has rolled out a social campaign on 'Responsible Diwali' to motivate its listeners to observe a pollution-free Diwali. The campaign is titled 'Iss Diwali Lighting Karo Dil Se!' The radio station shall motivate its listeners to celebrate the festival of lights, good luck and prosperity in a safe, secure and environment-friendly manner by renouncing crackers and celebrating with lights instead. The other aspects of this campaign include the contest - 'The Best Lit House on Diwali Nite' which will see MY FM teams visit residential societies and announce the best lit house. The contest carries three awards ranging from Rs 25,000 to Rs 10,000.

'Office' happy

That's what students, home users and self-employed professionals can look forward to being. Microsoft has announced a slash in the price of Home and Student edition of Office 2007, earlier priced at Rs 4,600 in the Indian market, the software package will now be available for Rs 3,699. The package includes Word 2007, Excel 2007, PowerPoint 2007 and OneNote 2007. This festive season offer aims to make it easier for consumers to get "the world's leading productivity software along with their new PC or laptop."

Heading: BSF begins talks with Pak Rangers - Indian Express
Content:
The Gurgaon administration found itself on a sticky wicket following the arms renewal application submitted by Harsimrat Badal, wife of MP Sukhbir Singh Badal.

Harsimrat was granted the arms licence on May 28, 2002, on a hotel address, owned by the Badal family in Udyog Vihar, Gurgaon. The licence was renewed in 2005 on the same address. According to the India Arms Act, the applicant must be a resident of the area from where he or she wants an arms licence.

Harsimrat had mentioned her address as 443, Phase V, Udyog Vihar, Gurgaon, in her original application and two renewals. A five-star hotel (Trident) stands today on that address.

It is believed that Harsimrat was granted the licence in May 2002 due to the pressure from high-ups as at that time Haryana was ruled by Badals' close friend, Om Prakash Chautala.

During this period, Anurag Rastogi was the Gurgaon Deputy Commissioner (DC), Kuldip Singh Siag the Senior Superintendent of Police and RS Kharb the Sub-Divisional Magistrate. These three officers are primarily responsible for the lapse. In 2005, when her licence was renewed, Bhupinder Singh Hooda was Haryana's CM. At that time, Sudhir Rajpal was the DC, Yoginder Nehra the SSP and incumbent Jai Singh Sangwan the SDM.

Harsimrat was granted permission to have three types of weapons-- revolver, pistol and rifle. She has an all-India permit to carry her weapons. As per her licence, she had bought a rifle from her husband Sukhbir Singh Badal.

For the renewal, Harsimrat had attached papers of land allotment issued by the Haryana State Industries and Infrastructure Development Corporation (HSIIDC) for industrial plot number 443, UV, Phase V, Gurgaon. The land had been allotted to M/s Orbit Resorts Pvt Limited, which has three directors, Harsimrat, Sukhbir Badal and Sukhbir's mother Surinder Kaur. While applying for renewal on September 26, 2008, in an application addressed to SDM Jai Singh Sangwan, Harsimrat had stated her address as the area where Hotel Trident stands. The Badals had tied up with the Trident Group to run the hotel.

However, the Lok Sabha Secretariat record mentions two addresses of Sukhbir Singh Badal (MP). His permanent address: house number 256, Sector 9-C, Chandigarh, and his present address is 12, Safdarjung Road, Delhi.

SDM Sangwan said as per the laid procedure, the application was forwarded to the Police Department for verification. Sub-Inspector Dayaram has categorically stated in his verification report that the said property was owned by Harsimrat, Sukhbir Singh Badal and Surinder Kaur. "Harsimrat visits the place (Trident hotel) regularly (aati jatti rahti hai) to look after her property," said the SI report.

Confirming the report, Station House Officer (SHO) of Udyog Vihar Police Station said in his statement that Harsimrat visits this place (kabhi kabhi aati jatti hai) and forwarded it to the Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP).

Commissioner says...

Gurgaon Commissioner Rajiv Sharma said licence could be renewed on the basis of the fact that Harsimrat had a family property at Udyog Vihar, Gurgaon. Haryana DGP Ranjiv Dalal and Home Secretary Feroza Mehrotra were not available for comments.

Heading: Give Rs 50 lakh to fight Capt case: House to govt - Indian Express
Content:
The increasing influx of fake currency would be discussed at the bi-annual talks between the Border Security Force (BSF) and the Pakistan Rangers that began in Lahore today.

BSF's 17-member delegation, led by Additional Director General UK Bansal, today left for the meeting during the wee hours. He said all border-related issues, including intrusion, smuggling of drugs and fake currency, would be discussed in length in the next two days.

Bansal, who was received by Pak Rangers Deputy Director General Shafagat Nawaj on Pakistani side at the Attari-Wagah border, said talks would focus on joint operations and cooperation to check smuggling.

"There is no single point from where the fake currency is being thrust into the Indian territories. It is coming from Bangladesh, Nepal and Pakistan," said Bansal.

The Pakistani media gathered on the other side of the border and asked Bansal about the recent death of Pakistani prisoner Asif when he was waiting for repatriation in Amritsar Central Jail. The ADG said they were willing to send Pakistani prisoners who have completed their sentences to their country, but there were problems from the Pakistan's High Commission.

Heading: Ex-BJP minister Karan Singh joins Cong - Indian Express
Content:
For the first time ever, the assembly has asked the Punjab government to allocate Rs 50 lakh to fight the case against former chief minister Capt Amarinder Singh in the Supreme Court.

Notably, Capt has challenged his unseating from the assembly and the Vidhan Sabha is a party in the case.

Sources said Speaker Nirmal Singh Kahlon wrote a demi-official (DO) letter to Punjab Finance Minister Manpreet Singh Badal, demanding Rs 50 lakh to be allocated to the assembly budget. "The Finance Department has written to the assembly that it has decided to allocate the money and would initially release Rs 15 lakh.

The department also said that the Vidhan Sabha should get in touch with the Advocate General's office to take legal advice and hire a lawyer, and accordingly inform the department," said an officer.

Assembly Secretary Madan Mohan said, "We have no budgetary provision for such a purpose, so we had to request the government to give us money."

Sources said the Vidhan Sabha has not yet decided on the lawyer, but the name of SC advocate Harish Salve is doing the rounds. It was learnt that he charges Rs 3 lakh per court appearance.

Former chief minister Capt Amarinder Singh has a team of three lawyers, PP Rao, TR Andhyarjuna and Abhishek Singhvi, while the Punjab government has Advocate General HS Mattewal, Ravi Shankar Prasad and standing counsel Ajay Pal.

Heading: Mastermind of attack on dera chief is in Pakistan, say police - Indian Express
Content:
Former BJP minister Karan Singh today formally joined the Congress party. This development comes as another shot in the arm for the Congress, that had last week succeeded in attracting BJP stalwart Jagdev Chand's son, Narender Thakur. Karan Singh was a BJP member for 27 years. Last year, just before the Assembly elections, he had quit the BJP to contest from Banjar constituency of Kullu district on a BSP ticket, only to lose.

His joining the Congress was marked by a jubilant ceremony by the party in Kullu, which was attended by Pradesh Congress Committee president Kaul Singh Thakur. Karan Singh had indicated a desire to join the Congress about four months ago, but the party kept the decision pending for a long time.

Talking over phone from Kullu, Karan Singh said, "I had tried to return to the BJP and had even met the Chief Minister five months ago, when I had conveyed my intentions. However, I did not get a favourable reply." He said he had got a "respectful entry" into the Congress.

"CM Prem Kumar Dhumal has become too ambitious and has ignored many genuine party workers," he alleged, adding that the BJP was crumbling in the state and this would have an adverse impact for the party in the upcoming general elections.

Karan Singh served as education minister in the previous Dhumal government from 1998-2003. He is the younger brother of former BJP state chief and former MP Maheshwar Singh and is considered a prominent leader in Kullu area. Karan Singh said, "When my brother Maheshwar Singh has not been given his due by the party despite being a two-time MP, two-time MLA and holding various important posts in the party, my chances were bleak."

His decision has come as another jolt for the BJP, which is already shaken after Narender Thakur's departure.

Heading: PTA stir gets new lease of life with support from rights body - Indian Express
Content:
Following the interrogation of the alleged human bombs who were planning to strike at Dera Sacha Sauda chief, the Punjab police have come to know of the whereabouts of Bakhshish Singh, the alleged mastermind in the case.

Police sources say Bakhshish has escaped to Pakistan, and is funding and plotting terrorist activities from across the border. Sources add that he is planning to spread communal distress in the state.

"Those planning the terrorist activities across the border understand the sensitivity of the dera issue. Gurmeet Ram Rahim Singh is a soft target for them despite his Z-plus security," says an official.

Sources add that the the plot was unearthed after the arrest of Amarjit Singh, a Samana resident, by Jalandhar police almost two weeks ago. Amarjit was arrested for possessing explosives and was in constant touch with another Samana resident, Bagicha Singh.

"Jalandhar police shared this vital information with Patiala police, who subsequently arrested Gobind Kaur and Bagicha Singh," say sources.

Patiala police are now procuring the mobile numbers used by the accused to get in touch with Bakhshish to expose their network.

"We are awaiting the details of the mobile phones that were used," Investigating Officer Shaminder Pal Singh says.

Jalandhar SSP PK Rai says, "We also know that Bakshish Singh is in Pakistan. We had earlier speculated that he is in India. We are sharing all our information with Patiala police."

Bagicha Singh, Amarjeet Singh and Gobind Kaur had allegedly procured mobile numbers using fake identity proof. Patiala SP (D) GS Chauhan says a joint probe is being conducted by Patiala and Jalandhar police to nab the persons involved in the case. Regarding fears that some persons may be inside the dera masquerading as devotees, Chauhan says investigations are on, and nothing concrete can be said yet.

Bakhshsish was earlier a member of the dreaded Bhindrawale Tiger Force of Khalistan, and later joined Khalistan Commando Force. He was out on bail since 2003. After an attack on the dera head the same year, he went underground.

Heading: ‘I will protest Sukhbir’s re-laying of stone’ - Indian Express
Content:
The agitation of PTA teachers was today infused with fresh enthusiasm after the Global Human Rights Council extended support to their stir. The protest was on the verge of waning off a day ago following the arrest of all protesting teachers. A group of 20 PTA teachers, 15 from Ani and Mandi, have also decided to approach the Himachal Pradesh High Court with a petition challenging the criteria of inquiries held by SDMs and ADMs into the complaints of irregular appointments of PTA teachers.

During the past three days, the government had released three lists that included names of PTA teachers whose recruitments were found to be irregular and names of these 20 teachers had also figured in the lists.

The human rights council today said that besides filing a complaint with the National Human Rights Commission against Chief Minister Prem Kumar Dhumal, Education Minister I.D. Dhiman, DGP G.S. Gill and Shimla ASP Mahinder Singh, it is also preparing to file a petition of contempt of court in the Supreme Court against Chief Secretary of Himachal Pradesh and Superintendent of Police, Shimla, for initiating violent action against the agitating teachers, which is in violation of the Supreme Court's rulings.

President of central body of the council Arvind Thakur today said the complaint would be heard by a three-member bench of the NHRC, New Delhi, on November 2.

"The petition of contempt of court would be filed in the Supreme Court on Tuesday and notices would be served to the Chief Secretary and SP Shimla", said Thakur, while talking to mediapersons in Shimla. He added that use of force against peacefully protesting teachers and beating them up brutally is violation of human rights.

Vivek Mehta, president of PTA Association, said the mode of protest through indefinite hunger strike was disrupted on Monday, but from Wednesday they would begin the strike at the same place near the Secretariat. "And if the government still does not allow us to do so, we would seek the intervention of the High Court through a PIL to give us a place where we can hold our protest peacefully," he said.

Heading: Ahluwalia’s police remand extended by another day - Indian Express
Content:
The Congress MLA from Bholath constituency, Sukhpal Singh Khaira, was released unconditionally by the Kapurthala civil administration late last night when he refused to take the bail.

Khaira today said he had information that SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal would re-lay the foundation stone of Sant Baba Prem Singh Memorial Gate at Begowal in Kapurthala district that was dedicated to the people by the previous Amarinder Singh government two years ago.

In a letter to the Punjab CM, Khaira has threatened to launch a peaceful demonstration in case the "plan" was not cancelled. He said the foundation stone was laid on September 16, 2006, by Amarinder Singh, "who had agreed to my proposal for the gate and had allocated Rs 25 lakh out of his discretionary funds for the project". The construction work was given to PWD (B&R) and the work was completed in January this year. "I, being the elected representative of Bholath, dedicated the gate to the people in January last," he said.

"As Sant Prem Singh Murale Wale had served relentlessly in fields of education and health, I had requested Amarinder Singh to construct a memorial gate in his honour," he said. Khaira alleged that in order to achieve "cheap political publicity" Bibi Jagir Kaur has invited Sukhbir to re-lay the stone. He said SAD's former MLA Bibi Jagir Kaur has misinformed the government on the facts of the memorial gate. He said Sukhbir was not entitled to inaugurate or lay the foundation stone of any project other than Faridkot parliamentary constituency from where he is an MP.

Meanwhile, today large number of Congress workers staged a dharna in front of Kapurthala DC office against the arrest of Khaira.

Heading: DGP asks for report on gunmen given to VIPs - Indian Express
Content:
Just before Special Judge J.L. Gupta was to announce his order on the bail petition of Subhash Ahluwalia today, his advocate N.S. Chandel presented before the court a fresh calculation of the bank accounts under question. This left the public prosecutor seeking more time from the court to consult his accountant to verify the correctness of these accounts. As the decision on the bail petition could not be given today, the court extended Ahluwalia's police remand by another day. The case would now come up for hearing on Wednesday.

While submitting the fresh calculations, Ahluwalia's advocate Chandel stated that if these calculations are taken into consideration it cannot be said that the assets and the expenditure of the accused is disproportionate of his known sources of income. He added that in this case there is no need for custodial interrogation of the accused.

Ahluwalia was first given police remand till October 13, which was extended on Monday by a day as the Judge had reserved his order for Tuesday. As a copy of the fresh calculations of the defence was supplied to the Special Public Prosecutor today, he sought time to consult his accountant to verify the facts and in view of this, no order was passed today.

On request of both the parties, the court allowed for fixing Wednesday as the day for further arguments and the parties were directed to bring along their accountants so that no dispute remains regarding the income and expenditure of the accused and his family members. Ahluwalia's accountant was also present in the court on Monday when the team of five lawyers of Ahluwalia had asked the Judge to allow the accountant to clarify the stance on financial transactions through the accounts of the accused.

On Monday, the Vigilance Bureau had put up an application for interrogating Subhash Ahluwalia in the IGMC Hospital, where he is admitted after he was arrested, but it was turned down by the medical officer saying that he was not fit to support investigation. Ahluwalia also underwent an MRI for his spine on Monday.

No interrogation could be conducted by the Vigilance today, which is planning to put up an application to allow interrogation by late evening.

Heading: No state mass media officer for over a year - Indian Express
Content:
The diamond robbery case in which son of an SSP was involved along with his gunmen has raised the hackles of Punjab DGP NPS Aulakh.

He today ordered police officers to check the deployment of gunmen and give him a certificate, saying that that securitymen given to the VIPs were not on duty of some other person, including family of the person. In case of a lapse, the security should be withdrawn, said the order.

Sources said Aulakh issued orders to all the head of the wings, commandants and SSPs, besides ADGP (Security). By November 1, all the police officers will have to get back to the DGP with the certificates. Aulakh said, "It has been done so that the security is not misused."

Sources said the state police provide security cover to 1,800-odd persons, of which 800 were police officers, both serving and retired, from the rank of DSP to DGP. Some 250 of them are with IAS and PCS officers and a few judicial officers and rest are with politicians and a few journalists. A police officer said, "About 15 per cent of the total force of the state police (9,000 policemen) is deployed as securitymen. The state police spend about Rs 200 crore every year on them. A question in this regard was tabled in the last Assembly session by a legislator, but the government gave no answer."

Heading: BJP, Cong bicker over sports body election - Indian Express
Content:
The post of state mass media and education officer has been lying vacant for the past one and a half year, as the Punjab Health Department has found no time to conduct the meeting of the departmental promotion committee (DPC) since June 2007.

Sources in the department said names of three district mass media and education officers were empanelled over a year ago. But, the four officers, including Principal Secretary, Health; Director, Health; Secretary, Personnel, and Secretary, Social Welfare Department, were yet to call the DPC meeting.

The state mass media officer plays an important role in spreading awareness about family welfare programmes and arranging special health-related programmes for women, youth, farmers and labourers.

He also initiates studies on the effectiveness of various health programmes, said sources, adding that in his absence, the health authorities lose the link with people at the grassroots.

Principal Secretary, Health and Family Welfare, Vijay Kain, could not be contacted despite repeated attempts.

Director, Health, Dr SPS Sohal said he would soon look into the matter.

Heading: Splitting of SGPC will push Punjab into dark days: CM - Indian Express
Content:
The Congress and the BJP in the state are yet again entangled in a controversy, this time over election of a sports body. BJP MLA Virender Kanwar today submitted a complaint to the Superintendent of Police, Shimla, R.M. Sharma, on the basis of which an FIR was registered against two supporters of former minister Ram Lal Thakur for allegedly attacking Kanwar and his security guard while he was on his way to participate in the election of HP Volleyball Association. The election was held at Rampur on Monday and the complaint was submitted to the SP today.

"I have seen the complaint and have directed the Rampur Police Station to register an FIR against the persons involved," said the SP. He confirmed that Kanwar's medical examination at IGMC shows injuries. The complaint alleges that former secretary of the association H.K. Pathik and Suresh Thakur attacked Kanwar and three more persons entered into a scuffle with BJP MLAs Satpal Satti, B.K. Chauhan and Tejwant Negi and former BJP minister Praveen Sharma, who were heading to the election venue.

Addressing mediapersons in Shimla today, Kanwar said he was unanimously elected as new president, but later Thakur went out of the election venue and declared himself as the president. Thakur has held the post for the past 20 years. The central observer and state observer were also present during the election. However, Kanwar announced his future plans as president and said that a volleyball championship would be organised before November 20.

Heading: 2,000 handpumps for state - Indian Express
Content:
Punjab Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal today warned that any move to "divide the Sikh community" by splitting the Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (SGPC) would push the state "back into the dark days of eighties and early nineties".

"Sikhs are known to be a brave community that made the most significant sacrifices for securing freedom of the country," he said, while addressing the National Integration Council meet here.

"Without mincing words, let me say that despite this, Sikhs have been treated most unfairly and condemned as traitors, thanks to the highly opportunist and dangerous political games players by the rulers," Badal said. "The latest example being the dangerous move to try and divide the Sikh community by splitting their religious organisation, the SGPC, and setting up a separate committee outside Punjab," he said.

Badal had recently met Prime Minister Manmohan Singh to protest the move.

He said the SGPC was formed after the community earned the right to manage its shrines. "It is shocking that a national party, which calls itself secular, has not only tried to sabotage this glorious representative religious body of my community, but even put the splitting of the SGPC on its election manifesto," Badal said. He claimed that a very "dangerous situation was emerging". He thanked the PM for his "timely intervention in the matter".

The Punjab CM said the country's social structure and economic health were facing some of the greatest challenges and "communal harmony was facing threats from several quarters".

"It may sound a bit harsh but the impression one gets of India at this juncture is of a nation almost at war with itself...and this calls for an immediate and massive nationwide initiative to come out of the situation," he said. Badal claimed that political outfits and social groups were exploiting the situation due to their vote bank politics.

Heading: Complainant says Daler should surrender passport - Indian Express
Content:
To solve the problem of drinking water in the rural areas, 2,000 handpumps would be installed in various parts of the state, said Irrigation and Public Health (IPH) Minister Ravinder Ravi, while talking to mediapersons at the Circuit House today. He said in order to streamline the working of various departments, an award of Rs 2.5 lakh would be given to the best department. He said the drinking water schemes for Nahan would be released so that pending sewerage system of Rs 14 crore can be approved.

He said it was unfortunate that the Union government had cut the supply of rice for BPL and antyodya families. He said the state government has urged the Centre to release the full quota of rice and increase the quota for refined oil from one kilogram to two kilogram per family. He said the state government has increased subsidy budget from Rs 90 crore to Rs 141 crore for 2008-09. He blamed the previous Congress regime for encouraging corruption in the state.

Later he went to Paonta and laid the foundation stone for drinking water and irrigation schemes at Kiratpur, Fatehpur, Kishanpura and Badaripur. He also presided over the closing ceremony of Yamuna Sharad Mahotsava at Paonta Sahib.

Heading: Hisar awaits Astroturf promised 8 yrs ago - Indian Express
Content:
The complainant in the case of illegal human trafficking against Punjabi pop singer Daler Mehndi has sought the surrender of his passport before the trial court.

Moving an application before the court of JMIC PS Rai, complainant Gurpreet Singh pleaded that since the court had already framed charges and Daler was the main accused in the case, he should surrender his passport, just as all other accused had done.

Defence counsel BS Sodhi objected, saying that since Daler has been participating in the proceedings of the case every time the case was heard, surrendering of the passport was not required. The decision would be taken by the court only after hearing the arguments on the next date of hearing.

Meanwhile, Daler Mehndi, through his counsel, also moved an application under Section 207 of the CrPC, seeking copies of the statements made by all the prosecution witnesses before the court under Section 164 of CrPC.

Heading: BJP, INLD work out seat-sharing formula - Indian Express
Content:
Getting an Astroturf of international standards in their township seems to be a distant dream for the hockey players here, even though an announcement to this effect had been made about eight years ago.

In 2000, the then Union sports minister, Uma Bharti, during her visit to Hisar, had announced the setting up of a hockey academy in Hisar, along with an Astroturf of international standard. Yogram Sharma, a social worker, has been knocking the doors of the Prime Minister and the President in this regard.

Talking to The Indian Express, Sharma said, "I have written letters to the President, Prime Minister Manmohan Singh and also AICC chief Sonia Gandhi, but no action has been taken in this regard."

In information sought under the Right to Information Act, the Haryana Sports Department said that 10 acres of land has been earmarked and handed over to Hisar District Sports Council for the purpose. It was also stated that the Hisar Deputy Commissioner has also been approached for preparation of a detailed project and estimate of expenditure, so that it can be approved.

But the District Administration has taken no initiative for the project. Sharma pointed out that Hisar has two universities, and the talent of the youth can be harnessed for representation in national and international hockey games. Sharma said it is unfortunate that the district administration is not working on the project.

Rajendra Sihag, a national hockey player, has also expressed his concern over the delay in setting the hockey academy, even after adequate land has already been handed over to the district administration.

When contacted, Deputy Commissioner O.P. Sheoran said that he had visited the land allocated for the construction of the hockey academy, and that the required steps would be taken soon.

Heading: Shall we dance? - Indian Express
Content:
A disgruntled Haryana BJP can seek solace from the fact that it would contest the Lok Sabha elections on majority of seats in the state. The BJP is expected to contest six out of the 10 Lok Sabha seats in Haryana. Its alliance partner, Indian National Lok Dal (INLD), will have to be content with the remaining four.

The seats to be shared have also been tentatively worked out, said sources. The BJP is likely to contest the Ambala, Karnal, Sonepat, Faridabad, Gurgaon and Rohtak Lok Sabha seats. BJP has just one sitting MP seat from Sonepat, while the INLD failed to open its account during the last Lok Sabha elections. Kurukshetra, Bhiwani, Sirsa and Hisar seats will be left for the INLD to contest.

BJP sources say the rationale behind getting to contest majority of the seats in Haryana is that the party had polled 18 per cent of votes during the previous Lok sabha elections. A senior BJP leader, requesting anonymity, said, "We were second on at least five seats during the previous poll. Besides, during the Parliament elections, votes are cast essentially between the two national parties — BJP and the Congress."

INLD leaders are so far tightlipped on the seat sharing. If sources are to be believed, the Indian National Lok Dal is unlikely to put up a resistance to this 6:4 ratio heavily tilted towards the BJP.

An INLD leader quipped, "It is the NDA which will contest all the 10 Lok Sabha seats in the state." The two newly-formed alliance partners are now viewing the prospects of winnable candidates for the elections. Given the bitter-sweet relation between the BJP and the INLD in Haryana, the state unit of the BJP is unhappy with the alliance worked out by the party high command with the motive to defeat the Congress. The alliance is also planning a joint rally in November at Sonepat. Prime ministerial candidate L.K. Advani, INLD supremo Om Prakash Chautala and other senior leaders of both the parties will participate in the rally.

Heading: Hafed to form small farmers’ agri-business consortium - Indian Express
Content:
Maitreyee Pahuri will get bhangra, giddha & bharatnatyam on the same stage for Poompoohar

She's looking for a single beat where the dancers can blend and create a mesmerizing melange. Dancer and choreographer Maitreyee Pahuri is here for Poompoohar, a cultural extravaganza of Tamil Nadu in collaboration with the Chandigarh Administration and is looking forward to presenting the diverse dances as a single piece. Essentially a kathak dancer Maitreyee's well-conversant with other classical and folk forms of the country and agrees in India the role of choreographer especially for classical and folk dance forms is still vague. Maitreyee has a repertory in Delhi and has choreographed for international events like Incredible India in New York, Moscow et al, besides other important shows for the Ministry of Culture and Tourism. "I travel across the country and abroad to do shows. This one's special for I've never got bhangra, giddha, bharatnatyam and mohiniattam together,'' the dancer talks about the shows titled Kalai Kolam and Kalai Tamarai. Dance and rangoli, explains Maitreyee is the essence of Kalai Kolam and more than 200 dancers will be involved in the show, the idea being to give the artists freedom to showcase their talent, yet give the audience a unique experience of seeing divergent cultures and moves on the same stage. Language, agrees Maitreyee can be a barrier to get the point across, "but we as dancers can speak with gestures, which I am really doing and also improvising on the steps, music, lights etc so that it's a perfect mix, yet the dancers have an identity of their own,'' Maitreyee gets back to the stage.

Heading: Tube talk - Indian Express
Content:
In an effort to give a boost to the agri-business activities of small farmers in the state, the Haryana State Cooperative Supply and Marketing Federation (HAFED) is planning to form Small Farmers' Agri-business Consortium (SFAC) on the same pattern of the existing Central body of farmers. SFAC, working at the Central level, has been undertaking various initiatives to link the small farmers to technology as well as to the markets in association with private, corporate or cooperative sector.

Giving information about the proposal, Sudhir Rajpal, Managing Director, HAFED, told ENS, "We will soon register SFAC as a private limited company and the total capital investment will be around Rs 2 crore. The board will comprise representatives from Hafed, Kisan club and the NGO. The equity will be also be shared by these three organisations. About Rs 1 crore will be obtained from the banks as term loan, Rs 50 lakh will be granted by the Government of India as subsidy and the rest will be equity in the form of share capital and venture capital. Our consultants have prepared the project report and soon it will be sent to the Central government for approval. At first SFAC will work in Sonepat district and after it becomes successful, the farmers of other regions will also be involved."

Hafed plans to promote organic farming through SFAC initially and it has already identified 160 acres of certified area for producing organic vegetables. "About 30 farmers will be engaged at first in the venture and we aim to cover an area of 1,000 acres over a period of five years. The project, once implemented, will help farmers to streamline the marketing process of their products," said another senior official of Hafed.

The agricultural products to be marketed under SFAC initiative will be brought into the market under a new brand name. These will be exported as well as sold in the NCR region. SFAC will also provide post-harvest management support to farmers. "This will include picking up crop from fields, grading, sorting, storing and transporting them to markets. Refrigerated vans will be available for preventing damage to crop and, if required, the products will be stored in cold-chains," said the official.

Heading: Health Bulletin - Indian Express
Content:
'Dance has always been my passion'
Veteran actor Asha Parekh comes back to television, this time as a judge

She's worn many a hat before, but this is a brand-new one. After a long sabbatical, veteran actor Asha Parekh is on screen again. This time on the all-new channel 9X that sees Parekh step into the shoes of a judge on the show 'Tyohaar Dhamaaka'. "The concept appealed to me instantly and I didn't take too long to say yes," mentions Parekh, speaking to us from Mumbai where she's currently shooting. Here, she's referred to as 'Mahaguru'. "Television has changed so much over the years and when I heard they were putting together a show that would showcase major festivals of India along with Indian classical dance forms, I was impressed," mentions the Bollywood queen of the '60s, revered for her dancing skills. Interestingly, while she's directed many soaps for television, not many are aware that she runs a dance academy back home. "Yes, it's nice to work with young people. There's so much talent in the country and equally large number of reality talent shows on television. It's a great way for aspirants to make a mark," tells Parekh, who is to date best remembered for her directorial venture Kora Kaagaz, a weekly that ran to a full house on Star Plus. "And that was much before the daily sagas of today. Even I had a saas and a bahu in my script but the treatment was so different," the director makes her point. On why she decided to take a break, the answer's equally blunt. "There's a time for everything. Kora Kaagaz had a beginning and an end. As for me, I wanted to give direction a break," says the former Censor Board Chairman who is taking her time to get behind the camera once again. "Whenever I do, I will tell a woman's story again," she puts across firmly.

But before that she's happy to be sitting in the judge's seat. "Dance has been my passion. I am so glad that I will get to see traditional dances on television and performances by some of the best actors of TV today," she sums up. As for the show, produced by SOL Productions, it will pit TV stars in teams from four zones. The four teams will compete on different festive themes, and the best team will be crowned by Parekh. While Parekh is the judge, the show is hosted by actor-dancer Sudha Chandran. 'Tyohaar Dhamaaka' will air Mondays to Thursdays at 8.30 pm.

Heading: The Love Stone - Indian Express
Content:
Student agendas are changing. The latest is health

When you go to the mechanic, you talk mechanical language. You say your engine has a ping, a rattle, or a grrrrch. And you sure know the reason for it — rash driving, bad roads or untimely service. But when it comes to your own engine (read body mechanism), you pull a blank or better still pose to be ignorant. Is it right? "Not at all," chorus these youngsters, who are waking up to the call of fitness and not only realise, but also preach the benefits of a healthy lifestyle. Here's talking to a few who are striving to make Chandigarh a healthy city.

Walking in DAV School, Sector 8, we meet a group of 30 shuttling in and out of classes. Priyanka Shandlya of GCG-11 taking permission from the principal Vibha Ray, Abhinav Sharma of Chitkara College handing out the survey forms to the students and Karan Bhatia of SD College, preparing for a speech. "We as a part of AIESEC are here to spread awareness about AIDS," Rohan Sahni of DAV College tells us that for the purpose they have received sponsorship to the tune of Rs seven lakh from Standard Chartered Bank and have had a training session in Pondicherry. While 10 students took formal training, they taught another 90 and are now visiting eight government schools, Rayat School and Shivalik Public School among others. The purpose, they say is to educate the students in their language. "The infotainment way," chirps Ankita Deambi, a BCom first-year student, who says something stated by peers has greater retention.

In another corner of the city, PEC students too spread nuggets of wisdom in their own statement style. "We request the youth to go vegetarian," smiles Pranav Talwar, a first year Electrical Engineering student and member of Yes!+ club (Youth Empowerment Skills Workshop), who as a part of his group has crossed the first hurdle. "Combo, a non-vegetarian joint, was converted into a vegetarian one after we stated the positives of a green diet," says Ramnik Bansal, who is an IIM-Bangalore pass-out, citing global researches that promote vegetarian diet for wholesome well-being.

Stated as a sure-fire win-win, teachers, mentors and parents are a happy lot with this transition. "The youngsters are now raising their voice for India's health. Rather than we guiding them about the do's and don'ts of good health, they do the preaching," says Aparna Kaushal of Government College, Sector 11, as she takes us to the gymnasium hall, where about 100 students are practicing yoga. Holding these classes and asking more to join in, here too AIDS is what they spread awareness about.

As for the members of Rotract, polio and shortage of blood are the core concerns. Having been a part of pulse polio camps in the past, "we organised a blood donation camp at the UT Guest House on Tuesday," Akaash, a member tells us.

While, the UT administration is going head-over- heels trying to make the city smoke free, "Nothing really happens till the time the citizens realise the ill- effects and decide to give up the habit," says Bharat Sharma, a student of DAV College. And helping the cause is Burning Brain Society. "With about 5,500 young volunteers, it's only youngsters, who can bring in a revolution and provide aq much-needed healing touch to the increasing number of lifestyle diseases," says Hemant Goswami of Burning Brain Society.

Ho to health!

Heading: Foot Loose - Indian Express
Content:
Are girls trained in their cribs to adore pink or is it the loving vibration of the stone and its colour that pulls us towards it? Rose quartz represents love, emotional healing and balance. Rose quartz is the macro crystalline variety of the quartz family. The colour band includes pale pinks to the rarer rosy-red hues and stands unique in inheriting colour owing to titanium impurities and iron and manganese. Available mostly in translucent form, the few transparent ones are breathtaking. Its lustre is vitreous. It is found in coarse grained rock usually granite and is sourced from India, Brazil, Japan, Germany, US and some of the best ones come from Madagascar. The soothing, hazy crystal is loved around the world for its unique powder pink colour. Historically revered as the symbol of beauty and love it is still known as the stone of unconditional and gentle love. The origin of this absorbing stone is still under debate though beads were found in Mesopotamia (today's Iraq) that date back to 7000 BC. Rose quartz jewellery was evidently the ultimate romantic statement and Assyrians and Romans were the first ones to enjoy it for carving seals use it as a healing stone. Egyptians believed the dazzling pink stone to inhibit anti-aging properties. As per Greek mythology white quartz was once stained by the co-mingled blood of Adonis and Aphrodite, hence the romantic colour and beliefs. Romans still use it customarily as a gift of love. Early Chinese used it for carving the statues of the Goddess of Peace as they revered the colour for its gentleness. Even today many beliefs are associated with it. Believers esteem it for balancing Yin and Yang energies and strengthening communications. It is accepted for strengthening friendships and balancing emotions.

Rose quartz, some say, benefits the heart and circulation. It may help in healing migraines if worn close to the heart. Feng Shui values it for strengthening the flow of love and some romance in marriage. Besides spiritual beliefs, it is often carved into popular ornamental shapes like hearts, spheres, obelisks, pyramids and figurines. Rose quartz is used in landscaping, as mineral specimen, in tiles and in lapidary work .Often available in translucent form more cabochons are used in creating jewellery. Actual crystals of rose quartz are very rare but the occasional few found styled with diamonds and accenting stones make beautiful and most dazzling jewellery. Rose Quartz and diamond jewellery add the right amount of feminine sparkle to most attires and makes it truly beautiful.

This semi-precious stone is photosensitive. Since it cracks and chips rather easily, it should be handled cautiously. Rose quartz is not enhanced. The darker shades are usually dyed. Evenness in colour should be prioritized while choosing this gorgeous stone. The Cullen Hall exhibits one of the largest 1400+ carat Star Rose Quartz .Follow your heart, wear any ensemble and accessorize with it with a rose quartz.

(The writer is a city-based researcher specialising in jewellery art and can be contacted at sameeraahaan02@gmail.com)

Heading: What is a totem? - Indian Express
Content:
For the occasion
This is perhaps the best time to go on shopping spree. With Diwali not too far off and Karva Chauth around the corner, sisters-in-law Neha and Shilpi have put together a festive spread for the ladies at Sector 8 (H. no 555). "This is one time that everyone is looking forward to," tells Neha who has rolled out a four-day special for Karva Chauth by bringing in an exhibition of suits and sarees along with diamond jewellery. Completing the festivities is a mehndi- wallah and colourful bangles on sale. First up are heavy suits with sequines, gota patti and stone work. "The sequins we are using are imported from Japan," explained Neha. While colour is at play here with bright tones and equally bright motifs and embellishments, it's the block print collection that's worth a dekko. Working with pure fabrics such as crepe, silk, georgette, the two have designed block-printed sarees that look far from being just prints! The block print suits come in crepes with heavy dupattas complete with fine trimmings and there's also a range of kurtis and semi-formal wear. The exhibition is on till October 15.

Heading: ‘Discrimination with Majha’ to be Congress poll plank - Indian Express
Content:
Some would argue that modern-day totems exist in the modern-day art and to some extent that may be true, however the content would have changed drastically and the votive nature of the totem has been transformed to modern concerns.

The original totemic art originated in the Pacific Coast northwest from Alaska and British Columbia. Native Indians carved wooden totems, imbued them with a spiritual symbolism and have been protected by the dwindling tribes who live on the coast. The monumental totems of the Haida and Tlingit in the Totem Bight State Historical Park in Alaska, and the intricate artwork of the Kwakuitl, Salish, and Bella Coola are worth mentioning. The significance of totems is that their verticality lends them a status that is both intimidating and sublime. Historian Eddie Malin (1986) has proposed a theory of totem pole development. He argues that the poles served the purpose of house posts, funerary containers, and memorial markers into symbols of clan and family wealth and prestige. In popular culture, totems have also been associated with witchery and the black arts.

The carvings on totems are highly symbolic but they have also been adapted to bags, T-shirts for tourists and souvenirs. Unfortunately very few of the original poles remain because they were made of wood and decayed easily in the rainforest. The custom of carving these poles may pre-date the existing ones that date back to the 1880s, since there are many accounts by European travelers. Post-Impressionist painter Paul Gauguin who set up an artist's residency on the islands of Tahiti was also influenced by totemic art and it reflects in his art time and again. One lyrical depiction of this influence is his painting of a girl lying on a yellow blanket being watched over by a spirit-a totem that has glowing eyes and presence that is neither benign nor aggressive.

(Demystify art, e-mail georgina.maddox@expressindia.com)

Heading: Bansal, two others out on bail - Indian Express
Content:
With the debate on 'discrimination against Majha' raging, the Congress leaders from the area are trying to make the issue their main poll plank.

The Congressmen, who have already demanded a White Paper from the government on the issue, alleged that mega projects and developmental schemes were heading towards Malwa at the cost of Majha and Doaba.

Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal hails from Bathinda in Malwa and his son, the ruling SAD (B) chief Sukhbir Singh Badal, has been focusing on the home town, they said. "I had raised the issue earlier too. Badal family sees nothing beyond their home town. All projects are being taken to their region, while Majha and Doaba are being neglected," said former Congress minister and a senior leader from Majha Partap Singh Bajwa.

His views were seconded by former MLAs Sukhjinder Singh Randhawa, Jasbir Singh Dimpa, Ashwani Sekhri, Harpartap Singh Ajnala and MLA Sukhbinder Singh Sarkaria.

"We have taken up the matter with our state party chief Mohinder Singh Kaypee and election committee in-charge and former CM Captain Amarinder Singh. The issue will be one of the main agenda of our party," said Sekhri.

"Show me one major project that this government brought to the border region during the last one-and-a-half-year rule," said Dimpa, adding that some of the projects, including elevated road, broadening of the Jalandhar-Amritsar GT Road and widening of Amritsar-Attari Road were initiated during their government's rule.

Notably, during the last assembly polls, the Congress was routed in Majha, where it could bag just three assembly seats out of the total 26, while the rest 23 went to the SAD-BJP.

And as the SAD had failed to make an impressive show in Malwa, its stronghold, it was Majha that coasted the combine to a win.

When asked about the discrimination, Sukhbir Badal, who was in the city recently, had said it was a mere political stunt by the Congress leaders. "We gave Rs 100-crore grant for the Holy City, and are completing the multi-crore elevated road project and work is also going on the GT Road. A Central university is being opened in Amritsar, and there are plenty of other projects for power generation, water supply and sewerage lined up," he said.

But the Congress leaders are unimpressed.

"Ever since the Partition, the border areas have been neglected. The biotechnology park coming up at Dera Bassi was originally planned for Majha. The government is also dilly-dallying on the multi-crore integrated border post at Attari," alleged DCC (Rural) head SS Lally Majithia.

Heading: Month after rape, cops say accused had no role - Indian Express
Content:
Prime accused, a Ludhiana resident, still absconding

Mischievous Internet-savvy youngsters eager to befriend girls and chat with them online — Suryansh, prime accused in the 'web extortion' case, was reportedly always on the lookout for such targets. Posing as a girl, the accused would let himself befriended by such youngsters and then strike it rich by blackmailing them after allegedly morphing their photographs and threatening to make them public, the police said.
