The cyber crime cell of the Chandigarh Police cracked the case on Sunday, by arresting a couple — Deepak Singh and Puja Negi — who allegedly worked for Suryansh, a resident of Ludhiana, as his messengers.

According to members of the cell, due to his unique email ID — khoonkar_darinda840@yahoo.com — complainant Navkaran Singh fit the profile of a perfect target for the accused who laid a trap for him by posing as 'Shelly' in the Yahoo chatroom. As their friendship grew after regular chatting, police sources said, Navkaran showed 'Shelly' the pictures of his family. The accused then morphed the pictures, making them obscene, and allegedly started blackmailing him into parting with money and valuables.

"The two never met, but the complainant sent his photographs to the 'girl' through Internet, completely ignorant of the racket," a police officer said.

While Suryaansh is still absconding, a local court sent Deepak and Puja to two days' police custody on Monday. The sources said the accused had an affair with Puja prior to her marriage and that he had blackmailed her the same way into making conversations with Navkaran on the phone, posing as Shelly. The police added that while it was Suryaansh who ran the racket with the help of a fake email ID — shellyjindaal@yahoo.com — he had roped in Puja because he needed a female voice for talking to his target.

According to the police, the accused had managed to rope in Deepak, an employee with a courier firm, too, by blackmailing him.

Navkaran was forced to give away valuables worth over Rs 1 lakh, including a Rado watch, Nokia mobiles and an MP3 player.

"The youngsters should be careful while making friends on the Internet and falling prey to such frauds," a police officer said.

The police managed to contact Suryaansh over phone soon after Puja Negi's arrest on Sunday, but the latter anticipated trouble and threw away his SIM card. The police sources said it being a Sunday they were not able to get the tower locations of the phone number from the cellular service provider immediately. The police are now studying his call details to arrest him.

The police said it was possible that many more youths like Navkaran had fallen prey to the accused.

Heading: Forest dept objects to master plan, Nayagaon development stalled again - Indian Express
Content:
Almost a month after the alleged gangrape of a 17-year-old girl in Panchkula, the Panchkula police have failed to trace two accused in the crime — Jatin and Chhavi. Now, it seems the police have chosen to sing a different tune — that the two 'absconding accused' had no role to play in the crime.

According to Station House Officer of the Sector 16 police station, Inspector Surjit Kumar, "The victim had alleged the involvement of three boys and a girl. Two of the accused, Jitesh and Aman Ahuja, have been arrested. But even after interrogation, there is no evidence to suggest the involvement of more accused in the case."

The FIR specifically names Jatin, Chhavi, Jitesh and Aman Ahuja for allegedly raping the girl. The victim's statements were even recorded before the Magistrate. But Superintendent of Police Sandeep Khirwar has nothing more to say on the issue, except that "the investigation is on".

"With each passing day, the hope that justice will prevail is fading away. The police is taking the episode very lightly. Instead of nabbing the accused, the police have turned around and claimed that we are not cooperating with them. My daughter and I were last called for investigation on September 28; now we just get a call on the landline for queries," said the victim's father.

He added: "My daughter also requested the police officers to get sketches of the accused made but the police seem least interested in solving the case."

The victim said: "A police constable told me that I should feel free to call him home whenever I am alone and feel bored. I got very scared and informed my mother."

Heading: Plastic ban: full marks to most  shopowners and shoppers - Indian Express
Content:
Tussle within the Punjab government has once again stalled the development and expansion of Nayagaon, comprising Karoran, Kansal and Nada villages in the periphery of Chandigarh.

The forest department has objected to the development and expansion plans envisaged by the Department of Local Government in the Draft Master Plan of Nayagaon-2021 released in August.

The local government department has decided to seek Punjab Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal's permission to approach the Supreme Court and the Union Environment and Forests Ministry for seeking clearance to execute the planned development and expansion.

Confirming the development, that is bound to hamper the renewed plans of the state government for Nayagaon, Local Government Principal Secretary D S Bains told Newsline that the forest department had represented the two conditions on which the Nayagaon Nagar Panchayat was constituted on October 18, 2006.

The conditions said "the forest and land preservation area under the Nagar Panchayat shall continue to be so unless it is duly approved or cleared for other uses by the competent authority to do so" and "the constitution of Nagar Panchayat shall not impinge upon any orders of the courts of competent jurisdiction particularly with regard to illegal construction, if any. The department and Nagar Panchayat shall adhere to such orders".

The forest department, Bains said, suggested the local government department to become a party in the pending litigation pertaining to unlock forest and land preservation area before the apex court besides representing the Union government for procuring requisite approval and clearance for such area for other than agriculture and allied purposes.

Bains said the department had received 46 suggestions and claims on the draft master plan. "They mainly pertained to demands of civic infrastructure, changing locations of certain proposed facilities and disputing the forest and land preservation area restriction on the grounds that the restricted areas were already being used for other than agricultural or allied purposes."

All those who wrote to the department were given a personal hearing in Chandigarh on Monday and asked to produce relevant documentary evidence to substantiate their claims.

Bains said the genuine claims and suggestions would be examined within a week before tabling the detailed report before the Punjab Regional Town Planning and Development Board, headed by the Chief Minister.

"Within a month, we will finalise the master plan, following which, as and if allowed by the CM, we will knock at the doors of competent authorities to procure requisite approvals and clearances for undertaking the planned development and expansion of Nayagaon," said Bains.

Heading: Posturing Posters - Indian Express
Content:
The ban imposed in the city on use of polythene carry bags has found residents totally complying with it. More than 10 days have passed since the ban came into effect, and no one has so far been fined for violating it.

While shopowners in the markets of different sectors have already switched to paper and cloth bags, roadside vendors, too, seem to be moving in the right direction.

The ban was imposed on October 2. "We have started using paper bags. Polythenes are completely out. We would rather not have raids at our shops for failing to follow the ban. Customers are being encouraged to get their own bags," said a shopowner in Sector 22.

In many retail stores, customers are being given incentives for bringing carry bags. At other places, the customers have to pay anything between Rs 5 and 10 for one.

Charanjeev Singh, chairman of the Chandigarh Beopar Mandal, said: "Shopkeepers have shown voluntary compliance. A majority has switched over to paper or cloth bags. In the case of smaller shops, however, the price of such bags has to be passed on to the customers, who are paying it without any grudges. We would want that the Administration be a little lenient with us during the festivals."

The only place where the orders have not percolated down properly seems to be the grain market where polythene bags are freely available. Not many seem to be aware that the ban also extends to storing, transporting or carrying them.

Additional Deputy Commissioner I S Sandhu said whoever was found flouting the ban would be taken to court. "The awareness drives by the Administration have led to voluntary compliance by shopowners. On the second day of the ban, teams visited around 486 places. Around 20 per cent of these places, where we found violations, were scrutinised."

Heading: Exhibition van on non-conventional energy inaugurated - Indian Express
Content:
Jerry Pinto and Sheena Sippy's next collaborative is yet another delicious ode to popular culture

The films that are churned out by this industry, decade after tireless decade, are varied in genre and employ millions in its main and ancillary functions. The films themselves, and the industry at large, have been at the very heart of academic discourses, and one should not be surprised today to find a research paper on 'The Treatment of Time and Space in Karan Johar's Films', in the cavernous depths of the Stanford University Library.

An object generating fascination over years has been the Film Poster. Writer Jerry Pinto and lenswoman Sheena Sippy's Bollywood Posters (India Book House) pays tribute to the dying art form that has played sutradhar to generations of film audiences.

Stylishly designed and shot by Sippy, the book juxtaposes de-saturated vibrant images of posters from the early hand-painting days of Do Bigha Zameen and Sahib, Biwi aur Ghulam with the digitally shot, mechanically reproduced monstrosities of Abbas Mustan's Race or Yash Chopra's Dhoom:2. Interspersed with the images are insightful essays by Jerry Pinto, who is also a pop-culture enthusiast. He claims that the industry, which relentlessly spins out around 800 films a year with a majority of flops, works without any economic logic. "It runs on glamour, on its own solipsistic appeal and on its self-generated aura," Pinto writes. He also goes on to claim that Bollywood, though perceived as working outside of genres, has a built-in differentiating logic. And to demonstrate this, he divides the chapters and the posters in the book into six categories—drama, crime, history, mythology, romance and fantasy.

In this, the book stands out in stark contrast to another, very unforgettable, book to have come out this year in the South—The 9 Emotions of Indian Cinema Hoardings by V Geetha, Sirish Rao and famous film poster painter MP Dakshna (Tara Publishers). 9 Emotions categorises the legendary poster art of popular Tamil cinema within the framework of the Navarasas as proposed by the Natyashastra, the second-century text on performance and aesthetics.

All the paintings used in the book were painted exclusively for the book and do not show any film titles. But they do allude to some of the most iconic images from Tamil cinema classics. The book also playfully blends in popular film song lyrics with the images thereby lending meaning and context. 9 Emotions holds a certain academic value in interpreting the grammar of cinematic images that have been integral to political propaganda and posturing in the south. Tamil film plots in the 60s reflected the DMK's steady rise to power-changing stances. This was obviously reflected in the iconographic posters that grew to gigantic proportions, literally giving cinematic images that larger-than-life image.

The emergence of two such books in the Indian publishing arena also reflects the changing views towards popular-culture paraphernalia and their preservation. When Neville Tulli of Osian displayed a poster of Guide beside VS Gaitonde's work a few years ago, he laid the foundation for an interest for investment in film posters as art. And though, the art is nearly dead, recognition of this kind may salvage the dust-gathering relics of yesteryears.

Heading: Gun goes off accidentally in Ambala court complex, no casualties - Indian Express
Content:
A mobile science exhibition van based on the theme Non-conventional energy — developed by the National Science Centre — was inaugurated at Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya (JNV), Sector-25, by Sumita Mishra, director, Renewable Energy Department, Haryana and director, Science and Technology Department, Haryana. S M Khened, director, National Science Centre and C M Sharma, principal, JNV, were present.

The van will be in Chandigarh for two weeks and will be stationed at different schools in Chandigarh and Panchkula to ensure maximum exposure to the students. Subsequently, the mobile science exhibition van will tour the urban and rural areas of Haryana.

"The National Science Centre (NSC), New Delhi, is a constituent unit of the National Council of Science Museum (NCSM), Kolkata, which is an autonomous body under the Ministry of Culture, Government of India," said the spokesperson of the department.

He added, "It is a pioneering institute engaged in the popularisation of science among the people of North India in general and among students in particular."

Sumita Mishra said, "This is a unique concept in which exhibitions on non-conventional energy, displayed in a specially-designed bus, is taken to different schools in rural as well as urban areas," added Mishra.

"Conventional fossil fuels such as coal, oil and gas are likely to deplete with time. The non-conventional sources of energy have therefore become very important in today's world," concluded Mishra.

Heading: Health officials take stock of dengue spread in Mohali - Indian Express
Content:
Panic prevailed in the court complex on Monday morning after bullets shattered the windowpanes of an office adjoining the court of Ambala judicial magistrate. Hearing the gunshots, all those present in the corridor started running for shelter, leading to chaos on the premises.

No one was, however, injured in the incident.

According to information, the official carbine of Sher Singh, a gunman posted with Judicial Magistrate Vijay James, had gone off accidentally. It is learnt that six rounds of bullets had been fired.

Deputy Superintendent of Police (Headquarters) Bhupinder Singh and his team reached the court to assess the situation. He said the gunman had been dispossessed of the carbine and placed under suspension. Further action would be taken against the cop for negligence in performing his duty, he added.

Heading: SAD-BJP combine fails to conquer Kharar MC - Indian Express
Content:
Principal Secretary to the Department of Health and Family Welfare, Punjab, Vijay Kain expressed concern over the dengue situation in Mohali on Monday.

At least 120 dengue cases have tested positive from different parts of Mohali district during this season, said Kain adding that negligence in the awareness, detection, prevention and treatment had led to the spread of the disease.

Scrapping the civic body's claim of fogging the areas after every 11 days, Kain said the dengue mosquito had a life cycle of seven days. "Fogging should be repeated every week to ensure complete eradication of the mosquito. Until and unless, fogging is done inside houses and shops, external fogging is useless."

Kain directed that the Senior Medical Officers (SMOs) should identify the breeding grounds of mosquito while in rural areas, this task was entrusted to the Block Development and Panchayat Officers. Mohali Civil Surgeon Dr Avtar Singh said 15 teams of the Health department had surveyed 12,090 houses in the district.

"Almost 45 per cent of the total dengue cases were detected from Phase 3 in Mohali. Mohali, Kharar and Dera Bassi Civil Hospitals are offering free testing and treatment of dengue," he said.

Fresh case in Ambala

Ambala: A fresh case of dengue was reported from the city on Monday. The disease has already claimed one life last week. Nirmala (45), wife of daily wager Mohinder, was referred to the PGI Chandigarh by the Civil Hospital as she was suffering from high fever for a few days. Mohinder said that doctors at PGI discharged her after a few days of treatment. On reaching Ambala, she started vomiting blood and was again rushed to the PGI, where hospital authorities allegedly refused to admit her.

Heading: Now, farm advisory on cellphones - Indian Express
Content:
Chandigarh Sports Department will organise the inaugural Administrator's Challenge Cup Hockey Tournament for boys from October 16 to 22 at Sector 42 Hockey Stadium.

According to Inderjit Singh Sandhu, Sports Director, the matches would be played on league-cum-knockout basis under the rules and regulations of the Indian Hockey Confederation.

"The tournament will also serve as a spotting meet for the benefit of the Chandigarh Hockey Academy being run by the Chandigarh Administration. If any outstanding player is noticed, he may be included in the CF Academy, if any vacancy exists,"said Sandhu while addressing a press conference at Sector 42 Sports Complex.

This tournament is being held after the Sports department successfully conducted the recently concluded Administrator's Cup All-India Football Tournament. The winner will walk away with a cash prize of Rs 50,000 and the runner-up will get Rs 25,000.

The following teams have been divided into different pools:

Pool A: Surjit Academy Jalandhar, Hockey Academy Gurgaon, Sukhchain Hockey Academy Faridkot, Maharaja Ranjit Singh Hockey Academy Amritsar.

Pool B: Chandigarh Hockey Academy, Hyderbad Hockey Academy, Cheema Hockey Academy Batala, Kurukshetra SAI Academy.

Pool C: PNB Hockey Academy Delhi, Chandigarh Sports Deptt Coaching Centre, Punjab and Sind Bank Academy Jalandhar, Mehta Gurukul Hockey Academy Doraha.

Pool D: Rail Coach Factory Kurukshetra, Hockey Academy Lucknow and Amritsar XI.

Heading: Minor girl raped for months - Indian Express
Content:
Updates on crop prices, weather, import, export information will be sent through SMS

Updates on crop prices, weather and an advisory on farming will on your fingertips, literally.

In April, the Punjab Mandi Board had signed a MoU with Reuters for Reuters Market Light (RML) project, which would be formally launched by Punjab Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal on October 21. With this, all farming-related information will be available through SMS alerts.

The service has already become a hit. After its soft launch in Punjab in September-mid, 2,600 farmers have subscribed to it. "The RML project is an information service for farmers that will have a positive impact on their livelihood. We are covering nine crops, including wheat, paddy, maize, cotton, potato, kinnow and a few vegetables, in about 70 out of 145 mandis of the state. We are using mobile phones as a medium of disseminating information in Punjabi language using Roman and Devanagari scripts since majority of the handsets do not support Gurmukhi," said a company officer.

He said, "The farmer can chose from three packages of three months (Rs 260), six months (Rs 500) and a year (Rs 850)."

The service provides price updates of different crops, particularly during the harvest time, weather updates and crop advisory duly validated by agriculture experts from Punjab Agricultural University (PAU) or other reputed institutes like Indian Council for Agricultural Research (ICAR). Farmers are being given information regarding prices of two crops of their choice prevailing in three mandis near their village or any other place of their choice.

"Our focus is on high value crops, like fruits and vegetables," said the

officer.

The weather updates will include maximum and minimum temperatures, humidity, chances of precipitation and forecast for the next 24 hours at the tehsil level. Besides, RML will also inform farmers about the impact of import and export of a particular crop on local markets.

"We launched our services in Maharashtra on October 1 last year and have about 50,000 farmers as subscribers. We have a tie-up with the Maharashtra State Agriculture Marketing Board (MSAMB)," said the official.

Talking to The Indian Express, SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal said, "This service will link Punjab farmers with national and international markets. Like in the West, the Punjab farmers can also plan their crops now."

Heading: Woman alleges she was stripped, paraded by sarpanch - Indian Express
Content: The police on Tuesday registered a case of abduction and rape against nine persons on the complaint of a minor girl of local Sunder Nagar. In her complaint to the police, the victim alleged that Kaka and Hari told her that her brother had met with an accident and was admitted to a hospital in Jalandhar and abducted her in the first week of July. The accused took her to an office premises in Lame village, near Jalandhar, and raped her repeatedly for a week. From there, she was taken to the house of one Muskan and raped by Gola and Vicky. The complainant said she was then taken to a religious place in HP and the accused raped her for months. Then, they brought her to Jalandhar, from where she escaped.

Heading: Dacoits’ gang  busted; five arrested - Indian Express
Content:
Sarpanch says she was caught in a compromising position with a painter

A 30-something woman of Atta village, near Goraya, whose husband lives in Dubai alleged that some of her kin and the sarpanch, who is also one of her relatives, stripped naked her and forced her to parade in front of her family members, including her teenage son, on the night of October 7.

She alleged that they also shot her video. However, the sarpanch and villagers claimed that the woman was caught in a compromising position with another man and now this was her cover-up act. The woman, who is living here along with her mother-in-law and two children, has also lodged a complaint with the Phillaur DSP.

She alleged that the sarpanch used to make advances at her, but she always snubbed him, and he wanted to take revenge. She said sarpanch Lakhbir Kumar, along with Kamaljit and Dara, entered her house and bashed her up and forced her and Surjit Kumar, a painter who had come to paint her house, to parade naked.

Lakhbir, however, said, "I went to her house along with other villagers, who had complained that the woman was bringing a bad name to the village. Why had she called the painter to her house at 10 pm?" He said the allegations of making her video were baseless.

Phillaur DSP Rajinder Singh Sohal said he had marked an inquiry and they were yet to recover the video film.

Heading: A bitter-sweet Diwali as sweets become dearer - Indian Express
Content:
After the draw at Bangalore, all eyes will be on the 22 yard pitch at the PCA Stadium here, venue of the second Test of the India and Australia series. And going by the chief curator Daljit Singh there is bound to be a smile on Ricky Ponting's face: Seamers and not spinners will have a bigger role.

"This has been an unusual season and we have seen heavy rains in this part of the country. Honestly the pitch and ground preparations have been hampered," Daljit admits, "We are trying our best to have a hard and a dry wicket with consistent bounce." As ever, especially with winters around the corner, the faster bowlers will find movement both on and off the wicket. "We can see the data. The morning sessions are always loaded in favour of seamers while the pitch eases out as the game goes on. We have a few days left and hope the sun shines," Daljit said.

"I think bowlers can exploit the bounce at this wicket resulting in batsmen edging deliveries. Also, there would be no reverse-swing here as we don't have a rough outfield," he added.

The pitch would also keep the Indians engrossed in a debate over the final XI. Will India go in with the two spinner and two pacers theory or drop a spinner for the third pacer? Even though Anil Kumble has picked up two Man of the Match awards, his shoulder injury has hampered his bowling of late. "I feel he enjoys the bounce here and if he is fit he would love to bowl here," Daljit felt.

The Stadium has seen a few drawn games but Daljit is optimistic this time of a result. "The rains have to stay away," he concluded.

Heading: ‘We must pledge to stand united against evil forces in country’ - Indian Express
Content:
The rise in milk prices —recorded twice this year, by Re 1 per litre each time — has resulted in a spurt in the prices of sweets this festive season.

While the city sweetshops are gearing up for making the most of this festive season, the hike in prices of sweets has come as a big letdown for consumers.

The much-preferred Kaju Katli has witnessed a rise in price by Rs 30 per kg as compared to last year. Currently priced between Rs 280 and 300 per kg, a year ago the prices were in the range of Rs 240 to Rs 270 per kilogram.

A simple milk barfi will now be priced between Rs 180 and 200 per kg, around Rs 10 more as compared to the last season.

"Not only milk, the prices of desi ghee have also increased this year. We were forced to raise the prices of sweets by 15 to 20 per cent," said Neeraj Bajaj of Sindhi Sweets in Sector 17.

At Gopal Sweets in Sector 8, coconut barfi is priced at Rs 180 per kg while gulabjamun is valued at Rs 8 a piece. Kalakand has seen a hike of Rs 10 per kg over the previous year and is currently priced at Rs 180 per kg.

"With time, the prices were bound to increase. Almost all the commodities made in desi ghee have witnessed a rise of more than 10 per cent," said Rishav Sharma of Gopals-8.

With Karva Chauth approaching, the price of feniyan has also spiralled by about Rs 30 over the previous year and will now be available between Rs 220 and Rs 250 per kg.

Heading: Schools give norms on school-leaving papers a miss - Indian Express
Content:
The recent spate of terrorist attacks has dampened the festive spirit this year. The deserted shops and lack of enthusiasm bear testimony to the fact that the anti-social elements have succeeded in their design to create fear in the mind of the common man.

Even the youth are keeping aloof of crowded hotspots. Many of my friends, who never missed the latest flick in the multiplex earlier, now keep procrastinating the outing fearing the worst.

People prefer sitting inside their houses rather than venturing out and making merry. Why? They do not want to be a casualty in a bomb blast.

The destroyers of peace want this only: the agenda is to instil fear in the hearts of Indians. Not many people were upbeat about Dussehra — they valued their lives more than the holiday fun. The city is on a red-alert and it will not be surprising if terrorism raises its ugly head once again in the city.

Rather than blaming an 'external hand' for disrupting peace in the country, we must introspect. The communal riots in Orissa, in which thousands of Christians were butchered mercilessly, are a national shame.

If we continue to fight over such petty issues, people with vested interests will definitely try to attack us. Once we show that we are vulnerable, we become susceptible to harm.

During such distressing times, we need to maintain peace and calm. Panic will only worsen the situation and those with vested interests will try to cash on this situation of unrest. We must pledge to stand united against the forces of evil.

Heading: EWS rule violation: notices to 40 schools - Indian Express
Content:
Schools in the city are not following the guidelines issued by the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) while issuing school-leaving as well as character certificates.

In a circular, dated March 10, 2008, the CBSE had made it mandatory for all affiliated schools to mention the status of the student in terms of his/her behaviour pattern in the school-leaving and character certificates.

These certificates, however, continue to have the age-old statement of the "child bears a good moral conduct".

The school authorities, however, express ignorance about the orders.

"A character certificate is an official document, which the student has to submit at different institutions where he seeks admission. If the child's behaviour is not up to the mark and it is mentioned in the certificate, it can pose problems for him in the long run. It may also lead to biased behaviour and he may be denied admission," says Dr Rakesh Sachdeva, principal, DAV Model School, Sector 15.

The CBSE had taken the decision keeping in view of the findings of the Raghavan Committee, which had instructed schools to implement an effective programme of counselling for students.

A detailed assessment of the child's behaviour was a step in this regard.

"We are not aware that is has been made mandatory to write the details of the student's behaviour in the character certificate. Mentioning a negative remark in the certificates can harm the child's future," says the principal of a government school.

The Board has also issued an assessment booklet for the child that is filled by teachers but does not form part of the character certificate.

"We have the assessment performa which is duly completed after observing the child during the academic year. Since it is sufficient and also because we do not want to discourage a child, we refrain from making any remark against him in the school leaving document," explains Sanjay Sardana of Manav Mangal Smart School.

Heading: Citibank to cough up damages for adopting unfair trade practices - Indian Express
Content:
Taking note of the news report that appeared in Chandigarh Newsline on Monday, highlighting that some schools were violating the norm of admitting 15 per cent students from the Economically Weaker Sections (EWS), the Education Department has sent notices to all the erring schools.

Talking to Newsline, Samwartak Singh, Director Public Instructions (Schools), said the issue needs to be addressed seriously.

"We have issued notices to over 40 schools that have not admitted the minimum 15 per cent students from the economically weaker sections, asking them to explain the reason behind the violation. This is a grave lapse on part of such schools," he said.

Some of the schools that have not admitted students from poor families claim that they teach children in their adopted colonies.

"This is not the right way. It is against the entire spirit of the plan. We will not take this plea anymore. As per the EWS scheme, poor students should be studying in the school along with other students," Singh maintained.

Apart from demanding an explanation from these schools, the Education Department has also decided to take action against those who fail to follow the instructions even after the notice.

"To ensure that the rule is followed properly, we have decided that a team from the Department will form part of the admission committees of these schools from next year onwards. If these institutions deny admission to any student, strict action will be taken against them," said Singh.

On October 13, Newsline had reported that according to the data procured from the Education Department, of the 57 schools that were assessed for the Economically Weaker Sections norm as on June 2008, only eight schools had admitted the required 15 per cent of their total strength from the Economically Weaker Sections category.

Strawberry Fields, Moti Ram Arya, Bhavan Vidyalya, Ryan International, DAV Public School, Sector 8, are among the gross violators, with less than 5 per cent students from the Economically Weaker Sections category.

Heading: DPI(S) given additional charge of Tourism director - Indian Express
Content:
The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum has directed the Citibank to pay Rs 25,000 as compensation for adopting unfair trade practices.

The bank has also been directed to overhaul the account of the complainant and adjust any amount, deposited in excess of the installment amount, towards the next installment.

The complainant, Pradeep Goswami, availed a loan of Rs 4.5 lakh from Citibank at the rate of 14 per cent per annum against his credit card repayable in 48 equated monthly installments (EMI) of Rs 12,297.

It was averred that the complainant was repaying the loan amount regularly by drafts and cheques in advance and every time the amount used to exceed the EMI of Rs 12,297.

It was also averred that a letter dated January 23, 2008, was sent to the complainant by the bank thereby threatening that his missed payment details were to be shared with the credit bureau as he (complainant) had missed making the EMI payment for January 2008.

But Goswami said he had already deposited a draft of Rs 15,000 on January 2.

The bank also imposed late-payment charges, service tax and interest on account of dishonoring the said draft.

In its reply, the Citibank denied that the complainant had been depositing amount in excess of the EMI. Rather, the bank said he had deposited less than the required EMI for the months of November 2006, May 2007, August 2007 and November 2007. For July 2007, no amount was deposited as EMI.

The bank also denied that the complainant was sent a threatening letter as alleged.

Also, the bank said the draft of Rs 15,000 (for January) of Union Bank of India was incapable of being released as the same was mutilated.

The forum found that during from October to December 2006, the complainant was to deposit Rs 36,891 but had deposited much in excess (Rs 65,000).

Thereafter, from January 2007 to December 2007, he was to deposit Rs 1, 47, 564 but the total amount deposited during this period was Rs 1,26,000.

The forum observed: "The bank has not been able to cite any terms of the agreement under which they were permitted to adjust the excess amount towards the interest instead of adjusting it towards the principal amount or towards the next installment as and when it fell due."

"This act of the bank — adjusting the amount towards interest instead of adjusting it towards the principle amount or installment— amounts to grave deficiency in service," ruled the forum.

The bank has also been directed to pay Rs 5,500 as costs of litigation.

Heading: Age no factor as Kaushik defeats Kharbanda to reach last eight - Indian Express
Content: After Haryana Civil Services officer Vivek Atray was relieved from the UT Administration on Monday, Director Public Instructions (Schools) Samwartak Singh has been given the additional charge of Director (Tourism). The additional charge of overseeing the Milk Village project was assigned to UT Special Secretary Finance Raji P Shrivastava. R S Verma, Additional Director (Administration), Government Medical College of Health, Sector 32, Chandigarh, has also been given the additional charge of Director Public Relations and Cultural Affairs. UT Joint Secretary Finance Pirthi Chand has been assigned additional charge of Joint Secretary (Technical Education) and Joint Secretary (Housing). The charge of Labour Commissioner has been assigned to Deputy Commissioner R K Rao while Sub-Divisional Magistrate Prerna Puri will hold the charge of Joint Director (Food and Supplies).

Heading: Squash shows the way - Indian Express
Content:
Waiting to turn thirty within a couple of months after the best years of his career were marred by recurring injuries, hanging up his competitive shoes would have been the most obvious choice for badminton player Rudra Kaushik. The worst phase came right after his three-month training under former world champion Ichuk Sugiarto in Indonesia in 2000, during which he had an accident, injuring his wrist and knees. Following that, he needed surgery twice on his knee.

On Monday, though, he pulled off the biggest upset of the Delhi state ranking badminton tournament at the Punjabi Bagh Club, dumping fourth seed Himanshu Kharbanda 24-21, 21-19, 22-20 in the pre-quarters.

After losing the one-sided first game, Kaushik was again looking down the barrel at 14-19 down in the second. But then, a couple of points off unforced errors and more aggressive play gave him seven consecutive points. None of the strategies he employed, however, worked in the decider as Kharbanda, trailing 7-14 at a point, rushed to 19-20, only to give away the match off an unforced error. While those around kept calling it the biggest upset of the tournament so far, Kaushik wasn't fussy about it at all. According to him, it only shows the falling standards of the game in the Capital. "Calling it an upset would be wrong as on head to head I'm leading 2-1. I lost to Himanshu (Kharbanda) in last year's JD Tytler final and in 2006 I had beaten him in the Pramod Mahajan quarters. It was a win alright but it only shows the deteriorating quality of Delhi badminton. You have 37-year old Srikant Bakshi as the top-ranked player who came back early this year after a big lay-off," the 2001 Chandigarh state champion said, adding, "The problem with youngsters is they are too quick to get on with things, ending up with too many unforced errors. In a 21-point match, experienced players play a waiting game rather than going for it straightway."

Three out of the eight quarter-finalists at the tournament are 32-year-old Devender Dhillon, Vijay Sharma(38) and Srikant Bakshi (37).

Heading: Yuki returns to top five - Indian Express
Content:
A recent mention of squash in Forbes magazine as the healthiest of all sports would have been the last idea that inspired the 500-odd participation in the 15th DDA Squash Open tournament at the Siri Fort Sports Complex. Foreign participation provided added spice with Malaysia no. 4 Mohammad Asyraf bagging the men's title after Egyptian Tariq bowed out in the semi-finals. The u-12s and u-13s also made up the numbers.

"I've seen my father playing squash every day for two-three hours. I started practising with him and thus the interest grew," says nine-year old Pavan Jaini.

Father Vijay Jaini, the current over-50 national champion, feels the popularity levels of the game must be attributed to its accessibility to the common man today, unlike the way it was during his time (the mid-seventies and early eighties) and how that has changed the perception of the game.

Elite sport no more

"It used to be an elite game during our time, played only in the big clubs or government organisations. As a result, the public had virtually no access to the courts. Now DDA has come up with the infrastructure that is available to everybody," says Saini.

Bharatinder Singh, a doctor and the convenor of health services, Commonwealth Games 2010 stresses that the health enhancement factor associated with the sport has given it a new face.

"Being played indoors, you can pick up a racquet and start banging the ball anytime. And in half-an-hour you would end up burning more calories than an hour-long tennis match or 90-minitues of football. It is the best for health in the shortest available time, thus suiting modern-day lifestyle perfectly," says Singh.

Not spectator friendly

A former athlete and a regular squash player now, Singh defines the sport as 'twist, turn and back' in physiological terms and thinks the only hindrance to further popularity is viewership. "It's not the game fit for a live telecast. Being so fast, the cameras often fail to track the movement of the ball," he adds.

Men's champion Mohammad Asyraf cannot recall the number of times he has been to India or lost to Saurav Ghosal as a kid, but his experience has only bettered over the years.

"I have lost to Ritwik (Bhattacharya) and Saurav Ghosal in the junior categories. However, I haven't played them for a long time now. During my initial visits to India, I found the courts a bit slippery, but now they are world class, especially here and in Chennai. The more important thing is the money here in India. It is far more than Malaysia at this level. That's why I still keep coming here," says Asyraf.

Heading: BJP to announce candidates for Delhi polls before Diwali - Indian Express
Content:
Less than 12 hours after returning home to Delhi, tennis player Yuki Bhambri was on the way to the airport again.

One would think that winning a Grade A tournament a couple of days ago merits a bit of rest as a reward, but not when the Commonwealth Youth Games awaits its second seed in the tennis event.

Yuki won last week's Osaka Mayor's Cup in Japan, and with it moved to number four on the ITF junior circuit charts, two weeks after leading the Indian Junior Davis Cup team to its best finish at the world finals in Mexico, and the 16-year-old's game appears to be back on track.

"It is very hectic right now, but I'm playing well, so it's good for me to get a lot of tennis," he says.

"The clay and grass was just a bad patch, it was the first time I was playing on grass, so I was bound to find it tough. Hopefully as the hard court season continues, I will keep improving."

The US Open, too, ended in a disappointing second-round exit for the youngster, but the weeks put in at Nick Bolletieri's academy in Florida clearly brought about a world of change.

A fourth-place finish in Mexico at the Junior Davis Cup, and now the Osaka Mayor's Cup singles title — which earned him a whopping 250 circuit points — and the going looks good again. Grade A tournaments on the ITF junior circuit are just a notch below the Junior Slams, and consequently offer the most points after the Slams.

"The junior Davis Cup performance was something I never expected. It was going to be very tough because there were so many good teams there, but we got a few crucial doubles results to go our way, and that helped," he says, leaving out the fact that it was his singles victories that played a much more vital role.

"There were a lot of high quality players in Japan last week as well, it was Grade A after all. The Europeans are always good, and even the Japanese were a threat, since it was their home territory. The amount of local support was unbelievable when I beat Hiroki Moriya in the final, there had to be at least six to seven thousand people," says Yuki.

"This time at Bolletieri I changed my serve and worked on being more aggressive, coming to the net a lot, and in the past few weeks, I've had a chance to try it all out in the tournaments. It's always a great experience to train there, because I get to train with so many good players."

After the Youth Games, Yuki will be playing a Grade B1 tournament in Indonesia, followed by another training trip to Florida.

Heading: Missing for 3 days, manager of Noida IT firm found dead - Indian Express
Content:
The BJP is in the process of finalising the names of its candidates for the coming Delhi Assembly elections and is likely to announce the list of nominees within ten days.

"The formal process for finalising the list will start in a couple of days and we expect to announce it within a week to ten days. We will have the list before Diwali," BJP Delhi president Harsh Vardhan said.

The polling for the 70-member Delhi Assembly will be held on November 29 while the counting of votes will be on December 8.

Harsh Vardhan said the days of the Congress-led Delhi government are "numbered" and the saffron party will emerge victorious.

"We are happy that the dates are announced. The Sheila Dikshit government is on ventilator. It is gasping for oxygen.

We will end the misrule of Congress for the past ten years," he said.

The BJP has already announced that senior BJP leader and South Delhi MP V K Malhotra will be its Chief Ministerial candidate.

Heading: ‘Minority’ Stephen’s has right to select own head, says apex court - Indian Express
Content:
An associate manager with Portech India Infoservices, a call centre in Noida's Sector 63, was found dead near Shipra Suncity in Indirapuram, Ghaziabad, on Monday morning.

The deceased, Ashwani Sharma, 43, went missing on Friday, the police said today. The body was found behind the CISF camp in the ridge area in the Ghaziabad sururb.

Ghaziabad Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) L Ravi Kumar said the postmortem report has confirmed that Sharma died of strangulation.

According to the police, Sharma stayed in Noida while his family is based in Patiala.

Superintendent of Police (City) Vijay Bhushan said, "We are interrogating the friends he used to stay with." Bhushan, though, said the police have ruled out robbery as the murder motive: "His watch, rings and wallet were intact when the body was recovered."

Sharma stayed at GAIL Apartments in Sector-62, Noida, with three others.

Bhushan said, "Sharma went to Shipra mall on Friday evening. He stayed there for 40 minutes and left around 8.30 pm. The CCTV footage showed him entering and leaving the mall."

Sharma's wife Tripta Rupal told Newsline over telephone from Patiala that she cannot imagine her husband had any enemies. "He was a polite man and only his roommates can offer clues as to what might have happened," she said.

Sharma's family, meanwhile, alleged that Ghaziabad police failed to take prompt action in the case. Vikas Sharma, the victim's brother-in-law, claims he approached Indirapuram police to lodge a missing complaint on Friday itself, but the police refused to take down a complaint.

Indirapuram Station House Officer Ashutosh Kumar had told Newsline on Friday that Sharma's relatives came to inquire about his whereabouts that day, not to file a missing person's report.

But on Monday, the SHO said the missing report was filed on Friday itself.

"As Sharma lived in Sector-62 Noida, we were in touch with the Noida police," SHO Kumar said, "but they refused to take any responsibility. As we had CCTV footage showing him going out of the mall, we thought he must have gone to Patiala to meet his family."

Heading: Imam Bukhari turned away by police from Jamia Nagar - Indian Express
Content:
Upholding the power of St Stephen's College to appoint its own principal, the Supreme Court on Monday dismissed a petition filed by Delhi University and ruled that minority educational institutions have a constitutional right to appoint heads of their institutions.

The government cannot encroach upon this right of an institution, the apex court observed while dismissing Delhi University's appeal challenging the High Court's recent order that allowed Stephen's to "select a qualified person as its principal".

In a reprieve for the college locked in a legal battle over the process of selection of its principal, the Supreme Court bench of Justices R V Raveendran and J M Panchal today approved its status as a "minority institution".

"It's a valuable right guaranteed under Article 30, otherwise you are encroaching into it," the Bench warned as senior advocate P P Rao pressed hard, challenging the High Court's decision.

Rao submitted that the university had the right to frame regulations for prescribing standards of education and uniformity "in national interest". But the argument did not convince the apex court. The Bench observed, "You show us one minority college not maintaining the (educational) standards. Otherwise we will be making minority institutions only a farce."

The apex court upheld the High Court's ruling that the right of a minority educational institution to appoint its head cannot be taken away by any rule, regulation or any enactment made by state even if the institute is receiving 100 per cent government aid. Delhi University had appealed against the High Court order on the ground that Article 30, which grants minorities the right to establish and administer their own institutions, was "not an absolute right".

On August 21, the High Court quashed Clause 7 (2) of the Delhi University's Ordinance XVIII, which gave the varsity the power to appoint principals of all colleges under its jurisdiction. Allowing the college's petition, the Division Bench of Chief Justice A P Shah and Justice S Muralidhar made it clear that the pertinent clause would not be applicable for Stephen's, which is a minority institution.

Heading: Now, a triple-ton from city lad - Indian Express
Content:
The Jamia Nagar police on Monday afternoon stopped the Shahi Imam of Jama Masjid from entering the area telling him his presence could create a 'law and order' situation.

Imam Bukhari was on his way to L-18 — the site of last month's encounter — after locals called him to say they had spotted certain unidentified men going inside the flat on Monday morning. Batla House residents described their activities as 'suspicious'.

However, officers of the Jamia police, the Special Cell as well as the Crime Branch denied their men had been sent to the flat in the morning for inspection.

The Imam's car was stopped by police near the Holy Family Hospital around 2.30 pm. Officers refused to give way and also had arguments with members of the recently-formed Jamia Coordination Committee.

Imam Bukhari said: "The police then allowed my nephew Tariq Bukhari and a member of the coordination committee Irfanullah Khan to go inside the house." They could not find anything suspicious, police sources said.

Local police officers on Monday also included local residents in a four-member committee formed to accompany the police when it conducted investigations inside house L-18.

However, police sources said members of this team — Irfanullah Khan, Asif Mohammed Khan, Javed Alam and Wasim Gazi — would not be allowed inside if officers of the Special Cell or the Crime Branch were on an inspection.

Heading: Arrest ‘foster parents’ of love child: court to cops - Indian Express
Content:
The city's school cricketers are setting records with such regularity this season that even the professionals might be a little stumped. On Monday, as the Test match elsewhere headed towards a draw, Ankit Dabas of Vidhya Jain School hit the Sardar Patel Vidyalaya grounds looking only to survive at the crease. Soon, he was bludgeoning opposition to death.

By end of the innings, the 15-year old had created history: scoring a triple century in 50-overs cricket, and also sharing a record 495-run partnership with Gaurav Kocchar. The total? 614 for 4 in 50 overs. Another record? Ankit's side registered the maximum margin of victory, ever, defeating Amity International School by 544 runs in an inter-school tie.

"I took my time to get my eye in. Initially I and Gaurav decided to just hang in there," Ankit said after the match, "but when both of us reached our hundreds, we just decided to have our own little competition of who will score faster and reach a double-hundred."

The "own little competition" got over with Ankit scoring 303, hitting 24 sixes and 27 boundaries to eclipse Modern School student Milind Gautam's recent record of 241 set in the same tournament (Newsline, October 4).

Ankit's partner Gaurav says they never realised it was record: "We knew it was getting bigger and bigger. When I got out, I was very disappointed because I knew I missed out on a bigger knock but my teammates and the organisers said it was a record partnership!"

Gaurav fell on 203 but Ankit went on: "I reached my hundred in the 21st over, the double-hundred in the 29th, and my triple hundred came in the 42nd over. I was desperate to break Milind's record after I reached my 200 — he is a good friend, we live in the same locality and I wanted to go one-up on him."

"I got out with eight overs left," he said, with a twinge of regret. Four-hundred, though, was a long shot, he admitted.

But then, the way Delhi lads are going, who knows...

Heading: After cops flop, MP issues reward: find my dog, take home Rs 10k - Indian Express
Content:
A city court on Monday issued non-bailable warrants against a couple who refused to hand over custody of a one-year-old boy to his biological mother, who had given them the love child last September to escape "social stigma".

The court also directed police to trace the child within 48 hours and produce him in court on Wednesday.

The order came after Delhi Police failed to produce the child in court despite a search warrant issued earlier in the day. Asked to produce the baby in court by 3.30 pm, the police submitted that they could not trace the infant as his current custodians were not at their house, in West Delhi's Rohini.

"The investigating officer (IO) was directed to execute the search warrant by 3.30 pm but he has failed to do so," Metropolitan Magistrate Savitri said. The child, the court noted, should now be produced in court on October 15 and "the IO be replaced, if needed."

After the infant's biological parents handed over the child to an acquaintance, the two got married and sought back the boy's custody. The parents claimed the child had been given away on "temporary basis", for a period of "four months". The current custodians, however, claimed in court that the child had been given to them in adoption.

Last week, the court had observed that rights of natural parents were prima facie superior and had ordered the current custodians to hand over the infant. The court also noted that since no valid adoption deed was executed between the two couples, no legal rights could shelter the custody of the caretaker parents.

Heading: We Are Like This Only - Indian Express
Content:
A Member of Parliament has announced a reward of Rs 10,000 for anyone reuniting him and his family with their missing dog. Devwrat Singh, a Congress MP from Rajanandgaon (Chhattisgarh), first lodged a complaint with Delhi Police about a fortnight ago stating that the family pet, named Bullet, had gone missing. The police, however, failed to get any clues about the dog's whereabouts; Singh then announced a reward of Rs 10,000.

Singh has even distributed and got pasted posters across the Capital, giving information about his missing dog and soliciting help. The dog went missing from his apartment in North Avenue.

Posters released by Singh says the dog is "about two-and-a-half years old and is white in colour".

Singh said the dog is a St Bernard bought from Uzbekistan: "We bought him for about Rs 35,000."

His wife Padma Singh said all family members are close to the dog — "we love it as much as we love our children." She said the family was in Jaipur on the night the dog went missing. "There were two domestic helps in the house at the time," Padma Singh said, "and one of them told us that he had taken Bullet and another dog (the family owns) for a stroll at about 8 pm.

"After that, he left for some work leaving the dogs at home."

This was the last anyone saw the dog, she said; it apparently escaped when another household help was "working in the kitchen".

Singh said the police told the family about involvement of some miscreants who lure these dogs for breeding as they aren't easily available in India. "One officer told me that some people might be involved in a racket that takes away imported dogs as they have seen such cases earlier as well," he said.

The police, meanwhile, said that a missing complaint has been lodged. "We are doing our best to trace the dog," a senior officer said.

Padma Singh said they also spoke to a few local vendors who gave them some names of persons who could be behind luring the dogs away — either to sell them or to breed them with other dogs.

Police officers said they are questioning some people in connection with the incident; they have not been able to get any specific clues about Bullet.

Heading: Man, Ain’t it Smart? - Indian Express
Content:
Isn't a possible recession George W Bush's problem? Should debut designers in Delhi be worrying about sliding rupee and market meltdown? But look keenly at the collections of some of the 18 first-time designers at the Wills Lifestyle India Fashion Week Spring-Summer 09 that began on Wednesday, and you will find recession in the ruffles. With minimalist designs characteristic of post-war Europe and austerity associated with post-modern architecture inspiring them, a tempered palette and severe silhouettes will be out on the runway. And even when a couple of them are going retro, they are slipping into the dainty dresses of early Sixties that would look chic at a derby.

Designer duo Gaurav Jagtiani and Ritika Gupta, both 24 and the youngest on the block, have created "Definite Space" revolving around the postmodern design movement in which ornamentation is shunned. And the source of inspiration is British-Iraqi architect Zaha Hadid, who stresses on deconstructive designs. On the runway will be dresses in austere silhouettes and tempered colours.

The duo have mixed whites with ivory and icy mint. "There are no prints, no embellishments, no sequins, no Swarovski-studded tunics. There will be no external influence; it is all about playing with the concept of design," says Jagtiani.

IIM graduate Anupama Dayal has since moved to the ramps, but the 34-year-old is as much bothered about market as she is about fashion. "With the slowing down of the economy, business is changing and people are increasingly designing resort dresses for the upcoming season," says Dayal, who has been on the circuit for five years, with four Paris fairs and a Lakme Fashion Week under her designer belt.

She has cranked out "The Gallerina", inspired by Swedish, post-war minimalism and rustic Bengal life. The square-cut dresses in intense colours and "European sophistication" are embellished with Indian motifs, with Jamini Roy's classic, big, dark eyes and paisley prints blending impeccably on a tunic.

"I have referenced Scandinavian textile companies such as Nordiska Kompaniet and the Stromma," says Dayal, whose palette ranges from faded gold to amethyst.

Even the '60s look borders on girlish prettiness, with practical trousers and chic dresses in muted colours sans indulgence. Rohit Mittal, 28, with his Audrey Hepburn-inspired collection "My Fair Lady" has a potpourri of creamy dresses paired with a dainty parasol. "The colours are mostly whites," says Mittal. While a white crepe skirt is brightened by a green, ruffled hemline, an old-fashioned, full-sleeve blouse is paired with a white sari set off by scarlet flowers and an English hat. The Delhi-based designer, says, "It's a light, summery collection meant for Sunday brunches, polo afternoons and resort wear."

Practicality bodes well for 29-year-old Ashima Singh as well. Her "Sonnets", a daywear collection for 20-somethings, includes such unembellished, non-OTT dresses as lime-green frock and a pink frilly top paired with purple trousers that gather at the knees. "The wardrobe is practical and could be easily worn as evening wear as well," says Singh, who has had a successful stint at a London fashion fair this year.

And with two fashion weeks ready to run neck-and-neck, will these sequin-less ensembles stand out? The newcomers are ready to give it a go and earn enough reputation and rupees in these Sensex-wracked times.

Heading: Animal Kingdom - Indian Express
Content:
After the success of his solo Lambi Judaai, Pakistani singer Kamran Ahmed is optimistic about his first album, Judaai, releasing soon

Song writer, composer and singer Kamran Ahmed never imagined that Lambi Judaai of the Emraan Hashmi starrer Jannat that he actually wrote for his parents would turn out to become one of the most downloaded love tracks of all time. "My parents live in Pakistan. And I have been staying away from them in Dubai, since 2001, meeting only occasionally. This song brought back memories of time spent with them. I am glad people understood how I felt," says Ahmed, 26. Fresh from the success of his first single, Pakistani artiste Ahmed, is performing in India for the first time at Elevate, Noida. Ahmed is thankful to Bollywood for putting him in the spotlight. "It is an honour that Bhatt saab (Mukesh Bhatt) selected my song as one of the tracks for his movie. It has really turned the tide in my favour and I am getting offers from music directors. Even though the song did fairly well in Canada, USA and the UK, nothing compared to the success I received from Bollywood. Appealing to an Indian audience is always much easier," reasons this self taught singer.

His song however, was slightly tweaked to suit the movie, explains Ahmed. "The initial composition did not have a female voice. But in the movie a female voice adds a dynamic undertone with the aalaps. Even the arrangement of the lyrics and timing of the various instruments was slightly customized. Bhatt saab told me, 'one should hear the song and get the feeling of being lonely in a crowd'." Other singers from Pakistan in the past have complained of being robbed of the credit of creating the music but Ahmed says his first outing in Bollywood has been more than satisfactory. Now Ahmed is busy wrapping up his first album, Judaai, which releases early next year, comprising eight soulful rock ballads. "There is a soft rock track Gin Gin I am excited about. Its video has been shot in Pakistan and will air in a few weeks time. The album maintains my signature sound, fusion of the electric guitar and vocals and has my hit song Lambi Judaai as well," says Ahmed. If given a chance he would love to collaborate with AR Rahman for an album. "I admire his passion for music. Singing with him would be an honour, but first I would like to finish my album," says the self taught singer who picked up the electric guitar at 14, and counts Pakistani band Junoon as among his favourites. No one hit wonder, this.

Heading: Swede Somethings - Indian Express
Content:
Jugal Hansraj readies for the release of his directorial debut Roadside Romeo

At the Yash Raj Films' canteen, debutant director Jugal Hansraj purrs in excitement about his forthcoming animation movie, Roadside Romeo. The boyish smile and light green eyes still hold a charm. Sweet. "With the release barely two weeks away, I have been practically living at YRF, you know?" he laughs.

By the walkway of the manicured gardens, Hansraj narrates the genesis of the project. "I am an animation-film buff, and Adi (producer Aditya Chopra) knows it. So when he planned a high-end animation film for YRF, I was his first choice. Initially, I was only to write the script, but then he insisted that I direct as well," he gesticulates.

Roadside Romeo is the story of how Romeo, a pet dog in an affluent household, becomes a stray overnight when the family decides to shift out. Pampered all his life, Romeo feels helpless on the streets till he falls for Laila, a canine beauty, and then fights the bully Anna Charlie. The voiceover is given by Saif Ali Khan, Kareena Kapoor and Javed Jaffrey.

"When I thought up the characters, I just knew Romeo had to be Saif, for Romeo is street smart and has style. Laila is a diva, and who else would've portrayed her better than Kareena?" says Hansraj, who was last seen in Aaja Nachle. Jaffrey was a natural choice for "he is a versatile actor and would sound great in animation".

Over tea, he explains how the production work of an animation movie differs from that of a regular one. "An animation film is made backwards," he says. The dubbing happens first. The actors enact the dialogue during the recording, which is used as reference for expressions of the characters. Then the toil begins. "We spend months getting right the expression in each frame. And one change in the frame takes a week for completion as the whole frame needs to be redone," he says. The songs, which are catching on, were done in 10 days flat, he boasts. "And, I've got Saif and Javed sing a hip-hop number too!"

Does the man, who has glorified pets, have any? "Well, now I do." Touché.

Heading: Month on, dustbins upturned, trash all over - Indian Express
Content:
This chef has fed Nobel laureates

Have you wondered what Paul Krugman and Jean-Marie Gustave Le Clézio would dig in at the Nobel Prize banquet on December 10? The American and the Frenchman and 1,298 others at the Blue Hall of the Stockholm City Hall, better be prepared to eat fish glue. Mark Phoenix, a member of the chefs' team that hosts the Nobel banquet, is tight-lipped about the menu, but finally lets on that he plans to fix a dish with a mix of Japanese fish and meat glues.

Phoenix is not worried about the December feast. "Preparations began in January and by May we were ready with the first draft of the menu. After several food-tasting sessions with the Nobel committee, the final menu was put together in September," he says, tossing and turning fillets of river sole at Machan at the Taj Mahal Hotel, where a Swedish food promotion is on.

"I was in India last year and many guests were apprehensive about raw meat. People often returned half-eaten salmon, assuming it was carelessly left uncooked. The response is better this year," he says. But Phoenix is treading with caution. Even when he is pushing pickled herrings and the classical raw, spiced, Norwegian salmon, he has also put together Swedish dishes that will suit the Indian palate. A yellow pea soup, served with pork in Sweden, for instance, is vegetarian here and the lunch buffet has enough well-done meats.

The pickled herrings are equivalent to kebabs, he says, a must to begin the meal. A platter with four fillets, pickled with basil, mustard, Swedish caviar and traditional spices, is served with a scoop of sour cream, chopped onions and a triangle of robust Swedish cheese. The notorious raw salmon is artistically laid out, fenced with potatoes and cream and strokes of mustard sauce on the edges. "Raw food is what stops most European cuisines from venturing to India," says the British-born chef, who has been working for the past four years as a sous chef at the Guild Hall in Stockholm. He will be back there to feed Clezio.

The festival is on till October 17.

Meal for two: Rs 2,000

Contact: 23026162

Heading: MCD eyes mine for ‘eco-friendly’ garbage disposal - Indian Express
Content:
It may have been a month since the serial blasts rocked Delhi, and the city may have moved on, but it seems that things will never be the same for municipal dustbins in the New Delhi area.

Newsline found that dustbins near the Supreme Court, the Mandi House Metro Station and India Gate continue to remain upturned despite the garbage strewn around them.

After bombs were planted in dustbins at Connaught Place, Barakhamba Road and Greater Kailash during the serial blasts, these dustbins were upturned to avert any threat of further blasts.

But a month on, they continue to remain unused. When asked, officials at the New Delhi Municipal Council (NDMC) passed the buck on to the Delhi Police. "We have not issued any specific orders to the sweeping staff or ragpickers for keeping them upturned. It's the Delhi Police. We set them upright every morning but beat officers upturn them again," Dr P K Sharma, NDMC Medical Health Officer, said.

'We have already written to the DCP of the area but the police continue to upturn them everyday," he said. Area DCP Anand Mohan was not available for comment.

In the aftermath of the blasts, the NDMC has already decided to issue identity cards to ragpickers, part of the door-to-door collection project of the municipal council. It will be hiring Ramky Enviro Engineers Ltd, which is already in charge of garbage collection in residential and commercial pockets in the New Delhi area, to lift garbage from government offices and VIP bungalows.

Heading: Factors responsible for widespread shortage of landfill sites - Indian Express
Content:
A Bhatti mines pit is going to be the Municipal Corporation of Delhi's new landfill site. The Corporation says that unlike existing open and unhygienic landfill sites, the new site will be more sophisticated, eco-friendly and away from crowded areas of the city.

The existing landfill sites in Ghazipur, Bawana and Okhla are overflowing with garbage that has never been treated properly. Not only are these sites an eyesore but present a health hazard for people living close by.

The Bhatti mines pit, lying unused for 30 years, is not only off city limits but has a depression that can accommodate Delhi's waste for another 25 years, officials said. This site is going to be engineered in an environment friendly fashion.

The landfill site will be constructed keeping in mind garbage handling guidelines created by the central government. Before the pit is put to use, an environment impact assessment study and a groundwater biological study of the area will be conducted.

"The entire process is very complicated and time consuming. The area has to be treated properly. We shall be hiring an expert agency to provide lining on the surface of the pit to ensure that no toxic waste seeps under ground and pollutes the water table," Municipal Commissioner KS Mehra said.

The Corporation has already started door-to-door collection and segregation of garbage. The garbage that will reach the new landfill site will be waste that cannot be recycled further in any form. "A hundred units of garbage will be compressed to twenty five units by the time they reach the landfill site. It will be ensured that any waste that can be recycled does not reach the landfill site. Only waste that has no scope of recycling will be compressed and dumped in this pit," the commissioner said.

Besides domestic and industrial waste, Delhi produces about 500 metric tons of construction waste each year. Next to the Bhatti mines landfill site the Corporation shall also be setting up a plant to treat construction waste.

"The Corporation shall set up a plant in Burari, where construction waste will be crushed to powder and will then be sent to tile and brick factories, where this dust can be reused," a Corporation official said.

Landfill sites will also be developed in Jaitpur, Narela and Bawana. "The site identified at Jaitpur also has a 25-meter-deep pit. An environment study will be conducted at all three sites before they are made operational. The Corporation will ensure it does not cause any harm to the surrounding environment," the official said.

Heading: Coming soon at Greater Noida: an integrated police control room - Indian Express
Content:
* There is a resistance to waste disposal facilities being located within or near urban communities, since it leads to a fall in the value of residential properties in areas around the sites

* Market forces lead to excessive consumption of landfill capacity, as the price of waste disposal has often not incorporated the cost of replacing landfills when they are exhausted

* Furthermore, the fact that disposal costs through use of landfill sites have been set too low means waste minimisation initiatives, recycling and waste processing industries have not been economically attractive

Landfills elsewhere

Sydney

Sydney has only six years left in its landfill sites. However, with increased waste minimisation, development of further recycling and processing industries and the establishment of some new landfills, the waste service is expected to last for about 30 to 40 years. The government has also set up waste-to-energy plants to take care of Sydney's domestic waste

The Netherlands

The Netherlands is the only European country to have specific plans to develop and reuse landfill sites. The old landfill sites in the province of North-Brabant (NL) were the first to be put to reuse in 2005. Eighty landfill site projects have been identified in the Netherlands.

A Rotterdam site was converted into a golf course; a Zoetermeer site was converted into a ski run; and the Boxtel site into a nature and recreation centre United Kingdom

With an increase in quantity of waste being disposed at landfill sites, the UK government has started imposing a tax from October 1996. Landfill operators in UK are licensed under the Environmental Protection Act (EPA) or the Pollution Control and Local Government Order 1978

To promote the recycling of garbage, the government has allotted and designated tax-free sites to landfill owners and operators.

Source: (For Sydney): Department of the Environment, Water, Heritage and the Arts, Canberra. (For the Netherlands): W.J. (Willem) van Vossen, MSc Senior Consultant Soil, Waste and Spatial Development allot and Royal Haskoning, Hertogenbosch

Heading: JNU to hold student union polls on November 3 - Indian Express
Content:
The Gautam Budh Nagar police integrated police control room at Surajpur set up on a budget of Rs 1.5 crore will be fully functional within a month. The month-long trial has been completed succesfully, according to R K Chaturvedi, SSP Guatam Budh Nagar.

According to Malay Tondon, assitant general manager of HCL Info System, the integrated control room will be used to track down police patrol vehicles.

"Around 55 police patrolling vehicles will get GPS and automatic vehicle tracking system installed in them. Using a digital display screen, the location of all these vehicles can be traced. Along with this, a digital map of the district has also been prepared," said Tandon. The system would ensure immediate police presence at the crime spot. "On receiving the call, a message would be recorded and after tracing the location (of the caller), control room staff would inform the nearest patrolling vehicle. The project is funded by Noida Authority.

The reason why integrated control room will take a month to be functional is that a tower needs to be installed in Phase II.

Infrastructure also needs to be provided before the control room starts functioning. Personnel training will start from next week," he added.

Heading: Bouncers held at Noida nightspot after brawl - Indian Express
Content:
Students' union elections at the Jawaharlal Nehru University will be held on November 3, after a notification was issued to this effect by the Election Committee of the Jawaharlal Nehru University Students' Union.

"Councillors to different schools and two student representatives to the Gender Sensitisation Committee Against Sexual Harassment (GSCASH) will also be elected on the same date," committee chairperson Sarada Prasanna Das said.

The committee issued the notification after consultations with representatives of different student organisations and independent candidates. "Nominations will be filed by October 16 and 17 and can be withdrawn on October 19. A final list of candidates will be displayed the next day," Prasanna said.

The presidential debate will be held on November 1, the elections will take place on November 3 and results will be declared on November 5.

The outgoing union has been dissolved and has handed over charge to the 28-member Election Committee, which comprises student representatives from different schools of the university.

According to the students' union constitution, the Election Committee is responsible for conducting free and fair elections in JNU and has to hand over charge to the new union within 28 days of taking over from the outgoing union.

The election process for 2008-09 was initiated on October 10, with the formation of the Election Committee, and Sarada Prasanna Das, a PhD student from Centre for the Study of Social Systems, School of Social Sciences, was elected unanimously as chairperson of the committee.

Heading: Traffic police to get new, improved wheel clamps to nail offenders - Indian Express
Content:
The Noida police have registered a complaint against two bouncers of a restrobar in Sector-18, for allegedly beating and misbehaving with customers.

The complaint was lodged after Aditya Goswami, a resident of Ghaziabad, alleged that the bouncers of Ice Cube, a restrobar, manhandled him and two of his friends, Ashish Kumar and Nischal. They had gone there for drinks and dinner.

Kumar lives in Laxmi Nagar, while Nischal is a resident of Jalvayu Vihar in Noida. The FIR lodged by Goswami states that they were coming out of the restrobar when one of them slipped from the stairs. "The bouncers made fun of us and when we objected, they started beating us," the FIR reads.

The incident took place just 50 metres from the local police post, located right opposite the restrobar. Police sources claimed they intervened after the brawl became violent and arrested the bouncers. "Vikki, a resident of Badarpur and Aamir, a resident of Zakir Nagar, were arrested after the complaint," Vijay Singh, Sector-20 station house officer, said.

Meanwhile, questioning the role of bouncers in nightspots across the city, the police have decided to hold a meeting with nightspot owners soon. "The owners should employ guards who are trained and wear uniforms. Bouncers do not wear uniforms and could easily be mistaken as another customer. Moreover, they are not disciplined. We will hold a meeting with all bar owners on the issue," SHO Singh said.

Heading: Decks cleared for minority status to Jains - Indian Express
Content:
The Delhi Traffic Police is renewing its efforts to take strict action against parking offenders across the Capital. The Delhi Traffic department has sought to purchase 500 new wheel clamps to be used against those who park their cars in no-parking areas.

According to sources, the police are hesitant to use the existing clamps as they are not very user-friendly. "Wheel clamps currently in use are very heavy and are used in few areas of the Capital. There are several improved models available in the market. That is the reason why we have asked for 500 more clamps which are being used in countries like the US and the UK," said a source in the Delhi Traffic Police.

The police have invited quotations from companies manufacturing wheel clamps and are hopeful that new machines will be available soon. Confirming orders for the new wheel clamps, Joint Commissioner of Police (Traffic), S N Srivastava said, "We want to purchase advance and improved versions of wheel clamps which are also easy to use."

Police sources added the clamps which are in use are old, heavy and work by tightening nuts and bolts. "Fixing the clamps is time-consuming and extremely difficult. To avoid these problems, we decided to go in for more sophisticated and technologically sound wheel clamps which can be fixed directly onto the wheel, and quickly," a senior police officer said.

Sources said the new wheel clamps will be used in several busy markets of South Delhi apart from New Delhi district areas. Senior police officers , added that the cost of the new clamps would be higher than the existing ones. "There cost is more as compared to the existing ones, but considering the parking woes across the capital, more use of these machines have become very important. Parking violators need to realise that violation of traffic rules is a serious offence and should not be done."

Police officers added extensive use of clamps will help curbing parking problems in the Cpital as violators are left with no other option than to pay the challan. They are also easy to operate as compared to the current practice of the vehicle being towed away.

Heading: Seven schoolchildren hurt as minibus overturns in East Delhi - Indian Express
Content:
Community will be on par with Muslims, Christians, Parsis and Buddhists listed as notified groups in Delhi

With Delhi Assembly elections round the corner, the Congress-led Delhi government issued an order approving the long-standing demand of the Jain community for minority status in the Capital.

As reported by Newsline earlier, the move came following a High Court order, in which it had held the community should be given the status of a minority community in order to clarify that it may establish minority educational institutions. It also came through after a fair amount of lobbying by Chief Minister Sheila Dikshit and Chandni Chowk MP Kapil Sibal, who has a sizeable population of the community in his constituency.

After the sealing debacle that cost it the municipal corporation elections, the move is believed to have been made to appease this section of the traders' community which otherwise is known to favour the BJP.
