Dikshit cleared the decks for granting the status to the community on par with Buddhists, Christians, Sikhs, Muslims and Parsis, listed as notified groups under the Delhi Minorities Commission Act, 1999 earlier in July.

As per the 2001 census, there are about 4-5 lakh Jains in the Capital They comprise about 0.45 percent of the Capital's population.

The move will benefit the community at large, Diskhit said, adding this would help the community to effectively manage their educational institutions as per parameters specified for such institutions.

Heading: Woman, 37, jumps into Yamuna off DND flyway - Indian Express
Content:
Eight people — seven school children, and the driver — were injured after a minibus overturned on the way to school in New Ashok Vihar area of East Delhi on Monday.

The police said the incident took place around 6.45 am, when the driver lost control over the minibus (RTV). Police said though they initially suspected the driver was drunk, medical examination confirmed he was not.

Initial investigations suggest the incident took place because of the bad condition of the road. "He reportedly lost control when he was trying to overtake a chartered bus," the police said.

The victims have been identified as Manju Devtulla (18), Aasha Bhatt (17), Laxmi (18), Babita (16), Ritika (17), Priyanka (15), Shalu (15) and Chandan (31).

While the victims were given preliminary medication at a local nursing home and discharged, two school children with more serious injuries, Manju and Shalu, were referred to the Lal Bahadur Shastri Hospital, from where they were discharged after treatment in the afternoon. Doctors said they operated upon Manju, who received multiple fractures in her right hand. Her condition is stable, the police said.

Officers said Manju was sitting next to the door of the minibus and her right hand reportedly came in between the panes of a window.

Some local shopkeepers immediately rushed to the spot and tried to take her out by breaking the glass.

The police said Manju's father, Manohar Dutt, runs a grocery shop and reached the hospital immediately after being informed about the incident by a local shopkeeper.

Officers said the injured students were of the Rajkiya Sarvodaya Kanya Vidyalaya in Mayur Vihar Phase II. The police have arrested the driver of the RTV for rash and negligent driving. The conductor is, however, still at large and a case has been registered against him at the local police station. Further investigations are on in the case.

Heading: No decision yet over Congress final list of candidates - Indian Express
Content:
Clerk at AIIMS, victim left home in rage after row with in-laws: police

A 37-year old woman allegedly jumped into the Yamuna from the Delhi-Noida-Delhi (DND) Flyway on Sunday evening, reportedly a result of marital discord.

Almost 24 hours on, the police and fire department officials have not yet been able to recover her body.

According to the police, the victim, Indu Prabha, a junior clerk at the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), stormed out of her house in Noida reportedly after a heated row with her in-laws and drove on to the DND Flyway. "She was in her Maruti 800 car and we suspect she was enraged and was driving really fast," a police official said.

Eyewitnesses have told the police that her car first crashed into a divider on the flyway; after that she reportedly abandoned the car and jumped into the river.

A bystander called the Police Control Room at 9.15 pm and though the police called in fire department officials and formed a rescue operation team the body has not been recovered yet.

Police officials said Prabha's husband Bhagwati Prasad is a sub-inspector with the CISF and is posted with the Ministry of Home Affairs.

Senior officers said the reason for the suicide has not been established yet as her parents, who live in Sadiq Nagar, Southeast Delhi, have said told police Prabha did not have any reason to commit suicide. Her in-laws have, meanwhile, told police that she left home after an argument.

The police are yet to ascertain the reason for that argument.

After the incident, a reporter from a TV news channel went to her parents' house on Sunday night but Prabha's brother reportedly beat him and snatched his chain. After the local police refused to take action, the reporter took his complaint to Delhi Police Commissioner Y S Dhadwal's residence at 3.30 am. The police registered a case against unknown people at New Friends Colony police station after directions from the police chief.

Heading: MCD, Bar body lock horns over land in Old Delhi - Indian Express
Content:
Congress Screening Committee met on Monday once again to make the final list of candidates. The screening committee met the 26 members of the Delhi election committee.

"At present, no decision has been taken and we are merely hearing out people and analysing viable options," said Delhi Pradesh Congress president Jai Prakash Agarwal. There are several seats over which the Congress is finding itself in a tight spot. Both Tajddar Babbar and Tarvinder Marwah, Congress stalwarts, are at loggerheads with interests in the same constituencies. Following delimitation, a large chunk Babbar's Minto Road consistuency is now in Marwah's Jungpura area.

Down South, Kiran Walia and Health Minister Yoganand Shastri are caught in a similar tussle. A large part of Shastri's constituency has gone to Walia's area in Hauz Khas. The remaining portion of Shastri's area has been merged with Greater Kailash. The Congress leaders are now in a fix over allocating areas for Shastri and Walia. Sources claim Shastri will emerge as a loser in the battle.

In North Delhi too, with delimitation, Sadar Bazar and Kamla Nagar have been merged. Here two Congress leaders Rajesh Jain and Shadi Ram are stuck in a battle for the seat. Meanwhile, there are several names doing the rounds for Greater Kailash — the constituency of BJP's CM candidate V K Malhotra. Although no decision has been taken at present.

"For at least these three constituencies, the final decision will have to be made by the Central Election Committee headed by Sonia Gandhi," said a senior Congress leader.

Heading: Gurgaon jailer in dock for ignoring court directive - Indian Express
Content:
Having fought encroachment till the other day, the Municipal Corporation of Delhi has allegedly built itself a parking lot on land that belongs to the Delhi Bar Association.

Right across from the Old Delhi Railway Station was an open patch of land with an illegal khoya mandi. This space was also used as an illegal parking for buses and to load and unload trucks at night.

Since the area is very close to Town Hall, the corporation cleared the encroachment and put pavement tiles to level the ground. The area was cleared and ready for use in just three weeks time. Not realising the land did not belong to them, they were using it as a free parking lot for councillors and bureaucrats coming to Town Hall.

That was till Friday. On Monday, when officials returned to duty, they found that boards that said MCD Parking were replaced by boards of the Delhi Bar Association.

The land has been with the Delhi Bar Association since 1912. It has been marked out for a bar association club. But this is not the first time the corporation has trespassed on the Delhi Bar Association land. "In 1992, the corporation said the land belonged to the bar association. They wanted to carry out some construction there. We went to court and got a stay. There was a similar situation in 2000. We again went to court to get a stay," Rajeev Khosla, president of the Delhi Bar Association, said.

The Bar Association has now filed a contempt petition in court.

The association heard of the parking lot about ten days ago, and members approached the police. "We registered a complaint in the Chandni Chowk police station but the police did not take any action," Khosla said.

The corporation, however, says the land belongs to them and the Bar Association had encroached upon it and was using it as illegal parking. "The land belongs to the corporation. The Bar Association case is not valid. We will go to court," MCD spokesperson Deep Mathur said.

Heading: HC closes 20-yr case, brings relief to former SBI staffer - Indian Express
Content:
Callousness regarding a court's directive by the Superintendent of Bhondsi Jail in Gurgaon has spelt trouble for him as a magistrate has now issued a warrant against him through the department's top cop.

Metropolitan Magistrate Vikas Dhull issued a bailable warrant against Superintendent S S Dahiya for a sum of Rs 5,000 last week, directing the coercive process to be served through the Gurgaon Police Commissioner.

The magistrate has also issued a show cause notice against Dahiya asking as to why contempt of court proceedings should not be initiated against him for disobeying its directions repeatedly.

Singh is in the dock for his failure to produce Neeraj, accused in a criminal case filed by the North-east district police in 2006, currently lodged in Gurgaon district jail in connection with a different case.

Deepak, a co-accused in the case, is in the custody of Delhi Police.

Despite production warrants being served on the officer, the accused was not brought to the court. The case is presently at the stage of recording of prosecution evidence.

"Issue showcause notice to the Superintendent to appear in person and apprise as to why contempt proceedings should not be initiated against him for failure to obey orders of this court," said the magistrate in a recent order.

The magistrate has also shot another notice against the officer under Section 175 of the Indian Penal Code, spelling out the offence of failure of a man to produce documents before a court though being legally bound to do so.

Dahiya is already under scanner following the suicide of jail head warden Hawa Singh as the suicide note reportedly blamed him for goading him to take the extreme step.

An FIR under the abetment of suicide section of the IPC was subsequently lodged by the local police.

Heading: Grover murder case: Susairaj moves HC for bail - Indian Express
Content:
For 37 years of his life, R N Bhargava worked for his bank and an "unblemished" service record. The next 21 years saw him engage in courtroom battles against the same bank. Now at the end of the "long torture", all the 81-year-old wants is to be left alone to "die in peace".

The State Bank of India (SBI) had in June 1988 unceremoniously removed R N Bhargava, then assistant general manager, for drawing an excess amount of Rs 8,400 towards travel allowance. Though Bhargava returned the amount to the bank and even went on to draw a pension, the "blot" on his service record continued to bother him enough to file a case against his employer in 1989, least expecting the case to drag on for over two decades.

Now at 81, he has finally won the long sought reprieve from prolonged litigation with Delhi High Court willing to bury the "lingering controversy" between him and his bank.

The Division Bench led by Justice Madan B Lokur, however, is careful to term their decision on the octogenarian's case as an exception based on the "peculiar facts of this matter" rather than as a precedent.

"The view that we (court) have taken should not be construed to mean that there should be dilution of integrity by an employee of any bank. Lack of integrity jeopardises the credibility of any banking institution only to make it virtually impossible for a customer to repose faith in the institution," the Bench observed in the recent judgment.

The case had dragged on till July 21, 2008, when the 81-year-old pleaded with the court for a "peaceful burial of the controversy" taking into consideration his advanced years and the long service record with the bank since had joined it in October 1951.

The SBI was, however, in no mood to forgive. The Chief General Manager in court termed Bhargava's action as "breach of trust", made worse by the fact that he had been occupying a senior post at the time. The bank dismissed his plea of old age as a case of "misplaced sympathy".

"We are of the opinion that on the facts of this case, the lingering controversy should not continue. The petitioner (Bhargava) has an unblemished record of 37 years with no allegation made against him in this period," the Bench differed with the bank. "This matter has been pending for over 20 years and the petitioner is above 80," the court said, setting aside the "order of removal" against the former bank employee.

"I am grateful to the honourable High Court," said Bhargava.

Heading: Mapkar made absconding accused in Hari Masjid firing case - Indian Express
Content:
Kannada actress Maria Monica Susairaj, accused in the murder of TV executive Neeraj Grover, has moved the Bombay High Court for bail, pleading not guilty for the murder charges slapped against her.

In her plea, she stated that there was nothing to prove her motive behind the murder and there was no evidence to sustain the murder charges against her.

According to her lawyer G S Kannur, this is a fit case for granting bail. The application also stated that there was no possibility of tampering with the evidence.

The sessions court on September 16 had rejected her bail plea for the second time on the grounds that prima facie evidence available in the case pointed fingers towards Maria and her naval officer fiancé and co-accused in the case, Emile Jerome Mathew.

The court had rejected defence's plea of making Maria an accused only in the part pertaining to the destruction of evidence. The court also observed that the murder was not pre-mediated as Susairaj had called up Mathew 20 times over her mobile phone on the night of May 6 and asked him to come to Mumbai.

Despite Susairaj's statement that she was party only in part of the case pertaining to the destruction of evidence, the police in June named her as the main accused who had engineered the crime.

"The bail hearing will come up on October 18," said Kannur.

Heading: Sena plans monuments to attract tourists - Indian Express
Content:
A designated special sessions court has declared Farooq Mapkar, who has been absconding for 16 years, as an absconding accused in the Hari Masjid firing case. Mapkar, both a victim and an accused in the case dating back to the Mumbai riots of 1992-93, was declared absconding after he failed to be present before the court in second half of the trial.

However, on October 6, Mapkar's case was scheduled for trial. But, when Mapkar complained of ill health, he was taken to the St. George Hospital. Meanwhile, when his case came up for hearing, the judge R D Jadhav declared him absconding as he was not present.

Farooq, a security guard in a cooperative bank, had also moved an application seeking permission to examine witnesses and recall the defence witnesses who were not been tried so far. However, the court has rejected the plea.

Farooq was one of those injured when police opened fire at Hari Masjid on the afternoon of January 10, 1993. Farooq along with 57 others was made accused by the police for mob violence. According to the chargesheet filed by the police in 1994, there was firing from the mosque also and later the mob went to a house that was a kilometre away and burnt it, killing a man.

Heading: Seven PWP men arrested for attacking Panvel firm over hiring labourers - Indian Express
Content:
Includes 160-ft Mumbai Eye at Bandra, wax museum at Girgaum, a memorial to 1857 revolt

A 160-feet-high 'Mumbai Eye' at Bandra Land's End offering the city's ubiquitous view; a replica of Madam Tussaud's wax museum at Girgaum Chowpatty, a memorial of 1857's revolt opposite Azad Maidan and an information centre on the Samyukta Maharashtra Movement — these are the urban monuments which the Shiv Sena-led BMC hopes will attract more tourists to the city.

Unveiling plans to make Mumbai a tourist attraction, Sena leaders said the projects will be developed without putting much money—by way of MP funds and Build, Operate and Transfer (BOT) basis. "Mumbai is visited by so many tourists, but they hardly have anything to see here. By developing these monuments, we hope people will get to know more about the city and enjoy as well," said Sena leader and standing committee chairman Ravindra Waikar, who recommended Mumbai Eye, modelled on the famous London Eye and a wax museum after his trip to London early this year.

Representative of Great Wheel Corporation and Spanco Telesystems and Solutions Ltd, who are setting up the giant wheels in Singapore, Beijing and six other locations across the world, have already approached the BMC. "Beijing will have the largest eye in the world at 200 meters, but it's difficult to go beyond 160 meters in Mumbai due to long monsoon period here," said an official of the company.

The civic body, after scouting for land at Malabar Hill and Worli, has settled for a four acre site at Bandra Land's End and will study its technical feasibility. Once approved, the Mumbai Eye will be come up in three years' time. The wax museum, earlier planned in in the Byculla Zoo, will now come up on a 10,000 sq feet land at Chowpaty —in Birla Krida Kendra, a public performance space that itself is set for a revamp.

Sena, on insistence of its vice-president Uddhav Thackeray, also plans to develop a memorial 'Amar Javanjyot' at Azad maidan to commemorate the sacrifice of a Hindu (Mangal Gadiya) and a Muslim (Sayyed Hussain) in the 151st year of the 1857 revolt. MP Bharatkumar Raut is contributing Rs 25 lakh for the project.

The information centre, displaying information on the 106 martyrs and the events of 1960s that led to the separation of Maharashtra and Gujarat from the Bombay Presidency, will be built at Shivaji Park.

Heading: IM men planned to kidnap two in Pune: Police - Indian Express
Content:
Seven activists of the Peasants and Workers Party from Panvel in Navi Mumbai were arrested for attacking a warehousing firm on Monday. Accodring to sources, the warehousing premises of the Flyjet Logistics was ransacked by a mob of PWP activists over the issue of employment of unskilled labourers in the firm.

According to Kamlesh Desai, regional manager, Flyjet Logistics, the firm had set up warehousing facility at Taloja to service it client Technova Imaging Sytems and hired as many as 7-8 unskilled labourers provided by the gram panchayat. Local PWP leader G R Patil and PWP MLA from Panvel Vivek Patil have been putting pressure on the firm to hire labourers affiliated to the party, he said.

"We explained to them that our firm has been hiring labourers through gram panchayats across Maharashtra. As our requirement at Taloja was already met, we suggested those desiring to get hired be first enlisted with the gram panchayat and we would hire them when we need more requirements," said Desai.

PWP has been putting pressure on the firm for the last two months to hire activists affiliated to the party by either firing the already hired local villagers or hiring surplus labourers that the firm would not require, he said.

"Today morning I was tipped on the impending attack on the company premises at Taloja as several people had spotted a mob of 100-150 people gathering in the vicinity. Fearing the attack, we had not commenced operation. However, the mob managed to gain entry into the company premises by assaulting the security and other staff. The mob ransacked the office destroying everything that came within their reach," said Desai.

The instructions to the mob to attack the office was apparently given by G R Patil over his mobile phone in the presence of police and him at the police station on Monday morning, Desai alleged.

When contacted, PWP MLA Vivek Patil said the firm had failed to keep the promise that it would hire labourers from the gram panchayat and the party as well. "As many as 50-60 youths had gone there today to seek employment and were subsequently attacked by the goondas hired by the company," said Patil.

Deputy Commissioner of Police Ashok Dhude said the situation was under control and police have lodged the First Information Report. According to him, as many as seven people were arrested for assault. DCP Dhude was not able to confirm if Patil, who had allegedly instructed the mob to attack the company, was among those who had been arrested by the police.

Heading: NKC members say India needs at least 1500 more universities - Indian Express
Content:
The Mumbai police say the 20 Indian Mujahideen members they arrested in connection with the probe into bomb blasts and terror email had planned to kidnap a builder and a jeweller from Pune. The Pune police say they have no idea of any such plot, even though the details emerged during the interrogation of two of the persons picked up from Pune.

The Mumbai police had seized anaesthetics from some of the arrested and according to them, a probe led to the unearthing of the plot. "This looks like one of the modes they were planning to fund their terror operations," said Rakesh Maria, Joint Commissioner of Police (Crime Branch).

"They conducted a recce of the area where the two persons lived for 15 days early this year. The idea of holding people to ransom seems to have come from Riyaz Bhatkal as he has a background in crime," Maria said.

Citing a "heavy police bandobast" as the reason for the failure of the kidnap plan, Maria said, "The amount of drugs and anaesthetics found is huge. One needs a prescription for getting such drugs and we are probing the source of the drugs."

While the IM's media wing was busy learning hacking, this group was told to pick up the two persons and hold them at Ashoka Mews which the group had rented. "The idea was to drug the kidnapped and hold them till a ransom is paid," Maria said.

The Pune police, however, denied any police protection being provided to any builder or jeweller. "We have got no such report from the Mumbai police," said Pune Police Commissioner Satyapal Singh. "The joint commissioner of Mumbai crime branch has all the details."

According to Intelligence agencies, there is sufficient evidence to suggest that kidnapping for ransom was a mean to fund terror activities. The last such case was the kidnapping of shoe baron Partho Burman in Kolkata in which a part of the ransom paid was believed to have reached terror outfits via Aftab Ansari, the main accused in the American Center attack case.

Heading: In times of realty slump, city has oversupply of malls - Indian Express
Content:
Three years since its inception, for the first time ever, the members of the National Knowledge Commission (NKC) had an interactive session with management students and faculty members at a conference by the NKC and the All India Management Association (AIMA) on Monday.

Sam Pitroda, chairman, NKC, and other members of the NKC- Dr Sujata Ramdorai, Professor (School of Mathematics) Tata Institute of Fundamental Research, Dr Ashok Ganguly, Chairman, Firstsource Ltd and ABP Pvt Ltd and Professor Amitabh Mattoo, vice-chancellor of University of Jammu addressed students of Narsee Monjee Institute of Management Studies (NMIMS) and other B-schools. They spoke of the state of education system in India, emphasizing on school education, e-governance and other core areas.

"We have just 380 universities for a population of over 1 billion. As per NKC recommendations, India needs at least 1500 more universities . Even as we speak of increasing the number, we also need to focus on improving the quality. There are not enough trained qualified professionals in India today." Dr Ashok Ganguly said, adding, "Unless vocational education is not modernized, our demographic dividend will be in a chaos."

Pitroda who is considered to be one of the pioneers in transforming India's telecommunications and information technology infrastructure as the founding chairman of the Telecom Commission in India, reminisced on how it took the telecom industry 20 years to change the face of India but said that the same journey for a 'knowledge revolution' would be longer and more complex.

"We have started the journey but we require more of political will, public opinion and more importantly insistence by the people to demand change," he said. Taking a dig at the central government, Pitroda said that people should not wait for "Delhi to take decisions" but local commutates could take up initiatives . Pitroda also stressed on the need for children to know English in order to be a 'global player'. "English should be taught from standard one in all the schools. The idea is not to replace the mother tongue but to capitalise on the capacity of young children to grasp different languages."

Pitroda concluded by urging the students to 'get into teaching'. "We need more and more people to join us in our journey," he said.

Heading: Classic Art registers shocking win in the AP Racehorse Owners Trophy - Indian Express
Content:
Developers shelve plans for new ones; some let out mall space for commercial use

* The Kohinoor group which had planned a six-storey mall as part of its Kohinoor City at Kurla has now decided to go in for a less ambitious two-storey one. The group has decided to instead increase the commercial component of the project.

* Even a strategic location bang opposite Santacruz station couldn't help bail out the Hi-life mall which failed to get retailers for the top three floors of the five-storeyed mall. After six months, these floors are now being let out as office space after retaining the retail outlets on the first two floors.

* The swanky two lakh sq ft Atria mall at Worli has a high vacancy rate of more than 24%, the average vacancy rate in malls usually being 5%.

The glut caused by the burgeoning number of malls in the city has led to several developers shelving their plans for malls and instead going in for office spaces. A few have been compelled to lease out part of their already constructed mall complex to offices after they found no takers amongst retailers.

To make matter worse, at a time when the economic slowdown has caused retailers to go slow on their expansion plans, 1.7 million sq ft of supply is near completion in Mumbai and is expected to enter the market over the coming few months.

According to Pankaj Kapoor, CEO of the real estate research and analyses agency Liases Foras, Mumbai's real estate has an oversupply scenario in the retail sector with 125 malls in the city including the under construction ones. "Retailers are cost-sensitive and with inflation the profit margin of retail companies has gone down. The same is true for consumer affordability. DLF and India Bulls were the first to do away with their plans for malls or reduce the area for the same at their under construction projects at Lower Parel."

"Let alone the price factor, we were not getting any retailers in our project Hi-life at Santacruz. As developers we have to finish a project and move on to the next one. Instead of waiting for two years, we took a call to let out our mall for commercial use and we immediately found takers for one entire floor," said Mukesh Patel from Neelkanth group.

Another upcoming mall at Prabhadevi as well as a newly constructed mall at Bhuleshwar are amongst the ones to join the commercial bandwagon. Property analyst point that that a successful mall in central Mumbai has been witnessing their retail tenants periodically changing while another one in Malad has been of late seeing lower footfalls than before after the opening of a new mall in the nearby suburbs.

Besides the slump, analysts state that in many cases the decision to convert upcoming malls projects into commercial has been fuelled by a September 2008 state government notification allowing IT parks to utilize 80% of the total constructed area for financial services and banks. IT parks that are allowed to build double the area allowed for normal buildings were initially allowed to let out only 30% of its space for activities other than IT and IT enabled services.

Developer Vimal Shah, who had earlier announced plans for Akruti city mall at Andheri is amongst the many who will now construct a commercial project in place of the mall. Shah states that one reason for his choice is that in India anchor stores (the chief attraction at a mall meant to draw customers) offer very low rents. "It is so low that to make up for it the other retail stores in the mall are charged heavy rents. This makes it difficult for them to remain in the malls for long," said Shah.

Heading: ONGC thrash off-colour Central Railway - Indian Express
Content:
The police investigating the alleged suicide of four members of a family in Borivali now believe that the elderly Nair couple might have been smothered to death by their son and daughter before they committed suicide by hanging themselves from ceiling fans.

Senior Police Inspector P Suryavanshi of Kasturba Marg police station said, "During our investigation in the apartment premises where the four deaths had taken place, we did not find any evidence to suggest that the couple might have been poisoned as there were no bottles or any containers which could have contained poison. We have reasons to believe that the parents might have been smothered to death with a pillow by their children before they killed themselves by hanging. However, nothing concrete can be said till the autopsy reports arrive."

The decomposed bodies of the Nair family members were discovered on Sunday afternoon when a neighbour complained of foul smell emanating from their flat on the seventh floor of Ekta Woods building at Raheja Estates, Borivali (East). The residents of the building contacted the owner of the flat, Venu Madhavan, an advocate, who opened the door with a spare key to discover the bodies of the siblings, Suchitra (46) and Sudhir (42), hanging from ceiling fans.

"The residents immediately closed the door and contacted the police and we went there and further discovered the bodies of the parents, A K Nair (81) and wife Shyamala (70), on the bed in an inside room. A most unusual fact is that all the four bodies had ceremonial marks and 'tikkas' on their foreheads. We suspect that Suchitra and Sudhir applied the markings on their parents either before or after killing them," said Suryavanshi.

He said the police also found a suicide note written by Suchitra in English and dated October 10 in which it was written that they were frustrated due to financial problems and that they "had no means to sustain themselves."

A K Nair, a former BHEL employee, working with the company's Bhopal plant, had retired a few years ago. The two children are engineers by profession and whereas Sudhir, the son, had worked in Dubai for a few years, the daughter, Suchitra, had worked with BHEL for 10 years and had resigned her position as Deputy General Manager. "Suchitra had resigned from work in September last year because of which they had to surrender their BHEL quarters in the same locality. At the time, Suchitra had told her colleagues that she had plans to open a dairy farming and agricultural products business in her native place in Kerala and the whole family had shifted there," Suryavanshi said. However, after an year of staying there, the family discovered that Shyamala's asthma problem was aggravating because of the weather conditions in Kerala and they came back in February this year and contacted a local estate agent to find them a house on rent in the Raheja Estates area as they had stayed there before, Suryavanshi said.

When contacted, Tukaram Sawant, the estate agent said, "The family had contacted me and told me about their desire to stay in a flat at Raheja Estates. Apart from that, I do not know much about them as they never used to mix with anyone in the locality and even when dealing with me, they were absolutely professional in their approach and I never disclosed anything about their family positions or background." Another reason Suryavanshi feels why the family took the extreme step was probably because they had no friends or relatives to whom they could turn to in times of distress. "They usually kept to themselves and did not mingle with anyone. Moreover, thy do not seem to have kept in touch with any relatives, if they had any," he added.

Heading: Mumbai link to part two of LHC experiment - Indian Express

ONGC recorded their second straight victory in the Mumbai Hockey Association (MHA) 2008-09 Super League by upstaging Central Railway 3-0 at the MHA-Mahindra stadium on Monday. The Railway side had themselves to blame though as they simply miffed a number of opportunities including five penalty corners that they won during the game.

In fact both teams failed to really capitalize on the penalty corners that were awarded to them, as ONGC themselves converted only one out of four successfully.

Jayanta fired the first goal for ONGC in the 15th minute through a drag-flick. Amit Bharadwaj then added to Central's woes by scoring the second, two minutes later. He slotted in a cross-pass unleashed from the axis by Sandeep Antil. ONGC remained 2-0 up at the lemon-break.

The railway outfit's disappointing display continued in the second-half, as they simply couldn't match up to the pace set by their opponents. Antil then netted in his second goal of the evening, as he fired from the top of the D leaving Central's custodian Mohd Akhil stranded.

This gave ONGC a 3-0 lead, which they held onto till the final hooter.

Heading: BoI inch closer to Super 7 - Indian Express
Content:
A tier of the Worldwide LHC Computing Grid that allows scientists to analyse data is located in premier research institute

The city will have a connection to the next installment of the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) experiment underway in Europe, with the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR) in the city housing a computer that is part of the Worldwide LHC Computing Grid (WLCG), the system that will allow scientists to understand and analyse the data from the experiment.

The LHC experiment, which made waves around the world last month, will require scientists to analyse large amounts of data from each aspect of the experiment, and the WLCG, which became functional last week, will be used for this. The grid technology, as it is called, has immense computing power and data storage capability, and is distributed in three tiers around the globe.

Tier 0, the central and uppermost level, is located in Geneva, Switzerland at the European Organisation for Nuclear Research's (CERN), the headquarters of the experiment, and will receive raw data. "One set of countries have tier 1, whereas the rest have tier 2 systems. In India, Mumbai's Tata Institute of Fundamental Research and the Variable Energy Cyclotron Centre, Kolkata, have tier 2 systems," says Nagaraj Panyam, one of the system administrators for the tier 2 system at TIFR in Mumbai.

The Baba Atomic Research Centre (BARC), too, has contributed to the software used in the grid technology. "BARC's contribution has been towards making software tools, problem-solving tools, and monitoring tools. The main aim is to see that smooth operations go on, since it is a wide network of countries from over the world. Around 25-30 people were involved in the work, which lasted over 15 months," says G P Srivastava, director of Electronics and Instrumentation at BARC, which is connected with computer activities. The tier 2 system has approximately 2,000 times the computing power compared to a typical desktop.

"Scientists from over the world will feed their data to the computer which goes to any grid that is free. After it is computed, the data then returns to the scientist who submitted it within a few hours or a few days. We have to simulate millions of events in the detector and these results will require a statistical-level analysis. Several petabytes will be analysed every second," says Kajari Mazumdar, a professor at TIFR who is associated with the project.

"The entire project itself is huge and unprecedented, and requires a good network of computing systems," adds Panyam.

As the WLCG became functional on October 3, the data from the experiment will now be available to scientists working on the experiment. The computing system will allow scientists from over the world who are involved in the LHC experiment to analyse the data that is produced during the experiments. The main computing system will be located at CERN, and will be connected to 11 major computer centres in Europe, North America and Asia, from where the data will further be dispatched to more than 140 centres in 33 countries the world over. While the Mumbai system is connected to the Compact Muon Solenoid (CMS), the Kolkata system is connected to A Large Ion Collider Experiment (ALICE).

Heading: Shipnekar blanks fancied Gathe - Indian Express
Content:
Bankmen post comfortable 2-0 win over Akbar Travels; Navy win

Bank of India (BoI) moved closer to booking a place in the Super 7s of the MFL Elite Division League from Group A by beating a below par Akbar Travels outfit 2-0 at the RCF ground on Monday. In the second match of the day between Indian Navy and Central Railway Mumbai Division (CRMD), the former posted their first win in five matches, by coming back from a one goal deficit to win 2-1.

Akbar Travels, who had finished sixth in the Super 6 last year, took the field today without their star performer Jonathan 'Bobo'. Though their other foreign recruit, Ezekal Okwulum exerted a lot of pressure up front, the Akbar Travels players looked worn out. And once Shankar Thakur put the bankmen ahead in the 18th minute, their struggling opponents looked a defeated unit. The second goal by Salesh Jadhav, which went in through the hands of the Akbar Travels'custodian Naufil sealed the fate of the match.

Akbar Travels were unlucky not to get a penalty when Ezekal was brought down in the box, but a few minutes later when Jadhav entered the Akbar Travels'six-yard-box and was tripped, the referee was quick to point at the penalty spot. However, Hassan Rizvi made a mess of the shot, pummeling the ball over the crossbar.

The second match, which was only of academic interest, was fast paced and the sailors did their best to redeem their standing in the Elite Division. Though as usual the CRMD players operated from their box, the Indian Navy players, especially Shaji D'Silva, worked hard to create openings. However against the run of play, Asif Jamal scored for CRMD in the 43rd minute. After the lemon break, the sailors exerted a lot of pressure and missed quite a few chances. But then substitute Ramesh Kumar scored in the 65th minute to level the game, and P Kumar pumped in the winner in the 75th minute after goalkeeper Shanmugam fumbled while collecting a grounder.

Heading: Face value - Indian Express
Content:
Musician Nitin Sawhney's latest album London Undersound has a series of high-profile collaborations and Paul McCartney singing about his breakup with Heather Mills

When the tabloids blitzed London with the bitter split of the former Beatle, Paul McCartney, and his former wife Heather Mills, the musician Nitin Sawhney couldn't help calling up Macca, his friend of 12 years, and ask if he wanted to write down his feelings in a song. That's what The Beatles always did. The call eventually resulted in a maudlin, acoustic, love ballad called My soul and features in Sawhney's latest album, London Undersound.

"Paul came down to my house for a couple of days and we started putting together the track which delves into the paparazzi infiltrating his life during the breakup. More than the split, it's about his soul being stolen," says Sawhney, who also penned the lyrics of the song with McCartney. The alimony is not part of the song that goes, "I long to know all your secrets/ I want to walk through your fire/ Light up my eyes with your smile", which is also believed to be McCartney's dedication to Mills and has a tinge of Indian classical vocals in the background.

But it is not just one collaboration that Sawhney has lined up. "The entire album is a series of collaborations and represents the changing dynamics of London as a city, and hence the name," says the 44-year-old, who is concerned about the fear trickling in the city after 9/11 and 7/7. "There's a lot of unease about issues like race and civil liberties in London and across the world," he says. Sawhney who, along with Sanjeev Bhaskar, created the music for the hit series Goodness Gracious Me, says the British-Asian community is perceived differently now than when the funny series was conceptualised. The shadow of terror is there in the album as well, with the reggae artist Natty interpreting his first-hand account of the 7/7 bombings in Days of fire.

Sawhney has also collaborated with Tina Grace and Anoushka Shankar in Transmission and Charukeshi respectively. "I've know them through their music, but this album is special as it reflects the vision of various artists," he says.

Sawhney, who is of Indian origin, now plays many roles in London — a club DJ, a songwriter, composer, classical pianist and flamenco guitarist. After composing the score for Mira Nair's The Namesake, he's also working on four more films, including Deepa Mehta's next, Exclusion. Meanwhile, his first performance in India is yet to be. In the diary, he has marked the 2010 Jaipur Festival, but he is hoping it happens sooner.

Heading: meal ticket - Indian Express
Content:
Things are looking up for this debutante director as he readies for the release of Roadside Romeo

As we walk towards the Yash Raj Studios' canteen, a hangout frequented more by film journalists than by the cast and crew of films being shot there, debutante director Jugal Hansraj sounds excited over his forthcoming animation movie, Roadside Romeo. Ah, that boyish smile and those light green eyes still hold the charm. Sweet. "With the release barely two weeks away; I have been practically living here, you know?" Yes, I see those bags that threaten to cloud the magic of his eyes.

Ever since the promos of Roadside Romeo went on air, Hansraj has been inundated with calls for interviews and promotional events. But the last-minute production work has kept him from obliging. The film will hit theatres on October 24.

As we stroll along the walkway of the manicured gardens, Hansraj narrates the genesis of the project. "I am an animation film buff, and Adi (producer Aditya Chpra) knows that. So when he planned a high-end animation film for Yash Raj Films, I was his first choice. Initially, I was only to write the script, but then he insisted that I direct it too," he says.

Roadside Romeo is the story of how Romeo, a pet dog in an affluent household, becomes a stray overnight when the family decides to shift out. Pampered all his life, Romeo feels helpless on the streets till he falls for Laila, a canine beauty, and then fights the local don, Anna Charlie. The voices to the characters have been lent by Saif Ali Khan, Kareena Kapoor and Javed Jaffery respectively.

"When I thought up the characters, I just knew Saif would fit best as Romeo is street smart and has style. Laila is a diva, and who else would've portrayed her better than Kareena?" says the actor, who was last seen as Sanjeev Mehta in Aaja Nachle. Jaffery was a natural choice for "he is a versatile actor and would sound great in animation".

Over tea, the debutante, like a pro, explains how the production work of an animation movie differs from that of a regular one. "An animation film is made backwards," he says. The dubbing happens first. The actors enact the dialogues during the recording, which is used as reference for expressions of the characters. Then begins the toil. "We spend months getting the expression in each frame right. A single change takes a week to be completed as the whole frame needs to be redone," he says.

The music has been catching on, I tell him. They cracked it all in 10 days flat, he boasts. "And, I've got Saif and Javed sing a hip hop number for it too!"

Roadside Romeo has kept the director busy and his acting plans, for now, are on hold "till something interesting comes up". Hansraj is still best remembered for his role in the iconic movie Masoom. But he does not mind it. "I am remembered for my good work. Why should I complain?" he asks.

A huge sigh escapes him as he watches the waiter carry the order to another table. He has been eating all his meals at the canteen of late, he complains. And what's his favourite dish from the kitchen? "Omelette sandwich," he grins. And does he have any pets? "Well, now I do." Touché.

The last memorable meal I had was in Mauritius, at a restaurant called Le Pescatore. For drinks, we had a South African red wine. I am a vegetarian so everything on the table was vegetarian. We had a Mezze platter for starters, followed by Grilled Aubergine with Ratatouille and mashed potatoes. We concluded the meal with chocolate fondue.

Heading: Catch ‘em if you can - Indian Express
Content:
Sujeonggwa

(Pronounced soo-jyong-wah)

Most of us are as familiar with Korean food as we are with black holes. Usually, it is thought that Korean food is synonymous with a vegetable dish called Kimchi. However, there's a popular concoction of the Koreans that deserves to be much loved. It is known as Sujeonggwa.

A traditional fruit punch, Sujeonggwa is a mildly hot, spicy and sweet beverage. It has distinct flavours of ginger and cinnamon. It is often served with pine nuts. Although earlier it was served at exclusively at special occasions like weddings, these days it is a must on Korean dessert menus.

It is also available extensively in canned form although there's nothing better than freshly made Sujeonggwa to end a whole Korean meal. Try the drink at India Jones, Trident.

Heading: Kidnap plot in Pune: Mumbai cops. Plot? What plot, ask Pune cops - Indian Express
Content:
There's time for little else when we have so much fish to fry

'Shellfish are the prime cause of the decline of morals and the adaptation of an extravagant lifestyle. Indeed of the whole realm of Nature the sea is in many ways the most harmful to the stomach, with its great variety of tasty fish.'

Pliny the Elder (AD 23-79)

Is there a better indoor activity than scooping out oysters from their comfortable beds and reaching out every now and then for a glass of Pinot? October is the perfect month for such hard work — there are plenty of holidays and more fresh seafood than you can dedicate your holiday to.

The fish markets in Mumbai cater very well to our appetite for seafood. From exotic crustaceans in wine to fried Bombay Ducks, there's all that a sea-foodie's dreams are made of. Truly, if it weren't for the sea, Mumbai wouldn't be such a food destination.

Wasabi at the Taj Mahal Hotel, Apollo Bunder, is the second seafood rich place in the city (the first is the ocean, of course). "I dine here as often as I can afford to eat and end up with my palate singing (and wallet stinging). Go for the delicate and subtle Chilean Sea Bass, Oyster Foie Gras, full-bodied flavoured Lobster Espice and Rock Shrimp Tempura. Superlative raw sliced fish 'Sashimi' and exquisite Maki and Nigiri Sushi. There are 28 varieties of fish," says food critic Rashmi Uday Singh. Another good name in Japanese food is Tetsuma where the Crab Harumaki, Prawn tempura and Scallops are dishes to go for on the menu.

Chef James Biaka of Tetsuma, counts the benefits of Japanese style seafood, saying, "Vitamins, proteins, no oil and style, Japanese food has all of it. Bite-sized servings are ideal for those who watch their weight. You don't have to wash your hands or rinse your mouth after a meal. Pickled ginger served with fish refreshes the mouth naturally."

Porcini Dusted Chilean Sea Bass in Turnip rice sauce and Spice rubbed tuna with clove reduction are great at gourmet magnet Indigo, Tiger prawn carpaccio with zucchini stew and coral sauce and Grouper fillet with potato timbale, oregano and a tomato reduction are excellent at Stax. At the seafood festival at Frangipani (Trident), dry marinades such as parmesan with rock salt and pickled lime are being used for seafood. Chef Prakash Pawakar says, "Apart from those, Indian marinades such as curry leaf, peppercorn and cumin are also an interesting feature."

The stretch between Fort and Colaba is fit for a seafood pilgrimage. The restaurants that continue to top our list year after year are Apoorva (for Prawn biryani, Tandoori crab), Trishna — anything, Mahesh Lunch Home (crab, squids), Café Leopold (Batter-fried prawns) andCafé Churchill (Tiger prawn in fire crack sauce and Fried fillet of fish). For home-style Goan food, Martin's and Gable's are quite good. Home to Chef Ananda Solomon's famous food is Konkan Café (Taj President). It is one place everyone must eat at to understand how good Mangalorean cooking is. Ditto for Trishna. Farzana Contractor attributes the discovery of Trishna to husband Behram Contractor. "It was the early '90s when we chanced upon this little place for fish curry and rice. Busybee then wrote about it. Its fortunes turned. The price of crab went from Rs 65 to Rs 2,000, such was the impact of his writing. Its clientele changed; from advertising junta to people like Imran Khan and Jemima Khan became patrons."

Heading: Plenty of buses to stadium, few board them - Indian Express
Content:
Crime branch says terrorists planned to abduct builder and jeweller to fund operations

The Mumbai police say the terrorists they have arrested planned to kidnap a builder and a jeweller from Pune. The Pune police say they have no idea of any such plot, even though the details emerged during the interrogation of two of the persons picked up from Pune.

The Mumbai police had seized anaesthetics from some of the arrested; a probe led to the unearthing of the plot. "This looks like one of the modes they were planning to fund their terror operations," said Rakesh Maria, joint commissioner of police (crime branch). "For 15 days early this year, they conducted a rece of the area where the two persons lived. The idea of holding people to ransom looks to have come from Riyaz Bhatkal as he has a background in crime," Maria added.

"The bulk of drugs and anaesthetics found is huge. One needs a prescription for the drug and we are probing the source of the drugs. While the media wing from Pune was learning hacking, this group was told to pick the two persons and hole them up at Ashoka Mews that the group had rented. The idea was to drug the hostages," Maria said.

He cited a "heavy police bandobast" as the reason for the failure of the plot. The Pune police, however, denied any police protection being provided to any builder or jeweller. "We have got no such report from the Mumbai police," said Pune Police Commissioner Satyapal Singh. "The joint commissioner of Mumbai crime branch has all the details."

Deputy Commissioner (special branch) Ravindra Sengaonkar, who is in charge of the bandobast section, too said, "I have got no inputs from Mumbai police." He too denied protection being provided to any builder of jeweler.

Intelligence agencies cited evidence that ransom was being looked at as a means to fund terror activities. When Kolkata shoemaker Parthapratim Roy Burman was kidnapped, part of the ransom was believed to have reached terror outfits via Aftab Ansari.

The Pune police crime branch, meanwhile, picked up a suspect from Raviwar Peth on Saturday and freed him after questioning. "It is not that we have started working now. Our operations have been going on for the last few months," said Additional Commissioner (crime) Rajender Singh.

Heading: ‘Fall’ into river: mother survives, children drown - Indian Express
Content:
The 200 buses set aside for Balewadi for the Commonwealth Youth Games by the Pune Mahanagar Parivahan Mahamandal Limited (PMPML) found few takers on the opening day on Sunday, with most spectators opting to use their own vehicles. On the other hand, commuters on other routes struggled to find buses.

"We were told by the organising committee 1,000 people would need public transport and we supplied 200 buses. We were fully prepared, perhaps over-prepared. But many buses ran empty," agreed S B Patil, PMPML chief.

The additional director general of the CYG organising committee, Ashok Kapoor, agreed. "Most people are using their own vehicles. The PMPML has told us that not many people are using their service. But it will take two-three days to assess the response," said Kapoor.

Buses on 16 routes headed towards Balewadi were diverted from the city's regular routes. No decision has been taken towards reducing the numbers of these buses on the closing day, despite the poor response.

PMPML authorities said that 50 of the 200 buses ran empty, while the rest had about 15-20 passengers on each run. On Monday the response was "nothing remarkable" and worse than Sunday, officials said.

Meanwhile, of the 19 CNG buses made available to PMPML for the CYG, six were used to ferry commuters between the parking stand and the stadium. The rest of were used on the other routes to Balewadi. "The CYG committee initially wanted 50 CNG buses between the parking lot and the stadium but we were working with six buses and it was enough," he said,

For the opening ceremony, the PMPML had earmarked 10 parking lots for 1,000 vehicles. However, with the exception of Swargate and Kothrud, the zones reported a poor response.

"Swargate parking lot can hold 100 vehicles and Kothrud 400. The rest of the zones did not see many vehicles parked," an official said.

Among the routes that saw poor response were Khadakwasla, Khadki Bazaar, Chandan Nagar routes and Shanipar.

Heading: President comes and leaves, villagers kept waiting - Indian Express
Content:
A five-year-old-boy and his four-year-old-sister were swept away in the river Pavna while their mother, who appears to have slipped and fallen with them on Monday, was rescued near Ravet-Punavle Bridge at Ravet.

Initially, it was thought that the woman, Savita Manikrao Late (30), had jumped from the bridge and that her son Tushar and daughter Vaishnavi had fallen. This was based on the account of a relative, Vinayak Anandrao Late, who said Savita had not been feeling well for the past few days and had jumped. However, police investigations later indicated that Savita had not jumped but slipped and fallen.

Sub-inspector Ashok Vanjari of Hinjewadi Police Station said, "Savita had gone to the temple at Ravet along with her children this morning after her husband had left for work. Initially we got information that Savita had jumped into the river. Now, it appears that Savita was walking around the temple along the banks of the river when she slipped and fell. Her children too slipped and drowned.

"People called the police control room. A fire brigade team was sent to the spot and Savita was rescued. The bodies of Tushar and Savita were fished out by professional swimmers," said Vanjari.

The incident occurred at 8.30 am; Tushar's body was not fished out till noon. Savita was taken to Talera hospital in Chinchwad and was discharged after first aid.

Hinjewadi police have registered a case of accidental death.

Heading: Beyond the field - Indian Express
Content:
Hundreds of villagers of Gawadewadi, 70 km from Pune, waited on Monday for Pratibha Patil. The President did arrive but the villagers could not even catch a glimpse amid tight police security and the absence of entry passes.

Only about 40 privileged ones from the village of 3,000 were allowed into the venue where the President addressed the people. It was otherwise overflowing with politicians from other parts of the state. Even some journalists were stranded outside the venue where the function was held to laud the efforts of the "model village" that has become self-sufficient. With the assistance of Vanarai, a Pune-based NGO, Gawadewadi has become a self-reliant village and received a number of awards.

Apart from the dignitaries, the hall was full of invitees, including office-bearers of local governing bodies. The villagers had spent days sprucing up the area and beautifying their houses. They returned home dejected.

Three Indian Air Force choppers, one with the President on board, landed at 10.45 sharp. But it blocked the view of the President and immediately after landing, the convoy left for a function. All the while, police officials kept driving the villagers away. Once the function was over, the President was rushed to the choppers and flown back at 12.45 pm.

Laxman Gawade, a villager, said, "We had been looking forward to the President's visit for long. It is disappointing that they did not allow even the villagers at the venue. We could not even get a glimpse of the President, as the police were restricting movements. They should have organised her speech in the open, which would have made all of us glad."

A woman waiting outside the venue said, "We were ready to receive the President and see her from close quarters. This was a golden opportunity to see her in person, but we were made to stand outside the venue, while office-bearers could easily go in." The only solace for some villagers was that some of the houses had televisions on which they could see the President giving her speech.

Vanarai president Mohan Dharia has apologised to the villagers.

Heading: Equipped to excel - Indian Express
Content:
In the city for CYG, Scottish sports minister Stewart Maxwell wishes to uphold sports as well as boost education, tourism and trade

The country has fostered some of the finest sportsperson like Andy Murray and displayed their sporting spirit through games of football, rugby and golf. With sports playing a prime role in its culture, team Scotland is all set to accrue experience and accreditations for its budding athletes in the Commonwealth Youth Games.

As children from the Hutchings High School cheer the Scottish athletes at the games, the Sports Minister Stewart Maxwell visited the School and conversed with the students on the Bond Forever project.

Communicating about CYG, Maxwell said, "This is a right platform where the young athletes will get to develop themselves to get more competitive for bigger games like the Olympics. I would be indeed happy if my athletes bag a few medals but at the same time this is an opportunity to get exposed to the diverse cultures, climatic conditions and many such challenges that a player faces when he competes away from his home. Along with upholding sports we also wish to boost education, tourism, trade and business through this visit. "

Maxwell feels that sports as a hobby or enjoyment is to be imbibed at a young age to help identify the talent in the children and also raise their self-esteem. "The National Sports Body in Scotland funds 134 million pounds to coach and sponsor athletes and 12 million pounds on sports in all the schools. India and Scotland have different strengths in diverse games that have to be appropriately invested. India, I believe along with a strong youth population has a huge untapped potential. It is now rising in the sports arena and will definitely put in substantially," adds Maxwell.

The students of Hutchings High School have adopted Scotland as their second team. The activity is intended to learn and bond with the players apart from heartening the team. "We have 44 members participating in nine sports. We all are delighted to visit India. It was a fantastic and colorful welcome at the opening ceremony with wonderful dances and music. It is inspirational to see the schools interacting with the countries. I would request these students and all the people to visit Scotland next year for our Homecoming Celebrations. The 10-month long celebration will host a variety of events portraying the various aspects of the country. We will further accentuate our bonds through this visit," added Maxwell.

Heading: High voltage - Indian Express
Content:
For Indian athletes, world-class training is at reach now, thanks to the advanced Sports Science Centre at Balewadi

A co-existence between human body and technology does not necessarily mean robots. Science and technological advancements have long been used to enhance the performance of sports persons. A perfect example of how technology can assist, enhance and better the performance of the athletes is the newly set-up Sports Science Centre (SSC) at the Commonwealth youth Games 2008 venue.

The most modern Sports Science Centre in India and the first-of-its-kind in Maharashtra, this centre is set with a vision to train Indian athletes using equipment of international standards. Some of the most fascinating equipment at the Sports Science Centre include Isokinetic machine that measures the strength of human muscles, VO2 max machine that measures in numbers the cardio respiratory capacity of the sportsmen, motion analysis centre and so on. What also adds the glam quotient to the centre is the modern-techno look of the machines. Dr D S Bhamare, head, SSC says, "These VO2 max machines will help us categorise the short listed athletes. Depending upon the cardio respiratory capacity of the heart, we can suggest the potential athletes which sports suits them better. The talent searching and screening process will thus become simpler."

After the screening, the most important aspect is training and the centre ensures that the candidates are trained for becoming the best. An important and state of the art section of the centre is the Low Oxygen chamber, a glass room that trains the athletes at the atmospheric conditions present at altitudes as high as 6000 meters. According to Dr Bhamare, "High altitude training is a must for training the sportpersons. The reason being that at such high altitudes, the pressure drops and Oxygen level is low. When the athletes get used to performing in these adverse conditions, their performance in normal conditions is much better. Also, The government of India spends over Rs 25 lakh on training the athletes at high altitudes, this amount will now be saved because we will be training the athletes for Commonwealth games as well as Olympics in this centre."

What adds excitement to the centre is the ice bath area. Dr Anand Gangwal says, "The research is still on as far as the effectiveness of the ice bath is concerned. This is useful when a fast recovery and immediate results are needed. When a player is tired and needs to perform immediately, an ice bath is advised." One of the most recent developments that is a part of SSC is EMG, meaning - Electro-myography. Similar to ECG, the EMG calculates the forces exerted by the muscles while performing. In Dr Bhamare's words, "This gives us information about which muscles are involved in a particular action. It also lets us know if any of the muscles are reacting slowly. The right word that describes the phenomenon is muscle firing and this is what the machine helps us know."

SSC, which is currently a part of the medical facility, will be operational after the games. The authorities are also planning to introduce a number of facilities like Sports physiology, nutrition, sports physiotherapy, sports psychology and so on. Well, if gold medals are the targets for the Olympics to come we can surely say, that we are well equipped for that!

PT Usha visits SSC

Sports icon PT Usha visited the Sports Science Centre (SSC) today. She was suffering from tennis elbow injury. Appreciating the centre, she said, "This is a world class place. I have visited many other centres like this but I feel that this is the most technologically advanced one. We are planning to come up with one such center in South India as well to help our players perform better." The athlete who recently suffered from tennis elbow said, "The event has come as a great opportunity for the athletes to practice for Olympics. And if we utilise it to thebest we will definitely prepare our players better for the Olympics."

Heading: The Regal Fashion - Indian Express
Content:
Jalebee Cartel goes the electronic way to win the hearts of music lovers

For sometime now, techno, trance, progressive dance music have all fused into one electronic blur. Repetitive rhythms, banal beats and missing melodies have made what's futuristic, stagnant. To think that variation would come, and how! To think that it would arise from India? Yet that is exactly what Jalebee Cartel has done in the past 3 years. Djs Ash, Arjun, G-Force and Ashwin have re-energised the phoren phenomena of electronic dance music by infusing it with a traditional twist. Loaded with laptops, tablas, guitars and synths they play God with the sonic spectrum. The booming bass, ethnic beats and fluid arpeggios defy categorisation.

In town for a performance at North Main Club, DJ Ash and DJ Arjun Vagale talk about their band, their music and some more. "Three of us (Arjun Vagale, Ashvin & myself) in the band have been dj-ing for a long time and we were always into Electronica. A lot of producers in India do Electronica but we just do it in a different way, our way!" quips Ash. "The music scene in India is really huge but electronica is on its way to explode, more and more people are opening their minds and accepting different styles of music, which works well for us!"

Everything, from their music, track titles to the band name has an unconventional and bizarre edge, one wonders what inspires them! "Each one of us in the band inspires the other! Our performances are very spontaneous, we don't prepare for it! I guess we just enjoy performing with each other. Every time we sit and work on a track we try out something different. Right now we are producing a lot of tech house and techno. It took us a while to discover our sound. You can call it IDM – intelligent dance music," ventures Arjun. Talking about their long-term goals and careers, they have just one simple wish, "We all want to just stick together and keep making music and performing in every part of the world. We are working on our album and our video is going to be out soon!"

After performances at France, Singapore and Dubai their success is evident by the huge international following that spins to their tracks, right from Argentina to Indonesia! The gig at North Main too, drew a full house. Every person present danced non-stop to the last beat of their music, with an enthusiasm that even the rains and a sudden power cut could not dampen.

So why did they choose Pune? Simply put, Pune chose us!

Heading: Words worth - Indian Express
Content:
Blending culture and couture, Damyanti Raje Bhonsle's new venture will offer designer labels, art collection and world music all under one roof

It's a totally newfangled endeavour for the lady who has till now concentrated her energies more towards empowerment issues. For this time round though, Damyanti Raje Bhonsle is launching herself into the designing sphere with her first designer store Araliya in the city. What makes the place more interesting is the fact that along with the twelve designer labels, the store will also accomodate cultural activities such as music, art and book reading.

Belonging to the erstwhile royal family, Bhonsle has embarked several initiatives at her hometown, Satara. "We undertake many activities through my charitable trust Nakshatra that mainly revolves around the women and children and concentrates on their economic independence, health, education and so on. Besides I also run a school called Satara Parents association School. Apart from doing my schooling from Nigeria, I have been travelling for work around the world for the last ten years. However with this store I deviate from my usual role and try my hands at style which I have been always fond of," adds Bhonsle who has a Masters Degree in human resource from the Tata Institute of Social Sciences.

Having pursued her graduation from St. Xavier's College in Mumbai, Bhonsle finds Pune more appealing. But Satara is where home is for the entrepreneur. "Although small, Satara is a beautiful place with a lot of talent. Pune for me is a big city and I have been very regular here for the last one year."

Elaborating more on her new venture,Bhonsle says, "Along with a collection of festive and western wear from designers like Rocky S, Shantanu, Nikhil and many more I am also launching Putumayo World music which is about familiarising people with world culture." Bhonsle says that it was the perpetual complaint she heard from puneites about the lack of designer wear in the city that led her to step into the realm. Well, given the rush there has been of late of designer labels tripping into the city, sure won't be long it seems when the drought gives way to an absolute flood of designer wear. More the merrier though.

Heading: College Bytes - Indian Express
Content:
For 60 years, Scrabble has managed to string together people from around the world

Form being a simple word game to a cultural icon, Scrabble has created history by upholding its magnificence for six decades. A popular birthday gift and a family favourite since 1948, Scrabble's meteoric rise began after an out-of-work architect Alfred Mosher Butts from Poughkeepsie, New York decided to invent a board game. He attempted to create a game that would use both chance and skill, by combining features of anagrams and crossword puzzles. Initially turned down by two companies because of the fear of lack of commercial potential, the game's journey has been one of the most fruitful

chapters in history.

In a world where the shelf life of a board game isn't more than two years, it is a huge achievement for Scrabble to have survived 60. "What has actually helped it survive is the edutainment value it generates and the group play it involves," says Rahul Bhowmik, head of marketing, Mattel Toys India. FYI, since 1994 it is Mattel that has taken over the manufacture of Scrabble outside of USA and UK.

To mark the 60th year, Hasbro games, (owner of Scrabble in USA) launched the diamond anniversary edition game. From the sleek folding case to the two slide-and-store trays, there has never been a more convenient way to enjoy a game.

As a popular board game of all time, Scrabble has had a large impact on the Indian pop culture scene. Mattel is conducting quizzes on Scrabble's history and the Scrabble Association of India (SAI) has held a national tournament to celebrate the game's success. "It is not merely about word power today. It is a memory game which requires learning superfluous words," says Udayan Grover, committee member and Scrabble player, adding, "We have a tournament coming up next month in Pune which will part of the celebration. Also, a new committee has been established to bring about a few altercations."

The game instills healthy competition and has been a favourite with cricket commentator Gautam Bhimani as well. "I reckon playing it from the age of 10. It was an exercise to form newer words that are not just superficial but genuine. During your formative years it is the best way to build your vocabulary." While it was a convenient way to spend time with friends, to make it more interesting, a few conditions were added. For instance, forming words related to cricket; like bat, ball, stump, pitch and so on. Retired english teacher Dorothy Mascarenhas, swears by the game and encourages parents to gift their children a set each. "While the best way to improve your English is read good books, Scrabble comes a close second."

While it is essentially a team game, played by two to four people, celebrity make-up artist Clint Fernandes at times plays it all by himself using two sets. "It is my favourite hobby and it jogs my mind a bit. Recently, I bought the

Hasbro online version of the game, which I can travel with anywhere I want," he smiles. Prior to this, many have launched online versions of the game, the most popular being Scrabulous.com launched by the Agarwalla brothers, Jayant and Rajat. "But none have been able to compete with the original," says Bhowmik.

Heading: Trek file - Indian Express
Content:
Seminar on economy wreck

The CFA Council (A constituent of ICFAI University) had organised a seminar on 'The Wall Street Crisis- Its impact on Global Financial Market' at MCCIA, Senapati Bapat Road on October 4. Naac visit to Indira College
