Heading: Go back to villages, President tells youth - Indian Express
Content:
Alumni of Nowrosjee Wadia College, Rajeev Baheti, Sanjay Jandial and Abhijeet Ubhe paid a victorious visit to Nachiket Tal while the college celebrated its platinum jubliee

When the going gets tough the tough gets going. The troika of Rajeev Baheti, Sanjay Jandial and Abhijeet Ubhe seems to have imbibed this spirit in their lives to the deepest core. The gorges of death and unknown pitfalls fail to deter them from scaling great heights, which happens to be just a hobby for them.

These three intrepid mountaineers have made Puneites proud by successfully finishing their 15-day expedition to the Kedar Glacier and Nachiket tal in the Gharwal Himalayas after braving life threatening challenges. Alumni of Nowrosjee Wadia College, undertook the expedition at a time when their alma mater is celebrating its platinum jubilee. While Baheti, 53 and Jandial, 45, have been trekking since college days, Ubhe, 31, fell in love with the sport since his school days. "My initial practice sessions in trekking started in Lonavla when I was still in school." reminisces Ubhe. The threesomes have enjoyed each other's companionship in innumerable trekking expeditions.

Talking about their latest expedition Baheti, the team leader who has a been a student of geology, says "We had to face myriad difficulties all through the expedition specially in the Gangotri valley. While climbing the Kedar glacier, heavy snowfall and rains greeted us all through the way and our return journey down the glacier saw us fighting against blizzards and the fact that we three survived all this has to be attributed to divine intervention."

Recalling his past experience, Baheti highlighted some changes that have taken place there. "The nature is definitely is in its best, however, pollutions and greedy motives of humans have not left it untouched. In past 15 years, I have noticed that Rishikesh , which was once beautiful and clean, is now covered with smoke (pollution) if seen from a bird's eye view. Apart from this, smuggling of medicinal herbs is affecting the locals as they depend mainly on herbs for treatment."

After successfully climbing 14,700ft in the Kedar glacier, the team's next stop was Nachiket Tal (8200 ft), which is surrounded by dense forests of Pine trees.

"Throughout the expedition we used to receive day to day weather reports from the Indian meterological department , Pune which gave us a lot of assistance" says Ubhe who hails from a family of trek lovers.

However the trio also wanted to make minute observations of the global warming effect on the glaciers but the unfavourable weather conditions ruined their plans. This team of adventure lovers has many feathers to its cap. While Baheti and Jandial have successfully climbed Rudugaira, Koteshwar, Thelu, Baby Shivling and Matri glacier, Ubhe has Meru glacier adorning his list of mountaineering expeditions.

"We go on trekking expeditions almost every year and Sundays are booked for our practice sessions at Sinhgad fort. Although the sport involves a lot of risk but the thrill and adventure that accompanies it is irresistible. In fact it teaches you to face all difficulties in life," concludes Baheti.

Heading: E-books facility at BoM library - Indian Express
Content:
Appealing the educated youths to go back to villages, President Pratibha Patil on Monday said, "Until and unless the rural economy gets a lift, the inclusive development of the country is not possible, as the heart of India still throbs in villages." She, however, expressed concerns over the rising unemployment and decreasing foodgrain production in the country.

Patil was speaking during her two-hour long visit to Gawadewadi, a village located on Pune-Nashik Road. She had come to see the development of the village, as it had become a self-reliant village through the efforts of Vanarai, a Pune-based NGO.

She said, "Almost 60 per cent population is dependent upon agriculture. When we think of the country as a whole, we find that the production of foodgrain is not increasing. The climate change is taking its toll. After getting independence, it was considered that the coming generations would become educated, which would bring a revolution. However, after getting educated, these youths preferred to settle down in cities. But now, if we want to sustain our culture, we need to strengthen the rural sector."

Dwelling on the issue of women empowerment, the president said, "Half of our total population consists of women. Therefore, empowering the women is like empowering the economy, politics and all spheres of life."

Governor S C Jamir, Devisingh Shekhawat, husband of the President, Vanarai president Mohan Dharia, Water Resources Minister Ajit Pawar, Energy and Higher Education Minister Dilip Walse-Pati, MP Shivajirao Adhalrao-Patil were present on the occasion.

Heading: Unity runs an extra mile for CYG - Indian Express
Content:
Allen C A Pereira, chairman and managing director, Bank of Maharashtra inaugurated the E-books facility at Prof V G Kale Library recently.

The library is located at Head Office, 'Lokmangal', 1501, Shivajinagar. With this facility now members can read educational CDs on the computers provided at Bank's library. On the occasion, Mahasaraswati Pooja was performed by B K Piparaiya, general manager, Planning.

To inculcate a healthy saving habit right in the early age, BoM has recently introduced 'Mahasaraswati' scheme. Under this scheme students can save regularly in small amounts and make it a large deposit over the period. This scheme is open for students who have attained the age of ten years and above. Free accident insurance cover of Rs. 50,000 is available under the scheme. The students will get preferential treatment in education loan with concession of 0.25% in rate of interest. In case beneficiary hails from the Below Poverty Line (BPL) family, concession would be 0.50%, stated a press release.

Prof. V.G. Kale Library was founded in 1978 and is named after the first Chairman of the Bank - the late Prof. V.G. Kale, a well known economist of the country. The library is open to all. Students above 10th standard, bankers, entrepreneurs and general public can obtain membership free of charge. Educational & Reference CD/DVDs are available. The CD/DVDs are particularly useful for students of 10th & 12th Standard of CBSE, ICSE & Maharashtra Board.

The library is well equipped with latest books on Banking, Management, Foreign exchange, Human Resource Management, Economics, Risk Management, Investment, Information Technology, Accountancy, Law etc.

Some special features worth mentioning are:

* All text books & reference books for10th Standard, 12th Standard & above

* Text & reference books for Engineering

* Books for various competitive examinations like CET, GRE, TOFFEL, GATE, CAT, UPSC, MPSC etc. along with CAIIB/JAIIB and promotional examinations are also available.

* The library has also good collection of reference books viz Encyclopedia Britannica, World Book Encyclopedia, Encyclopedia of Management and Information Technology, Columbia Encyclopedia etc.

* More than 100 periodicals/journals on various subjects are being subscribed.

* E-books & educational CD/DVDs.

Heading: Marvel Isola to come up at NIBM Road - Indian Express
Content:
Unity Infraprojects ran an extra mile to create a record by completing the construction of an eco-friendly five-star hotel complex at Balewadi, for Third Commonwelath Youth Games, in just 12 months against heavy odds.

"In normal course, it would have taken six to eight months to finalise the design and complete formalities before construction on a five-star hotel starts," said K K Avarsekar, CMD of Unity Infraprojects Limited at a press conference held

"But, we managed to complete the challenging task of building the world class facilities for hosting participants from over 70 countries in one single location and an environment friendly, zero-garbage hotel with five star and three-star facilities."

"When I look back, I am overwhelmed with emotions that this Rs 300 cr edifice with 600,000 sq ft area is up, ready and running," he said.

"Many in Pune and elsewhere thought that we were made to take up the project since no one could imagine that the project of this size could be ready in a year. That did not deter us. We mobilised men and machinery to ensure that the pride of Maharashtra and India does not get dented for want of accommodation for CYG," Avarsekar said.

Had the accommodation not been ready as stipulated by the games officials, the venue would have shifted and the State would have earned a bad name. "I did not want that to happen as I am patriotic citizen," said Avarsekar.

The project faced many hurdles like the tremendous shortage of workers in the wake of the agitation against migrant labour and a Public Interest Litigation. Unity floated an SPV for the project and roped in well known hotelier cum environmentalist Vithal Kamat as a partner and operator for the eco-friendly, zero-garbage hotel.

The JV appointed M/s. Renowned Architects Upasni Design Cell for the design of the hotel project. Prof M GGadgil, head - structural engineering department, VJTI was the proof checking consultants.

Heading: Apna Loan ties up with Reliance Money - Indian Express
Content:

Vishwajeet Jhavar, CEO, Marvel Realtors said Marvel Realtors has created a benchmarking of high-quality luxurious living. Even today, when market sentiments are being talked to be on a shaky side, all of our projects are on track, he said.

Heading: Now, Lavale villagers have toilets, thanks to NSS students - Indian Express
Content:

Heading: Towering concern over health hazard prompts citizens to revolt - Indian Express
Content:
It is only 10 kilometres from Aundh, and is very close to the sprawling campus of the Symbiosis International University; but a sizeble population of this 1,100-household strong Lavale village resort to open defecation, because they do not have toilets. Now, there is something to be happy about as the students of College of Agriculture, Pune, who they have hosted as part of the college's National Service Scheme (NSS) programme have started the primary works for building toilets in the village.

"The students were here to encourage villagers to build toilets in their families and to create awareness on eradicating open defecation. We found that there is lack of awareness among the people. Students enacted a play to spread awareness and also talked to individual families. During the time spent here between September 24 and October 2, they dug 47 pits around which toilet blocks will be constructed soon," said B R Ulmekh, associate dean, College of Agriculture.

On October 2, these pits were handed over to the village for them to build toilets on it to achieve 100 per cent implementation of the Nirmal Gram Yojna, a government scheme that promotes toilets in every family. The villagers here are optimistic about achieving this target in the next two months. At present, the village already has 700 toilets; but about 400 families defecate in the open.

"During the monsoon, a lot of people fall ill because of the spread of diseases due to open defecation. The camp is definitely going to help the village in spreading awareness and eradicating open defecation," said Sobha Satar, a gram sevak of the village panchayat.

According to the deputy sarpanch, Dondhiba Tukaram Kedari, most of the forty Dalit families in the basti have built their own toilets. A handful does not own one because they can't afford to build one. Now, we are spreading awareness about the various government subsidies available for the construction of toilets, he said.

A good toilet in this village will cost around Rs 15,000. But a simple toilet block with a soak pit would cost around Rs 3,000 to Rs 4,000, while a safety tank pit would cost a little more and require more water as well, said Kedari. "Some people, however, resist building a toilet because of a mental block," he added. For some, this mental resistance was due to traditional beliefs and for others it was lack of awareness. Students had to deal with people such as devotees of Shiva, who preferred open defecation because the shape of the commode resembled the shiva linga, people who can't afford to build a toilet and aged people who would rather prefer to use the traditional defecation method out of habit.

For the NSS, this was a concerted way to mark their 40 th anniversary. NSS was first initiated on September 24, 1969. "Between September 24 and October 2, 1,012 such camps were held across the state, where students spread awareness through plays about total sanitation and toilet blocks in villages. It was also to mark the International Cleanliness Year 2008," said M S Jambhule, assistant program coordinator, NSS.

Heading: At CYG, foreign athletes experience the bliss of yoga - Indian Express
Content:
A day after angry residents of Sector 16 of Raje Shivajinagar, Chikhli, brought down a half constructed mobile tower belonging to Reliance, the residents are not willing to relent and in fact have vowed to fight the battle out in the court if need arises.

The incident occurred on Sunday, when a group of people led by Corporator Mauli Jadhav entered the premises of the house of Rajendra Shinde and hunted off the labourers working on the construction of the mobile tower and toppled over the half constructed tower.

When asked about the incident president of the Pimpri-Chinchwad Property Holders Association Uday Patil said, "We had found out about the ill effects of the high frequency radio waves and their effects on human life. So we have been opposing the tower construction from the beginning. According to a recent Supreme Court ruling, the construction of such mobile towers have been banned at places like schools and hospitals owing to the health hazards posed by the radio waves. If towers cause health hazards then how are they constructing a tower in a residential area like ours?"

The whole incident sparked off controversy about a year ago when the telecom company started the construction of the tower at Shinde's place. The residents of the area claimed that the tower was a health hazard because of the emission of high frequency radio waves. They had also lodged a complaint with the police but with little effect as they gave Shinde the clean chit to go ahead with the construction.

Speaking about the entire issue, Shinde said, "There are 22,000 mobile towers in the city and to this day no one has been affected by any radio frequency waves or anything. No one has died because of it. I do not understand why people have a problem with the tower being constructed over my house. People came and beat the workers and caused a lot of losses to the materials here. Who will repay these losses?"

Corporator Mauli Jadhav, Seema Patil, Archana Karle, Shrda Ingle, Ujwala Babar and others led the agitation on Sunday. Jadhav said, "We had written to the police as well as to Pradhikaran but they did not do anything. That is why the residents of the area had to go up in arms against the construction. As of now, the work has been suspended there, but if they resume work we will strongly oppose it." He also said, "We did not hurt anyone nor did we cause any damage to the property. We only asked the labourers working there to leave the site."

"The radio waves have been known to cause damage over extended period of exposure, according to doctors around the world. We have filed an RTI application to know how Shinde was given the permission to construct the tower in a residential place in the fist place. After getting it we are going to take a legal course," Patil said.

When contacted, a Reliance official said, "We are not authorised to give any statements or make any comments about the situation. Whatever the decision of the company is, we will let you know though the proper spokesperson."

Heading: Jewellery worth Rs 16 lakh stolen from bungalow - Indian Express
Content:
The grand display of culture and tradition that the Commonwealth Youth Games began with is not limited only to the opening ceremony. Along with a traditional welcome and the Indian hospitality, what has also been offered to the foreign athletes here are Yogic exercises.

Explaining the motive behind the Yoga classes that have been taking place at the venue, Suresh Jadhav, Yoga teacher, Patanjali Yoga Samitee said, "We have been conducting Yoga classes twice a day-6 am to 7.30 am and 5 pm to 6.30 pm. The foreign athletes are well-versed with the physical training part of it but what separate a winner from a loser are the concentration levels. We will be training them for increasing the concentration levels during this seven-day training session. These techniques have been designed by Ramdev baba and he will be personally training the athletes on October 17."

Designed specifically to meet the requirements of the athletes, the yogic training consists of eight types of pranayams, seven subtle exercises and nine asanas. It also consists of training the sportsmen on omkar and breathing exercises.

Swapna Pednekar, a Yoga teacher said, "We have received a wonderful response from the athletes. There have been a number of them who have heard about Yogic exercises but not experienced. In fact, a couple of them also came and informed us that they have learnt Yoga from a guru in Germany. This way we are sharing with them the true culture of India."

Though flexibility is not a challenge with athletes, most athletes find doing asanas like padmasan, vajrasan and paschimottanasan challenging as it involves sitting on ground. According to Jamie Peterkin, coach, Team St Lucia, "I have learnt yoga in my own country but the kind of exercises that we are doing here are pure. The pranayam techniques are wonderful and I am planning to make all my athletes do this."

What has also come as a surprise for most of them is the power of breathing. Nataly Regis, coach, Team Grenada said, "We had heard about yoga before, but this is the first time that we realised that each finger represents one of the five elements of the nature. We were also unaware of the fact that inhaling and exhaling means so much to our concentration levels and that cells in the body can be activated using breathing techniques."

Esau Simpson, swimmer, Team Grenada, who got introduced to yoga for the first time said, "I felt the peace after doing these exercises. I am planning to continue with the exercises for the entire week."

Heading: Two killed as dumper falls into quarry - Indian Express
Content:
Diamond and gold ornaments worth Rs 16 lakh and Rs 2 lakh in cash were stolen from a bungalow at Chandrikar Society in Bibewadi. The police said that the incident would have occurred on either of the two days— October 11 or October 13. Satyanarayan Agrawal (38), the owner of the bungalow has lodged a complaint with the Sahakarnagar police station on Monday.

The thieves broke the lock on the main gate of the bungalow using a cutter. They also broke the lock of the bedroom door in the fourth floor and stole diamond and gold jewellery and cash.

Agrawal is a businessman. He owns a warehouse at Wagholi. Assistant Police Inspector AA Jagdale is investigating the case.

Heading: DP for Baner-Balewadi: Activists meet CM - Indian Express
Content:
In yet another case of reckless driving, a dumper fell into a quarry filled with water near the Kanifnath Mandir, in Moshi claiming two lives. The incident occurred around 7.30 pm on Saturday.

The deceased have been identified as Kishore Mohite (21) and Moinuddin Kulsumbh. Driver of the truck Ganesh Mohite(30) escaped with injuries.

Blaming Ganesh for the accident, Kishore's father Narayan Mohite lodged an FIR against him at the Vishrantwadi Police Station.

The police have arrested Ganesh. Both Kishore and Moinuddin were residents of Pathardi Taluka, Ahmednagar while Ganesh is a resident of Kilbill Chal, in Moshi.

Heading: Central committee gives clean chit to Buddha govt - Indian Express
Content:
A delegation of Green Pune Movement (GPM), an association of social activists, met Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh on Sunday to register their protest against the changes in the proposed Development Plan (DP) for Baner-Balewadi even as it continues to conduct awareness drive for the registration of objections and suggestions to the plan.

"Chief Minister assured that the state government will not make any changes in the biodiversity reservation in the proposed DP," Aneeta Benninger, Director of Centre for Development Studies and Activities (CDSA) said.

She said that the civic administration has allegedly submitted wrong maps of the DP draft submitted to the state government for approval.

"We had served a legal notice to the Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) in 2005. The civic administration had admitted that it was due to a mistake and will be corrected," Benninger said.

Meanwhile, the Green Pune Movement would carry on with its awareness campaign and provide guidance to register their suggestion and objections. The Green Pune Movement has also demanded a public hearing for the same and transparency in the process.

Heading: Bengal gears up to welcome another automobile company - Indian Express
Content:
The CPM central committee on Monday endorsed the strategy adopted by the party's West Bengal unit to handle the Singur crisis. It also approved Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee's decision of not applying force to suppress the protest launched by the Trinammol Congress.

Central committee member Shyamal Chakraborty slammed Mamata Banerjee and criticised Governor Gopalkrishna Gandhi for their handling of the Singur crisis.

Reacting to the Trinamool chief's claim that in the forthcoming Lok Sabha elections CPM will get no seat, Chakraborty said, "We will get 40 seats. Banerjee is going to Delhi but Congress is a sinking ship." She played the spoilsport by opposing the Nano factory, he added.

Regarding the Governor's role in Singur, Chakraborty said: "He is the friend, philosopher and guide of the Trinamool Congress."

During the party's state committee meeting a few days ago, some leaders like Amitava Nandi and Tarit Topadar had felt that the state government could have handled the protest firmly by removing squatters on the Durgapur Expressway. Others, however, felt that such an action might have helped the Trinamool instigate violence at the Nano factory site and create a Nandigram-like situation.

On Monday, the central committee disapproved the view that the government should have used force to quell the protest launched by Mamata Banerjee. The committee expressed its satisfaction over the way the state party unit handled the Singur situation.

Party sources said there was no doubt that the Tatas had left Singur because of the Trinamool's protest. "Our government had tried its best to convince Mamata Banerjee but she was adamant from the very beginning and organised her protest in such a manner that forced the Tatas to quit Singur."

Application of force by our government to suppress her protest could have worsened the situation, added the source.

A senior CPM leader said: "For the last two months, Banerjee had been maintaining close rapport with Gujarat Chief Minister Narendra Modi. She was also making an irrational demand of returning land from within the Nano factory's premises. Now the Tatas have left our state and rushed to Gujarat."

The central committee also explored possibilities of developing alliances with secular forces in different states to counter the Congress and the BJP.

The CPM is planning to finalise its list of candidates for the forthcoming Lok Sabha polls and formulate its campaign strategy by November.

Heading: Mamata receives threat call - Indian Express
Content:
Barely one week after Tata Motors pulled out its Nano project from Singur, the West Bengal government has roped in another automobile company to set up a plant in the state.

This was reiterated by Transport and Sports Minister Subhas Chakrabarty, who had revealed this information to a private TV channel on Sunday.

"The MoU will be signed between the company and the state government before October 30. The decision has been taken both at the political and administrative level. And the company which is coming to Singur is aware of all the developments there," the minister told the media on Monday at his office at Writers' Buildings.

He, however, did not reveal the name of the company that was coming to Singur to replace the Tatas.

Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee, meanwhile, on Monday flew to Delhi to put forward her demand of returning land to those Singur farmers who did not receive compensation for their land. Banerjee is scheduled to meet President Pratibha Patil and Prime Minister Manmohan Singh.

On Monday, a 12-member delegation of the Save Nano Committee, that was formed in Singur to bring the project back home, met Governor Gopalkrishna Gandhi and handed over a memorandum containing their demands.

The willing farmers and those associated with the Nano factory demanded that the Governor intervene and coax the Tatas to come back to Singur. "We pleaded that thousands would lose their livelihood if the Tatas did not return," said Udayan Das, president of the committee.

Das claimed the Governor had promised to talk with the state government as well as the opposition party to sort out the problem.

Earlier, members of the committee held a rally at Rani Rashmoni road at Chowringhee. They came in 52 buses and demanded that the state government take steps to start the Nano factory soon. They came to Writers' Buildings and met the CA of the chief minister.

"We brought the agitation to Kolkata so that our voices could be heard," said Das.

Heading: Holed up in city for years, Bangla criminal held near Buddha’s house - Indian Express
Content:
At a time when there is heightened tension between the CPM and the Trinamool over the Singur issue, Mamata Banerjee allegedly received a threat call on Monday.

The call was received by a leader of the Trinamool medical cell, Majhi, around 1.45 pm on Monday when several Trinamool leaders were seated at the office-cum-residence of Banerjee. According to Majhi, an anonymous caller cursed Banerjee and even threatened her with dire consequences. Another call came on the same number at 2.10 pm.

Banerjee was in Delhi to meet the President and the Prime Minister over the Singur issue. Sources in the police said that it was not clear whether the second call was made by the same person. A complaint was lodged at the Kalighat police station by the Trinamool. "The caller ID attached to the phone in Banerjee's office showed that the call originated from a local booth," said a police officer.

"We have initiated a probe into the matter," said Rajesh Suborno, Deputy Commissioner (South). Trinamool leaders, however, refused o comment on the matter.

Heading: Dasmunsi back to hospital; Cong in a fix - Indian Express
Content:
The Special Task Force of the Kolkata Police on Monday arrested one Subrata Bayen or Fateh Ali of Bangladesh, who is wanted in several criminal as well as terrorist activities in the neighbouring country, including a grenade attack on an Awami League rally in 2005 that had left 24 dead.

He was picked up from a house on Palm Avenue, very near to Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee's home.

Police officers said Bayen had built his crime dossier funding terrorist organisations and dealing in arms in Southeast Asia-acts that had catapulted him to the Interpol's 'most-wanted' list. The Interpol had put out a lookout notice for him in 2005.

The police sniffed Bayen was hiding in Kolkata, and might have settled here as early as in 2005, soon after the grenade attack on Awami League leader Sheikh Hasina's political gathering. Bayen is among the 23 Bangladeshi criminals who have crossed into Bengal and Tripura in recent years, intelligence reports indicate. The Interpol had alerted the Central Bureau of Investigation about this list in June, 2007.

The force's special additional commissioner Rajeev Kumar said: "We had reports that Bayen had been to China a few days ago. He came back to India via Nepal." Bayen, having changed his name from Fateh Ali, had also purchased a property on Palm Avenue, now on rent.

On Monday morning, when the police rounded him up, Bayen had made attempts to throw off the force, pleading he was a trader.

But he soon cracked under interrogation, and confessed his hand in several cases, including murder, extortion, kidnap and other crimes in Bangladesh, police sources said. He was produced before the Alipore court and remanded in police custody for two weeks. Bayen was born in Barishal, officers said, and grew up under political patronage. He had also been sentenced to a life in prison by a lower court in 1991.

A thorough search of Bayen's home threw up 27 SIM cards of various countries and also a pistol. A senior officer said: "Since Bayen was not involved in criminal activities in Bengal, we have booked him under the Foreigners Act and Section 25(1B) of the Arms Act."

Bayen is not the first Bangladeshi to be caught from Bengal. Earlier, Tanvir-ul Islam alias Joy was arrested from his hideout in Kaikhali, near Dum Dum. Both Bayen and Tanvir are said to have been involved in the 2005 grenade attack. Intelligence reports also state that many of those in 'hiding' here are into profitable business, mostly legal. Bayen's arrest has prised open chinks in the police's armour, sources said. Questions are being raised how a wanted criminal, sitting pretty on the Interpol's list, can change his name and stay in Kolkata, manipulate his gang in Dhaka from here and also buy a house on the chief minister's lane?

Heading: Charu Market violence: accused produced in court - Indian Express
Content:
West Bengal Pradesh Congress Committee president Priya Ranjan Dasmunsi's recent hospitalisation — the second time in three months — seems to have left the state unit of the party in a limbo. Party leaders are, however, tight-lipped about an alternative leadership for the party's Parliamentary election campaign in the event of a protracted illness of Dasmunsi.

Subrata Mukherjee, who had rubbed Dasmunsi the wrong way and was reprimanded for joining Trinamool chief Mamata Banerjee on stage in Singur, stressed that an alternative leadership of the Pradesh Congress Committee was out of the question at the moment.

"We are all praying that Priya babu gets well soon. At the moment, we are not thinking about replacing him. If such a situation arises, the decision will be taken by the party high command in New Delhi," Mukherjee said.

Congress leader Manas Bhuniya, who was enroute to the airport to board a flight to New Delhi, said: "This is not the time to talk about an alternative leadership. We are confident that Dasmunsi will return hale and hearty soon."

In July, Dasmunsi had complained of chest pain at a party meeting in Malda and was moved to the Malda circuit house for treatment. Thereafter, on his way to attend another meeting, he had to be admitted to a medical facility in North Dinajpur district headquarters Raiganj. Later, he was airlifted to Bihar from where a BSF chopper brought him to the city. He underwent primary angioplasty at a private hospital in Kolkata.

In West Bengal, the party is on the backfoot as never before. With apparently no reaction by the party, either for or against a number of issues that have made headlines in the state, party insiders expressed apprehension that the party would be without a strong issue-based plank in the run-up to the general elections.

"The Congress has had almost no role to play in the land acquisition imbroglio. With Pranab Mukherjee too busy at the national level, Dasmunsi is the only other important Congress leader in the state. However, his illness has created doubts about a strong election campaign in the minds of many partymen," sources said.

With senior leader Somen Mitra leaving the party, the Congress has already lost a significant number of party supporters to the Trinamool Congress. The Trinamool has accused the party of being hand-in-glove with the ruling CPM while the latter has termed the Congress as the former's mouthpiece.

Heading: Rizwanur case: SC asks High Court to complete hearing; family appeals against bail to cops - Indian Express
Content:
Swarup Biswas, younger brother of MLA Arup Biswas, who was arrested in connection with the Charu Market violence, was produced at the Alipur police court on Monday.

This is the third time when Swarup was produced in court after his arrest. Earlier, the court had remanded him to two days of police custody. But soon after hearing the judgment, he fell sick and was admitted to SSKM Hospital. Swarup will be produced in court again on Wednesday. Swarup was arrested on October 8 on charges of attacking the police and ransacking the Charu Market police station on October 4. The police said he led a mob, which attacked the police personnel at the station.

On the evening of October 4, a bus had overturned near the charu market injuring a number of passengers. But soon a mob gathered at the accident site and started pelting stones and setting police vehicles on fire. A group of youths also barged into the Charu Market police station and injured 21 officers, including two deputy commissioners. Rapid action Force had to be called in to control the situation. The police rounded up 29 people, including Biswas, on October 5 and charged them with arson, assaulting policemen and rioting.

After Biswas was remanded to police custody today, trinamool supporters led by his brother Arup Biswas, alleged that the police were acting on behalf of the CPM. They said the people behind the incident were roaming free on the streets.

Heading: Khejuri bandh peaceful - Indian Express
Content:
The Supreme Court directed the Calcutta High Court on Monday to complete the hearing in the Rizwanur Rehman case as early as possible. An appeal against the HC order, filed by the accused in the case, is pending before a Division Bench headed by the Chief Justice of the Calcutta High Court.

The apex court also ordered that trial in the sessions court should not start during the pendency of the appeal.

Kalyan Banerjee, counsel of the Rehman family, told The Indian Express, "The Supreme Court had earlier refused to stay the CBI probe. After Monday's order, apart from the trial, other proceedings can take place."

Justice Dipankar Dutta had directed the CBI on August 14 to file a chargesheet against the accused policemen and members of Todi family and observed that the police officers had acted in unconstitutional and illegal manner. The order was challenged by Ashok Todi and the police officers before a Division Bench headed by Chief Justice S S Nijjar.

While the Division Bench allowed the CBI on September 19 to file chargesheets against the accused, the appeal challenging the order was pending before the Bench. Then Todi moved the Supreme Court seeking a stay on the CBI probe but the petition was rejected.

The Rehman family, meanwhile, filed a petition in the High Court on Monday challenging the interim bail granted to the three police officers— Ajay Kumar, Sukanti Chakraborty and Krishnendu Das. The trio had surrendered before the CBI court on September 30 and the court had remanded them in judicial custody. But the next day, the sessions court magistrate in the Bankshall court had granted them an interim bail.

The Rehman family argued that the magistrate was not empowered to grant the interim bail. The police officers could have influenced the witnesses of the case. The case is likely to come up for hearing on October 16.

Heading: Silence rules Calcutta Stock Exchange - Indian Express
Content:
The 12-hour bandh called by the CPM in Khejuri on Monday to protest against the attack on its supporters last week passed off peacefully. The protesters blocked the Digha-Mecheda Road for more than an hour leading to traffic snarls. No violence was reported during the bandh.

Khejuri, situated near Nandigram, had reported several clashes during the Nandigram violence.

The district administration did not take any chance on Monday and a huge police force was deployed in the area. Additional forces were deployed in the sensitive areas. On Wednesday, two CPM supporters were allegedly beaten up by Trinamool men in Khejuri Block II.

CPM supporters took out processions in different parts of both the blocks against the terror unleashed by the Trinamool. Shops and business establishments remained closed till 4 pm.

East Midnapore Superintendent of Police Ashok Prasad said: "The bandh passed off peacefully."

Himanshu Das, CPM district committee member, claimed that the locals had supported the bandh.

In a related development, both CPM and the Trinamool leaders have claimed that there were incidents of firing at Ranichak, Satengabari and Jambari Sunday night. Each blamed the other for the incidents.

The police, however, denied having any knowledge of this. "We have no reports of firing at any village of Khejuri last night," Prasad said. The administration is keeping a close watch over the area keeping in mind the incidents in Nandigram in the recent past.

Heading: 75 children escape death in Malda fire - Indian Express
Content:
It's the silence which rules all three trading floors of the Calcutta Stock Exchange. Phones have stopped ringing and adding to the gloom is a power cut. Ensconced in their cubicles, traders stare listlessly at the flickering figures on their computer screens. The mood swings from stoic to somber.

The CSE-40 index, which closed on Friday at 5021.12 points after a fall of over 742 points, declined further on Monday by another 328.89 points only to close at 4692.23. And the signs are evident. At the traders' cubicle, almost everybody refused to be quoted and many scorned at the mention of Finance Minister P Chidambaram's speech.

"The measures being taken now should have come six months ago. Investors have suffered terribly. Many of us are selling our apartments and cars to meet the lack of liquidity," said Dhanraj, an investor.

"If everything would have been normal, do you think we'd have had the time to even talk to you? The fault lies with heavy premiums on IPOs allowed by the SEBI. Offering a Rs 10 share for Rs 500 or more has also contributed to this situation," added another investor.

Outside the CSE building, brokers and investors were standing in groups sipping tea and exchanging information on the latest downfall in the prices of their shares. "Even after the market stabilises, it will be virtually impossible to take it to its previous position any time soon. There's no money to invest further and loans are not available in any form," said an investor.

Heading: Teachers unhappy over academic parameters fixed by pay panel - Indian Express
Content:
Around 75 children admitted to the paediatric ward of the Malda District Hospital had a narrow escape, after a fire broke out on the hospital premises early this morning. The children were saved from asphyxiation with hospital staff taking prompt action, senior medical officers said.

Malda Chief Medical Officer (Health), Dr R Banik, said the fire broke out on the ground floor of the hospital around 4 am.

"There were some spare mattresses stored in the ground floor. We suspect the blaze was set off by someone carelessly throwing a lighted bidi or a cigarette stub. Luckily, the paediatric ward was on the second floor, which gave us time to take action", he said.

With smoke rapidly filling the paediatric ward, the hospital staff resorted to breaking down the locked terrace door and evacuating the children to the terrace.

"Simultaneously, we broke the panes of some windows in the ward to create ventilation for the smoke to clear. None of the children suffered adversely due to the smoke. The fire service personnel arrived in the meantime and put out the blaze. Now the children are back in the ward," Banik said.

The incident once again brings highlights the poor level of maintenance at government-run district hospitals. Last week, around 25 infants aged below one year had died over a period of three days at the Behrampore Sadar Hospital due to the lack of staff and infrastructure.

Several doctors were said to have gone on festival leave, while the limited capacity of the paediatric ward there could not accommodate the heavy rush brought in by the outbreak of viral pneumonia.

Heading: Shortage of coal results in powercuts - Indian Express
Content:
After the G K Chaddha Pay Revision Committee of the University Grants Commission recommended a massive hike in the salary of college and university teachers, various teachers' organisation across the country had hailed the recommendation as pathbreaking. But as the recommendation report is being discussed by the Human Resource Development Ministry, the academic parameters fixed by the committee to avail a third promotion is drawing resistance from them.

"The aim of the pay review committee was to make the teaching career attractive and challenging," said a member of the pay review committee.

However, the All India Federation of University College Teachers Organisation (AIFUCTO), one of largest teachers' organisations in the country is against the mandatory qualification of having a PhD for getting the third promotion.

According to the recommendations, the existing five tier structure of promotions should be replaced by a three tier set up and only candidates having PhDs should be entitled for the third promotion.

"Denial of the third promotion to a section of college teachers will be unjust, as Central and state government employees get a minimum of three assured promotions during their careers," said Asok Burman, general secretary of AIFUCTO.

Of all the university and college teachers across the country, only 15-20 per cent teachers have PhDs.

Teachers are also insisting that promotions in the case of senior associate professors should be made more "honourable". According to the committee recommendations, teachers are also required to submit a number of articles published in noted journals for promotions. The teachers' organisations also want the implementation of pay band 4 for selection grade lecturers and lecturers in the existing set up. The West Bengal College University Teachers Association and

Jadavpur University Teachers' Association have also supported the view of AIFUCTO.

Heading: Suspicion, hatred led septuagenarian to murder wife - Indian Express
Content:
The power situation in the state remained grim on Monday, as a number of power-generating units remained closed and the Santhaldih plant was still not operational.

Power department officials claimed that there was a shortage of coal for power generation. "Because of the shortage of coal in the plant, one unit each of Bandel and Sagardighi has been closed for the last few days," said Sunil Mitra, power secretary. He also said thermal power plants at Kolaghat, Bakreswar, and Bandel are being operated below their capacity, except during peak hours, in order to keep the stock of coal above the critical level till the coal supply becomes normal.

Mitra said that coal producers have ensured that there would be a steady supply of coal within the next couple of days. "Ten rakes of coal have reached the different power plants today. Another 11 rakes are expected to reach by Tuesday," he said.

Heading: KMC lacks data on city’s vector breeding zones - Indian Express
Content:
Rashbehari Pal (79) had been suspicious of his wife Minu (65) ever since they got married in 1965. The suspicion had been so much that love never managed to blossom between the couple. The story had a tragic ending on Sunday, when overpowered by his hatred for his wife, Pal murdered her.

"On Saturday, there was an altercation between the two and Pal killed his wife on Sunday morning in a fit of rage," said police. The old man, who is in police custody since Sunday, showed no signs of remorse.

"During interrogation, Pal claimed that he was tortured by his wife. He also accused her of having several extramarital relationships," said a police officer of Jorabagan police station.

Police said he reportedly told them, "She was unfaithful to me." There seemed to be a sense of relief in Pal, said the officer.

The house at 56 Nimtala Ghat Street, meanwhile, remained closed to outsiders even on Monday, with no one willing to explain why Pal killed his wife. One of their daughters, who lived nearby, was present in the house on Monday.

Pal never had a job and used to do business occasionally. He, therefore, never had a steady income, which was apparently another reason for the fights between the couple. "There used to be altercations between my parents since a long time," said Kakoli Dam, who said she often had to interfere to sort things out.

Kakoli was also present in the house on Saturday evening, when her parents had another heated argument. Kakoli and her husband intervened to resolve the issue, and went home.

Pal, however, was not to be pacified, and he murdered his wife the next morning.

Heading: Sister Nirmala in Orissa to give healing touch - Indian Express
Content:
At a time, when several vector-borne diseases like malignant malaria, dengue and Japanese Encephalitis are claming lives, the Kolkata Municipal Corporation does not have a quality data on their breeding zones in the city.

The Project Management Unit of the civic body, which prepares Geographical Information System (GIS) survey maps of KMC areas, has rapped the Health Department for not providing information about areas prone to various kinds of vectors.

"We had prepared maps of the vector prone wards of the city in 2005, but they were never updated since then. We only need to feed specific data into the system to know the vector prone areas at a click of the mouse. The GIS mapping system could have helped the Health Department to carry out anti-larval measures in a more systematic way to prevent the outbreak of dengue and malignant malaria," said a civic official.

Tata Consultancy Services, consultant for the GIS mapping programme has, meanwhile, approached government departments to add specific information into the GIS system. "Had the Health Department asked the consultant to add the entomological map in the GIS system, we would have given special attention to the vector prone areas," a senior civic body official said.

Heading: Commercialisation eats into traditional charm of Laksmi Puja - Indian Express
Content:
Disturbed by the violence against the Christian community in Orissa, the superior general of the Missionaries of Charity, Sister Nirmala, is on an extended tour of Janla and Bhubaneswar.

Out of the charity's 18 centres in Orissa, two located at Phulbani in Kandhamal district, were completely destroyed in the communal violence.

"The Missionaries of Charity had a centre in Phulbani called Sukhananda, where we used to run courses for girls. Some of them were even staying at the centre. When the violence broke out on August 30, 16 girls and four nuns were at the centre," said Sister Suma, regional superior of the Missionaries of Charity.

She added that apprehending violence, all the residents of the centre fled to a nearby forest. "They got in touch with me and now they are safe in the G Udaygiri camp," she said.

The fate of other centres run by the Missionaries of Charity in Phulbani and Srasananda was no different.

The centres catered to the patients of leprosy, tuberculosis and other communicable diseases. The centre in Kandhamal district used to provide free health care services to nearly 33 patients.

On October 2, Sister Nirmala had left for Orissa and her first stop was the regional centre at Bhubaneswar.

From Bhubaneswar she went to Janla where the charity has a leprosy centre. Nearly 350 people from violence-torn areas have taken refuge in the centre. "Sister Nirmala is here with us. Everyday she meets people and tries to motivate them. We have not visited Kandamal as it is not advisable for us to do so now," Sister Suma said.

This is Sister Nirmala's second visit to Orissa in the last two months. She has also written to Prime Minister Manmohan Singh expressing concern over the continued violence in the state.

In his reply to her letter, Singh said that the Centre is monitoring the situation in Orissa.

Heading: CM woos Muslims, seeks probe into Delhi encounter - Indian Express
Content:
While the city may be all set for Laksmi Puja on Tuesday, there are many who are not happy, as the essence of tradition is gradually getting lost in the shadow of the new-age celebrations.

With time being a rare commodity for the people of the state today, the elaborate rituals and traditions have given way to fast, time-saving methods to perform the puja. The old-timers lament the disappearance of the traditional methods and rituals from the puja, and also the fact that the rituals, that were once a bigger celebration than the puja itself, have now faded into oblivion.

The homely rituals that once formed an essential part of Laksmi puja celebrations are now being increasingly outsourced to save time for the fast-paced generation. Be it the narkel nadus, alponas, or even garlands made of plastic for the deity, the essential constituents for Laksmi puja are easily available at the nearest market. People prefer to shell out money and purchase these goods, rather than go the elaborate, traditional way to worship the Goddess of wealth.

"I remember waking up early in the morning to bathe and help my mother with the alponas. These days we simply pick up the plastic ones available at the market. Today's hectic lifestyle leaves one with little time to spend on making alponas. Sometimes I feel it's a miracle that we manage to even perform the puja at home," said Malabika Biswas, a resident of Padmapukur.

Laksmi puja was a time that saw grandmothers rolling out batches of sticky narkel nadus. These days, however, that ritual seems to have disappeared completely, with nadus being easily available in packets in most sweetshops.

In fact, making nadus and selling them in sealed packets has become a source of income for many families living in the fringes of the city.

For Deepak Chatterjee, a resident of Bangur, the biggest loss to the Laksmi Puja celebrations is the commercialisation of the traditional boats made out of banana plant and filled with grains, which form an important part of the ritual.

"Today the boats are easily available in the market. It was such a traditional thing to make these at home but no one really has the time now. Today the puja may be performed at home, but nothing else is homemade," rued Chatterjee.

Ironically, the flower garlands — an integral part of the ceremony — are also losing their charm, with most people picking up garlands from the market in bulk.

Some even opt for plastic garlands, but no one makes them at home.

Heading: Maya clips wings of her trusted lieutenant - Indian Express
Content:
Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Mayawati wooed Muslims by seeking a probe in Jamia Nagar encounter and announcing several schemes for the community during the BSP convention on the "Problems of Muslim community: its causes and solutions" on Monday. Prominent Muslim clerics, who attended the meeting, however, raised issues like lack of legal defence for terror suspects, arrest of innocent Muslims, growing sense of insecurity in the community and harassment of Muslims in Azamgarh.

Mayawati told the gathering that she has written a letter to the Prime Minister requesting him to resolve the controversy over the Jamia Nagar encounter. "Doubts among the Muslim community over the incident must be removed," she said.

The chief minister said the Muslim Community was feeling a sense of insecurity in the country. "No action will be taken against anyone in Uttar Pradesh without concrete evidence regarding involvement in terror cases," said the BSP chief.

She also attacked the Congress over the nuclear deal and its failure to act on the Sachar Committee report. 

Shia cleric Kalbe Jawwad said: "While the killers of Mahatama Gandhi and Indira Gandhi could defend their cases, it seemed Muslims have no right to live and they can't even contest their cases." The cleric advocated constitution of a committee comprising non-government Muslims (Gair Sarkari Musalman) to look into the cases of terrorism. He demanded adequate representation of Muslims in police force and making Urdu compulsory up to high school. He also said he wished to see Mayawati as Prime Minister of the country.

The Naib Imam of Lucknow's Aishgah Idgah and All India Muslim Personal Law Board Member Khalid Rashid Farangi Mahali said innocent Muslims are being taken into custody in the name of terrorism and Madrasas are seen with suspicion. He asked the government to deploy honest officers in Azamgarh. Referring to Gorakhpur MP Yogi Aditya Nath, he said Muslims in various parts of Eastern UP are living under fear and Islam has nothing to do with terrorism.

Blaming the Centre for terrorism in the country, Mayawati said the root cause of terrorism was the failure of the Central government to secure borders of the country. The CM also announced the constitution of a special cell headed by BSP general secretary Satish Chandra Mishra to review the progress of the schemes announced by her government for minorities.

She announced to set up an Arabic-Persian University and a Unani Directorate in Lucknow soon and said her government has already earmarked Rs 10 crore for this.

She also announced various government measures including launching of employment scheme for minorities, setting up of a Rs 4 crore coaching centre for IAS and IPS aspirants from the minority community in Lucknow, opening of 964 primary schools, 1,212 high schools, 58 government secondary schools and appointment of Urdu teachers in Muslims-dominated districts. The government has also decided to increase the annual grant for Urdu Academy from Rs 1.5 crore to Rs 3 crore.

Heading: Conventions for OBCs and Sarvajana Samaj - Indian Express
Content:
When Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) national president Mayawati became Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh in May last year, the first thing she did was to change the government's Transaction of Business Rules to accommodate her most trusted lieutenant Shashank Shekhar Singh as Cabinet Secretary. One and half years later, however, she has clipped his wings.

On Sunday night, the chief minister promoted Principal Secretary ( Information) V S Pandey to the post of Additional Cabinet Secretary. She also ordered that the other principal secretaries in the Chief Minister's Office would report to Pandey.

Till now, they used to report to the Cabinet Secretary. Though Singh refused to comment on the issue, there seemed to be general consensus in the bureaucratic circles that Singh had been cut to size.

When Mayawati had appointed Singh as the first ever Cabinet Secretary of the state, she also made him the administrative head, a position that till then belonged to the Chief Secretary. This had caused much resentment in the bureaucracy.

Though the IAS officers of the state did not protest against the move, a PIL was filed by a lawyer in the Supreme Court pleading that Singh's appointment be quashed. The petition had argued that the appointment was unconstitutional and violated the cadre rules.

Subsequently, the state government again amended the Business Rules and restored the position of the chief secretary as the head of the administration.

It, however, was only a cosmetic change and did not affect the administrative functioning. A senior IAS officer said: "Even after Singh had ceased to be the administrative head, he kept calling the shots and principal secretaries at the CMO continued to report to him, who held regular meetings of officials."

After Sunday night's order, "he is neither the administrative head nor can he summon the principal secretaries who will now report to Pandey," remarked an officer. Singh is the last man left from the team of officers who were brought in the CMO soon after Mayawati became chief minister. One by one, all of them have been shown the door. Shailesh Krishna, Rohit Randan, V N Garg, Anup Chandra Pandey and V K Sharma — were all part of the chief minister's trusted brigade.

Heading: Bajrang Dal to campaign for temple: Togadia - Indian Express
Content:
It is not the Muslim community alone, which is being wooed by the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP). Eyeing the Parliament elections, the target list of the ruling party includes Other Backward Castes (OBCs) and Sarvajan Samaj. National conventions of these communities are going to take place in the state capital soon.

Sources confirmed that BSP national president Mayawati had ordered officials to gather information relating to work done by her government in different sectors for these communities.

Separate booklets are being prepared for each community to be distributed among the prominent people of the community in the same way as was done in Monday's convention of Muslims.

The details being gathered are not only from the present term of Mayawati but right from her first term as Chief Minister of Uttar Pardesh in 1995-96. The booklets have department-wise description of all schemes along with details of projects completed and money spent.

Similar details of her other two terms - from 1997 to 1998 and from 2002 to 2003— have been collected and the draft is being readied by officers.

Explaining the need for organising such conventions, party state president Swami Prasad Maurya said: "SC/STs are already with the BSP and now we are trying to bring in all those who are not in our fold through our Bhaichara committees."

Heading: HC orders status quo on Rae Bareli land - Indian Express
Content:
The firebrand leader of Vishwa Hindu Parishad, Praveen Togadia said Bajrang Dal will launch a nationwide campaign for the construction of Ram temple at the disputed site of Ayodhya from next month.

Addressing a gathering on 25th year of the foundation day of Bajrang Dal, Togadia said, "Hindus will no longer have to wait for the Ram Temple as the movement will take its final shape by November with the beginning of Parikrama Mela in Ayodhya."

Later he told the media that preparations are on across the country by Hindu activists for the movement.

"VHP wants to create a blazing atmosphere in favour of Hindutva for which training camps are going on in different parts of the country," he added.

He said three thousand youths and several retired government officers as full timer VHP activists and nearly one lakh Bajrang Dal workers are fully prepared for the final battle.

VHP has started a seven-day training camp at Ayodhya for Bajrang Dal activists. "VHP is planning to organise a major event on the 6 December, the sixteenth anniversary of Babri mosque demolition," Togadia added.

Heading: Now, no plots from LDA, only highrises - Indian Express
Content:
A day after the Uttar Pradesh Government decided to withdraw 189.25 hectares of land it had given for the proposed rail coach factory at Lalganj in Rae Bareli, the Lucknow Bench of the Allahabad High Court on Monday ordered status quo in the matter.

The Bench consisting of Justice Pradeep Kant and Justice S Hasnain passed the order on a petition filed by the Railway Ministry and a PIL filed by two villagers — Dinesh Chandra Mishra of Ahar village and Avindra Pandey of Balemau village.

The Bench, however, refused to stay the state government's order of October 11, by which it had taken back the land from the Railways. Next hearing is fixed for October 22.

Interestingly, the opposing litigants had different takes on the issue. While counsel of the villagers, Mohammad Arif Khan claimed that the status quo meant the land would remain in the possession of the Railways, chief standing counsel of the state government, Devendra Upadhyay claimed the status quo meant that the land would remain with the Gram Sabha.

During the hearing, the court asked the state government to present facts on the basis of which it had cancelled the land allocation. The state government gave an undertaking that it will not allocate the land to anyone and there will be no construction on the land. Following which, the court ordered the status quo.

Railways adamant, goes ahead with project

Though the UP government has taken back the land it had given for the proposed rail coach factory at Rae Bareli, the Railways are going ahead with acquisition of the additional land they had identified for the project.

On Monday, the Railways carried out a ten-page advertisement in local newspapers, inviting applications for acquiring 543 hectares of land.  

A Northern Railway official said the only land they had received was the one given by the UP government but the project required more land, which belonged to local farmers. "After conducting surveys and consulting the farmers, we are planning to pay compensation at around Rs 4.65 lakh per acre and employment to at least one member of nearly 1,600 families in the area," said the officer.

He said in spite of the UP government's action, they were determined to go ahead with the project. If the UP government did not agree, they would acquire the land from the villagers, he said.

Heading: BSP leader arrested for attempted rape - Indian Express
Content:
From now on, the Lucknow Development Authority (LDA) will not develop residential plots. It will only construct highrise apartments to accommodate the growing population of the state capital. It will also develop a railway overbridge from Sahara Sahar to

Gomti Nagar. The LDA Board approved these proposals on Monday.

LDA officials said the board has taken this decision because there were hundreds of plots in areas like Gomti Nagar, where construction has not been carried out even 20-25 years after allotments.

"Those who purchased the plots, did it for investment purpose only, they were not needy persons. If they genuinely need a house, they will purchase our flats that will ensure quality services," said LDA Vice-Chairman Mukesh Kumar Meshram after the board's meeting. He said the cost of flats in apartments developed by the LDA will be 40 per cent less than those developed by private builders.

"To ensure quality development, help of engineering institutions would be taken as third party. Even the allottees will be able to check the quality of construction," he said.

In another decision, a four-lane 700-metre-long overbridge will be constructed to approach the Gomti Nagar Extension. The overbridge, which will be built at an estimated cost of Rs 50 crore, will start from the entrance gate of Sahara Sahar.

Meshram said as the overbridge will be in public interest, Sahara Sahar authorities have agreed to this proposal and an MoU will be signed between both parties soon.

To authorise the construction of a police chowki on Gomti embankment adjacent to the Ambedkar Memorial, the LDA Board has given approval to change the land use of 900-sq m area, from the road to public utilities and services. A 950-m stretch behind the police chowki will be developed as road and green area. Meshram said park and pathways will be developed there.

The board also decided to develop the 80-acre land of a regional park (Smriti Upwan) as Kanshiram Sanskritik Sthal, at a cost of Rs 90 crore — to organise cultural programmes.

The LDA will charge an amount of Rs 50,000 for public functions. But in case of functions organised to observe national festivals, concession could be given, Meshram added.

Delhi Metro gets nod to prepare report

LDA Board gave its go head to Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) to prepare the detailed project report (DPR) for Metro rail transport in Lucknow. DMRC has already completed feasibility study of Lucknow for this project. It has proposed to develop East-West and North-South corridors to connect all four corners of the city with Metro rail.

The Centre and UP government will pay Rs 4 crore to the DMRC for preparing the DPR in nine months. The 27 km-long North-South corridor will connect Amausi Airport with Musnhipulia.

Another14-Km East-West corridor will start from Gomti Nagar to reach Rajajaipiarm.

Heading: SMS campaign spews venom against Joshi in Varanasi - Indian Express
Content:
A BSP leader, Ganga Singh Kushwaha, was arrested on Monday for attempting to rape a woman in Beheta Bujurg village under Ghatampur police station. Singh, the BSP general secretary for Bithoor Assembly seat, has denied the charge.

Rajendra Sharma, the woman's husband, said Singh had visited his house on Saturday night and asked him to call a villager, Devi Prasad. When he went out, Singh tried to rape his wife at gunpoint.

Hearing her cries, neighbours rushed in but Singh tried to browbeat them. Angry villagers thrashed him and he took shelter in the house of BSP legislator Ram Prakash Kushwaha.

The villagers pelted stones at the legislator's residence and tried to set Singh's motorcycle on fire.    

Locals said Singh and his wife Gayatri, a former Zila Panchayat member, tried to pacify Sharma on Sunday but did not succeed. Sharma lodged a complaint with the police.

Refuting the charges, Singh said: "I had given a loan to Sharma and had gone to his house to recover the amount. Sharma had made a false allegation against me to avoid  the payment."

The BSP legislator denied having any knowledge about the incident. He said, "A inquiry will be set up and action will be taken against the guilty."

Superintendent of Police (Kanpur Rural) Lal Bahadur said, "Some incidents of violence were reported in the village on Saturday evening but peace has been restored since then." A case has been registered and investigations are on, he added.

Heading: Police say suicide case closed; kin rubbish theory - Indian Express
Content:
Ganga Mahasabha, a Varanasi-based social organisation, has launched a campaign against senior Bharatiya Janata Party leader and former Union minister Murli Manohar Joshi, who is likely to contest Lok Sabha elections from the city.

The Mahasabha that runs the 'save Ganga' programme has been circulating several SMS across the city that carry slogans like Joshi bhagao, Banaras bachao, with a rider: 'if you want to save the city and Ganga ma, forward this message to 11 people.'

The campaign comes on the heels of BJP's Vijay Sankalp rally on October 18, when Joshi is expected to address the public.

The Mahasabha claims that they have sent their message through SMS to a sizeable number of people.

Acharya Jeetendra, an official of the Mahasabha, said they are opposing Joshi because he is not committed to the cause of Ganga.

"We have heard Murli Mahohar Joshi's offensive comments on Tehri dam.

We don't want to accept anyone who has no respect for the lifeline of the city," he said.

The acharya added, "We cannot prevent any party from announcing their candidate, but we can always tell the public about him." Though the campaign has been suspended at present, the Mahasabha claims that it would be resumed soon.

City Mayor Kaushalendra Singh, a BJP member, said the party has taken serious note of the hate campaign. "This propaganda is being undertaken by people who are against the development of Varanasi. We have managed to stop the campaign but some people are still propagating it," he added.

Advani, Joshi to address rally in the city

Continuing with their plan to carry the Vijay Sankalp rally  across the state, senior BJP leaders Lal Krishna Advani and Murli Manohar Joshi will address the rally in Varanasi on October 18. UP election coordinator Kalraj Mishra, state president Ramapati Ram Tripathi and leaders like Vinay Katiyar and O P Singh will also address the gathering. According to party coordinator Swatantra Dev Singh, the rally is being organised to reveal the truth behind rising inflation and increasing terror activities in the country.

Heading: Medical Education Secretary inspects CSMMU - Indian Express
Content:
The suicide theory put forth by the police in the case of a youth's body found in the home of a BSP legislator is being contradicted not only by relatives of the deceased, Amit Mishra, but also by the policemen.

Senior Superintendent of Police Akhil Kumar said the suicide note has not been sent to experts for verification.

On the other hand, Baliram Saroj, Station Officer of the Hussainganj, where the FIR was lodged, said: "The handwriting has been verified. The note was written by the victim and the case is almost closed and a final report will be filed soon."

Refuting the police claim, Mishra's cousin, Vipul Mishra said, "The well-written note was too neat to be of the boy who had studied only up to Class III."

Mishra's uncle Rajkumar said: "The police have never taken any specimen handwriting of my nephew. They also never verified his signature with his bank account or any other authentic document. How can they claim that the note was written by him?"

On September 9, the body of Mishra was recovered from the Royal Hotel, Vidhan Sabha Marg residence of Danpur MLA, Sushil Kumar. Mishra's hands were tied and the police claimed to have found a suicide note from the spot.

Vipul Mishra said, "The suicide note shows him to be a resident of Sitapur but our entire family is settled in Lakhimpur-Kheri. In fact, he had never been to Sitapur."

Asked why the case was not sent to the Crime Branch Criminal Investigation Department (CB CID), the SSP said, "Since inquiry by the CB CID involves formalities and takes time to begin, we decided to carry out investigation at our level."

Claiming that Mishra's suicide was fallout of his love for a girl, Saroj said, "He killed himself because the girl he wanted to marry had declined to marry him. His call details show that he had spoken to the girl before committing suicide."

Rajkumar, however, said, "He did not own a mobile phone and used to call us from a PCO."

Mishra's relatives had lodged an FIR but it did not name any accused.

Heading: Wanted UP cops are at work, but police say can’t find them - Indian Express
Content:
The Kolkata Police's Special Task Force (STF) on Monday arrested Subrata Bayen alias Fateh Ali, a Bangladeshi "terrorist", believed to be involved in several crimes in that country, including the grenade attack on a rally of Awami League leader and former Bangladesh prime minister Sheikh Hasina that left 24 dead.

He was arrested from his house at Palm Avenue, close to the residence of Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee.

On Interpol's most wanted list, Bayen is accused of funding terrorist organisations and arms dealing in South East Asia, apart from the 2005 attack on Hasina's rally. He is believed to have fled Bangladesh after the attack.

Bayen's name, in fact, is part of the list of 23 Bangladeshi criminals who, according to Intelligence reports, took shelter in West Bengal and Tripura after the Bangladesh Police launched a massive manhunt for them.

Many of the fugitive dons like Bayen have started their own businesses in West Bengal and are owners of bheris (large fish ponds) or transport companies.

"We have reports that Bayen went to China a few days ago to expand his business and he came back to India via Nepal," said Rajeev Kumar, Special Additional Commissioner, STF. After STF men raided his house today, Bayen initially claimed he was a trader, but reportedly confessed later to being involved in several cases in Bangladesh, including murder, extortion and kidnapping. He has been remanded to police custody for two weeks.

Heading: Bring it on - Indian Express
Content:
For the last two years, Uttar Pradesh police have been searching high and low for two of their men wanted for an alleged fake encounter in 2003 in Sonbhadra district in the state's southeastern corner. The police seem to have looked everywhere — except among their own ranks.

For, the men — both of whom have been declared absconders by the court and have had their properties attached — have been working all this while, marking their attendance, participating in police parades, drawing salaries, and even facing disciplinary action for alleged negligence at work.

Sub-Inspector Kamleshwar Pratap Singh was in charge of Berana outpost in Allahabad until recently, when he was suspended for negligence in a murder case.

Sub-Inspector Jai Nath Mishra is attached to the Mirzapur district police. He too is under suspension.

Additional Director-General (Law and Order) Brij Lal told The Indian Express he wasn't aware that the two wanted S-Is were on the rolls of the police. "I will look into the matter and find out", he said.

Senior Superintendent of Police, Allahabad, Lalji Shukla, Kamleshwar Pratap Singh's boss, said he had come to know that "Singh is wanted in a case, but I have to cross-check details".

A senior officer of Mirzapur confirmed that Mishra is posted in the district. "He was transferred from Sonbhadra to Mirzapur while under suspension", the officer said.

Singh and Mishra were part of a police team that shot dead two people in Rungtola forest in Sonbhadra district on September 2, 2003, saying they were gangsters involved in a highway robbery that had taken place the day before. The two alleged highway robbers, however, turned out to be Prabhat Kumar Srivastava and Rama Shankar Shahu, both residents of Jharkhand's Garwa district adjoining Sonbhadra. There were allegations of foul play, and Srivastava's father, Lallan Prasad, a retired schoolteacher from Garwa, demanded an inquiry.

After the inquiry found the encounter had been fake and the policemen were chargesheeted, all involved cops turned themselves in, except Singh and Mishra.

Heading: EU warns youth: turn your MP3 players down! - Indian Express
Content:
The students from Leeds Metropolitan University, UK get hands on practice, while volunteering for CYG

Amongst thousands of volunteers playing a part of 'Team Pune' at the CYG 2008, a group of 25 foreign students have come down from the United Kingdom to be a part of the volunteering team. They are students of the Leeds Metropolitan University (LMU), UK, who say that this event is not only a part of their annual curriculum but also an enriching and learning experience.

The students are divided in three groups, namely - workforce – to supervise the other volunteers, media help – to guide the media on the various venues of the games and the games operation centre – to co-ordinate with the senior officials of the games. These students are pursuing their bachelors degree at the university in various fields like sports development, sports management, public psychology, sports marketing, public relations and so on. "This mega sports event held in Pune will give the students an experience overseas. Apart from this they also get to witness a land of culture and education," says David Braham, director of international development LMU. Earlier these students who volunteered in events like IFFA awards are experiencing a sports event for the first time. "This is our first encounter with any sports event. Before coming to Pune for the CYG we were working with Snehalaya and the Sanjay Nagar project in Ahmednagar," adds Braham.

"International Games like CYG gives them a true exposure. Before we get the students we train them in various aspects like understanding the psychology of the people of the country we go to, creating a network for communicating at the event, how to mix up with the other volunteers and so on. This is like a practical experience of what is taught in books," says David Jackson, director of international development, sports faculty, LMU Carangid.

The university has entered as educational partners with commonwealth games. "The experience at CYG 2008 will provide the opportunity for contributing to major international sport events that have great significance. Also, this is like a preparatory mode on testing grounds for the Commonwealth Games in Delhi in 2010 where we would be volunteering on a greater scale," says Jayashree Raghuram, manager of LMU Delhi branch.

"I was very excited when I was informed about my selection. It was a great opportunity to come down to the cultural city of Pune. I would be visiting various tourist places once the games are over. It is a very beautiful city and the sports complex is very well built," says 22-year-old Esther Crane, an event management student of the university.

"I am working on the venues and coordinating with the staff. I am looking forward to visit tourist places in the city if time permits," says 21-year-old Michelle Jhonston a graphic and event design student. Tehmina Hussain, a 21-year-old, who is studying sports development and physical education says, "This event will help me know how things work and I will get practical experience to understand things better like how to manage a crowd, how media works alongside the event, what are the requirements during the event and so on."

Heading: Luxury mall showcases wealth gap in India - Indian Express
Content:
Millions of youngsters across Europe could suffer permanent hearing loss after five years if they listen to MP3 players at too high a volume for more than five hours a week, EU scientists warned Monday.

The scientists' study, requested by the European Commission, attacked the concept of "leisure noise," saying children and teenagers should be protected from increasingly high sound levels – with loud mobile phones also coming in for criticism.

"There has been increasing concern about exposure from the new generation of personal music players which can reproduce sounds at very high volumes without loss of quality," the Commission, the EU's executive arm, said in a statement.

"Risk for hearing damage depends on sound level and exposure time," it said. More and more young people were exposed to the significant threat that leisure noise posed to hearing, it said.

Commission experts estimate that between 50 and 100 million people listen to portable music players on a daily basis.

If they listened for only five hours a week at more than 89 decibels, they would already exceed EU limits for noise allowed in the workplace, they said. But if they listened for longer periods, they risked permanent hearing loss after five years.

The scientists calculated the number of people in that risk category at between five and 10 per cent of listeners, meaning up to 10 million people in the European Union.

Sales of personal music players have soared in EU countries in recent years, particularly of MP3 players.

Commission experts estimate unit sales between 184 and 246 million for all portable audio devices just over the last four years, of which MP3 players range between 124 and 165 million.

Mobile phones used at excessive volume also came under fire from Meglena Kuneva, the EU's consumer affairs commissioner.

"I am concerned that so many young people ... who are frequent users of personal music players and mobile phones at high acoustic levels, may be unknowingly damaging their hearing irrevocably," she said in the statement.

Heading: Money and fame await Booker prize winner - Indian Express
Content:
With gold-plated ceilings, exotic fountains and the clink of champagne glasses, the Emporio Mall in New Delhi is the perfect place to wile away a hot afternoon browsing through designer boutiques.

The mall, adorned with palms and scented with lavender, is the exclusive playground of India's rich, which despite the effects of the credit crisis still have plenty of cash to buy designer accessories with thousand dollar price tags.
