Heading: Is that Kim Jong Il? - Indian Express
Content:
Iraq's Prime Minister said the 4,100 British troops in southern Iraq are no longer necessary to provide security, a newspaper reported on Monday.

Prime Minister Nouri al-Maliki told The Times of London that there may be a need for a few British troops to remain for training and technical issues. But as a fighting force, al-Maliki said the British were no longer needed.

"Definitely, the presence of this number of British soldiers is no longer necessary. We thank them for the role they have played, but I think that their stay is not necessary for maintaining security and control," al-Maliki said in the interview.

"There might be a need for their expertise in training and some technical issues, yes, but as a fighting force, I do not think it is necessary," he said.

His comments were in line with an August report that most of Britain's contingent in Iraq would be withdrawn over the next nine months, leaving only a few hundred soldiers there.

In July, Prime Minister Gordon Brown promised a major troop withdrawal in the early months of 2009, but Britain's military has said it's premature to discuss specific figures.

Al-Maliki also expressed disappointment with the British performance during last spring's fighting in the southern city of Basra.

"The British forces withdrew from the confrontation from inside the city to the area of the airport," he said. "They stayed away from the confrontation, which gave the gangs and the militias the chance to control the city."

The British military turned over provincial control of Basra to the Iraqi Government in late December despite vicious infighting between Shiite factions and widespread militia infiltration of the local security forces. But British troops remained on standby at their airport base outside the city, 550 km southeast of Baghdad.

Heading: Genome mapping to find out why Pandas are sex-shy - Indian Express
Content:
The 66-year-old man in the photos appeared the picture of health, full of vigor despite reports he underwent brain surgery less than two months ago.

He was surrounded by serious, crisply uniformed soldiers and in the background there was plenty of verdant greenery, more reminiscent of summer than mid-autumn in a temperate clime.

To seasoned North Korea watchers, the country's weekend release of photos of leader Kim Jong Il for the first time since the middle of August are raising a host of questions about his health - as well as the motive and timing behind their publication. The images came less than a day before the United States on Saturday removed North Korea from Washington's terrorism blacklist, dousing rising tensions over North Korea's nuclear development.

Kim had disappeared from public view in mid-August, just when Pyongyang stopped dismantling its nuclear program in anger with the United States over its refusal to delist the North, a long coveted demand of the country's communist regime.

"They didn't appear to have been taken recently," Kim Yong-hyun, a North Korea expert at Seoul's Dongguk University, said on Monday of the pictures carried by the North's official Korean Central News Agency. "To me, it looked like they were taken in June or July."

Sporting his trademark dark shades and khaki jumpsuit, Kim was shown inspecting a military unit. He viewed troops in training, clapping and talking to them while looking around their barracks dotted with red-and-white slogans urging loyalty to him.

They were the first photos of the "Dear Leader," as he is known in North Korea, available since Aug. 14. That is the date around which Kim — believed to have long had diabetes and heart disease — suffered a stroke and then underwent brain surgery, according to South Korean and US officials.

But the latest images — though undated — gave no indication Kim had been ill, let alone offered any sign of the alleged operation. His bouffant-hair remained as puffy as before, and their was no change in his pot belly. He also appeared in the images to have no problem walking and using both his arms.

Brain surgery usually involves shaving off of at least some hair and results in some body paralysis in many cases.

"Looking at his hands, arms and facial appearances in the still pictures, he doesn't appear to have had any problems," said Myoung C Lee, a neurologist at Seoul's Asan Medical Center. "It's doubtful if they were taken recently, but it's all guesswork."

But the oddest thing about the photos to some were the verdant grass and trees visible in the background: They were too green to believe the pictures were taken recently, considering it's autumn on the Korean peninsula. Foliage in South Korea has begun showing the tinge of fall, with yellowing leaves mixed with those still green. North Korea is latitudinally farther north than South Korea and autumn arrives faster.Newspapers in Seoul had similar observations. "Grass and trees in the photos show the typical sight of a summer landscape, though it is time that autumn leaves are visible in North Korea," the daily Kukmin Ilbo said .

The paper also said South Korean intelligence had seen no unusual movements where the military unit Kim reportedly visited is located, which would have been expected had he visited.

South Korean officials declined to comment on their analysis of the photos.

Heading: Paul Krugman wins Economics Nobel - Indian Express
Content:
Scientists in China have mapped the genome of the giant panda, which could yield a better understanding of why the endangered animals are so famously sex-shy, state media said on Monday.

"We hope the genome map could help genetically explain why giant pandas have little reproductive capability so that scientists can help them deliver more cubs," Wang Jun, a scientist with the Beijing Genomics Institute, was quoted as saying by the China Daily.

Chinese experts say there are only about 1,600 wild pandas in China, mainly in the southwest, with another 200 or so raised in captivity in Chinese breeding centres.

The animals' notoriously low libidos have frustrated efforts to boost their

numbers.

Breeders have resorted to tactics such as showing them "panda porn" videos of other pandas mating, and putting males through "sexercises" aimed at training up their pelvic and leg muscles for the rigours of copulation.

The Chinese-led genome-mapping effort also involved scientists from Britain, the United States, Denmark and Canada, the China Daily said.

The scientists mapped the genome of a three-year-old female named Jing Jing, with the results confirming the widely-held belief that the panda is a subspecies of bear, it said.

The panda had been previously thought to be related more closely to raccoons and similar animals.

A more detailed genome map could be completed by the end of this year, it said.

Heading: Water row may affect Indo-Pak ties: Zardari - Indian Express
Content:
Paul Krugman, the Princeton University scholar and New York Times columnist, won the Nobel prize in economics on Monday for his analysis of how economies of scale can affect trade patterns and the location of economic activity.

Krugman has been a harsh critic of the Bush administration and the Republican Party in The New York Times, where he writes a regular column and has a blog called "Conscience of a Liberal."

He has come out forcefully against John McCain during the economic meltdown, saying the Republican candidate is "more frightening now than he was a few weeks ago" and earlier that the GOP has become "the party of stupid."

"Krugman is not only a scientist but also an opinion maker," economics prize committee member Tore Ellingsen said. He added that Krugman's analyses tend to back free trade and his research gives no "support for protectionism."

The 55-year-old American economist was the lone winner of the 10 million kronor award and the latest in a string of American researchers to be honored. It was only the second time since 2000 that a single laureate won the prize, which is typically shared by two or three researchers.

The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences praised Krugman for formulating a new theory to answer questions about free trade.

"What are the effects of free trade and globalization? What are the driving forces behind worldwide urbanization? Paul Krugman has formulated a new theory to answer these questions," the academy said in its citation.

"He has thereby integrated the previously disparate research fields of international trade and economic geography," it said.

The award, known as the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences, is the last of the six Nobel prizes announced this year and is not one of the original Nobels. It was created in 1968 by the Swedish central bank in Alfred Nobel's memory.

Besides his work as an economist at Princeton University in New Jersey, where he has been since 2000, Krugman has written for publications including Foreign Affairs, the Harvard Business Review and Scientific American.

Commenting on the global economic meltdown, Krugman told a news conference in Stockholm by telephone from the United States that some of his research was linked to currency crises and related issues.

"This is terrifying," he said, comparing it to the financial crisis that gripped Asia in the 1990s. He said winning the Nobel award won't change his approach to research and writing.

"The prize will enhance visibility," he said, "but I hope it does not lead me into going to a lot of purely celebratory events, aside from the Nobel presentation itself."

Krugman's work on new trade theory also garnered him the John Bates Clark medal from the American Economic Association in 1991.

That prize is given every two years to an economist under the age of 40.

The Nobel citation said Krugman's approach is based on the premise that many goods and services can be produced at less cost in long series, a concept known as economies of scale. His research showed the effects of that on trade patterns and on the location of economic activity.

Heading: Hopeful about Taliban war : General McKiernan - Indian Express
Content:
Pakistan President Asif Ali Zardari has warned a brewing row with India over the waters of the Chenab river in the Kashmir could harm improving ties between the old rivals.

The warning came two days after Prime Minister Manmohan Singh inaugurated a 450-megawatt hydro power project at Baglihar dam on the Chenab, which flows from the Indian side to the Pakistani side of Kashmir.

"Pakistan would be paying a very high price for India's move to block Pakistan's water supply from the Chenab River," the official Associated Press of Pakistan quoted Zardari as saying in a statement late on Sunday.

"Prime Minister Manmohan Singh had assured me in our meeting in New York that his country is seriously committed to our water sharing treaty," he said, referring to their meeting on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly last month.

"We expect him to stand by his commitment."

Pakistani newspapers reported last week that India had blocked water from the Chenab river, which raised Pakistani concerns about water availability for crops.

Zardari warned that violation of the 1960 Indus Water Treaty would damage the bilateral ties the two countries had built over the years.

Under the accord, each country controls more than three rivers draining into the Indus river basin.

India has rejected Pakistan's contention that the Baglihar dam reduces the flow of water and says the project is crucial for power-starved Kashmir. A World Bank team of experts conducted an inquiry into the dispute in 2005 but did not make its findings public.

Pakistan's water commissioner is due to go to New Delhi on Tuesday for discussions, officials said.

Heading: ‘Taliban leader killed last year was a Pakistan army man’ - Indian Express
Content:
Less than 12 hours after NATO troops in Afghanistan defeated an ambitious attempt by the Taliban to storm a provincial capital in the far southwest, killing dozens of the fighters, the top American commander in the country urged doubters on Sunday to believe that the war against the Taliban would be won. The commander, Gen. David D McKiernan, who leads more than 65,000 troops from about 40 foreign countries, including 33,000 Americans, said at a news conference in Kabul that there had been "too many" reports in the media recently asserting that the foreign forces and their Afghan allies were losing the war.

"I absolutely reject that idea, I don't believe it," the general said, adding: "It is true that there are many places in this country that don't have an adequate level of security. We don't have progress as even and as fast as any of us would like. But we are not losing in Afghanistan."

Heading: Pashtun singer takes refuge in US fleeing the Taliban - Indian Express
Content:
A taliban commander killed by British special forces in a raid in Helmand in Afghanistan last year was in fact a Pakistani military officer, providing first hard evidence of covert Pakistani military presence in the war-torn country, a media report said.

The commander, targeted in the raid on a complex in the Sangrin valley, was one of the six killed in the past year by British Special Forces — SAS and SBS. When the British soldiers entered the compound, they discovered a Pakistani military ID on the body.

"It was the first physical evidence of covert Pakistani military operations in Afghanistan even though Islamabad insists it is a close ally in the 'war against terror'," The Sunday Times said.

The paper said British officials covered up the evidence and its refusal to share the information with Afghan President Hamid Karzai led to a row.

The British move to keep the information under wraps irked Karzai who has long accused London of viewing Afghanistan through the eyes of Pakistani military intelligence, which is widely believed to be helping Taliban.

According to the report, British officials in Kabul refused to comment on the allegation that they had covered up the discovery of a Pakistani soldier.

They insisted Karzai's government had been informed of the negotiations with the Taliban, adding that "the camp was just a place for them to be reintegrated, learn about hygiene and things."

The Afghan claims of Pakistani involvement in Helmand were backed by a senior United Nations officials who said he had been told by his superiors to keep quiet after Pakistan's ambassador to the UN apparently threatened to stop contributing forces to peacekeeping missions.

Pakistan is the UN's biggest supplier of peacekeeping troops.

The coalition's refusal to confront Pakistan changed after the bombing of the Indian embassy in Kabul last July when 55 people were killed.

According to both British and US intelligence, phone intercepts led directly back to an Afghan cell of Pakistan's military intelligence.

Repeated accusations from Karzai about Pakistan's active support for the Taliban have been backed by a senior US marine officer.

Lieutenant Colonel Chris Nash, who commanded an embedded training team in eastern Afghanistan from June 2007 to March this year, told the Army Times that Pakistani forces flew repeated helicopter missions into Afghanistan to resupply a Taliban base camp during a fierce battle in June last year.

"We were on the receiving end of Pakistani military D-30 (a howitzer). On numerous occasions, Afghan border police checkpoints and observation posts were attacked by Pakistani military forces," Nash said.

Heading: Hockey mom booed at hockey game - Indian Express
Content:
The threats started about a year ago, telling Haroon Bacha to stop singing or else.

"There were letters, there were phone calls, there were text messages," Bacha said, sitting upright on a floor in Brooklyn, surrounded by smoke from Pakistani cigarettes. "They used to come very frequently back home, just telling me to stop music, or else I would be killed and my family would be..."

He trailed off, tears welling in his eyes. Bacha, 36, is a Pashtun, the Muslim ethnic group of the mountainous northwest of Pakistan and southeast Afghanistan, and at home he is a star, with dozens of albums, slick videos and regular television appearances. In a sweet high baritone, he sings of peace, tolerance and resistance to war. Those liberal themes have endeared him to his war-weary Pashtun fans, he says, but made him a target of the local Taliban, which has been waging an escalating campaign against music and popular culture, calling it un-Islamic.

Two months ago Bacha escaped from his home near Peshawar, in Pakistan, and came to New York, leaving behind his wife, two young children and an extended family. If he goes back, he said, he will be killed. With a sharply reduced audience in the United States, Bacha faces an uncertain career, but on Saturday he sang at a small but lively benefit concert in Queens, organized by the Pashtun immigrants who have adopted him and held at an unlikely place: the Forest Hills Jewish Center.

"Anybody who is hated by the Taliban is starting out with a check in my column," said Rabbi Gerald C Skolnik, the leader of the centre, a Conservative synagogue. Rabbi Skolnik said that an initial phone call from one of the organizers had "raised a red flag," but that after the groups were vetted to make sure none of the money raised would go to terrorist groups, he was happy to rent the space.

In the Northwest Frontier Province of Pakistan, the Taliban has intimidated musicians and record store proprietors; recently dozens of music shops have been bombed, reportedly by pro-Taliban militants.

"Cultural activities are badly affected by what's going on in the region," said Hasan Khan, news director of the Islamabad-based television channel Khyber News, in a recent phone interview. "We have lost everything. We have lost music, we have lost local games, we have lost children playing in the street. It is almost impossible to visualize what is happening there."

The soft-spoken Bacha, who has striking green eyes and short brown curls, is a slightly unusual figure as a Pashtun star; he has a university education and, unlike most Pashtun singers, he does not come from a family of musicians. He said he saw his role as helping to lead a broad cultural resistance to Islamic fundamentalism.

"These people are bringing Pashtuns a very bad name," said Bacha, at one of the apartments in Brooklyn where he has been a guest. "The reason I didn't succumb to these threats is that I should work for my people, for Pashto as a language and rich tradition. I need to promote it and show to the world that we are not like these people."

Heading: Pentagon divided over McCain - Indian Express
Content:
The world's most famous "hockey mom" was loudly booed by fans before her children Willow and Piper as she made an appearance to ceremonially drop the first puck at an ice-hockey game between the Philadelphia Flyers and new York Rangers at Pennsylvania over the weekend.

ABC News reported that the booing was so prevalent that the music had to be cranked up to "deafening" levels in order to drown it out. The latest RCP average shows Barack Obama ahead by a whopping 13.8 percentage points in the state, leading John McCain 53.6 to 39.8.

Heading: The man behind the whispers about Obama - Indian Express
Content:
For decades, the nation's military officer corps has identified steadfastly with the priorities and values of the Republican Party. So the brass should be reveling in the presidential campaign of John McCain.

Yet, in a culture that typically prefers one of its own, many are wary of the Vietnam War hero.

McCain, a former Navy officer and prisoner of war, would arrive in the White House with more military experience than any president since Dwight D Eisenhower. But he also would bring a long congressional career as an outspoken critic of the Pentagon — prone to harsh assessments of its spending practices, weapons programs and military leaders.

As a result, defenders of some of the Pentagon's biggest weapons systems are worried that if McCain is elected, he will order sweeping changes, killing a number of big-ticket programs. Perhaps unlike other civilian leaders, McCain would be able to draw on his experience and knowledge of the military to reject the advice of generals and admirals.

"He is more feared in the Pentagon because he is impervious to the usual methods the military uses to roll the civilian leadership," a senior Defense official said.

Heading: History says it’s all over for McCain - Indian Express
Content:
The most persistent falsehood about Barack Obama's background first surfaced in 2004 just two weeks after the Democratic convention speech that helped set him on the path to his presidential candidacy: "Obama is a Muslim who has concealed his religion."

That statement, contained in a press release, spun a complex tale about the ancestry of Obama, who is Christian.

The press release was picked up by a conservative Web site, FreeRepublic.com, and spread steadily as others elaborated on its claims over the years in e-mail messages, websites and books. It continues to drive other false rumors about Obama's background.

Until this month, the man who is widely credited with starting the cyberwhisper campaign that still dogs Obama was a secondary character in news reports, with deep explorations of his background largely confined to liberal blogs.

But an appearance in a documentary-style program on the Fox News Channel watched by three million people last week thrust the man, Andy Martin, and his past into the foreground. The program allowed Martin to assert falsely and without challenge that Obama had once trained to overthrow the government.

An examination of legal documents and election filings, along with interviews with his acquaintances, revealed Martin, 62, to be a man with a history of scintillating if not always factual claims. He has left a trail of animosity — some of it provoked by anti-Jewish comments — among political leaders, lawyers and judges in three states over more than 30 years.

He is a law school graduate, but his admission to the Illinois bar was blocked in the 1970s after a psychiatric finding of "moderately severe character defect manifested by well-documented ideation with a paranoid flavor and a grandiose character."

Though he is not a lawyer, Martin went on to become a prodigious filer of lawsuits, and he made unsuccessful attempts to win public office for both parties in three states, as well as for president at least twice, in 1988 and 2000. Based in Chicago, he now identifies himself as a writer who focuses on his anti-Obama Web site and press releases.

Martin, in a series of interviews, did not dispute his influence in Obama rumors.

"Everybody uses my research as a takeoff point," Martin said, adding, however, that some take his writings "and exaggerate them to suit their own fantasies."

Heading: 6 from state killed in UP bus accident - Indian Express
Content:
Prosecutors in an Italian court Thursday asked the key middleman in the IAF's VVIP chopper deal whether the initials 'AP' in an alleged "budget sheet" for bribes to politicians referred to Ahmed Patel, the political secretary of UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi.

The middleman, Guido Haschke, who has consistently denied bribing Indian officials or politicians, replied that he did not know who or what 'AP' stood for.

As first reported by The Indian Express, Italian prosecutors had last month produced a handwritten document they alleged was a "budget" drawn up by two middlemen — Haschke and Christian Michel — which purportedly lists initials of Indian politicians and designations of bureaucrats and IAF officers who allegedly had to be "handled" to fix the Rs 3,546 crore deal.

The alleged "budget sheet" detailed how kickbacks of 51 million euros would be divided and under the heading "POL" — Haschke has claimed this referred to Indian politicians — there is a reference to "AP" against which "3 million euro" has been listed.

Another amount of 15/16 million euros was listed against "FAM" which is said to be "Family". Haschke has claimed the note was dictated to him by British consultant Michel during one of their meetings in 2008.

On Thursday, Italian prosecutor Eugenio Fusco asked Haschke during a court hearing in Busto Arsizio near Milan whether "AP" in the note was a reference to Ahmed Patel.

In his reply, the middlemen said he did not know what AP meant when he wrote it down. Haschke also denied any bribes were paid for the contract and said that the "budget sheet" was just an imaginary note drawn up and was never acted upon.

He also said the budget sheet was merely bragging by Michel about his Indian contacts and that Haschke tried to disassociate himself from the Briton.

Strongly denying any wrongdoing in the deal, Haschke also claimed to Indian interrogators in the court that no bribes were paid for the contract and that the money he received from AgustaWestland - in excess of 24 million euros - is justified as fees for engineering consultations.

Italian prosecutors also produced another note in court Thursday - a March 2008 fax by Michel to Peter Hulett, said to be the then head of region, govt sales at AgustaWestland's India office. The fax said that among the politicians who would use the choppers once acquired by India would be UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi and her senior advisors, including Ahmed Patel.

However, Sonia is not entitled to use government helicopters. She can use VIP aircraft only when she flies with the PM, President or ministers who are officially entitled to the aircraft. This fax by the British middleman has also been shared by the Italian side with the CBI team that is in Busto Arsizio for the hearing.

Michel has been elusive and no investigative agency has been able to reach him.

Haschke, who is facing a case in Italy for being part of a conspiracy to bribe Indian officials to ensure the AW 101 chopper was picked by the IAF, faced several questions from the Indian side and denied any irregularity.

But the Indian side did not ask Haschke to explain what AP, FAM or any of the other acronyms in the note - "DS", "JS AIR", "AFA", "DG Acquisition", CVC" etc - referred to, source said.

The middleman, who was quizzed about his association with former Air Chief S P Tyagi - named as an accused in the CBI case in the deal - denied that any money had been paid to the retired Indian officer. Haschke, sources said, admitted that he was in regular touch with three cousins of Tyagi who have also been named in the case.

In response to a question from the Indian side, Haschke said he was not aware if any money was paid to S P Tyagi.

The UPA government had come under pressure in connection with the alleged kickbacks last month after The Indian Express report on the budget sheet of the middlemen. The opposition BJP had demanded the government reveal what or who "AP" and "FAM" stand for. The party also said that it wants a detailed discussion in Parliament on "alleged payments to persons close to the ruling establishment" in connection with the controversial chopper deal and has accused the government of "running away from discussions".

The discussion did not take place as the Parliament session was abruptly called off midway.

Heading: BSP important, Maya among PM contenders, says CPM - Indian Express
Content:
Six residents of North 24-Parganas, who had gone to visit Ajmer Sharif, were killed and a few others injured in a road accident in Pratapgarh district of Uttar Pradesh early on Tuesday morning. The deceased included two women and a 15-year-old girl. While five of the victims were from Deganga, the sixth belonged toBijpur. The bodies will be flown back on Wednesday.

The Deganga residents —- Golam Rasul (55), Piyara Bibi (30), Sabir Ali (35), Margina Bibi (36) and Chandana Khatun (15) — had set off along with Bijpur's Sanjoy Das (22) in a bus from Burihata. The trip was organised by a travel agency. Sub-Divisional Police Officer Barasat Joy Biswas said the relatives of the victims have been informed. The bodies will be brought back and handed over to the relatives on Wednesday, he said.

Asraf Ali Mondal, one of the injured from Deganga, has told the police that he was sitting on the backseat of the bus and suddenly experienced a jerk. He was hit on the head and fell unconscious.

A pall of gloom descended on the area after news of the accident reached. Chintamoni Das, a relative of Das, said: "He had left saying he would return before Diwali and would bring some gifts for me."

Relatives of Khatun, a resident of Deganga's Matikumra village, said she had gone with her parents. "Her parents did not want to take her but she wanted to go. We cannot believe she is no more," said her aunt Ayesha Begum.

Rasul, who belonged to Deganga's Subarnapur village, was a tailor and the only earning member of his family. His family was in complete shock on hearing the news. Some residents called off the Lakshmi puja celebrations on Tuesday.

Joydip Bhattacharya, the owner of the travel agency, said he contacted the police as soon as he heard of the accident. "We will make all arrangements to bring back the bodies," he said.

Heading: CPM leader fires at TMC member, held - Indian Express
Content:
The CPM has termed its strategy as one of "defeating the BJP and rejecting the Congress" in run-up to the Assembly elections in six states and the Lok Sabha.

Talking to reporters on Tuesday, after a three-day session of the party's Central Committee here, general secretary Prakash Karat said "the party will adopt an electoral platform aiming to defeat the BJP, which is a communal party advocating reactionary economic policies, and for rejecting the Congress that is forging a strategic alliance with the US and pursuing anti-people economic policies".

Karat's revelation of his party's poll strategy coincided with the Election Commission's announcement to hold elections in Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Delhi, Mizoram and Chhatisgarh. The EC postponed a decision on Jammu and Kashmir for the time being.

Karat also did not rule out the possibility of Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Mayawati being one of the contenders for the Prime Minister's post after the Lok Sabha elections.

"The BSP is an important political party ruling the largest state in our country. We expect them to fare well in the forthcoming Lok Sabha polls. It will depend on the mandate after the elections and she will be among the ones," Karat said when asked whether his party will support Mayawati as the next Prime Minister.

After the CPM's withdrawal of support to the Manmohan Singh Government on the issue of Indo-US civil nuclear deal, the party has attached much importance to the economic issues being followed by the Centre rather than hitting on the nuke deal issue. At the same time, it has also criticised the Congress-led coalition Government for its "pro-US stance".

Karat denounced nationwide attacks on Christians and pulled up the Centre for being a mute spectator. "All this is being done eyeing the upcoming polls. Attacks on Chtristian minorities are recurring in Orissa, Karnataka and other states. What happened in Kandhamal is shocking, now efforts are on to reconvert the victims. We want action against Bajrang Dal under the same laws which are used to curb terrorism," he said.

He announced that the party would conduct a nationwide campaign against terrorism and communalism from Octover 30 to November 5.

While approving the West Bengal CPI(M) and Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee's way of handling the Singur situation, Karat also hoped that the Left Front Government would try to find out an alternative option in Singur after the Tata Motors' pullout.

Heading: Nano supporters prevent shift of machines from Singur factory - Indian Express
Content:
A CPM leader was arrested on charge of firing at a Trinamool Congress supporter allegedly in front of some policemen during a clash at Barkhantala village near Pursurah in Hooghly on Monday night.

The police, however, claimed that no policeman was at the spot when the bullet was fired.

The injured Trinamool supporter was admitted to the Arambagh sub-divisional hospital.

The trouble broke out around 9.30 pm on Monday when Trinamool supporters took out a rally at Barkhantala village where the CPM had lost a few seats in the last panchayat elections.

Local CPM supporters, allegedly led by a former member of the Hooghly zilla parishad and CPM leader Jaharlal Ghorui, assaulted Trinamool worker Soumen Chatterjee, inviting strong retaliation from their rival party cadres.

Soon, a clash ensued and policemen from the Pursurah police station had to be deployed in the area. Trinamool supporters alleged that Ghorui had fired a bullet at Trinamool leader Lakshmi Moitri during the clash. The situation was brought under control after additional policemen were deployed in the area.

"A few policemen were present when the bullet was fired. We have lodged a complaint against five CPM men in connection with the incident," Trinamool leader Parvez Rehman said.

"We have arrested a CPM supporter for firing at a Trinamool Congress supporter. But, reports that the firing took place in front of policemen are wrong. The police had left the area when the firing took place," said Swapan Bagchi, Sub-Divisional Police Officer, Arambagh.

Hooghly district committee member of CPM, Asit Patra, said: "The Trinamool Congress cadres have unleashed terror after winning a few seats in the last panchayat polls in Pursurah."

He further added: "No CPM leader was involved in the incident. The violence was the result of an internal rivalry between two groups of Trinamool cadres."

Patra also said our leader was arrested without conducting proper investigating into the incident. "We will launch a movement against this," he added.

Heading: Given a new life by Big B, girl now prays for his recovery - Indian Express
Content:
Supporters of the Save Nano Committee (SNC) prevented the employees of a private company, engaged by Tata Motors, from shifting some heavy machinery from the Singur plant on Tuesday.

A police officer said around noon, nearly 20 SNC members intercepted five trucks, in which a pay-loader machine and a few generator sets were being taken out of the factory through gate number five.

The vehicles belonged to the company that the Tatas had engaged to dismantle the machines and shift to other places.

The employees of the company, who were in the vehicles, requested the SNC members to let them go but they refused to budge. The protesters, who sat outside the factory gate, demanded that Ratan Tata should reconsider his decision to pull out from Singur.

After a few minutes, the trucks were taken back to the project area, as the SMC supporters blocked the factory gate for several hours.

A senior police officer said the Singur police went to the spot to pacify the protesters, but their request to withdraw the blockade was turned down by the SNC supporters.

SNC convener Sadai Koley said: "We want to make it clear that the Tatas will not be allowed to shift machines from the project area. We will allow only the entry of machines and not the exit. The Tatas will have to come back because almost 90 per cent work on the project is over."

He added, "We also requested those who were shifting the machines today to support our movement for holding back Tatas in Singur."

Heading: Nirupam Sen admitted to AMRI following chest pain - Indian Express
Content:
When nine-year-old Mita Mondol says she loves Amitabh Bachchan more than any other actor, she has a strong reasons for saying so.

For, she is taking his illness very personally because it was the Bollywood icon, who had given her a new life in July this year.

Mita was born with a rare heart disease and her father was too poor to afford her treatment. It was Bachchan's generosity that saw the little girl finally getting the required treatment.

So, to express gratitude to the superstar, the little girl quietly made her way to the Kalighat temple with her parents on Tuesday afternoon, and offered a special puja for his speedy recovery.

Debu Mondol, Mita's father who works in a tea-stall in the city, said: "Mr Bachchan's generous donation of Rs 2.5 lakh saved my daughter's life. Not only did he give the money, but he also asked his doctors to suggest correct treatment for Mita. They explained her condition to me and also offered me their services."

He added, "Even after the operation, he kept in touch with us to enquire about her health."

Last month, when Bachchan had visited Kolkata for the premier of The Last Lear, he had invited the Mondol family to his hotel and spent time playing with Mita.

Utpal Roy, the general secretary of Diganta, the welfare organisation helping out the Mondol family, said: "We were amazed by Mr Bachchan's generosity. When we decided to help Mita, we requested media to ask their viewers and readers to donate Re 1 for her cause. When Mr Bachchan watched the story on a news channel, he got in touch with us."

Since the Mondol family did not have any bank account, the NGO opened an account in Debu's name where the money could be deposited. Although the girl's treatment is a long process, Roy said the money was used for the first stage of the treatment where Mita had to undergo an operation to expand her veins to facilitate more blood flow.

Mita is now on medication and doctors are monitoring her condition. In the next stage, she will receive a valve and artificial veins that will be connected with the valve.

Mondol said: "For us he is more than just a screen idol. He helped save a life when we had lost all hopes. What touched us was that he was genuinely concerned for us. We spoke to him a few days ago and are sad to hear that he is so ill."

When the Mondol family was told about his illness, they were keen to offer prayers at Kalighat and contacted a priest who told them to do it on Lakshmi Puja as it was the most auspicious day. All that Mita, a Class III student in a school in her village Nila in South 24 Parganas, now wants is that her real-life hero gets well soon.

Heading: Kidnap bid foiled in Park Street, woman held - Indian Express
Content:
State Commerce and Industries Minister Nirupam Sen was admitted to the AMRI hospital in Salt Lake on late Monday night after he complained of severe chest pain.

A medical bulletin released by the hospital around 11.45 am on Tuesday stated that Sen's condition was "stable." A special medical team has been constituted to monitor the minister's health.

On late Monday night, Sen's blood pressure had shot up and he was immediately hospitalised. A CT angiogram was performed on him under the supervision of Dr Susrut Bandopadhyay. In 2003, Sen had suffered a cardiac arrest during a trip to New Delhi and was admitted to AIIMS. On Tuesday morning, several visitors, including state Health Minister Surya Kanta Misra, state Housing Minister Goutam Deb and state Fisheries Minister Kiranmay Nanda and Politburo member Brinda Karat, came to meet Sen.

After meeting Sen at the hospital, the health minister said there was no cause for concern. "We are satisfied with the treatment. There is no cause for tension. He is undergoing some medical tests and is being kept under observation," Mishra told mediapersons.

Heading: Civic body asks govt to scrutinise STM report - Indian Express
Content:
The police have arrested a woman after she tried to kidnap a two-year-old child in the Park Street area on Tuesday.

The police said the woman, aged around 50 years, picked up Khushboo from Wellesly Second Lane, where the child was taking a walk with her elder sister Sajida.

"Sajida raised an alarm when the woman tried to run from the spot," said an officer of the Park Street police station.

According to the police, local residents caught hold of the accused and rescued the child. The woman, who later said that her name was Baby, was tied to a pole and beaten up by the locals.

Part of her hair was also cut off by the angry residents. She was rescued only after the police intervened.

Later, Mohamad Hashmel, father of Khushboo, lodged a complaint with the Park Street police station.

The police, however, said the woman seemed to be mentally unstable. She will be produced in court on Wednesday.

Heading: Ashtadhatu idol theft: Minorities Commission visits Alipore Jain temple - Indian Express
Content:
The death of 34-year-old Pralay Choudhury by Japanese Encephalitis (JE) has sparked a new row after the health department of the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) challenged the report of School of Tropical Medicine (STM) that had concluded Choudhury died of "Asphyxial Pneumonia with Hyponatraemia — a case of Japanese Encephalitis".

In a letter written to the state Health and Family Welfare Department and director of National Vector-Borne Disease Control Programme, the chief medical health officer (CMHO), Debdwaipayan Chattopadhaya, has called for scrutinising the reports of STM to ascertain the cause of Choudhury's death. In the letter, he mentioned that there is no paddy field and piggery — habitat of JE vector — within six kilometres of Choudhury's residence.

Senior officials of the civic body's Health Department, however, were not aware about the development. "I was not informed by the CMHO prior to writing to the Central and state governments. The health officials should have gone to the place and looked for the reasons how the person got infected rather than expressing doubts on the reports of the most authentic institute like STM," said Subodh Dey, Member Mayor-in-Council (Health) KMC.

The civic body has, meanwhile, asked the World Health Organisation to carry out a joint survey in Behala.

"We are still not clear as to how Choudhury got infected with Japanese Encephalitis. But it does not imply that the STM report is wrong, as the school conducts several tests before coming to a conclusion. The patient may have suffered multi-organ failure or immune complex due to encephalitis," former director of STM Dr Amiya Hati said.

"There are several piggeries and slaughterhouses in the city from where the person could have got the infection. Moreover, there are paddy fields on the fringes of the city also," Dr Hati added.

Earlier, the state Health Department, citing the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) report, had pointed out several discrepancies in the figures of dengue cases presented by the civic body. While the KMC report had said at least 24 people were afflicted with the dengue virus, ICMR report put the figure at 89.

"The civic body can never have the exact figures of the vector-borne disease cases as it always collects the passive data. Unless it starts collecting data from houses, it cannot present an authentic report. Our researches say that dengue and malignant malaria have not come down in the city, whereas the civic body says just the opposite," Dr Hati said.

"Every year, we send proposals to the KMC to carry out active surveys of various diseases in the city, but it has never been implemented. And now, to save their own skin, the civic officials claim our report to be wrong," said a senior health official of STM.

Heading: Train cancellations annoy commuters - Indian Express
Content:
A delegation of the West Bengal Minorities Commission on Tuesday visited the Alipore Jain temple from where an idol of Lord Parasnath was stolen almost a week ago.

The delegation comprised state Minorities Commission Chairman S S Z Adnan, Vice-Chairman Kalyan Chaudhuri and another member Narayan Prasad Jain.

The temple located at 9, Alipore Park Place has three idols of Jain lords —- two of Lord Parasnath and another of Lord Santnath. On the morning of October 8, the temple authorities found one of the idols of Parasnath missing.

"All the other articles, including silver wares and other idols, were intact," recalls Narayan Prasad Jain. The idol, believed to have been stolen, is around eight inches by four inches in dimension and was made of "Ashtadhatu", an alloy of eight metals.

The temple is thronged by hundreds of devotees of the Jain community every day and the idols are of immense historical significance.

The members of the community have already met Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee on October 12 and the Commissioner of Kolkata Police Gautam Mohan Chakrabarti on October 13 requesting them to ensure that the idol is recovered soon. The case has been taken up by the Kolkata police's Detective Department.

The Jains from both Howrah and Kolkata will now submit a memorandum to the state minorities commission, urging the state government to look into the matter.

The community will be represented by the temple committee of the Alipore Jain temple under the banner of Sri Parasnath Digambar Jain Mandir Alipore.

"We visited the temple today. We will discuss our observations tomorrow. Only then will we be able to finalise our next course of action," said Adnan.

Heading: Trader files robbery complaint, police find anomalies - Indian Express
Content:
Angry passengers went on a rampage at the south-suburban section of the Sealdah division on Tuesday after they found that 12 trains had been cancelled. One GRP personnel suffered serious head injuries in the stone pelting that followed.

Commuters in the Sealdah-Baruipur section were infuriated with the decision of the Eastern Railway authorities to cancel 12 pairs of trains in the section because of maintenance work. Out of the 12 pairs of suburban EMUs, six were cancelled during the peak hours between 6:20 am and 9:50 am. A large section of people commuting in the EMU locals in this section comprises domestic helps and day labourers. The decision of the Railway authorities to suspend services was prompted by the fact that there would be no crowd with Tuesday being a holiday for Laksmi Puja. This, however, did not go down well with the commuters and they turned violent throwing stones and ransacking station premises at Subhashgram and Docharan stations.

The agitation that broke out at 7 am continued for more than two hours. "The announcement that 25 pairs of trains in different sections will remain cancelled was made in advance with advertisements in newspapers in September," said a senior railway official.

Commuters, however, felt that it was not the first time that the Railway had suspended train services. "They could at least run trains on an hourly basis which could not have caused so much inconvenience. We have to report to work or end up losing a day's wage," said Rubina Alam, a commuter.

Heading: Decomposed body recovered in Shibpur - Indian Express
Content:
A 35-year-old trader lodged a complaint with the city police on Monday night, claiming that four unidentified men had kidnapped him from the Eastern Metropolitan Bypass near Tiljala on Sunday afternoon and then snatched Rs 56,000 from him at gunpoint.

The victim, Atiq Ahmed, a resident of 15/16 Bibi Bagan Lane near Entally, told the police that he had gone to Tiljala on Sunday afternoon to collect payments from his business associates. While returning, Ahmed claimed, four unidentified men, aged around 30, intercepted him near 24 Bus Stand on EM Bypass near Tiljala and dragged him into a Maruti. He was then taken to an apartment in Rajarhat where the quartet kept him for a day.

"They allegedly forced Ahmed, who deals in plastic products, to part with Rs 56,000 that he had collected from his business partners. After being forced to part away with the money, Ahmed claimed, the goons took him to Tiljala in a car and pushed him out of the vehicle in front of Science City around 10 pm on Monday," said a senior officer of Topsia police station.

Ahmed later contacted Topsia police station and reported the matter. Police admitted him to the Chittaranjan National Medical College and Hospital for treatment, from where he was released after preliminary first-aid.

"There are some anomalies in Ahmed's statement. He claimed that he was kidnapped from near 24 Bus Stand on EM Bypass in broad daylight. There is a traffic police outpost located in the area that remains crowded during afternoon.

Also there is no witness to the incident. He also didn't raise an alarm while being dragged into the car," said a senior officer of Topsia police station. A probe has been initiated, but no arrests have been made so far, he said.

Heading: KMC to adopt waste-management system on trial - Indian Express
Content:
The decomposed body of an elderly woman was recovered from her house in Howrah on Tuesday. Police said the woman had probably died a few days ago, but no one came to know as she lived alone.

Fifty-two-year-old Mun Mun Ghosh lived in a small dingy rented room in Baishnabpara Lane in Shibpur. Police said she was poor and had no relatives. On Tuesday morning, locals informed the Shibpur police station of a foul odour coming from the closed room where Ghosh lived. When the police broke open the door, they found the decomposed body of the woman.

Locals informed the police that the woman had not stepped out of the house for a few days. Police said the cause of death was probably poverty and hunger, as all the food containers inside the house were empty.

In another incident, a teenager drowned while bathing in a pond at Garmirzapur in Sankrail on Tuesday afternoon. Police said two Class IX students of Jhurhat High School had gone to bathe in a local pond, when one of the students drowned around 1 pm. Locals tried to rescue the boy but could not save him. His body was fished out after about an hour. Police said cardiac failure was possibly the cause of the boy's death, as he knew how to swim. The boy was declared dead at the West Bank Hospital.

Heading: A day after the fire, Malda DM blames hospital for lackadaisical attitude - Indian Express
Content:
Although, the Supreme Court directed all the civic bodies to segregate organic and inorganic waste more than a decade ago, the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) has failed to implement the order successfully. Other municipalities of the state like Chandernagore, Bhadreswar and Kalyani have, however, adopted the system.

With the Supreme Court-appointed Environment Monitoring Body (EMB) insisting that the waste segregation system be implemented, the KMC has finally decided to start it on an experimental basis in ward 115, followed by other wards of the city.

"We tried to implement the waste segregation system in 1994-96, but it failed due to the lack of awareness among the general public. So, we need to organise an awareness campaign first. Moreover, the system is not cost-effective," said Arun Sarkar, Chief Engineer, Solid Waste Management Department, KMC.

According to Sarkar, the system will be implemented through a contractor and will cost around Rs 4 to 5 lakh per month for every ward. He said the contractor will provide a container to every household to collect the inorganic waste that will be carried to a factory directly. The civic body will provide a list of inorganic waste items, including plastic, glass pieces, paper and cotton. The order to start the work will be issued within a week.

"Some municipalities have already implemented the system and have set up separate landfill sites for solid waste management. We have funded a number of pilot projects after issuing a circular through the West Bengal Pollution Control Board. Besides, about six months ago, we earmarked Rs 50 lakh for solid waste management system. So, if the KMC introduces the waste segregation system then we can provide them financial support," said ML Meena, Principal Secretary of the Environment Department.

"We have made waste segregation mandatory for new housing complexes. We will not issue environmental clearance certificates to promoters until they implement it. We have also asked housing societies to use 40 per cent of the organic waste for making compost and use it in their gardens," Meena added.

Heading: Oz media accuses Sourav of ‘delay tactics’, calls him ‘serial offender’ - Indian Express
Content:
A day after a section of the district hospital in Malda caught fire, the district magistrate, C R Das, on Tuesday blamed the hospital authorities for negligence and said their lackadaisical attitude led to the spread of the fire.

The fire broke out in a corner of the groundfloor where old soiled mattresses were stored. The smoke had spread to different wards, even filling the children's ward on the third floor.

"No children were harmed. Although, a few did fall ill after inhaling the smoke, they recovered quickly. The fire was small and probably began when someone threw a lit bidi or cigarette over there. The hospital is being cleared up and will soon be disinfected," said Das. In a press meet organised earlier on Tuesday, Das along with Chief Medical Officer Radharaman Banik blamed the hospital authorities for being irresponsible. The DM blamed the doctors for not reporting to duty on time and for admitting patients in wards even when there weren't enough beds.

The children's ward, which has 40 beds, had accommodated over 60 children, forcing many to share a bed or sleep on the floor.

Heading: Karim skips Bagan practice - Indian Express
Content:
Sourav Ganguly, who will retire from international cricket after the ongoing India-Australia Test series, continues to hog the limelight. This time, the former Indian captain is facing the wrath of the Australian media, that has accused Ganguly of resorting to delaying tactics in the drawn opening Test.

The last day's play on Monday had to be cut short midway into the last session at the M Chinnaswamy Stadium after Ganguly and VVS Laxman complained of bad light due to overcast conditions.

In various newspapers across Australia on Tuesday, Ganguly has been singled out and castigated for allegedly delaying action during the crucial closing moments of the Test.

The Australian media commented that, had the Indian batsmen not resorted to delay tactics, Ricky Ponting & Co could have taken a 1-0 lead in the four-Test series. The Oz media also attacked the ICC rules, claiming that the existing bad light rule unfairly favours batsmen.

A member of the popular National Nine News sports bureau took a stinging dig at Ganguly, whom he described as a "serial offender".

He wrote: "Serial offender Sourav Ganguly firstly persuaded the umpires to go off. Then, when play resumed, Ganguly made Australia's fielders and (batting) partner VVS Laxman wait an eternity because he'd apparently 'forgotten to put his thigh pad on'. Please! Can't you be timed out in this game?"

The same media unit also lamented that the spectators were the biggest losers after what happened on the final day. The team further wrote: "The players got something out of it. Pedantic officials got their moment of the glory. But billions of fans and more importantly, the game itself, got nothing out of this farcical finish in Bangalore."

Criticising umpire Asad Rauf and Rudy Koertzen, the writer commented: "With the match in the balance, a crucial hour's play on the final day was lost, with not one, but two stoppages for bad light — when at times the sun was shining! Umpires strutted about like Emperor Penguins, holding out their light metres — a device that, like performance-enhancing drugs, should be banned."

A Fox Sports commentator demanded amendments to the ICC's existing bad light rules. "I thought the light was fine and they really need to change the rules regarding that aspect of the game," he observed. "There has to be some pressure on the ICC over this as there was no danger at all. Fox Sports also invited readers to comment whether poor light should be allowed to influence the outcome of a Test match and whether India played the match in the right spirit.

Heading: Seeds crash out on Day 2 of U-14 meet - Indian Express
Content:
Coach Karim Bencherifa was absent as Mohun Bagan players sweated it out at the Howrah Stadium today. Officially, it was said that an indisposed Karim preferred to take rest. But if you read between the lines, there might be more to it.

After the loss against Sporting Clube de Goa in the I-League encounter recently, the Moroccan coach had said that he would give it a serious thought about continuing with his job. The club officials played down the issue, asserting that he would stay.

Assistant coach Satyajit Chatterjee today conducted the show and told the boys in no uncertain terms that it's high time they pull up their socks. Mohun Bagan will play their next match against Mohammedan Sporting on October 19.

Meanwhile, after Sunil Chhetri and Surkumar Singh, now Asim Biswas and Renedy Singh have joined the list of injured players that has left East Bengal searching for options ahead of their match against Vasco Sports Club of Goa on October 18. Biswas today injured his knee during practice that will render him ineffective for at least a couple of weeks. Renedy is uncertain for the next match.

National coach Bob Houghton, who is in the city, is mulling over going to East Bengal's practice tomorrow. It would be a great morale-booster for a depleted a red-and-gold brigade should he go there.

Heading: Of Things Unread - Indian Express
Content:
Two seeds tumbled out on the second day of the 2nd Asian Under-14 Tennis Tournament being played at the synthetic courts of the Bengal Tennis Association (BTA) here. The event is being held under the sanction of the All India Tennis Association (AITA) and the Asian Tennis Federation (ATF).

Fourth seed Nishchay Rawal was ousted by city boy Md Azhar 4-6, 6-7 (3-7). Nikhil Reddy defeated the fifth seed Kuwar Singh Tater 6-4, 6-3. The rest of the seeds proceeded as expected to book their berths in the quarter-finals.

In the girls' matches also, two seeds were ousted. Second seed Bhavika Wadhawan was ousted by wild card Sneha Reddy 3-6, 4-6. Dhruti Venugopal lost to seventh seeded Spurthi Shivalingaiah 6-2, 6-1. Top seed Amrita Mukherjee did not break sweat in defeating compatriot Srijita Ghosh 6-0, 6-2. Fourth seed C Sai Samitha defeated Aandrita Deb 6-2, 6-1.
