Heading: Full Circle - Indian Express
Content:
Shatrughan Sinha's daughter is the showstopper for Kolkata designers, Dev and Nil's menswear line

It's a menswear collection that explores the element of androgyny, but Sonakshi Sinha, daughter of yesteryear actors Shatrughan Sinha and Poonam, thinks it is just right for her ramp debut. "My role is to embody that element of femininity in the male psyche," says the 20-year-old, who will model for city-based designers Dev and Nil for their Lakme Fashion Week show in Mumbai on October 22.

Sinha, who has known the designers for about three years, have often helped them backstage. "We have been saying that she should consider modelling.

This time when we asked her to walk for us, she agreed," says Nil, adding, "Since this is our first menswear collection, we wanted the right personality to project the theme. She fits the bill splendidly with her height and strong personality."

Sinha, in fact, has worked hard on her look. "The concept requires me to look toned and fit so I have been gymming regularly and lost a lot of weight.," she shrugs.

Even though this will be Sinha's first stint in the limelight, she is unfazed. "I have been groomed since I was born, thanks to both my parents. It is not something that I have had to work for," says Sinha, who has just graduated in design from the SNDT Women's University, Mumbai, and hopes to launch her own designer label in a few years' time. Film offers, says Sinha, have been coming in for a while, but she'd rather let her parents do the choosing. "I won't be allowed to do anything and everything. Thus, I have left the decision to them. I know whatever they decide will be the best for me."

Heading: Gem of an Auction? - Indian Express
Content:
Mugdha Godse on moving from the real world of fashion to Madhur Bhandarkar's reel version of it

She had strutted the ramp and faced enough flashbulbs, but did not quite realise how nerve-wracking it would be to act it all out — until she faced Madhur Bhandarkar for her first shot for Fashion. The dusky Mugdha Godse is now happy about her role as a failed model, as Bhandarkar ponders on the seamy side of the extravaganza we see on the runway.

Dressed in a black singlet and denims, her minimalistic look a sharp contrast to her glam avatar on screen, the 23-year-old confesses to exhaustion, as she juggles ad shoots, promotions and dubbing. "I am so excited — and nervous. Ever since the promos started on the TV, the expectations have gone up though the enormity of the situation has yet to sink in," she says.

In the movie to be released around Diwali, Godse plays Janet Sequeira, alongside Priyanka Chopra, Kangana Ranaut and Arbaaz Khan. "The movie is about the emotional journey of models at different stages of their careers and Madhur has captured it aptly," she says. Between posing for photographs, she says she had no inkling she could act. Hers has been the typical small-town-girl story. "I studied in a Marathi-medium school in Pune. It was in college that I understood the basics of grooming," she says. Her ambition drove her to the sequined universe of fashion. Then at an ad shoot, Bhandarkar spotted her and offered the part in Fashion — and Bollywood easily became part of her resume.

It was after Godse signed the film that the grill began. She attended a crash course in acting at Anupam Kher's school and took Kathak lessons, which she claims helped her synchronise expressions, movements and feelings. Recounting her first time in front of the camera, she boasts at having given her first shot in just two takes. "And once the shot was okayed, everybody applauded. I can still hear the sound of those claps," she adds.

The Bollywood bug has bitten and the debutante is clearly not keen on continuing her old life as a model — she has cut down her ad assignments and has been attending script-reading sessions. Her three-movie deal with Percept is also in the pipeline, but there is one more bow on the runway. "You will see me at the forthcoming Lakme Fashion Week ... this time as a show stopper," she laughs.

Heading: Rs 2.5 crore recovered during Income Tax raid on Ghaziabad property developers - Indian Express
Content:
Not quite. The first public auction of jewels in the country did not dazzle with its results, but more are following

At 42.02 carats, it is the world's largest Forevermark yellow diamond, estimated between Rs 2.7 crore and Rs 3.2 crore — one best friend for a man or a woman. But when the unmounted gemstone came under the hammer at the recent Saffronart Fine Jewels auction, it failed to invite a bid that touched the reserve price. The fate was shared by 74 of 130 lots that went on sale, and the closing figure stood at Rs 6.3 crore, far from the estimated Rs 22-28 crore, but that did not deter the spirit of Minal Vazirani, co-founder of the online auction house. "Keeping the current global economic conditions in mind, we did well," she said, still beaming at having organised what is arguably India's first public auction of fine jewels and watches on October 7 and 8.

With only international auction houses to look for guidance, Vazirani had formed an in-house team of experts that scouted precious jewels from the world over. Apart from the diamond, there were a natural pearl necklace with a seven-strand cascade that invited the highest bid of Rs 1 crore, a diamond necklace that sold for Rs 79.8 lakh and a diamond sarpech that went for Rs 49.8 lakh. "The auction comprised jewellery made over the past 100 years," says Vazirani.

Saffronart's results might not have dazzled, but in his Bangalore office Maher Dadha, CMD of the auction house Bid & Hammer, is busy examining the provenance of vintage jewellery. It will be part of the auction that will take place in January 2009. Unlike Vazirani, Dadha will bring to the auction, jewellery that is a minimum of 50 years old and will tap sources that have remained outside the radar of international auctioneers that are bound by trade regulations that restrict the export of heritage jewellery from India. "There is a lot of demand in India and it will not be difficult to find buyers," says Dadha.

Mumbai-based Ma Passion, meanwhile, hopes to revive the craft of gemstone carving with its October 22 auction. Curated by Nisha Jamwal, this will comprise, among others, emerald Ganesha, Krishna and Radha in blue sapphire and crystal Buddha under the Bodhi tree carved by craftsmen from Rajasthan.

Even as the country wakes up to hammer coming down on jewels, foreign shores will as usual be glitzy. At its Geneva auction next month, Sotheby's will have enough Indian jewels, while later this month Christie's will bring under the hammer, in Dubai, an early 20th century rose-cut diamond sarpech, estimated at $50,000-70,000, and two India-influenced Cartier jewels — a pendant estimated at $200,000-300,000 and a 1940s clip brooch priced at $13,000-18,000.

Heading: 3 held for stabbing cook in Anand Vihar - Indian Express
Content:
In a major crackdown on property developers, the Income Tax department raided SVP Private Builders, dealers in real estate, hospitality and education, late on Tuesday.

Approximately Rs 2.5 crore in cash and documents related to various properties were recovered in the raid. Shikha Darbari, additional director of Income Tax, said the developers, who were earlier not co-operating, had handed over keys and documents of various properties they owned.

Giving a list of properties, Darbari said the developers own four malls in Ghaziabad. "They are developing the Gulmohur Green Apartments at Mohan Nagar. On GT Road, they own the under-construction OPM mall. On Rakesh Marg, the builders have Gulmohur Enclave. They also own one college and one girls school in Ghaziabad. The group also owns two hotels, including the Pelican. Investigations are going on and the raid will end around 5 am. It started this morning," she said.

Houses number E-90 to E-94 in Nehru Nagar-II, which belong to Keval Krishan Bansal, Naresh Bansal, Tarseen Goel and Vijay Jindal, were raided.

Heading: Noida: Two robbed by bikers in separate incidents - Indian Express
Content:
With the arrest of three persons, the Northeast district police claim to have solved the murder of a cook, who was killed for not serving papad to them. The arrested have been identified as Mahender Kumar (24), Sandeep Sharma (21) and Pankaj Kumar (22).

They were also involved in the murder of a builder in Gokalpuri on September 29, police said.

On October 11, they attacked four persons at a restro-bar in Anand Vihar. The argument started over papad, which the assailants demanded from the cook. They then attacked the hotel staff. Later, one of them, Mohammad Sajid, succumbed to his injuries in hospital. The hotel owner and his son also suffered injuries after they tried to intervene.

In another case, a builder identified as Mohammad Hanif (45) had tried to resist a snatching bid and hit one of the accused with a brick. In order to take revenge, the trio killed Hanif two months after the incident.

The police also recovered a stolen motorcycle, a country-made pistol and knife from their possession. The accused have been involved in a number of theft, murder and burglary cases.

Heading: UP cops seek custody of blast accused - Indian Express
Content:
An assistant producer with a media company was robbed by two motorcycle-borne assailants in Noida on Monday night, when he was returning home to Kishangarh in Delhi.

Tej Narayan Rai lodged a complaint against the two unknown assailants in the Sector-20 police station, after he was robbed around 11.45 pm. "When I reached Sector-19, three motorcyclists stopped me and started beating me up. They asked me to give them all the valuables I had on me. They snatched everything, even my motorcycle," Rai stated in the FIR.

The motorcyclists made off with Rs 10,000, two mobile phones — one Samsung and one Reliance handset — and Rai's credit and debit cards.

"As my mobiles were snatched I had no option but to walk till the Sector-20 police station and lodge the complaint. With no police patrolling the area, I was terrified and had to give away the valuables I had," Rai said.

In another incident, Urmila Dalal, a resident of Noida's Sector-27, was robbed of Rs 5,000 and other valuables in Atta Market. Two motorcycle-borne assailants snatched her purse, which contained her documents, money and jewellery, she stated in a complaint filed in the Sector-20 police station. She is the wife of Lieutenant Colonel S N Dalal (Retd).

Heading: Oppn raises price pitch, Cong trumpets development - Indian Express
Content: The Anti-Terror Squad of UP Police has moved a Delhi court seeking custody of Mohammad Saif, the alleged Indian Mujahideen (IM) operative, wanted in cases related to the blasts in the state in 2006 and 2007. Arif, alias Abdul Qadeer, another alleged IM man, who was arrested in Lucknow recently, had spoken of Saif's role in the UP blasts during interrogation. Rajiv Krishna, Deputy Inspector General of ATS, said: "We have intimated our Delhi counterparts about taking Saif's custody. He is a key accused in the case of court blasts and those at the Sankatmochan temple in Varanasi. The interrogation of Saif would help us connecting the chain between IM and HuJI. Two of the five IM men arrested in Mumbai too had played a role in executing blasts here. We will initiate legal proceedings to seek their custody after the remand of the Mumbai police is over." Those arrested in Mumbai were Afzal Usmani, Mohammad Sadik Shaikh, Mohammad Arif Shaikh, Ahmed Zakir Shaikh and Shaikh Mohammad Ansar. The ATS would seek custody of Sadik and Arif.

Heading: Sheila’s BRT dream hits roadblock, Finance Minister Walia says no more funds - Indian Express
Content:
No sooner were election dates fixed for the Capital, the swords are out. Both the ruling Congress and rival BJP took guard against each other on Tuesday — and well within earshot of the media — to rattle off the various planks they hope will fire up voter sentiment by the time November 29 arrived.

The BJP's chief ministerial candidate Vijay Kumar Malhotra is confident of a comfortable win, tooting last year's success in the civic polls. 'Price rise' and 'terrorism' will be highlighted by his party as the Congress' failures.

The Congress, which rode to power on the politic of sky-high prices 10 years ago, is steering towards development this term, serenading its pet project — the regularisation of unauthorised colonies — as a crucial achievement. Delhi Congress chief J P Aggarwal said: "The state government has already subsidised LPG prices and taken measures to lower those of essential commodities. We won't harp on that. Look instead at the improved transport services and infrastructure facilities and the low-cost houses we provide under the the Rajiv Gandhi Awas Yojana."

He said nearly 40 lakh people had benefitted after unauthorised colonies were made legal, adding: "These people now have access to electricity, water and roads. We have done good work and should be back for the third term."

The Election Commission on Tuesday announced Assembly elections in the Capital on November 29. The counting will be on December 8. Delhi has a total of 70 Assembly seats, of which 58 are for candidates belonging to the general category and 12 for those of the reserved category. At present, the Congress has 47 seats in the Assembly, the Opposition BJP has 20, while one each are with the Nationalist Congress Party, the Janata Dal (Secular) and an independent.

Meanwhile, the BJP has finalised candidates for nearly 30 seats, V K Malhotra said, adding the leadership is looking at more women candidates this election. At present, there are only five.

These two parties apart, another key player this time might be Mayawati's Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP). The party's Delhi head Brahm Singh Bidhuri said, "We are ready and have announced candidates in 66 constituencies." The BSP leader added his party's main issue would be full statehood for Delhi.

Heading: Lovely rejects demand for 50 pc hike in school fees - Indian Express
Content:
At a time when elections for the State Assembly are round the corner, uncertainty shrouds the dream project of Delhi Chief Minister Sheila Dikshit — the Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) Corridor. The project now faces flak from none other than her Cabinet colleague, Finance Minister Ashok Walia.

Walia has refused to approve additional funds of Rs 119 crore demanded by the Transport department for the next phase of BRT from Moolchand flyover to Delhi Gate, citing poor planning as the main reason, a senior Transport department official told Newsline.

"The matter came up for discussion before the Expenditure Finance Committee (EFC) headed by Delhi Finance Minister Dr Ashok Walia last Tuesday," the official said.

Walia is learnt to have vetoed the proposal saying he will survey the first phase of the project himself and only then consider allocation of funds.

The Finance Minister also sought an explanation from RITES officials, consultants for BRT, for the poor planning, lack of smart signals and manning of strategic points which causes accidents every now and then.

When contacted, Walia said, "I have ordered to release Rs 12 crore for construction of a parking lot and a portion of the road to help reduce the traffic load on the Moolchand-Ambedkar Nagar stretch."

With regard to the transport department's demand of Rs 46 crore for erection of a foot-over-bridge, Walia said, "I have dismissed the demand and asked them what arrangements have been made for pedestrians at bus stops. The decision for release of funds will only be taken when the proper infrastructure will be created."

It may be noted that the state finance department had sanctioned Rs 215 crore for the Ambedkar Nagar-Delhi Gate stretch. Fifty per cent work on the project has already been completed on which Rs 115 crore have been spent.

After a slew of accidents on the BRT stretch caused a public furore, Dikshit had assured a review of the project and work was stopped three months ago.

To complete the project, the state transport department had demanded additional funds.

Heading: Alone in GK-I, 82-yr-old tied up, attacked with knife by robbers - Indian Express
Content:
The Directorate of Education will not concede to the demand of private, unaided schools to hike the fees by at least 50 per cent in order to clear arrears and pay the salary scale as recommended by the Sixth Pay Commission.

Delhi Education Minister Arvinder Singh Lovely said the request of schools for a fee hike will be reviewed and only after assessing their balance sheets will they be allowed to hike fees.

"The fee hike will depend on a case-by-case basis," he said. "If some school is in financial crisis, we will help."

Earlier this month, the National Progressive Schools Conference had sent a letter to the Directorate of Education for permission to increase fees by 50 to 60 per cent. The letter said schools' expenditure will increase by 50 per cent on an average.

Principal of Mahavir Model Senior School and Chairman of the National Progressive Schools Conference S L Jain said he was hopeful the government would consider their request.

The NPSC had approached the state under Section 17(3) of the Delhi Education Act to allow us to raise tuition fees.

"It is essential. If they don't do it, then the implementation of the Sixth Pay Commission will be delayed," Jain said. Though each school will determine the increase in fees, the average is expected to be Rs 2,000 per quarter. The hike could be effective as soon as November.

The schools will have to send in a proposal for the fee hike, which will then be evaluated by a committee, Lovely said.

There are about 110 schools under the NPSC. But Lovely said the government would not permit a blanket hike for all schools. School have been increasing tuition fee by 10 per cent every year and that money could be used for paying the arrears, he said.

"Where is all that money?" he said. "We have records of all the schools. Some schools really need the money. Some might not." But the statement is already drawing flak from private schools.

S K Bhattacharya, the president of the action committee for all associations of private schools in the city, said the minister must refrain from making such statements before reviewing the implications of the Sixth Pay Commission's recommendations.

"We have worked it out. It is going to be more than 60 per cent," he said. "We have to pay arrears for 32 months."

He said the private, unaided schools rely on tuition fees for disbursing salaries and any other expenditure unlike the government schools.

"What is our source of income? Fifty per cent is quite reasonable," he said.

Heading: Recession fails to dampen Capital glam quotient: twin fashion weeks on a roll - Indian Express
Content:
Here is yet another example that only serves to show how unsafe Delhi is for elders living on their own or depending on domestic helps for their everyday needs.

On Monday afternoon, 82-year-old Subhadra Sharma was tied up and beaten mercilessly by an agent through whom she hired domestic helps and his accomplices. They bound her in the kitchen and kicked several times on her stomach and face demanding money.

One of them even slashed her with a knife as he held it to her neck.

With blood clots in both eyes and chin, deep gashes on her skin, Subhadra said, "I kept asking them to stop hitting me but they would not listen."

Subhadra lives alone in her flat at R-8, Greater Kailash-I. For the last seven months she was in touch with a man called Vijay, an agent who hired helps for her. On Monday, he came to her house around 3 pm with a woman to help her around the house. Subhadra asked him to come later in the evening so that she could call in the police for verification.

Just then, Vijay asked for water and as Subhadra went to fetch it, the two of them and another unknown man entered her house, tied her hands and feet and carried away cash and valuables.

Divya Jyoti Sharma, Subhadra's daughter, who flew in from Mumbai, says jewellery and cash worth lakhs of rupees have been stolen. "I want those robbers to be caught so that I can see the faces of people who can be so cruel," she said.

A stoic Subhadra says, "It could have been worse. They could have broken my bones or killed me."

A case has been registered with the Greater Kailash police station and the police are investigating the matter.

Heading: 29/11: All set for the last lap - Indian Express
Content:
A slow market might not be the ideal storyboard for fashion designers but with two parallel fashion weeks, Delhi seems all set to live it up at least till the end of this week. While the Delhi Fashion Week (DFW), with its melange of about 30 designers and an exhaustive list of buyers took off at the Emporio Mall in Vasant Kunj on Tuesday, the bi-annual Wills Lifestyle India Fashion Week (WIFW) will go on the floor tomorrow (October 15) at Pragati Maidan.

With 79 designers in its kitty, the WIFW already has a lot up its sleeves. Even though the Fashion Design Council of India (FDCI) has outsourced the event management to Abhishek Mehta, he has apparently had generous inputs from designers like Rina Dhaka, Ritu Kumar, and Rajesh Pratap Singh on the show area set up.

The stakes are high for the designers too. This year, each designer has had to shell out Rs 1,20,000 for the show, including choreography, make-up, music, models, and stage set-up. With the buyer registration on an all-time high, organisers are confident the sales figures will not suffer.

While WIFW has names like La Rinascente, Harvey Nichols, Anthropologie on their list, DFW boasts of Isetan from Japan, Henri Bendel, Le Grand Bazar, Cannes, Seibu from Hong Kong.

Shows apart, there's also a lot happening on the fringes. There's the annual Fiama Di Wills Elite Model Look Contest that will see 15 probable models from across the country being flown to Delhi for an intensive grooming session. The winner will walk the ramp for designer brothers Shantanu and Nikhil's show.

Audi, the German luxury car brand, one of the major sponsors of the event, will also exhibit one of their models painted with designs by Vivienne Tam, a well-known Chinese designer based in New York. Tam will be showing in India for the first time.

Recession will have to wait.

Heading: Foreign hand adds exclusive touch to high-end realty market - Indian Express
Content:
BJP debars candidates who contested MCD elections from getting poll ticket

BJP leaders declared on Tuesday that no BJP candidate, who stood for MCD elections, would be given tickets for the present Assembly elections. Family members of these candidates have also been kept out of the race.

Delhi BJP president Dr HarshVardhan and BJP chief ministerial candidate Vijay Kumar Malhotra made the announcement on Tuesday in a media conference in the Capital. The BJP claims 3,500 to 4,000 candidates have been flooding the office with their CVs to get a berth. Only 70 candidates will be selected.

"All the 272 candidates who had run for municipality elections, regardless of whether or not they won, will not be given tickets this time. Their family members will also be debarred," said Dr Harsh Vardhan.

Senior leaders clarified all candidates had been clearly told last year that they will not be able to contest the Assembly elections. With this declaration, the hopes of many councillors who lost the municipality elections have come crashing.

Delhi Mayor Arti Mehra had been lobbying with senior BJP leaders including V K Malhotra for the ticket. MCD standing committee chairman, Vijender Gupta, has also been chasing a nomination. Asked if even Mehra's candidature would be rejected on the same grounds, Dr Harsh Vardhan said, "The fact that no councillor would be given a ticket is enough to answer this query," he said.

The decision might lead to unrest among party cadres.

"We will not accept defeat so soon. We will still fight for a ticket," said a senior MCD councillor.

The ballot plot: same issues, no new takes

PRICE RISE
Sheila Dikshit Congress: The party believes sky-high prices is a national issue and will not affect its chances in the Assembly elections. It is also 'proud' of the fact that Chief Minister Sheila Dikshit cushioned the hike in LPG through generous subsidies.

V K Malhotra BJP: A poster in its Delhi office declares: Mehenga ration, sasti jaan, yahi hai Congress ki pehchaan — indicating what the party's predominant refrain will be during campaign. Leader V K Malhotra said: "Prices of basic commodities have gone beyond the common man's pocket — all during the Congress' rule."

DEVELOPMENT
Sheila Dikshit Congress: "In the last ten years, this government has worked relentlessly on infrastructure. The result is there for all to see. There is more electricity and water, better roads in the city. The Capital's transport system is better, there is less pollution," state chief J P Aggarwal said.

V K Malhotra BJP: "The work on flyovers and the Metro, which the Congress passes off as its own achievement, began in our times. They might trumpet development, but in reality have not been able to lessen infrastructure problems in the city," BJP president Dr Harsh Vardhan said.

UNAUTHORISED COLONIES
Sheila Dikshit Congress: The Congress has questioned why the Opposition — despite being in power before — has overlooked unauthorised colonies. It is obvious the party is counting on the 40 lakh 'beneficiaries', as Aggarwal puts it, to shore up its chances in the November polls. "Why didn't the BJP do anything for them?" Aggarwal emphasised.

V K Malhotra BJP: On the other hand, the BJP claims the Congress' move to issue provisional certificates of regularisation to residents in 1,637 colonies is an 'eyewash'. Dr Harsh Vardhan said: "They didn't do it for the last 10 years, but only managed to pull it off a few months before the polls. Moreover, provisional certificates don't mean anything."

GOVERNANCE
Sheila Dikshit Congress: The party leadership has claimed its rule has largely been corruption-free and transparent. Aggarwal said the BJP's recent clamour about corrupt governance is conveniently aimed at the ballot, as it has never spoken up on the subject before.

V K Malhotra BJP: The Opposition, on the other hand, is adamant that the government's dealings in electricity has not been exactly smudge-free. Dr Harsh Vardhan said: "The Comptroller General of India's report says there there was a loss of Rs 12,500 crore in the privatisation of power. The Congress government's own report accepts this."

SECURITY
Sheila Dikshit Congress: The Congress believes the Capital is among many other cities that is on a terrorist's map. "We are committed to fighting terror, but the matter largely rests with the Centre. The BJP has forgotten that the Parliament attack and that on the Akshardham temple happened when they were in power at the Centre," said J P Aggarwal.

V K Malhotra BJP: Dr Harsh Vardhan replied: "The Congress government is both at the Centre and the state. But the party has not been able to make Delhi safe. It is called a city of rapists and incidents like the recent murder of journalist Soumya Vishwanathan is a reminder that all is not well. There is no proper system to check terrorism either."

Heading: Observing a champ from close quarters - Indian Express
Content:
The demand for exclusive housing options is no longer a necessity today, rather a fashion statement. Adding to this craze, major builders across Delhi and NCR are hiring internationally renowned teams (architects and interior designers) to offer world class designs. For instance, a single condominium at the Assotech Celeste residential towers in Noida, Sector 44, is equipped with internally accessible private elevators, an all-weather pool, an internationally styled kitchen with wet and dry places and a rooftop helipad. A team of renowned landscape artists, lighting consultants and interior decorators have been hired to deck up these condominiums that cost an average of Rs 4 crore each.

"The reason for foreign design teams collaborating on this project was simply due to the fact that the apartments cater to NRIs. The design aesthetics should therefore match international standards," reasons Ritesh Mishra, head of Corporate Communications, Assotech.

The 35-storey twin towers, which are slated for completion by September 2010, are ready to set new boundaries for luxury housing.

The interiors are its most striking feature. The furniture is customised and each floor has a separate yoga or meditation centre with private enclosures to host guests. The shades are muted with minimum furniture and a focus on open spaces. "The trend internationally is to keep the room clutter free, allowing free movement. We have even kept a lot of provision for natural lighting and applying principles of feng shui in the bedroom and bathrooms," says Rodney Ongswee Huat, senior project manager, Leo International, Bangkok, responsible for the interior designing. The firm has had prior experience in hospitality projects across Asia.

While Celeste Towers offer luxury housing, the upcoming 2-4 bedroom homes and penthouses of Millennium Spire Greens in Sector 37C, Gurgaon, focus on green architecture. The buildings adopt an elaborate rainwater harvesting system that partially reduce water woes, a comprehensive waste management and segregation set-up and an in-house sewage treatment plant.

"To prevent the building from heating up, we planted screens which cloaked the rise in temperature. These are simple ways to create comfortable indoor and outdoor living spaces and which have been used for centuries in India. We are simply reinterpreting them to face new challenges," explains Alan Hennessy, president, Groupe 6, a French architecture firm working on the residential area with designs that have an urban outlook.

Although the prices of the residential apartments range from Rs 50 lakh onwards, they have nothing to do with the choice of a designer. "A firm whose designs suit the needs of the project is selected. Obviously an internationally reputed firm will bring to the table more experience," says Ashish Bhalla, MD, Millennium Spire, a Singapore-based investment firm which has tied up with local builders for development projects.

The 'trump card' for the real state sector in India is the involvement of Malaysian architect, Dr Ken Yeang, known as the father of eco skyscrapers. The 1.6 million sq ft Millennium Edge eco-office complex coming up by 2010 in Manesar, Gurgaon, is the handy work of Yeang. The commercial project boasts of being operational 24x7, for 365 days, conserve water and cut down energy bills by 30 per cent. Our repeated attempts at reaching Yeang failed.

So if you desire exclusivity, start saving up for your dream home from today.

Heading: Abhinav shows second seed Bakshi the door - Indian Express
Content:
Caddying for Indian Open winner Liang, Delhi player Dipankar picked up a few tips

Their team of two began the morning with fist-pumps, and moved on to easy smiles as the lead stretched by afternoon. But with the win coming down to the last hole, their four-day stint finished with wild celebrations and whoops of joy. Living every moment of that last round of Liang Wen-chong's dramatic victory at the Indian Open this Sunday with the Chinese was Delhi boy Dipankar Kaushal, a full-time player, and first-time caddy.

For Kaushal, who scooped up the pint-sized Chinese after he sank the last-hole birdie, the title was nothing short of a personal victory. "It felt just terrific," he says, speaking to Sportline. "Just the way he had played through the week, I knew there was no way it was getting away from us."

But it almost did, as Liang gave up his huge four-shot lead before getting it back together with an error-less last two holes. The watchers were biting their nails, but Kaushal says their duo was never in doubt. "Liang is just too mentally strong a player. He knew just what he had to do, and despite two errors, the win was always in his hand," he says.

Kaushal trains under senior pro Amit Dube, who in turn is coached by Kel Llewellyn, Liang's coach, and that's how the idea of caddying propped up. "I had never caddied before. But Kel and Amit thought it would be a great chance for me to learn, and so we fixed this up.

"He's one of the best players around on the Asian Tour, and to get to see him from so close, to watch how he conducts himself, deals with things, was a huge learning experience," says Kaushal.

It turned out to be an experience of a lifetime, as the 22-year-old had the prime spot to watch Liang's record opening round of 12-under 60. "That was something else," says Kaushal. "He was in a zone of his own, and I had great fun that day."

Kaushal's own story is a little out of the ordinary too. A cricket player through his childhood, he only picked up golf clubs three years ago, on the insistence of his father. "My father asked me to give golf a try, and I was hooked from the first shot," says Kaushal, who now plays on the national amateur circuit. "I've been off the tour this season because I was in the USA for a training stint. I'll be playing the coming events," he says.

The professional tour is on his plan of action in another two years. He won't be short of inspiration.

Heading: Track One - Indian Express
Content:
Abhinav Prakash admitted to have tried doing a Sourav Ganguly after ousting second seed Srikant Bakshi 21-18, 24-22 in the quarter-final of the Delhi state ranking badminton tournament. While approaching the net for a customary handshake, he tried taking off his T-shirt when coach Surjit Singh told him to maintain decorum. The 19-year-old could not celebrate the way he wanted but there was no stopping a full house at the Punjabi Bagh badminton arena that erupted and a standing ovation to the young shuttler. Calling the sight unfamiliar would be an understatement, considering the current plight of Delhi badminton in the senior categories.

After getting a pat from 'Golu bhaiya' (Srikant Bakshi), Abhinav wasted no time in explaining his moment. "This is the biggest win of my career. I played him for the first time and I won. I continued with the rallies to tire him out and that's exactly what happened. Add to that the wrong judgement by Golu bhaiya when he was on game point in the second game. He also tried to finish off the game in a hurry," Abhinav said.

The u-16 National School Games silver medallist in 2004-05 was an underdog going into the match, given the fact that his opponent was Delhi state champion and former India No 2. Delhi Badminton Association vice president and Delhi coach Malvinder Dhillon called it a much-needed break for Abhinav. "He's been a promising player all through but his game was very negative. Today he played positively and the result was there for everyone to see. He needed this kind of a victory to reappear on the courts," said Dhillon.

"I was not satisfied with my recent performances. In the Delhi state badminton tournament at the Karnail Singh stadium I had lost to Himanshu Kharbanda in the preliminary rounds while in the JD Tytler tournament Devender Dhillon got the better of me. So, I had a point to make here," Abhinav said.

Heading: Everything in a Platter - Indian Express
Content:
The inaugural Delhi Fashion Week kicks off in the city — sans a ramp

Possibly one of a handful of female designers making menswear, Rajvi Mohan, 27, kicked off the maiden Delhi Fashion Week that started at the DLF Centre, adjacent to Emporio Mall, on Tuesday. The Delhi Fashion Week is small in scale, with less than 30 designers participating (at last count, the Wills India Fashion Week had over 70). However, on Day 1, things went off as they should — right from efficient valet parking to well-spaced out show area to food options, you can pick between AD Singh's new Japanese restaurant Ai and a more familiar Costa Coffee counter. There are teething issues, of course. Late starts apart, the ramp here is a flat strip of white cardboard (diligently covered with a white sheet at other times and guarded by a pack of ushers). "The idea was to make the shows compact and closer to the audience, so we decided to do away with the conventional ramp," says Geetanjali Kashyap of the Fashion Foundation of India (FFI).

Mohan made her first ever participation at a fashion week in the country with "Rat Pack Nirvana", a tribute to her fashion icon, Dean Martin. The Delhiite comes with impressive credentials, having trained with the famed Vivienne Westwood and studied at the Parson's School of Design, New York. Her collection, which has a hint of Indian prints, is otherwise inspired by the grunge look of the Forties and the Fifties and a generation of entertainers like Frank Sinatra, Sammy Davis Jr and Martin. "I wanted to do a line that would look at Martin's sense of dressing in an Indian context. This is what I felt it would be like," she said. There were front pleats and generous layering, intelligent panelling that highlighted the contrasts and an interplay of summer hues, from bright yellows to aster blues and wild limes.

Akshay Kumar and his costume designer Shabinaa Khan can pat themselves on the back for sparking off a trend. Mohan's show had a liberal sprinkling of trousers cut to the knee for more formal capris, a look that Kumar has made famous in his movie Singh is Kinng. We liked the jackets in particular, with their streamlined lapels and play on essential summer textiles like linen and stretch cotton. The only patchy part of the show was the fittings of some of the ensembles — a few sherwani bottoms looked like a cross between zoaves and fitted pajamas.

Abhijeet Khanna's collection, which came next, focussed on all things luxurious, even in these times of near-recession. His collection — an assortment of shift dresses, harem pants and tops, inspired by the Indian styling of French Rococo — was embellished with sequins and incorporated Indian embroidery in otherwise western silhouettes. Khanna had been design assistant to Manish Arora for over four years, and the affinity to Arora's sensibilities clearly shows. The fish-scale-patterned dress that ended the show was reminiscent of Arora's warrior collection.

The day also saw a fair presence of buyers. "We have commitments from 160 buyers and nobody has cancelled so far. It should be a fair turnout," said Sumeet Nair of FFI. While Khanna's show had quite a few buyers, the second half of the day was expected to have a stronger buyer presence. Those expected include Isetan from Tokyo, Ovo Studio from Madrid, Design Best from Bordeaux and Seibu from Hong Kong.

Heading: Fear of blasts, global meltdown keep shoppers away this festive season - Indian Express
Content:
Printed on LP records, the menu boasts something from everywhere

In case you hadn't noticed, the Indian fine diner Mystic Heights at New Friends Colony is no more. A month ago, it was reborn as an equally trendy restobar, Raga. The USP here is world cuisine in wholesome platters — from Turkish platters of kibbehs and shish touk to Italian pastas and Indian kebabs. And if you were wondering about the name, Raga is influenced by world music and has the menu printed on LP records. Phonograph records, by the way, are also called platters. Restaurateur Gaurav Khandelwal, 28, says, "Platters eliminate the hassle of ordering repeatedly. I thought world-cuisine platters would be the best bet," he says.

We started with a seafood platter (Rs 575) comprising generous portions of skewered shrimps and fish rolls, accompanied by a tartar sauce dip. The German platter (Rs 450) was robustly Teutonic, and comprised a meaty chicken breast stuffed with minced pork and cheese, laced with a garlic sauce dressing and accompanied by sautéed vegetable. The grilled chicken breast was tender and succulent, with the stuffing making it quite a mouthful. If only the vegetables weren't so limp!

The menu, unfortunately, tries to accommodate diverse tastes without focusing on getting a platter perfect. The experience of penne with mushroom (Rs 300), for instance, was ruined by the pasta being too bland. Even the ice-cream platter (Rs 145), that gets you scoops of vanilla, butterscotch and chocolate, could not boast of variety.

Meal for Two: Rs 1,000
Location: 15 Community Centre,
New Friends Colony
Contact: 41328184

Heading: Agreement signed to ease movement of vehicles in NCR - Indian Express
Content:
A month after the serial blasts in Delhi, the number of shoppers across the main Capital markets has seen an unprecedented dip. Despite a lot of companies offering whopping discounts, the pre-Diwali sales have gone down drastically. While customers are still wary of moving about freely, shopkeepers are uncertain if the festive season holds anything for them to cheer about.

GAFFAR MARKET, KAROL BAGH
Gaffar Market was the scene of maximum number of casualties in the September 13 attack. The once bustling and crowded market has seen a sharp drop in footfall since. "Sales have fallen and people still seem gripped in fear," said Gurpreet Singh of Satnam Pagri Store.

"It is hard to believe that Navratras have just gone by and Diwali is round the corner. The sales are 50 per cent less than last year," adds the owner of Shop Number 62.

And while many believe that the low turnout is because of the fear of a possible terrorist strike again, others attribute it to the slump in the stock market. "The pre-Diwali sales have been dampened by the fact that most of the shoppers are locals," a shopkeeper on Arya Samaj Road said.

For the determined shopper, however, blasts are not a deterrent. Ira Sharma, who was in the market when the blasts happened, is back shopping, but: "The blasts have made me more alert. I now look around twice in a public place."

To ensure security, volunteers, chosen from among the vendors, have been asked to keep vigil at every street. "Thirty-two such groups have been formed for the special market held on Monday, along with fifty for the daily market. In addition, a public address system has been put in place with 8-10 Delhi police personnel, supplemented by special forces, doing the rounds in the market," said Amarjit Singh, HSPO, Karol Bagh. 

With 28 CCTVs and eighteen private security guards been deployed to keep an eye on unattended objects, shopkeepers in this market still seem unsatisfied by the security arrangements.

CONNAUGHT PLACE
Bombs were found at several places here, including the Regal building. A month later, Suresh Kumar, one of the constables who found the bomb here, still stands guard. He is accompanied by four other policemen and supplemented by two or three more on weekends to handle the crowd.

At Regal Cinema, currently screening Hello, the cinematic version of Chetan Bhagat's best-selling novel, ticket sales have been restored. "While there was a dip in the first week following the blasts, sales have now picked up," says PS Mathur, the man at the ticket counter. The hall has notched up security, is not allowing any bags inside besides thoroughly frisking the visitors.

At the Central Park, which was recently opened to the public after the blasts, the crowd is very thin. "We are scared despite the security and make sure we do not stay at one place for long. We are scared to let our children wander off alone or touch unattended objects," said Rajesh Kumar Gupta, a visitor to the Central Park.

At Janpath, the shoppers are missing. Checking points with metal security detectors are in place at four points, manned by ten odd personnel from the Home Guard and additional members from the Delhi Police, along with 15 private guards appointed by the shopkeepers.

"Business is down by almost 70-80 per cent," says Rakesh Sood, owner of Shop No. 8 in the Mini Market, Janpath. "While the market used to be jam-packed on Saturdays, we have very little work now," Sood's neighbour Raj Wangley adds.

Sood says foreign tourists are clearly avoiding the place. "The markets seem deserted by 6-6.30 pm, whereas people would hang around till 9 pm earlier," he adds. Sanjeev Arora, president of the Janpath Bhawan Market Association adds, "The maximum footfall has been felt during the Puja holidays, which usually see a considerable number of Bengali shoppers. The reason could be the threat of a terrorist attack and the fall in the share market."

GK M-BLOCK MARKET
In the upscale M-block market, crowds seem conspicuously their absence and the parking lots are relatively empty.

"After the blasts, there has been a fall of 40-45 per cent in the customers that usually come to the market, and in the evenings, the market is simply desolated," said Sanjeev Garg of Garg Fabrico, a shop that has been in the market since 1970. Others are equally baffled. "Earlier, Saturday was the most crowded day of the week. People now do not come here, especially on Saturdays," says Dev Singh of the famous Prince Pan Corner.

The Traders's Association has notched up the security by making available four hand-held metal detectors. The security personnel manning the market have also been increased with four SSB personnel and five from the Delhi Police. The number of private security guards has been raised to 14. Though the number of CCTVs has been increased from 4 to 15, there seem to be occasional lapses with no one monitoring them, as Newsline found out during the visit to a Delhi Police booth in the market. The Traders' Association has also replaced dustbins in the market with trolleys that are carried periodically by the sweepers.

Heading: Turned away from hospital, woman gives birth on the road - Indian Express
Content:
The governments of Delhi, Haryana, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh have signed an agreement that will allow the public transport of one state in the National Capital Region to ply freely in the other states. The Reciprocal Common Transport Agreement (RCTA) was signed under the chairmanship of Dr M Ramachandran, Secretary, Ministry of Urban Development, here on Tuesday.

Ramachandran said this agreement would facilitate the movement of taxis and autorickshaws within NCR. People will be able to hire taxis and autorickshaws from the airport, railway stations and inter-state bus stops in Delhi and reach their destinations in NCR, such as Noida, Greater Noida, Ghaziabad, Faridabad, Gurgaon, Bahadurgarh etc.

"The agreement will also pave the way for arriving at mutual agreements on other important inter-state issues. The agreement will come into effect after all the constituent states of NCR will notify the agreement in respective gazettes to implement the same," he said. The agreement will ensure that autorickshaws and taxis will not be required to pay any additional passenger tax, road tax or permit charges.

Contract buses, however, will be required to pay passenger tax at the prevailing rates till a uniform tax structure is established by all the constituent states.

Vehicles will conform to Euro III norms and operate on CNG. They will be given a common colour code and logo for easy recognition so that vehicles, including contract carriage vehicles, are not stopped at borders in the NCR.

The colour code and logo wil be decided by the constituent states on a mutual agreement basis. The number of autorickshaws will be restricted through the issue of permits by respective state governments according to the number agreed and mentioned in this agreement.

The licence/permit fee/tax/counter signature fee for all contract carriages will be fixed by members of the participating states as per their own policies. Single point tax collection and uniform tax rates will apply to vehicles covered by contract carriage permits. Till uniform rates are decided, existing tax rates for collection of taxes may continue.

The constituent states are also in the process of finalising a Common Transport Agreement with regard to "stage carriages", which will facilitate commuter bus movement in NCR as part of the public transport system and help in reducing the movement of private vehicles in the region. This agreement is also expected to be signed shortly.

Heading: JNU says no to Lyngdoh poll guidelines - Indian Express
Content:
A woman gave birth to a baby girl on the road after a city hospital refused to admit her. The child was delivered on term and both mother and child are said to be doing fine.

While Babita Devi's family maintains hospital staff refused to admit her, hospital authorities insist the patient's husband was in an inebriated condition and took her away against medical advice. Babita (23) is from Bihar.

The incident took place at the India Population Project (IPP)-VIII Hospital, which is a World Bank project under the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD).

Babita's family said: "She (the nurse on duty) told us there was no doctor and asked us to leave. When we protested, she threatened to call the police," Angoori Devi, Babita's mother-in-law, said.

When the family insisted on admission or referral, the hospital staff told them to leave, she said. "Despite seeing her in excruciating pain, we were forced to bring her down from the first floor. She was already in labour and delivered the child near the hospital's exit gate," Suresh, her husband, said.

"After she delivered the child, we had to call a PCR van to have the baby and Babita admitted in hospital," Angoori Devi said.

The family maintains they had come to the hospital on Tuesday morning after Babita complained of stomach pain. "The nurse gave us a medicine and told us to come back when she went into labour," Suresh said.

Meanwhile, the MCD too has said the family had taken Babita away against medical advice. "The patient's husband was inebriated and created a ruckus inside the ward. The nurse told him to leave but he took his wife despite protests from the hospital staff," Dr V K Monga, chairman of MCD health committee, said.

Heading: Civic body set to revamp community centres - Indian Express
Content:
After inspiring others to follow suit by implementing the guidelines on college elections, framed by the Lyngdoh Committee, the Jawaharlal Nehru University has refused to officially put them into practice for the upcoming student union polls on November 3. The Election Commission will follow the constitution of the Jawaharlal Nehru University Student Union guidelines and the election will be based on the code of conduct dictated by it.

Prime among the Lyngdoh guidelines that will not be implemented in the JNU are the ones on the age limit and the ban on one candidate contesting more than once. The university also does not have any limit on the expenditure made during the campaigning. The code of conduct, however, allows students to use only handmade posters and photocopied pamphlets.

Sandeep Singh, president of Jawaharlal Nehru University Student Union (JNUSU) told Newsline that the age limit of 25 can be implemented only in universities with more undergraduate courses like the Delhi University. Because JNU caters more to researchers, most students are above the age of 25. "Besides, the Lyngdoh Committee guidelines should not be taken mechanically. Rather, we should look at the spirit of the committee in a positive manner and ensure a free and fair election," Sandeep said.

Sarada Prasanna Das, chairman of the Election Commission that has been set up temporarily to conduct the elections every year, said the election guidelines are completely based on the JNUSU constitution. "As the chairman, I cannot make any changes but if the new student union wants to incorporate the Lyngdoh guidelines, they will be able to do so," he said.

It is, however, clear that the any party that comes to power will abstain from doing so. "Already, many of the Lyngdoh Committee guidelines match those of JNU but some other clash with the constitution of JNUSU. So, after a lot of debate, it was decided that it will not be implemented," said Brundaban Mishra, a representative of Youth for Social Justice who is coordinating his party in the elections.

Heading: Court asks MCD to pay Rs 2.5 lakh for wedding fiasco - Indian Express
Content:
The grim and filthy community centres of the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) will soon be a thing of past. In a year's time, the corporation plans to turn all such centres into a major source of revenue.

The MCD has 204 community centres, which mostly have a vacant ground floor and a market on the first floor.

Under its plan, the MCD would renovate the ground floor of these centres, redo the walls and the ceiling. The community centres that fall in the A, B and C category colony will be made centrally air-conditioned.

"The MCD will rent out the ground floor and the terrace to the public for weddings and other social functions. Along the market on the first floor, a kitchen area will be created to cater to the needs of the social gatherings in the community centre," said an MCD official of the RP Cell.

To provide food at a subsidised rate, the MCD will also fix up its kitchen price. "The agency that will be given the contract for the kitchen will be permitted to create a temporary structure on the terrace and the agency will also have the parking rights of the community centre," said the official.

The renovation cost is expected to be about Rs 35 lakh per centre and the booking price of the centre is expected to rise one and a half times.

The corporation will be renovating these centres in BOOT (Build Own Operate and Transfer) basis.

The agency in contract with the MCD will be responsible for the upkeep and maintenance of the community hall and providing amenities like air-conditioning the community hall, water supply, electricity, sanitation, adequate number of toilets and a well-equipped and designed kitchen from its own funds.

The MCD is expected to earn revenue of Rs 40 crore per year from these community centres.

Heading: NSIT fest to showcase defence equipment - Indian Express
Content:
It was a day for which L D Bansal had been preparing for years. On his only daughter's wedding day, however, things went horribly wrong and, for no fault of his. A few hours before the big event, Bansal, a Delhi University employee, found the park he had booked as the marriage venue already occupied with tents put up for some other marriage.

Left with no other option, Bansal was forced to conduct the ceremony in a street behind his Karol Bagh residence.

The fiasco has proved costly for the MCD with a city court now ordering the civic body to pay Rs 2.5 lakh as compensation to Bansal. The court has also directed the MCD to make a detailed inquiry and institute criminal prosecution against erring officers. The court also pulled up the MCD for the delay in conducting an inquiry.

Taking note of the connivance between MCD officials and decorators, Additional District Judge Kamini Lau held the incident amounted to a breach of trust on part of the civic body.

"This is a fit case for detailed vigilance inquiry into the alleged connivance between MCD officials and the decorators," the ADJ said.

"No explanation is forthcoming as to why it took almost 15 months to initiate an inquiry into the incident and that too after the present suit was filed by the defendants. The detailed record of the inquiry conducted by the defendant has not been placed before this court," she added.

In his complaint, Bansal told the court he had booked Ajmal Khan Park with the MCD in November 2003, for his daughter's wedding after paying a sum of Rs 11,000. However, on the morning of January 22, 2004, the day of the wedding, when he went to the site to make the necessary arrangements, he was shocked to find that tents were already in place. On inquiring, he found that the tents belonged to one Grover Tent House that had made arrangements for some other marriage.

When he approached MCD officials, they refused to help, he told the court.

The MCD, in its defence, denied the allegations, claiming the ceremony had been organised at the same venue and the case was lodged by Bansal just to extract money. It also produced a set of certificates signed by its officers who were in charge of the affair at the time, to prove its case.

The court refused to accept the above and termed the argument "illogical".

Heading: Sonia dares Maya: I’m ready to go to jail - Indian Express
Content:
In a bid to strengthen laws dealing with terrorism, the Government has formed a committee under National Security Advisor M K Narayanan to study the recommendations made by the Administrative Reforms Commission (ARC) in this regard.

The committee, which has the Home Secretary, Defence Secretary and Law Secretary among its members, will study the ARC report and suggest to the Government whether and how the existing legal framework could be amended to incorporate recommendations made by the Veerappa Moily panel.

The findings of this committee would be referred to a Group of Ministers comprising, among others, Home Minister Shivraj Patil, External Affairs Minister Pranab Mukherjee, Defence Minister A K Antony and Law Minister H R Bhardwaj.

With the Parliament session starting later this week, the Government is keen to ensure that it is ready with whatever amendments are required to be made in the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act to firmly deal with terror-related incidents.

Patil told The Indian Express editorial team at its Idea Exchange programme on Tuesday that the Government did not mind strengthening the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act but certain suggestions, like making confessions before police as admissible evidence in court, which were present in some previous terror laws and also recommended by the ARC, were not acceptable.

"Any law has to be acceptable to the public in order to be effective," he said.

Patil said the Government was also opposed to suggestions to shift the burden of proof from the prosecution to the defence and relaxing the norms for electronic surveillance like telephone interception of terror suspects to monitor their activities. Both these suggestions have been made by the ARC as well in keeping with its stress on dealing with terror-related crimes in a much more stringent manner than normal crimes.

The ARC, in its eighth report — titled Combating Terrorism, it was released for public last month — had said that "a comprehensive and effective legal framework to deal with all aspects of terrorism" needed to be enacted.

Each of the recommendations made in the report, whether they pertained to stringent bail provisions, or increasing the period of detention or making confessions before police as admissible evidence, was exactly similar to the infamous POTA, repealed by the UPA government months after it came to power in 2004.

Meanwhile, the Government is all set to bring in a modified Communal Violence Bill in the upcoming session after incorporating the suggestions made by the Standing Committee. The Bill, seeking to create a special law to deal with incidents of communal violence, was introduced in Parliament in 2005 and referred to the Parliamentary Standing Committee.

Heading: Rajya Sabha polls to test SP-Cong electoral affair - Indian Express
Content:
Lands in 'karmabhoomi' Rae Bareli, says no one can stop me

Unfazed by the Mayawati government's moves to scuttle her visit to Rae Bareli, Congress president Sonia Gandhi today landed in her Lok Sabha constituency, calling it her "karmabhoomi" and declaring she was "ready to go to jail" for the sake of development.

"Rae Bareli and Amethi have been the karmabhoomi of Feroze Gandhi, Indira Gandhi and Rajiv Gandhi. It is also Rahul and my karmabhoomi. Rae Bareli and Amethi are like my home. Can anyone prevent me from coming home? No one can," she told reporters in Lalganj.

Taking a swipe at Chief Minister Mayawati, Gandhi said that like the rail coach factory in Rae Bareli, allotment of land for which was cancelled by the UP government, several other schemes were being blocked by the state. "There are over a dozen such development projects that the Central government has funded and plans to bring to the state. But in each, the state government has put some hindrance or the other," she said.

Gandhi declined comment on the cancellation of land allotment for the rail coach factory. "The matter is now before the court, I will not make any comments."

But she made it clear that her party would battle it out with the Mayawati government even if it meant going to jail. "We will not sit idle. Our state Congress wing will organise protests against the attitude of the government. If required, even I am willing to go to jail."

Despite Section 144 being imposed in the district to foil her planned rally, the administration failed to stop people from collecting in large numbers to greet Gandhi. Even the route of her cavalcade was changed minutes before her plane touched down at the Fursatganj airfield. At the coach factory site, people told her they were all for the factory.

Maya will be in race for PM post, says Karat
KOLKATA: Asked if his party would back Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Mayawati as the next Prime Minister, CPM general secretary Prakash Karat on Tuesday said: "The BSP is an important political party ruling the largest state in our country. We expect them to fare well in the Lok Sabha polls. It will depend on the mandate and she will be among the ones." Karat said the CPM's strategy for the coming general elections would be one of "defeating the BJP and rejecting the Congress".

Heading: On an average, CM transfers two officers daily - Indian Express
Content:
The proposed electoral alliance between the Samajwadi Party (SP) and the Congress will face its first test during the biennial Rajya Sabha (RS) elections scheduled for November 21.

Ten members of the RS in the state will complete their term on November 25. These include four members of the SP, three of the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP), Rajnath Singh and Mukhtar Abbas Naqvi of the BJP and Akhilesh Das, a former Congress member who had resigned from the membership of the House and joined the BSP.

The electoral rules of RS ensure that only 401 existing MLAs of the UP Assembly are authorised to cast their votes during the elections. A candidate requires 37 first preference votes of MLAs to win the election. It means that the SP with 94 MLAs in the Assembly can comfortably get two of its candidates elected. It will still leave 20 spare votes for the party. The Congress with 21 legislators will need at least 16 votes of the SP for getting its one candidate elected for the Rajya Sabha.

SP sources said the party could consider supporting the Congress candidate in RS polls if the party extends support to its candidate in the UP Legislative Council (LC) polls scheduled for January 2009.  Twelve members of the LC will complete their term on January 30 next year.

With 217 MLAs in the Assembly, the BSP can comfortably send its five members to the RS, while the sixth candidate can also be elected with the help of 22 spare first preference votes and remaining second preference votes. Three BSP Rajya Sabha MPs will complete their term on November 25, of which Isam Singh has already been disqualified from the membership of the House.

It means the BSP is likely to get six seats, Samajwadi Party two, BJP one and with the SP's help, the Congress may also get a seat.

The Samajwadi Party stands to loose two members since its four  members will be completing their terms and the party could send this time only two members. The SP members who are completing their tenure are Amar Singh, Abu Asim Azami and Uday Pratap Singh. The fourth member, Shahid Siddiqi, has already left the party and joined the BSP. The rebels in the SP, however, could affect the party's calculations. Two SP MLAs have recently joined other parties while many others are fence sitters and may opt for the best bargain during the RS polls.

SP legislator Gauri Shankar (Lucknow ) has crossed over to the BSP and is likely to contest the next Lok Sabha polls from Etawah constituency, while Sandip Agarwal (Moradabad) had joined the BJP recently during the Sankalp rally of L K Advani.

The role of the eight Independent MLAs and small parties like Rashtriya Lok Dal, hence, becomes crucial in the Rajya Sabha polls, as all the major contenders will need their votes.

Heading: ‘Maya lights her parks but keeps state in dark’ - Indian Express
Content:
In the last one month, over 60 IAS and PCS officers have been transferred in the state

Almost a month has passed since Governor T V Rajeswar spoke about the irrational and frequent transfers in UP during the Governors' Conference in New Delhi, which was followed by a public rebuttal from Chief Minister Mayawati.

But it seems that nothing has changed as bureaucrats continue to get shifted almost on a daily basis.

In the last one month, over 60 IAS and PCS officers have been transferred, which when counted on a daily basis comes to two transfers a day. For obvious reasons, no official is ready to comment on the issue.

After Mayawati came to power, she had promised to stop this practice. She had formulated a transfer policy and constituted a Service Board for taking up such matters.

On May 15, the government had issued an order, stating that all transfers, relating to department heads, divisional and district-level officers should be completed between May 15 and June 30 and that there would be no transfers after June 30.

The order also said: "If transfer is inevitably required in any special circumstance, the permission of the Chief Minister should be sought in such cases."

It also said that transfers after June 30 should be done only under unavoidable circumstances.

As claimed by Principal Secretary (Appointment) Kunwar Fateh Bahadur: "The transparent transfer policy does not cover the IAS officers." Therefore, transfers of IAS and PCS officers have been carried out even after the June 30 deadline.

IAS officer R C Srivastava has been shifted 11 times since Mayawati came to power. There are IAS officers like Rohit Nandan, K Chandramauli, Pankaj Agarwal, Balwinder Kumar and Govindan Nair, who have been transferred four to five times in the last 17 months. The list of officers who have been transferred three or four times is a long one.

A senior IAS officer said that the state government was also sitting on the Central recommendations regarding changes in IAS cadre rules. The proposed changes will make it mandatory for senior officers on important posts such as Principal Secretaries, Commissioners and District Magistrates to have a minimum tenure of two years at one post.

Under the Mayawati regime, the UP IAS Association, too, which was a vibrant body and had even named most corrupt officers among its ranks, has become almost defunct.

Forget taking up the cudgel to highlight the issue of frequent transfers, the association has even failed to hold its annual event — the IAS Week. The website of the association that has a section of "transfer postings" is silent on the issue and the web page is blank.

During the Mulayam Singh's regime, the same association had passed a resolution seeking withdrawal of the state government's power to suspend them.

Through another resolution the association had demanded fixed tenures for chief secretary as well as principal secretaries of all key departments. The recommendations are pending with a committee for over two years. Regarding the transparency issue, one has to check the official website of Appointment department.

The site has a section called "transfer watch" that offers the options to find out latest to date-wise transfers.

Click on it and a message pops up saying — "The service at present is under construction."

Heading: State police seek Saif’s custody to trace the IM-HuJI link - Indian Express
Content:
Making a scathing attack on the Mayawati government over the poor power situation in the state, the members of the Electricity Monitoring Committee of Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council said the incumbent government is more bothered about providing electricity to Chief Minister's pet projects.

Chairman of the committee Dayaram Prajapati said: "In a state which is facing acute power crisis, a large quantity of electricity is being provided to Kanshiram Sthal, Ambedkar Maidan and Ramabai Park in Lucknow and the ruling party is least bothered about the deplorable power scenario in other parts of the state." On Tuesday, the committee visited Kanpur to take stock of the power situation.

Holding the ruling Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) responsible for the poor power scenario, Prajapati said if electricity supply to "unwarranted projects" is stopped with immediate effect then only the power situation in the state would improve.

"The committee has asked various power distribution companies in the state to hand over the details of power supply that are given to them and the amount of electricity being misused," he said, adding that a report in this regard would be handed over to the Chairman of the Legislative Council.

On the issue of wrong billing, he said that the Electricity department employees are either directly or indirectly involved in the racket.

"For last many years, departmental clerks with the billing section deliberately prepare wrong bills, as it provides them with an opportunity to negotiate with complainant and earn money through illegal means," Prajapati added. Taking a serious note of the issue, the committee members has called for a list of clerks who have been working with the billing section for past several years.

"We will recommend the state government to lodge a case against clerks who are found guilty of corruption," Prajapati said.

Annoyed by the use of sub-standard products by the electricity department, Prajapati said that a letter in this regard would be written to the State Energy Minister, Ramveer Upadhyay. "If the state energy department fails to take an action in 15 days, the Electricity Monitoring Committee will probe the matter," he said.

He added companies providing sub-standard electrical equipment will be blacklisted and will not be entertained in future projects.

Other members of the committee, including Ravi Pappu Singh, Anil Raju Singh, Mohan Lal Khattar and Khwaja Haleem, also held the state government responsible for the poor power situation in the state.

Heading: Clerics’ call for protest divides Azamgarh Muslims - Indian Express
Content:
The Anti-Terror Squad of Uttar Pradesh Police has filed a petition at a New Delhi court, seeking custody of alleged Indian Mujahideen operative Mohammad Saif. Saif is accused of carrying out several blasts that rocked UP in 2006 and 2007.

UP Police said that Arif alias Abdul Qadeer, another alleged IM man who was arrested in Lucknow recently, had confessed to Saif's involvement in the UP blasts during his interrogation.

Deputy Inspector General of ATS Rajiv Krishna said: "We have intimated our Delhi counterparts about taking the custody of Saif. He is a key accused in the UP court blast case and also the explosion that took place at Sankatmochan temple in Varanasi. Saif's interrogation will help us in connecting the chain between IM and HuJI."

Krishna said that the state police will soon initiate legal proceedings to get the custody of two alleged IM operative arrested by Mumbai police.

"Two of the five IM men, Mohammad Sadik Shaikh, Mohammad Arif Shaikh, arrested in Mumbai too had played a role in executing blasts here. We will initiate legal proceedings to seek their custody after the remand of the Mumbai police were over," the DIG said.

Krishna said they decided to name Saif and Ariz alias Junaid in the blast cases following Arif's confession. Arif had revealed specific information about Saif's role in the court blast at Lucknow and Ahmedabad blasts, the DIG said.

Sources in the ATS said the interrogation of Arif helped them in collecting evidence, corroborating his journeys between Lucknow and Delhi and Delhi and Ahmedabad before the blasts.

Heading: High Court to LDA: What’s the need to close three roads? - Indian Express
Content:
The issue: Killing of muslim youths in delhi encounter

The Muslim community in Azamgarh is divided over an agitation called by the newly-constituted Ulema Council against the killing of Muslim youths in the Delhi encounter and the string of arrests that followed in connection with several blasts in the country. The council has decided to hold a one-day protest on October 20.

The Muslim Yuva Manch and Madarsa Imamiya of Azamgarh claimed that most of the clerics, including the Imam of Jama Masjid of Azamgarh, have agreed to boycott the protest. They added that none of the members of the community would join the protest.

Convener of the council, Maulana Aamir Rashadi Madani, however, said: "We are trying to bring together those who are opposing our programme. If someone does not join us, it will not affect the protest."

Asked about the Imam of Jama Masjid, whose name figures among the members of the council, Madani said: "I am not aware if the Imam has backed out from our programme. He had agreed to join us." Clerics like Maulana Jauhar Ali of Madarsa Imamiya, Sinhi in Azamgarh hinted that they backed out of the protest since it had political overtones. "The clerics are not supposed to tread on the politicians' track," Maulana Ali said, adding, " The decision to organise a protest was taken by a group of clerics and the madarsa will stay away from this."

Convener of Muslim Yuva Manch, Qazi Arshad Wafi said: "We will ensure that common people do not join the programme."

Maulana Madani was imprisoned in 2001 after a case under various sections of the IPC, including the one for disturbing communal harmony, was registered against him in Azamgarh. The action was taken after the Union Home Ministry had declared a nationwide ban on SIMI. The case is still pending after a stay ordered by the High Court on the legal proceedings.

Heading: HC questions LDA for renaming Smriti Upwan after Kanshi Ram - Indian Express
Content:
Police barrack, parking space For Ambedkar Sthal

A day after the Lucknow Development Authority (LDA) Board decided to change land use of 900 sq m area at Gomti embankment to make way for a police barrack, a Lucknow Bench of Allahabad High Court asked the body why three roads around Ambedkar Memorial were to be closed to provide for the barrack and the parking space.

Hearing a public interest litigation (PIL) challenging the closure of roads, the Bench, comprising Justices Pradeep Kant and Vedpal, expressed dissatisfaction over closure of roads for any construction work. The PIL was filed by Gomti Nagar Jankalyan Mahasamiti.

The state government has planned to block the roads to make way for parking space for visitors to the Ambedkar Memorial and a police barrack for security purposes.

In the previous hearing held on September 23, the Bench had asked the state government and LDA to review its decision to close roads. It had also asked the LDA to see if the barrack could be shifted to another place. On Tuesday, the LDA in an affidavit submitted that following a review, it has decided against any change in the plan.

Chief Standing Counsel Devendra Upadhyay, arguing for the LDA, apprised the court that the authority's Board has decided to go ahead with a police barrack on the Gomti embankment and will give passage to commuters through Sahara Sahar.

B K Singh, the petitioner's counsel, told The Indian Express: "The court has asked the LDA to submit a reply within the next week."

On Monday, the LDA Board had approved the proposal for changing the land use of 900 sq m area — on which the police barrack is being constructed — from public utilities and services.

In its meeting held on September 6, LDA Board had also changed the land use of two other roads from "road transport" to "public utilities" to make way for development of parking slots.

Heading: BHU student found dead in her hostel room - Indian Express
Content:
A Lucknow Bench of the Allahabad High Court on Tuesday sought an explanation from the Lucknow Development Authority (LDA) for developing the 80-acre land of Smriti Upwan for cultural activities and renaming it Kanshi Ram Sanskritik Sthal.

The Bench comprising Justices Pradeep Kant and Abhinav Upadhyay sought the explanation during a hearing of a public interest litigation (PIL) filed by one Ashok Dev Yadav.

Yadav had challenged the LDA's plan to develop Sanskritik Sthal in Smriti Upwan and name it after Dalit icon Kanshi Ram.

While former Advocate General Virendra Bhatia argued as the petitioner's counsel, Chief Standing Counsel Devendra Upadhyay contested the case from the LDA's side.

Bhatia argued that the 101-acre area, on which Smriti Upwan was being developed, is part of a green belt. While plantation work was conducted and Kargil Pushkarini developed along with a water body in a 21-acre area, the remaining 80-acre land was lying unused.

The LDA had planned to develop Kanshi Ram Sanskritik Sthal on the 80-acre are, citing the need for an open and safe place to hold cultural activities like the Lucknow Festival, he added.

After hearing the arguments, the Bench directed the LDA to reply why the 80-acre area was renamed as Kanshiram Sanskriti Sthal. The next hearing of the case will be held on October 17.

On Monday, the LDA Board had approved the development of Kanshi Ram Sanskritik Sthal at the cost of Rs 90 crore.

Heading: Applied for connections 2 decades ago, farmers want load enhanced - Indian Express
Content:
A medical student of the Banaras Hindu University (BHU) was found dead in her hostel room in Varanasi on Tuesday. The police claimed Shailly Tyagi, a post-graduate student of anaesthesia, committed suicide by injecting poisonous drug.

Assistant SP (Varanasi) J Ravinder Gaur said: "We have recovered an empty ampoule and a used syringe beside the body of Tyagi, who belonged to Ghaziabad. The room was bolted from inside and circumstantial evidence suggested the girl had ended her life by injecting the drug." The motive behind the suicide is yet to be known, as no note has been recovered from the spot.

Station Officer of Lanka police station, A K Verma, said: "The incident came to light around 5 pm when Shailly's batchmate, knocked on her door at Kasturba Hostel." When Agarwal did not receive any response, she informed the warden who, in turn, asked the watchman to break into the room.

Heading: PM for Amritsar seat: Leaders submit resolution to observer - Indian Express
Content:
Though it is late by nearly 18 years, farmers who had applied for tubewell connections way back in 1990 will shortly hear good tidings, as 12,000 pending applications will be cleared by the PSEB this year.

But farmers are still unhappy. Hardev Singh Sandhu, president of Kirti Kisan Union, said, "In 1990, we had applied for a load in the range of 3 and 5 horse power (HP), which will now be of no use, as the water level has gone down. Now, minimum load of any motor is 7.5 HP, and it can go as high as 20 HP. The PSEB should release connections on enhanced load because the delay was not on part of farmers."

A deputation of farmers met Ludhiana (Central) Chief Engineer BS Bath and would also meet the PSEB chairman. Sandhu said all the pending cases were of small and marginal farmers who had been taking connections on rent or had even given their land on contract.

Tarlochan Singh, another farmer, said, "In Ludhiana and around, the minimum load required is 10 HP, while in Moga it's not less than 20 HP. So the 5-HP connection will be of no use."
