HS Brar, PSEB, Member (Distribution), said, "We will see that their load is enhanced after looking into their demand.

"However, farmers are adamant that they would not pay extra charges, as they have already suffered the extended delay.

Meanwhile, the release of 12,000 connections will increase the load, leading to more cuts.

Heading: ‘GM crops unhealthy’ - Indian Express
Content:
With Navjot Sidhu and Vinod Khanna as MPs in Amritsar and Gurdaspur, respectively, the Congress is working hard to find candidates who can give a tough fight to the celebrities

Demanding that Prime Minister Manmohan Singh contests the parliamentary polls from Amritsar, the urban and rural units of Amritsar district Congress today submitted a resolution to Congress observer GS Sapra, who has been sent by Congress high command to look for candidates for Amritsar and Gurdaspur parliamentary seats.

As many as seven observers have been assigned the job to find winnable candidates. The observers are also compiling information related to party cadres and strengths and weaknesses of the SAD-BJP, said sources.

Talking to The Indian Express today, Sapra, an MLC in Mumbai and vice-president of the Mumbai Congress, said, "A separate resolution by the Congress councillors was submitted. I have observed that party cadres in Amritsar want that only Manmohan Singh should contest from there. I will convey the feelings to the high command and AICC general secretary Margaret Alva."

With cricketer-turned-politician Navjot Sidhu and Bollywood actor Vinod Khanna as MPs in Amritsar and Gurdaspur, respectively, the Congress is working hard to find candidates who can give a tough fight to the celebrities. "I have been asked by Alva to lay special focus on these constituencies," Sapra claimed.

The other observers selected by Congress high command for Punjab are Maharashtra MLA Yousuf Abrani (for Anandpur Sahib and Hoshiarpur), Mumbai MLC Subhash Chawan (for Ludhiana and Fatehgarh Sahib), MLA Jagannath Shetty (for Patiala), MLA Nitin Raut (for Faridkot and Ferozepur) and Mumbai Congress general secretary Nitin Deshpande (for Jalandhar and Khadoor Sahib). While a few of the observers started the exercise today, others are expected to do it in a couple of days.

Interestingly, Punjab Pradesh Congress Committee (PPCC) chief Mohinder Singh Kaypee said he was not aware of any such exercise being carried out in Punjab.

Congressmen root for Raninder

Dr Sanjay Patil, who is observer for Bathinda and Sangrur constituencies, interacted with Congress workers, who proposed the name of Raninder Singh, son of former Punjab chief minister Capt Amarinder Singh, for Bathinda LS seat. "During the assembly polls, he had led the party efficiently in the region and is best suited to contest from here," said Ajaib Singh Bhatti, Congress MLA from Nathana.

Heading: Problems crop up due to late sowing - Indian Express
Content:
Canada-based microbiologist Dr Shiv Chopra and Kheti Virasat Mission (KVM) today demanded a ban the use of genetically-modified (GM) crops, including Bt Brinjal, in the country.

Chopra said its consumption would adversely affect people's health and environment. Talking to mediapersons along with Executive Director of KVM Umendra Dutt here today, Dr Chopra said he was here as part of his mission to make farmers aware about the adversities of using GM food.

He said, "Genetic engineering is quite similar to chemical pesticides, which are being promoted by various MNCs. GM crops can affect human reproductive system. World over, only 12 countries have allowed GM crops," added Dr Chopra.

Notably, in Punjab, only Bt cotton is being cultivated after genetic modification, but the trials have been conducted on rice and potato too.

Heading: Hoardings dot Mohali-Kharar NH-21 - Indian Express
Content:
The enforced delay in paddy sowing has thrown up a slew of problems. Moisture content in paddy harvested this year will keep the farmers and the state government jittery for the next few weeks, when the mandis will be deluged with the produce.

The mandis have received 10 lakh metric tonnes of paddy less than what it received in the corresponding period last year. Gurinder Singh, a farmer from Moga, said, "The late sowing has resulted in browning of the grain. While our yield is good, discolouration and high moisture content, which almost 25 per cent, have affected the procurement. This needs to be checked in the next season."

Another farmer, Gurraj Singh, said, "The pest attack has been severe in some cases. This is the first time that paddy has been sown late, so the problems have baffled farmers."

Meanwhile, to ensure smooth paddy procurement, Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal has sent 13 principal secretary-level officials to various districts. The MDs and senior officials of all the five procurement agencies too have been allotted headquarters and the officials have been asked to stay put there instead of their offices in Chandigarh.

B S Sidhu, Director, Agriculture said, "The moisture content is because of high humidity level. This year, October is not dry as usual. A few changes in the ordinance are being considered, such as a different dates for sowing paddy in waterlogged areas. June 10 will not be binding for the farmers who will adopt new methods of cultivation such as direct seeding or bed planting."

Meanwhile, the price for PUSA 1121 has increased. Dr P S Rangi, who has been touring the state mandis, said, "This variety is picked up by the exporters and its price in the international market is very high."

Sukhbir demands Rs 300 bonus

Akali Dal president Sukhbir Singh Badal called upon the Centre to announce a bonus of Rs 300 per quintal. In a letter to Union Agriculture and Food Minister Sharad Pawar, the SAD president said Punjab farmers had risen to the nation's clarion call to produce a record harvest this year and contributed over 30 lakh MT extra wheat to the Central pool as compared to last year. "This extra procurement has contributed significantly to maintain food security at a time when the world is witnessing food shortage and the international prices are on a rise," he added. He demanded an MSP of Rs 1,400 per quintal. He asked the Union government to relax the ban on the export of non-basmati rice in view of the bumper paddy crop and buffer stock. He also urged the Union Food Ministry to send a team to Punjab to examine the problem of high moisture content due to late rains in the region.

Meanwhile, the Punjab unit of Bharti Kisan Union (BKU) accused the Centre of deliberately fixing a low minimum support price (MSP) of paddy this year. "In the name of checking inflation, the Centre fixed MSP of Rs 850 and 880 per quintal as against the recommendation of Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP) for Rs 1,000 and Rs 1,050," Punjab BKU chief Balbir Singh Rajewal said here.

Heading: Newlywed dies in hit-and-run accident - Indian Express
Content:
Supreme Court, High Court rulings flouted with impunity

No one seems to care for the directions issued by the Supreme Court and the Punjab and Haryana High Court to free all highways and important roads of hoardings and display boards. Huge hoardings and neon signboards dot one of the busiest highways — the National Highway-21 that passes through Mohali and Kharar.

These colourful hoardings, which attract the attention of drivers, can be seen at strategic traffic intersections and bus stands. Besides several multinational and national companies, local concerns have also jumped on the advertisement bandwagon on the national highway to compete with rivals.

With the open green fields along the highway fast turning into concrete jungles, access and approach roads connected to the highway grossly violate the provisions of the Punjab Regional and Town Planning and Development Act, 1995, to which the Punjab Scheduled Roads and Controlled Areas Restriction of Unregulated Development Act, 1963, was merged.

Besides the access and approach roads, all constructions within the restricted areas along the highway amount to encroachment.

Hundreds of such encroachment and violations detected so far in the successive surveys conducted by the Forest department, PWD and the Kharar Municipal Council have so far escaped punitive action.

Among the violators are several mega-housing projects, colonies, professional colleges and filling stations on the NH-21 and the Kharar-Banur road, also a scheduled road.

On the around 20-km Balongi-Kurali stretch of the highway, Newsline found a number of hoardings, neon signboards and display boards erected by various companies, societies and individuals.

Almost all upcoming colonies, educational institutions and private concerns have put up boards to attract the attention of the passers-by. Bus stops at Balongi, Kharar and Kurali are the places where most bill boards can be seen.

It is clear that state agencies have overlooked the directions issued by the Supreme Court in 1997 and the Punjab and Haryana High Court in 1998 on regulating vehicular traffic, with "greater emphasis on the removal of all hoardings and advertisement boards from the roads, which were considered hazardous and disturbance to safe traffic movement".

Complying with the High Court's directions, the state government had long ago undertaken a massive drive to remove the signboards, hoardings, neon signboards, advertisement boards facing the highways, main roads, side roads and lanes. A large number of such commercial and other hoardings and their supporting structures were removed in Mohali and Kharar after July 1998.

In the absence of follow-up action, however, things are back to pre-1998 days.

Heading: PNB told to pay Rs 5,000 for losing cheque - Indian Express
Content:
A Newly-wed woman died while her husband was seriously injured after a speeding unidentified vehicle rammed their scooter near Shekhpura village in Kharar around 4.30 pm on Tuesday.

Shivani, in her mid-20s and a resident of Patiala, succumbed to injuries at PGI, Chandigarh. Her husband Gujinder Kumar, aged around 30 and a resident of Ward 7, Kurali, is struggling for life at the hospital, said investigating officer Daleep Singh.

Gujinder told the police that he failed to identify the vehicle or note down its registration number as he had covered his eyes with a cloth to shield them from a sudden dust storm.

A case under Sections 279 and 304-A of the IPC has been registered. The police have launched a manhunt to trace the vehicle and its driver.

Shivani and Gujinder were married on October 4. The couple was returning home to Kurali from Chandigarh after meeting Gujinder's brother.

Gujinder was employed as a salesman with a chemist in Chandigarh while Shivani was a housewife.

"She was still wearing the traditional chura in both her arms and heena was applied on her hands and feet," added the investigating officer .

Heading: ‘Use natural elements in designing homes’ - Indian Express
Content:
Holding the Punjab National Bank (PNB) guilty of deficiency in services after they lost a cheque worth Rs 20,000, the District Consumer Grievances Redressal Forum has directed the bank to pay Rs 5,000 as compensation to the complainant.

The bank has also been told to pay Rs 500 as the cost of litigation.

The complainant, Ram Krishan, a resident of Dhanas, deposited a cheque worth Rs 20,000 with the PNB. The cheque was drawn at the Panchkula Central Cooperative Bank on November 7, 2007 for encashment. But the complainant alleged that the amount was never credited to his account.

Despite numerous queries by Krishan regarding the status of the cheque, he was never given a satisfactory reply.

In its reply, the bank admitted that the cheque was deposited with them and sent for collection.

The amount was not paid by the Panchkula Central Cooperative bank as "payment was stopped by the drawer".

However, the original cheque was not received from the payee branch despite repeated visits and may have been misplaced, said the bank's counsel.

It was stated that the complainant was advised to take an electronic image of the truncated cheque, which is valid for all intent and purposes as per amendment of the Negotiable Instrument Act, 1881, but he never came to collect the same.

The forum found that the bank's offer to issue the truncated cheque proves that they lost the cheque in transit and that amounts to deficiency in services.

Heading: Safety on campus: PU hires trained security staff after private agencies fail to deliver - Indian Express
Content:
Seminar on 'Intelligent & Sustainable Buildings' held

Imagine a house where the first rays of the sun light up the rooms, minimal need for air-conditioning and greenery all around — welcome to the Age of Sustainable Housing.

"A building should be constructed in a manner that it does not face west. This will help reduce the load on air-conditioning," said Professor Sohan Lal from Chandigarh College of Architecture.

He was talking on the sidelines of a seminar on 'Intelligent and Sustainable Buildings' organised by the Bureau of Indian Standards on Tuesday.

"Making use of natural elements in houses is a technique that our ancestors used in abundance and with success. However, over the years we seem to have forgotten much of it," added Lal.

According to the professor, there are active and passive elements in a building. While the passive include elements that cannot be changed like the shape of a building, active elements are those which can be adjusted as per needs.

For example, in case of a circular room the amount of light required is less. Therefore, by making optimum use of glass, low-intensity lights can be used.

"The sun and wind are two important elements that take care of the thermal environment of a building. These need to be tapped in order to avoid mechanical heating and cooling," added Lal.

Architect Sangeet Sharma said: "Provisions for natural ventilation should be made while designing buildings. The materials used in construction should be eco-friendly and recyclable. A range of such products are available in the market."

Intelligent buildings

Construction of houses that can sense the presence of people and adjust the lights as well as air-conditioning accordingly is fast-catching on, say architects. The lights turn off automatically if there is no one in the room. Some have lux sensors near windows to keep a track of sunlight. When the sunlight reduces, bulbs in the room are lit automatically.

Heading: UT Education dept steps up infrastructure at school in Daria - Indian Express
Content:
In a move to revamp security on the campus, Panjab University authorities have started hiring trained

security personnel.

Fifty of them have already been hired on a contract

of one year. Also to check the entry of outsiders and miscreants in the premises, manually operated barriers are being placed at

different gates.

The move comes after private security failed to maintain peace and security on the campus even after the university had spent a whooping sum of around one crore in the last two years.

Sources said that private security would be done away with in a phased manner as the recruitments for trained private security personnel are already on.

The university had given the job of providing security into private hands with an aim to save money but an amount of around Rs five lakh per month was being paid to them.

With the experiment failing, the authorities have decided to go back to trained staff.

Meanwhile, the trained security personnel are being hired on a contract basis and would be paid Rs 5,000 per month.

Talking to Newsline, PU Registrar S S Bari said:

"The work of installing the manually operated barriers is in progress and the same are being installed to check the entry of outsiders in the campus. These manually operated barriers are being installed around 50 metres from the gates and the aim is to stop those vehicles, which despite being stopped by the security officials enter the university."

The authorities did not wish to comment on the money being spent on the installations of these barriers.

Bari added: "We are not going into the cost factor as security of students is our priority. All the guards who are being hired are professionals and have undergone proper training."

Meanwhile, the students have also appreciated the idea of hiring trained staff. Appreciating the move, NSUI president Nitin Goyal said: "PU should have long ago done away with the private security system long time back. It is in the regime of private security when the stabbing incident took place, but it is better late than never. Trained private security personnel are any day a better choice to deal with any untoward incident."

Heading: Private coaching centres in govt schools in the doldrums as students allege fraud - Indian Express
Content:
More than a month after Newsline highlighted upon the sorry state of affairs at the Government High School, Daria, the Education department has now taken steps to improve its condition. A large number of problems have been taken care of, toilets in the school are still crying for attention.

Talking to Newsline, one of the teachers said the school now has a regular supply of drinking water. "The department has installed a new motor to pump water in the storage tanks. Also, we have been provided with a water treatment plant, which ensures that children are now consuming clean water."

Newsline had reported that the staff at the school had to do clerical work, owing to shortage of staff. "The school has now outsourced a clerk from a private organisation. Having administrative staff is a huge relief as things will be now organised," said another teacher.

New drain pipes have also been laid to address the problem of waterlogging. Classes had to be suspended earlier, during heavy rains, in the absence of an outlet for rainwater.

The number of toilets for over a thousand students, meanwhile, has not been addressed and remains three. Samwartak Singh, Director Public Instructions (Schools) said: "I am aware of the problems being faced by students. The department is consulting higher authorities to determine the amount of funds required for the construction of new toilets. We will make sure that the situation is resolved at the earliest." Newsline had reported about the lack of infrastructure in a school in Daria on August 24.

Heading: India leading player in generic drugs: Union Pharma secretary - Indian Express
Content:
The scheme to get private coaching centres to teach students in government schools seems to have become a source of embarrassment for the Education department, with some students alleging fraud on part of these centres. 

In a written complaint submitted to Director Public Instructions (Schools) Samwartak Singh, some students have alleged that they have been duped by a private coaching centre that was taking classes in Government Model Senior Secondary School, Sector 18.

The students complained that a coaching institute by the name of Academy of Computer Accountant (SCO 226-227, Sector 34, Chandigarh) had discontinued with the classes despite taking the entire fee for the course.

"We had paid the fee for a six-month course in Accounts and Tally, but the institute discontinued with the classes after four months. The institute has neither given us any certificate nor refunded our fee," said Bijender, a student of BBA, first year.

The students also allege that the school authorities were not of any help either.

"When we inquired why the classes were stopped abruptly, the school authorities were unable to give us a satisfactory reply. Since then we have been running from pillar to post to know the status of the course," says Deepak, a student of DAV School, Sector 8.

Commenting on the issue, Samwartak Singh, Director Public Instructions (Schools) said that the department will look into the matter. "The institute is playing with the future of these children, which is very grave.

I am looking into the details of the case and necessary action will be taken against them." Meanwhile, coaching classes are also going on in many other government schools as part of the plan initiated by former DPI, S K Setia.

When contacted by Newsline, Anujit Kaur Jassal, principal of Government Model Senior Secondary School, Sector 18, refused to comment on the issue.

"I had met with an accident a fortnight ago and I am at rest. Since I am on leave for the last couple of days, I do not know what is happening in the school," she said.

Heading: Bank to pay interest on prematurely withdrawn FD - Indian Express
Content:
The secretary to the Union Department of Pharmaceuticals, Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers, Ashok Kumar inaugurated a two-week intensive course on 'Advanced Analytical Techniques: Basic Principles and Application for Quality Assessment of Drugs and Pharmaceuticals for Export' at the National Institute of Pharmaceutical Education and Research (NIPER) in Mohali on Monday.

Addressing the inaugural function, he said: "India has become one of the leading international players in generic medicines and has been able to considerably improve access to low cost medicines for the common people not only in India but many other developing countries."

He said that this programme was meant to bring awareness among the officials of regulatory bodies in the developing countries about various aspects of the prevailing standards of quality. He said this programme will act as a bridge between the participating countries and India.

Nipar Director P Rama Rao said that 220 personnel of regulatory and research organisations from 36 countries have been trained in the last eight programmes of such kind.

About 29 resource persons drawn from the pharmaceutical industry will deliver lectures and participate in the deliberations.

A total of 19 participants from countries like Sudan, Iraq, Sri Lanka, Ethiopia, Laos, Mauritius, Tanzania, Belarus, Uzbekistan, Nigeria and Afghanistan attended the workshop.

Heading: Jan Shatabdi on popularity track - Indian Express
Content:
Holding that it is incumbent on the bank to pay interest on a deposit that has been prematurely withdrawn with an interest rate less than one per cent of the fixed rate, the District Consumer Forum directed Canara Bank to pay interest on a fixed deposit of Rs 5 lakh.

The bank had earlier refused to pay interest as the amount was withdrawn within six months while the fixed deposit was made for a period of one year.

Asserting that it is a clear case of deficiency on the part of the bank to refuse , the bank was directed to pay an interest of nine per cent on the 9 per cent (10 per cent -1per cent = 9 per cent) on the pre-mature deposit for the period it remained with them.

The bank has also been directed to pay Rs 5,500 as costs of litigation.

The complainant, Ashwini Luthra, a resident of Sector 15, said after his retirement he received various benefits and deposited the amount in his bank account at the Canara Bank branch in Bhopal.

Since he was to settle in Chandigarh after retirement, he requested the bank to transfer these funds to his account at the Sector 17, Chandigarh branch of Canara bank.

For this, he was requested to keep the aforesaid money in the fixed deposit as this would give him credit.

The complainant then did not transfer the funds. During April 2007, on noticing that the bank had increased the rate of interest for senior citizens from 8 per cent to 9.5 per cent, he requested the branch in Bhopal to encash the FDs and transfer the funds to the Chandigarh branch, so that he could avail a higher rate of interest.

He said that once again he was requested not to transfer the funds as his old FDs will be cancelled and converted to high rate of interest. While this was done in April 2007, in the third week of October 2007, the complainant required the funds and requested the bank branch to encash one of the FDs worth Rs 5,00,000.

Then, he was advised that the FDR had to be signed by both the account holders as this was a case of "premature withdrawal".

After all the formalities were completed, the amount was credited to his account, whereupon he realised that the interest due for this period of six months was not credited in the account.

On inquiring, he was told that since the FDR was in a scheme, which had a lock period of one year, the premature withdrawal did not entitle him to any interest.

It was alleged that the bank never informed this aspect either at the time of conversion of FDs at the higher rate of interest in April 2007 or when the complainant asked for premature withdrawal. Thereafter, when despite protracted correspondence with the bank, nothing positive could come out, he moved the consumer forum.

The Canara Bank, in its reply, stated that immediately after retirement the complainant did not fall within the senior citizen category to claim additional interest.

It was asserted that as soon as the request was received from the complainant by the Bhopal branch, the fixed deposits were immediately transferred to Chandigarh.

They said that as per the scheme, the complainant was informed that premature closure was not permissible under the terms of the deposit, therefore, the deposit be continued till its maturity.

The bank also said that the complainant was also informed that in case of premature closure of the deposit, no interest would be payable for the period.

The forum found that the scheme was floated by the bank for a limited period only, but at the same time it could not be proved that for any premature withdrawal no interest shall be paid.

"The complainant did not receive any information from the bank that he will not be entitled to interest if he made a premature withdrawal of his FD amount. In fact, the complainant was led into a bonafide belief that he will be paid interest similarly in this deposit scheme also as used to be made in other FDR deposit schemes. However, when the complainant lodged his protest with the higher authorities, he was told that the interest was payable to him for the full amount only on the maturity date. For premature withdrawal no interest was payable," the forum said.

Heading: Zirakpur flyover open for traffic till Thursday - Indian Express
Content:
With the Jan Shatabdi drawing a good response from passengers with its changed schedule, from July 1 earlier this year, it appears the load has been taken off from the Shatabdi Express. The train, now running on all the days, has seen a spurt in the number of passengers, particularly on weekends.

Having been extended to Nangal, the train provides a direct link between Chandigarh and Anandpur Sahib, and benefits passengers from Morinda, Kurali, Kharar and Mohali.

"Though initially, the response to the change in timings was lukewarm but soon the train has picked up on popularity. The occupancy has now increased significantly from Nangal as well as Chandigarh," says R K Saxena, additional divisional rail manager.

A senior official at the railway station said that nearly 100 passengers arrive daily by the train from Nangal and Ropar adding that during the last ten days, the New Delhi-bound train from Chandigarh has been leaving completely booked.

Saxena said that owing to the demand and requirement, the change in the starting station as well as timings was implemented.

Vikas Jain, a passenger said: "On days of heavy rush, especially the weekends, it is very difficult to get reservation in the Kalka Shatabdi. I prefer travelling by the Jan Shatabdi as the fare is less."

Heading: High Five - Indian Express
Content:
The much-awaited Zirakpur flyover was temporarily thrown open for vehicular traffic on Monday afternoon.

The work on carpeting of the flyover, which links Chandigarh with New Delhi via Ambala, will take another month to complete, after which, it will be permanently opened for traffic.

The vehicles between Ambala and Chandigarh were allowed entry on Monday, at 1 pm, to avoid traffic jam and congestion, which has become a regular feature on the service roads under the flyover.

Sanjiv Puri, Project chairman of GMR, which is undertaking the construction work of the flyover said, they had no option but to allow movement of vehicles as the final layer of carpeting on the service roads is still on.

He said the present arrangement will continue for four days, during which, traffic from Chandigarh towards Ambala will be allowed over the flyover.

Heading: In whispers - Indian Express
Content:
Some Mumbai clubs have mastered the trick to keep the party going year after year

In a city where half a dozen discotheques and nightclubs open each year and double the number pull the shutters down, Rock Bottom turning five calls for celebrations. But aging gracefully is not the only reason for the Juhu disco to cheer about. The ever increasing footfall has given it another pretext to uncork the bubbly.

In a city where early deadlines and newer nightclubs connive to kill older ones, what is it that has helped Rock Bottom survive? Bhavik Bhatt, the manager, confirms that it isn't just plain good luck. "We have introduced a lot of corporate strategies that has kept us going. Every fortnight, we scrutinise all the necessary elements that make a club rock, prepare a monthly gig calendar and organise international acts," says Bhatt, who is credited with doing most things right during his stint at this hotspot.

When Club Seven, Bandra, shut down four years ago, Rock Bottom borrowed its Ladies Night concept. In the last six months, it has successfully redefined its business by starting Bollywood Nights.

Though strategising helps to a great extend, location and management play an equally significant role in a club's success, says DJ Akhtar, resident DJ of Enigma for the last four years. "Enigma has been around for seven years and its biggest advantage is the location (located inside JW Marriott). While most clubs in the city have a deadline of 1.30 am, we are open till 3 am which attracts a large crowd. Besides, I always make sure I play what the crowd demands and on most occasions it is Bollywood." This does not mean that they steer clear of popular culture in music. "From Atif Aslam performing live to Infected Mushrooms Concert, there is always a variety on offer," says Akhtar.

Proper location, Sadhna Romy of Hawaiian Shack, agrees is vital in keeping the business going. Romy feels her other franchise in plush Colaba shut shop last year because of the location blunder considering that they were targeting the young crowd. Having a host of trustworthy people around you is very important when running a night club, she says. Shack has been around for almost six years and it is the constant changes in its food/cocktail menu as well as introduction of karaoke, ladies and hip hop nights that have kept things flowing. "It's important to pay personal attention to guests and listen to their needs, and problems if any," Romy says.

According to Vishal Shetty, the co-owner of Magic, the life of a discotheque depends on its service and ambience. Shetty along with Ketan Kadam once owned the popular discotheque Fire N Ice, Parel, before it shut down three years ago. They have now opened Magic in its place. "Closing down Fire N Ice was a conscious decision as there was no point renovating it. There was too much competition at that point and we thought it is best to shut shop when at the peak."

While most nightclubs have experimented with international acts and various genres of music, Ghetto at Mahalakshmi has stuck to what it offers best—retro music, Polaroid photography and chilled beer. On one hand, places like Ghetto has survived 20 years, on the other the once popular nightspots like Velocity, Insomnia, Club Seven, Athena and Mikanos have wound up business due to various reasons. "Insomnia shut down because of the change in management. They wanted to have an elite club and ban entry to teenagers, which obviously did not work in their favour," says Akhtar.

Heading: Comic relief - Indian Express
Content:
Sink into the otherworldly charm of Shrift's debut album

On certain days, when it seems like the whole world is out to get you and all you want to do is relax in your comfortable chair with a steaming cuppa, the right music seems so important. You don't want the usual radio fare - hip hop beats and smashing guitar riffs. What you want is something soft and soothing; something that lulls you into dreamland, even as it seduces you with its playful melodies. If you're in such a mood, then Shrift's debut album Lost in a Moment is the one for you.

Shrift comprises singer/songwriter Nina Miranda and multi-texturalist/producer Dennis Wheatley. Miranda has sung for Bebel Gilberto, Nitin Sawhney, Arkestra One, Jah Wobble and Da Lata and is the vocalist for Smoke City, a British group which was one of the first to blend bossa nova, trip hop, jazz, reggae and funk. Wheatley has worked with British electro band Atlas, which has a history of taking existing elements like Brazilian singers and string quartets and combining them to create danceable new ethno-electro mixtures. The merger of these two different kinds of music is evident in the varying mood of the tracks.

The best thing about Lost in a Moment is how smoothly Miranda blends her soft vocals with the slightly mystical, yet modern and edgy music on the tracks. The music alternates between gentle and uncomplicated rhythms such as on Hum and the big-band and orchestral sounds of the highly-danceable To the floor. The violin- and cello-heavy sound of the album is at times laidback and at times upbeat. The highlight of the album is the track Yes I love you, which has Miranda breathily repeating 'Yes, I love you' amidst choral sounds, crowd noises and cello music. In fact, many of the tracks feature unorthodox elements like sounds of children talking and sea waves to create a very atmospheric album.

The lyrics are quite simple, but therein lay their beauty. Miranda's soft voice is perfect for lending an emotional pitch to the simplest of words. The lyrics also up the exotic quotient of the album as they alternate between English, French and Portuguese.

All in all, the album is a good buy at Rs 199, for people who enjoy easy, mood-uplifting music.

Heading: An Emperor’s Tale - Indian Express
Content:
The Amar Chitra Katha website shows a modern perspective but retains its original charm

There is a reason why moral story books are gathering dust on our shelves. The fact is we just don't need them anymore. Technology has changed the rules of reading and the Internet takes away from the charm of buying books from our pocket money. But like a lone soldier on a shipwreck, Amar Chitra Katha, India's most popular comic series, launched by Anant Pai in 1967, has managed to survive the advent of Archie Comics, Adventures of Tintin and DC comics to India. In fact, ACK laid a foundation of comic culture in India and gave India the much-needed boost in comic readership.

And now, keeping in tune with the changing times, ACK has launched their website amarchitrakatha.com. The website, just like the original, takes you on a cultural ride to the world of great epics, Indian mythology, history and folk tales. The homepage is divided into a five sections with maximum weightage given to the Digital ACK section, which includes the Story of Week and E-comic. Although the website is not visually appealing, it makes sure that the content makes up for it. There are a lot of novel features and topping them all is the digital versions of the comics that can be read online. Currently, they are available in regional languages, including Telugu, Kannada, Tamil, Gujarati, Bengali and Marathi. To give the visitor a feel of reading a real comic book, it flips the pages as if you were holding the comic in your hands. You can read one for 99 Cents (Rs 45.50) or if you are lucky, you can avail ACK's best discount offers. Predictably, it has a shop where one can order comics online.

The best feature of the website is their interactive section, Create With Us, where the reader can write stories or draw art. Children, who have admired the enchanting and inspiring stories of great Indian heroes, now get a chance to narrate their own tales and share it with other users. Similarly, if you want to design a new Amar Chitra Katha cover for an existing title and join the likes of Ram Waeerkar, Pratap Mulik and Yusuf Bangalorewala, names synonymous with Indian comic art, this is your best chance.

The Culture Beat section carries updates of cultural events all over India and is of significance because of the news value it carries. From an advertisement on Amateur Radio classes in Mumbai to a talent hunt contest in Delhi and a painting contest in Hyderabad, this section helps you plan your child's itinerary.

They also have an encyclopedia on India called ACKpedia. Although the name reminds us of a very popular search site, the section doesn't live up to it. The section, still under construction, promises to offer you information on people, places and culture of our nation in the months to come. For the moment, let's wait and watch.

PRIYANKA PEREIRA

Heading: The rebel king - Indian Express
Content:
Unlike his popular warrior themes, Kurosawa's Throne of Blood is steeped in Japanese culture and theatre

T S Elliot said Akira Kurosawa's Throne of Blood (1957) was his favourite film of all time. Kurosawa's captivating retelling of Macbeth, Shakespeare's tragic tale about the fall of a man led by the lust for power finds itself re-contextualised in Kurosawa's hands within a Japanese feudal setup. Kurosawa's adaptation is enthralling for the way it adapts the classic story of treachery and greed into a uniquely Japanese warrior tale using the formal techniques of traditional Noh theatre.

Toshiro Mifune, Kurosawa's leading man and long time collaborator plays Washizu (Macbeth) with an obsessive energy that leaves one spellbound. Legendary Japanese actor Isuzu Yamada plays Asiju, the conniving lady Macbeth, who is a pale white even before being overcome by guilt of murder. She is a quaint, seemingly demure creature of evil. In Kurosawa's adaptation there is the obvious element of the theatrical as Kurosawa self consciously reminds the viewer that it is indeed great theatre that unfolds before us. Shot in exquisite black and white, Kurosawa sets his story in a haunting misty, mountainous landscape.

The film begins with a message of mutiny in the kingdom. Washizu and Miki, two trusted commanders quell the mutiny and venture out to Spider's Web castle to tell the good news to their King. But they must cross the maze-like Spider's Web forest to get to the castle. While in the forest, they are trapped in torrential rain. A spirit appears to prophesise their rise to power.

Washizu and Miki finally find their way to the fortress, where they are promoted in grand ceremony, just as the spirit had predicted. Washizu is disturbed by the prophecy but his wife feeds him with lies and reassurances about the inevitability of his rise to power. What follows is a series of murders and Washizu's becoming the emperor of the castle. In the end, a power hungry and delusional Washizu is murdered by his foes, with a rain of arrows that crucify him to the wall.

Kurosawa was both criticised and praised for the film, which like a lot of his other work is influenced by the West; particularly his warrior films like Seven Samurai and Yojimbo which borrowed from the westerns he loved. But Throne of Blood is story bound in Japanese culture and theatre and reminds one of Kurosawa's last epic — Ran, an adaptation of King Lear. There is the same haunting windy landscape shown in the unsettling sound of the bamboo flute.

The DVD version released by the Criterion collection has an Audio commentary by Japanese film expert Michael Jeck, an original theatrical trailer and an essay by Stephen Prince called The Warrior's Camera: The Cinema of Akira Kurosawa.

Heading: In good stead - Indian Express
Content:
Navtej Sarna bares Maharaja Duleep Singh's trauma in The Exile

There is something in the look of the young prince that strikes a familiar note—the yearning for his motherland. Maharaja Duleep Singh's life in exile in England was a continuous search for the flavours of Punjab. This, even the company of Queen Victoria and her family could not assuage. A photograph taken by Prince Albert, Queen Victoria's husband, in the 1850s, captures his lost look.

This tell-tale photograph was on a postcard of the Victoria and Albert Museum. Navtej Sarna picked it up during a visit. Now, the image has made it to the cover of The Exile, second novel by the diplomat-turned-writer. "The young King of Punjab, who was banished to England to live the life of a country squire, was favoured by the Queen. That, however, lasted only till the disillusioned prince wanted to return to India," says Sarna.

In this book, Sarna tries to unravel the deepest dilemmas and longings of the last Maharaja of Punjab—something that history books have overlooked. "I'm not a historian. I chose novel format over non-fiction to tell his story," says Sarna. History provided the skeleton of facts, based on which he builds the story, told by Duleep Singh and five other narrators.

Duleep Singh's tragic life had moved Sarna ever since he heard Duleep Singh's story from his mother 40 years ago. The story of a king (Duleep Singh was the youngest of Maharaj Ranjit Singh's acknowledged sons) duped of his kingdom at the age of 11 has always evoked a "predominant feeling of poignancy" in India's longest-serving spokesman for the Ministry of External Affairs.

Duleep Singh signed away the kingdom and its treasures including the Koh-i-noor diamond. He was later separated from his mother and people. After he was taken under British guardianship, he was converted to Christianity. At 16, he was living under exile in England. A late realisation of his lost legacy made him a rebel. He became Sikh again and longed to be in India. Instead, he was sucked into the murky politics of 19th century Europe. He died on October 22, 1893 as a lonely, defeated man in a cheap hotel in Paris.

Piecing together his life and giving vent to Duleep Singh's inner thoughts have kept Sarna occupied for the last 10 years, when not engrossed with India's foreign affairs. Over the last decade, he has read extensively, researched and travelled to places where the king lived. In between, he also wrote his first novel We Weren't Lovers Like That and Folk Tales of Poland.

These efforts have helped Sarna in giving a sense of Duleep Singh's grievance. "The events, dates and places on the novel are all true but the emotional dimension to the characters have been attributed by me," says the novelist.

The book, published by Penguin, was released at Crossword, Kemps Corner, yesterday. Sarna, however, is still recovering from the hard work that went into its making. "I will take a while to plan my next."

Heading: Fast and furious - Indian Express
Content:
The inaugural Delhi Fashion Week took its first step without a runway

The Delhi Fashion Week is small in scale with under 30 designers participating (at last count the Wills India Fashion Week had over 80 designers). However, the first day saw things move as they should — right from the efficient valet parking to the well-spaced out show area to ample food options, you can pick between AD Singh's new Japanese restaurant Ai and a more familiar Costa Coffee counter.

The ramp here is a flat strip of white cardboard (diligently covered with a white sheet at all other times and guarded by a pack of ushers). "The idea was to make the shows compact and closer to the audience," says Geetanjali Kashyap of the Fashion Foundation of India.

With 'Rat Pack Nirvana', Rajvi Mohan's tribute to one of her fashion icons, Dean Martin, she made her first-ever participation at a fashion week in the country. The Delhiite—possibly one of a handful of female designers making menswear—comes with impressive credentials, having trained with the famed Vivienne Westwood and studied at the Parson's School of Design, New York. "I wanted to do a collection which would look at Martin's sense of dressing in an Indian context. This is what I felt it would be like," she says.

Akshay Kumar and his costume designer Shabina Khan can pat themselves on the back for sparking off a trend. Mohan's show had a liberal sprinkling of trousers cut to the knee for more formal capris, a look that Kumar has recently made famous in his movie Singh is Kiing. We also liked the jackets in particular, with their streamlined lapels and play on essential summer textiles like linen and stretch cotton.

Abhijeet Khanna's collection, which came next, focussed on all things luxurious, even in the time of near recession. His collection— an assortment of shift dresses, harem pants, and tops— inspired by Indian styling of French Rococo were richly embellished with sequins and incorporated Indian embroidery in otherwise western silhouettes. Khanna had been design assistant to Manish Arora for over four years, and the affinity to Arora's sensibilities clearly shows. The fish-scale patterned dress which ended the show was reminiscent of Arora's warrior themes.

The opening day also saw a fair presence of buyers. "We have commitments from over 150 buyers and nobody has cancelled so far. It should be a fair turnout," comments Sumeet Nair of the Fashion Foundation of India. While Khanna's show had quite a few buyers, particularly from Japan and Hong Kong, the second half of the day, with shows by Vineet Bahl, Lecoanet Hemant and Raghavendra Rathore, will have stronger buyer presence. Those expected include Isetan from Japan, Ovo Studio from Madrid, Design Best from Bourdeaux and Seibu from Hong Kong.

Heading: Chatterati - Indian Express
Content: It's going to be the It-acquisition of the year for sure. The new Bentley Continental Flying Spur Speed, launched at Delhi's Inter Continental Hotel recently can go up to a maximum speed of 322 km/hour. The new Speed variant, priced at a whooping Rs 2.5 crore comes in a whole new avatar, packing a healthy dose of power and luxury in her light frame. With a sprint time of just 4.8 seconds (0-100 km/hr) it has earned the title of the fastest saloon in the world. "We are launching this car for youngsters who enjoy speed and luxury at the same time," says Satya Bagla, Managing director, Bentley Motors India. Responsibly fast, let's hope.

Heading: Divekar, Mane prevail - Indian Express
Content:
A 226-run partnership for the second wicket between centurions Swapnil Asnodkar and Anand Singh enabled DY Patil to take a big lead of 258 runs over Mumbai Police on the second day of their three-day 'A'Division Times Shield Cricket Tournament match on their home ground in Nerul on Tuesday.

Asnodkar's knock of 169 was studded with two sixes and 21 hits to the fence while Anand Singh's unbeaten innings of 152 included 19 fours. Singh was then involved in a unbroken 118-run stand for the third wicket with in-form batsman Siddharth Chitnis who remained not out on 61.

An unbeaten century by Onkar Khanvilkar kept Bharat Petroleum's (BPCL) hopes alive to take a first innings lead over Tata Sports Club as they finished the day at 171 for 3 at Police Gymkhana. Tata Sports Club resumed at 270 for 6 and went on to score 358, which included 40 penalty runs as BPCL bowled five overs short. Southpaw Nishit Shetty was unlucky to miss his century by six runs.

Leg-spinner Sairaj Bahutule was the pick of the bowlers with 4 for 84 while medium pacer Rajesh Varma finished with 3 for 63. Western Railway did well to take a vital first innings lead of 31 runs over Indian Oil at the Mahalaxmi ground.

At close of play, Indian Oil were 67 for 1 in their second innings. A half-century by Hrishikesh Kanitkar (61) helped Air-India to finish the second day at 156 for 3 in reply to Central Railway's total of 358. Harshad Rawle scored an unbeaten 122 off 243 balls with the help of 19 fours. Mohammad Kaif was still batting at 41 at the end of the day's play.

Heading: Customs win amidst controversy - Indian Express
Content:
Cdr Mahesh among top contenders

Commander R Mahesh starts clear favourite to win the ISAF (International Siling Federation) Nations Cup Regional Finals Asia, which gets underway at H2O Complex, Girgaum Chowpaty from Wednesday.

Many top teams from the Asian Region which include Thailand, Pakistan, Bahrain and others are participating in this event sponsored by West Coast Marine Services and conducted by the Indian Naval Watermanship Training Centre (Mumbai) under the aegis of Yachting Association Of India and Match Racing Association Of India.

The Indian challenge is spearheaded by Arjuna awardee Cdr R Mahesh who is rated among the top 50 in the International Sailing Federation Match Racing rankings. Other Indians in fray are Arjuna awardee, Olympian and two-time world champion Farokh Tarapore, Arjuna awardee and Asian Games medalist Aashim Mongia, Arjuna awardee Nitin Mongia who is also multiple Asian Games and World Championsip medalist.

With women's match racing competiton now included in the Olympics from upcoming London Games in 2012, two Indian women's teams will also be seen in action led by Pallavi Naik and Ayesha Lobo.

Heading: Subh Subh and Winning Chick claim feature honours - Indian Express
Content:
Playing their third game on the trot, Mumbai Customs overcame Maharashtra State Police by a narrow 2-1 margin in the ongoing Mumbai Hockey Association (MHA) 2008-09 Super League at the MHA-Mahindra stadium in Churchgate on Tuesday. After being stunned in their last game by MbpT, the Customs outfit, who were without Olympian Rahul Singh, prevailed to win the closely contested encounter.

Both teams started on an even keel, as the MS Police went in without their coach Dhanraj Pillay. But the absence of the two stars did not seem to deter either of the teams, as they made a positive start to the match. The cops, who lost their opening tie to ONGC, stunned Customs with an early goal, when Vinod Nimbhore put the ball into the wooden cage of a direct pass unleashed from 25 yards by Amol Bhosle in the 9th minute. But their joy was short-lived, as Customs came right back with a controversial equalizer, which resulted in play being stopped for 15 mins. The MS Police players were unhappy with referee Mohd Amin's decision to allow the goal, and staged a walk-out. Amin claimed that Customs player Chinglen Sana's diagonal shot was deflected in by Stanley Fernandes, a claim that the MS Police players refuted.

But, when play resumed the goal stayed, and the teams started off with the score at 1-1. The teams went into the lemon-break without the deadlock being broken. Content:
Had specific brief to circulate notes, police suspect they may have come from Nepal

Two teenaged boys attempting to get change for a Rs 1,000 note were arrested from the Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus (CST) early Tuesday morning after a Railway Police Force constable found them to be carrying fake currency worth more than Rs 1 lakh in a bag.

The duo, both aged 15, were initially taken into custody by the Railway Police Force and later handed over to the GRP police station at the Chhatrapati Shivaji Termius, which is now probing the case.

"This morning, around 7.30 am, they were trying to exchange a 1,000 rupees note with our RPF men who were dressed in plainclothes. Our men got suspicious as they were trying to get change for Rs 1,000. On checking their baggage, we found 33 notes of Rs 1,000 denomination and 149 notes of Rs 500 denomination. On interrogation, they gave evasive answers which raised our suspicion further," said Kiran Bhosale, sub-inspector with the RPF.

Preliminary investigations revealed that the boys live in Govandi. "First, they identified themselves with Muslim names, but now they claim to be Hindus," said A K Sharma, Commissioner of the Mumbai GRP. "As per the interrogation, one of them is from Bihar and the second boy is from Nepal. But we strongly suspect that both are from Nepal. We are still verifying their claims," said Sharma. He added that the railway police has sought assistance from the Maharashtra State Anti Terrorism Squad.

Questioned further about their families, the boys only gave evasive answers, said police officials.

The two boys also told investigators that the money had been handed over to them along with a specific brief: To circulate the notes. "They had been promised some commission for the work, by a man whose description they have given us," added Sharma.

The RPF also got the notes checked by the State Bank of India (SBI) which confirmed the notes were fake. "We have also obtained a certificate from the SBI for the same," added Bhosale.

Heading: Lay down norms for sharing probe info with media, HC tells cops - Indian Express
Content:
A year after it embarked on a project to cut down the waiting time at traffic signals by implementing the Intelligent Area Traffic Control (ATC) system, the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) has so far been able to make only four of the 53 traffic junctions selected in the first phase fully functional. After the long delay, the civic administration has now assured that all 253 busy junctions that are to be part of the ATC system will be equipped with the real-time traffic management system within the next six months.

"There has been considerable delay due to problems in getting permission for digging and even special traffic signal poles. However, the traffic department has how given permissions for the remaining 249 junctions and we are confident of completing the entire project in the next six months," said Additional Municipal Commissioner (city) R A Rajeev, after a meeting with joint commissioner of traffic Sanjay Barve in the civic headquarters on Tuesday.

So far only four traffic signals in Tardeo and Nana Chowk area are equipped with the technological solution which is expected to reduce travel time and cut down pollution levels and fuel consumption by vehicles idling at red lights.

While the project began in October last year, the actual digging of roads for laying cables and sensors began only in December. Spanish IT firm — Telvent GIT S A — is carrying out the work of designing, constructing and commissioning the traffic management systems at an estimated cost of around Rs 49 crore.

The BMC had expected to finish the project within six months from the date of starting the project, however, as per the revised deadline, the project is still behind the schedule by three weeks.

The ambitious project under the World Bank's Mumbai Urban Transport Project (MUTP) was rapped by the bank's official in March this year for its slow pace of work. "We have already taken action against contractor by issuing show-cause notice and even laying penalty as per terms of the contract," said Rajeev.

The first phase of 53 junctions included Wilson College, Band Stand, Kemps Corner, Dahanukar (North) at its junction with Peddar Road, Mahalaxmi Temple, Haji Ali, Opera House, Churchgate junction, Air India junction, Mantralaya junction and Regal junction.

To start the system, cables will be laid underground at the junction which will act as sensors and record the number of vehicles arriving at intersections from each access point. The acquired data will be used to constantly adjust traffic lights at each intersection in accordance with real-time demand and in coordination with neighbouring intersections, thus reducing road traffic congestion.

BMC's skywalks

In addition to skywalks being constructed by the MMRDA, even BMC will construct skywalks at six places. "We have selected the places where MMRDA was planning to construct skywalks and where BMC felt it was necessary to have one," said Rajeev. The skywalks will come up at Siddhivinayak temple, Worli naka, Haji Ali, Lower Parel and Parel and tender notices will be issued soon.

Heading: Sultry Oct has city breaking into a sweat - Indian Express

Court rejects Susairaj's plea for a copy confessional statement

The Bombay High Court on Tuesday suggested to the police department to lay down norms for its officers regarding sharing of information on investigation with the media. The suggestion came while rejecting Kannada actress Maria Monica Susairaj's plea seeking a copy of her confessional statement.

"We would appreciate if the police department creates a system, by which a responsible police officer shares information, rather than each of the investigating officers, as we consider it also a duty of the police to inform the public of the progress in a crime investigation," a division bench of Justice Bilal Nazki and Justice Ashutosh Kumbhakoni held.

The court has refused to set aside a June 2008 trial court order rejecting a similar application filed by the actress who is the main accused in the Neeraj Grover murder case.

The bench rejected the plea on the ground that copy of the confessional statement cannot be furnished to the accused before filing of the chargesheet. Susairaj's lawyer Nitin Pradhan had contended that since a part of her confession had already been published in newspapers she is entitled to the same.

Meanwhile, the court directed the police to "issue appropriate clarification in regard to factually incorrect, if any, alleged confessional statement made by the petitioner, which if at all have appeared in the media, within two weeks."

"We trust and hope that the media will publish appropriate clarification in this regard at the earliest," the judgement states.

The judges observed that they believe that the press and the judiciary, both, should be independent and free. "Both should not have any fetters, but the more freedom you have, the more the responsibilities, and, therefore, both these institutions are required to have self-imposed restriction."

The judgement observes that while reporting a crime or an investigation, the report should not be tilted as it creates a perception in the minds of the people and ultimate decision of the court going against such perceptions may affect the credibility of the courts.

The court has observed that it is only a "responsible press" which can claim not only freedom but also immunity from being compelled to divulge the source of its information. The court also observed that the police should not provide tailored information to the media which is factually incorrect.

The state had earlier told the court that confessional statement of an accused could be given in accordance with law, at a stage where it did not prejudice further investigation. The sessions court had rejected Susairaj's application for the confession statement on June 19, following which she moved the High Court. Susairaj had given her confessional statement to the police on May 28.  Susairaj and her naval officer fiance Emile Jerome Mathew were arrested in May this year for the alleged murder of Grover.

Heading: An eye on the continent’s cinematic best - Indian Express
Content:
Even as the India Meteorological department (IMD) on Tuesday confirmed the withdrawal of monsoon from the city, a sudden change in wind direction sent day and night temperatures soaring, giving Mumbaiites a taste of the typical October heat.

Though rains disappeared from the city after a few spells of thundershowers in the second week of September, it was on Tuesday that the IMD officially confirmed the end of the monsoon season. And, according to IMD officials, a sudden change in the direction of winds from westerly to easterly, coupled with high post-monsoon humidity, has sent the day temperatures soaring up to 36 degree Celsius and the night temperatures up to 25 degree Celsius over the past few days.

October in Mumbai is referred to as the 'second summer' with temperatures closely competing with that of March, April and May. K Sathi Devi, director of IMD, Mumbai, said: "By October, the monsoon system slowly withdraws from the western and southern regions. Mumbai stops enjoying its cool westerly sea breeze, which is replaced by the dry and hot landward easterlies. Besides, the sky is virtually cloudless this month and as a result, the mercury soars."

While it is usual for the maximum temperatures to rise up to 35-37 degrees this month, Mumbai has never seen the minimum temperatures rising to 25 degrees over the past decade, according to IMD statistics. Between 1998 and 2007, the highest minimum temperature for October recorded in the city was 23.6 degrees Celsius — on October 8, 2000 as well as October 2, 2006. On Tuesday, the city's minimum temperature touched 25 and 24.5 degrees Celsius in Colaba and Santacruz, respectively.

Sathi Devi said, "While we are expecting the north-eastern monsoon winds to hit the southern states soon, Mumbai won't have respite from the hot weather for a while, unless some stray system causes thundershowers."

The IMD forecasts clear skies and maximum and minimum temperatures hovering around 36 and 25 degree Celsius, respectively, till Thursday.

7th Third Eye Asian Film Festival opens with Berlin Fest's Golden Bear-winning Tuya's Marriage on Oct 16

Films by Asian masters will be rolled out for Mumbai's cinephiles for a week from Thursday. The seventh edition of Third Eye Asian Film Festival, featuring 80 films from 20 countries of the continent, will take off with Tuya's Marriage (Chinese) at the YB Chavan Centre, Sachivalaya.

For years, Asians films struggled for an identity. To ward off the influence of the West — which ruled many Asians countries — took time. "But now, both Indian as well as Asian cinema has carved out their places in the world of cinema," feels actor Atul Kulkarni. This annual festival is a celebration of their cinematic excellence. And the opening film is a proof of that.

Tuya's Marriage, which bagged Golden Bear in Berlin International Festival, is directed by Wang Quan An. This poignant film revolves around Tuya, the persevering wife of Bater, a herdsman who lost his legs while exploring water in the Neimenggu (Inner Mongolia) grassland. The couple decides to divorce so that Tuya can seek a better life. Imposing her own conditions of a remarriage —her new husband must take care of Bater and their children — Tuya started an arduous search for a new husband.

Sharing spotlight with Tuya's Marriage are Park Kwang-su's 1995 film Single Spark and Somaratnee Dissanayake's King Siri (2008). Kwang-su, a celebrated filmmaker of South Korea, will also receive Asian Film Culture Award on the opening evening. "Park is renowned for his realistic cinematography that often gives a strong narrative voice to many social and political issues of his country," says Sudhir Nandgaonkar, programme director.

Thursday will also witness P K Nair, former director of National Film Archive, receiving Satyajit Ray Memorial Award. From October 17, film screenings will be held at Chavan Centre, Plaza Theatre and Fun Republic. Some special features of this year's festival are debutant director and short-film competitions. While 52 entries are competing for the top honour in the debutant director section, the latter has received 155 entries.

The festival also pays homage to Egyptian director Youssef Shahine, who died in July, and the legendary dramatist Vijay Tendulkar. Playwright Tendulkar's Manthan, Ardhasatya and Umbartha will be screened during the festival.

There will also be a showcase of six of Dan Wolmer's films and five of Korean director Kim Ki Duk's. The retrospective section will focus on six films of Japanese director Keisuke Kinoshita, who died in 1999.

For those looking for a contemporary fare, Spectrum Asia has films made in the last two years and Indian Vista will add a regional flavour with films in Kannada, Bengali, Marathi, Telegu and others.

Two persons, including a two-year-old, died and four others were injured in a major fire that broke out in a building at Johri Bazaar, Kalbadevi, on Tuesday. According to the fire department, the fire was caused by a short circuit and gutted almost the whole building. The injured, including a fireman, were rushed to the JJ Hospital and Bombay Hospital. One of the victims has been identified as 55-year-old Laxminarayan Nemichand.

Vrindavan, the five-storey building that caught fire, houses a branch of Vijaya Bank and some other offices and residences. According to fire officials, 12 fire engines, 6 water tanks and 3 ambulances were rushed to the spot. The building was almost completely gutted though the cooling operations by the Fire Brigade continued till late in the day.

One of the residents, Monica Baheti, threw her two-year-old child from the first floor of the building into the hands of the crowd in a bid to save her. Unfortunately, the baby succumbed to her head injuries. Baheti threw her other child also who luckily survived.

Baheti suffered multiple internal injuries and burn injuries and is being treated. Another injured, Pankaj Patel (38), who sustained multiple injuries was reported to be in a stable condition by Tuesday evening.

"Considering the injured lost their homes and property, Bombay Hospital will treat the injured free-of-cost," said Dr Ashish Tiwari, spokesperson for Bombay Hospital.

Heading: HC allows Kasliwal to enter Mumbai for 4 weeks - Indian Express
Content:
Court says station in-charge must note down reasons for not registering a complaint

Officers who are in-charge of a police station have to immediately register a First Information Report (FIR) based on a complaint or an information given by a victim regarding any cognizable offence, a full bench of the Bombay High court ruled on Tuesday. The police, henceforth, cannot avoid lodging a complaint on the pretext of preliminary investigation that's being conducted by them, said the court.

The bench comprising Chief Justice Swatanteer Kumar, Justice S J Vazifdar and Justice A A Sayyed has held that if the police station in-charge does not register the FIR instantaneously, he has to note it in the station diary or daily dairy in the police station, giving reasons for not registering the complaint. The order further stated that the police would take a maximum of two days to register the offence.

While passing the order, the court observed that the stability of the state governance is relatable to the status of the public law and order in the state. "Every criminal trial is initiated by registration of the FIR which sets the mechanism of criminal investigation into motion and is the first step for commencing a legal process. The law inescapably requires the police to register an FIR. Under Criminal Procedure Code no choice is vested in a police officer," the court observed. The full bench went through several judgments of the apex court and also the procedures prevalent in UK, US and Sweden before passing the order.

The full bench was settling an issue raised by a division bench of the High Court comprising Justice Bilal Nazki and Justice A P Bhangale, in May this year. Hearing a writ petition filed by one Sandeep Rammilan Shukhla, the division bench had stated that in light of various conflicting case laws, it was unclear whether the police had the discretion to postpone registration of an FIR until it completed preliminary inquiry. Thus, it referred the matter to the larger bench.

The judgment comes as a major relief to citizens who at present are being shunned away— mostly the lower class— by the police without registering their complaints. In a 146-page judgment, the bench stated, "In interpreting and applying a penal statute, it has to be borne in mind that respect for human rights of the accused is not the only value at stake. The purpose of criminal law is to permit everyone to go about their daily lives without fear of harm to person or property. And it's in the interest of every one that serious crime should be effectively investigated and prosecuted. There must be fairness on all sides," the bench observed.

The court also stated that sometimes cases pertaining to cognizable offence were registered even if they were patently false. "They're filed just to harass the party complained against at the behest of some influential persons," the bench observed. However, the bench also said that a genuine complainant who is the real victim of a crime is neither attended to nor heard at police stations as the officer-in-charge refuses to record his complaint.

"This leads to consequences which result in not bringing the influential people to the command of law," the bench observed.

Heading: Big B’s condition improves, say hospital authorities - Indian Express
Content:
Abhishek Kasliwal, accused of raping a 52-year-old woman in 2006, has been finally allowed to enter the city by the Bombay High Court after a period of two-and-a-half years. Earlier, he was allowed to travel anywhere but Mumbai to avoid any manipulation of evidence or witnesses.

The High Court has granted interim relaxation of conditions for a period of four weeks as there has been no progress in the trial since 2006. Justice D B Bhosale has, however, directed Kasliwal to attend Worli police station twice a week before the next hearing scheduled after four weeks.

Prosecution had reiterated their earlier arguments that if allowed to enter Mumbai there are chances he might tamper with evidence or witnesses.

Meanwhile, the police have been directed to give a status report on the missing woman who was allegedly raped before the next hearing.

The court had earlier directed the state government to file a reply regarding what efforts they have taken to trace the woman who was supposed to be given protection by the police based on earlier HC directions.

Justice Bhosale has also sought copy of the Police Commissioner's report regarding the efforts made to trace the woman which has been filed before the trial court. Abhishek Kasliwal had moved a fresh application before the High Court seeking relaxation of conditions so that he can come back to Mumbai.

Kasliwal, who is in Delhi following court directions, wanted to come to Mumbai as his work is getting affected and the trial is still pending.

"We are awaiting copy of the order after which he can come to Mumbai," said his advocate Shamsher Garud.

Kasliwal, son of Shree Ram mill and S Kumar's brand owner Ambhuj Kasliwal, contends that there has been no progress in the trial even after the elapse of one year. According to Garud, summonses have been issued to the witnesses and the trial is expected to resume in November.

Kasliwal, who was arrested on March 12, 2006, got bail in April and was directed to stay in New Delhi and his entry into Mumbai was restricted to avoid any manipulation of evidence. According to the prosecution, Kasliwal had offered a lift to the woman from Colaba area in the wee hours and then allegedly raped her.

Heading: Hashish worth Rs 13.2 lakh seized, two arrested - Indian Express
Content:
Bollywood actor Amitabh Bachchan's condition improved on Tuesday though hospital officials ruled out his discharge from the hospital during the day. Bachchan was admitted to the hospital four days ago after complaints of abdominal pain.

He was initially taken to the Nanavati Hospital which is close to his residence, before shifting to the Lilavati Hospital. Hospital sources said that he was admitted for incision hernia.

In an official statement released by the hospital on Tuesday afternoon, hospital authorities said, "He's definitely improving and there is no doubt about this. Doctors are pleased with his progress. He's converse with his family members, who are by his side throughout the day."

The statement also denied rumours about his condition worsening on Tuesday morning. It also stated, "Any news not contained in this communication regarding his health is an absolute rumour at this moment and must not be believed."

Heading: MMRDA to invite bids for plots at Wadala - Indian Express
Content:
In a late night operation on Monday, the Ghatkopar police seized over 16 kg of hashish worth Rs 13.2 lakh and arrested two persons in connection with the case. While one of the accused, Peter Fernandes (36), is wanted in two similar cases dating back to 2006, the other accused Rustom Pirmohammad Sheikh (30) reportedly runs a paan shop.

G T Padwal, Senior Police Inspector from Ghatkopar police station said they had received a tip-off on Monday afternoon that the accused were expected to arrive at Jambhulpada on the Ghatkopar-Andheri link road near Asalpha village bearing a drug consignment. "We informed the ANC and immediately formed teams comprising two police inspectors, two sub-inspectors and a couple of constables who laid a trap at the site. After spotting the accused with two white bags our officials nabbed them. While the total estimated cost of the drugs in Indian market is Rs 13.2 lakh, its international value is around a crore," said Padwal.

According to Police Inspector (Community) F S Pawar who is the investigating officer, both the accused are residents of Moholi vilage in Saki Naka. "While Fernandes revealed that he procured the drugs from Gujarat through a middleman, neither he nor Sheikh has revealed the names of the seller or the buyer of these drugs. Both have been booked under the Narcotics and Psychotropic Substances Act and the drug samples have been sent to the Forensic lab," said Pawar.

Fernandes hails from a small flower merchant's family and also claims to supply tourist vehicles. While he is wanted in two cases, Sheikh does not have any police record, said the police.

Both the accused have been remanded to police custody till October 22.

Heading: Former Shiv Sena corporator acquitted  in murder case - Indian Express
Content:
The Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA) will open bids for two of its plots at Wadala on Wednesday.

A 7,029 sq metre commercial plot and a 4,340 sq metre plot, reserved for malls and multiplexes, are in the vicinity of the Wadala Truck Terminus close to IMAX Adlabs multiplex.

The two plots have been put on the block as part of MMRDA's plans to develop a part of the area as a business district on the lines of the Bandra Kurla Complex. The bids were earlier supposed to be opened on September 23 but the process was deferred by a month.

With a permissible built-up area of 24,000 sq metre for the commercial plot and 13,500 sq metre for the latter and a reserve price of Rs 1 lakh per sq metre, MMRDA is expecting these plots to fetch a minimum price of Rs 240 crore and Rs 135 crore respectively.

MMRDA officials said that plans to develop the Wadala truck terminal as an inter-state bus terminal and the presence of several residential complexes in the area is expected to bolster the demand for the plots.

"At the MMRDA's reserve price, the price works out to be Rs 50 crore per acre. The deal is viable in a good market. However now developers have no interest in land acquisition nor do they have enough money to develop their existing land stock. It is very difficult for any Indian developer to have the capacity to buy the land unless the prices are made more lucrative," said a real estate consultant who did not wish to be named.

The MMRDA is looking at banks, financial institutions, insurance agencies, mutual funds and asset management companies to take up its commercial plot.Corporate offices of leading Indian companies with an annual turnover of 250 crore, IT firms as well as corporate developers are allowed to participate in the bidding process.

Heading: Amid security alarm, suspects give police the slip - Indian Express

A sessions court on Tuesday acquitted a former Shiv Sena corporator in a 11-year-old murder case. Surekha Patil, a former corporator from Sion and Chunabhatti, was accused of murdering a person and throwing his body on the railway track.

The case dates back to 1997 but Surekha was made an accused only in 2000. She was booked for the murder of Raj Patil, whose body was found on the railway track near Sion Railway Station.

Following this, a case was registered against Surekha after the deceased's parents complained that Patil had reprimanded the victim for eveteasing some girls in that area.

Surekha and nine other Shiv Sainiks were charged for murder under section 302 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC).

According to the prosecution, Surekha was enraged by the victim and hence had decided to teach him a lesson. In the process, Surekha along with nine others assaulted Raj Patil and threw his body on the railway tracks

However, during the course of the trial, a central railway motorman Vijay Pawar who was on duty deposed that the victim was crossing the tracks while the train was coming a died.

Hearing the case, Additional Sessions Judge SB Agarwal acquitted Surekha and nine others in the case.

Heading: Shiv Sena changing stripes? - Indian Express
Content:
Car with fake national emblem spotted during President's visit: three days after hoodwinking constables, duo nabbed

In a major embarrassment to the Pune police, it has come to light that two persons — a man and a woman — who were nabbed at Balewadi phata with a car (DL 9 CL 2140) carrying a fake national emblem and a "Govt of India" sticker, managed to hoodwink the traffic police constables and escape.

On Tuesday, the police managed to save face and said they had nabbed the duo, according to a press release sent late in the evening.

The incident had taken place on October 11, when traffic police inspector Surendranath Deshmukh impounded the car some six km from the Raj Bhavan, where the President was to be put up that day. Incidentally, on Sunday the police received a terror mail threatening an attack on President Pratibha Patil.

Police are now investigating the motive of the duo behind using such a car, though initial questioning revealed that the motive was only to con people by posing as government officials and not to break into the President's convoy.

Joint Commissioner of Police Rajendra Sonawane said, "Inspector Deshmukh was heading to Balewadi when he spotted the car with the national emblem. He found out that the emblem was a forged one. On being questioned, the driver of the car identified himself as Pinto Sengupta (40) and his friend as Susan (35)."

"Deshmukh asked two police constables (new recruits), who were on bandobast duty, to take the car and the duo to the police commissionerate. The constable went along with them to the Poona Gate police chowky.

On their way to the commissionerate, Pinto said they wanted to visit a relative in Jehangir Hospital and gave the constables the slip after getting down the vehicle," Sonawane said.

Soon, the Bomb Detection and Disposal Squad (BDDS) of Pune police was pressed into action but the car was found clean.

The terror mail that surfaced the next day put the onus on the police to trace the duo and now the police are probing whether the car was trying to enter the President's convoy. "The President was at Raj Bhavan and the car was stopped at Balewadi phata. As of now we have nothing to confirm that the car was part of some conspiracy," said Sonawane.

When questioned by the constables at Poona Gate chowky, Pinto had provided four addresses — three Pune references and the fourth one, a Delhi address.

"Pinto had given three Pune addresses in Senapati Bapat Road, Baner Road and Kalewadi and a Delhi address. The Delhi address is B-7 Safdarjung Enclave, New Delhi. He said that his brother-in -law is a resident of Kalewadi," said Sonawane.
