Police are now verifying all the addresses. Pinto's brother-in-law was also questioned. Pinto has told the police that he was a programme officer with a company in Delhi and earned Rs 6.2 lakh annually. He said that he joined the company in 2006 and was staying on rent at the Delhi address.

Sonawane said that the crime branch was investigating the case.

Heading: Grand Carnival adds to Games colour - Indian Express
Content:
Sena decides to reach voters with specific issues; Sainiks don't like it

The Shiv Sena has come up with a campaign to woo the voters in a systematic way. Though the idea is based on reaching every voter with specific issues, it has not gone down well with the Shiv Sainiks, who are used to hearing slapstick speeches.

A meeting of party workers of Pune Parliamentary Constituency on Tuesday was a reflection of this mindset. The Shiv Sena has planned to go to all the 48 Parliamentary constituencies, meeting party workers and telling them tactics of reaching the voters in an effective way. The responsibility has been put on the shoulders of 12 senior leaders. The party has equipped them with a booklet and even with a power point presentation, which tells about how to convince the voters on the issues of suicides of farmers, electricity crisis and wrong policy on sugarcane and cotton.

Senior leaders Diwakar Rawate and Vinod Ghosalkar have been assigned the responsibility of Pune Parliamentary Constituency.

They made a presentation before the party workers on Friday. But to the dismay of these leaders, many party workers left the auditorium during the presentation that lacked the verbose appeal to which the Shiv Sainiks are used to. The auditorium, which was packed to capacity of more than 1,000 seats, wore a deserted look as the meeting proceeded, with merely 400 workers staying back till the end.

However, the shift in the tactics of the Shiv Sena was noticeable in the speeches. "We had won the raging war of words in the past. But with the changing times, we should be more careful and reach out to voters with solutions to their problems," said Ghosalkar.

Sunil Prabhu, leader of house in BMC, stressed the need for reading the voter list and identifying devoted voters. "Every block level leader should take the responsibility of 1,200 voters in his block. He is expected to take a review of the portfolio of the voters and address issues accordingly," he said.

The handbook prepared for block leaders is well equipped with instructions on how to survey the voter list and the aims of the party. It also suggests homework by party workers.

Earlier in his speech, Rawate lashed out at the state government on the issue of Dow Chemical R&D unit. Rawate ridiculed the state government for putting warkaris behind the bars for opposing the unit. "It is shameful to see harmless warkaris getting such treatment in this state," he said.

Heading: Athavale’s turn to bat for Maratha reservation - Indian Express
Content:
As the city revels in the festive atmosphere of the Commonwealth Youth Games (CYG), which commenced at Balewadi on Sunday, the Pune Cantonment Board (PCB), in collaboration with BRAND Knew, an event management firm, has joined the party by organising the 'Grand Carnival,' a three-day event on M G Road. The gala opened on Tuesday to an enthusiastic response from Punekars .

"The celebration kicked off with a carnival, where children from PCB-run schools welcomed visitors," said Amreysh Dubey, director, BRAND Knew. Apart from music and dance performances, laser shows, bicycle stunts, a couple of surprise elements were lined up, he said. This was followed by a music performance from ROCKYS Dynamites. "The atmosphere is fantastic. The Walking Plaza has been given a whole new look and we are enjoying it immensely," said Ashish Dixit, a visitor.

According to Dubey, "The Grand Carnival aims at sending out a positive message and commemorate the CYG. The response has been good. Many stalls, including food counters, handicraft stores and artificial tattoo parlours have been put up. Several events have been planned for the next two days and eager participation from citizens will ensure that the carnival is a grand success."

PCB president Brig R J Sharma said, "The CYG is being held in the city and this is a special occasion for Pune. The M G Road region will sport a festive look throughout the Grand Carnival and during the CYG. Foolproof security measures are in place. This is just the first day and the response, which has been enthusiastic, is sure to pick up in the next two days."

Expressing confidence in the security arrangements, Dubey said, "We at BRAND Knew are confident about the security arrangements made by the PCB. Further, the company has hired private security guards who are deployed in and around the venue. We will jointly strive to ensure that the public have a gala time."

The total mark-up for the carnival is Rs 65 lakh, of which the PCB has contributed Rs 35 lakh. The remaining has been raised through sponsors. A major chunk of the total investment has been spent on hoardings and giving the M G Road area a facelift, thus showcasing the old charm of Pune to visitors and CYG participants.

However, the first day of the carnival saw some visitors gazing at empty stalls and hunting for chilled bottles of soft drinks. Shashank Pethekar and friends had a hard time looking for cold drinks. "The cold drinks stall did not have any bottles because the cooling machine was yet to be set up," he said.

With five empty stalls and strings of lights yet to be put up to add to the glitter of the carnival, some who had high expectations from the carnival were a bit disappointed. Thus, Chamandeep Singh found the first day no different from the regular weekend at Walking Plaza. "Big and bright are not the words you can associate with this carnival. There is only one stage that has been put up. The other end looks almost deserted."

Heading: Bharati Vidyapeeth University makes a campus shift - Indian Express
Content:
After the Nationalist Congress Party (NCP), it's now the turn of the Republican Party of India (Athavale) to bat for reservation for the Maratha community.

RPI leader and MP Ramdas Athavale on Tuesday came out in open support of the reservation demand of the community.

Clearly being targeted are the Maratha votes and at stake is the new Lok Sabha constituency of Shirdi, reserved for the Scheduled Caste category after the delimitation process.

While Athavale said he was in favour of reservation for the Maratha community, he added that it should not be at the cost of reservations for other communities.

"We support the demand of reservation for the Maratha community as it would go a long way in removing the inferior way in which those currently availing of reservation are seen. Our party would hold a rally in Kolhapur on November 28 to extend our support for the demand," Athavale told reporters at a press conference here.

Athavale was elected from the Pandharpur constituency, reserved for the Scheduled Caste, but now Shirdi will be the reserved seat.

The Shiv Sena had been raking up the Marathi cause for long and the Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) has been aggressively pursuing the sons-of-the-soil stand for over two years since the party's inception. More and more parties are now jumping onto the bandwagon, but in a restrained way.

A few days back NCP chief Sharad Pawar had said that he was in favour of reservation for the Maratha community. Pawar had also added that caution should be shown in this regard and other communities should be taken into confidence before taking a decision.

In fact, Athavale is looking at NCP support in Shirdi constituency. "I have urged the NCP to support me in the newly reserved Shirdi constituency," Athavale said.

Athavale said it was a good sign that those opposing reservations were now seeking the same, adding there should be separate reservation for the Brahmin and Muslim communities as well.

However, Athavale was quick to add that any new reservation should not be at the cost of the existing reservations.

He was not in favour of reservation on the basis of economic status of a person.

"The reservation system is based on caste and should not be mixed with the economic status of any individual," Athavale said.

The RPI leader reiterated the demand for an independent Vidarbha state saying the development of the region would not take place unless it got the status of a separate state.

Athavale said that his party would take out a rally in Nagpur on November 25 during the forthcoming Winter Session of state legislature demanding immediate passing of a resolution to grant the status of independent state to Vidarbha. The RPI (A) has also organised a rally for the rights of Dalits and Muslims on November 16 at B J Medical College ground.

Heading: All eyes on Ashoka Mews Society - Indian Express
Content:
Policy change forces university to relocate proposed campus from Dubai to Ras Al Khaimah; batch to start in Feb

The Dubai bug has caught up with Bharati Vidyapeeth University (BVU), months after University of Pune (UoP) was laid low. But the BVU has taken remedial measures unlike the UoP and has decided to put an end to Dubai campus dreams and instead concentrate on a campus at Ras Al Khaimah, an emirate at the north end of the UAE, 64 km from Dubai.

A change in policy by the Dubai authorities had put paid to the efforts of BVU to flag off its Dubai campus in September. With this setback, the BVU has also revised its timeline to February 2009 to roll out its BBA and MBA courses from the Ras Al Khaimah campus.

Plans to move to Ras Al Khaimah were confirmed by S F Patil, coordinator of the BVU project. "We had been trying hard to meet the deadline to start our Dubai campus. Owing to some changes in the policy by the Dubai authorities, we were not able to meet it. As we had taken up land in Ras Al Khaimah as well, we shifted our focus there," he said.

Ras Al Khaimah is reportedly the third preferred destination for educational campuses in the UAE, after Dubai and Abu Dhabi. With the UAE government promoting educational activities in each of the seven emirates and thereby creating free zones for foreign institutes to set up their campuses, Ras Al Khaimah was an easy choice for BVU to make, a source said.

BVU had planned to start the campus at Dubai International Academic City (DIAC) and had been working at it for the past one year. BVU had declared in April that the Dubai campus would start by September 2008.

"The shift in the policy of the Dubai authorities says the present land of one lakh sq ft that we have at DIAC, should be used for a school. This forced us to change our plans," said Patil.

Patil reiterated that the management courses would definitely be started from February 2009 at Ras Al Khaimah. "The initial intake will be 120 students, 60 each for the BBA and MBA courses," he said.

The university has initially invested around Rs 5 crore for the Dubai campus. "Many Indians have settled down in Dubai. Normally, their children come to India for degree courses. We will be targeting such students as well as the natives," said Patil.

There are more than 10 Indian institutes in Dubai including BITS-Pilani, S P Jain Institute and Manipal University. Besides BVU, University of Pune and Symbiosis International University are the premium universities from Pune that have been planning their Dubai campuses.

Too many Indian players?
The authorities in Dubai feel that the Dubai International Academic City (DIAC) should have a global face and it will not be achieved if there are too many institutes from only one country. And that is why the authorities have put a restriction on the number of institutes from India and decided to give preference to European, American and Australian institutes.

Meanwhile, Symbiosis International University has already declared that its Dubai campus would start in September 2009.

Heading: Terrorist activities are politically motivated: Expert - Indian Express
Content:
Fear and suspicion loom large among the residents of Ashoka Mews society in Kondhwa, from where four alleged terrorists affiliated to Indian Mujahideen were nabbed by the Mumbai Crime Branch. The recent spate of arrests of terror suspects has unnerved the residents of the society.

When this reporter tried to ask one of the residents of the society where the flat rents have gone down in the society, she said " You might be a terrorist, I do not know. We don't give flats on rent in the society without police verification, don't give any news about our society. There already has been much bad press." Other residents also were reluctant in talking to us.

" Rent rates in the area around Ashoka Mews society have decreased, but this has no overall effect on Kondhwa area as a whole. Yes, but buying and selling rates for new and old flats have been affected. You can get discounts from Rupees 200 to 400 per square feet" said Prashant Gangekar, a manager working with a construction company in Kondhwa.

Heading: IT firms may make police verification mandatory - Indian Express
Content:
Ram Puniyani, professor with IIT-Mumbai and author of 'Terrorism: Facts versus Myths' said that all terrorist activities are politically motivated and that it is wrong to tag a particular community as 'terrorists'.

"Violence in the name of religion is a destructive political agenda in disguise. It is similar to what happened in Germany," he said. He hinted that the two largest political motivators are sitting in Washington and Nagpur.

Puniyani was one among the four speakers in a discussion on 'Religious Violence: A threat to democracy' organised by Lokayat and Haji Gulam Mohammed Trust. As a reply to the common message being circulated – "All Muslims are not terrorists, but all terrorists are Muslims", he cited three murder cases in history –that of Mahatma Gandhi, Indira Gandhi and Rajiv Gandhi to imply that none of the murders were by Muslims. "The phrase Islamic terrorism was coined by the American media after 9/11 and is later picked up by the Indian media," he said. Puniyani added that the words 'jihad', which actually means self-purification has been given a completely different shade of meaning by the terrorists organisations.

Later, the discussion revolved around need for secular and learned citizens to be well informed about issues in order to take a stand against violence. The other three speakers -Irfan Engineer, director of Institute for Peace Studies and Conflict Resolution, Mumbai, Dolphy D'souza, president of Bombay Catholic Sabha and Pranab Mukherjee, United Nations Fellow for Human rights and exponent of alternative theatre experiments focused on the need to have a 'secular agenda' just as communists have their own agenda.

Mukherjee said that today, protests by secularists are largely a business game. "Indian academics is largely communal and there is a need to bring secularism in the notebooks of school students. The persons in the Indian performing arts, too have become inert to communal violence," he said adding that secularists must be able to tackle the communal agenda by being informed.

D'souza mentioned a list of five points to mobilise the common man against any kind of communal violence. "Instead of playing the spectator game in case of communal violence, citizens should stay organised and informed to counter terrorism. There should be inter-religious dialogue and citizens must ensure judicial intervention in cases of communal violence," he said.

Engineer said that no terrorist is fighting for a particular religion, but against law and order and democracy. "Gandhiji and Maulana Abul Kalam Azad were the two people who were extremely religious, who viewed religion in terms of morality. Today, religion is brought down to being a reason for immorality," he said. Engineer quoted that according to the Ministry of Home Affairs, 35,000 persons, majority of whom were Muslims, have been killed since the 1961 communal riots.

Heading: Pimpri grapples with dengue, malaria cases - Indian Express
Content:
With four out of eight Indian Mujahideen men arrested in the city from IT and engineering backgrounds, IT companies as well as the recruitment firms are now making stringent measures on making police verification and documentation important aspect of background checks.

Professionals in the industry say that with the involvement of terrorists in white-collar jobs, the demand for police verification is likely to go high.

Geeta Monga who runs recruitment firm named MGA systems says, "We have been receiving enquiries on doing stringent background checks from our clients. We have been doing the reference checks but they have till date been limited to behaviour, previous employment and so on. If the demand for such verifications goes high, we would be introducing such verifications for the safety of our clients."

While this is about the recruitment firms that are all prepared to make police verification a part of reference checks, the background check agencies are already equipped and following the procedure. CRP is an external agency that has been doing reference checks for a number of well-known corporate houses. Imran Shaikh who deals with such references checks in CRP says, "Police reference checks till date were organization specific. They involve an in depth analysis of the involvement of the candidate in any kind of terrorist activity.

Another factor is that doing a police verification is a tedious and a costly affair and hence a budget related activity. But with these kinds of connections, organisations are finding these police checks more affordable than employing wrong people. We have thus made police verification check a part of our process. We go to the police station and check if the candidate has any FIR or criminal record for the past three years."

Police verification is a time consuming process and by the time the results come out, the possibility of the candidate having joined and served the organisation cannot be neglected. Shilpa Rajput, an HR professional with an MNC says, "We have an external verification check agency that does reference checks for us. Police verifications were till date limited to senior positions.

But now we have made it mandatory for all the positions be it senior or junior.

In fact we have increased the number of audits taking place in our company and now the external audit agencies will also be checking the pending background checks of candidates. We take care of the other documentation by the time the reference check results come to us."

Heading: CYG: Mobile counter irks spectators - Indian Express
Content:
312 malaria, 178 dengue cases since Jan 1; figure much more than what PCMC says, 260 hospitals not providing patients' details

From September 1 to October 14, 99 citizens have been affected by dengue and 72 by malaria in Pimpri-Chinchwad. From January 1 to October 14, there have been 312 malaria cases while the figure of dengue stands at 178. These are the figures put out by the medical department of the Pimpri-Chinchwad Municipal Corporation.

The figures clearly reveal that dengue and malaria cases, like last year, have been spiralling in the industrial town. But they are not for real. The reason: these figures have been collected only from eight civic-run hospitals, 13 dispensaries and three big private hospitals.

Nearly 260 private hospitals and over 50 private pathology laboratories do not provide PCMC the details about dengue and malaria patients — a fact revealed by the medical department itself. This means, the dengue and malaria figures are much more than what the PCMC regularly puts out. "They could actually be in thousands since over 200 hospitals don't care about providing details about malaria and dengue patients undergoing treatment or those treated by them," say private practictioners.

Under the Bombay Nursing Act, it is mandatory for all the hospitals to provide details of the patients treated by them or about those who have died. "The rule says hospital should provide us with the details rather than we seeking information from them," PCMC medical director Rajshekhar Iyer.

Though the hospitals not have been keeping the PCMC updated with the information, the medical department of the PCMC too has done little on this front.

It has not initiated any punitive action against any hospital though the Act clearly specifies that the licence of a hospital which fails to provide details about patients treatment is not furnished to the local civic authority. "We have every right to cancel the licence of such a hospital. So far, no action has been initiated against any hospital. But we will soon first sound the hospitals about this and then if they fail to act, we will initiate appropriate action," said Dr Iyer.

Apart from hospitals not providing information, there are also patients who undergo treatment in private hospitals in Pune.

The figures of such patients is also in big. The PCMC has no clue about them which further confirms the fact that both malaria and dengue far bigger in number.

Heading: ‘Cradle’ rally to save girl child - Indian Express
Content:
The second day at the Commonwealth Youth Games venue angered several spectators.

At mobile deposit counter many got irritated and a number of them left without utilising the purchased tickets. The reason being the alleged mismanagement of mobile phones and camera storage system at CYG.

An agitated visitor, Usha Sharma who waited in the long queue for submitting her mobile phone for more than two hours said, "I didn't know that mobile phones are not supposed to be carried to the venue. Later I came to know that we could submit our mobiles at a counter but we had to wait in the queue for two and a half hours."

The counter was not present on Monday. Initially, the visitors who were writing their names and mobile numbers were asked to switch off their mobile phones before depositing at the counter.

Sudhakar Gaikwad, a spectator said, "There were no tokens given to us. They were randomly searching for mobile phones when we came back to collect them. My phone was fortunately on and the men at the counter had to call up my number in order to find it from the mess. After this they started allowing everyone to keep their mobile phones on before depositing. The queue was so long that a person, who had come to watch a particular match went without seeing it."

Police officials, who claimed that their duty was limited to screening and checking if anyone was carrying any electronic item and had nothing to do with mobile deposit counter, were seen running the mobile phone counters.

Police person in charge Narayan Khaire said, "We allowed them to carry the phones yesterday because there was no storage system but today the management committee in a meeting informed us that mobile phones are not supposed to be sent. We have been doing our job and have nothing to do with the deposit counter."

There were allegations that tickets were not available in some counters and people were asked to go to the other centres to get one.

According to Ashok Kumar Roopani, a spectator, "I had gone to the counter at CYG yesterday to buy tickets for the closing ceremony and was told that tickets were sold and I could get it from ICC towers. When I went to ICC towers, I was informed to go to Sanas Ground. There should be a system where we come to know about the availability of tickets in all the counters." The ticketing officials at the CYG counter refused to comment on this.

The confusions at the boxing arena were between organising committee and volunteers.

According to D S Kadam, police official at the boxing arena, "Over 150 volunteers wanted to get into the boxing arena to see Indian boxers performing. Volunteers have specific working areas and are not allowed entry at other venues except for their own. So we had to stop them from entering."

A volunteer who does not want his identity to be disclosed said, "The infinity symbol on our cards means that we have access to all the venues. So we see no reason why we should be stopped from entering any of the sports arenas."

Heading: Coming soon: cyber cafe for  visually-impaired - Indian Express
Content:
The Indian Medical Association (IMA) along with Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) will conduct a 'cradle' rally to create awareness on sex determination test among the public and a workshop for doctors—'safe practices under Pre-Conception and Pre natal diagnostic techniques (PC-PNDT) act' on October 18 and 19.

Dr Vaijayanti Patwardhan, President of 'Garima manch' of the IMA told media persons on Tuesday that the cradle rally is organised to create awareness about saving the girl child. The rally will be taken out on October 19 from Sarasbaug and culminate at Dr Nitu Mandke IMA building in Tilak Road. Focus will be given to create awareness about nutrition for pregnant women. Actress Nishigandha Wad and others will be present.

Patwardhan said efforts are on to revive Doctors Opposing Sex Selection Trends (DOSST) cell, as part of it's save the girl child campaign. The cell was set up to counsel doctors and patients, who opt for sex determination tests.

If the doctors here are not willing to do the test, patients go to other places like Jalgaon and Aurangabad. So we aim to counsel patients, as it is doctors who are always blamed for misusing the ultrasound machine for sex determination tests, said Patwardhan .

The campaign will also reiterate the importance of PC-PNDT act.

Heading: Appoint expert committee to probe land grab: Medha Patkar - Indian Express
Content:
In yet another attempt to bring visually challenged on to the mainstream, Rahul Deshmukh, a social activist, who himself is visually- impaired plans to come up with cyber café for them.

Deshmukh, has been running an organisation, Snehankit Association, for visually-challenged, offering degree courses in information technology. To provide them with an opportunity to access Internet he is planning to start National Association of Welfare of physically-challenged. "The cyber café, which will be first of its kind in the city, would open doors of e-world to the visually-challenged students. American software, Jaws for Windows will be installed in the computer. With this they can send and receive e-mails and even chat with their friends," says Deskmukh, who looks forward to provide much more to visually-challenged people.

The café will provide free Internet access to visually challenged people. Apart from the treasure of knowledge that lies at click of a mouse, visually students will also be able to enjoy networking through Internet. Giving the credit to his students, he says that they are his inspiration. "The demand came from my students, who said that after doing a course in IT they don't get any place to be in touch with practical application of programme or softwares. And because of this they cannot keep themselves updated and thus lag behind. This made me think of such project. This would be our first project after the organisation is formed," says Deshmukh. Recalling his struggling days, the 30-year-old activist says that he was denied admission in regular IT colleges given his visual impairment. And he had to struggle hard to come up to this position where he can lend a helping hand instead of asking for one." The noble project is, however, facing a financial crunch and needs Rs 2,50,000 for the café. "The amount is big and we are trying hard to arrange for this. I would also like to make an appeal to the public to donate for this project and make our lives a bit more live," appeals Deshmukh.

Heading: Daily soap - Indian Express
Content:
Social activist Medha Patkar has demanded the appointment of an inquiry committee to probe into the land acquisition and diversion of water for developmental projects. Patkar who was in Pune on Monday is touring the state to take up issues of those, who have to bear the ill affect of industrialisation.

Demanding a probe into the alleged cases of land grab in and around Pune for various projects, Patkar said a report should be readied soon to check on the surplus land acquired for various projects.

Terming the shifting of Tata Motors Nano project from Singur as a victory for local farmers, she stressed that development was possible with minimum displacement. She said setting up of a Special Economic Zone (SEZ) was not industrialisation but just land grabbing.

In Pune she earlier visited Mulshi and Maval areas to address the issues of the displaced families of the Tata Power project, Pavana dam and Khed SEZ. Patkar had earlier submitted a memorandum to the divisional commissioner of Pune, Nitin Kareer on the rehabilitation policy and is carrying out a state- wide agitation to get the government to work towards investigating the land grabbing in Pune and other parts of the state. Meanwhile, Tata Power in a media statement said that the land acquisition done for setting up its hydro projects 80 years ago was done legally and officially. The statement further mentions "Tata Power's hydro power station has been serving clean and green power to Mumbai since last 8 decades. The Company maintains that there are no dues pending of the concerned persons. In meetings held with Tata Power representatives and the relevant local Government officials it has been acknowledged that Tata Power has met all legal obligations pertaining to the issue,''

The company has clarified that they had extended all support to the government in their land inquiry and has produced records pertaining to the land acquired through the government for the hydro facility to the Collector (Pune).

The records included details of each parcel of land acquired for the project, compensation paid to the government for the acquired land and for other essentials.

Heading: Fitness mantra - Indian Express
Content:
Global Hand-washing Day aims to control communicable fatal diseases and thus control mortality rate among children

Up to a million microbes could have touched your child's lunch before they do! Whilst you – and they – think that they're tucking into a healthy meal of roti and sabzi or daal and rice, chances are that they're also likely to be swallowing germs that have the potential to make them sick, if they haven't washed their hands with soap first.

A million microbes reach our children's hands every day – from their journey to school, the hands of their classmates, their books and desks in the classroom, the toilet. Though their little hands might look perfectly clean, they are likely to be squirming with someone else's germs by the time they sit down for lunch.

Hands are the principal carriers of disease-causing and potentially life-threatening germs, causing diarrhoea, pneumonia, cholera and dysentery. But a simple hygiene habit – washing hands with soap after the toilet and before lunch – will help make sure these germs don't enter your child's body.

Global Hand-washing Day on October 15 is a platform to create a global culture of washing hands with soap. Lifebuoy, in partnership with the coalition, will be launching the inaugural Global Hand Wash Day in India on October 15 even as 20 other countries across five continents do the same across the world.

Every year, millions of children across the world don't live to celebrate their fifth birthday. The objective of establishing Global Hand-washing Day is to control communicable fatal diseases like diarrhoea and pneumonia, a release issued here stated. Vision on Global Handwashing Day is to foster global and local culture of handwashing with soap, which is also the most effective and inexpensive ways to prevent diarrhoeal diseases and pneumonia.

Washing hands with soap is a significant contribution to meeting the UN Millennium Development goal of reducing death among children under age of five by two-third by 2015.

Heading: Art Attack - Indian Express
Content:
The well-equipped medical centre - Polyclinic at CYG ensures safety and fast recovery of the athletes in case of medical emergency

Games and injuries go hand in hand. And where performance matters, recovery has to be fast. The polyclinic in the Commonwealth Youth Games (CYG) premises is well-equipped to handle the emergencies that arise during the matches or competitions.

The polyclinic that will be converted into a section of the existing Sports Science Centre (SSC) after the games get over, hosts a hospital with a number of sections like casualty, out patients department, rehabilitation centre, dental clinic, ophthalmology centre and so on.

In addition to the set up, all the nine sports venues and the training centre consists of a team of five medical members including-venue medical officer, emergency supervisor, physiotherapist, nurse and a medical attendant. It is after inspection by theses primary attendants, that the injured person is brought to polyclinic. According to Dr Parag Sancheti, convenor, Polyclinic, "We have a system of tackling health-related queries. When we get a case of medical emergency, we admit the patient in casualty department. More serious cases are transferred to the OPD and if we diagnose a serious medical problem the athletes are taken immediately to the Aditya Birla Hospital."

Dr Anand Gangwal further adds, "We have 24X7 orthopedics from Sancheti, ENT specialists and dentists from the command military centre. A newly introduced concept called ice bath. The ice bath is given for fast recovery here at SSC. Due to over exercising, the lactic acid secretions go high and ice bath is used to control that. We get about 250 kg of ice every day for the ice bath section."

Also a part of the Polyclinic is the physiotherapy centre that has equipments like traction machine and diathermy for fast relief. It also hosts a small rehabilitation gym that is used specifically for training injured athletes. According to Dr D S Bhamare, head, SSC, "The main gym is different from this. We also have a steam and sauna bathroom in this centre."

An interesting part of the polyclinic is the anti-doping cell, which is part of the CYG for the first time in the history of the games. Approved and assessed by World Anti Doping Association (WADA), the centre will be conducting random checks during the tenure of the games. According to the authorities, "We have maintained a transparency in operations. The sample collected from the sportsmen are divided into two parts A and B. Sample A is sent to Delhi for examinations and sample B is kept in case the player wants to challenge the results. We also do doping checks on request. For instance if an athlete has not won an event but has still managed to create a national record for his own nation, the authorities of the country request us to get a dope check done. The whole set up is created with a motive that the players should be aware of the fact that if they cheat, the systems here are sound enough to detect and take disciplinary action."

Heading: Click 'N' shop - Indian Express
Content:
Artistes from across the country, handpicked for the talents, have been given a platform at the CYG to showcase their creative skills and craft

As the country puts its best foot forward while hosting the international mega sports event, fine artistes from various pockets of the country, have been chosen by the organisers, to display the traditional handicrafts from diverse cultures at the CYG cultural centre in Balewadi.

Exhibiting their fine art works at the centre, many of them are state or national award winners. They feel that such a platform would help in getting international appreciation and also give them an idea of trends overseas. "I have been getting offers to exhibit my works abroad in countries like London, Japan, America and so on. The CYG platform is likely to help me get an idea of the demand of consumers abroad," says Manmohan Soni, a chann-hatodi kalakaar from Kulpahar in Mahoba, Uttar Pradesh, who hammers in fine designs of different deities on brass metal. "This is the traditional art of Uttar Pradesh, which has been there for over 100 years, I learnt it from my father and now I teach it to other aspiring artists at Gyasi Purtan Kala Kendra in UP," adds Soni, the first in his family to bag a state and national award.

With the skill of superior carvings, the association of national award has been there for three generations with the family of Rajender Parshad Bonndwal from Haryana. Bondwal, 1984 national award winner for ivory carvings has participated in impart training in Germany and is now the general secretary of Haryana State Karigar Assosiation. "The main reason to come to the games at Pune was to display our work and let more and more people know about it. Initially we made carvings on ivory, but after ivory was banned now we make them on wood, sandalwood and bone. This is an art inherited to all the men in our family."

Nazda Thakur, artisan, who is displaying the handicraft grass puppet, says that CYG platform is an opportunity to display our rural craft that she learnt from her grandmother and mother and will teach it to her daughter and daughter-in-law. "Strips of coloured hay are turned and plated to make different items like baskets, dolls that are replicas of the goddess and so on. Our works have been recognised by many associations and we earn our living from it," says Thakur.

Doll puppets have been there everywhere, but leather puppets made by Khande Ramdaas, showcases a different art. "First a drawing is made on the translucent leather sheet, which is painted with powder colours then strings are attached," explains Ramdaas from Andhra Pradesh.

Coming from the snow valley, the Wani brothers are displaying traditional Kashmiri Hazara painting work on paper mache box. "This is the traditional art of Kashmir, the boxes are used to store jewellery and other antique items," says Nazir Ahmed and Mohammed Maqbool Wani from Srinagar, who use almost 10 colours on each box and say that the procedure is long and expensive. Conversly, a terracotta artist from Tamil Nadu, can make attractive Ganesh idols idols with just pieces of a Renolyds pen, an ice-cream stick, wet clay and 30 seconds in hand.

An not to miss on the Pune kid, Haris Khan, a standard five student from Sinhagad City School who is also showing his portraits besides the Pottachitra paintings by Sudam Charan Sahu from Puri, Orrisa, Tanjore painting by J Mohan from Tamil Nadu and traditional Rajasthani paintings by Hari Narayan, from Jaipur.

Crowing the counter, the foreign athletes and the volunteers enjoyed seeing the course of action Rehana and Mohammed Salim from Hyderabad undertook to make colourful and stone-embedded lac bangles. Along with the bangles other ornaments, accessories and outfits from various places like Rajasthan and Kutch and Bhuj district of Gujarat are also at display.

Heading: Sporting grounds - Indian Express
Content:
One of the oldest and busiest shopping areas in Pune, the Laxmi Road goes online from this season

Instead of fuelling the engine of her car to sail through the sea of extremely congested moving -to-office traffic on a Monday to satiate her kids sweet tooth needs, Pradnya Jawadekar simply switched on her CPU to log on to laxmiroad.in and shopped online for Bakarwadi and Moti chur ke laddu to her heart's content. For Jawadekar who stays in Aundh finding about the very city centric online portal laxmiroad.in was pure bliss. "The idea of hunting for a parking place in the shopping pockets of the city makes me shudder and Laxmi road tops the chart of the busiest shopping hubs in the city. The thought of honking repeatedly in that traffic and slipping like a snail in itself is very de - motivating for a shopping spree. So many a times with a heavy heart we have compromised with the kind of stuff we get in Aundh and its surroundings, only occasionally mustering up enough courage to fight the traffic to go to Laxmi Road or Camp," shares Jawadekar who now simply buys online thanks to the 43-day old portal.

It was some two years back when Amit Dixit a software engineer stumbled upon the idea on coming with an online portal for laxmiroad. " The idea would have never hit me if I too would not have undergone the same pathetic experience like other shoppers at laxmiroad." It was in the year 2006 when Amit Dixit happened to witness the traffic and the parking problem at Laxmi Road for the first time. "When I returned that day I decided I will do something about it," shares Dixit.

As the motivation came so followed the planning for the idea of making this busy shopping hub easily accessible to shopoholics and that's how laxmiroad.in toddled towards its existence. "I thought about getting most of the shops online and give home delivery facility. This would have been really useful for those staying quite far in areas like Aundh, Baner and Kondhawa because the people living in these places miss out on enjoying shopping a wide range of shopping materials which are available at shopping hubs."

Going about giving his idea a concrete shape Dixit spoke to the various shop owners in Laxmi Road "I started talking to some of the shopkeepers in 2007 just to get their opinion and judge their mindset. The response was very positive and so finally I decided to jump into this from February 2008."

The domain now displays the items available at seven shops at Laxmi Road including Kheliya toy shop and Chitale Bandhu Mithaiwale. Also the portal has Varma Book Centre and Venus traders showcasing their items and rates at the site. "When Amit came to us with the idea we agreed to it at once because we know it will increase our sales as shopping will be a much more easy affair for the people," says Kamal Somani, owner, Shri Krishna Perals

The portal, which is functional since September 2, till now has more than 30 orders that have been placed through the domain and has more than 50 members who have registered themselves as members. The portal charges a nominal amount of Rs 20 for home delivery.

Heading: Watery grave for eight as boat capsizes in Jamnagar - Indian Express
Content:
Sculptures representing Indian games are a favourite hangout for a number of foreign athletes

Indian games might not have found place in the nine games at the Commonwealth Youth Games, but that does not mean that they have not made their presence felt inside the CYG campus. In fact most of the athletes after the hectic schedules find time to relax at the squares that are decorated using the sculptures designed to represent over six Indian games.

Immediately after one enters the sports city, a giant globe held in a massive hand being showered continuously by a picturesque fountain attracts the attention of the visitors. This is the Garden Of Youth. With flags of 71 countries circling the globe and the CYG baton on top, this beautiful creation symbolises the spirit of CYG. Explaining the logic behind the structure, Gaurish Chandawarkar, landscape architect, SGC design group responsible for designing the landscapes at CYG says, "We have formulated the youth garden in such a manner that there is a spiral way that leads one to the fountain. This spiral way represents the fluidity and dynamism that youth carries. The hand in the centre is India with symbols of all the nine games carved on it. We have planted Champa trees in such a manner that while going inside, one sees white flowers and while returning- red."

Ahead of the Garden Of Youth as one takes a left, a giant rising sun represents the ball in the traditional Indian game – Lagori. While most of the athletes find this as a relaxing place to sit and chat after the tiring day, what satisfies their curious looks is a board that gives information about Lagori as a game and the places where it is played in India.

Almost all the athletes have to visit the warm-up grounds before the actual competition and what has become a funny habit amongst the sportsmen is to climb up huge spinning top by the side of the tracks and watch their team mates practice. According to Vishwas Kanekar, head, Space Constructive creations, who have conceptualised the idea of putting sculptures of Indian sports for beautification, "We have made this spinning top from the waste metal material from the CYG venue. The shaft of the spinning top has stairs and one can climb up from the shaft and come down from the slide at the other side." Not many know that there are over 25 types of tops in the world and that China has the largest spinning top in the World. A lot of interesting information unveils on the information board displayed by the side of the top.

No child can ever miss this. A huge red and yellow climbing wall that resembles the snake and ladder game that makes many adults become children. Kanekar says, "In fact this as well has stairs from which one can climb and enjoy the view around." A concept which is still under development is the Yoga garden. With two yogic positions on two sides of a ground, this garden is designed to give peace of mind to the observer. "We want the landscapes to be remembered even after the games are over so much so that it should become a tourist attraction after the games," adds Kanekar.

Heading: Principal offenders: Two headmasters accused of running recruitment racket - Indian Express
Content:
Four women, four kids among dead; twenty suffer injuries

Four women and four infants, drowned and at least 20 others sustained injuries, in a boat mishap off the Bedi Port in Jamnagar on Tuesday morning. All the deceased have been identified as members of the Muslim community who were on a pilgrimage to a dargah in the nearby Pirotan island.

According to officials of the Gujarat Maritime Board (GMB) in Jamnagar, the incident occurred around 11 am when a group of 30-35 people boarded the vessel that was to ferry them to the dargah about 8 km off the Bedi Port. "Once the boat began moving, some passengers huddled together at one corner. When others too moved to that side, the boat first tilted and then turned turtle, throwing the people on board into the water," said a GMB official.

Teams of the GMB and the Jamnagar Fire Brigade launched a rescue operation soon after the mishap. Jamnagar Superintendent of Police R B Jotangiya said though many people have been rescued, there were many others trapped under the overturned boat, who could not be saved.

"We have registered a case of accidental death and investigations are on to find out if there was any negligence," he said.

The eight deceased have been identified as Amina Habib (45), Hussaini Anwar (27), Kulsum Asam (28), Husaina Salim Buchar (24), Amir Hussain (5), Abbas Salim (7), Sirin Anwarbhai (12) and Samir Asam (3) — all residents of Bedi village on the outskirts of Jamnagar. The injured have been admitted to the G G Hospital in Jamnagar.

Heading: In rural Gujarat schools, cleaning toilets is still the job of Dalit students - Indian Express
Content:
Arrest of two teachers exposes nexus between school authorities and job camp organisers

The arrest of a government school teacher and a clerk for issuing fake NCC certificates has exposed the nexus between the school authorities and recruitment camp organisers.

Two government schools principals and recruitment drive officials have now been charged with heading the primary school teachers' appointment racket.

According to the police, school teacher Ramsu Charel and clerk Mahendra Patel, who were arrested on Monday , "admitted that they worked for Vadodara's Motenath School principal Pravinchandra Thakkar and Girdhar School principal Vinodbhai" to issue fake certificates. The latter is located in Padar Masar village.

Investigating officer and Panigate police station Sub-Inspector B F Zala said: "At Badoli in Vadodara district, the racket was run through a network of camp organisers, teachers, clerk and principals". The police on Tuesday visited Badoli to gather evidence in the case.

The police have found that school stamps and letterheads have been misused while handing out fake NCC certificates to five aspirants. Each aspirant reportedly paid about Rs 1.5 lakh for the certificate. Charel has been accused of accepting Rs 20,000 from each aspirant, while clerk Mahendra Patel reportedly took Rs 5,000 each.

More than 40,000 schools across the state are operating with an acute shortage of staff after the recruitment drive got stalled following revelation that fake certificates exceeded the genuine ones. A co-curricular activity certificate fetches five extra points to an applicant.

Earlier, the Education Department had registered a complaint against five Ahmedabad-based institutes of for issuing fake certificates. Now a case of fraud, cheating and conspiracy under Sections 420, 465, 467, 468, 471, 34 and 120(b) of the IPC has been registered against Charel and Patel. The police had recovered 34 fake NCC certificates, two sealed covers of applications, 17 blank letterheads of Girdhar Vidyalaya and receipts of applications sent from Charel and Patel.

For 10,200 seats in 40,000 schools across the state, the primary Education Department received over 1.5 lakh applications. The recruitment drive was supposed to get over before the beginning of the current academic session in last June. But the drive came to a standstill when the department found that many applicants had attached fake sports training or participation certificates with degrees and marksheets, as they fetch extra five points on merit.

Heading: The journey of a car: From a troublesome ‘S’ to a trouble-free ‘S’? - Indian Express
Content:
Authorities feign ignorance, say action would be taken against those who perpetrate this injustice

Little Kanku Waghela doesn't know much about her caste, but at her school in Changodar village of Sanand – the would be boom-town waiting for the Tatas and their state-of-the-art Nano car plant – she is never allowed to forget her place in the social order.

As the day starts, all students of her school are asked to clean up the compound. There's a catch, though. While students from the higher castes get on with tidying the fields and the classrooms, Kanku and her fellow students from the Valmiki-vaas begin their exclusive daily assignment, cleaning the school lavatory, which no child from the higher caste is asked to do.

Kanku's case is no exception. Across many such villages in rural Gujarat, Dalit children are the ones who have to clean the toilets in their schools. School authorities hasten to claim that all students are made to clean the school compound and there is no discrimination along caste-lines. But the reality cannot be wished away.

"Yes, we are asked to help clean the premises," says Dhvanika Vaghela a Class VI student from Kadi Kanyashala No 4. "But girls from other communities never pass by the toilets . It is only us (Dalits) who must do the lavatory cleaning. We clean the toilets using brooms and a piece of tin that we are given," she adds. Last month, she says, she fainted while cleaning the toilet.

Kiran Jagadia, who was in the same school, says: "It is always girls from our community, who will be called and asked to clean the school toilets."

The story remains unchanged for Pravin Parmar, a Class III student from Raska Prathmik Shala in Limdi taluka of Surendranagar District and his school senior, Meena Parmar, who studies in Class V. "Only children from our community are asked to clean the toilets, no one asks others to do this," she says. Incidentally, parents of most of these children are the village sanitary workers.

School Principal Navalsinh Menia, however, refuted what his students said. "All the students are asked to clean the school premises, there are no exceptions. But for cleaning toilets, we usually call the bhangis (Dalits) from outside," he says.

But high caste students insist they don't do the dirty work. In the Darbarvaas (Kshatriya caste neighbourhood) of Changodar, Karan Chavda, a Kshatriya boy of Class VII says the schools authorities ask children to clean the premises, but not the toilets. "Nahin, woh hum nahi karte, who log karte hain (No, we don't do it. They do it)," he says, pointing to the nearby ghetto where only students of the Dalit communities live.

Teachers, however, claim things are actually better now. "As a Dalit, I faced a lot of hardship in even finding a house for myself when I joined another school at Suriavadar village in Jamnagar, way back in 1978. I was forced to live in a house outside the village, when I shifted to teach at this school a few years ago. Things had been quite bad and Dalits had to face a lot of discrimination," says Mohanlal Makwana, Vice-Principal of the Navapur Prathmik Shala at Sanand Block. But things have improved now, he says, adding that he will not allow any casteist discrimination in his school.

State BJP's SC Morcha Convenor Atmaram Parmar told Newsline he will take the matter up with both the Education and the Social Welfare Departments. "This should not be happening. We will ensure stringent action against who ever is responsible, if this is actually happening," he said. "It is very strange. Give me the names of those villages and action will be taken immediately," added Anita Karval, state Secretary for Primary Education.

"It's linked to manual scavenging"

"The phenomenon has direct links with the issue of manual scavenging," says Dalit activist Manjula Pradeep. "Such practices stem from the idea of injecting the caste hierarchy early in the young minds," she said, adding that the situation remains as such across north and central Gujarat and Saurashtra. "This has got a lot to do with the state mindset, otherwise how can you explain the state ranking third in terms of manual scavengers with a population of about 65,000 when Dalits comprise of only 7 percent of the total state population," she added.

Heading: Govt’s unflinching support to Tatas for training manpower - Indian Express
Content:
Sanand will not be another Singur as ground realities differ, say government officials

Is Sanand going to be another Singur? If the developments after the signing of the agreement between the state government and Ratan Tata are any indication, Sanand will not become another Singur and the Nano project will be a reality.

According to senior government officials, there are a number of dissimilarities between Singur and Sanand, the first being that the land allotted in Singur was acquired from private persons, while the land transferred to Tata Motors at Sanand is government land.

Second, there is no direct opposition to the project from the locals residing in villages around the project site. Whatever opposition is there is coming from individuals and the farmers making claims over a part of the land being handed over for the project are demanding fair compensation and not coming in the way of the project.

In fact, none of the agitating farmers have so far opposed the project. In fact, farmers as well as other locals, irrespective of their political alliances, have welcomed the project with open arms.

Third, no political party has so far declared open opposition to the project on any ground, either at the local or the state level. Though certain quarters are accusing the Congress of provoking the farmers, the Congress has officially not made any statement against the project. In fact, senior party leaders including GPCC president Siddharth Patel and Porbandar MLA Arjun Modhwadia have categorically said that the party is not against the project.

They have welcomed the project but are demanding that the state government should let people know about the deal entered with the Tatas to ensure transparency. So, the demand of the main Opposition party, according to officials, is quite genuine. The fact that the government is not revealing the terms of the deal is a different matter altogether. The Congress has now filed an RTI application to seek details about the deal.

Finally, no public movement is building up against the project despite a bunch of farmers making claims over a portion of the land being given to the Tatas. The farmers are getting support neither from the locals nor any political group. In fact, Maharajah Jaisinh alias Tika Bapu, the scion of the erstwhile Sanand royal family has said, "We don't want the project to go away from Gujarat."

According to officials connected with the transfer of the land, most of the farmers are happy with the project as prices of the nearby land would shoot up manifold with the setting up of the Nano plant here. "The Gujarati society is entrepreneurial and rooted in capitalism and hence there is no chance of any public movement building up against the project," said an official on condition of anonymity.

Also, none of the farmers demanding compensation have so far been able to produce evidence to prove ownership of the land in question. District collector Hareet Shukla said there was no ambiguity about the ownership of the land. "There is only one entry in the land record papers which shows that it is in the possession of the state government.

Yet, we have asked the agitating farmers to come with proper evidence if they have any, in support of their claim over the land," he said.

Meanwhile, 40 farmers from Khoda, Amareli and Bhod villages submitted a five page memorandum demanding compensation for the land. They have said that the land belongs to their forefathers. Though they said they had land records in their favour, they did not produce the same to the media saying they would submit them to authorities at an appropriate time.

Accusing the district collector of threatening the farmers with dire consequences, Mukeshsinh Vaghela, who is leading the agitating farmers, declared to move the court if the government did not concede to their demand. He said their forefathers had not sold the land but given it on lease to the government and hence they should be paid compensation now that the lease period has expired. "We have submitted the documents to the district collector," he said.

But the land acquisition officials contend the claims of the farmers. Quoting from government records, they said that in 1911, Thakur Saheb (royal family) of Sanand was paid a sum of Rs 1,00,203 for acquiring 1062 acres and 20 gunthas from Kalan and Bhod villages, Rs 24,873 was paid for 323 acres and 35 gunthas of Bhod village and another sum of Rs 74,193 was paid for 865 acres and 12 gunthas to the talukdar of Khoda village. The total land acquired was 2,250 acres out of which 1,100 acres have now been given to the Tatas for the Nano project, they said. According to government records, several royal families and businessmen contributed for the compensation to be paid for the land. Donors included Ratan Tata's forefather Jamshedji Nusserwanji Tata who had contributed Rs 1,000, the Maharaja of Kolhapur, advocate Pestonji and N M Wadia.

Heading: Govt to open 500 new schools, all on its own - Indian Express
Content:
After successfully striking the Nano car project deal with Tata Motors, the Gujarat government has extended full co-operation to the auto giant in churning out trained manpower required at the Sanand project site near Ahmedabad. As part of the exercise, Chief Secretary D Rajagopalan called a meeting of senior officials of the Industries, Labour and Employment and Technical Education Departments on Tuesday. He reportedly directed them to focus on how to help Tata Motors create trained manpower for the Rs 2,000 crore project, besides ensuring that local youths get the maximum employment opportunities.

Later in the day, a technical team from Tata Motors held a prolonged discussion with senior officials of the State Technical Education Board at Gandhinagar.

They discussed the existing educational and training facilities available at engineering and polytechnic colleges located within a 50 km radius of the project site.

Manish Bhardwaj, Director, Technical Education Board, said: "The Tatas' technical team members informed us that they have decided to set up an Auto Academy and a driving school at the Nano car manufacturing complex."

He added: "But since it would take some time, they suggested that the government should permit the company to use the existing facilities in engineering and polytechnic colleges to conduct the training programmes."

Bhardwaj told Newsline that he assured the Tata team members that the Board will extend full co-operation in this regard.

He said: "The state government and Tata Motors will jointly carry out training programmes using the existing facilities at these institutes till the latter sets up its own Auto Academy at its project site."

A Board official said the Nano project will help generate ample employment opportunities not only for the automobile engineering students, but also for those studying in the mechanical and electrical branches in these colleges.

Since the project involves large scale skill development and training of manpower, the government will further strengthen the existing facilities in technical institutes across the state, he added.

Heading: Gujarat school students to master the mathematics of 64 squares - Indian Express
Content:
At a school function on Monday, state Education Minster Ramanlal Vora announced the government's decision to open 500 Secondary and Higher Secondary schools in the state. But the state government is planning to go about it all alone as, so far, not a single educational trust has shown any willingness to enter into a partnership with it.

Though the state Education Department has met the trustees of several educational bodies in this regard, it has failed to meet with any success. Nonetheless, the state government is planning to open two sets of schools – one for students of Class VIII to X and another for students of Class VIII to XII.

"The proposal and budget for these schools have already been passed in the 2008-2009 state budget and we have also begun identifying areas where there is an urgent need for schools. But as of now, I will not be able to give you any details," said Vora.

"Our first priority will be areas where there are no schools within a 10 kilometre radius. The next priority will be areas that have no higher secondary schools within a 15-kilometre radius," he said.

He added: "There is no doubt that we have to spend crores of rupees on a single school. But nonetheless, we are willing to start schools from as early as the next academic year. And, till the entire infrastructure is in place, we are willing to run schools from rented accommodation."

A senior official from the state Education Department said on condition of anonymity: "In order to open a school for students of Class VII to XII, we need at least nine teaching and three non-teaching staff members. On a larger scale, where 500 schools are involved, the state government will have to recruit 6,000 people. And recruitment on such a large scale is no joke."

As of now, there are 3,968 Higher Secondary and 7,868 Secondary schools in the state, which has around 22 lakh students studying in classes between Standard VIII and Standard XII.

Heading: When all Surtis say ‘kuchh meetha ho jaye’ - Indian Express
Content:
State education board plans to include chess in Class X syllabus

The Gujarat Secondary and Higher Secondary Education Board (GSHSEB) is seriously considering making chess compulsory for Class X students from the next year onwards. This comes after the board included the game in the Physical Education syllabus for Class VII and IX and provided an intensive training to 392 PE teachers from across Ahmedabad district.

Under the plan, students of Class VII, IX and X from 500 schools across the state, both granted and non-granted will be trained in the game. The Education Department plans to train at least 100 students from each school in a year's time. The PE teachers are being trained by participants in international tournaments to handle the compulsory course and the ones who missed the five-day training programme, are now being trained on Sundays.

R I Patel, the Secretary In-charge of GSHSEB said: "While chess has been included as a compulsory part of physical education for Class VIII and IX in schools across the Ahmedabad district as per a decision taken in August this year, the examination structure and the marks allotted is yet to be decided. It will also be included in the theory papers. The District Education Officers (DEOs) of all the districts have been sent a notice and they will have to forward it to the schools. We plan to include chess in the syllabus of Class X from next year onwards."

At present, the training is being imparted in schools in Ahmedabad district and the experimental project will soon spread to other districts.

P B Gahdvi, DEO of Ahmedabad said: "The training project for students in the Ahmedabad district started two months ago with a nominal expenditure. The project will be extended to cover primary students later. Chess is an intelligent game and will improve the mental faculties of the students."

Heading: Three yrs rigorous imprisonment and fine for electrocuting five lions - Indian Express
Content:
Chandi Padva is the time for lip-smacking 'ghari'

The diamond city that Surat is widely known as, is also famous for its 'ghari' — a sweet prepared to celebrate Chandi Padva festival.

Prepared only in this city, 'ghari' is eaten on the roadside, on the terrace of a building, on the beach, or anywhere under the open sky. 'Ghari' worth crores of rupees is made during this festival, which falls a week after Navratri. This year, it will be celebrated on Wednesday.

Not just the poor, the middle-class and even the rich prefer enjoying 'ghari' and other snacks from roadside vendors to having lavish dinners in big restaurants.

Adding loads of mawa, dry fruits and ghee, sweetshops start preparing 'ghari' a week before Chandi Padwa to meet customers' demand. Choryasi Dairy, that has nine outlets in the city, prepares 'ghari' in large number. Keeping in mind the increasing number of diabetics in the city, this year the dairy has prepared sugar-free as well as low sugar 'ghari'.

Its cost varies anywhere from Rs 250 to Rs 310 per kilogram, depending upon its quality.

Tuesday night is for shopkeepers to throw open the doors of their shops so that the people of Surat can make all their purchases.

Chairman of Choryasi Dairy Chandrasinh Bakrola said: "We are one of the oldest to prepare 'ghari' in the city. This year, we have made 7,000 kg of 'ghari'. For people suffering from diabetes, we have put less sugar into it. We start preparing the sweet ten days before Chandi Padva so that we can meet the demand of the festival that lasts just a day".

Mansukh Panwala, a Chowk Bazaar resident said: "This is neither a Hindu, nor a Muslim festival. Chandi Padva is an age-old tradition of the original Suratis. We invite our relatives, especially the sons-in-law, and sit together to eat 'ghari' with farshan, bhajiya and ice-cream at the terrace. We sing, dance and generally have fun in this festival. We will also send 'ghari' to our relatives in the US and the UK

Heading: South Gujarat sees an increase in rape of minors - Indian Express
Content:
Five lions were electrocuted on the outskirts of Prempara village on October 19, 2007

The Dhari town Judicial Magistrate (First Class) court has sentenced the prime accused in the electrocution case of five lions, to three years rigorous imprisonment and levied a fine of Rs 30,350.

Two co-accused, have been fined while the time spent by them in judicial custody before they obtained bail, have been considered as their punishment. The fourth accused has been released as no evidence was found against him.

According to the details of the case, five lions were electrocuted on the outskirts of Prempara village near Dhari town on October 19, 2007. The Incident occurred at a stone's throw away from the Gir East headquarters.

In a bid to save his standing crop, prime accused Durlabhji Vadodariya had passed electricity through the wired fencing surrounding his field. A group of five lions came in contact with the live wire fencing and were killed instantly. In a bid to destroy evidence, Vadodariya then buried the carcasses in his fields with the help of his son Purushottam Vadodariya and two others, namely a tractor owner and a tractor driver.

The Forest Department intensified its search when they found that five lions were missing and arrested four people for their involvement in the killing of the big cats.

The four were booked under various provisions of the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972. At that time, in charge, Deputy Conservator of Forest (Gir East) J S Solanki and his team had busted the case and submitted the same in the JMFC court and monitored it till the judgment was delivered on Monday.

Solanki, said: "Yet, they have not received a copy of the judgment. But further action will be decided upon receipt of the same."

According to primary details of the judgment, Purushottam and the tractor driver have been fined Rs 250 and 150 respectively, while the period they passed in jail during their judicial custody have been considered as the punishment period. The tractor driver has been set free. The JMFC court delivered the 150-page verdict within a year of the incident. The trial was on for 11 months.

Heading: Man arrested for raping infant - Indian Express
Content:
At a time, when the State Health Department is observing Beti Bachao Abhiyan from October 14 to 20, south Gujarat is witnessing a series of rapes of minor girls.

While an eight-month-old baby was raped at Tankaria village in Bharuch on Sunday, the decomposed body of a minor girl, allegedly raped, was found in the bathroom of a bungalow near Somnath temple a few days ago. The tribal girl is suspected to have been raped and then murdered in the empty bungalow of an NRI at Billimora taluka in Navsari district.In a third such incident, a five-year-old child of Vadod village, Pandesara, in Surat was raped by three youths on Sunday. The girl is still unconsciousness and undergoing treatment at New Civil Hospital.

Again, a chocolate shop owner at Salabatpura in Surat tried to rape a three-year-old on Monday. According to the police, a girl was playing outside her house in the slums at Navsari Bazaar when Pathan Hussain (45) lured her with chocolates. The accused took her inside the shop and tried to rape her. However, he released her when she began screaming. Her condition is stable now.

Heading: Fake currency racked busted - Indian Express
Content:
The Bharuch rural police on Tuesday arrested 20-year-old Suresh Rawal in connection with the rape of an eight-month-old infant in Dankaria village on October 12. While the infant underwent a surgery at a local civil hospital, the police on Tuesday denied reports that Rawal was mentally unstable.

"Rawal, a resident of Mehsana, had been given shelter by the infant's parents at their house in Dankaria after he fled from his home. Investigations have revealed that Rawal was upset, but not mentally unstable," said Bharuch DySP and investigating officer B S Ninama. He also added that the victim's family had promised a job to Rawal.

Tara Vasava, the mother of the infant had registered a complaint against Rawal after he went missing immediately after the incident.

The police said that since there appeared to be nothing wrong with Rawal, he would be subjected to regular legal procedures including being sent to judicial custody. He has been booked on charges of raping a minor.

Ninama also said that though the infant's condition was stable she would be kept in hospital for another week.

Heading: Mega city dream a nightmare for slum dwellers - Indian Express
Content:
Acting on a tip-off, the Junagadh police busted a fake currency racket and recovered counterfeit notes to the face value of Rs 1.72 lakh. The police raided the house of Aasif Amreliya (32), a resident of Kidi Faliya in Vanthali town on Monday night and recovered 136 fake notes of Rs 1000 denomination 56 notes of Rs 100 denomination from his possession.

Sub-Inspector U B Raval has now lodged a complaint against the accused under Section 498 (6) a, b and c of the Indian Penal Code.

The police said the accused had obtained the fake currency from one Raju alias Ashok Koli, a resident of Botad town in Bhavnagar district. Teams have now been rushed to Botad to nab the other accused, the police said.

Investigating Officer, Inspector J K Jala of the Local Crime Branch, said Aasif has been produced before the Judicial Magistrate (First Class) court of Vanthali town. He added that the "investigation is now focused on to nab the real culprit behind the racket and from where actually these fake currency notes were being produced.

Meanwhile, till reports last came in, the JMFC Court had passed order sanctioning a seven day police remand of the accused.

Heading: Cops fail to find missing businessman - Indian Express
Content:
Ahmedabad is on the verge of becoming a mega city. But, the 710 pockets of slums that house 41 per cent of the city's population, are on the mercy of rehabilitation in the wake of the constant efforts of the government to urbanise the population living there.

Evacuation of slums often leads to loss of occupation, rise in poverty, less access to community services and health problems. The Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation (AMC) gives slum-dwellers Rs 5,000 as compensation, a land area of 10 ft by 15 ft and arranges for a mode of transport for shifting, when evacuating slums. But in most of the evacuations, the slum-dwellers neither receive compensation, nor any basic amenities at their rehabilitation sites. Besides, most of the relocation is on the periphery of the city.

"We migrated to Ahmedabad 65 years ago. We were first given a notice to shift in 1997. Then we were asked to move to Santosh Nagar, but we opposed it for a year. Then we were shifted to the Danilimba area but no compensation or basic amenities were given," said Abdul Hamid of Ahmednagar Chawls in the Muslim Society in Danilimbda.

The ongoing infrastructure projects such as the storm water drainage, river front development, roads and flyovers have led to major evacuations in last few years in the city.

Piplag — a rehabilitation site near Ahmedabad —houses more than 1,200-1,500 hutments evacuated from Danilimba, Mahakali, Hajibavani Chali, Machhipir, K K Vishwanath ni Chali, Banasnagar and Khodiyarnagar. But it falls on the city's outskirts where slum-dwellers have no access to schools, hospitals and other emergency services. Besides, it has one bore well and a few public toilets for the 900 families living there.

Gajanan, a slum-dweller in Piplag said: "We have been promised a two- room kitchen flat under the JNNURM (Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission) scheme. We were shifted from Machchipir. I had a bangle-box manufacturing business, but after getting shifted in this area, which is far away from city, I am not getting work from the past four months."

The central and the state government are running several programmes like the Deendayal Awas Yojana, Valmiki Ambedkar Awas Yojana, Slum Networking Project of the AMC, Sabarmati Riverfront Development Programme, JNNURM and the EWS (Economically Weaker Sections) Housing of the AMC for the betterment of the slum-dwellers. But, the efficiency has posed a question.

Bina Jadav from Action Aid, an NGO working for the slums in Ahmedabad, said: "On the pretext of putting them under JNNURM, the slum-dwellers are evacuated for some or the other project. The SNP slums are also under threat in case they too, get evacuated. How does the AMC not know what their town planning schemes are, at least for the next five years. This constant reshuffling of slums has led to a major employment crisis in this section of the society."

Incidentally, the Slum Networking Project (SNP) of the AMC, which has been effective in 45 slums has also witnessed some evacuations due to infrastructure development. Anand Patel, Additional City Chief Engineer, AMC said: "Machihipir was required for the Kankaria Lake Front Development project; so the people were evacuated. The authority has the flexibility to shift slums, otherwise how will the city develop?"

On his part, Ahmedabad Mayor Kanaji Thakore said: "We are working towards their betterment. We are also asking the state government to give us more land for rehabilitation. Reshuffling of the people is an understandable problem but it must have happened in a major infrastructure project. We will be ready with 50, 000 EWS houses for the urban poor in the coming five years."

Heading: Folk Tales - Indian Express
Content:
Ten new designers focus solely on accessories at the Delhi Fashion Week

As Delhi witnesses the clash of the fashion weeks, the Delhi Fashion Week and the Wills India Fashion Week that start barely a day apart, fashion watchers can be sure of one thing; to see more holistic work since the fallout of the FDCI has opened the platform to many new young designers, eager to showcase their work, some of it startling in its originality.

For the first time since the inception of Indian fashion, accessories, crucial elements in fashion will not be neglected.

Ten accessory designers are showing for the first time at Delhi Fashion Week that began on Tuesday. Bags, scarves, shawls, wrap dresses, jewellery stalls, even blankets dot the venue, Emporio Mall in Vasant Kunj.

The look is defined by etching Kalidasa's poetry on silver, weaving sequins in hand weaves of Bengal and using Moroccan designs on a Cashmere shawl.

"We received an overwhelming demand from buyers who attended the fashion week last time. Most of the designers showing here are currently exporters," says Geetanjali Kashyap of Fashion Foundation of India.

Bangalore-based jewellery designer Deepti Sudhindra who has been in the circuit for nine years has found her niche by etching Henry David Thoreau's poetry on to silver, transforming a ubiquitous coconut shells into delicate beads, pendants and necklaces and contemporising the 200-year-old filigree craft of Karimnagar artists of Andhra Pradesh.

"I take a coconut shells and embellish it with silver," explains Sudhindra, 32, who will be showcasing eight different collections.

"My look is contemporary but the design element is essentially Indian," says Sudhindra who works on a commission basis.

Turning scarves, shawls and wraps into a heritage label is Kolkata based designer Bappaditya Biswas, 36, who founded Bai Lou in 2002. Closely working with weavers of Bengal, Biswas uses Jamdani and double cloth weaving techniques. "We don't believe in embellishments on top of the fabric. Everything is woven in and comes out as a finished product," says Biswas who works with 350 weavers.

His collection has stoles in malta silk with geometrical patterns, scarves in a blend of silk and wool in an oyster pink and aqua blue. "Wearing scarves is a recent trend in India and the hand weaving craft of Bengal has got a boost," says Biswas.

But it is Nepal based fashion designer Yasmine Rana who has given the jaded crafts industry in the neighbouring country a lift, by incorporating traditional Nepalese designs into luxurious loungewear.

Rana, of French origin, has been in the field for 25 years. Her collection—lounge wear, chic jackets in shining blue and jade green, cashmere shawls and blankets have a bourgeoisie elegance. "My designs are classy, multi-cultural and bold. I pick-up ideas from my travels, use local designs and natural material," she emphasises.
