The court's observation came while hearing a PIL filed by gay activists seeking to decriminalise gay sex among consenting adults.

Additional Solicitor General P P Malhotra, appearing for the Centre, cited an article which contained quotes from religious texts to justify the ban.

Not satisfied with the government contention, the Bench, also comprising Justice S Muralidhar, asked the government to show scientific proof that gay sex is harmful to society.

"This is just one-sided version of a religious body which cannot be relied upon. This is part of religious doctrine. Show us some scientific report which says that gay sex should be criminalised," a Division Bench headed by Chief Justice A P Shah said.

Earlier, the Centre had justified the criminal provision against homosexual acts and had said that it is required to curb the spread of HIV infection.

It had further said that homosexual behaviour is a reflection of a perverse mind and it could not be allowed in the society.

The petitioner, Naz Foundation, an NGO, had said that Section 377 which criminalises homosexual acts is unconstitutional and it should be amended to allow gay sex among consenting adults.

Heading: Apple cuts prices on notebooks - Indian Express
Content:
Motorola Inc, the world's third-biggest phone maker, unveiled a touch-sensitive phone to be sold by Verizon Wireless, as both companies look to compete with Apple Inc's iPhone.

Motorola, which has been losing ground in the cell phone market as it has failed to come up with a hit phone to replace its once-lauded Razr, said the Krave ZN4 would go on sale on Tuesday for $149.99 after rebates to customers who sign a two-year contract with Verizon Wireless.

The Krave has a see-through cover that flips open to uncover a touchscreen virtual keypad, but users can also access popular features such as mobile television and navigation by pressing their fingers on the cover without opening the phone.

For several years Motorola has sold a touchscreen phone called the Ming that has been popular in China, but it has focused on phones with physical keypads in the United States, where it is the market leader.

The popularity of iPhone -- a touchscreen phone sold exclusively through the No. 1 US mobile service AT&T Inc, has led rivals such as Motorola and Verizon Wireless, owned by Verizon Communications Inc and Vodafone Group Plc, to come up with touchscreen alternatives.

Motorola shares were up 7 cents or 1.3 per cent at $5.64 on New York Stock Exchange.

Heading: After Express story, Rs 78 lakh RTI ‘fee’ waived - Indian Express
Content:
Apple Inc on Tuesday cut the price on its entry-level notebook computer to $999 and introduced a line of aluminum-clad machines starting at $1,299 in moves catering to budget-minded buyers at a time when recession fears loom over the global economy.

But shares of Apple, which have risen about 20 per cent since the company last week invited reporters to a notebook event, fell 3 per cent in heavy trade on the Nasdaq to $106.99 after first falling as much as 5 per cent. Many analysts had expected the entry-level notebook price to fall to $899.

"Bad for the stock today, good for the stock over the next couple of months," said Piper Jaffray analyst Gene Munster, who said that the new machines looked good even if the new entry-level price was not as low as Wall Street had hoped.

Chief Executive Steve Jobs, looking thin but active, put the focus on the new line of MacBooks, although he took a few moments at the end to joke about his health.

His blood pressure was 110 over 70, he said. "And that's all we're going to be talking about Steve's health today," he added lightly, referring to concerns earlier this year that the cancer survivor's health was deteriorating.

He said he would not take questions on the economy or his health.

The new line of metal notebooks, starting at $1,299, are in what Gartner analyst Van Baker called the sweet spot of Apple's line. Previously a white plastic-body machine held the spot.

"The biggest news is the $1,299 MacBook," he said.

The $999 price will be for an updated model of the white-body notebooks. The new aluminum machines will use Nvidia Corp graphics and Intel Corp processors.

When asked if Apple would get into the market for small "netbook" notebook computers, Jobs said, "It's a nascent market," and that Apple would see how it went.

Apple also rolled out an $899 24-inch wide display for the new MacBooks.

Heading: Atif ‘faked’ degree - Indian Express
Content:
The State Information Commission has directed the official concerned to provide information free of cost, under the RTI Act provisions, to a Bhojpur resident, who was asked

to submit an "unreasonable" fee of Rs 78, 21,252 for seeking PDS-related information.

The District Supply Officer flouted RTI rules by giving the first information after the 30-day deadline. The applicant is entitled to get information free of cost after the deadline.

The Indian Express had published an article on September 23 about Gupteshwar Singh, a social activist, being charged the said amount by Bhojpur District Supply Officer Jawahar Prasad after Singh sought information on distribution of ration and kerosene oil from 2000 to 2008 at

Udvantnagar, Agiyaw, Tarai, Garhani, Sandesh and Sahar. Prasad reportedly "worked out the unreasonable fee" to discourage Singh.

Assistant Director of State Information Commission, Sugandh Chatterjee, directed Public Information Officer, Food and Consumer Protection, Patna, to give Singh the desired information by December 8, 2008.

In a letter, dated September 30, 2008, Chatterjee wrote: "As no information was made available to the applicant within the 30-day deadline, he must be given the information free of cost." The Commission also issued a showcause notice to Prasad regarding a Rs 250 per day fine for the delay.

Singh said: "My case will set a precedent. No official will now try to discourage an applicant." The Commission will hear the matter on January 12, 2009.

Heading: President Pune visit: couple caught with fake emblem on car - Indian Express
Content:
Delhi Police's Special Cell unit claims to have found that alleged Indian Mujahideen (IM) activist Mohammed Atif had taken admission in Jamia Millia Islamia's MA in Human Rights course on the basis of a fake Allahabad University BA degree. Atif (24) was the alleged mastermind of the September 13 serial blasts in the national capital and was gunned down in a shootout last month. Four alleged accomplices of Atif have reportedly revealed this. "On Tuesday, Allahabad University confirmed to us that the certificate was fake," claimed Joint Commissioner, Special Cell, Karnal Singh. However, when contacted, Allahabad University officials said they needed time to check the documents.

Soni on travel advisories

NEW DELHI: Keen to ensure that the spate of terrorist attacks in recent months did not affect growth of tourism in the country, Tourism Minister Ambika Soni has urged the international community not to issue negative travel advisories. "The challenge posed by terrorism can only be surmounted through international cooperation and collective action by the global community," Soni said at a meeting of the UN World Tourism Organisation in Madrid.

Heading: No Pak agency involved in Kabul embassy blast: Durrani - Indian Express
Content:
The Pune police on Tuesday claimed that they have nabbed two persons who were found driving a car with fake national emblem and a Government of India sticker, barely six km from Raj Bhawan on October 11 when President Pratibha Patil was here. After being caught at Balewadi phata, the duo had managed to escape. On Tuesday evening, the police released a press statement saying that they had caught the duo.

On October 11, traffic police inspector Surendranath Deshmukh had seized the car some six km from Raj Bhavan, where the President was staying that day. Incidentally, on Sunday the police had also received a terror mail threatening an attack against the President.

Police are now investigating the duo's motive behind using such a car, though initial questioning revealed that the motive was only to con people by posing as government officials and not to break into the President's convoy.

Joint Commissioner of Police Rajendra Sonawane said, "Inspector Deshmukh spotted the car with a forged national emblem. On being questioned, the driver of the car identified himself as Pinto Sengupta (40) and his friend as Susan (35). Deshmukh asked two police constables (new recruits), who were on bandobast duty, to take the car and the duo to the police commissionerate. The constable went along with them to the Poona Gate police chowki. While on their way to the commissionerate, Pinto said that they wanted to visit a relative in Jehangir Hospital and gave the constables a slip after getting down from the vehicle."

Soon, the Bomb Detection and Disposal Squad was pressed into action, but nothing was found inside the car. The terror mail that surfaced the next day put the onus on the police to trace the duo. Now, the police are probing whether the car was trying to enter the President's convoy or not.

"When questioned by the constables at Poona Gate chowki, Pinto had given three Pune addresses — Senapati Bapat Road, Baner Road and Kalewadi — and a New Delhi address, B-7 Safdarjung Enclave," said Sonawane. Police are verifying all the addresses.

Heading: 9 hurt as bomb placed on bicycle explodes in Kanpur - Indian Express
Content:
Keen to placate India's concerns, Pakistan's National Security Advisor Mahmud Ali Durrani has told the Indian leadership that "no Pakistani agency" was involved in the bombing of the Indian Embassy in Kabul. New Delhi had, on the basis of assessment US and NATO intelligence agencies, had alleged ISI's involvement in the embassy bombing.

It is learnt that Durrani also said that all security agencies, including the ISI, were "firmly under the control of Pakistan's political leadership". This, according to the Indian diplomatic establishment, is a first such claim by a top official of the civilian Government in the last eight months of being in power.

Sources said that Durrani - who met Prime Minister Manmohan Singh and External Affairs Minister Pranab Mukherjee on Tuesday and held talks with NSA M K Narayanan on Monday - conveyed this as the Indian leadership wanted to know of the progress on the "internal probe" into the allegations of ISI's involvement in the bombing.

The internal probe had been assured by Pakistan Prime Minister Yousaf Raza Gilani in August this year, on the sidelines of the SAARC summit, when Singh had taken up the matter regarding the Indian Embassy bombing that claimed the lives of an IFS officer and a senior Army official posted in Kabul, along with two ITBP security personnel.

Sources said Durrani, who has been an armyman and a diplomat having served as Pakistan's ambassador to the US between July 2006 to May 2008, also "assured" the Government of India that Pakistan was committed to upholding the ceasefire and that there is a "need to strengthen the mechanism, in which the concerns of both sides fairly".

This assurance came as there were repeated allegations by the Government of India on the ceasefire violations — which the Indian side accuses Pakistan of giving a cover to the infiltrating militants and allow them to crossover. The Indian Army has reported over 50 ceasefire violations this year.

While the Indian Embassy bombing and ceasefire violations dominated the discussions between Durrani and the Indian top brass, the Pakistani NSA raised the issue of reduced flow in the Chenab river.

Durrani, sources said, expressed concern over the reduced flow of water in the Chenab river and was assured that India would abide by the provisions of Indus Water Treaty.

The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), however, on Tuesday issued an official statement where it said, "The two National Security Advisors reviewed the status of bilateral relations against the backdrop of recent summit level meetings between the leadership of both countries."

"The discussions, which were held in very cordial atmosphere, covered all issues of mutual concern and interest, including the regional situation. The discussions were most productive," the MEA statement said.

The two NSAs "affirmed the utility of a dialogue of this nature and regarded their discussions as providing an important channel of communication between the highest level in the two governments", the MEA said.

Besides meeting Foreign Secretary Shiv Shanker Menon, Durrani also interacted with the National Security Council Secretariat and members of the National Security Advisory Board.

During his 40-minute meeting with BJP President Rajnath Singh, the issue of terror figured prominently. "India and Pakistan both have witnessed a series of blasts in recent days in which hundreds of innocent people lost their lives," said Rajnath, to which Durrani replied that the Government of Pakistan was "trying hard" to control terrorism and that "Pakistan, too, had been a victim of terror".

Rajnath also said that incidents of "rampant violation of ceasefire" by Pakistani Army at the LoC were creating an "atmosphere of distrust".

Heading: Nano: Gujarat farmers threaten to move court - Indian Express
Content:
Nine persons were injured when a bomb placed on a bicycle exploded in the Purani Sharab Gaddi area under the Colonelganj police station on Tuesday evening. The police were quick to claim that it was not a case of terror bombing.

Of the injured, Ravi (4), his sister Mansi (8), Rani Devi (50), Krishna Gupta alias Punnu (30), Twinkle (6), Jeevan Lal (65) Shanta Tulsa (65) were admitted in Ursula Horsman Memorial Hospital, while Nupur (10) and Katori Devi (60) were discharged after first aid.

On November 23 last year, bombs placed on bicycles had exploded in Lucknow, Faizabad and Varanasi courts, causing 14 deaths. The police have blamed the bombings on HuJI and Indian Mujahideen.

Kanpur SSP Hari Ram Sharma said Tuesday's blast appeared "accidental". It was caused by a crude bomb while the blasts in Lucknow, Faizabad and Varanasi were different in nature, he said.

"It seems somebody was carrying a crude bomb on a cycle which exploded in the area," Sharma said.

The blast took place outside a general store around 6:30 pm. Owner of the store Pintoo said, "It is a densely populated area, so no one even cared to notice that a cycle was stationed near the shop. No one knows who left the cycle there."

The explosion shattered glasspanes of nearby houses and shops and enveloped the area in smoke. The injured were all residents of the area, which has shops on the ground floor and residences on upper floors.

The anti-sabotage team and bomb disposal squad searched the spot for clues.

IG of Kanpur Zone S N Singh said he would not like to say anything about the type of explosives until he got a report from experts.

"No other explosive has been found from the area, and the motive behind the blast is still unclear," he said.

Union Minister of State for Home Shri Prakash Jaiswal visited the hospital and the site of the blast.

Chief Medical Officer Subodh Tiwari said the victims had pallet injuries. "None of them is in a serious condition, all of them are likely to recover within a week," he said.

This is the second explosion in the city in two months. On August 24, an explosion in a house in the Rajeev Nagar area killed two Bajrang Dal members — Bhupinder Singh and Rajeev Mishra. Several hand grenades, timers, batteries and explosives were found in the house. The case still remains unsolved.

Heading: Amar in tow, Mamata says she is not against industry - Indian Express
Content:
A group of farmers demanding compensation for the land allotted to Tatas for the Nano project on Tuesday threatened to move court. "We met Ahmedabad District Collector Harit Shukla and told him that now when the land has been given to Tata they should compensate us for it," farmer leader Mukesh Vaghela said.

Claiming that the Collector told them that the Government would not compensate them as they did not have any proof, Vaghela said they did not expect such an answer from the District Collector and now they had no option but to go to court.

Heading: Dasmunsi still in hospital, ‘serious but stable’ - Indian Express
Content:
Being targeted for forcing Tatas to pull out of West Bengal and acting against the state's industrialisation drive, Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee on Tuesday sought to clarify her position and termed the criticisms as a "propaganda" against her.

"We are not against industry or industrialisation. It is a bad propaganda against us. But, if the state Government thinks itself so powerful, nothing can be done, we are not bonded labour. This false propaganda is being carried out against the agitation in Singur. I want to tell that Bengal is a case of state-sponsored terrorism. The administration and police have been politicised in the past 32 years of the Left rule," Banerjee said in the Capital.

She, along with SP general secretary Amar Singh, on Tuesday met Prime Minister Manmohan Singh and President Pratibha Patil here to apprise them about the situation in Singur.

Criticising the Tata group, Banerjee said one-sided and concocted stories of an individual business house was being spread. "Tatas have money to publicise against us and there seems to be some politics behind their exit from the state," the Trinamool chief said.

Banerjee and Amar Singh told reporters that they had "requested the President and Prime Minister to take action under Article 355 in West Bengal over the failure of the state Government to honour the agreement which was brokered by the Governor".

Mamata demanded that the West Bengal Government should honour the agreement reached with Singur agitators by returning the land back to farmers who were unwilling to part with their lands.

"What is puzzling is that while the Left parties demanded all the finer details about the nuclear deal to be put in public for their own sake, they (in West Bengal) do not even want to disclose the details of agreement between the state Government and the Tatas," said Banerjee.

Taking on Ratan Tata, Amar Singh said, "Ratan Tata spoke about Good M (Gujarat Chief Minister Narendra Modi) and Bad M (Mamata Banerjee). On what basis did he make this comment. Mamata Banerjee only wanted the surplus land of farmers to be given back to them, while we all know how 'good' Modi is. We want to know whether Tata wants to remain an industrialist or a politician."

Heading: Priest who witnessed nun rape refuses to help Orissa Police, says no faith in it - Indian Express
Content:
Information and Broadcasting Minister Priya Ranjan Dasmunsi's condition continued to be critical a day after he was admitted to the All India Institute of Medical Sciences after a cardiac arrest. Dasmunsi was admitted with complete left ventricular failure of the heart on Monday.

As per the latest medical bulletin, Dasmunsi's condition is 'serious but stable'. "The patient no longer requires cardiac support system. His vital parameters, including blood pressure and heart rate, are well maintained and his blood sugar is under control," said Dr D K Sharma, Medical Superintendent of AIIMS. Dasmunsi is, however, on respiratory support. "His condition is being closely monitored by a multi-disciplinary team of doctors," added a doctor treating him.

President Pratibha Patil visited Dasmunsi and spoke to his family. Dasmunsi suffered a heart attack late night on October 12 and was admitted to the hospital. He was put on life support system at the cardiac intensive care unit .

Heading: Fresh violence in Kandhamal, CRPF man hacked to death - Indian Express
Content:
The lone eyewitness, a Christian priest, in the alleged rape of a nun in Orissa's Kandhamal district has refused to cooperate in the investigation, saying he did not have faith in it.

The priest, Father Chellan, who was accompanying the 29-year-old nun when she was allegedly raped at K Nuagaon during the Orissa bandh on August 25, told police officials who met him at Chelanthera in Kerala that he he did not have faith in them, DSP CB Jayshree Kundu said on Tuesday, after returning from Kerala along with the three arrested there in connection with the case on October 11.

The priest has also lodged a separate complaint on the assault by a mob. Earlier, the state government had sought the nun's cooperation in the investigations.

Heading: Posco protests take a knock - Indian Express
Content:
Kandhamal's fragile peace was shattered once again after a 46-year-old sweeper working with the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) was hacked to death on Monday night by tribals while he was on his way to the CRPF camp.

Baksish Singh of D company of 175 Battalion had gone to Sisapanga village, under Raikia police station, along with a local driver on Monday evening to buy chicken for the jawans. They were stopped at Gundhani village by some tribal women. Mistaking Singh to be a jawan, they beat him up as well as the driver before the men of the village arrived at the spot. "The driver, a local person, managed to flee while Singh was herded to a nearby hillock and hacked to death," said R N Barik, Inspector at Raikia police station.

The driver, who escaped the mob fury informed the CRPF and police officials who found the battered body of Singh in the forest, about 12 km away from the place where he was stopped. His body was sent for post-mortem early Tuesday morning and then sent to his native place in Dibrugarh district of Assam.

CRPF Inspector General of Police M Nageswar Rao said, "Singh was a safai worker attached to a CRPF company. Sweepers are not given arms." There are 42 companies of the CRPF posted in Kandhamal district.

Rao said the killing could be a retribution by tribals who are peeved over large-scale attacks on villagers in the last fortnight. So far, 600 people have been arrested in Kandhamal for their alleged involvement in riot, murder, rape and arsoning.

Singh is the second policemen to die in the hands of mob in Kandhamal. In September, constable-recruit of Special Security Battalion of Orissa Police, Bibhudhendra Biswal fell to the bullets of a mob that stormed the Gochhapada police station in Kandhamal.

Meanwhile, Kandhamal District Kui Samaj Coordination Committee secretary Lambodar Kanhar threatened that the tribals in the district would gherao police stations in riot-hit areas and get themselves arrested if "indiscriminate midnight" arrests by the police did not stop. Kanhar, who held a meeting of his fellow tribals at Phulbani on Tuesday afternoon, demanded sending back Madhusudan Padhi, newly-appointed special administrator of the district for his anti-tribal activities in the past. "During his collectorship in 1997-98, he favoured non-tribals from other districts to get jobs in Kandhamal. He can't be trusted," Kanhar told The Indian Express.

Chief Minister Naveen Patnaik, who returned from Delhi on Tuesday said action will be taken as per law against CRPF jawans who misbehave with tribal women in riot-torn Kandhamal. Kanhar has demanded withdrawal of paramilitary force from rural pockets of Kandhamal, alleging that the jawans had misbehaved with the women there.

Naveen told NDTV that he believed the Bajrang Dal to be a fundamentalist group. "Let the Centre take a decision on banning Bajrang Dal, then we will react," he said.

Union Minister Ram Vilas Paswan also told reporters in Bhubaneswar that Bajrang Dal should be banned for its anti-national activities.

Officials said that the relief camps would be shifted from block headquarters to panchayat to facilitate the return of people to their homes. Earlier, Christian leaders like Swarupananda Patra had alleged that villagers were migrating to other states, as they were scared of returning to their homes.

Heading: A century-old journey through the  Blue Mountains - Indian Express
Content:
It is the piece of news that Orissa Chief Minister Naveen Patnaik may have wanted to hear for quite a long time. Having been rebuffed for over three years by the farmers of Jagatsinghpur, where South Korean steelmaker Posco proposed to build the largest steel mill in the country, Naveen and his officials had almost given up on the Rs 52,000-crore project. That is until a police team stopped Abhay Sahu near Jagatsinghpur on Sunday evening and took him into custody. The portly 40-something Sahu, president of the Posco Pratirodh Sangram Samiti — an anti-Posco front — and the person who single-handedly united villagers of three gram panchayats to rail against the project, was returning to his native village in Jagatsinghpur district after a diabetes check-up when he was whisked away to prison on charges of rioting, arson and abduction.

Sahu had frustrated the attempts made by Posco and the Government to agree to the lucrative compensation package for the 12 million-tonne steel plant. Like the Nano project, the firestorm of protests against Posco since 2005 had almost derailed the project, as the company could acquire only 193 acres out of required 4,004 acres.

Clashes at the site over the last couple of years had left hundreds of people injured. In May and October last year, some officials of the company were held hostage for hours by the protestors. With tension simmering around the project site, the area resembled a police cantonment.

At an international seminar on steel-making this year, Posco India managing director Soung Sik Cho said people needed to open their eyes to the possibilities the steel plant could offer them.

For impoverished Orissa, the importance of the deal cannot be overstated. Orissa, which has 25 per cent of the country's iron ore and over 90 per cent of chrome ore, has Rs 5 lakh crore in investments waiting at its doorstep.

The region has been infamous for its gut-wrenching poverty, natural calamities and violence over ethnic and communal issues. A project as ambitious as Posco's plant would not only funnel millions of dollars for developmental work but also spawn jobs for the unemployed.

Even though the Centre and the state Government worked overtime to give regulatory approvals, their measures failed to address the concerns of hundreds farmers who are worried that the land for the steel plant would deprive them of fertile agricultural ground.

In 2006, the state Government announced a rehabilitation package for 450 farmers and fishermen, but the locals were not convinced. "First, they'll make us homeless and then give us some money. If the company wants to build its plant let it do so over our bodies," said a villager.

However, the project was stalled due to reasons other than the popular resistance as well. The company could not acquire the land it needed, as it did not have the clearance to use over 3,000 acres of forestland in the project area.

Though the Forest Advisory Committee (FAC) of the Union Ministry of Environment and Forests had cleared Posco's proposal for diversion of forestland for the steel plant, the Supreme Court last year said all clearance by the FAC would be reviewed by the Centrally Empowered Committee of the Court. The SC cleared the use of forestland in August this year.

Another roadblock for the Posco project has been cleared after the Orissa Government completed the hearing on granting a prospecting license (PL) for the Khandadhar iron ore reserve in Sundargarh district for which Posco is one of the contenders. Though the state Government had recommended Posco for the PL over Khandadhar in December 2007, public sector company Kudremukh Iron Ore Company Ltd dragged the matter to the High Court.

Posco executives and senior government officials believe that the roadblocks to the project have been mostly cleared with the arrest of Sahu.

The story so far

June 22, 2005: Posco signs MoU with Orissa Government for setting up a 12 million-tonne steel project in Jagatsinghpur district.

September, 2005: Posco applies for prospecting licence for mining.

November, 2005: Protests start in at the project site. State Government serves notices for land acquisition, but officials can't enter three gram panchayats — Dhinkia, Nuagaon and Gadakujanga — as villagers erect barricades.

October, 2006: Medha Patkar leads a dharna of anti-Posco protesters outside the residence of Chief Minister Naveen Patnaik.

April, 2007: Prime Minister Manmohan Singh asks Naveen to expedite land acquisition.

May, 2007: Three Posco executives held hostage by villagers.

October, 2007: Four Posco executives, including three South Koreans, abducted by villagers. They are later released.

November, 2007: Violent clash between pro-Posco and anti-Posco villagers in Jagastsinghpur leave at least 20 injured.

June, 2008: Centre slams Orissa over delay in Posco project.

August, 2008: Supreme Court clears Posco using over 3,000 acres of forestland for its steel plant.

Posco India fact file

Location: Erasama block in

Jagatsinghpur district

Land required: 4,004 acres

Plant capacity: 12 million tonnes per annum The 12 MTPA integrated steelworks will be completed in three phases of 4 MTPA each. In Phase I, hot rolled coil (2.5MT) and slab (1.5 MT) will be produced.

Iron Ore required: 20 million tonnes per annum for annual steel production of 12 million tonnes over 30 years

Jobs: An estimated 48,000 direct and indirect jobs in the region.

Deadlines: Phase I was expected to conclude in 2011-12; Phase II to was to be completed 3 years after Phase I; and Phase III will be commissioned within 3 years of Phase II's completion.

Estimated Investment for Phase I: Rs 16,650 crore

Heading: Labouring Land-less - Indian Express
Content:
An engineering marvel from the early 20th century, the Coonoor-Ooty section of the Nilgiri Mountain Railway (NMR) will celebrate its centenary on Wednesday. Fired with three to four tonnes of coal per trip, these metre-gauge steam engines made it to the prestigious UNESCO World Heritage list in 2005, and continue to chug along on a technology that has long been obsolete in its parent country, Switzerland.

First, the history: even after discovering the beauty of the Nilgiris, the British were practically stuck at the foothills, Mettupalayam, as the 46-km journey from there to the Ooty plateau involved a climb of 169 feet to 7,228 feet — obviously not an easy task. The only way out was a mountain railway system built with British entrepreneurship and Swiss technology. While climbing steeply through the eastern side of the Western Ghats, the train had to negotiate 208 curves, pass through 16 tunnels, 250 bridges — a nightmare for engineers even now.

To surpass the challenge posed by the steep gradient, the Madras Railway Company accepted the 'Riggi Pattern' put forth by Swiss inventor M Riggenbach. They used a rack-and pinion-system, in which an alternate biting system powers the climb or slows the descent and reduces the chances of slipping. .

Though the first section between Mettupalayam and Coonoor was completed on June 15, 1899, the Ooty plateau, the summer retreat of the English, was still 18 km away. After 60 months of work and an expenditure of Rs 24.4 lakh, the railway line was finally opened on October 15, 1908, providing easy connectivity between the foothills and plateau.

"Several tourists from European countries like Germany and Switzerland come here to take pictures and learn more about the functioning of these engines. It's ironic that even though these are Swiss-made X-class locomotives, they have to come here to see one in operation," said Narayanan, a coal engine mechanic at the Coonoor Loco Shed, which opened in 1899, making it the oldest in the railway zone.

Nearly 90 members of the Loco Shed's staff are busy cleaning and polishing four of the best engines selected to take part in the 'black beauty' contest for steam engines on October 18, organised by Southern Railway to celebrate the centenary of NMR. And with the railway system being one of the showpieces of the Indian Railways, the revelry is will last well into the next month. "There will be a heritage exhibition on wheels till November 31, apart from other cultural activities to observe the occasion," said R Velu, Minister of State, Railways, kick-starting the 45-day celebrations.

But the trains along this section are much more than mere relics of the past, even in this age of instant connectivity. While locals have taken to commuting by bus to save time, this does not reduce the rush on the trains, filled by tourists from all parts of the world who are drawn by the old-world charm of the coaches as much as by the beauty of the scenery. In fact, there has been a 44 per cent increase in the number of passengers in the last five years, said railway officials. And unlike some other 'heritage' joyrides, this journey is surprisingly easy on the pocket — from Ooty to Conoor, an ordinary ticket costs only Rs 4, with similar rates in all the sections.

Once the 'toy trains' leave behind the chaos of Ooty town, the journey covers woods, lush tea plantations, deep valleys and misty mountains. Seen through the wooden frame of the coach, the slow journey offers one of the best train tours in the country and certainly the best views of the Nilgiri mountains — all at a price that's lower than the cost of a cup of standard south Indian coffee.

Heading: A Hungry State - Indian Express
Content:
The UP Government's decision to cancel the land allotted for the railway coach factory is not the first of its kind that UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi has had to face in her attempts to develop her constituency of Rae Bareli and that of her son's - Amethi — into the industrial and educational hub of northern India. Several projects of national importance that Sonia approved for both the constituencies have been stalled for more than a year-and-a-half because the UP Government has not allotted the necessary land. These projects included National Institute of Pharmaceuticals and Education Research (NIPER), the Hindustan Papers Mills, the Central Reserve Police Force's (CRPF's) Group Centre and the National Automobile Training, Research and Infrastructure Project.

• To begin with the case of the proposed Rae Bareli branch of the NIPER project that is considered to be a centre for advanced studies and research in pharmaceuticals. Sources said the Union Ministry of Chemical and Fertiliser had cleared five NIPER projects to be set up in five states — Ahmedabad (Gujarat), Hyderabad (Andhra Pradesh), Kolkata (West Bengal) and Hajipur (Bihar), Guwahati (Assam) and Rae Bareli (UP) in August 2007. "While other states gave us the land to make the project functional in their proposed cities, we are waiting for a permanent site for the project in Rae Bareli," a source added. According to him, the Chemical and Fertilizer Ministry has written at least seven letters to the UP Government requesting the allotment of the land. The project has the potential to prompt major pharmaceutical companies to set up their plants near NIPRA. "We need at least 100 acres of land for the project, which will cost about Rs 300 crore to implement," said a source.

In absence of land, the ministry has managed to temporarily begin the NIPER project in a block of the Indian Telephone Industry Limited in Rae Bareli city. "We can't stop the beginning of the project in our wait for the land allotment," confirmed G S Sandhu, joint secretary in the Chemical and Fertiliser Ministry. According to him, the land for the project is supposed to be given by the state Government free of cost. "We will construct the building for the institute, besides adding other infrastructure," he added.

On being contacted, Rajesh Moza, the deputy registrar of NIPER, Mohali, said that the counselling of the 20 selected candidates for the Rae Bareli-based NIPER will take place tomorrow. "Every June, a joint entrance test is held for the selection of candidates across the country. Then in July, counseling of the selected takes place. The decision for starting the Rae Bareli-based NIPRA came late," he said, adding that if the project becomes fully operational, it would be ale to accommodate about 400 students.

• The story is no different for setting up the CRPF Group Centre in Amethi. This project was cleared by the Ministry of Home Affairs in February 2007 and the CRPF needs about 200 acres of land. When contacted, N P Singh, the IG of CRPF's central sector said the force has selected a site at Trishundi in Amethi and has requested the state to allot the same. The land is owned by the Uttar Pradesh State Industrial Development Corporation (UPSIDC), which IG Singh says, is "in correspondence with the Government".

Little wonder then that Amethi's newly created Group Centre is currently on the premises of CRPF's Group Centre, Bijnore (Lucknow). "We thought it better to develop the infrastructure for the Amethi's Group Centre without waiting for land," said the IG.

This CRPF project is important as it gives scope for the regular appointment of local youths. "Since 1990, the CRPF recruits about 1,500 youths from UP. I hope the youths of Amethi would also get full scope for their appointment," a source in the CRPF said. "The CRPF procures all the requirements of the jawans from the areas that house the Group Centre," the source explained. "Besides, all the families of the jawans reside in the Group Centre. This develops the areas concerned as a good market, he added.

• Another important project that could not take off in Rae Bareli because of not being allotted land is the National Automobile Training, Research and Infrastructure Project. At an estimated cost of Rs 125 crore, the project can generate employment for more than 1,000 persons directly or indirectly. According to K L Sharma, the representative of Sonia Gandhi's constituency, this project has been pending for more than two years.

• The project of Hindustan Paper Mills suffers the same fate. "This project needs about 500 acres of land. UPSIDC has a suitable site at Utelawa in Amethi's Jagdishpur area. The same was preferred for the project," the source disclosed. Initially, the UP Government was ready, he added.

Heading: Armed Forces: panel on pay holds 1st meet - Indian Express
Content:
In the first of attempts to map state-wise hunger index of the country on the lines of the Global Hunger Index, US-based International Food Policy Research Institute released an India State Hunger Index (ISHI) report on Tuesday, saying, "India is home to the world's largest food-insecure population, with more than 200 million hungry people".

Lack of proper nutrition among the children and poor calorie count are behind India's dismal performance, says the report, released by G K Chadha, member of the Prime Minister's Economic Advisory Council.

• India, which ranked 66th in the Global Hunger Index of 88 countries, does not have a single state in the 'low hunger' or 'moderate hunger' categories.

• The five worst performing states in hunger level terms are Madhya Pradesh, Jharkhand, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, and Gujarat. The supposedly prosperous Gujarat ranks below the poor state of Orissa

• Madhya Pradesh, which falls in the "extremely alarming" category, would rank between Ethiopia and Chad in the global list

• Twelve states, including Andhra Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Karnataka, Gujarat and West Bengal, are in the 'alarming' category.

• Four states — Punjab, Kerala, Haryana and Assam — are in the 'serious' category. Punjab, the best-performing state in the country in terms of hunger, would rank below countries like Gabon, Honduras and Vietnam, placed low in the global index.

Though the index is titled India State Hunger Index - 2008, it has used data from the NFHS survey of 2005-06 and the NSSO survey of 2004-05. The researchers hoped that the performance would improve after the next round of NFHS and NSSO data is compiled.

The India State Hunger Index was compiled by IFPRI along with Germany-based Wethungerlife and the California University. They analysed hunger levels in 17 major states, which represent more than 95 per cent of the population.

Heading: Kosi course to be restored by Dec 15 - Indian Express
Content:
A three-member committee set up to look into alleged "anomalies" in the new pay scales for Armed Forces held its first meeting on Tuesday. External Affairs Minister Pranab Mukherjee, who heads the committee, had said on Monday following a meeting with the Prime Minister that the issue would be settled soon.

Mukherjee held a meeting with Finance Minister P Chidambaram and Defence Minister A K Antony, the committee's other members, during which they are understood to have explored ways to address the issue to the satisfaction of the forces. The Service chiefs have expressed their dissatisfaction over the Sixth Pay Commission recommendations, alleging that they compromised their status and honour.

Heading: Assembly polls schedule - Indian Express
Content:
Kosi's course will be restored by December 15 and the breach would be plugged by March 31, 2009.

Union Water Resources secretary U N Panjiyar held a meeting with state Water Resources Secretary Ajay Nayak, Kosi Breach Closure Advisory Technical Committee chairman N Sanyal and Ganga Flood Control Commission chairman R C Jha here on Tuesday to finalise modalities on plugging the breach.

The Central team would conduct an aerial survey of Kushaha breach on Wednesday.

Speaking to The Indian

Express, Water Resources Minister Bijendra Yadav said tenders for the breach closure have been invited and bidding will take place after October 21.

"We expect the work to start from first week of November. The river course will be restored by December 15, and initial plugging will stop the flow from Kushaha breach," he added.

Yadav said that Kosi Committee, headed by Sanyal, will monitor technical aspects of the plugging. "The state Government, as the executing agency, will bear the cost and seek advance and reimbursement from the Centre periodically," he added.

The Centre has sanctioned Rs 40 crore for the project and Bihar Cabinet has sanctioned Rs 197 crore.

Heading: ‘I begged, told them I’m a soldier... I was told I’m Muslim, nothing else’ - Indian Express
Content:
With terrorism likely to set the tone for the coming Lok Sabha elections, the Shahi Imam of Delhi Jama Masjid Syed Ahmed Bukhari, with the visible support of the Samajwadi Party, began efforts to forge a platform of Muslim clerics and leaders.

Although leaders of the Jamaat-e-Islami and Jamiat Ulama-i-Hind and several Islamic clerics were present at a conference organised by Bukhari on Jama Masjid premises, it was clearly a Samajwadi Party show with party heavyweight Abu Azim Azmi and its Rajya Sabha MP Shafiqur Rahman Barg in attendance.

Setting the tone, the Shahi Imam slammed BSP chief Mayawati for organising a Muslim seminar in Lucknow on Monday, a day ahead of his conference, and alleged that the Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister had only offered promises and not done much for the community. He was also scathing on the Congress.

The presence of SP leaders at the conference is significant as the party is making all-out efforts not to lose its sizeable Muslim votebank, especially since it reversed its opposition to the Indo-US nuclear deal. The attempt seems to be to retain its pro-Muslim image even while extending support to the Congress-led Government at the Centre.

The conference resolved to demand a judicial inquiry into the Jamia Nagar encounter, a demand that has already been made by SP general secretary Amar Singh, setting up of a judicial commission to look into cases registered against Muslim youths in connection with the terror attacks and enactment of a law to protect Muslims on the lines of the SC/ST Prevention of Atrocities Act.

Although the conference stopped short of floating a proposal for the formation of a national party for Muslims, it decided to set up a committee — Quami Muslim Majlis-e-Amal — to take up their demands with the Centre.

Bukhari accused the Government of harassing Muslims in the name of fighting terror.

Heading: With Seven Years in Tibet behind him, French director ‘plans film on Kashmir’ - Indian Express
Content:
EID was usually the time BSF soldier Arif Hussain Khati came home to Dhule in northern Maharashtra from his posting in the militancy-torn Jammu and Kashmir.

However, this year, the festivities turned nearly fatal for him. Three days after Eid, on October 5, Hindu-Muslim riots broke out in Dhule, and the soldier who puts his life at risk everyday in Bandipora, guarding the country's borders, had to beg frenzied mobs to spare him and his family.

They burnt his uniform, his identity card, even his gallantry certificates, besides ransacking the house, says the Constable, posted with the BSF's 51st battalion. "I saw my house being set on fire by our own neighbours. They were in thousands. Then they tried to throw my brother Sikandar into the fire. My wife fainted," Khati told The Indian Express. "I pleaded with them. I told them I am a soldier. I told them I am fighting for the country at the border. They didn't listen. For the first time in my life, I felt alone. I was told I am Muslim and nothing else."

But what hurt him more, Khati says, was the indifferent attitude of the police. "The situation was tense since the day riots broke in Dhule. We were anticipating attacks. But not one policeman came to rescue us," he said. "We spent the entire night outside the police station urging the officer to register our complaint. Instead of assuring us relief, the police asked us to leave our house at the earliest."

The violence in Dhule started as a minor conflict over some Muslims allegedly tearing up posters put up by local Hindu groups urging Hindus to wake up following the spate of bomb blasts around the country. But it soon escalated, resulting in 10 people being killed and nearly 200 injured. It also spread to areas like Khati's Shirud village, which is about 25 km from Dhule town.

Khati was given a job in the BSF on compassionate grounds in 2002 after his father Riyaz Khati, also a Sub-Inspector in the force, died on duty. "I have taken part in several (counter-insurgency) operations but I have never felt scared. That day, I was frightened. I thought we will all be killed," said Khati, who has been living with relatives in the neighbouring town of Malegaon since the attack.

Late last week, when The Indian Express visited Dhule, Inspector-General of Police S P Gupta claimed: "Khati is just floating stories. Earlier, he asked us to provide transport to the neighbouring village of Challisgaon claiming he had to resume work. Now he says his house has been ransacked. Since he is in Malegaon now, he should first lodge a complaint with the Malegaon police."

But bureaucratic wheels have since moved, what with the BSF promising to take up the matter with the Maharashtra administration and also assuring Khati and his family help. On Tuesday, an FIR was finally registered in Malegaon, eight days after Khati and his family were targeted.

The experience has made Khati distraught and bitter. "I have been serving for years now and I had never felt that I was treated differently because I am a Muslim. In my battalion, we are all like brothers. But here it is different. I have no home now," he says, adding that the family plans to move to Muslim-majority Malegaon. "We feel safe in our area, amongst our people."

Heading: Knowledge panel gets extension till March 31 - Indian Express
Content:
After inviting China's fury with his much-talked-about Seven Years in Tibet, Oscar-winning French director Jean-Jacques Annaud has reportedly decided to tackle Kashmir next. According to a report in UK daily Guardian on Tuesday, Annaud is in the final stages of talks to make a terrorism thriller set in Kashmir, on the border between India and Pakistan.

Annaud's first feature film Black and White in Color was awarded an Oscar for the Best Foreign Language Film in 1976.

His third film Quest for Fire (La Guerre du Feu) received two Césars for best film and best director. Annuad is however best known for Seven Years in Tibet, which had managed to cause a fair amount of controversy.

Angered by the positive depiction of the Dalai Lama in the film, the Chinese authorities had banned Annaud and stars Brad Pitt and David Thewlis from ever entering the country.

The film on Kashmir reportedly centres around terrorism. The Guardian says the story has been penned by D B Weiss, and involves three ex-mercenaries who head for the region after hearing that a terrorist leader with $30 million price on his head is going to be in town for a while.

However, it turns out, each of them has other reasons for being in the area.

Director, Kashmir Tourism, Farooq Ahmad Shah, whose department handles provision of facilities to visiting film crews, says they have not been contacted over any plans to shoot the film in the Valley. "No foreign film director has approached us so far," he said.

However, Annaud is known to shoot as close to the area he is depicting in the film as possible — he admitted two years after Seven Years in Tibet that parts of it were secretly shot in Tibet. Variety reports that location scouts are looking at sites in Argentina, Mexico and other parts of India.

Heading: Centre ‘won’t protect’ Sethu, says no proof of religious importance - Indian Express
Content:
The Prime Minister's Office has given a six-month extension to the National Knowledge Commission (NKC) to focus on 'implementation' of its various recommendations aimed at making India a 'knowledge society'.

Set up in 2005 by Manmohan Singh, the NKC headed by Sam Pitroda will now have an extended term up to March 31, 2009 even as the HRD Ministry has been rather non-receptive to the Commission's several ideas.

The NKC has made over 200 recommendations on education, health, science, entrepreneurship, e-governance and so on since it was set up in October 2005. "We have got a great deal of support from the PM. He is very happy with the Commission's work. He wants us to continue," Pitroda said at a seminar on "Demography, Disparity, Development". He later told reporters that a communication had been received from the PMO extending the NKC's term.

"During this period till March next year, we will see how our recommendations can be implemented. We are beginning to interact with the public on our recommendations," he said. Pitroda admitted that the response of the HRD Ministry to their recommendations had been slow.

Heading: BSP important, Maya among PM contenders: CPM - Indian Express
Content:
The Centre today categorically refused to accord protection to the Rama Sethu, saying that "the belief of a community" has to be proved like any other fact in a court of law. "... and thereafter, a secular judge is bound to accept that."

Putting its views forth in black and white, the Government reiterated its earlier arguments that the petitioners opposed to the Sethusamudram Shipping Canal Project "have not alleged, much less proved that Rama Sethu forms an integral or essential part of Hindu religion".

Saying that the bridge held no sacred significance, the Government refused it protection under Articles 25 (Freedom of conscience, and free profession, practice and propagation of religion) or 26 (Freedom to manage religious affairs) of the Constitution.

Referring to arguments raised that Sethu holds religious importance for millions of Hindus, the Government said: "It is not even alleged that it (Sethu as a place of worship) is the belief of the Hindu community." Even though it earlier withdrew a controversial affidavit questioning the existence of Lord Rama and in relation to the case, the Government continues to take the line that Rama Sethu is not a place of worship.

Further, the Centre submitted, the petitioners had not proved that the Hindu community did not believe Lord Rama himself broke the bridge. "Nor it has been established that whatever remains of the Rama Sethu as a place of worship is an essential part of the Hindu religion."

Interestingly, the Government referred to texts like Padma Purana, Valmiki Ramayana, Bhagwat Purana and Gazatteer of Southern India of 1855 for its arguments, the same texts which were relied upon by the petitioners to build their case.

Heading: 23 die in Assam bus crash - Indian Express
Content:
The CPI(M) has termed its strategy as one of "defeating the BJP and rejecting the Congress" in run-up to the Assembly elections in six states and the Lok Sabha.

Talking to reporters on Tuesday, after a three-day session of the party's Central Committee here, general secretary Prakash Karat said "the party will adopt an electoral platform aiming to defeat the BJP, which is a communal party advocating reactionary economic policies, and for rejecting the Congress that is forging a strategic alliance with the US and pursuing anti-people economic policies".

Karat's revelation of his party's poll strategy coincided with the Election Commission's announcement to hold elections in Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Delhi, Mizoram and Chhatisgarh. The EC postponed a decision on Jammu and Kashmir for the time being.

Karat also did not rule out the possibility of Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Mayawati being one of the contenders for the Prime Minister's post after the Lok Sabha elections. "The BSP is an important political party ruling the largest state in our country. We expect them to fare well in the forthcoming Lok Sabha polls. It will depend on the mandate after the elections and she will be among the ones," Karat said when asked whether his party will support Mayawati as the next Prime Minister.

After the CPI(M)'s withdrawal of support to the Manmohan Singh Government on the issue of Indo-US civil nuclear deal, the party has attached much importance to the economic issues being followed by the Centre rather than hitting on the nuke deal issue. At the same time, it has also criticised the Congress-led coalition Government for its "pro-US stance".

Karat denounced nationwide attacks on Christians and pulled up the Centre for being a mute spectator. "All this is being done eyeing the upcoming polls. Attacks on Chtristian minorities are recurring in Orissa, Karnataka and other states. What happened in Kandhamal is shocking, now efforts are on to reconvert the victims. We want action against Bajrang Dal under the same laws which are used to curb terrorism," he said.

He announced that the party would conduct a nationwide campaign against terrorism and communalism from Octover 30 to November 5.

While approving the West Bengal CPI(M) and Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee's way of handling the Singur situation, Karat also hoped that the Left Front Government would try to find out an alternative option in Singur after the Tata Motors' pullout.

Heading: India’s first air show begins in Hyderabad - Indian Express
Content: At least 23 people including five women and six children were killed when a bus carrying brick kiln labourers met with an accident near Bilasipara in Dhubri district of lower Assam on Monday night. The bus on its way from Golakganj near the Assam-West Bengal border to Hojai in central Assam, lost control near Beltoli on the NH-31 and crashed into a stationary truck from behind.

Heading: Sangma: fear of conversions to Christianity unfounded - Indian Express
Content:
Hyderabadis are awaiting the arrival of the world's largest aircraft Airbus A 380 on Wednesday, when India's first air show 'India Aviation 2008' starts at Begumpet Airport.

About 150 countries are expected to participate in the four-day air show being organized by the Union Civil Aviation Ministry and FICCI, with the US as partner country.

AAI officials said while defence air shows would be organized at Bangalore, Hyderabad's Begumpet airport will host air shows every two years.

Several seminars, conferences and an exhibition on Indian aviation industry will be held during the four-day show. There will also be flying and static display of aircraft and customer demonstration flights.

While the Airbus A 380 will be the major attraction, 36 different types of aircraft manufactured by world famous companies like Dassault, Bell, Cessna and Boeing besides the indigenous Pushpak will also participate in the air show.

Heading: Mahanta back in AGP - Indian Express
Content:
In the backdrop of attacks against Christians in Orissa, Karnataka and Kerala, former Lok Sabha speaker and NCP leader Purno A Sangma said that it had become imperative for Christians to address these concerns as citizens of this "great country" and as followers of Christ.

Speaking at the inaugural session of a national seminar, "Christianity: National Integration", organised by Synod College on Tuesday, Sangma said: "As a faith, Christianity has been under relentless provocations in recent times and it is important that we address these concerns at two dimensions — as followers of Christ as well as citizens of this amazing nation, India."

Pointing out that the total Christian population in the country is just 2.5 per cent, he wondered as to "why should this be a cause of worry for our antagonists".

Sangma said when there is documentary proof of Christians being a minority religion in India, the fear of conversion and ultimate consummation of Indian society is unfounded.

He, however, said: "Conversion is a matter of one's personal conviction which one exercises as a responsible citizen and should be practised on the foundation of secularism and freedom of religion as enshrined in the Constitution of India."

Sangma described Christianity as "highly accommodative" faith and said it had considered the local needs of such a diverse nation which has led to Indianisation of Christianity.

Heading: MPA panel asks minister to explain hand in assault case - Indian Express
Content:
Three years after former Assam Chief Minister Prafulla Kumar Mahanta was banished from the Asom Gana Parishad (AGP) that he founded in 1985, the party on Tuesday took him back under its wings. Mahanta's re-entry into the AGP also puts him at the centrestage of state politics.

The AGP received a much-needed shot in the arm with newly-installed president Chandra Mohan Patowari also taking back into the parent fold as many as three breakaway factions of the regional party on a day when it marked its 23rd foundation day. A central unification rally was held at Golaghat, the town in Upper Assam where the AGP was constituted.

Others who returned to the fold on Tuesday included former speaker Pulakesh Barua and former ministers Atul Bora, Biraj Kumar Sharma and Rekharani Das-Boro.

Mahanta's re-entry into the AGP however faced several hurdles, which included a statewide protest staged by AASU. Patowari said the reunited regional party would strive to free Assam from the burden of illegal migrants and solve other burning issues.

Heading: Goa minister also booked in rape case against son - Indian Express
Content:
As pressure is mounting on Meghalaya Chief Minister Donkupar Roy to drop Donkupar Massar from the Cabinet, the NCP-United Democratic Party (UDP)-led Meghalaya Progressive Alliance (MPA) coordination committee met late Monday night and decided to ask for an explanation from Massar on the alleged assault and threat to kill four labourers in Borsora.

Massar has been accused of assaulting and threatening to kill four labourers in Borsora in West Khasi hills district. Three of those who were allegedly assaulted by the minister had filed an FIR with the Ranikor police station in West Khasi district. West Khasi hills Superintendent of Police W Kharkhrang told The Indian Express: "We have registered the case, but need Assembly Speaker's permission before questioning the minister."

Ten NGOs have taken up the assault case and have submitted a memorandum to the Chief Minister, demanding removal of the minister within 10 days. The MPA coordination committee chaired by Roy was attended by NCP leader Purno A Sangma among other state ministers.

Heading: Split poll panel postpones decision on J&K dates - Indian Express
Content:
The elder son of Goa Minister Atanasio Monseratte was on Tuesday charged with raping a minor German girl in a case, which also sucked in the politician who faced charges of abetting the crime.

The case also had a violent overtone after a social activist and lawyer Aires Rodrigues was attacked for apparently helping the victim's mother to get justice.

In an embarassment for the Congress-led coalition Government, the state police booked 21-year-old Rohit for alleged sexual and mental abuse of the 14-year-old girl and was charged with offences including rape, abetment to crime and outraging her modesty.

Hours after the police action, Monserratte, who is the state's education minister and unattached MLA of regional party UGDP, was also booked. Superintendent of Police Bosco George said the Minister was charged with "abetting the crime" by handing over his mobile phone to his son for the purpose of sending lewd text messages.

The minister claimed his son was innocent and that he was not involved in the crime and the police action smacked of a political conspiracy.

Police, who swung into action 12 days after a complaint was filed, could not find Rohit at his residences at Taleigao and Miramar in Panaji.

The police teams, however, served the notice on Rohit. "The complaint was lodged by the girl's mother Fadela Fuchs, a German researcher. In her October 2 complaint, she had alleged that Rohit sexually assaulted her daughter, outraged her modesty and sent obscene SMSes ," George told a press conference on Tuesday evening.

"He (Rohit) has been asked to immediately appear before the police for interrogation," George said.

Heading: RBI Governor, FM meet PM, Montek: For more liquidity,  Round 2 soon - Indian Express
Content:
A divided Election Commission on Tuesday decided to postpone the decision on holding assembly elections in Jammu and Kashmir by a few days. The Commission announced a schedule spread over November and December for elections to the Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Delhi, Mizoram and Rajasthan assemblies.

The final call on the Jammu and Kashmir election dates will be taken in the "next two or three days", a top Election Commission source said. Governor's Rule in the state ends on January 9.

The three-member Commission was split down the middle when it met in New Delhi on Tuesday. Chief Election Commissioner N Gopalaswami argued early polls "could mean a poor turnout" and rob the exercise of "required legitimacy", going against colleagues who said that "there was no guarantee that there would be a higher turnout even if elections were to be held at a later date," EC sources said.

Under the rules of procedure for the Election Commission, in case of a split opinion, the majority view prevails.

According to the sources, the central government has already conveyed to the EC its two major points about the J&K elections.

One, an early election would help India's reputation. At an Idea Exchange programme with The Indian Express journalists on Tuesday morning, Union Home Minister Shivraj Patil said the "Union government is ready to hold elections on time, but it's a decision to be taken by the Election Commission."

Two, elections without adequate voter turnout would, however, raise many "inconvenient questions". In this context, the situation in Pakistan should be kept in mind — "if (Pakistan President) Asif Ali Zardari were to walk the talk on pronouncements such as militants in J&K are 'terrorists', it could open up a window of opportunity in the state," said a government official.

A top EC source told The Indian Express: "Issues like voter turnout and the legitimacy of the election in case of a poor response, and the possibility of a political vacuum in the state if elections are put back, were discussed in the meeting. There will be further discussions in the next meeting."

Election Commissioner S Y Quraishi said: "Conducting an election requires careful planning, and one weighs various pros and cons of the situation. One cannot say it (the inability to reach a decision) was (due to) a difference of opinion."

Sources in the Valley said the unwillingness of mainstream Kashmiri parties was a reason for the EC's refusal to take an immediate decision.

At their meetings with the EC over October 7-8, the PDP, National Conference and even the Congress and smaller parties like the J&K Panthers Party had expressed themselves against early polls.

"They said they would go by whatever the Election Commission decides but at the same time they said ground realities would make it difficult to hold polls. They were not sure about the safety of their workers. Even Congress leaders seemed unsure," said an official who was part of the EC delegation to the state.

The EC also did not get enough evidence to conclude an early poll would see a healthy voter turnout, especially in Srinagar, the official said. "Besides the uncertain participation of people, we fear that the local staff might not turn up for poll duty," he said.

In New Delhi, the BJP predictably slammed the EC move.

"The Election Commission must clarify why poll dates were deferred in Jammu and Kashmir. By doing this we are telling the world that India is incapable of conducting polls in Jammu and Kashmir and have bowed to some separatist forces," general secretary Arun Jaitley said.

Congress spokesperson Manish Tewari said, "It is for the poll panel to decide whether the situation there is conducive for elections or not."

Heading: Taking on terror: Govt forms panel to explore tightening of laws - Indian Express
Content:
The Reserve Bank of India is likely to slash the cash reserve ratio (the portion of deposits banks have to keep with the central bank as cash) by at least 50 points and also reduce the statutory liquidity ratio (the portion of deposits banks have to invest in government securities). The possibility of a cut in the signal repo rate (the rate at which the RBI lends to banks) has also gained currency within the government in the last couple of days.

Finance Minister P Chidambaram and RBI Governor D Subbarao, who met Prime Minister Manmohan Singh and Planning Commission Deputy Chairman Montek Singh Ahluwalia this evening, discussed these measures for over an hour. After an earlier meeting with the Finance Minister, Subbarao said everything was under control and that he would now seek the PM's advice.

While an announcement on the second round of measures to boost liquidity within the banking system and to the corporate sector is likely soon, it is not certain if the RBI will cut the repo rate immediately. Chidambaram has already promised that more liquidity will be injected within the next 10-12 days. The expert group appointed by him under Finance Secretary Arun Ramanathan is also scheduled to meet tomorrow in Mumbai to finalise its suggestions for boosting liquidity.

The RBI also initiated measures to help mutual funds tide over their redemption pressures on debt funds by opening a special 15-day repo auction window allowing banks to on-lend exclusively to mutual funds. It eased the guidelines relating to certificate of deposits by letting MFs seek loans against these or even surrender them to banks before maturity.

The special auction, open to banks specifically for lending on to funds, saw only Rs 3,500 crore being taken up against Rs 20,000 crore on offer. Market circles said this is because of the short notice for the auction and the recovery in the stock markets in the last two days.

Despite the 150 basis point cut in CRR last week that released Rs 60,000 crore, liquidity continues to remain tight with huge injections by the Reserve Bank of India through the repo window during the last two days. Banks borrow from the RBI at a fixed rate of 9 per cent in an auction. On Monday, the RBI lent about Rs 70,000 crore and today banks again borrowed Rs 62,800 crore, indicating that the demand for funds continued to be high.

According to sources in the government, consensus was slowly being built about the need for an interest rate cut and a further cut in the SLR, from 24 per cent now. Both Ahluwalia and Suresh Tendulkar, Chairman of the PM's Economic Advisory Council, have said a small cut in the repo rate will help business sentiment and bolster growth.

RBI sources said a SLR cut will help banks in that it will free up more money for lending. Average holding of banks in SLR instruments is 26 per cent now, said a source in RBI. "If deposits rise at a rapid rate — which is likely given the 11 per cent interest rates offered by banks — a cut in SLR will free up significant resources for banks," he said.

Finance Ministry sources said other measures to liberalise foreign capital inflows were also being discussed. These included relaxing the external commercial borrowing norms and letting all companies — not just infrastructure firms — to tap the window for loans up to $ 500 million. The ceiling on the interest rate offered by banks on non-resident accounts too may go up by 100 basis points, they said.

Heading: Tendulkar slips to 24 - Indian Express
Content:
A Catholic bishop in Kerala has sparked off a controversy and embarrassed the Church by adopting a 26-year-old woman.

Following complaints from priests, the Latin Catholic Church has initiated a multi-level probe into the adoption by John Thattunkal, 58, the Bishop of Cochin.

Sources say the bishop adopted the woman with the consent of her non-Catholic Christian family, hailing from Pathanamthitta in central kerala.

Thattunkal met the woman during a pilgrimage abroad and was impressed by her "spirituality and divine experience." "I have only fatherly love towards the woman who has spiritual powers. This relation is giving me spiritual refreshment," Thattunkal was quoted by Mathrubhoomi, a Malayalam newspaper, as saying.

When The Indian Express tried to reach him on Tuesday, the bishop was not available for comments. "He has been in meditation the whole day," said Fr Thambi Antony, diocese public relations officer. Antony declined to comment on the controversy as the issue is being looked into by the Church authorities.

The bishop, who holds a doctorate in Canon law and civil law, cleared the adoption formalities at the sub-registrar office in Mattancheri. Sub-registrar Sudhakaran told this newspaper that the adoption deed was registered in the second week of September. "Two priests from the diocese had signed as witnesses and in the deed, the woman was stated to be adopted as a daughter of the bishop," he said.

After the adoption, the woman stayed in a guest house within the Bishop House compound in Fort Kochi. After this became an issue among a section of priests in the Cochin diocese, she left the guest house.

A senior priest from Cochin diocese said the issue is likely to snowball into a major scandal. "The moot question is why the bishop adopted a young woman for so-called spiritual nourishment. The future course of the issue would depend on his explanation," the priest said.

Kerala Catholic Bishop's Council Secretary Fr Alathara Stephen said that the Archdiocese of Verapoly and Apostolic Nuncio to India Arch Bishop Pedro Lopez Quintaine (Vatican's representative in the country) have already initiated separate inquiries after complaints from the Cochin diocese. Action, if any, would be taken by Vatican, based on the Nuncio's report.

"A bishop can adopt a person while a priest has to get the consent of his bishop for the same action. In the past, no bishop in Kerala has resorted to this kind of adoption," Stephen said. Asked whether the bishop's action amounted to a scandal, Stephen said the gravity of the offence would depend upon the position held by the offender.

Monsignor Sebastain Luis, the Vicar-General of Verapoly archdiocese, under which the diocese of Cochin falls, said the issue is being secretly looked into by the Bishops' Council and other Church bodies. "At the same time, we cannot hide action against the bishop, if taken at a later stage," he said.

Bishop Thattungal has maintained that he adopted the woman according to the Church laws. "In the past too, bishops and priests have adopted children... She did not stay in the Bishop's House, she stayed in the nearby guest house along with her father. We had travelled by the same car for spiritual programmes. I have explained my stand to Verapoly Archbishop Daniel Acharuparambil and Apostolic Nuncio Archbishop Pedro Lopez," he told Mathrubhoomi. "A lobby, including certain priests, has been working against me in the diocese," he said.

Heading: For Kynan, the Nelson’s not bad luck - Indian Express
Content:
Sachin Tendulkar may be on the verge of becoming the highest run-getter in Tests but his position on the ICC rankings continues to drop.

In the latest ICC list, Tendulkar has dropped to 24th spot. Virender Sehwag (11th) and Rahul Dravid (18th) also lost places while VVS Laxman (14th) is the lone Indian batsman to move up.

Australia's Michael Hussey returned to the top after scoring 177 runs in the Bangalore Test, followed by Sri Lankan Kumar Sangakkara and West Indies's Shivnarine Chanderpaul. Among the bowlers, Zaheer Khan gained seven places and is 11th in the rankings while Anil Kumble dropped to 18th.

Among the all-rounders, Brett Lee moved up one place to seventh.

Sourav 'serial offender'

Meanwhile, Sourav Ganguly continued to get under the skin of the Australians, with the visiting media lashing out at him for what they termed 'delaying tactics'.

The final day's play had been cut short due to bad light after Ganguly and VVS Laxman complained to the umpires.

In various newspapers across Australia on Tuesday, Ganguly was castigated for delaying action during the crucial closing moments of the Test.

The Australian media commented that, had the Indian batsmen not resorted to delay tactics, Ricky Ponting & Co could have taken a 1-0 lead in the four-Test series. They also attacked the ICC rules, claiming that the existing bad light rule unfairly favours batsmen.

A member of the popular National Nine News sports bureau took a stinging dig at Ganguly, whom he described as a "serial offender".

He wrote: "Serial offender Sourav Ganguly firstly persuaded the umpires to go off. Then, when play resumed, Ganguly made Australia's fielders and (batting) partner VVS Laxman wait an eternity because he'd apparently 'forgotten to put his thigh pad on'. Please! Can't you be timed out in this game?"

Heading: Meet the man behind Lance’s comeback - Indian Express
Content:
The Nelson - 111 - is said to bring bad luck in sport. To break the hex, David Shepherd used to hop when a batting side reached that score, and Aussie-rules football radio commentator Rex Hunt sends airwaves into an exaggerated frenzy when 111 points get scored.

Paused at 111 after his qualifying round, shooter Kynan Chenai Darius must've wondered whether he was poised for take-off or heartburn.

As it turned out, he broke the jinx as India's young trap shooter grabbed gold, as his one-bird lead of 111-110 over Malta's Burgia Ryan proved decisive.

The two boys went neck-and-neck in the final, blasting 17 birds each, but Kynan's cushion helped the 17-year-old Hyderabadi pip his rival 128-127 at the Balewadi range on Tuesday. Bizarrely, the scoreboard froze when the one-two from the pack were locked at 123-all, but needing to make good his last three shots, Kynan held his nerves in a manner that would have made his mentor — veteran shooter Mansher Singh — proud.

Kynan, who is doing his A Levels at boarding school in Ooty, had taken up the sport half a decade ago, guided zealously by his father Chenai Darius. But it wasn't until earlier this year when he won the Indian colts event, that he saw the tide turn from his earlier run of ordinary scores, making him one of India's fastest-improving trap shooters. "There've been ups and downs in my juniors career. But all the hard work was worth it," he said, kissing his medal.

Training alongside Mansher Singh and Manavjit Sandhu in Italy before the Beijing Olympics, Kynan took rapid strides, having benefitted from his stint under Marcello Dradi, whose association with Indian trap and skeet marksmen yielded some fine results.

He finished sixth amongst seniors this year, and was all diligence in Italy, but Kynan also made many friends here with his easy affability. As Aussie McNabb said going into the final, "He's a nice guy, I wouldn't be sad if he won gold."

What would get the boy to really whoop with joy is Mansher's measured approval. "It's the first big international medal for Kynan. More than the score, I'm happy he could win a high-pressure final. When you win at an early age, you know you belong," said the four-time Olympian. "He should start training more scientifically now, but all without changing his natural ability."

The veracity of Admiral Nelson's queer 'one eye, one arm' legend is still debated, but Kynan Darius sure took his 111 the whole distance today, and much will be said in coming days of this boy's innate hand-eye coordination.

Heading: Mr Universe... in his one-room world - Indian Express
Content:
This is the man who made Lance Armstrong cry "uncle."

On a recent weekday morning here 7,700 feet up in the Rocky Mountains, David Wiens (picture right) fed and packed his three sons and cajoled them to get to school, prepared for some volunteer work and hoped to maybe squeeze in an hour-long bike ride before rushing off to pick up the children. A day later, Wiens, a 44-year-old Denver native, will be catching passes for his flag football team. And soon, when the snow hits, he will stop riding altogether until spring. Instead, he will ski most days, when he is not playing on his recreational league hockey team.

That may not be the workout regimen expected of a cyclist who, two months ago, broke Armstrong, the man who seemingly could never be broken in his seven consecutive Tour de France victories. Their competition, in the Leadville Trail 100 mountain bike race, set in motion Armstrong's decision to make a professional comeback. "I'd thought a little bit about coming back to cycling before that," Armstrong said in a recent interview. "But the process of training for it and the excitement of being on the start line and competing again went a long way to kick-starting a comeback."

Armstrong had officially retired three years earlier, after winning his seventh Tour de France. But as someone who never fell completely out of race shape, he did not go to Leadville on August 9 to lose.

But he did. The 100-mile race is brutal, starting at 10,200 feet, climbing at one point to 12,600 feet and covering a total of 14,000 feet of climbs. The two men worked together for most of the race, taking turns in the lead, which put them 20 minutes ahead of the rest of the pack. Wiens moved aside with about 10 miles to go to let Armstrong take the lead as they headed onto an uphill trail. This time, however, Armstrong told Wiens: "No. Go. I'm done." Wiens, known to cheer on competitors even midrace, replied: "No. Come on."

"Go," Armstrong said. "I didn't ask him twice," Wiens recalled recently, and he rode away from Armstrong, though not completely. Wiens went on to break his own record, set last year, by finishing in 6 hours 45 minutes 45 seconds. He has won the Leadville Trail 100 six years in a row. Armstrong, who finished nearly two minutes behind him, said he had never in his career told another cyclist he was done during a race.
