With Tuesday's 174-point recovery, the Sensex has bounced back by 955 points (9 per cent) in the last two days. Who Are leading the recovery on Dalal Street that witnessed a 16 per cent fall last week? And who are lagging behind? Here's a look:

PERFORMERS

INFOTECH: IT stocks were in the forefront of the rally in the last two days. The BSE IT sector index rallied by 13.76% in two days. TCS which shot up 12.6% on Monday and Infosys which gained 5.9% on Tuesday were leading the rally.

BANKING: Battered ICICI Bank is back in the reckoning with a 16.8% rise on Monday and another 5.2% jump on Tuesday. The banking sector index (Bankex) soared by 13.51% in 2 days.

REAL ESTATE: The BSE realty index slumped by 28 per cent in the first ten days of October -- nearly one-third of the valuation of realty companies were eroded. But the BSE realty index bounced back by 11.16% in the last two days. DLF has recovered from the 52-week low of Rs 279.

LAGGARDS

METALS: Metal companies suffered heavily in the first week of October and the BSE Metal index lost 27.2% between September 30-October 10. Though the Sensex recovered by 9% in the last two days, the BSE Metal Index has showed a recovery of just 4.73%.

OIL: Oil firms fell by up to 19.5% in the first ten sessions of October. But the BSE Oil sector index underperfomed the Sensex by showing only a 4.83% recovery in the last 2 days.

MID-CAP FIRMS: Hundreds of mid-cap companies have also underperformed the Sensex. The BSE Mid-cap index plunged by 23.3% from October 1-10. But the index has recovered by only 5.88% in the last two days. Ditto is the story in the small-cap segment that showed a recovery of only 5.98%.

FOREIGN FUNDS turn investors after two weeks

Mumbai: After a gap of about two weeks, the flight of foreign investment has turned towards the Indian stock

market once again as they pumped in as much as Rs 898.25 crore in equities. FIIs invested in shares worth Rs 3,829.76 crore, and sold stocks valued Rs 2,931.51 crore, resulting in a net investment of Rs 898 crore, as per provisional

data available on the Bombay Stock Exchange. According to information available on the Sebi website, FIIs offloaded equities worth Rs 842.20 crore, yesterday.

Heading: Call money rates ease - Indian Express
Content:
What is causing the current liquidity crisis in the debt segment of mutual funds? Will the RBI's Rs 20,000 crore window suffice? And is there something wrong with debt funds' business model? Sanjay Kr Singh explains:

What has happened?

On October 14, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) announced a special 14-day repo auction to commercial banks of Rs 20,000 crore. This will enable banks to meet the liquidity requirements of mutual funds.

But why the need for such assistance?

A large number of mutual funds holding short-term debt assets — liquid plus funds and fixed maturity plans (FMPs), and to a smaller extent, liquid funds — are having trouble meeting redemption requests from investors.

Who is affected?

A majority of investors in such funds are large corporates and institutional investors. Retail investors constitute only a small percentage.

What led to redemption pressures in first place?

One, liquidity shortage has affected the entire financial industry, and mutual funds have not been spared. Liquidity pressures emerged last month. Normally, in September there is an outflow from short-term funds as corporates withdraw money to pay advance tax. Funds start flowing back in October. The inflow did not resume this October. The crisis in the western

financial markets has affected sentiments and investors are seeking safe havens for their funds. And many of them are themselves facing a cash crunch.

What was the immediate trigger?

Fund houses are resorting to a fire sale of debt paper to meet redemption pressures, and that is driving NAVs of these funds down. Normally, NAVs of cash funds do not decline over the previous day's NAV: they only go up. In the 13-year history of cash funds this has not happened. Now the NAVs of many cash funds have gone down in value.

Why are fund houses having difficulty meeting redemption pressures?

In India, even in the best of times, the market for short-term debt instruments is liquid but that for medium and long-term securities is not. Now, there is a liquidity mismatch inherent in debt funds. Investors can withdraw their money at a day's notice, but it's not so easy for the fund houses to sell off the underlying securities. And more so in the current environment where liquidity is tight. There is also a maturity mismatch. It means that many short-term funds have invested in longer-term paper, as the latter pay higher returns. But these papers, as said earlier, are even less liquid. Fund houses are in difficulty also because some have invested in poor-quality debt paper (say, bonds from real estate companies).

Will RBI's Rs 20,000-crore loan window suffice?

The scary scenario is that Rs 20,000 crore will prove insufficient and redemption demand will persist. The positive scenario is that RBI's move, besides providing much-needed liquidity to mutual funds, will give a psychological boost. The message it will send out is that the regulators will not allow mutual fund houses to go for distress sales. That will cause redemption pressures to abate.

What should you do?

If your debt fund belongs to a larger fund house, such houses are likely to be able to meet redemption pressures better. In future, before investing in debt funds, look up the ratings of both the fund house and the fund. Rating of funds remains optional, so they may not be available for all schemes. Avoid them.

What are the likely long-term consequences?

One, the scare could cause the short-term debt fund business to shrink.

Two, the need for creating a transparent and liquid bond market will gain urgency.

And three, the valuation model by which the NAVs of debt funds are calculated could be forced to change. Funds today hold bonds that are not traded daily. But their NAVs change daily. How are these calculated? By taking into account the maturity, liquidity, and coupon rates of bonds. All fund houses use one formula that factors in these characteristics.

In today's situation, actual NAVs have declined below what the formula suggests. Clearly, the model does not take into account a situation of large-scale redemption pressure on one side and low liquidity of underlying securities on the other. In future, calls for tweaking the valuation model could get strident.

Heading: IBSA is likely to issue a statement on financial crisis - Indian Express
Content:
In recent weeks, companies which are short of cash have withdrawn money from mutual funds where their treasury function was often outsourced. These redemptions led to sale of bonds by mutual funds. Given the illiquidity of the bond market, bond prices had dropped sharply as a consequence of this sale of bonds by mutual funds. Real estate companies and NBFCs, which are prohibited from accessing funding in most parts of Indian finance, were particularly affected since mutual funds are a key source of funding for them.

In an important move, RBI set up a mechanism for mutual funds to obtain liquidity support of Rs 20,000 crore. This reduces the disruption suffered by mutual funds, real estate companies and NBFCs. In the long run, India needs a well-functioning bond-currency-derivatives nexus, with a deep and liquid bond market where bonds can be easily sold. In coming months, the recommendations of the Patil, Mistry and Rajan reports must be implemented, so as to achieve this system of markets. In the short run, RBI has done well to recognise this element of the financial crisis and directly address it. Call money rates fell to 10 per cent from 20 on October 10 following RBI's liquidity moves. The rate is, however, still above the LAF corridor, indicating that liquidity will remain a concern.

On the stock market, Nifty rose by only 0.8 per cent — a weak gain, given the optimism in world markets. While the rupee-dollar rate appreciated marginally to 47.71, the currency futures trading at NSE ended with a forecasted rate of Rs 48.23 for October 27.

At 8:30 PM, the US stock market index was essentially flat, after having risen sharply on Monday. Share prices of US financial firms were up 3 per cent. The TED spread, which measures the mistrust of financial firms for each other, dropped from 4.59 percentage points on Friday to 4.22. While this was an improvement, the crisis will only have ended when this measure falls sharply.

Meanwhile, RBI released data about their currency trading in August. In August, the rupee-dollar rate had depreciated from Rs 42.26 to Rs 43.25. We now know that this depreciation was not entirely caused by fundamental economic factors. RBI was in the market pushing the rupee to depreciate. The net purchase of dollars by RBI in August was $1.2 billion. Thus, as late as August, RBI was working towards achieving a bigger rupee depreciation. There are many elements of the agenda for RBI reform that flow from a simple emphasis on transparency. Why were dollars purchased in August? Why is daily data not being released? Why is data for August only released in the middle of September? What has RBI been doing after August 31? A transparent central bank should have good answers for all these questions.

(Ila Patnaik is a senior fellow at National Institute of Public Finance and Policy)

Heading: Reserve Bank turns on the liquidity tap for mutual funds - Indian Express
Content:
The Delhi declaration of the third summit of leading emerging economies India, Brazil and South Africa (IBSA) is expected to include a significant statement on the international financial crisis. The heads of the three states — Prime Minister Manmohan Singh, Brazil President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and South African President Kgalema Motlanthe — will discuss crucial issues such as food security and high fuel prices and ways to mitigate the impact of the global turmoil.

IBSA, a trilateral development initiative between the three countries started in 2003, has revised the trade target among its members to $15 billion by 2010, up from around $ 10 billion a year ago. In the third summit, the countries were expected to sign upto seven agreements and action plans to cement ties in civil aviation and other areas of trade, said Nalin Surie, secretary (west), ministry of external affairs.

The Prime Minister will hold bilateral consultations with Lula and Motlanthe after the summit meeting.

The Delhi Summit will complete the first cycle of IBSA's annual summits. The second cycle will begin with the Fourth Summit in Brazil next year.

Heading: Is Guj offering more sops than WB, Uttarakhand and Himachal? - Indian Express
Content:
Prosecutors in an Italian court Thursday asked the key middleman in the IAF's VVIP chopper deal whether the initials 'AP' in an alleged "budget sheet" for bribes to politicians referred to Ahmed Patel, the political secretary of UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi.

The middleman, Guido Haschke, who has consistently denied bribing Indian officials or politicians, replied that he did not know who or what 'AP' stood for.

As first reported by The Indian Express, Italian prosecutors had last month produced a handwritten document they alleged was a "budget" drawn up by two middlemen — Haschke and Christian Michel — which purportedly lists initials of Indian politicians and designations of bureaucrats and IAF officers who allegedly had to be "handled" to fix the Rs 3,546 crore deal.

The alleged "budget sheet" detailed how kickbacks of 51 million euros would be divided and under the heading "POL" — Haschke has claimed this referred to Indian politicians — there is a reference to "AP" against which "3 million euro" has been listed.

Another amount of 15/16 million euros was listed against "FAM" which is said to be "Family". Haschke has claimed the note was dictated to him by British consultant Michel during one of their meetings in 2008.

On Thursday, Italian prosecutor Eugenio Fusco asked Haschke during a court hearing in Busto Arsizio near Milan whether "AP" in the note was a reference to Ahmed Patel.

In his reply, the middlemen said he did not know what AP meant when he wrote it down. Haschke also denied any bribes were paid for the contract and said that the "budget sheet" was just an imaginary note drawn up and was never acted upon.

He also said the budget sheet was merely bragging by Michel about his Indian contacts and that Haschke tried to disassociate himself from the Briton.

Strongly denying any wrongdoing in the deal, Haschke also claimed to Indian interrogators in the court that no bribes were paid for the contract and that the money he received from AgustaWestland - in excess of 24 million euros - is justified as fees for engineering consultations.

Italian prosecutors also produced another note in court Thursday - a March 2008 fax by Michel to Peter Hulett, said to be the then head of region, govt sales at AgustaWestland's India office. The fax said that among the politicians who would use the choppers once acquired by India would be UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi and her senior advisors, including Ahmed Patel.

However, Sonia is not entitled to use government helicopters. She can use VIP aircraft only when she flies with the PM, President or ministers who are officially entitled to the aircraft. This fax by the British middleman has also been shared by the Italian side with the CBI team that is in Busto Arsizio for the hearing.

Michel has been elusive and no investigative agency has been able to reach him.

Haschke, who is facing a case in Italy for being part of a conspiracy to bribe Indian officials to ensure the AW 101 chopper was picked by the IAF, faced several questions from the Indian side and denied any irregularity.

But the Indian side did not ask Haschke to explain what AP, FAM or any of the other acronyms in the note - "DS", "JS AIR", "AFA", "DG Acquisition", CVC" etc - referred to, source said.

The middleman, who was quizzed about his association with former Air Chief S P Tyagi - named as an accused in the CBI case in the deal - denied that any money had been paid to the retired Indian officer. Haschke, sources said, admitted that he was in regular touch with three cousins of Tyagi who have also been named in the case.

In response to a question from the Indian side, Haschke said he was not aware if any money was paid to S P Tyagi.

The UPA government had come under pressure in connection with the alleged kickbacks last month after The Indian Express report on the budget sheet of the middlemen. The opposition BJP had demanded the government reveal what or who "AP" and "FAM" stand for. The party also said that it wants a detailed discussion in Parliament on "alleged payments to persons close to the ruling establishment" in connection with the controversial chopper deal and has accused the government of "running away from discussions".

The discussion did not take place as the Parliament session was abruptly called off midway.

Heading: 1,100 acres at Sanand cost Tatas over Rs 400 cr - Indian Express
Content:
Though the Gujarat government is still keeping the details of the agreement reached with Tata Motors for the Nano car plant under wraps, the abandoned deal that the Tatas had struck with West Bengal would clearly point at the possibility that the carmaker would be looking at significant sops in Gujarat. Before Ratan Tata's short-lived honeymoon with Singur ended and he shifted to Sanand, the group had also considered Uttarakhand and Himachal Pradesh to set up the plant.

Both these states had offered the Tatas substantial incentives. These include 100 percent Excise Duty exemption for 10 years and 100 percent Corporate Income Tax exemption for five years (followed by 30 per cent exemption for another five years), and a slew of intangible benefits.

West Bengal Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharya had, however, offered to match those incentives, while he wooed the Nano to Singur, at a Net Present Value of benefits pegged at 11 per cent. The Tatas were offered 997.11 acres of land in Singur, which included 645.67 acres for the mother plant, 290 acres for the project's vendors and 14.33 acres for power substations. It had kept aside another 47.11 acres for rehabilitating the farmers to be ousted to set up the plant.

The Singur land was to be leased to the Tatas for 90 years, not sold, and West Bengal had also agreed to revise terms and extend the lease thereafter. The state government agreed to a lease price of only Rs 1 crore per year for the 645.67 acres for the Nano mother plant for the first five years, followed by a 25 per cent hike on it every five years till 30 years. After 30 years, the lease rental was to be Rs 5 crore a year, which was to go up by 30 per cent every 10 years till the 60th year. Thereafter, the Tatas needed to pay up a consolidated Rs 20 crore a year until the lease expired on the 90th year.

The Tata-specified vendors were to pay Rs 8,000 per acre for the first 45 years and Rs 16,000 thereafter till the 90th year.

Buddhadeb had also offered to support the Tatas to pay up the term loan it would take for the project, in the form of assistance with the land costs and interest subsidies. The West Bengal Industrial Development Corporation was to provide annual loans equivalent to the VAT and CST the state government would get from the Tatas, at a notional 0.1 per cent interest. Going a step further, the government had also offered to pay a hefty penalty to the Tatas if it failed to provide this loan within 60 days of the end of each financial year at 1.5 times the prevailing bank rates for the delayed period. That apart, West Bengal had also offered to fork out a loan of Rs 200 crore to the carmaker at a nominal 1 per cent interest. The Tatas were required to begin paying back this loan in five equal annual instalments, beginning after 20 years. As for the power supply to the plant, the state government had offered it at a dirt cheap price of Rs 3 per KWH. In addition, the Tatas were also offered adequately more compensating sops in case this power tariff went up by more than 25 paise per KWH in every successive block of five years.

Heading: Farmers’ body moves HC against govt-Tata Nano deal - Indian Express
Content:
Sources say two-year moratorium given to auto giant during which it will not pay any instalment

The Narendra Modi government has reportedly provided a few concessions to Tata Motors in the sale of the land for the Nano car project, which is coming up near Sanand in Ahmedabad district.

At its weekly meeting held here on Wednesday, the state Cabinet fixed the cost of 1,100 acres of land at Rs 400.65 crore. The land rates were calculated at Rs 900 per sq metre.

There was no official press briefing on the Cabinet's decision, but later, the government issued a one-page statement saying that the land cost was fixed as per the existing rules after the due process was initiated by the district and the state-level land price committees.

Sources in the Chief Minister's Office (CMO), however, told Newsline that the government had decided to provide some concessions to the Tatas while fixing the land price.

Sources said it was decided to give a two-year moratorium to the auto company, where it would not have to pay any instalment for the land to the government. But the company would have to pay eight per cent interest on this during the moratorium period.

The government has also exempted Tata Motors from paying about five per cent stamp duty on the land transaction. The exemption of stamp duty if calculated at 5 per cent on the total land cost of over Rs 400 crore will benefit the company by about Rs 20 crore, sources added.

The government has also provided a facility to Tata Motors to make staggered payment towards the land cost in eight equal instalments in as many years, with eight per cent interest on it. In case the auto giant fails to pay regular instalments, it would have to pay compound interest rates on the payment.

A senior CMO official said that the government had turned down Tata Motors' demand for converting the 1,100 acres of land from a new tenure to old tenure. But the government has agreed to the company's suggestion to waive the conversion tax of Rs 6 per sq metre (which is usually charged for converting the agricultural land into non-agricultural one).

The official said that although the government did not accept Tata Motors' demand for converting the land into the old tenure one, it did agree to provide this facility for the company's prospective vendors who plan to set up their units at the plant site.

"The government would have no restrictions on the land, had it conceded Tata Motors' demand for converting it into the old tenure land," he explained.

The official said that the District-Level Price Committee (DLPC) had earlier fixed the land price rate at Rs 850 per sq metre, while it was fixed at Rs 880 per sq metre by the Chief Town Planner (CTP). But the Cabinet decided to keep the price a bit higher.

Within two days of signing a State Support Agreement with Tata Motors, the government had handed over an advance possession of the land to the former on October 9, the official said, adding that, "The eight per cent interest rate fixed on the payment of land cost comes into force from the day the land possession was handed over to the Tatas."

Meanwhile, the government has reportedly decided to allot nearly 2,200 acres of land to the Anand Agriculture University somewhere in Anand and Kheda districts in central Gujarat, in lieu of the Sanand land. The government had offered the land to the agriculture university near Khambhat, but the latter refused to shift its activity there, and insisted on the land allotment in Anand and Kheda districts, sources said.

Heading: Government staff to go on mass leave in protest - Indian Express
Content:
A gandhinagar-based activist, representing the Rashtriya Kisan Dal, filed a Public Interest Litigation in the Gujarat High Court on Wednesday, seeking termination of the agreement signed between Tata Motors and the state government for the Nano car plant at Sanand.

A Division Bench comprising Chief Justice K S Radhakrishnan and Aquil Qureshi, however, adjourned the matter for post-Diwali holidays, that is after November 9. The court asked petitioner H K Thakar to file the petition in English. The application submitted today was in Gujarati language and the Chief Justice, who belongs to Kerala, is not acquainted with the language.

The petition running into 14-pages, besides documents and evidences in support of the contention, also urged that no construction be allowed at the plant site in Chharodi village and no financial or subsidies be extended to the Tatas. It contended that big industries are not eligible for any kind of subsidy under the state government's new industrial policy adopted a year ago.

The petitioner pointed out that the government's decision to allot land to the Tatas at "throw-away prices" was in total violation of the rules and regulations. He said the land in question was acquired by the British government on a 90-year lease for agricultural purposes and for change of use, the government should have issued notices and given a chance to the original owners of the land to put forward their views on the issue. But it was directly allotted to the Tata Motors, thus "raising apprehension of some kind of scandal in the deal," he said.

He said that out of the1,100 acres, 645.2 acres have been allotted for the Nano car project on the basis of lease for 90 years at a total rent of Rs 96.72 crore. While the total cost of the project is Rs 1,500 crore, the farmers and the public exchequer will suffer a loss of Rs 1,799.95 crore by way of loss of crops worth Rs 209 crore, reduced compensation worth Rs 881.91 crore and loss of government revenue amounting to Rs 707 crore, he said. Besides tax exemption of Rs 400 crore, stamp duty loss of Rs 231.45 crore and loss of Rs 76.11 crore through subsidy will also be lost, he said. Accusing the government of "illegally transferring 1,555 acres of private land into its own possession," the petitioner pointed out that the Tatas had begun construction of an approach road without paying any compensation to the farmers.

He said the cost of land per acre in Gandhinagar is Rs 2.5 crore, Rs 75 lakh in Kutch, Rs 1 crore to Rs 1.5 crore in Surat/Vadodara and Rs 1 crore in Halol/Kalol, but the Tatas were allotted the land in Sanand, just 30 kms from Ahmedabad, at a rate of Rs 14 lakh per acre. Elsewhere, Reliance was allotted land for its Jamnagar Refinery at a rate of Rs 53.24 lakh per acre, he said.

"The whole thing hints at some kind of scandal. Hence, the government's decision to allot land to the Tatas deserves to be scrapped," the petition said. Thakar also raised the issue of electricity supply to the Nano plant. He said when the state is facing 34 per cent of power shortage, how will it supply it to the Tatas. If the state has adequate power to run the Nano project, then why enough power is not being supplied to the farmers, it asked. He further said the project was "anti-people" as it would hardly generate employment for 200-400 people.

The entire plant would be automatic and would not require much of labour, he said.

Heading: Small-time TV actor murdered - Indian Express
Content:
Anger against delay in implementation of pay panel's recommendations

Over eight lakh government employees across Gujarat will go on a day's mass casual leave on November 5, to protest against the government's delay in announcing the implementation of the Sixth Pay Commission's recommendations to hike employees' salaries.

"We have already served an ultimatum to the government that the employees will go on a mass CL on November 5. We have also decided to intensify our agitation if the government fails to make an announcement on the Commission's recommendations before Diwali," said Girish Raval, Convenor of the Gujarat Rajya Karmachari Mahamandal.

Raval told Newsline today that a five-member Cabinet sub-committee, set up to study the implications of the Commission's recommendations, had on Monday last, submitted its report to the government, suggesting that it could be implemented in the state.

Despite the "positive" report submitted by a sub-committee headed by Finance Minister Vajubhai Vala, the Modi government was dilly-dallying in announcing the implementation of the Commission's recommendations, he said.

The Mahamandal leader said that apart from the Central government, six other state governments had announced that they will implement the recommendations in toto. But, the Gujarat government continues to keep its employees on tenterhooks, he said.

The various government employees' bodies in the state expected that the government would take a decision on this issue at the weekly Cabinet meeting on Wednesday. But, the Cabinet failed to take a decision on this, causing a great deal of disappointment among lakhs of its employees, Raval said.

Meanwhile, a senior official in the state Finance Department said the government would have to entail an additional burden of about Rs 3,000 crore in the first year when it decides to implement the Commission's recommendations for its employees with retrospective effect from January 2006.

Later, the government would have to shoulder an additional burden of Rs 1,000 crore annually if the recommendations hiking the employees' salaries were implemented in toto, at par with the Central government employees, the official said.

There are over eight lakh government employees, including those serving in the state-owned Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) in Gujarat. Besides, there are over two lakh pensioners in the state, who will also benefit from the Sixth Pay Commission's recommendations.

Heading: Court reserves order for in-camera hearing till Oct 17 - Indian Express
Content:
A small-time actor, Sajid Altaf Ahmed, working in tele-serial Ramayana produced by NDTV Imagine, was murdered at the Sagar Studios on the city outskirts on Wednesday evening.

Ahmed was reportedly attacked by four unidentified men, dressed up in drama costumes, in the parking lot around 7 pm. They are said to have come on horses used for shooting. According to doctors, he died of a wound sustained near the neck.

Sajid, a resident of Sayajipura, played the role of a soldier in Ravana's army in the tele-serial. The Vadodara taluka police are investigating the case.

Heading: Tortured woman jumps to death in Tapi - Indian Express
Content:
The designated Metropolitan Court hearing the Ahmedabad blasts and Surat bombs cases, on Wednesday, reserved the order for the in-camera hearings of seven accused till October 17.

An application seeking in-camera hearings was moved by the Ahmedabad City Detection of Crime Branch (DCB) on October 8.

The court reserved its order following arguments by the defence against the application.

The application filed under Section 44 of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act had cited security reasons and protection of the identities of witnesses in the case as the reasons for the in-camera hearings.

Appearing for the state, special public prosecutor J M Panchal said that 'in-camera hearings were necessary because the blast case was at a very crucial stage and the security of both the accused and the people in the court was at stake'.

He said: "The accused are terrorists belonging to the SIMI. Investigations so far have shown that they may have links with the Lashkar-e-Toiba and the ISI.

All the bomb blasts have taken place at public places, and such an event can also happen in a courtroom, which is also a public place."

The special public prosecutor also said that in-camera proceedings were vital to protect the identities of the witnesses and also to stop the photographs of the accused from being released by the media.

The defence lawyers led by advocate Hashim Qureshi objected to the application on the grounds that it was pre-mature and that the Metropolitan Court had no jurisdiction to decide on the issue.

He said: "The present court does not come under the ambit of the definition of the court under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, and the law under which the in-camera application has been moved."

He added: "Only the trial court, which is the Sessions Court in this case, can take such a decision. At this stage, there is also no question of any witnesses being brought to the court."

Heading: 15 arrested in Nadiad for stone-pelting, rioting - Indian Express
Content:
Tortured for dowry and too scared to embrace 'halala' (marrying a man for a day), a 32-year-old woman jumped into the Tapi and committed suicide on September 27.

The body of Sakera Belim was fished out by the fire brigade officers near Chowpaty the next day. Her father lodged a complaint against her in-laws with the Rander police station on Tuesday.

Sakera married one Shaikh Arif, an employee of Gujarat Electric Company and a resident of Lunsikui area in Navsari, eight years ago.

After two years of happy marriage, Arif and his family started demanding dowry from her family. Initially, she fulfilled their demands. The dowry demands, however, kept on increasing with time.

Her father, Gulam Belim, an employee with the Western Railway, failed to fulfill these demands any longer. With this began Sakera's troubles. Her husband and in-laws started torturing her mentally and physically. Tormented, she returned to her parents' house in Surat with her son, Minaz, and lodged a dowry complaint against Arif and her in-laws with the Rander police station.

The police arrested Arif and his family. But, the matter was settled after a mutual understanding, and in 2005 Sakera returned to her in-laws' house.

After two years of peace, her in-laws again started torturing her when she refused to ask her parents for money to purchase a house.

On May 9, 2008, she was thrown out of her in-laws' house with a seven-year-old son and on May 11, Arif sent Sakera a divorce letter. Accepting the divorce, she underwent three months of Iddat.

As per Muslim rituals, after divorce, a woman must undergo Iddat and not meet anyone except her own family members.

But on September 21, Arif contacted her again. He wanted to re-marry her. But for this, Sakera would have to embrace 'halala' and marry another man.

The marriage must last one full day. Arif arranged for a man who would marry Sakera for a day.

But Sakera was too scared to enter into 'halala' and refused. Angry, Arif threatened to take her son away if she did not give a positive answer within eight days.

Unable to bear the onslaught, Sakera jumped into the Tapi and ended all her miseries.

Heading: Now, gold coins at 103 post-offices - Indian Express
Content:
At least 15 people were arrested on Wednesday following a fight over the parking of pushcarts in Saiyyadwada and Malikwada area of Nadiad town late on Tuesday.

According to the police, about 50 people from the two groups started pelting stones at each other before brandishing sharp weapons, around 10.30 pm, but the police soon brought the situation under control.

Nadiad police Sub-Inspector S N Bhagoda said there were complaints from both parties. "In the first complaint, one Mushtaq Vohra alleged that six people from Malikwada burnt his pushcart on Monday because they had parking problems. His water tank was also damaged in the fracas," said Bhagoda. The six accused are Kalu Hussain, Shahid Alam, Pervez Ahmed, Mukhtar Ahmed, Inayat Belim and Saqid Ansari.

A cross complaint filed by Inayat Belim named Vohra and 15 others as the accused.

Bhagoda said infighting among the two groups is not very typical in the area and they have arrested 15 people from both groups. He added: "This kind of fighting is not very typical in this area as Nadiad has been a peaceful place for both Hindus and Muslims."

Heading: IIM-A comes up with ‘cross-cultural course’ for senior executives, entrepreneurs - Indian Express
Content:
India Post on Wednesday introduced the sale of gold coins through 103 post-offices in Gujarat, Maharashtra, New Delhi and Tamil Nadu.

The 24-carat gold coins of 0.5gram, one gram, five grams and eight grams denominations will be sold at 29 post-offices in Ahmedabad, Vadodara and Surat.

It will be sold in collaboration with Reliance Money, a part of the Anil Dhirubhai Ambani Group.

"The reason for starting such a service is to make gold coins reach consumers with ease. The rate of gold changes several times in a day, but we have asked Reliance Money to keep one rate for the entire day which will benefit consumers," said D K S Chauhan, Chief Postmaster General (Business Development), Gujarat Circle, India Post.

The service is being started as pilot project for a period of three months. On the basis of the feedback, India Post will decide whether it will introduce the service in other areas or not.

Reliance Money will get the gold coins packed in a sealed cover with the certification from world recognised Swiss company Valcambi.

Chauhan said: "We joined hands with Reliance Money as they have provided sound service to their gold coins consumers in the past two years."

He added: "The current market of Reliance Money is Rs 150 crore in gold coins and bars per year which is expected to go up with the India Post tie-up. The gold coins from India Post will have internationally recognised and certified, low risk duplication, quality packing."

He further said: "Both India Post and Reliance Money did a market study before starting this service. Gold coins at many places have something or the other mixed in it. The shopkeepers cheat the consumer."

India Post is not planning to appoint additional staff for this service, but they believe the service will benefit everyone.

"We are working as networking partner with Reliance Money and are not planning any profit margin. But Reliance Money will be taking this as a profit generating service," he added.

Heading: Close shave for Chief Justice: Car rams into pilot jeep - Indian Express
Content:
The Indian Institute of Management, Ahmedabad (IIM-A) is all set to introduce a new course for senior managers of multi-national companies and entrepreneurs from next January. The programme will be launched in collaboration with the Duke University's Fuqua School of Business.

The programme will aim to "enhance the capabilities of leaders to innovate, succeed and grow their business in the global economy."

According to IIM sources, the course is also targeted at exploring "new models of organisation and leadership in an inter-connected world."

Keeping in mind the multi-cultural environment of the present day corporate world, the programme will also build the capacity of the participants in this direction.

Named the 'Global Leaders Programme: Growing and innovating in a flat world,' it is divided into two eight-day modules separated by a short inter-session.

The first module will be held at IIM-A, while the second one will be held at Duke University in Durham, North Carolina.

"With the global interest on the Indian economy rising, this is the right time to offer such cross-cultural courses," said IIM-A Director Samir Barua. "We are offering quite a few such courses. By doing this, we are not only exposing the Indian entrepreneurs and managers to the global scenario, but also helping the managers from other countries to understand the management scenario in the Indian socio-economic milieu," he added.

IIM-A faculty member Deepti Bhatnagar will coordinate the course at Ahmedabad, while S Vishwanathan will be doing the same at Durham.

The course fee is 21,000 dollars (Rs 10.2 lakh approx).

It may be noted that the IIM-A had tied up with the Fuqua School of Business to design open enrolment programmes for executive education for the global market in 2006.

Duke had preferred IIM-A over its Chinese counterparts due to a higher number of multi-national companies and a high standard of management education in India.

Heading: Police bust gang of extortionists - Indian Express
Content:
The Chief Justice of the Gujarat High Court, Justice K S Radhakrishnan had a close shave on Wednesday morning when his car met with an accident in the Sola area of the city.

The mishap took place on the Sola Bridge near the high court around 10.30 am, when Justice Radhakrishnan was on his way to the court from his residence at Judges Bungalow in Vastrapur. No one has been reported injured in the accident.

According to the Sola police, the pilot jeep, which was leading the Chief Justice's convoy, had to apply sudden brakes while descending the bridge. Justice Radhakrishnan's Corolla car, which was following it, rammed into the vehicle and suffered heavy damage. Inspector M P Vasava said, "Justice Radhakrishnan escaped unhurt and no police complaint was registered."

A sudden commotion ensued because of the accident and the traffic movement on the road was stopped for sometime. Some press photographers, who rushed to the site to take photographs of the broken car and Justice Radhakrishnan, were allegedly roughed up, and their cameras snatched by the policemen on duty.

A special high court vehicle was immediately rushed to the site to ferry Justice Radhakrishnan to the court.

Justice Radhakrishnan was sworn in as the Chief Justice of the Gujarat High Court on September 4 this year. Prior to this, he was the Chief Justice of the Jammu and Kashmir High Court.

Heading: Top cop gets tips from consumer council on traffic chaos - Indian Express
Content:
The Sardarnagar police on Wednesday busted a gang of cheaters who extorted money from various businessmen in Naroda, Kubernagar and Sardarnagar areas.

Two persons were arrested in this connection.

The arrests were made after three traders — Murali Gotwani, Sundar Ghachani and Anoop Sukhwani — from the Kubernagar area registered separate complaints against four persons on Monday night.

Three of the accused were identified as Bhavin Hariyani from Bhavnagar, Santosh Chauhan from Ghodasar and Lalji Barot from Vatva GIDC area. The identity of the fourth accused has not been established.

According to the police, the accused had approached the traders at their units posing as officers from the Consumer Defence Committee and Anti-Corruption Committee. They told the traders that they wanted to check the articles being manufactured in the units.

Later, they threatened the traders of framing them in police cases by branding the eatables produced in the units sub-standard. Following this, they demanded money to keep the matter under wraps.

Gotwani had paid Rs 10,000, Ghachani Rs 25,000 and Sukhwani Rs 1,500 to the four on October 10 and 11.

Later, the traders realised that they were cheated by the four and lodged a police complaint.

Inspector A S Rathod said: "The four are members of a well-organised gang which extorted money from traders in Naroda, Kubernagar and Sardarnagar areas in the last few days."

He added: "At least five more traders have come forward as witnesses against the two accused who have been arrested. Investigations are on to trace the other two members of the gang."

Heading: Brothers kill man over property issue - Indian Express
Content:
The Consumer Protection Council (CPC) has submitted 10 suggestions to the City Police Commissioner to reduce the traffic chaos in the city.

K H Kaji, Chairman of the Consumer Protection Council, said, "As citizens, we are appalled by the traffic chaos in the city, particularly in the western part of Ahmedabad."

He added: "In a memo, we have asked the police to check the traffic jams, both major and minor, which mostly occur as car and bike drivers do not follow the basic rules of driving and of giving way. Bikes overtake or cut across the road from the wrong side in a very reckless manner and at high speeds."

He further said that for some "unknown reasons", most of the traffic lights don't work or show blinking yellow lights most of the times. "In the memo, we have requested that all traffic lights should function throughout the day and night, at least from 7 am to 10 pm with break," he said.

He said they have also asked him to check the way the bus drivers of the Ahmedabad Municipal Transport Service (AMTS) and the Gujarat State Road Transport Corporation (GSRTC) drive the vehicles. "Even the private tourist bus drivers are frequent violators. They drive recklessly, resulting in serious accidents," said Usha Sanghavi, Secretary, CPC.

R U Jani, Joint Secretary, CPC said: "We have also pointed out in the memo that the traffic lanes should be demarcated 100 yards before the crossroads and no car, bike or autorickshaw should be allowed to turn or violate their respective lane. Breaking the lane and cutting across traffic create jams and pose the risk of serious accidents."

Jani added: "As of now, the policemen are replaced with traffic posts at regular intervals. We have asked for the policemen not to be overburdened and exposed to heat or rain for long. Replacements should be there on suitable intervals. In the past also we have submitted such memos and steps were taken on them by the respective departments. So, we hope this time also they will take action soon."

Heading: Forty food poisoning cases reported in Vadodara village - Indian Express
Content:
After losing a property suit in a civil court, two brothers eliminated their youngest brother by giving a supari of Rs 5,000 in Ramol on Tuesday night. The Ramol police have registered a case of murder and arrested three persons in this connection.

The deceased has been identified as Mansukh Patel (49), a resident of Suraj Bungalows in the CTM area. The accused have been identified as Raghav Patel from Khokhra, Shambhu Patel from Isanpur and Bhikhabhai Gadhvi from Maninagar. Gadhvi was given the supari to kill Mansukh.

Some unidentified persons attacked Mansukh with a sharp-edged weapon near the Ahmedabad-Vadodara Express Highway on Tuesday night when he was taking a stroll after dinner, the police said.

Inspector K M Jadeja, who is investigating the case, said: "He sustained a major stab injury in the back and died on the spot."

Heading: Cop faces arrest for assaulting city-based family - Indian Express
Content:
At least 40 cases of food poisoning were reported from Kothara village in Dabhoi taluka of Vadodara district on Wednesday.

Six people, including five children, have been admitted to the SSG hospital in Vadodara.

The condition of the children is now stable, said doctors at the hospital. According to reports, the affected people had consumed a dudh-pauva at a community dinner organised in their village on the occasion of Sharad Purnima on Tuesday night.

"The cases of vomiting and diarrhoea started coming in from Wednesday afternoon. By evening, 40 people were admitted to the local government hospital," said Dr Dilip Vora, Superintendent, Dabhoi Civil Hospital.

Six people, who were severely affected, were referred to the SSG hospital. They are Khumansinh Baria (35), Deepika Vasacva (2), Mukesh Jain (1), Vidhya Vasava (5), Nehal Vasava (2) and Tejal Rathod (4).

Heading: Woman, six-month-old daughter succumb to burn injuries - Indian Express
Content:
Padara police station inspector Janak Sarvaiya is facing arrest following charges of assault, harassment and issuing life threat to a city-based family.

Sarvaiya, who had earlier created controversy by refusing to file a dowry complaint, allegedly barged into the house of Rajendra Patel on Sunfarma Road with his men and beat up Patel's young son, Anuj and wife Meena on October 13. Following the incident, Patel filed an FIR with the J P Road police station.

According to J P Road police station officers, Sarvaiya misused his powers to settle his personal scores with Anuj, a student of Vasad Engineering College, on behalf of his son's friends.

During college elections, Anuj reportedly had worked for the group, which was contesting against the group supported by Sarvaiya's son.

"Sarvaiya will be arrested soon. We have evidence to prove that Sarvaiya assaulted the boy and his mother at their residence," said J P Road Inspector A M Patel.

The officer added that the Patels have submitted a video clipping in which Sarvaiya is seen beating Anuj. "The process of evidence collection and verification is on," he said.

Sarvaiya is facing charges of assault, forced entry and giving life threats under Sections 452, 323, 504 and 506(2) of the Indian Penal Code (IPC).

In his complaint, Rajendra Patel said that Sarvaiya, one Kamal and some other people barged into their home on October 13 and started beating up Anuj.

According to the complaint, when Meena tried to pacify Sarvaiya, he beat her up too. He left the house after issuing threats to everyone.

On Tuesday, North Zone DCP B K Shirmani provided police protection to the Patel family.

"Though no special protection cover has been provided, a team has been deputed to do patrolling at their house on regular intervals," said Inspector Patel.

Heading: ‘Religious sects hampering anti-dengue drive in city’ - Indian Express
Content:
A 24-year-old woman and her six-month-old daughter died at the SSG Hospital after sustaining severe burn injuries, on Wednesday. Her second daughter, who was also severely injured, survived and is receiving treatment at the burns ward.

According to the Padra police, the incident took place on Tuesday afternoon at Luna village in Padra taluka of Vadodara.

The police said that the neighbours noticed flames coming out of the house

of Sushma Toyar. They rushed to the house and found the woman and her two daughters — Lali and two-year-old Ranu — lying severely burnt.

The three were immediately taken to the hospital where Lali and Sushma breathed their last.

Sub-Inspector K Jadeja said the incident occurred when Sushma's husband Subhas, who works as a fireman with a local chemical factory, was on duty.

"The postmortem and the FSL reports are awaited. On the basis of the preliminary investigation, the possibility of mass suicide cannot be ruled out," said Jadeja.

The police, however, could not ascertain any reason to support the suicide theory. "The couple was living peacefully," said the investigating officer.

Questioning her family members also did not point towards any reason that could have forced the woman to take the extreme step, Jadeja said.

"According to her brother, she was treated well by other family members, including her in-laws," said the police.

Subhas belongs to Madhya Pradesh and has been working in Vadodara for nearly six years.

Heading: Skywalk to ease traffic flow at railway station - Indian Express
Content:
One more case of dengue detected even as VMC tries to join hands with NGOs to make people aware about importance of anti-larval procedures

One more dengue case has been detected in the city and surprisingly the situation seems to be nowhere near control. One noteworthy factor that prevents health workers from taking up anti-larval procedures is a few religious sects that disapprove of the measures due to religious sentiments.

A new case was reported on Wednesday morning, wherein 33-year-old Sakina Motorwala of Bahar Colony from Ajwa tested positive for dengue. Four children, Keta Shah (13), Jayanti Shah (15), Manav Shah (8) and Bhoomi Shah (12) were tested positive for the disease last week.

Health officials revealed that though necessary precautions are taken, health workers undertaking fogging and other anti-larval measures in certain areas of the city are severely restricted by some religious communities.

"People have to be extra cautious within the house, as most of the dengue cases arise due to stagnant water. Some of the religious groups stop us from carrying out anti-larval procedures because of their religious sentiments," said an official on condition of anonymity.

VMC Health Committee Chairman Hitendra Patel said religious sentiments do come in the way while carrying out anti-dengue drives. "Some sects believe in Ahimsa, while others think that killing insects is a sin. Such beliefs hamper fogging and other precautionary measures," he said.

He added: "People do not keep their interiors clean and overlook places within the house which are susceptible to the vector borne disease. We are now trying to team up with NGOs to make people aware about the importance of anti-larval procedures."

Apart from the religious sects, health officials are restricted by the general public as well. "On several occasions, our health officers are not allowed to enter the buildings at all. Due to this, the susceptible areas in the houses and overhead water tanks are left out, giving rise to more dengue cases," said Dr. Dilip Asari, Health Officer, VMC.

Heading: Woman accuses in-laws of torture - Indian Express
Content:
The city is all set to get its first skywalk to ease the traffic congestion at the Vadodara railway station area. The project is the result of a joint effort by the Vadodara Municipal Corporation (VMC), Western Railway, the City Police Department and the Traffic Police.

But the VMC will not have to incur any cost at all. Municipal Commissioner M K Das said: "This will completely be on a BOD (Build-Operate and Transfer) basis and the contractor will incur the cost involved in the construction which they will recover from advertisements. The VMC will monitor the safety aspect of the structure."

The process of clearing out the traffic had already started at the railway station as part of the safety measures after the Ahmedabad bomb blasts. The skywalk will be an extension to decongest the traffic. The structure will connect the railway station to the VTCOS bus stand, passing over the road.

Das said: "This is a kind of pilot project that we are doing. If it is successful in bringing down the traffic in the area, we plan to put up more such skywalks in other areas as well." He said the VMC has also invited tenders for the same.

Meanwhile, the entry and exit points at the railway station have already been altered to ease off the traffic coming from Alkapuri.

"As per the direction of the city police, we have also introduced the stop and go system for vehicles at the station. All vehicles are now parked 50 metres away from the premises. Passengers from the railway station take a public transport that is on the other side of the road. So, the skywalk will enable the people to reach the place without having to face the traffic," said Suhas Kumar, DRM.

Along with the skywalk, the road at the area will also be widened to facilitate the free flow of traffic for which the garden in the railway station premises will be cut down.

"Now with the stop and go system, the garden will be made smaller by giving away a part of the parking area. Dividers and railings on the road will be constructed and the area will be broadened to decongest the traffic," said Kumar.

Heading: Green piece - Indian Express
Content:
A woman has filed a complaint with the Makarpura police station, accusing her in-laws of regularly beating her for the last seven years for not paying dowry.

The police said Saruchi Sharma filed the complaint on Monday night after escaping from her in-laws' house at Manjalpur.

The police said the woman's husband Parag Sharma, mother-in-law Hema and aunt Bharti Sharma, residents of Laxmidham Society, would gag her every day.

The victim was also tied and beaten up with an iron rod inside a chamber and was not allowed to speak to her parents, they said.

On Monday, when the family went out for dinner, Saruchi managed to open the door of the chamber and came to the Makarpura police station.

She is now with her parents who stay at Sundervan Society in Makarpura.

Heading: Glow of dusk! - Indian Express
Content:
Eco-chic is in & here's how you can be earth-friendly

It's a wave that's driven less by fashion and more by feelings. Food, bags, clothing, gifts...eco-friendly alternatives are everywhere and being lapped up by not only those who have a concern for the environment, but believe in going natural. Of course, banning polythene in the city has prompted many to put on their green caps and go creative.

For one, paper's what everyone is looking towards for initiating the drive. Nods Poonam Thakur of Khadi Plus, who is busy thinking of some funky ideas for paper bags for the store and also shows you around the all-new natural ensembles which are high on looks and make ideal gifts, especially this festive season. "Natural products are our mainstay, be it chemical and scent-free soaps, cosmetics and now even sweets, which come loaded with natural ingredients like honey almonds et al and are packed as lovely gift items too,'' Poonam recommends the latest designer stoles, hand-spun and made from all natural materials.

At Good Beginnings too, street children are learning environmental creative art from their teacher and 'creative head' Sangeeta Vardhan, who has designed eco-friendly block-printed reusable bags and also cloth bags made from left-over threads, old clothes, trimmings et al, "some of these are embroidered, look trendy and are so practical and we can hopefully wean people off leather too,'' all these along with "can tab" bracelets, kurtas etc will be sold by children to help them earn a living and make people more conscious. "And you can spread the word by gifting these too,'' she smiles.

At theTheatre Age, work's on full swing to make bags from old newspapers and in various sizes. General stores, vegetable vendors, boutiques, Zulfikar Khan is now planning to also get children to do cloth bags, "serves the dual purpose of earning a living and saving the environment.'' At Fabindia there's a huge collection of jute and bamboo bags, and also natural wrapping paper, papier-mache products, while Anokhi stocks funky cotton bags with Rajasthani prints. Natural oils, aroma essences, natural fruits, vegetables growing in the Arya Vihar Ashram are used to produce Sundaram soaps and face washes that are being promoted here for all the right reasons. "Life of yoga is more than economy and and we want to reach out to larger sections,'' says an ashram representative. Go green!

Heading: In Manimajra, hygiene, traffic suffer courtesy kabari market - Indian Express
Content:
'It's the perfect time to be in Bollywood,' feels Sayali Bhagat

Five years back she would have thought twice about doing films, but today model-turned-actor Sayali Bhagat is confident that she is at the right place at the right time. "The times when movies sold on sex and a huge star cast are history, Bollywood is undergoing phenomenal change and I'm lucky that I have arrived in this phase," smiles the dusky beauty, in town for the launch of a jewellery store. Dressed in a magenta suit, Bhagat keeps her best friends close to her skin, "diamonds are such a weakness, though I prefer simple jewellery," she twinkles. Post the Miss India crown, films were a natural transition for Bhagat since, "modelling became so repetitive. Moreover, films pay more vis-a-vis modelling and every project is an opportunity for new experiences and lessons." So after The Train, a song in Halla Bol, a film in Tamil and Telugu each, Bhagat's on a high. "I am glad I haven't done conventional roles, stereotypes restrict an actor's growth. I have the option to choose my films and I am picking the most varied of scripts." The lady does hope to be chosen by Madhur Bhandarkar, Sudhir Misra and Shyam Benegal. Next she will be seen in Subhash Ghai's Paying Guest with Celina Jaitely, Riya Sen and Neha Dhupia as her co-stars. But when do we see her as the leading lady? "Soon in Shout, a horror film, and Newton's Third Law." And as is the law of journos we move to an important point, her relationship with Pakistani cricketer Shoaib Malik. "Media loves to replace 'like' with 'love', there's nothing between us other than friendship," she clears the air adding the typical celeb favourite "We are just good friends." Anything you say lady!

Heading: Civic body gives nod to various projects in southern sectors - Indian Express
Content:
A kabari market, located few metres from the road leading to the IT Park, has been causing trouble to the residents of Manimajra. The large amount of polythene and plastic material present at the site has forced these residents to write to the authorities, but to no avail. The market came into existence nearly a decade ago and covers a large area at present.

Ajay Pal Singh, a resident of the area says, "Polythene carry bags may have been banned in the rest of the city, but they are available in this market. The plastic material is often burnt, thereby releasing poisonous gases which pollute the area."

Another resident complains, "Hundreds of labourers have started working in the area and their identity is unknown. It is a security hazard. Several thefts have taken place in the area. Even the police have failed in protecting the property of the residents."

Also, the approach road to the area is narrow and with a large number of vehicles, including trucks and canters operating here, traffic jams become inevitable.

Gurdev Singh, another resident, claims to own the land on which the market has come up. He, however, says that despite making efforts to get the land vacated, he has not succeeded.

The officials, meanwhile, maintained that the issue would be resolved at the earliest.

Heading: Sector-36 residents irked over pits dug up to lay pipelines - Indian Express
Content:
A delegation of the office bearers of the Chandigarh Social Welfare Council met UT Advisor Pardeep Mehra and apprised him of the hardships faced by the residents of the southern sectors of Chandigarh.

The council had demanded the development of markets in the D-Segment of third phase of the sectors, which was agreed to. It was decided that the Shop-cum-Office(SCO)/booth sites in sectors 48, 49, 50 and 51 would be put to auction before March 31. The necessary development works and zoning will be completed within a period of two months.

The Director of Health Services will be preparing a scheme for the construction and running of the healthcare centres in these sectors on a public-private partnership (PPP) mode immediately as sites have already been earmarked.

Regarding development of schools, it was stated that the earmarked sites already have the approvals of the Administration and the UT Finance department had to submit approvals for the release of funds.

A site for police station will also be earmarked in Sector-49 D and another site for building housing complex for some police personnel will also be earmarked soon.

The Chief Engineer of the Municipal Corporation (MC) has been asked to take care of streetlights in Sector 50 and other phase III sectors as electricity poles have already been transferred to MC. The green belts in these sectors would be handed over to the MC for development and maintenance. The work of building community centres would also be expedited.

As far as inclusion of names in the electoral rolls is concerned, the DC-cum-District Election Officer said that although a fresh survey will not be possible at this stage, the eligible persons can apply during October/November 2008.

The Chief Architect was instructed to spare one SCO in each sector for setting up of e-sampark centre. Also Sehaj Safai Kendra would be set up in each sector.

The delegation was led by S S Bhardwaj, co-Chairman, and Satish Chandra Sharma, General Secretary of the Chandigarh Social Welfare Council. Bhardwaj stated that the announcements come as a victory for the council, which has been taking up the problems time and again.

Heading: State Bank of India staff calls indefinite strike from October 20 - Indian Express
Content:
The laying of the storm water drainage pipes has spelled woes for the residents of Sector 36. The pits, dug up outside a few houses, have made the entry and exit cumbersome.

Supmeet, a resident of the area, says that the work had started a week ago. "Gradually it is spreading from one corner to the other. This makes it difficult for us to park our vehicles. Some vehicles are stuck inside and cannot be taken out. The pits are deep and lead to accidents," she adds.

The residents also complained that the electricity and telephone connections have been disrupted at some places, owing to the digging of the earth.

"Though we got the electricity connection repaired, the work needs to be completed at the earliest, as it is causing inconvenience for the residents," says another resident.

An official of the Municipal Corporation said the work for laying the storm water drainage system will be completed in a week. This will reduce the problem of waterlogging faced during the rains.

While claiming that the digging work is being carried out on MC-owned land, the official alleged that people have extended their driveways and gardens onto the MC land.

Heading: PF stuck for 14 years, employer to pay up Rs 25,000 as compensation - Indian Express
Content:
The All India State Bank Officers' Federation (AISBOF) today declared the launch of an indefinite strike from October 20, in response to the failure of the government to fulfill their long pending demands. This will be the second strike by the federation this year after the one-day strike on August 18.

Their demands include improvement in pension scheme, extension of superannuation benefits available at the State Bank of India (SBI) and implementation of various understandings reached with the Federation from 2005 onwards. They are opposing the merger of Associate Banks with the SBI; opposition to the merger of the State Bank of Saurashtra (SBS) with the SBI and parity in superannuation benefits between the SBI and the Associate Banks' Officers.

The Labour Commission at Mumbai, meanwhile, has called a meeting between the State and Associate Banks' management and the general secretaries of the bank unions on Thursday, to sort the issue.

Vijay Magon, state secretary, All India State Bank Officers' Confederation, said: "Tomorrow's meeting will decide on the strike. It has been called to see what proposals the management accepts."

The State Bank of India, meanwhile, in a statement issued today, said it will join the call of strike given by the All India State Bank Officers' Federation on October 20.

Heading: Deep pits in Sec 17 an open invitation to disaster - Indian Express
Content:
The District Consumer Redressal Forum has directed the Semiconductor laboratory, department of Space, Government of India, Mohali, to pay Rs 25,000 as compensation to an employee for holding back his provident fund (PF) for 14 years. They have also been directed to pay Rs 3,500 as litigation expenses.

It was alleged that the Semiconductor laboratory was the "parent employer" of the complainant Narasimhan Gangavaram since March, 1984, and the complainant was drawing his salary with all the other benefits from them.

All the deductions towards the contributory provident fund were made by them till September, 1992, from the basic pay and then the total amount was deposited by the parent employer in the provident fund account.

It was averred that side by side, the complainant was also commissioned with the Additional Directorate General, Territorial Army,

It was added that in 1992, a letter, for relieving the complainant of his services, was written to his parent employer by the Territorial Army Group. After an inquiry report was submitted, he was relieved from his services with the Semicondauctor laboratory.

The complainant averred that instead of communicating the calculated deducted amount towards the provident fund to the Territorial Army, as per Section 7-B of Territorial Army Act 1948, his parent employer sent a vague reply for the same.

Thereafter till April, 2006, a lot of correspondence was made between the two employers and in the process the complainant's PF was not settled.

Semiconductor laboratory, in their reply, said that they made every effort in asking the Territorial Army to remit the amount along with the employer's contribution in order to safeguard the interest of the complainant.

The forum, however, found the company guilty of sleeping over the matter.

Heading: Admissions of 30 students cancelled who failed to get cut-off marks - Indian Express
Content:
The Chandigarh Municipal Corporation (MC) has not learnt any lessons from the recent incident of the death of a two-year-old in Agra.

Sonu had died after falling into an abandoned 150-ft deep pit while playing and remained there for four days before being pulled out dead.

The situation in the city is no different. Deep pits have been dug up at various places in Sector 17 for laying pipes.

With no signs to warn people of the danger, the pits are an open invitation for disasters to happen.

Pits cover most of the area in the market near the General Post Office. The situation is particularly critical at nights due to the absence of streetlights.

"The pits were dug up a few days ago. No warning signs were put to inform people of the danger. The situation is especially dangerous for children; even animal can fall in," said a shopkeeper of the area.

S S Pannu, a resident of Sector 9, said: "I was passing through the area and saw these huge pits. I was shocked to learn that these pits have been left open so blatantly. The authorities should not be so negligent and action should be taken soon."

An civic official said work on these pits has just been started and it would take a couple of days to complete it. The Plaza is being extended and this is a part of the upgradation proposal.

Heading: Solid waste management in Chandigarh impresses expert from Netherlands - Indian Express
Content:
The future of more than 30 Class XI students, who had taken admission in various government schools, across the city, now stands uncertain owing to the carelessness of the Education department. They have now been asked to change their stream after the authorities realised that their scores had not met the cut-off marks for admission to the courses of their choice.

The students had taken admission in the streams of their choice and now, after attending class for a week, they have been asked to change their stream as they had not met the required cut-off.

"I took admission in Information Technology, which is a vocational course. While my aggregate in Class X was 57 per cent, the required cut-off was 62 per cent. The officials in the admission committee did not tell me about this and gave me admission," said Prakash Jha, a student of Government Model Senior Secondary School, Sector 33. "The school authorities have now asked me to either change my stream or leave the school. I am not even allowed to attend classes," he added.

The schools have asked these students to stop attending classes till they have changed their stream. "They should have been more careful at the time of admission. I always wanted to study electronics but now my career is at stake as almost half the session is over and seats in most schools are filled," said another student.

Taking note of the discrepancy, Samwartak Singh, Director Public Instructions (Schools) said the future of the students is of prime importance.

"We are looking into the matter and will come up with the best possible solution. Their right to study will not be violated," he added.

Heading: Members take PUSC to the doorstep of students - Indian Express
Content:
"Chandigarh has a well-developed solid waste management system. There could be improvements in the process of segregation of waste," said Theo Folmer, a Dutch expert, while speaking at a seminar, organised by the Rotary District 3080 on 'Rotary's Strategy to Address Environmental Concerns' on Wednesday.

Folmer is part of the four-member expert team that visited different cities and towns of North India — Shimla, Saharanpur, Panipat, Yamunanagar and Jagadhri ¿ and reviewed the situation of waste management at these places. They would submit their reports soon.

The four — Theo Folmer, Pieter Hilbrand, Joseph van Oudenhoven and Geert Boonzaaijer — have come as part of the Netherlands Senior Experts Programme (PUM), which is an independent Dutch organisation that provides specialists for working on voluntary basis in the field of agriculture, trade, industry, healthcare, private, public and state managed sectors.

Folmer explained that Chandigarh has an organised system where garbage is collected from different households and then taken to a common collection centre where it is segregated. Finally it is taken to the management plant and processed. He suggested that paper, glass and metals should be segregated before processing.

He also visited the PGI and the Institute of Dental Sciences in Panjab University and would be touring Mohali on Thursday.

Joseph van Oudenhoven, who visited Kufri, said: "For Kufri, it is a question of survival. The view from the place is beautiful if you ignore where you are standing. There is a need to improve community participation. There is no need to depend on the government. People talk of water conservation when the taps are constantly leaking," he said.

Pieter Hilbrand, who visited Saharanpur and Haridwar, said, "Haridwar is swarming with tourists. But there is filth all around. Not even a single dustbin can be found. However, what is encouraging is the small initiatives taken by NGOs as well as individuals for waste management."

Geert Boonzaaijer, who toured Panipat, Yamunanagar and Jagadhri, stated that landfilling is a major problem. The workers segregate waste with bare hands which should not be done, said Boonzaaijer, while adding, "At places I saw people being trained for garbage collection. This creates employment opportunities and should be encouraged. We are taking back the samples of compost being prepared. These would be studied in the lab."

Heading: Selection of site for court complex in Mohali resumes after two years - Indian Express
Content:
Members of the Panjab Univeristy Students' Council (PUSC) today launched a campaign titled 'student council at your doorstep'. Under this, members will approach students individually and inquire about the problems being faced by them in the campus.

The students will also be asked to fill feedback forms, asking them to give their opinion about council members, their views on academics, infrastructure and hostel facilities among others.

They have also decided to install drop boxes in different departments, where students can drop their complaints.

Talking to Newsline, Brinder Dhillon, president, SOPU said: "The aim of the student council is to reach every student in the campus and take care of any problems being faced by them. We shall leave no stone unturned and will help students in every possible way."

The council has also chalked out a schedule of activities, which they will carry out in the next few days. As per schedule, the members will cover Arts Block I and II and two girls' hostels on Thursday.

Sahil Nanda, president, Students' Council, said: "We have decided to ask students for their suggestions about what they want from the council. This is for the first time that any council has taken an initiative of visiting the students and asking them about their grievances."

The members will be accompanied by Dean Students' Welfare (Women) Nishta Jaswal and Dean Student Welfare Professor Naval Kishore.

Sahil Nanda added: "We want to be a council with a difference and that is why, we are aiming to reach every student at personal level. I am sure that this process will work."

Heading: City Beautiful gears up to meet Tagore Theatre in its new avatar - Indian Express
Content:
Locations in Sectors 76, 84, 87 and 81 under active consideration

After 30 months of Mohali becoming a district, the process to select a suitable site for the District Administrative and Court Complex (DACC) has begun once again.

Despite tall claims of the ruling SAD President Sukhbir Badal of transforming Mohali into a satellite district, Mohali is without a court complex.

After abandoning four sites earmarked and recommended for the DACC, four new sites are under consideration for the much-awaited project. All the new sites were located within Mohali city unlike the previous three sites, which were in the villages on the outskirts in Mohali.

Making another bid to finalise the DACC site, Mohali Deputy Commissioner Rahul Bhandari and Greater Mohali Area Development Authority (GMADA) Chief Administrator (CA) Vivek Partap Singh took along Justice Surya Kant of the Punjab and Haryana High Court to inspect the newly found sites in Sector 76, 84, 87 and near the Knowledge City in Sector 81.

Bhandari told Newsline that as per the preliminary drawing prepared by Punjab Chief Architect, at least 13 acres of land was required for housing both the administrative and judicial wings of the district administration in a joint complex without provision of residential accommodations. "Once the High Court gives its consent to any suitable site, I will move the case afresh to Punjab Chief Secretary for their final nod to start the work on the project."

GMADA CA Singh said though no formal request from state government or offer from the GMADA was made yet for any chunk of land required or available for DACC. But in view of the public cause, the new sites were inspected and even possibilities of acquiring requisite land in the upcoming sectors were explored.

After the visit, Justice Surya Kant said he has sought certain information regarding the sites and after which, he will submit a report to the High Court Building Committee, which will take the final decision on the site selection. Agreeing that the project was already over delayed, Justice Surya Kant added that the high court will soon finalise the site to start work on it.

In the absence of the DACC, the district civil, police and judicial officials lack permanent official and residential accommodation.

While the district civil and police wings are temporarily working from the old building of the Punjab School Education Board (PSEB) in Phase I, the district judicial courts are working from a community centre in Phase 3B1. Also, some community centres have been occupied to house police lines and a police station.

A 22-acre plot in Saneta village and another 3.83-acre site in Sector 62 were earlier earmarked for the DACC but due to certain reasons, both these sites were rejected. Later, two other sites in Barmajra and Balongi villages were recommended, but bth were rejected by the state government.

Former Punjab Chief Minister Captain Amarinder Singh had laid foundation stone of the complex in Sector 62 while inaugurating the district on April 14, 2006. Ironically, even the foundation stone has gone missing from the site.

The 3.83-acre in Sector 62 site was abandoned as it was "insufficient" in view of the High Court Building Committee norms, where it is stated that at least 16 acre is required for such a complex.

Heading: Beautification drive: Panchkula bus stand to don a new look by Nov - Indian Express
Content:
Come October 25 and the city will see the 1960-built Tagore Theatre in an all new look. After being shut down for over a year for renovation, the theatre will now be equipped with the best air-conditioning facilities, different colour scheme, better greenrooms and a spacious stage, besides an increased seating capacity to accommodate nearly 800 people.

The UT Home Secretary Ram Niwas had inspected the ongoing renovation work at the theatre on Tuesday and announced the fresh deadline. "We hope to inaugurate the theatre by October 25," said UT Home Secretary Ram Niwas.

Interestingly, the Administration had failed to inaugurate the same on the earlier fixed date of September 27, the World Tourism Day. The theatre has been renovated at a cost of nearly Rs 5.36 crore under the guidance of an architectural firm — Satnam Namita and Associates — who were appointed as consultants for the project. While even after the renovation, the outer facade of the theatre, created by P Jeanneret and Aditya Prakash, has been retained, the entry to the theatre would now be through a swanky glass door.

For better viewing from even the extreme corners of the theatre, the stage has been given a shift of 180 degrees. While the seats have been changed from the old chair-type to cushioned chairs, the entire floor has also been carpetted. Even the colour scheme in the theatre hall has been changed. "The greenroom's renovation, such as changing the colour scheme shall be done after the theatre is inaugurated," added Niwas.

On the other hand, the Administration is also all set to inaugurate the lake in Sector 42 by the end of the month, which would be open to the public for performing religious ceremonies.

Heading: Festive Fair - Indian Express
Content:
High Five
In yet another high score, the 'Chak De India', after having swept India, UK and the US, have now set their eyes on winning over Japan. The film has been invited to be a part of the 21st Tokyo International Film Festival, to be held in Tokyo from the October 18th - 26th 2008. The Tokyo International Film Festival is one of Asia's most prominent and vibrant film festivals. It is known for showcasing alternative cinema from all corners of the globe. 'Chak De India' will be showcased in the Winds of Asia-Middle East section. This section features the best films from East Asia, South East Asia, South Asia and the Middle East.
