This year's edition of the Tokyo International Film Festival is as comprehensive as ever, featuring 790 films from 72 countries in competitive section plus special sections devoted to world cinema Japanese cinema and many more. Other than Rajnikanth films, not many Indian movies have succeeded in this festival. Says Shimit Amin, the director, "We are truly honoured. It's a pat on the back for everyone associated with this film." Chak De!

Matter of Faith
NOT many know, but this Friday will also see the release of Provoked's director Jag Mundhra's Shoot On Sight. Produced by Aron Govil Productions, the film has an impressive starcast including veterans Naseerudin Shah, Om Puri and Gulshan Grover, and English actors Greta Scacchi, Brian Cox, Laila Rouass and Sadie Frost. All set to roll in theatres on October 17 in Hindi and English, the film is a thriller based on the July 7, 2005 bombings in London. It's a gripping family drama that unfolds the turmoil in the life of Tariq Ali (Naseerudin), a Muslim police officer at Scotland Yard. Commander Ali, born in Pakistan, married to an English woman, is tasked to investigate the police shooting of a suspected Muslim terrorist on the London Underground. Distrusted by both his British superiors in the London police, and his fellow Muslims, he finds his inquiry hampered from all sides. "I am not trying to appease the fundamentalists...I made the film because after the bombings, I was in London and I noticed that my looks went against me, probably because I have a beard and I resemble a Muslim. I couldn't even get a taxi back to my apartment," says Jag Mundhra. Watch out.

Heart & soul
KARZZZZ is a tribute to Anand Bakshi, says lyricist Sameer adding how he drew inspiration from Anand Bakshi, his mentor, while penning the songs for Karzzzz. "Himesh and I had formed a team. I did some of my finest and the most popular work for him from 'Tere Naam' to 'Aap Kaa Surroor'. But now that he has decided to compose only for his own movies, I have been forced to slow down," Sameer's writing the lyrics for Himesh's upcoming films - Kajra Re and A Love Ssssshtory. "Karzzzz is based on a theme of revenge which is not at all a soft theme, so writing romantic songs for this film was the biggest challenge. Every musical composition bears certain energy, a vibration and a life of its own; I had to drill down for words to create a romantic song. It was very difficult to write down songs for Karzzzz but, I would give the credit to my inspiration Anand Bakshi whom I consider as my guide." His other upcoming works are Golmaal Returns, Do Knot Disturb and Houseful.

Grab your copy
Bachna Ae Haseeno VCD has been recently released under the YRF Home Entertainment label and is now available for all film lovers who can go and get their copies to add to the collection of their favourite films. Starring Ranbir Kapoor, Bipasha Basu, Deepika Padukone and Minnisha Lamba, the film did fantastically well on the BO with its fresh treatment, vibrant performances and sunny locales. Directed by Siddharth Anand with foot tapping music by Vishal & Shekhar, Bachna Ae Haseeno is still running in the theatres. For those who prefer to buy the DVD, wait till the end of October for the same. In the meanwhile, the VCD is out.

The Devil wears Greene
AS a fictional Bolivian eco-resort hits the big, action-packed screen this November, James Bond's newest nemesis, Dominic Greene, the evil faux environmentalist, springs to life, using his Greene Planet Hotel to distract people from his schemes to seize valuable water resources in South America. Taking a detour from the typical Bond villains, Quantum of Solace shows the powerful who profess to have environmental credentials even as they pollute the earth and pillage natural resources. On his character, Dominic Greene, actor Mathieu Amalric says that "When you see Quantum of Solace, there's the fantasy of Bond, but it's also realistic. I'm not a villain on a secret island who wants to destroy the world - it's more complicated than that." Villains don't need a metal jaw, or a scar, an eye that bleeds, he adds. Encouraged by past Bond villains, Amalric wanted to wear make-up for the role, but director Forster explained that he wanted Greene not to look grotesque, but to symbolize the hidden evils in society. So, unlike the villains in 'Casino Royale' (Le Chiffre), 'Die Another Day' (Colonel Moon / Sir Gustav Graves) or 'The World Is Not Enough' (Renard, The Anarchist), it is difficult for someone not introduced to the story beforehand to imagine that such a pleasant looking man can be up to something so sinister.

Heading: The Mountain & Me - Indian Express
Content:
CII Fair will bring in a kitty of 168 exhibitors

It's getting bigger and better. With over 16 crore business queries last year, the CII Fair due from October 17 to 20, "is expected to grow by another 10 per cent this year," Charu Mathur, Regional Director, CII North Region, tell us , this being the 13th edition of the fair, here there will be nine concurrent expos including decor, auto, mega brands, persona, finmart, consumer, fascia international and infocom.

Been a launch pad for many a products earlier, this time round Samsung is bringing in as many as 23 new models of Plazma TV and five of refrigerators. "Also coming for the first time are stalls from Himachal Pradesh and Rajasthan," chips in CS Bachhar of CII and adds that stalls from West Bengal have increased to 75 from last years 32. For those looking for fitness deals, the persona section will have Aircell Technology treadmill and sugar free coconut water.

While the fest aims to unite India, it also brings in goodies from Kenya, Pakistan and Thailand. "Here we will have 15 artisans displaying their products," says Shahzad, who's here from Pakistan for the fair.

Heading: Fair weather - Indian Express
Content:
Despite being visually challenge, Erik Weihenmayer reached the top of the world

This week, it's all about the undying magical spirit of adventure. We've all heard about the tallest mountain in the world, Mt Everest. We know it's the most dangerous peak to scale. More than a heart, you need guts, and a endless supply of the survival kit. Even the best step down, but Erik Weihenmayer never knew what stepping down meant. Visually challenged, Eric's made a successful attempt to touch the peak of the world. Here's his story.

Erik Weihenmayer could have been just an athlete, a teacher or a public speaker. He could have been remembered as "just" a visually challenged kid. But instead, he chose to fight destiny and create a space for himself, where people would look up to him and say, there goes the hero. Born in 1968, Erik suffered with a rare eye disease called retinoschisis. The disease rendered him legally blind. It progressed into glaucoma, and by 13, Erik lost all sight. So, what made him take this step? He dared to dream, and that too big. "Twenty years ago, when I went blind, it was tough to even find the bathroom. Now that I've climbed Mount Everest, well, I guess I've come a long way," Erik said once. Erik knows that when you dream big, failure is always a possibility, but it is up to everyone to turn this failure into a positive step in the direction of one's life goals, make it only a temporary failure en route success. There is never a final defeat.

In his book, "Touch The Top", Erik writes, 'I didn't really want to accept blindness or look at myself as a blind person. Infact, I found something interesting, when I actually accepted blindness, I didn't try to transcend it or go beyond it or beat it but just accepted it that was the greatest thing I could ever have done.'

On his mountain climbing expeditions, he pens, "Part of my motivation was trying to understand this disease and its limitations. What can one expect from their life, living with glaucoma? If I can go to such high altitudes with such high pressure in my eyes that's pretty encouraging for everyone living with glaucoma." While setting goals in life is important, Weihenmayer says, "In my life and I hope in yours too, there has been something that's been more important than any one goal. And that is what I would call a vision. I see a vision as being deeper than a goal. It's where all our goals spring from, it's how we see ourselves living our lives and serving other people and impacting the world. What kind of legacy we want to leave behind us."

Today, when he is not scaling a mountain, Erik lives outside of Denver, Colorado with his wife Ellen, whom he married at the 13,000' mark of Kilimanjaro. A former fifth grade English and math teacher and a wrestling coach, Weihenmayer is admired worldwide for his incredible athletic accomplishments. His achievements have earned him the Helen Keller Lifetime Achievement Award, the Freedom Foundation's Free Spirit Award, an ESPY Award, recognition by Time magazine for one of the greatest sporting achievements of 2001, induction in the National Wrestling Hall of Fame and Nike's Casey Martin Award. He has also carried the Olympic torch for both the Summer and Winter Games.

At the age of 33, on September 25, 2002, he became one of the youngest of the elite "Seven Summiteers" - approximately 100 people who have scaled all seven summits, the highest peaks on each of the seven continents.

Erik is indeed an inspiration.

The writer is a city based gemologist and owns adventure club, www.clubfootloose.com. Mail solisethi@gmail.com.

Heading: Shortage of saplings hits Nanhi Chhaan project - Indian Express
Content: With the season turning and festivities in the air, it's now also the time for perfect shopping soirees. Bang on time as always is Priya Jagat's seasonal extravaganza, The Vanity Fair. This winter's tale, which rolls out on the weekend (October 18 and 19) brings in a mix of pret and couture collections along with jewellery lines, accessories et al. "This year we have over a hundred stalls and about twenty more in the Willow Bazaar," mentioned Jagat who has brought in exhibitors from all across the country. The clothes range from Indian festive wear to a Bridal collection, casual winter wear to westerns that go on to shawls and coats, jackets and sherwanis. The accessories lineup is equally strong with the latest trends in footwear, bags, scarves and stoles to be showcased. The jewellery selection brings in precious and semi-precious stones, silver and beads. Also finding space here will be furniture, artefacts, home decor and linen. "There will also be a Diwali special stall with designer candles, wrappings, chocolates, diyas  and assorted gifts," adds Jagat who points out certain highlights of the fair. This includes first time exhibitors like Sheytal's from Mumbai with designer tunics and suits; Adaa also from Mumbai with footwear and bags; the Curio Cottage brings in premium jewellery; The Ray Store from Delhi will exhibit very unique Equiliser T-shirts for men, women and kids. Then there's a label Kurti coming in from Jaipur with stitched kurtis, Living Trends brings along garden accessories, handicrafts and flowers in silk while Reshmi Dey comes with hand blown glass. As far as home decor goes, expect to see Delhi's 'Take Me Home', 'JWJ Furniture' and 'Hollywood Homes' from Bangalore. "To make sure that there's enough for everyone, we have got Kids Own to have a special play and activity area for children. Also there will be tarot card reading sessions by Namrita Chahal from Delhi," explains Priya. And there will also be plenty to munch on!

Heading: Moga police say it was hot milk, not acid - Indian Express
Content:
Nanhi Chhaan, the initiative started at the Golden Temple to give away sapling as 'parshad' to the newly-weds and expecting women over a month ago, is wilting. The authorities concerned have been unable to arrange saplings, and till date, only 70,000 have been given away.

The initiative is being promoted by Harpal Singh, chairman of Ranbaxy Labs and the Impact Group of Companies and founder of NGO Nanhi Chhaan, and Harsimrat Kaur Badal, wife of SAD chief Sukhbir Singh Badal, is the founding patron.

On October 19, Nanhi Chhaan will also be launched at Talwandi Sabo. On August 27, when the initiative was launched at the Golden Temple, organisers claimed that the twin issues of environment and protection of girl child would be addressed through it. The devotees take home saplings' parshad with a pledge in mind and a prayer in heart to plant it and protect it along with their daughters.

It was expected that about 5,000 saplings would be given away every day, but till September 30, only 2,600 saplings per day were being given away and the number reduced to 700 by October, despite the fact that there were serpentine queues for the green 'parshad'.

Sources said Harsimrat plans to take the programme to Malerkotla, Muktsar, Patiala, Fatehgarh Sahib and Anandpur Sahib in temples, mosques and gurdwaras. Gradually, it will cover entire Punjab.

Harpal Singh said, "We have distributed about 70,000 saplings and have bought some 70,000 more from the Forest Department at the rate of Rs 2.50 per piece for Talwandi Sabo. There is no shortage of saplings; actually this is not the growing season. People are also offering their land for setting up nurseries for this initiative."

He added, "I have already interacted with leaders of the Christian and Muslim communities for support for the programme. Besides, awareness will also be created at schools and corporate offices."

Sources in the Forest Department admitted that there was shortage of saplings.

Heading: Tables turned: Scribes, cop get stung - Indian Express
Content:
The Moga district police had yesterday registered a case against three persons for throwing acid on Paramjit Kaur, a Dalit woman of Ghalkalan who was allegedly raped by one of the accused on July 9 last.

However today, Senior Superintendent Police Ashok Baath said as per police investigations and the report of Moga Civil Hospital doctors, the burn injuries were not of acid, but hot milk. And, the injuries were on legs and not face and torso, which would have been the case if the accused were motorcycle-borne.

The police had yesterday booked Soni, alias Kirpal Singh, Nita and Jeeta of Ghalkalan.

The SSP alleged that the police were investigation the matter thoroughly keeping in mind the earlier rape case. Investigating officer Jaswant Singh alleged that the victim might have wanted to blackmail the accused.

In her complaint, Paramjit had alleged that the police had earlier failed to register a rape case against the accused.

Heading: State to launch project to tame Ghaggar fury - Indian Express
Content:
Seven arrested for conducting sting operation to blackmail

The Faridkot police today claimed to have unearthed a nexus between a couple of reporters working for a TV channel and a cop, who used to allegedly blackmail people to extract money.

Addressing a press conference today, Faridkot SSP Paramraj Umranangal said the police have arrested seven persons, including Head Constable posted at Kotkapura Sarup Singh and his son, Gurmeet Singh, a reporter.

The others arrested include Partap Singh, also a reporter, Sukhjeet Singh, Harinder Singh, Parminder Singh and Satish Kumar. The SSP said on Tuesday night, the accused snatched Rs 1.25 lakh from a tanker driver and demanded Rs 50 lakh more, threatening that they had shot a video of the tanker and would say that he had dumped the oil illegally.

Later, the deal was settled at Rs 7 lakh, against which a post-dated cheque of Rs 5 lakh was to be given by the Bathinda-based oil tanker owner, said Umranangal.

He said the tanker owner approached the police and the accused were arrested from Bajakhana Chowk, the place fixed for the deal. He said the accused used to introduce Sarup Singh as a CBI officer. "We had been receiving complaints of blackmail in the past too. With these arrests, we hope to solve those cases as well," said Umranangal.

Police claimed to have recovered cars and cameras allegedly used in the crime. A case has been registered.

Heading: GNDU research scholars jittery - Indian Express
Content:
Double siphon capacity at Khanauri

In an attempt to tame Ghaggar, which has caused floods in the region, the Punjab government is launching an ambitious project to increase the siphon capacity at Khanauri, near Sangrur.

The Rs 137-crore project, which would be launched by Punjab Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal later this week, would double the siphon capacity, which at present is 13,000 cusecs.

Former Patiala MP Prem Singh Chandumajra said, "I had first raised the matter in the Lok Sabha in 1996. A final sanction has come now. The project will help safeguard the life and property of thousands of villagers living along Ghaggar in Patiala and Sangrur."

This year, a number of villages in Patran, Ghanaur and Dakala were inundated, causing damage to crops and property.

The government wants to complete the project at the earliest. Sources said Nabard has already sanctioned Rs 137 crore for the project without conducting a survey, while the government has acquired an acre on each side of Ghaggar near Khanauri.

Chandumajra said, "Once the project is complete, the government will start the second phase, in which the capacity of Ghaggar will be increased and bandhs in Rajpura and Ghanaur, up to Haryana border, will be strengthened at the total cost of Rs 425 crore."

Chief Engineer, Drainage, Vinod Chaudhary said the work on the project would start on October 17 and the earth work would be complete within next three months.

The remaining work would be completed before the next monsoon, he added.

Heading: Sidhu: I am ready to face PM - Indian Express
Content:
Research degree panel postpones today's meet to Oct 20

With the Research Degree Committee (RDC) of GNDU postponing its meeting again, over 100 researchers doing PhD in education— whose topics were rejected after more than two years of their hard work— are getting edgy.

Many are planning to approach other universities to complete their degrees. The RDC has postponed its meetings twice this month. Sources said the committee was supposed to meet on October 6, but the meeting was postponed till October 16, and now it has been put off to October 20.

Ironically, the affected also include those doing their research under the guidance of Dean, Faculty, who is heads the RDC. "This is sheer mockery of PhD," said a researcher whose topic was rejected. "If nothing positive comes out of the October 20 meeting, I will not continue with my PhD," said another researcher. Dr Jyoti Sadana, a research guide, said some of her students were from far-off places and found it hard to travel every time the RDC planned a meeting. A researcher from Delhi said he was planning to complete his degree from another university.

Amit Kauth, Dean, Faculty, said the meetings had been postponed as some of the committee members were unable to reach. He said the university was aware of the problems of the students and the decision would be taken keeping in mind interests of the researchers.

Heading: Properties worth crores stand resumed with Estate Office - Indian Express
Content:
BJP Lok Sabha MP Navjot Singh Sidhu today said he was ready to face Prime Minister Dr Manmohan Singh in the coming Lok Sabha elections.

Notably, the Congress leaders have been demanding PM's candidature for the forthcoming polls. "I am ready to face any kind of competition. The people of Amritsar want development of the city, which had eluded them during the Congress rule," he said.

He charged the PM with not fulfilling the promises that he had made during his visit to the city on the occasion of 400 years of installation of the Guru Granth Sahib.

"The PM had promised a Special Economic Zone (SEZ), development of the Attari border and a bio-technology park, but none of the projects have seen the light of day," said Sidhu.

He said he had only promised three things, development of roads, tree plantation and solid waste management.

"The roads are being laid, new saplings are being planted and the solid waste management project will be implemented soon," he said.

Heading: Youth shot dead during Patiala college fest, accused on the run - Indian Express
Content:
STATISTICSPEAK: Most sites involved in legal tangle for decades, list gets longer day by day

Properties worth crores of rupees, including commercial and residential category plots or sites, stand resumed with the UT Estate Office. The resumption of a site or a site resumed is a situation where the Estate Office takes back the possession of a property from the allottee.

Be it the appeals pending before the concerned senior officials of the UT Administration or the courts, almost 90 per cent of such plots or sites are involved in some legal tangle. A few of them are even entangled in trials pending for over two decades.

According to the Estate records, around 750 commercial and residential sites stand resumed for two reasons — either for violating building bylaws or misusing the premises. At 580 sites and counting, the maximum sites have been resumed for violating building bylaws.

Officials at the UT Estate Office said the procedure to resume sites is such where the violator and authorities are bound to lock horns. "While the violator is never ready to admit to the violation committed by him, the rules speak otherwise. The option for appeals are mentioned in the rulebooks and are exercised by almost all the violators whose properties are resumed by the Estate Office. Such legal procedures take time," said a senior official of the Estate Office.

Properties which stand resumed include shop-cum-flats, shop-cum-offices, booths, residential accommodations and shops among others. After scrutinising records, it was found that the maximum number of such sites exist in Sector 22, followed by Sectors 35, 37, 23, 26, 7 and other southern sectors of the city. More than 80 such sites have been resumed in Sector 22 only.

There are numerous sites which are involved in legal tangles since 1976; 1984 and early 90s. According to the records maintained by the UT Estate Office, it was found that around 10-15 sites are resumed on annual basis, which further get entangled in the lengthy legal procedures.

The UT Estate Office had recently resumed one of the prime properties and landmark in Sector 17 — a hotel site, for not being able to complete the construction in stipulated timeframe. While the hotel owners moved an appeal to the UT Chief Administrator, the decision was not in their favour. Following this, they moved the Punjab and Haryana High Court where the matter is pending. The construction at the site, which stands in control of the UT Estate Office, stands stalled at present.

According to procedures, the concerned officials, including the UT Estate Officer, Finance Secretary who is the Chief Administrator and Advisor to the Administrator, hold court to settle such appeals. The list, however, is increasing and the properties are being put to no use.

Sanjay Kumar, UT Chief Administrator, said: "We decide the cases on merit. When I joined, there were about 190 cases pending out of which decision has been taken on 150. But fresh cases keep adding on to the list."

THE PROCEDURE, STEP BY STEP

* A violation is detected by the field staff of the UT Estate Office

* Notice to remove the building bylaws violation or immediately stop the misuse of the premises is served on the violator

* In case the violator refuses to acknowledge the notice, the Estate Office is left with two options — either to go in for demolition of the said site or resume it. In case the option of 'demolishing the site' is exercised, the Estate Office cannot resume it. In most of the cases, the Estate Office opts for resumption of the site.

* In case the option of demolition is considered, a notice for demolition is served on the violator, after which he could appear before the concerned officials to explain his side or opt to demolish the violated area on his own.

* In case the violator fails to comply with the notice, the Estate Office carries out demolition

* In case the option of 'resumption of the site' is opted, a notice for the same is given to the violator, followed by a subsequent hearing opportunity to him or her. The site is resumed in case the violator fails to justify the violation or negate the officials' claim on violation

* Then comes the 'appeals' part

* The first appeal against the order of Deputy Commissioner who is also the Estate Officer lies with the UT Chief Administrator, who is UT Finance Secretary. In case the appeal is dismissed or rejected, the violator can appeal to the Advisor to the Administrator. If Advisor too rejects or dismisses the appeal, then comes the High Court where the violator can appeal, followed by the Supreme Court, if need arises.

Heading: PCA fortified as India take on Aussies, commuters to bear the brunt - Indian Express
Content:
A 23-year-old youth was shot dead in broad daylight at the Government College of Physical Education during the its annual youth festival. The victim and the assailants were outsiders.

While police sources said Gurpal Singh 'Pala', a resident of village Shadipur in the district, was killed due to rivalry among student groups, the college authorities confirmed he was not their student.

The incident left the students terrorised. Most of them looked visibly shaken especially as the shootout took place on the college premises.

Eyewitnesses told the police that while the youth festival was on, some outsider (read Gurpal) had an altercation with others around 1.30 pm, leading to the fiasco. The two, the police were told, shared some old rivalry.

The police have registered a case of murder against one Pushpinder Singh alias Tau and his associates for the murder. They are also interrogating a youth, an alleged member of the rival group, who was nabbed by the college students immediately after the incident. Eyewitnesses said Gurpal was shot at from a country-made pistol from a close range. He died on the spot.

Gurpal was, however, rushed to the local Amar Hospital and then to the Government Rajindra Hospital. A postmortem was later conducted at the Rajindra Hospital.

Further investigations in the case are on, including raids to nab the main accused.

Heading: Quark City sacks 400 workers - Indian Express
Content:
Mohali residents are in to face restrictions once again as the Punjab Cricket Association (PCA) stadium gears up for the second Test of the Border-Gavaskar Trophy-2008 between India and Australia starting Friday.

The roads leading to and passing through the stadium will remain closed for general traffic for five days, from Friday till Tuesday. The traffic coming from Chandigarh will be diverted from Guru Nanak Colony Chowk in Phase X and that from Mohali Phase VII-VIII side will be diverted from Fortis Hospital-PSEB lightpoint. Vehicles from Phase XI will be diverted from Phase X-XI lightpoint, said Mohali Superintendent of Police (City) Varinder Paul Singh on Wednesday.

The traffic on the stretch passing in front of the PCA and parts of other three will remain closed from 8 am to 6 pm (one-and-a-half-hour prior and after) the start and close of the five-day play.

For the information of the public, the Mohali police released the route diversion, entry, seating and parking plan for the cricket fans on Wednesday.

Two alighting points have been earmarked for 5,000 rural students, who will be coming daily in 100 buses from different parts of Punjab as part of PCA's endeavour, at NIPER T-point and Phase IX petrol pump. From there, these special guests, who will be entertained free of cost, will walk all the way to gate number 7 and 11.

Covering a distance of 600-700 meters on foot, the students will get seated in two blocks reserved for them.

For the convenience of the residents of over 300 houses in the restricted vicinity of the PCA stadium, the Mohali police would issue them special passes at par with number of vehicles they have to exempt them from extensive route diversions, stretching up to 2.5 km distance of the stadium. "We will also issue passes to journalists to allow them to move freely within the restricted area up to the stadium entry gates," the SP said.

Singh informed that 18 checkpoints will be installed to divert traffic and maintain law and order at strategic intersections around the stadium.

Heading: Besides Rae Bareli, state industry faces heat of VAT hike - Indian Express
Content:
One of the major Information Technology mega projects, Quark City India Private Limited, sacked almost 400 daily wagers and contractual workers from its ongoing construction work at its project site in Industrial Focal Point, Phase VIII-B. This was part of the company's decision to slow down the work on its project, confirmed Quark City spokesperson Gurmohan Singh.

He cited the impact of the global meltdown on the country's real estate sector as the reason behind pulling back the strings of the project. While services of over 100 workers have already been terminated, those of remaining shortlisted excess staff will be handed the pink slips within the next couple of days, Singh said.

Associated with the project for the past couple of years, the terminated workers held a demonstration against the company officials at the project site and demanded immediate restoration of their services.

"As and when the present adverse conditions, which have impacted the real estate sector hard, improves, we will consider speeding up the work on the project," said Quark City spokesperson, while adding that till then the company will be adopting the 'wait and see' policy.

Dubbed as one of the prestigious projects of Punjab, Quark City had announced to set up the tax-free zone along with mega project for the IT sector over an area of 51.34 acres (34 acres for Special Economic Zone) a couple of years ago. The total project cost was expected to be Rs 3,600 crore on its completion.

Heading: Police stations run by women to come up in all districts - Indian Express
Content:
The rail coach factory in Rae Bareli is not the lone case, which has caused hurdles in the way of development in Uttar Pradesh. Industry in the state is passing through a rough weather due to a steep hike in VAT on 40-odd items.

According to the Indian Industries Association (IIA), this could lead to the closure of small and medium industries. In spite of several representations to the chief minister, chief secretary, industrial development commissioner, principal secretary and commissioner (commercial tax) over the issue, there has been no response from the government so far. On October 13, IIA submitted a representation to MPs and MLAs of the state.

Sanjay Garg, Chairman of the Tax Advisory Council, however, said: "The government is serious about the issue. It will hold a dialogue with the industry some time next week."

Last month, the state government had increased VAT on electrical goods, machinery, equipment, apparatus, tools, dyes, spare parts, moulds, pipes and several other items used for industrial purposes. Along with traders, industrial associations have protested against the hike.

"This will result in closure of weak industries. Those in a better financial position will start buying products from other states. This will make new industries reluctant to come to UP ," said IIA Executive Director D S Verma.

S B Agarwal, Secretary General of Associated Chamber of Commerce and Industries (ASSOCHAM) UP, said: "It is suicidal not only for the industries and the corporate sector but also for the government which had hiked VAT with an aim to increase revenue. The move will in fact bring down revenue."

Reacting sharply to the government's stand on industry , Agarwal alleged that industrial development was not in the list of priorities of the state government. "When Tatas had to leave Singur, even Uttarakhand was named as an option for relocating the Nano factory, but not the UP," he said.

The industry has demanded a complete withdrawal of the VAT hike and the entry tax. It has asked the government to tax capital goods and raw material at the prevailing rate of Central sales tax.

Heading: Two youths killed for ‘marrying’ sisters - Indian Express
Content:
The Uttar Pradesh government has decided to set up all-women police stations in all the districts of the state.

In the first phase, the government will open such police stations in 30 districts of the state.

It has already finalised the posts to run the police stations, which will be set up in the financial year 2008-09. Such police stations are being constituted with an aim stop incidents of crime against women.

According to Secretary (Home) Kumar Kamlesh, the 30 police stations will be set up in the district headquarters of Gaziabad, Aligarh, Gautam Budha Nagar, Mathura, Rampur, Mirzapur, Shajahanpur, Ferozabad, Muzaffarnagar, Fatehgarh, Saharanapur, Manpuri, Rae Bareli, Lakhimpur Kheri, Ambedkar Nagar, Sultanpur, Azamgarh, Ballia, Sonbhadra, Badaun, Bijnore, Jyotibaphule Nagar, Banda, Jalaun, Deoriya, Gonda, Basti, Baghpat, Bulandshahr and Kanshiram Nagar.

At present, police stations run by women are functioning in a few districts such as Kanpur, Allahabad, Varanasi, Lucknow and Meerut.

Heading: Two IAS officers transferred - Indian Express
Content:
Two friends, Vidyanand and Dolly, were shot dead in Bulandshahr on Wednesday, when they were returning home after attending court hearing in a case related to the alleged abduction of two women. The youths had married them, both sisters, in 2006.

ASP (City) of Bulandshahar J K Shahi said: "Relatives of the youths have accused the family members of the women for the killings. We are conducting raids to arrest the assailants." He added the incident took place around 2 pm when the youths, both 25-year-old, were on their way to Delhi in a taxi. Near Bilsuri in Siqanderabad, three youths on a motorcycle stopped their vehicle, dragged the duo out of the taxi at gunpoint and shot them in the head, leaving them dead on the spot. The assailants drove away immediately.

The deceased and their wives belonged to Ahmedgarh township of Bulandshahar. The youths had run away with the sisters in 2006, got married in Delhi and had been living in the Capital since then.

Mubeen, the father of the sisters, had lodged an FIR against the duo at the Ahmedgarh police station on the charges of abducting his daughters and forcing them for marriage. Trial in the case was going on in a Bulandshahar court and the youths had come to attend the hearing.

Heading: Coach factory hangover: UP govt agencies sit on Railways money - Indian Express
Content: The state government transferred two IAS officers on Wednesday evening. M A Khan, who was posted as Secretary, Minority Welfare, has been transferred to the Silk Department on the same post. Parth Sarthisen Sharma, who was waiting for posting, will join Purvanchal Power Supply Corporation, Varanasi, as the Managing Director.

Heading: Maya to hold maha rally in Rae Bareli - Indian Express
Content:
Not only had the UP government given 189.23 hectare land for a rail coach factory at Rae Bareli, its agencies had undertaken to supply water and electricity for the project and accepted more than Rs 5 crore in advance from the Railways.

Now, while the government has taken back the land and ordered a refund of nearly Rs 9 crore the Railways had paid, other state agencies are still sitting on their share. Officers of these agencies say they are waiting for the dust to settle.

In April 2007, the Railways had submitted a letter of intent to the district magistrate of Rae Bareli to acquire the land. Three months ago, the gram sabha land was allotted to the Railways. Talks with state government agencies to supply water and electricity to the site began soon after and the agencies submitted their estimates to the Railways. Official sources said Madhyanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam had received Rs 4.5 crore for the construction of a 33/11 kv sub-station and laying a 132 kv line from Dalmau to the site, while Uttar Pradesh Jal Nigam had received Rs 73 lakh for installing tube wells. The payments were made in July, after which the work started and was to be completed by March 2009.

Asked about the progress of the work, G S Gupta, Superintending Engineer of UP Jal Nigam, said: "The work was on but has been now stopped following a stay order by the court. They (Railways) had paid nearly Rs 73 lakh for the construction of tube wells." He added, "We would have completed the work but right now we are waiting for the issue to be resolved."

B B Singh, Managing Director of Madhyanchal Vidhut Vitran Nigam Limited, also said they were waiting for a final word from the government. "We have Rs 4 crore with us. We will decide about it when the matter is settled," Singh said. In a sudden about-turn on Sunday, the state government took back the land on the eve of bhumi pujan of the project, which was to be performed by Congress president Sonia Gandhi and Railway Minister Lalu Prasad Yadav.

Explaining the reason behind the move, the government had said local farmers were agitated and a Singur-like situation was developing in Rae Bareli. Subsequently, on petitions filed by the Railways and local villagers, Lucknow Bench of the Allahabad High Court had ordered status quo on the matter. The foundation stone of the Rs 1,685-crore factory was laid in February 2007 and the unit was expected to produce 1,000 coaches annually. Nearly 1,230 acre land is required for the project, of which 467 hectares belongs to the state government.

Heading: Congress warns Mayawati: we can stop you in your tracks - Indian Express
Content:
To counter Congress president Sonia Gandhi's road show in her constituency Rae Bareli, Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Mayawati will hold a maha rally in the city.

Making this announcement on Wednesday, Mayawati came up with an eight-page explanation clarifying why her government withdrew the land which it had given four months ago for Centre's project of a rail coach factory in Rae Bareli. 

She also asked her Principal Secretary Net Ram to conduct an inquiry into the issue and submit the report in three days. "Based on the report, the matter will be placed before the state Cabinet for a decision," said the Bahujan Samjawadi Party (BSP) president, addressing a hurriedly-called press conference at her residence.

Mayawati blamed not only Sonia Gandhi and Rahul Gandhi but also Samajwadi Party chief Mulayam Singh Yadav for limiting their development activities to Rae Bareli, Amethi and Saifai, neglecting the rest of the state. "Why a factory in Rae Bareli, when so many factories already exist in the area? Why not a factory in Bundelkhand or in the eastern UP? If the Centre plans some projects for these areas, the BSP government will readily give land," she added.

The chief minister termed Congress chief's interaction with farmers in Rae Bareli a political gimmick. Pointing at two projects of Railways proposed in 2006 in Rae Bareli and Lalu Prasad Yadav's constituency Chhapra, the BSP chief said: "While the work started long ago in Chhapra, in Rae Bareli, the Congress wanted to go for bhumi pujan now, just before the Lok Sabha elections to garner votes."

She added: "Rae Bareli has 20 factories, of which nine are operational and 11 have been closed down, leading to a waste of 92 acres of land. In Amethi, 16 factories were put up, of which nine are running, seven have been shut down and 862 acres of land has gone waste." She asked: "How many people received jobs from these factories? The coach factory would have given employment to mere four to five thousand people."

Denying allegations of Congress leaders, who blamed the BSP for taking up a political battle at the cost of development, the CM said: "It is the Congress that has always adopted a step-motherly treatment for the state and caused impediments to developmental schemes."

She also mentioned proposals of various projects pending with the Centre, including her demand of Rs 80,000 crore special package for the state.

Reacting to Sonia Gandhi's statement — 'who can stop me from coming to my home', Mayawati said, "My government did not restrict the entry of anyone anywhere in the state. If I had to stop them, I would not have let them enter my home town Badalpur and organise a rally." She added, "My government would have easily prevented the Congress chief from entering Rae Bareli and would not have let her hold a road show in the area."

Heading: Railways ready with Plan B - Indian Express
Content:
As Mayawati took on Sonia Gandhi in Lucknow, the Congress launched the second phase of its attack on the Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister in Delhi. After Mayawati attempted to prevent a Sonia rally in Rae Bareli, the Congress said its workers could stop the chief minister from moving around in the country.

"The Congress is an organisation which is present in every village of the country... Leave alone the Congress president, if she (Mayawati) threatens even a Congress worker and does not rein in her dictatorial style and continues her vendetta politics, she would find it difficult to roam around in the country. The Congress workers will prevent her Bharat Bhraman," Congress spokesperson Manish Tewari said.

He added that the Uttar Pradesh Congress had prepared a detailed agitation programme against the Mayawati government.

The Congress also criticised Mayawati again for her "intransigence" in stalling four projects in Rae Bareli, "dictated by her desire for political revenge".

"The entire political paradigm of Mayawati is based on fear, revenge and corruption. Her corruption is legendary, as is evident from the monuments she has built from Lucknow to Delhi," Tewari said. "She should stop dreaming of becoming a PM. Instead, she should focus on discharging her responsibility of Chief Minister of UP first," he added.

Heading: No consensus between state and wb, loan a distant dream - Indian Express
Content:
With litigation over land allotment for the Rae Bareli rail coach factory threatening to push the Rs 1,550 crore project way behind schedule, the Railway Ministry is considering using the newly-enacted The Railway (Amendment) Act, 2008 to acquire the same 189 hectares of land whose sale deal was cancelled by the Mayawati government.

Cleared during the last Parliament session, the Act empowers the Railways to acquire land for special projects. "It was enacted to deal with situations where state governments hinder the setting up of projects of national importance by not providing the required land," a senior Railway Ministry official said.

Even as the Railways are confident of securing a favourable decision from the Allahabad High Court in the case, which comes up for hearing on October 22, the possibility of acquiring the said land under the Act is being readied as Plan B.

"Since negotiations with the state government was already on, the use of the Act was not considered earlier. However, nothing prevents the Railways from acquiring land under this Act, if required," the official added.

As far as the ongoing litigation is concerned, the ministry is building up its case on the argument that the UP government's decision to sell off 189 hectares of land in Rae Bareli to the Indian Railways came after protracted negotiations were carried out for almost a year during which both the parties mutually negotiated the terms of the land deal. "In July this year the UP government decided to sell the land to the Railways. The sum of Rs 9 crore, determined as the cost of the land by the state authorities themselves, was paid to the UP government in August. The possession of the land was handed over to the Railways in September," a ministry official said.

"The land deal was negotiated at various levels in the UP government. The purpose for buying this land was always known and there was no malafide intention on the part of the Railways. The price of the land was paid to the UP government, the mutation in revenue records was carried out and the possession was handed over to the Railways. This kind of a transaction is irreversible," explained an official.

The ministry is also building up its case over the argument that the land in question is infertile and can't be of any use for agricultural purposes. "In fact, efforts made to try out farming on this land were made by a local agriculture centre, but it did not yield any result," a source said.

Announced in the Supplementary Demand for Grants in 2007, the foundation stone for this factory was laid by Sonia Gandhi in February this year. The Railways plan to procure 840 state-of-the-art coaches annually from this factory for a 10-year period, starting 2010-11. The ministry's plans include getting air-conditioned double-decker coaches manufactured at this unit with the ministry eyeing procurement of at least 20 double-decker trains, having 24 coaches each, by 2021 from this factory.

Congress puts up 'divided' show for Rae Bareli project
A day after UPA Chairperson Sonia Gandhi claimed she was prepared to go to jail for the sake of development, her partymen failed to come up with a united front to protest against the state government's decision to take back allotted land for the proposed rail coach factory at Rae Bareli.

On Wednesday, two groups took out separate processions from the party office in Lucknow and courted arrest to protest against the UP government's decision. While one group of about 40 was led by Satya Dev Tripathi, a former minister, the other group of 60-odd workers was led by youth wing leader Yogesh Dixit. They were let off by the police in the evening.

State Congress spokesperson Akhilesh Pratap Singh accused the state government of going back on its commitments. He presented the minutes of an official meeting held in July last year, where the state government had accepted seven developmental projects of the Centre in Amethi and Rae Bareli.

Jatin Prasad, Union Minister of State for Steel, also met the media and said the Mayawati government's decision was "against the youth of Uttar Pradesh" because the project would have created new employment opportunities. "Mayawati is doing exactly the same thing for which she has accused the Congress and the Samajwadi Party. In her own village Badalpur, she is developing a selected area by encroaching upon land," he alleged.

Heading: HC pulls up housing dept for demolishing 22 houses - Indian Express
Content:
Disagreement between the state government and the World Bank (WB) over anti-corruption measures and fixed tenure of bureaucrats is delaying the sanction of the UP Development Policy Loan of Rs 15,242 crore by the multilateral financial institution.

The bank wants the state government to make the vigilance and anti-corruption mechanism stringent by making the State Vigilance Commission independent on the lines of the Central Vigilance Commission.

At present, the vigilance commission in UP is a toothless body headed by a senior IAS officer.

The bank has also suggested the UP government to ensure fixed tenures of bureaucrats in field posting and all major governmental agencies at the district and state headquarter levels.

To meet the conditions imposed by WB, the state government had initiated a nine-point reforms programme.

It included reforms in public finance, legislation of the "UP Financial Responsibility and Budget Management Act", introduction of Value Added Tax, reforms in power sector, improving the industrial climate, e-procurement, civil service reforms, vigilance and anti-corruption measures and implementation of the Right to Information Act.

The World Bank and the UP government have reached consensus on seven points, but disagreement continues on the issues of civil service reforms and anti-corruption measures.

Principal Secretary (Finance) Anoop Mishra, however, said: "We are in the process of finalising the loan. There was no substantive difference with the WB over these two issues. We hope to arrive at a decision soon." The WB mission is currently in town on a three-day visit since October 13.

In May 2007, the state government had approached the Centre for the sanction of a structural adjustment programme (SAP) loan from the World Bank for tiding over its finances. A bank mission visited Lucknow in July 2007, and instead of an SAP loan, it agreed for a "development policy loan" linked to a reforms programme.

The UP Development Policy Loan is crucial for the state government, as it will help save up to Rs 700 crore annually by retiring the costly loan against small savings. While the state is paying 10 per cent interest on the loans it has taken against small savings, it will pay around 6 per cent on the WB loan.

The annual interest burden on UP government is over Rs 12,000 crore.

On March 31, its total loan burden stood at over 1,25,000 crore.

The UP government showcased before the WB officials the measures it had taken to promote investment via the Public Private Partnership (PPP) route.

According to sources, so far the government had identified PPP projects worth Rs 1,25,000 crore.

These include the 1,047-km long Ganga Expressway, a network of six other expressways, power projects, urban development projects, Taj international airport and projects in transport and tourism sectors.

Heading: Panel to probe admission scam gets CSMMU council’s nod - Indian Express
Content:
A Lucknow bench of the Allahabad High Court pulled up authorities of the housing department for demolishing 22 houses in Sector J, Bangla Bazar Road last week. It directed the Lucknow Development Authority (LDA) to either rehabilitate or provide compensation to families whose houses were razed.

The Bench comprising Justices Pradeep Kant and Abhinav Upadhayay issued the order during a hearing of four petitions filed by 18 people whose houses were demolished by the LDA on October 11. The court also asked the LDA to submit a report on October 17 stating where the displaced people were to be rehabilitated.

LDA had demolished 22 houses in Sector-J, Bangla Bazar on October 11 on the pretext that residents had not obtained the approval of the layout plan and building map of properties from the LDA.

After being summoned by the court, Principal Secretary (Housing) Sri Krishna, LDA Vice-Chairman Mukesh Kumar Meshram, LDA Secretary Mani Prasad Mishra, District Magistrate Chandra Bhanu and Senior Superintendent of Police Akhil Kumar appeared in the court on Wednesday.

While Additional Advocate General Jaideep Mathur and Chief Standing Counsel D K Upadhaya argued for the LDA, advocates O P Srivastava and N D Tiwari were the petitioner's counsels. They submitted that residents had purchased land from villagers and the registry deed of the properties concerned had already been executed.

N D Tiwari told The Indian Express: "First the LDA officials had claimed that they had no information how the houses were razed. At the same time, some officials presented a letter issued by LDA seeking police support for the demolition drive."

Pawan Agarwal, whose house has been demolished, said: "Immediately after the High Court directives, LDA teams rushed to the spot to video shoot the demolished structures."

Heading: Two shopkeepers arrestedfor Kanpur cracker blast - Indian Express
Content:
The executive council of the Chhatrapati Shahuji Maharaj Medical University (CSMMU) has approved the formation of a disciplinary committee headed by the Vice-Chancellor to probe the entrance examination scam, which had come to light last week. In an emergency meeting on Wednesday, the council suggested that the committee should also comprise a retired bureaucrat, a judge and a former vice-chancellor to ensure that the inquiry is unbiased and proper.

Vice-Chancellor Dr Saroj Chooramani Gopal said: "A few names for the members of the committee have been suggested. We will approach them for their approval. After the formation, the committee will submit a report in two weeks. Subsequently, the council will meet to discuss the report."

He added, "Irregularities in the examination have serious implications and we cannot let it go like that."

An admission scam was busted in the university last week, when many candidates, who had left their Optical Mark Recognition sheets blank in the examination, found place in the merit list for two courses — dental hygiene and dental mechanics.

While the initial enquiry had noted anomalies in the admission procedure following which a reexamination was ordered, an emergency meeting of the executive council was called to form a disciplinary committee as role of an insider was suspected in the case.

Heading: Atiq Ahmed loses BSP favour, aides face FIR - Indian Express
Content:
They were part of a racket involved in making and selling illegal firecrackers

With the arrest of two shopkeepers, the Kanpur police on Wednesday claimed to have solved Tuesday night's blast case in Purani Sharab Gaddi area. The blast was caused by the accidental explosion of firecrackers kept in a bag on a cycle, the police said.

The arrested persons — Kamal Sahu and Mohammad Atiq — were part of a racket involved in making and selling illegal firecrackers.

The police is searching for their three accomplices, identified as Ayaz, Raju and Illiyas.

The explosion took place near Sahu's shop Gupta General Store. While inspecting the shop late on Tuesday night, the police found large quantity of illegal firecrackers.

The police presented Atiq and Sahu before the media where Sahu said: "Each packet contained 25 pieces of firecrackers, which had exploded and lead to commotion and panic in the area."

Sahu said the firecrackers were manufactured at Sarsaul by Ayaz, Raju and Illiyas. "Atiq used to sell these firecrackers to small shopowners," said Sahu, adding that he had been selling these crackers for the last 10 years.

Narrating the events leading to the blast, Atiq said: "Ayaz came to my Colonelganj residence in the evening with the crackers in a bag and we left for Sahu's shop on a cycle." Atiq said he asked Sahu to get a glass of water, while Ayaz stood near the cycle.

"Suddenly, the cycle fell and the firecrackers kept in the bag exploded from the impact," Atiq said.

He said Ayaz too received injuries in the blast, but ran away. "When I saw Ayaz escaping, I too ran away," he added.

Kanpur Senior Superintendent of Police Hari Ram Sharma said the arrested men had no criminal record. "Instructions have been given to all circle officers and station officers to arrest and register a case against those found selling illegal firecrackers," he added.

Superintendent of Police (Kanpur West) Dayanand Mishra said a case has been registered against Atiq and Sahu on charges of disturbing the law and order situation, creating panic among people, sale and supply of illegal firecrackers and possession of explosives.

"Ayaz, Raju and Illiyas are residents of Sarsaul, and Maharajpur police has been asked to arrest them at the earliest," he added.

Heading: Cops to court: men we killed were militants - Indian Express
Content:
After keeping their hands off former Samajwadi Party MP Atiq Ahmed since he voted against the UPA government in July trust vote defying the party whip, the Allahabad police slapped a criminal case on 17 people, including 11 aides of Ahmed.

The case was registered on Tuesday night at Khuldabad police station following the complaint of a Dalit woman, Suraj Kali.

In her complaint, Kali stated that she was going to meet the Senior Superintendent of Police on Tuesday evening to register a complaint against Ahmed that his men were harassing her. Suddenly his armed associates—Kapil Deo Tripathi, Moti Lal, Bablu, Santlal, Khan Saukat Ahmad, Zafar, Farooq, Bachche, Nate, Khullu and Gul Hasan— waylaid her and threatened her, the complaint said.

Besides the abovementioned 11 people, the complaint also mentions six unidentified men. While Tripathi is Ahmed's accountant, Farooq is his personal secretary and Khan Saukat is his advocate. Zafar has been arrested. All the accused are facing the charges of house trespass, assault, threat to life and spreading fear at a public place.

Earlier, Kali had filed several FIRs against Ahmed, his absconding brother Ashraf and his aides, alleging that they had forcibly captured her land and killed her husband in 2007. On November 18 and December 6, 2007, the accused had barged into her house and assaulted her for lodging complaint against Ahmed, she had alleged. SSP Lalji Shukla said, "All the persons named by Kali are active members of Ahmed's gang."  

Till a month before the July trust vote, the police were after Ahmed and had even demolished some of his properties. As the trust vote approached, the police actions suddenly cooled off and attempts began to woo Ahmed to vote against the UPA government.

After the vote, the government transferred him from the Mainpuri jail to the local Naini jail, for which he had been pleading all along. On August 16, Public Works Department Minister Nasimuddin Siddiqui had met Ahmed in Naini jail. Later, the minister also announced that the SP leader had expressed his desire to join the BSP.

Heading: Encounter: Crime Branch to submit report to rights panel - Indian Express
Content:
Chief of Special Cell Karnal Singh gives court a detailed account of the Sept encounter

Delhi Police's first sworn affidavit on the September 19 encounter — a minute-by-minute account of that morning which will provide grist to the official chargesheet later — was submitted before the High Court on Wednesday.

The affidavit by Joint Commissioner Karnal Singh said the story of L-18, Batla House, started with a knock on the front door of flat 108. It was six days after the serial blasts in Delhi. At the door was Special Cell Inspector Mohan Chand Sharma and his team.

They were there to conduct a raid — an operation that germinated from a specific tip-off on September 19 that one Atif alias Bashir, resident of Azamgarh in Uttar Pradesh was "presently residing at Batla House, Jamia Nagar, Delhi". He was "involved in the serial blasts", the affidavit said.

"The team knocked at the main door of the flat and disclosed its identity but the occupants did not respond," Karnal Singh mentioned in his statement. The team found the door bolted from inside. "Thereafter the team tried the other door of the flat and found it unbolted. The team members entered the flat through the side door to apprehend the suspects," narrated Singh in his statement before a Bench of Chief Justice A P Shah and Justice S Muralidhar.

At this juncture, Singh specified the team had only meant to "apprehend" the "occupants of the flat". But "the occupants opened fire to evade arrest. The team members also fired in self-defence... " Singh said.

Singh added that Sharma and Head Constable Balwant Singh were injured in the "cross-firing". The affidavit then goes on to address the "occupants/inmates" of the flat as "militants".

"Two other militants — Junaid alias Ariz and Shahzad Ahmed alias Pappu — escaped from the flat by firing on the police," Singh said. By then, Atif alias Bashir, had "sustained bullet injuries" and was removed along with another, Sajid, to a hospital.

Mohammed Saif from Azamgarh and the only one apprehended that day spilled out the names of his friends to the police, the affidavit stated. Singh records the recovery of an AK-series rifle with two magazines containing 30 live rounds each "from the far end right side room of the flat". Two pistols of .30 calibre were "found lying near the injured militants".

"A case vide FIR no 208 dated 19.09.2008 was registered at the Jamia Nagar police station in this regard and investigation is being conducted by the inter-state cell unit of the Crime Branch," Singh confirmed the progress made in the case.

HC asks police how scribe got access to accused
The Delhi High Court directed the police on Wednesday to file a response on how a reporter from the news magazine, India Today, met and had a "long, detailed conversation" with some of the blast accused in the custody of the Special Cell. The direction came after Prashant Bhushan, counsel for one of the accused, complained on how the police could "make accused persons confess before a journalist". "Going by the cover story in the magazine, the accused had met the journalist even before the relatives or lawyers had a chance to meet them," Bhushan contended. Police counsel Mukta Gupta agreed to file a response by Monday and told the court that "the confessions recorded in the story were not in good taste and they had no evidential value".—ENS

Heading: Affidavit on Jamia encounter - Indian Express
Content:
In the clamour for a "thorough probe" into last month's encounter at Batla House, it has perhaps gone unnoticed that Police Commissioner Y S Dadwal has already handed over investigations to the Crime Branch.

Sources, however, said encounters were usually handled by the local police but the commissioner chose to go with the more experienced Crime Branch.

Though Deputy Commissioner Neeraj Thakur said the inquiry was 'routine', other officers said the elite wing will now sift through the evidence as the spotlight on the encounter continues to grow brighter. It would have been marked to the Jamia Nagar police otherwise.

An FIR was also filed last week against the alleged terrorists, charging them with murder, attempt to murder and offences under the Arms Act. Thakur said they had been booked under Sections 302 (murder), 307 (attempt to murder), 332 (voluntarily causing hurt to deter a public servant from his duty) and the Arms Act. On September 19, two alleged terrorists died, two others fled and one was arrested. Inspector Mohan Chand Sharma, who led the operation, was also killed. A senior police officer said: "The FIR states that deceased Atif and Sajid, and Mohammed Saif — in police custody — have been charged with murdering Inspector Mohan Chand Sharma and attempting to murder other officers. The entire shootout will be investigated. The morning of September 19 will be reconstructed from the accounts of officers, the arrested man and other residents of Batla House."

The inter-state cell of the Crime Branch will submit a report to the National Human Rights Commission and file a chargesheet within 90 days. Officers said a forensic team from the Central Bureau of Investigation had already collected evidence from the L-18 building. The police also said all questions raised by human rights organisations, certain independent fact-finding teams and the recently-formed Jamia Coordination Committee will be looked into.

Heading: Difficult times for fashion, recession is the buzzword in industry - Indian Express
Content:
On the FIR
The FIR accuses the "militants" of offences under Sections 186 (obstructing the duty of a public servant), 307 (attempt to murder), 332 (voluntarily causing hurt to deter a public servant from his duty), 353 (assault or criminal force to deter public servant from his duty) and Section 34 (common intention) of the IPC. The suspected terrorists have also been accused under Section 25 and 27 of the Arms Act. While Section 186 attracts a punishment of imprisonment up to three months or a maximum fine of Rs 500, Sections 332, 353 attract three and two years of imprisonment, respectively. Section 307 serves the maximum deterrent of imprisonment of 10 years to life. If found guilty under all the Sections, the accused would face punishment under all the Sections concurrently.

Calls operation a 'raid'
According to the affidavit, the Special Cell team had come to L-18 in search of Atif alias Bashir. Intelligence inputs, informers and technical surveillance/ analysis had earlier "revealed" his involvement in the serial blasts. The affidavit says the intention of the police was to "raid" the flat, matters turned ugly when the "occupants" fired at them, forcing them to reciprocate in "self-defence".

Inspector Sharma's role
Contrary to earlier reports, the affidavit does not mention a recce. Inspector Mohan Chand Sharma and his team were right at the main door of flat number 108, L-18, Batla House, from the start of the "raid". The rest were covering from the ground floor. When a knock and a push on the front door, bolted from inside, did not elicit any response, the team gained entry through an "unbolted side door". The firing started immediately. While Sharma and Balwant Singh were caught in the "cross-fire", two of the "militants" escaped "by firing at the police party". There is no mention in the affidavit about the duo's exit route and the waiting posse on the ground floor.

'Occupants' or 'militants'?
Paragraph three of the affidavit uses several terms to identify the men inside L-18. At the point when the police knock on the flat door, the men are described as "occupants of the flat". The next sentence catapults their identity to "suspects" who shot at the police to "evade arrest". In the following sentence, the men are back to being "inmates of the flat". From the sentence that describes the wounds of Sharma, the affidavit remains firm on the description of the "occupants" as "militants".

On the investigation
Mohd Saif, arrested from the flat, reveals the identity of the others. He is booked for murder, attempt to murder and conspiracy along with several provisions of the Explosive Substances Act and the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act. During interrogation, Saif and another accused Zeeshan disclose the hand of "Indian Mujahideen" in the blasts. The affidavit says: "The investigation is being conducted scientifically, impartially and there is sufficient evidence against the accused."

Corroboration
The affidavit claims that disclosures of the five arrested "militants" were corroborated by 20 others arrested in Maharashtra and UP.

On 'violations'
In case of any encounter death, a report is sent to the National Human Rights Commission. The so-called fact-finding reports have no locus standi in such matters, asserts the Special Cell.

Heading: Jet lay-offs fail to perturb crew training institutes - Indian Express
Content:
Recession may not be fashionable, but it's certainly the talk of the town. At the Wills Lifestyle India Fashion Week, it is one of the buzzwords. Even with about 160 buyers registered at both the Wills event and the Delhi Fashion Week, the highest ever for any Indian fashion week, concern is palpable.

"This year we have had to work things backwards, so it means more work at less price. We have decided to have multiple price points to fit different budgets," says Rahul Khanna, of the designer duo Rohit Gandhi and Rahul Khanna. Their collection is priced between Rs 3,000 and 15,000 — "just right for a sensitive market", says Khanna.

"Most of us are living in self-denial, but it's a crisis that will hit the Indian designers in another six months," says Sumeet Nair of the Fashion Foundation of India, which is organising the Delhi Fashion Week at the DLF Place in Vasant Kunj. "The luxury couture market and jewellery have already been hit. Unless we professionalise in prêt, it's a problem that will affect our overseas market badly," he says.

The buyers are concerned too. Even though the event at Pragati Maidan is being attended by those from some of the world's most well-known luxury boutiques and stores, purchasing may not be at a premium this time. Patt Liew of the British India (Asia) in Malaysia says they are being extremely stringent about the quality and the pricing. "We want to work with a select few and ensure they are worth the investment. These are difficult times for fashion. We have to ensure the customer gets value for money to encourage them to spend on luxury items," she says.

While US-based Anthropologie has already picked up seven designers, including Rina Dhaka, Ranna Gill, Pankaj Ahuja and Manish Arora, the volume of sales at this year's fashion week may be decidedly lesser than before. "We are here more to explore the potential of the new designers. Buying will only happen later," says Berna Erman, buying-in-charge, Villa Max in Kuwait.

The effects of the slow market, of course, do not bode well for the retail segment in India. With the advent of international ready-to-wear brands like Dolce and Gabbana and Gucci, it puts the Indian designers to severe test. "People are more likely to dress down now than deck up for occasions. Most of our target clientele would rather go for a foreign brand simply because of their accessibility," says designer Bobby Grover.

The effects of the downscale are evident on the clothes too. While fashion weeks in London, Paris and Milan saw an emphasis on comfort clothing, Indian designers, too, have downplayed their emphasis on embroidery and embellishments. "I have worked more on the constructions and used them as embellishments," says designer Rajesh Pratap Singh. Likewise, embroidery, a forte of the Indian designers, have been bypassed in favour of sequin works or use of stones, which is less costly, but equally effective. There's a greater emphasis on simplicity, with ensembles like dresses and jump suits doing the rounds.

There are, however, some who are optimistic the situation will turn around. "Recession will last for about three years, but the turnaround period will be a boom time for Indian designers. Besides, as long as we have the cocoon of the domestic wedding market, it won't be such a dismal situation for us," says Pradeep Hirani of Kimaya, owner of one of India's largest boutique chains.

Heading: GK electoral rolls miss deadline, to be out today - Indian Express
Content:
Not anxious about students' future, Frankfinn, AHA say aviation industry on the upward curve, will see growth

The lay-offs by Jet Airways and the proposed staff cuts at Kingfisher Airlines may have the existing airlines staff on tenterhooks, but the aircraft crew-in-training see this as a harbinger of good things to come.

The forthcoming 2010 Commonwealth Games and the burgeoning number of airports in the country are the reasons why air-crew training institutes do not seem anxious about their students' future.

Samir Valia, Vice-President, corporate communications, Frankfinn Institute of Airhostess Training, says mergers and acquisitions are good news for the industry in the long term. "The airlines may not be hiring a lot of staff at present, but the worst seems to be over now. As far as long term job prospects goes, the aviation and hospitality industry is definitely on the upward curve," he says.

The same seems to be the view of Sapna Gupta, founder and director of the Air Hostess Academy (AHA). She says the lean phase is a passing occurrence. "Layoffs are a result of short-term losses. The economic situation should be solved in the next couple of months and the aviation and hospitality sector will witness growth again," she says.

Kuku S Kumar of TMI Academy, Defence Colony, also reiterates that staff reorganisation is good for her students. "The airlines will probably take on new staff now. With the increase in the number of airports in the country and the slated expansion of airlines to foreign shores, there is no need to fear a slump."

The Students of the various academies are showing a similar attitude. Natasha, a student of Frankfinn seems confident that good students would now get job opportunities faster. "The airlines will probably take fresh recruits now because they work at lower salaries. This works out to be financially viable for them and also gives us better opportunities."

Natasha has completed four months of the year-long course at Frankfinn. "By the time we finish, they'll be hiring more people," she says confidently.

Gaurav Arora, a student of AHA, however, has a more cautious take on the subject. "Since we are witnessing a financial slump at present, there will now be lesser number of opportunities for students who have not done so well in their studies. Only the top few will get jobs easily. This will create problems for weaker students," he says.

Heading: MCD inquiry into delivery of child outside hospital - Indian Express
Content:
ASSEMBLY POLLS: Delhi only state yet to complete its voter list

Electoral rolls for the Greater Kailash constituency, from where Bharatiya Janata Party's chief ministerial candidate V K Malhotra plans to fight the Assembly polls, is the only constituency in Delhi which is yet to be ready.

On Wednesday, the office of the Chief Electoral Officer published the electoral rolls of 69 constituencies. With electoral roll of the GK constituency still remaining, Delhi is the only state now which is yet to complete its electoral rolls. The deadline for completion of the electoral rolls set up by the Election Commission was today.

Electoral rolls for 24 assembly constituencies were completed on October 6, while the rolls for the rest of the 45 were published today. In the electoral rolls of AC 56 or Greater Kailash, details of nearly 10,000 voters have been found to be fudged.

The Congress had earlier demanded an FIR be filed in the case. Chief Electoral Officer Satbir Singh Silas said that the electoral roll will be published by Thursday night.

"We will take the issue up strongly; if required we will even go for demonstrations. It is dangerous that in one of the most sensitive constituencies, irregularities have been found in the electoral rolls," said Congress President J P Aggarwal.

BJP, on the other hand, appeared nonchalant about the issue. "Even if the electoral rolls are published a day later, it does not matter. We will be checking the entire electoral roll very closely to ensure that no mistakes creep in," said BJP President Harsh Vardhan.

The rest of the electoral rolls will be published on the website of the electoral office in a couple of days.

At present, nearly 20 percent of the voters still do not have photo-id cards. "We have gone to each and every household to tell the voters to get it updated. Nearly 16 to 17 lakh people, however, have yet not come forward," said Chief Electoral Officer Satbir Singh Silas.

On Wednesday, Silas held a meeting for all deputy commissioners of Delhi. The electoral office will also begin an awareness campaign for voters' education and to ensure that the code of conduct is observed properly.

Heading: New forum to push for reservation in DU councils - Indian Express
Content:
The Municipal Corporation of Delhi has called for an inquiry into the child delivery that happened on the roadside right outside the Municipal Hospital in Jwala Heri, Paschim Vihar. The Commissioner has been asked to inquire into the incident and submit a report by next week.

"We are ashamed that such an incident took place near the MCD Hospital. After the inquiry report is submitted, the corporation shall take necessary action against the staff on duty," said MCD Chairman of Standing Committee Vijendar Gupta.

The incident took place on Monday night when the hospital refused to admit one Babita Devi who was in labour. Babita delivered a baby girl outside the hospital.

MCD has 32 maternity homes that are well-equipped to deliver a child. These hospitals work round the clock and also have resident doctors available in the hospital premises to take care of emergency cases.

Madhu Jain, Director of Hospital Administration, however, said that the incident occurred due to the improper distribution of staff and lack of trained nurses at the MCD Hospital. "We do not have sufficient trained nurses and nurses refuse to be transferred," said Jain.

After the incident, the MCD plans to develop a comprehensive plan to operate the maternity hospitals. "The MCD will now recruit trained nurses for maternity hospitals. Also, MCD hospitals do not have ambulances. In the new plan we shall have ambulances to especially cater to the maternity cases," added Gupta.

Heading: Congress, BJP blame each other for missing foundation stone of hospital - Indian Express
Content:
Several SC, ST and OBC forums of the Delhi University have joined hands under the name of "Democratic Teachers' Forum for Social Justice" (DTFSJ) to demand for proper implementation of SC/ST/OBC reservation in the Academic Council (AC) and the Executive Council (EC) of the university. Members say despite having reservation under various other categories like women and professional courses, the two most important bodies of DU do not have reservation for the reserved categories.

Representatives of the Enlightened Teachers Forum, Delhi University Forum for Social Justice, Delhi University SC/ST Teachers' Association , Forum of Academics for Social Justice, Academic Forum for Social Justice met on Wednesday to discuss the various reservation policy conditions in the Delhi University in general and the upcoming AC/EC elections in particular. All representatives have felt the need for collective effort to get reservations implemented properly.

They have decided to put up a common candidate for the forthcoming Academic Council/Executive Council elections as well as the DUTA elections to be held in December.

Commenting on the need for such a forum, the Media Coordinator of DTFSJ Ratan Lal said, "There are hundreds of faculty vacancies in Delhi University due to the improper implementation of the reservation policy. We want to remove all such discrepancies."

Heading: Now, more on the idiot box for Tihar Jail inmates - Indian Express
Content:
Both BJP and the Congress have demanded an inquiry into the missing foundation stone of the Kalkaji Municipal Hospital. The inauguration stone for this hospital was laid for the second time on October 6.

Opposition at the MCD, the Congress said the foundation stone of the hospital was laid by Congress MLA Subhash Chopra in 2003. It also alleged that the BJP plans to relay the foundation stone in an attempt to gain mileage before the Assembly elections.

"We want to know what happened to the inauguration stone that was laid by Subhash Chopra five years ago. The stone has suddenly gone missing from the site," alleged MCD Leader of Opposition Jai Kishan Sharma. "We had already inaugurated the hospital. The BJP has, however, organised another inauguration ceremony by V K Malhotra. The BJP is misguiding the public and misusing public funds," added Sharma.

The BJP also wants to call for an inquiry to find out the missing stone laid during Congress tenure. Before any MCD project takes off there is a budget allocated for it. It then goes for administrative approval and tenders are floated. The Standing Committee approves the tenders and only then does construction work start.

"Tenders for the work were approved just two months ago. How did the Congress lay the foundation stone five years ago? We too want to know what happened to the missing foundation stone. How could the Congress inaugurate the hospital when it was not approved by the Standing Committee; if it was approved then why was no work carried out during these five years?" asked the MCD Leader of the House Vijendar Gupta. "The Congress has played dirty politics during the last Assembly elections, and now they are raising fingers at us," added Gupta.

Heading: Jet Airways pilot dies in accident - Indian Express
Content:
What could be a better festive bonanza for Tihar Jail inmates than access to a bigger bouquet of satellite channels, including a couple of channels airing Bollywood movies round the clock and popular daily soap operas?

In a recent circular, Tihar Jail authorities have underlined the plan of a festive treat for all inmates, stating there would be an addition in the number of channels they could watch after work.
