Inmates are at present allowed to watch TV for five hours — from 6 to 11 pm— everyday after completing their tasks allocated according to their qualifications and specialisations.

A circular issued by V K Malhotra, Superintendent (PHQ) last month declared that superseding all previous directives on the issue of telecasting satellite channels inside Tihar premises, as many as 18 channels would now be aired for the inmates. Earlier, around six channels were being telecast.

The bouquet would now include four news channels, three sports channels, three Bollywood movie channels, four Hindi entertainment channels, two informative channels, a devotional channel and Doordarshan.

Talking to Newsline, Sunil Gupta, Tihar's Law Officer, confirmed the news, saying the same was being done keeping in view the interests and requirements of the prisoners. "We have taken into account the entertainment and information needs of the inmates while they serve their terms behind bars. The list of channels has been prepared so that they might have access to the happenings of the outside world, apart from entertainment," said Gupta.

When asked about the violence and obscenity content of various programmes and movies, the official replied that they were ensuring that no such programme would be aired. He added the inmates were happy with the change.

The issue of increasing the number of channels being telecast in Asia's largest prison, accommodating around 12,000 prisoners, had first come to forefront when Bihar MP Pappu Yadav had demanded that Star One and Zee Cinema be aired in the jail in May last year. He had also moved an application before a local court. The court had then directed jail authorities to discuss the issue with the inmates and decide upon a list of channels, not exceeding six, that they wanted to view.

Heading: Mount Kailash residents seek CM’s intervention against liquor vend - Indian Express
Content: A 31-year-old Jet Airways pilot died after his car crashed into a tree on the Mehrauli-Gurgaon Road in South Delhi in the early hours of Wednesday. Police officers said the deceased was on his way to a party in Gurgaon when his car lost control, swerved and crashed into a tree. Police said bystanders informed the police at 2.45 am. He was rushed to Neel Kant Hospital in Gurgaon, where he was declared dead on arrival. Police said the deceased, Dheeraj Sandhu, was speeding, due to which he lost control over his Maruti SX4 car and crashed. "Sandhu lived in Forest Lane at the Sainik Farms. He was unmarried and had been working as a pilot with the Jet Airways. His family members have been informed about the tragedy," a senior police officer said.

Heading: 2006 custodial death: CID issues warrants against six UP cops - Indian Express
Content:
Residents of Mount Kailash Apartments, located in the affluent end of East of Kailash, are up in arms against a government run liquor vend in the local community market.

Having agitated for years against the "nuisance" caused due to the liquor store, the residents had managed, through appeals to the Lieutenant Governor and chief minister, to have the vend relocated to another spot in Nehru Place. However, after a short-lived respite, the vend is scheduled to re-open, much to the annoyance of the residents in this area.

"We have no opposition to the consumption of liquor but the fact is this particular vend is a bit of a nuisance. Firstly, it is illegal because it is located a stone's throw away from two schools, the Delhi Public School and an MCD school," 75-year-old Satish Vaish, a resident of Mount Kailash for over 20 years now, said.

The liquor vend's proximity to two schools is serious enough; however what rankles the residents even more is the traffic bottleneck this area becomes during evening hours. "There is just one road leading up to the apartments, and every evening it is blocked by people who buy liquor and sit in their cars and drink. They play loud music, pass lewd remarks, eve tease, and insist upon using the road as a public toilet. Once, they are done they throw their bottles into our compounds and leave," Vaish said.

A DDA colony, Mount Kailash Apartments was built in the early '80s and many residents say it is now quite popular with senior citizens.

"This is largely a senior citizen's colony," R S Grover (75) said. Grover is also quick to point to an old DDA brochure that describes the community market as a small market meant to cater exclusively to the needs of the residents. "The brochure clearly says the market will cater to needs such as provisions. This market is not designed to accommodate the crowds that come with a liquor shop," he said.

The Mount Kailash Resident's Welfare Association has appealed to the chief minister to put an end to this nuisance. "We have submitted yet another petition to the CM's office, signed by all the residents, asking her to intervene in this situation," another long-time resident and former government employee said.

Heading: Trader, sons shot at in robbery bid - Indian Express
Content:
The UP Criminal Investigation Department's (CID) Crime Branch has issued arrest warrants against six policemen under IPC sections pertaining to public servant framing an incorrect document with intent to cause injury, abetment of suicide, punishment for wrongful confinement and voluntarily causing hurt to extort confession.

An informant also faces arrest along with the cops, who were deployed with the Noida police in 2006.

On September 2, 2006, Sonu, son of Dalbeer Singh, was detained by the accused policemen, three of whom were then with the Special Operations Group of the Noida police. The 25-year-old youth was picked up on charges of stealing vehicles from Hazratpur village of Khurja. He was found dead in the lockup the next morning.

"The family alleged that he was beaten to death and then hung to make it appear as a suicide," sources said.

According to sources, the family approached the Allahabad High Court after the government refused to order an inquiry in the custodial death. On the basis of directives issued by the High Court, the CID Crime Branch started investigations in the matter and consequently found the policemen guilty.

"On Tuesday, October 14, the investigating agency took approval from the Uttar Pradesh government to arrest the accused named in the case," a senior official said.

Among the seven against whom the arrest warrants have been issued are Hindveer Singh of the Anti Terror Squad; Vinod Pandey, station house officer of Pahasu, Bulandshahr; Mahesh Mishra, sub-inspector, Bulandshahr; Sector-20 police station constables Pradeep Kumar and Haripal Singh; and Sector-39 police station constable Pushpendra Kumar.

An arrest warrant has also been issued against Kunwarpal Singh, a police informer.

Confirming the news, R K Chaturvedi, SSP Gautam Budh Nagar, said the constables with the Noida police have already been suspended. "We have suspended the constables posted in Sector-20 and Sector-39 police stations till investigations in the case reach any conclusion. Arrest warrants were received after the UP government approval the CID Crime Branch inquiry. The arrests will also be made by Crime Branch," Chaturvedi said.

Bulandshahr SSP Rajkumar Kureel said Vinod Pandey and Mahesh Mishra have been suspended till they are proved innocent.

Heading: Foster parents challenge magistrate ruling - Indian Express
Content:
A businessman and his two sons were shot at in the Anand Vihar area of East Delhi. The police said five motorcycle-borne youths shot at the men, who were travelling on two scooters, in a robbery bid in front of the Karkardooma Court complex around 9.45 pm on Tuesday.

The victims' family claimed the whole incident took place in the presence of a police constable, who could not act as his gun failed to fire.

Prem Chand Goyal (54) owns an MTNL distribution shop in Vishwas Nagar. He was returning home with his sons. Family members said Goyal was driving one scooter and his son, Deepak, was riding pillion. He had two bags; one containing Rs 4 lakh in cash and another containing recharge coupons worth Rs 5 lakh. Goyal's second son, Sandeep, was following his father's scooter.

Goyal's brother, Rajesh, said: "Five masked men on two motorbikes stopped them at gunpoint and asked them to hand over the bags. When Deepak resisted, they thrashed him and my brother. Sandeep also reached the spot and got into the scuffle. My brother asked Deepak to hand over the bags. Deepak handed over the bag containing the money but the other bag got stuck on the scooter."

Offciers said the assailants fired two rounds because of the delay. One bullet passed by Goyal's ear and the other hit Sandeep between his left shoulder and chest. The assailants then fled with the bags.

Goyal and Sandeep were rushed to Max Balaji Hospital in Patparganj, where doctors referred Sandeep to Max Hospital in Saket. Doctors said his condition is critical, but Goyal is out of danger.

A robbery and attempt to murder case has been registered against unknown assailants. The police have not ruled out the involvement of a close relative in the incident.

Heading: Court orders case against cop for shielding accused in housing scam - Indian Express
Content:
The battle for the custody of a one-year-old boy, given away by his biological parents at the time of birth owing to "social stigma", took a new twist on Wednesday with his foster parents challenging the jurisdiction of the magistrate who passed the order.

Appearing before the court along with the child in pursuance of the non-bailable warrants issued against them, the current custodians told Metropolitan Magistrate Naveen Arora that since the boy's custody was disputed, only the district judge or a guardian judge was the competent authority to decide the matter.

"With due respect to the court, it is contended that the learned judge lacks the jurisdiction to decide the custody of the child," advocates D D Singla and Nitin Sharma said, after the magistrate gave them the opportunity to be heard before passing any further direction.

The case had hogged the limelight after the magistrate, acting on a complaint by the child's natural parents, had last week asked the foster parents to hand over the boy to the former couple, who had given the infant away because of his birth before their marriage.

Trouble began after the lovers got married and sought the custody of their child, alleging that he had actually been given away on a "temporary basis". His current custodians, however, refused to part with the boy, whom they have nursed for a year, saying it was a valid and permanent adoption.

The boy's foster parents today argued before the court that the way they had adopted the child was also good keeping in view provisions of the Hindu Adoption and Maintenance Act. "No particular ceremony or execution of any legal instrument is required for a valid adoption, and voluntary handing over of a child by his parents is sufficient to constitute a legally binding adoption," the counsel said.

Opposing this view, counsel for the biological parents, Kamal Singh Pundir, said that since the custody itself was wrongful, the court was empowered to decide the matter according to the legal position on the issue.

Metropolitan Magistrate Arora, who had earlier cleared that what he had written in his order was on the basis of prima facie evidence on record, chose to adjourn the matter till tomorrow and said the court would adjudicate the disputed issue on Thursday at 4 pm.

Heading: Insurance company directed to pay Rs 40 lakh to claimant after theft - Indian Express
Content:
A Special Court has ordered that a criminal case be registered against a CBI sub-inspector for allegedly attempting to screen some people from prosecution by conducting a flawed probe into a housing society scam.

Special Judge R K Yadav, in an order on Monday, indicted Sub-Inspector D Damodaran, the investigating officer in the case, for deliberately giving a clean chit to as many as four persons, while picking three others for prosecution in his chargesheet.

The matter concerns fraudulent revival of the defunct Geetanjali Co-Operative Group Housing Society by the accused, two of whom were working in the office of the Registrar of Co-operative Society at the time; and a few others.

The alleged intent was to revive the society with the help of false and forged documents for procuring land from the DDA at subsidised rates.

The chargesheet filed by Damodaran, however, named only Jitender Sharma (assistant registrar), Mohinder Pal Bajaj (dealing assistant) and Subhash Chand as the accused, which the court said was a purposeful act committed in order to save others who had also played roles in the attempt.

There was sufficient incriminating information in the documents to name four others — K Laxmi Narayan (treasurer of the society), Sukhbir Singh, Mayank Goswami, Shahjahan Begum (now deceased) and her son Alam Ali — as accused as well but Damodaran ignored their roles with a design, the judge said.

The court observed that though the aforesaid persons had also participated in the conspiracy to cheat the Registrar of Co-operative Society and the DDA, the chargesheet was silent regarding their roles.

"He (IO) deliberately disobeyed direction of law and prepared incorrect records with a view to save aforesaid persons from legal punishment. He knowingly made incorrect entries in the chargesheet," ASJ Yadav said.

Noting that the officer's acts prima facie constituted offences under sections 217 (public servant disobeying direction of law) and 218 (public servant framing incorrect records), the judge has asked the CBI director to investigate the matter and "bring him to book" after lodging a case against Damodaran.

The CBI director has also been directed to order a probe further into the society scam, with respect to roles the other accused played and get a supplementary chargesheet filed within two months.

Heading: No fund crunch for BRT project: Delhi govt - Indian Express
Content:
The State Consumer Commission has come to the rescue of a man claiming insurance for his stolen items, after the insurance company refused to bear insurance expenses, saying that he had been "careless" in guarding his valuables.

The insurance company has now been directed to pay about Rs 40 lakh, including the interest and cost of litigation, to the complainant, in a month's time.

Preparations to attend a social gathering went horribly wrong for Anoop Thatai, director of a business house, when jewellery worth Rs 40 lakh was stolen from his locked car when he left his vehicle for a few minutes to fetch medicines in March 2006.

His woes, however, did not end there. In spite of having an all-risk insurance cover for the stolen articles, the insurance company threw out his claim, saying they could not be held responsible for bearing the losses, as the claimant had been careless.

Thatai's contention that his car had a central locking system and that the jewellery box was inside his laptop bag, failed to impress the New India Assurance Company and in a communication sent in May 2007, he was formally informed that his claim for insurance money had been repudiated.

The entrepreneur then moved the State Consumer Commission, alleging the rejection by the insurance company amounted to "deficiency in service".

The company argued that Thatai had failed to take reasonable care towards safeguarding his valuables and that it was beyond imagination that a prudent and diligent man could leave jewellery worth Rs 39.25 lakh in an unattended vehicle, which was not even parked at a licensed parking place.

After a legal wrangle lasting over a year, the commission finally came to rescue of the complainant and slammed the arbitrary stance of the insurance company.

Commission president Justice J D Kapoor has ordered the company to pay about Rs 40 lakh, including the interest and cost of litigation, to Thatai within a month.

"The onus lay heavily upon the company to prove that the car was not locked properly. No one would leave such valuable items in the car without taking proper care to lock the car," said Justice Kapoor in his recent order.

The commission also took the company to task for stepping into the shoes of an investigator while assessing the damages and said the surveyor should not have started a probe into the theft, as the same was the duty of the police.

Heading: Shock and despair among Jet Airways staff given the pink slip - Indian Express
Content:
With the Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) Corridor set to become an election issue, the Delhi Government on Thursday said there will be no fund crunch for the ambitious project and it is being implemented as per schedule.

The government is expected to release an additional amount of Rs 119 crore next week for the second phase of the corridor between Moolchand and Delhi Gate.

Transport Minister A K Walia told PTI that there will not be any fund crunch for the project and the Expenditure Finance Committee (EFC) of the government will release the next installment of funds for the second phase "soon".

"The implementation of the project is going as per schedule and the fund for second phase of the project will be made available," he said.

A senior official in Finance Department said the EFC will meet under the leadership of Chief Secretary in a couple of days time when a decision on releasing funds for next phase of the project will be taken.

Walia, who inspected the implementation of the present corridor couple of days back, said the Transport Department had sought an additional amount of Rs 54 crore to build more parking space and foot-over bridges in the second phase of the project.

"Before taking a decision on approval of funds, I decided to inspect how these things are going to help. After the inspection, I am satisfied with their proposal," he said.

Asked whether announcement of assemble election will delay the release of fund for the project as code of conduct came into effect, he said the EFC under the leadership of the Chief Secretary could take a decision on it.

Walia said eight foot over bridges will be coming up on the stretch of which five will be built at bus stops and three will built at other crossings.

The Finance Department official said an amount of Rs 119 crore has been sought to complete the second phase of the work.

The BRT corridor has been mired in controversies, with accidents taking place even during construction of the first phase and citizen's groups opposing it as being not properly planned.

The lack of adequate pedestrian crossings on the existing corridor was also widely criticised. Aiming to exploit commuters' anger over the project, the BJP has said it will make the "flawed BRT corridor" an election issue.

Party's Chief Ministerial candidate Vijay Kumar Malhotra had already announced that he will order a review of the entire project if voted to power.

However the Congress Government wants to highlight the project as a showpiece, claiming successful completion of the project will smoothen the traffic congestion on the stretch.

Six more such corridors are being planned in the capital before the start of Commonwealth Games in 2010, but Chief Minister Sheila Dikshit has said the government will go ahead with them only if the first corridor proves to be successful.

The government had earlier sanctioned Rs 215 crore for the Ambedkar Nagar to Delhi Gate BRT corridor.

Heading: Edgy steps to success - Indian Express
Content:
Axe falls on 300 in Delhi, similar fate awaits many more; Jet Airways says it's just the first phase

Just a fortnight before Diwali, hopes came crashing for nearly 300 employees of Jet Airways posted in Delhi. While some of them got a call in the morning and were told that their services had been terminated, several others remained clueless about their fate throughout the day.

There will be many more to share the fate of these 300, as Jet Airways declared that this was merely the first phase of retrenchment and more personnel of all categories would face the axe.

The employees have been shown the door with merely one-month's salary and one call, saying they have been "de-rostered" due to the reduction in the number of flights. "The number of flights Jet Airways will be offering in its winter schedule will be approximately 15 per cent lower than what was originally planned. As a first step, around 800 flight attendants, recruited recently under an expansion programme that has now been shelved, have been released. We are in the process of releasing personnel in other categories also," said Wolfgang Prock Shauer, the chief executive officer of Jet Airways.

It's not only those on probation who got the pink slip. Micheal Canon (28) had been working as a transport supervisor for nearly three years. Canon supports his wife, two children, a younger brother and an elderly brother. "It is too shocking and no one has been able to react yet. We just got a call, saying our flights have been cancelled. When we came to the office, there were no clear orders. Some said we would get our termination letters by evening, while others just did not respond," said Canon, standing outside domestic terminal 1-B.

Among those retrenched were employees who had just started out on their professional life. "I was planning to get married in a year's time. I had left a good job in a BPO to get into this profession," said Pulkit Arora, the eldest of three siblings. "We all had paid Rs 55,000 each to Jet Airways for a four-month training and spent nearly Rs 70,000 more during the training. There will definitely not be any Diwali celebrations at home this year," he added.

The contract signed by the employees says if they leave work after three years the sum paid for training will be refunded to them. However, if they leave before that, they will be paid Rs 25,000 only. Jet Airways officials did not specify if the retrenched employees would be given back the full amount.

Many of the dejected employees are now ready to work for even less money. "I was getting Rs 35,000 per month and the fact that it won't be coming to my account any longer means my financial freedom has been taken away. I am even ready to work on a lower salary. They could have kept us as ground staff if they wanted fewer cabin crew members," said Harpreet Kaur. She said she had been saving money to buy an LCD TV and for a trip to Dubai for her parent's anniversary, something which won't be possible now.

Meenakshi Sharma had big plans for October 26, on her 20th birthday. "It would have been my first birthday after getting a job and I had planned a lot of things. All that is meaningless now," she said. Even as Sharma explained her situation, she was flooded with calls from her colleagues many of whom are still unaware about their fates.

Heading: Two players sent back from Ranji camp - Indian Express
Content:
Indian No 1 professional Partibhan Aiyappan's foray into squash is driven by survival instincts

Parthiban Aiyappan won the professional category at the 15th DDA Squash Open Tournament at the Siri Fort Sports Complex on Sunday, but that was neither a happy ending to a long story, nor a platform from which he will jump on to greater deeds. For Aiyappan's tale is long and engrossing, and this win was just one of the twists and turns the 23-year-old has seen.

Born and brought up in Kanchipuram, 75 kms from Chennai, squash, or any kind of sport for that matter, was not even a little blip on his radar, even until the late '90s.

This was a time when, after dropping out of school in Class VI, he turned to anything he could lay his hands on — he was being driven by need, he admits, rather than knowledge.

His only dream, if you can call it that, was to make money, and to that end he moved to Chennai. The crowded city streets led him to the Madras Cricket Club, where he started working on the tennis courts. "I started working as a marker at the tennis courts of the Madras Cricket Club, and then as a ball boy," says Parthiban.

The obvious next step would have been playing tennis, or even cricket at the club. How did he end up wielding a squash racquet?

Chancy beginnings
"I wasn't earning too much working at the tennis courts. Whenever I found myself doing nothing, I used to pick up the abandoned tennis and squash racquets and start banging the ball into the walls. I actually wanted to play tennis as I had a fair idea of the sport, having observed it closely. But they (MCC officials) said I can't play there, so I took up squash. I began well and after a few months I got my sponsorships."

Parthiban is into the seventh year of his career now, but his parents back home have little idea about what he does. "They know nothing about squash even today. I had told my father (Aiyappan) about the sport, but he didn't get it. He only knows I'm playing," says Parthiban.

Life today is very different from when he was a ball boy at the MCC, and as one of the coaches at the India Cements Limited academy (ICL) in Chennai, he is in charge of at least fifteen youngsters.

But among all this transition, the 'need' factor has remained a constant, much like the gravitational force that checks down every upward movement. He doesn't try to fight it though, and is satisfied with his modest salary (Rs 7500), for it's still more seven times of his earnings at MCC (Rs 1000).

At the venue on Sunday, more than a few players described squash as a 'lifeskill' sport. Parthiban likes to think of it as life itself.

Heading: Stephen’s golf on Friday at DGC - Indian Express
Content:
In a first of its kind incident, the DDCA on Wednesday, abruptly sent back two players attending the Ranji camp from the Ferozeshah Kotla Stadium on charges of cheating and misrepresentation of facts.

Raman Sachdeva and Sahn John arrived for practice but coach Vijay Dahiya asked the two players to leave midway following orders from the DDCA top brass. The DDCA had received a complaint that the two players had represented Guru Gobind Singh College in the University of Delhi competition without being valid students of the institution.

The college was subsequently debarred from the competition and the incident was communicated to the DDCA for further action.

"I was told by the sports secretary (Sunil Dev) today to inform them to leave the camp. I cannot confirm if the boys will be part of the camp anymore or not, that's up to the DDCA to decide," Dahiya told Sportline.

Dev, meanwhile, confirmed the incident and said the matter is pending inquiry. "We received a complaint initially and got it counter-checked from the University of Delhi officials. However, the final decision on the matter and the action, if any, will taken by the president in a day or two," Dev clarified.

This drastic action assumes significance because the Association of Indian Universities, of which DU is a part, and DDCA, come under the framework of BCCI. Both Sachdeva and John were included in the initial Ranji probables list following their performances in the DDCA league matches.

Heading: Opening Scene - Indian Express
Content:
There's some catching up to do, old jokes to recall, updates exchanged. But when old Stephanians get together, they also play golf.

The St. Stephen's College alumni association will host their annual golf get-together at the Delhi Golf Club on October 17 this year. This is the 26th year of the tournament, but it all started when a bunch of friends, golf enthusiasts all, decided their passion and their memories could be merged to make a memorable event shared by a much bigger number.

The number grew as the years did, and now, despite the working day scheduling, over 100 former students and their spouses attend. The tournament, though the founding members insist it's just a fun event, is a stableford competition with various categories and prizes. Two years back, the Cloud Nine event was added, which is a nine-hole tournament for some of the older participants.

The tee-offs will run from 8am to 11am, and the event, as always, will be followed by a dinner in the evening.

Heading: The Baron’s Back - Indian Express
Content:
It was just another day of shows at the two fashion weeks in Delhi

Day one of the Wills India Fashion Week began with Gauri-Nainika's collection. We liked the Grecian drapes and the fluid silhouettes, particularly the siblings' ingenuous way of working the single shoulder strap in some of the dresses. The pretty constructions that the two have created out of tulle and shaded or printed hiffon were show stoppers, however, it appeared that a few of the garments had been finished in a hurry.

The WIFW, being held in Hall No. 7 of Pragati Maidan, the venue of the Week has been done up with installations by Alex Davies, Gautam Seth and Prateek Jain of Klove Studio and designer Manish Arora. The number of stalls at one end of the hall might have dwindled but everything seems more organised, at least on the opening day. "There's not going to be a dull moment. There are great shows, lots of buyers and enough buzz. Just wait and watch," an affable Sunil Sethi from the Fashion Design Council of India (FDCI), assures the guests. Amen.

Meanwhile, the second day at the Delhi Fashion Week began with designer Sonam Dubal's sparsely attended show— flowing kaftans, bakhu skirts, silk wrap blouses, tunics and dainty kimonos. Gallerist Mamta Singhania of Anant art gallery and model Nisha Singh were spotted sitting on the front row. Dubal's "My Memory Garden" meandered between Victorian style silk hand-printed capes and old fashioned Indian sensibilities. Model Millen sauntered down the runway in a cream cutwork embroidered dress to the melodic chirping of the birds followed by a jade green dress paired with balloon sleeves. "The collection is an ode to nature. It harks back to another era when people had time to enjoy their surroundings," shared the Delhi-based designer backstage. Tunics were teamed with hand woven capes, while a cream khadi kurta and an orange churidar was paired with a silk striped jacket. As the music changed, so did the mood — model Fleur Xavier walked down the cardboard strip in a faded gold sequined Tibetan bakhu skirt with a Mexican striped bag. The showstopper was a mauve gown with a hand-printed jacket with motifs.

Heading: Glass of Cheer - Indian Express
Content:
eAravind Adiga dedicated his Man Booker-winning The White Tiger to the people of Delhi. The city's authors respond

William Dalrymple:
It's no longer surprising that an Indian author has won the Booker prize. What is commendable about Adiga's win is that this is an author who lives and works in India unlike Amitav Ghosh who is predominantly based in New York and their works tend to be very different in terms of their view point, but equally valid.

Dalrymple is the author of several books, including White Mughals.

Advaita Kala:
I'm a huge fan of the book. It captures India's underbelly with strong, dark humour. It's a literary novel, yet, not pretentious.

Kala is the author of best selling Almost Single.

Amitabha Bagchi:
It's great news for Adiga and great news for all Indian writers. But I must admit, I wished Amitav Ghosh had won, he is one of my formative influences.

Bagchi is the author of Above Average.

Heading: Doctors get a legal shield against attacks - Indian Express
Content: If it's French, it'll taste like heaven but cost the earth — is this your thumb rule for wines? Now, Bouchard Aîné & Fils, a winery from Burgundy, France, is out to prove that good taste can also be easy on the pocket. The company has launched eight wines in India, with tastes developed over 250 years of the winery's history. The price has been kept between Rs 750 and Rs 5,000 a bottle. The Bouchard Chardonnay, for instance, which has been nurtured on the hilly slopes of Burgundy and pampered by the soft rays of the continental summer sun. Brand ambassador Jacques Dioque, 40, who introduced the wines in Delhi at a small wine-tasting ceremony, said, "Our bestseller, the Beaujolis comprises100 per cent gamay grapes and is ideal for north Indian cuisine. Tandoori dishes like the tandoori chicken, especially, pair well with its flowery notes." Let's raise a toast to that.

Heading: Govt panel to assess Dow project - Indian Express
Content:
Strict new laws set to make attackers think twice

Doctors have finally got protection from the frequent attacks they face. The laws have been made stricter across the state: such attacks will now constitute a non-bailable offence, with the offender facing up to three years in jail.

The state cabinet approved the draft of an ordinance with a strict set of penalties on Wednesday, marking the culmination of a long struggle by doctors.

Among the penalties in the Maharashtra Medicare Service Persons and Medicare Service Institutions (Prevention of Violence and Damage of Property) Act, 2008, is a Rs 50,000 fine on anyone who attacks a doctor or a hospital employee. What should dissuade vandalism of hospital property is a provision that anyone causing such damage would be fined twice the value of the property that he or she has destroyed.

Doctors said the need for such laws was deeply felt. Only on Tuesday night, Sassoon General Hospital was attacked by relatives and friends of a boy who died.

"Doctors were fed up of the attacks. Time and again we had approached the authorities including Home Minister R R Patil. Now, after a struggle of two years, the cabinet has finally passed the ordinance," said Dr D K Shirole, president of the state unit of the Indian Medical Association (IMA).

The IMA's city unit president, Dr Avinash Bhondwe, too was delighted. He credited their October 10 token strike for spurring the state government into action.

Doctors had intensified their agitation citing several instances where hospital property was destroyed and staff humiliated, at places such as Malad, Amravati, Beed and Chandrapur.

The doctors' cell of the Nationalist Congress Party agreed that the strike had worked in their favour. "Doctors had been seething and their resentment showed when they went on a flash strike on October 10.

The government had to take action," said Dr Dilip Ghule, chief of the cell. He mentioned attacks on doctors at several places, such as Mumbai, Beed, Akola, Amravati, Nashik and Latur.

The ambit of the ordinance runs across medical units and staff. It will benefit not only doctors but also nursing staff, interns, medical and nursing students and clerical staff; not only registered hospitals but also private ones and clinics, besides units runs by government local bodies like municipal corporations, zilla parishads and panchayat samitis.

The government-run Sassoon Hospital has engaged 100 security personnel after Tuesday's attack. They will start functioning with a week, said Dr Nirmala Borade, acting dean of BJ Medical College. Pune Zilha Suraksha Sangh will provide the personnel.

As of now, Sassoon, frequently the target of attacks, has only 21 Class IV employees as watchmen.

PENALTIES
* 3 years in jail
* No bail for attackers
* Rs 50,000 fine for attack on docs
* Payment of twice the value of property damaged

Heading: Sengupta, the conman, braked to a halt - Indian Express
Content:
A three-member committee headed by retired Supreme Court judge SP Kurudukar will look into the imbroglio over Dow Chemicals' proposed project at Shinde village. It will submit a report in a month's time, after assessing whether the project is environment-friendly and hearing the objections of villagers at the site.

An order to set up the committee was issued on Wednesday by principal secretary (environment) Valsa Nair Singh, 11 days after an announcement by Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh.

Dow proposes to set up a research and development centre. Villagers have been agitating against it alleging that it would pollute the river Indrayani. On September 26, the CM's office issued a stay order on the project while the CM pledged to set up a committee.

The three-member panel includes IIT-Bombay scientist Dr SK Gupta and Groundwater Survey and Development Authority (GSDA), Pune, official SB Khandale. Member secretary of the Maharashtra Pollution Control Board (MPCB) Sanjay Khandare will be the secretary to the committee.

"The committee will hear the grievances and complaints of the public and conduct site inspections," Nair told The Indian Express from Mumbai.

The committee will examine whether it is likely to cause damage to the environment in terms of health, ground water pollution and air pollution. It will check whether the proposed centre has a sound plan on environment impact assessment and environmental management; it will also examine the list of chemicals and raw materials and plans for their storage, transportation and waste disposal. At the site, the committee will take the views of local people, NGOs and government agencies.

During the agitation, most political parties have climbed on the anti-Dow bandwagon. The Warkaris, who are spearheading the agitation, constitute almost 70 per cent of their vote bank.

Heading: Malaysian tech for Hadapsar slum rehab - Indian Express
Content:
Investigations have revealed that Sureshnath Sengupta (40) of Baner, who was arrested for using a car (DL 9 CL 2140) with a state emblem and 'Government of India' stickers, used to con people by calling himself an anti-human trafficking commissioner.

"Sengupta's only motive behind using the state emblem was to con people. We have verified his vehicle documents, passport and residential address. Everything was found to be legal," said additional commissioner of police Rajender Singh.

Inspector Surendranath Deshmukh of traffic control branch had nabbed Sengupta, his wife and their child after spotting their car with a state emblem at Balewadi phata on the President's route on October 11. The car was seized. While two police constables were taking the car along with suspects to police commissionerate, the suspects gave them the slip and escaped near Jehangir Hospital. They were however nabbed again on Tuesday evening. Police have arrested Sengupta under IPC section 353 for obstructing government work. Investigations are on to find out whether he committed any fraud in the guise of a government officer. When asked why Sengupta and his wife escaped, Singh said, "They left Pune fearing police action on October 11 and went to Saibaba temple in Shirdi," Singh said. "We have confirmed that Sengupta was not trying to break into the President's convoy. Sengupta is born and brought up in Pune. He has a B.Com and MBA degree. He also owns a two-wheeler and was not using the car regularly," he said. "Sengupta used to work in a Delhi-based non-governmental organisation for sometime.

He returned to Pune some 10 months back and was planning to join another NGO working on animal rights issues," he said. Singh said that Sengupta was residing with his wife and child at Anjor Apartment in Baner on rental basis. "He was earlier booked for harassing his first wife. The case was registered with Yerawada police station in 2003," he added.

Non-cognisable offence
Using state emblem for conning people is non-cognizable offence, say cops. "Using a state emblem on a car for conning people is non-cognizable offence. But we have arrested Sengupta for obstructing government work, which is a non-bailable offence punishable upto three years of imprisonment. A complaint has been registered with the Chatushringi police station, " Singh said. Meanwhile, Sengupta was produced before the court on Wednesday. He was remanded to police custody till October 17.

Heading: Baner-Balewadi DP row: Activists misleading citizens, says PMC boss - Indian Express
Content:
The Pune Municipal Corporation has launched the construction work of tenements at Hadapsar under the Integrated Slum Rehabilitation Scheme, funded under the Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission. The distinctive feature about this project is that the PMC is using a Malaysian technique of aluminium shuttering for r einforced cement concrete (RCC) construction, which is enabling them to work at a faster pace and to use the same equipment repeatedly.

Civic officials, including city engineer Prashant Waghmare, superintendent engineer (special projects) V R Patil briefed the mediapersons during a visit to the slum rehabilitation tenements on Wednesday.

Patil said, " The aluminium shutter is a lightweight product, which, a single man can easily lift and one floor of construction could be completed in a week's time, whereas the conventional shuttering methods is more time-consuming. The repeatability of this product is around 200 cycles. One it is done, there was no need to plaster the walls and the thickness of the wall remains uniform."

"Even though, it takes a long time for the aluminium shutters to be installed, it is speeding up the construction and reducing the requirement of labour. Though the cost of the material cannot be called cheap, it benefits during mass construction activities," he added. "At the Hadapsar project, the construction work for 4,800 tenements is going on and the work started in January 2008 and is supposed to be over by December 2010," said Waghmare.

As per the sanction of the Central Sanctioning and Monitoring Committee (CSMC), PMC is implementing the slum rehabilitation scheme at five different locations spread across the city including Hadapsar, Lohegaon, Kothrud, Kondhwa and Warje. At the Hadapsar project, residents from the Ramtekdi slum will be rehabilitated. The work at Warje, too, has started off. However, the lands at Kondhwa and Lohegaon are yet to be acquired by the PMC.

Heading: DIWALI BONUS - Indian Express
Content:
Municipal Commissioner Praveensinh Pardeshi on Wednesday refuted allegations made by city activists regarding the purported change in the draft development plan (DP) for Baner-Balewadi. He strongly asserted that the activists were misleading the citizens and they were basing their premise on false information.

"The controversy on the Baner-Balewadi development draft being changed by the civic administration while sending it to the state government is based on false information. Civic activist Aneeta Benninger is misleading the public," Pardeshi said while rejecting the allegations against the civic administration.

On Monday, Green Pune Movement member Benninger had alleged that the civic administration had sent wrong maps of the draft DP to the state government for approval.

"The entire issue was fictitious and I am willing to resign if the serious charges made against the civic administration are proved. It would have been a big crime if the wrong maps would have been sent," Pardeshi said.

The civic general body meeting had passed a resolution to send the draft DP prepared by the civic administration, published in 2005, for approval of state government, he said.

Pardeshi said the civic activists had raised the same objections in 2005, but they were overruled by the general body meeting while sending the draft DP to state government for approval.

The Pune Municipal Corporation was pushing hard for the approval of long pending DP for the 23 villages, but the controversy will merely freeze the process for next few years, Pardeshi pointed out.

The civic administration has nothing to say on the proposed amendment by the state government in the draft DP for Baner-Balewadi and the citizens have already been asked to register their objections and suggestions over it, he said. On the objection that the bio-diversity park reservation was redefined in the proposed draft DP based on the Monarch survey report, the commissioner said the state government suo motto had asked the PMC to send the report for its consideration and it was not the civic administration that had sent the report on its own.

"However, the civic administration would soon be tabling the Monarch survey report in the general body for approval," Pardeshi said.

He said the PMC has also been urging the state government to implement the Town Planning scheme for the 23 villages so that the development process gained speed.

City engineer Prashant Waghmare said the allegations of the reservation for various basic amenities has been deleted from the draft DP was not true.

Heading: MSEDCL fines 1.38 lakh offenders, collects Rs 53-cr - Indian Express
Content:
Property tax: PMC collects Rs 6-cr, PCMC Rs 7-cr in one day

Wednesday proved a record-setting day for both the Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) and the Pimpri-Chinchwad Municipal Corporation (PCMC), as far as the collection of property tax was concerned. The PMC and PCMC garnered Rs 6 crore and Rs 7 crore of amount respectively, in a single day.

The deputy commissioner of PMC and tax collector and assessor Vilas Kanade said, "In a single day on Wednesday, we collected Rs 6 crore, which is a sort of record collection in the history of PMC. This tax came from over 8,000 property owners in the PMC limits. On Tuesday too, we received Rs 3 crore of property tax. This has taken the total tax collection till now to Rs 214 crore." Kanade added, "This year, we had been quite stringent with the tax collection and through various systematic measures, we could collect a good amount of property tax. We had even launched an amnesty scheme, from August 15, which came to an end on Wednesday." He has also appealed the citizens to make timely payments of property tax and thereby contribute for the development of the city. Assistant commissioner of PCMC Sudhakar Deshmukh said, "We had given the deadline for the property owners to pay up the property tax till today, therefore people came forward and paid up the tax on their own to avoid future action and penalty. In a single day, we received Rs 7 crore. This has taken the total tax collection this year to Rs 53.40 crore. Last year, it was Rs 45 crore in the same month."

Heading: World Arthritis Day brought a little hope for the afflicted - Indian Express
Content: The Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Company Limited (MSEDCL) has slapped fines against 1.38 lakh offenders and disconnected supply while recovering a total of Rs 53 crore in an intensified drive in the state while in Pune a total of Rs 8.58 crore has been recovered and action taken against 23,594 offenders. In an official statement, Ajay Bhushan Pandey, managing director of Mahavitaran, said that the campaign was taken up in the last week of September and in seven days itself a total of Rs 22 crore was recovered. He told a monthly meeting of all chief engineers that number of offenders was huge and each division should work harder to ensure that the offenders are brought to book. Other divisions like Kalyan had a recovery of 11.64 crore, Latur 5.82 crore, Nashik 3.68 crore. The statement also warned consumers that the electricity connection should not be misused. The MSEDCL has lodged a complaint against 43 agriculture consumers in Ahmednagar and Thane for misusing the connection for domestic purposes. The power theft drive will also be subsequently intensified the statement said. Meanwhile, activists with Sajag  Nagrik Manch while welcoming such a campaign however feel that the officials are not adopting the legal route by sending a 15 day notice to the defaulter before disconnecting the meter. Manch president Vivek Velankar has sent a letter of Pandey and S P Nagtilak, Chief Engineer, Pune division, that officials were not adhering to Section 56 of the Electricity Act of 2003 which entails that there should be a 15 day notice period before the officials disconnect the metre.

Heading: CoEP: Entrepreneurship the buzz word - Indian Express
Content:
Sixty-seven-year-old Ramakant (name changed) from Mumbai sought treatment for his deformity that led to a severe bowing of both knees. His appearance was like an `O' and walking inside his own house was extremely painful. After a bi-lateral knee replacement surgery, Ramakant can now walk for hours and travels on his own from Mumbai to Pune.

Fifty-year old Shanta (name changed) from Hadapsar, suffering from rheumatoid arthritis for many years was bedridden and was dependent on others for day to day requirements. She was treated by Dr. Neeraj Adkar and underwent bilateral total knee replacement and right side hip replacement one and half years back. She is now completely independent and walks without any support.

These are just two among several cases of patients suffering from arthritis that can lead to deformity and crippling pain. Adkar points out that while arthritis is one of the most common ailments among the elderly, today there are many new technologies and techniques available that can help them restore their joy of motion and give them their life back ridding them of the pain and suffering.

October 12 was observed as World Arthritis Day and several camps to create awareness about the disease and treatment modalities were conducted. Arthritis, which is one of the most common causes of disability, affects nearly one person in every family and actually refers to a group of over 100 different conditions.

It is common after the age of 50, but some forms can affect younger people as well. The elderly generally suffer from 'osteoarthritis', which affects hip and knee bones, says Dr Satyasheel Naik. Orthopaedic surgeon.

'Rheumatoid Arthritis', which affects more than one joint, is prevalent in women between 20 and 50 years of age. The cause could either be genetic or a weak immune system. In both, the thick pad of cartilage that acts as a cushion between our bones gets damaged. As a result, bone ends grind against each other and cause pain. The only common feature to all types of arthritis is that joints are affected and there is constant pain which gradually increases with time affecting our everyday activities.

For millions of people, arthritis limits everyday activities such as walking, getting up and sitting down, stair climbing, dressing or bathing.

What is not known is the fact that today there are treatment solutions available, which allow the patients to restore their joy of motion and provide enhanced quality of life, say doctors.

Heading: Freedom fighter Maruti Ghatge passes away - Indian Express
Content:
Alumnus, friend to invest a crore each for setting up an institute for benefit of students

Aiming to not only produce engineering graduates but also a few entrepreneurship aspirants, the College of Engineering Pune (CoEP) on Wednesday said it was starting an institute for innovation, entrepreneurship and leadership. Significantly, an alumnus of CoEP and his entrepreneur friend have come forward to set up the institute and have invested Rs one crore each as seed money for it, without expecting any return.

Founder-chairman of Kale Consultants Narendra Kale and founder of Flucon Equipments Sanjay Inamdar have come forward to set up the institute at CoEP. Kale, Inamdar and director of CoEP Anil Sahasrabuddhe announced setting up of the Bhau Institute for Innovation, Entrepreneurship and Leadership at a press conference on Wednesday. The institute is a result of entrepreneurship courses run at CoEP for last two years.

"We started the entrepreneurship course in 2007. The course was given as an elective (optional subject) for the final year students. So far we have conducted the course for two batches with 60 students in each batch. Considering the response to the course, we decided to start a dedicated institute on the suggestion of F C Kohli, chairman of board of governance of CoEP," said Kale.

The course has produced one company, which deals with the wastewater management and has already got contracts from various companies including PCMC for the purpose of wastewater management.

The institute will benefit the students of CoEP, as the course will be offered as a part of the curriculum of the last year and students will not have to pay anything for the course. "The institute will be built on 21,000 sq ft land in the CoEP campus and house an incubation centre. The structure of the institute will be an eco-building and will be complete in nine months," said Kale.

"The incubation centre will help students in the initial stages of starting a company," said Inamdar. "The institute will also run three to six month certificate courses for budding entrepreneurs and second generation entrepreneurs who may not be CoEP students. But they will be charged for the courses," he said.

"We are trying to rope in faculty from Harvard University and Massachusetts Institute of Technology for the course. Industry people, chartered accountants and management experts will also come as visiting faculty," said Kale.

Microsoft to set up innovation centre
In addition to this institute, Microsoft has agreed to set up Microsoft Innovation Centre in the same building. It will be the first such centre in India. So far Microsoft has 110 such centres in 60 countries. "The Microsoft has decided to set up the centre in CoEP as they are impressed with the talent of the students and rate of placements," said Sahasrabuddhe. "Microsoft will set up the infrastructure such as software and hardware required for the centre. It will benefit our students to explore newer ideas. Any student can use the facility," he said.

Heading: Arty confluence - Indian Express
Content:
Freedom fighter Maruti Dagdu Ghatge, who served three years rigorous punishment for setting ablaze the Kubharves police chowky during the 1942 freedom agitation after the historic Capital bomb blast in Pune, passed away on Wednesday. He was 90 years old.

Ghatge was residing at Jui Apartment on Pashan-Sus Road. He is survived by a son, two daughters and grandchildren. Britishers had opened fire in Pune, killing several innocent persons soon after the historic bomb blast at Capital Theatre in 1942. To protest against the British government, the Kubharves police chowky (now Kasba Peth police chowky) was set ablaze by a group of youths led Ghatge.

He was arrested and then sentenced to rigorous imprisonment for three years. He served one year in Yerwada prison when he came in contact with freedom fighters Nilubhau Limaye and Dr Shankarrao Kharat.

The trio tried to escape from the prison. But they could not succeed. They were further shifted to the Ahmednagar prison and subjected to severe harassment. Ghadge never opted for a professional job after being released from jail. "He was involved in various social activities," said his son Arun Ghatge. Ghatge was born on August 9, 1918. He completed his schooling at Camp Education society in Pune.

Heading: Exploring avenues - Indian Express
Content:
Painting the everyday life in India in different shades, four artists come together to provide Puneites with a visual treat

Reflections 2008 brings together under one roof the paintings of four renowned Indian artists. The works of Suhas Bahulkar, Vasudeo Kamath, Milind Mullick and Ravi Paranjape on display skillfully blend the diverse styles and mediums of these painters to present the common theme of everyday life in India, which bonds all the paintings.

" My art is influenced by the nostalgic memories that I have of this city," says Suhas Bahulkar whose paintings depict women draped in the traditional nine-yard sari and gold jewellery with predominant use of the colour orange. Using oil, acrylic and gold leaf as his medium, one of his prize paintings at the gallery, has been inspired by the hanging of the Chapekar brothers of Pune in 1897, who shot Charles Walter Rand, who while in charge of the Plague in Pune had unleashed a reign of terror and atrocities. " The impact of circumstances on human nature move me, like the impact that the hangings of the brothers must have had on their family."

Milind Mullick on the other hand portrays his impressions of everyday life as cityscapes. His paintings depict slick street scenes on a rainy day and rooftops all splashed in blue-gray watercolours. In complete contrast and spaced strategically were the vibrantly hued paintings of Ravi Paranjape. "I try to find visual melodies hidden behind reality and then infuse my canvas with that music," he says of his art, which runs into a riot of pinks, mauves, aquamarine and purple. Using oil on canvas, his paintings are more of a representational style, where the subject is easily identifiable.

Vasudeo Kamath had on display three of his watercolours and had chosen the elephant as his main subject. "No where else in the world do people share the cultural bond that we share with these majestic animals," he feels. Speaking of the burgeoning art market in India he says," Mumbai is still undoubtedly the best place for art but with exhibitions like these we create interest and can cultivate that culture in places like Pune also.

The exhibiton of the works of these artists is a visually harmonious experience.

(The exhibition is on till October 28 from 11am to 7 pm at Ray Art Gallery)

Heading: The big C-Courage - Indian Express
Content:
After 14 years in medicine, Kavita Kareer decided to follow her heart and take up interior designing and also work for underprivileged children

She has been giving just the right dosage of drug required for anaesthesia during the 14-year-long career as anesthetist at Sasoon Hospital. And now she knows just the perfect piece of furniture that needs to be placed in a corner to elevate its appeal in a home. Moreover, Kavita Kareer, a doctor turned interior designer, also has a soft corner for deprived children.

"Calling a well established career a day and starting with another at this stage was a tough decision for me to take. However, my family gave me strong support and encouraged me when I told them that after all these years, I would like to follow my heart," says Kareer, wife to Nitin Kareer, divisional commissioner, Pune.

Her association with Sassoon is not entirely a thing of the past though, as she continues to be a part of the orphanage, Sreevatsa, run by the Society and Friends of Sassoon Hospital (SOFOSH). "While working in Sasoon I use to give limited time to these children, but now I not only give time but also employ my art as a tool to help them," says Kareer, who would exhibits her creations of fabric art for raising fund for Sreevatsa from today at Residency Club.

"Last year also I organised for an exhibition, Ehsaas, and the fund went to Tara, an organisation run by SOFOSH for mentally and physically challenged children. Children of Sreevatsa will inaugurate today's exhibition," she adds.

Talking about her newfound passion, that is, interior designing, she says that she is enjoying every bit of it. "Finally I am able to express my creativity. Designing my own home was my first assignment and this brought me a couple of more projects which were well appreciated."

When asked about the sudden change of career, she says that both her parents were doctors and she took up medicine despite having a flair for designing. But now that her children have grown up she took up a course in interior designing. Guess it's all about following your heart.

Heading: Builder booked - Indian Express
Content:
Cancer survivors will walk down the ramp this Saturday to convey the importance of having a healthy attitude in life

Although Amy Figueredo feels she should have done it at 17, she is equally thrilled to be walking the ramp at 70! And the enthusiasm is contagious as 14 other women join her for the catwalk. There is also another twist. All of these intrepid ladies renaissance women — they are cancer survivors of the Prashanti Cancer Care Mission who have been fighting the illness with fortitude and emerged triumphant too.

Commemorating the Breast Cancer Awareness Month the mission has organised a fashion show and a host of programmes to honour the women and communicate their unusually courageous tales. Speaking on it Rebecca de Souza, clinical psychologist at the centre says, "The activity will not only convey the spirit of these ladies but also motivate other patients and let the community know that cancer is just a comma, and definitely not a full stop. There is life beyond that. These ladies have been defying odds and circumstances extremely valiantly. We give them individual counseling, hold several workshops on all information about the illness, reach out to them through financial, emotional and social support along with reiki, yoga and other exercises pertaining to holistic healing."

Sheela Kurien, a teacher who was diagnosed nine years ago and has been coming to the mission for the last one year, says, "It is an incentive to share the pain and smile. This togetherness gives us a lot of positive energy and through the show we will be encouraging others." Figueredo adds, "If you go in self pity you have lost it. It happened to me in 2004 but I have believed in rising over the pain and embracing life in all its wonder."

The Prashanti Cancer Care Mission through the support group has brought together not only the women but also the caregivers to inculcate awareness, information and motivation. "The show will portray the experiences and the life after cancer of these women. They will also display the designs of Ashely Rebello and Sushila Gugale and share their facts. It is to explain that they are leading a very normal life and that it is not pity but empathy that they need," adds psycho oncologist Khushnud Dhanbhoora.

Sixty-year-old Meher Bharucha has been coming to the centre for several years. "When we put our problems in perspective, we gain strength from each other and an assurance that 'I am not the only one'. The problems seem easier to handle," adds Bharucha.

And about walking the ramp, the opinion is unanimous-thrill underlines with slight nervousness. "But we are all fulfilling a secret desire. And age does not matter," smiles Kurien.

(The fashion show will be held at Hotel Taj Blue Diamond on October 18)

Heading: JIMS to hold meet on services marketing - Indian Express
Content: The Sahkarnagar police have booked a builder Sandeep Walimbe of Sadashiv Peth for allegedly abetting suicide of his employee Ramesh Shivaji Borkar (23) on April 11, last year. Ramesh's father Shivaji Borkar, a resident of Mahadev Nagar in Hadapsar has lodged a police complaint in this case. According to the complaint, Ramesh was working as a site supervisor for Walimbe. Ramesh came to know about some of the alleged illegal activities of the builder. Police said that Ramesh committed suicide by hanging self at a construction site in Bibwewadi. Police sub inspector A A Jagdale is investigating the case. Meanwhile,  last month, Shivaji Borkar had demanded CBI probe alleging that his son's death was not a suicide, but a murder. Deputy Commissioner of Police (Zone II) Satish Khandare had assured proper investigations into the case.

Heading: I have asked Centre to extend CNG facility to Ludhiana: CM - Indian Express
Content:
The Jayawant Institute of Management Studies (JIMS) is organising a national seminar on "Strategic insights in marketing of services" on October 17 and 18.

The seminar will focus on issues like strategies adopted by service industry, the emerging trends and the impact of globalisation on services industry. The seminar will be graced by eminent personalities from Aditya Birla Foundation, Sun and Sand, Airport Authority of India, ITW, Mumbai Dabbawala, Pantaloon and likes. This seminar will provide a good platform to management students and faculty members to get insights into the strategic aspects of service industries.

For further details, contact: 9960268778 / 9730475071, email: seminar.jims@gmail.com

Heading: Badal wants Ganda Nallah covered - Indian Express
Content:
Directs construction of a ramp near the Jagroan Bridge

Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal has finally realised that the pollution level is rising in the city. While addressing mediapersons at Jain Public School today, Badal said, "I have asked the Centre to provide CNG facility to Punjab ,especially Ludhiana, for the city is choking with pollution. It is increasingly getting difficult to breathe on the city roads."

It was Badal's fourth visit in the past six days. He was in the city to attend the Sangat Darshan in the Satpal Gosian's constituency.

He also asked the MC Commissioner to construct a ramp near the Jagroan Bridge for the smooth flow of traffic from the Clock Tower side towards the city side. The Chief Minister has asked the Ludhiana SSP to introduce one-way traffic norm in the city for the smooth flow of traffic.

Further talking about the paddy bonus, CM said it is a Centre subject and hence his government cannot do much. But added, "Though the Agriculture Commission had proposed Rs 1,000 as the minimum support price for paddy, the anti-farmer policies of the Centre have kept the price at Rs 850."

Badal said that he had launched Sangat Darshan programs for the effective on-the-spot redressal of problems of the people at the grass-root level.

The Chief Minister, today presided over Sangat Darshan Programs at five places including Mitter Sen Jang Ghar for ward numbers 36 and 39, Jain Public School for ward numbers 37 and 38, Trade Center in Miller Ganj for ward number 44, Shiv Shakti Mandir Park for ward numbers 42, 43 and at New Shivaji Nagar for ward numbers 40, 41, 17 and 18. In all, the Chief Minister sanctioned development projects worth Rs 80 crore in the city.

Heading: I-T raid: cash, valuables worth Rs 3 crore seized from Mittals - Indian Express
Content:
Asks authorities to formulate a plan at the earliest

The issue of covering the Ganda Nallah, which flows through five wards in old city, may soon see the light of the day. Though the project was inaugurated more than four years ago with the total cost pegged at Rs 15 crore, work had to be aborted after paying Rs 1.25 crore to the contractor as the authorities failed to decide whether to cover it or let it remain open. The 1.3 km stretch has thus become a garbage dump.

The chief minister visited the site today and asked the MC Commissioner to make a concrete plan about the nallah at the earliest. He was, however, keen to cover the nallah.

The new cost of the project is being pegged at Rs 30 crore. Filth can be seen lying in the nallah with encroachments galore as the sullage from the nallah falls into the Buddha Nallah. However, no deadline has been given by the CM to formulate the project.

In yet another case, Joginder Kumar, President of electroplaters association complained to the CM that water-logging from Vishvkarma Chowk till Dholewal Chowk has been causing problem to the commuters since 1963. He said, "The augmentation of the sewer system is needed apart from storm sewer facility in the area. Nothing has been done till date."

Early bird
The CM today reached five minutes before the scheduled time at ward number 16 but he found the hall vacant. He got angry and forced the SAD leaders to run amok to get the audience.

BJP is SAD
Although today's function was in Deputy Speaker Satpal Gosian's constituency, who hails from the BJP but once again BJP leaders and councillors were feeling left out. They were seen grumbling that most of the seats on the stage were grabbed by the SAD leaders.

Heading: GADVASU brawl: Student rusticated from hostel - Indian Express
Content:
From Tuesday's raids, cash and valuables worth Rs 3 crore have been seized from the house of Kasturi Lal Mittal, President, Punjab Pradesh Beopar Mandal and his five brothers. A few lockers have also been sealed. I-T officials revealed that it shows that the assesses have been whitewashing their black money by way of introducing the capital into their businesses and also there are big investments made in land and buildings.

The incriminating documents also show the suppression of purchases, manufacturing and sales. According to I-T officials, statements of various family members have also been recorded showing inconsistencies. In the coming days, all these documents will be analysed and co-related to arrive at the actual extent of tax evasion.

Heading: Residents, MC responsible for spread of dengue: health minister - Indian Express
Content:
The Guru Angad Dev Veterinary and Animal Sciences University (GADVASU) has rusticated BVSc student Kuljotveer Singh from the university hostel for allegedly thrashing another student Deepinder Singh Chahal.

A brawl in hostel number 8 on Sunday evening had left Chahal severely injured on his head.

He is currently recuperating at the DMC Hospital.

Deepinder was hit on his head with an iron rod while he hit Kuljotveer with a stick.

Dean Students Welfare Dr K S Sandhu said, "Both sides have reached a compromise.

While Kuljotveer has been shunted out of the hostel, action has been initiated against Deepinder and also the boy who had allowed him to stay in his room illegally. The parents of both the boys have been summoned."

Dr Sandhu added, "Deepinder has been involved in fights on earlier occasions as well. We could have taken a more drastic step but keeping their careers in mind, we decided to be lenient."

On the regular occurrence of brawls on the campus, Dr Sandhu said, "There is a lot of groupism on the campus.

In this brawl too, the students of PAU are equally responsible. So we cannot say that fights occur more frequently at GADVASU, it is just that this time our boys were at the front and it happened in our hostel," added Dr Sandhu.

Heading: Toxicological meet all set to kick off at GADVASU today - Indian Express
Content:
Health department's job is to treat sick patients, says Lakshmi Kanta Chawla

For the first time since the dengue cases spiralled in the district, Health minister Lakshmi Kanta Chawla visited the city along with Health Secretary Satish Chander and held a meeting with the officials of district health authorities and the municipal corporation.

Taking stock of the situation in the district, which has recorded four dengue deaths out of six in the state so far, the Health minister said the health department needed to work in tandem with the municipal corporation to fight the dengue menace. She said the department had not shown any lapse in reacting to the problem in time and has been able to control the loss of lives.

"We had started holding meetings well in time and have been regularly taking stock of the situation ever since," the minister replied to a question, adding that in order to oversee the work of fogging, committees including SDM and SMOs will be constituted in the district.

Today's dengue count stood at 908, which is well over 100 cases more than yesterday's 802. While the overall figure, including the suspected cases in the state has reached 1501. Of them, nearly 70 per cent cases (1,174) have been reported in the district alone.

However, Chawla blamed the spread of the disease on the lax attitude of residents and the municipal corporation adding that the health department was only confined to treating sick patients.

While answering a question as to why only a small number of patients were able to receive treatment at the Civil Hospital, she admitted there was lack of machines - 13 cell separator for Random Donor Platelet (RDP) and five SDP machines (Single Donor Platelet). She added in order to deal with the dengue problem in a better manner, the department would be better equipped next time, though it had acquired dengue detection kits in time for the detection of the disease.

"We want to beat the mosquito next time and therefore we are going to acquire machines worth Rs 1.75 crore to provide better treatment facilities in the government hospitals," said the minister. She added that the Civil Hospital will also get a cell separator (Random Donor Platelet) and SDP machines. She further said the number of beds in the Civil Hospital should be doubled as per the increased requirement. "At Amritsar, more than half the patients have been treated at the Civil Hospital," she remarked.

Notably, a few days ago, Chief Minister Prakash Singh Badal, during Sangat Darshan Programme in the city, had ordered to provide free treatment in the government hospitals.

However, as per the statistics, only a very small number of patients (17 out of 908 confirmed cases) have headed to the Civil Hospital for treatment. Dayanand Medical College and Hospital, on the other hand, has reported nearly 1,000 patients.

Heading: 2 lakh cases to be resolved through mega adalats - Indian Express
Content:
The 28th annual conference of Society of Toxicology (STOX), India, and international symposium on "Monitoring and modulating global resources of environmental and food contaminants: Nature versus chemicals" will be inaugurated at Guru Angad Dev Veterinary and Animal Sciences University here tomorrow. The Department of Veterinary Pharmacology and Toxicology is organising the meets.

Dr Hardyal Singh, Ex-Director Research and Medical Education, Punjab, will the chief guest and Dr V.K.Taneja, Vice-Chancellor, GADVASU, will preside over the inaugural function. The conference and symposium bring scientists and research workers from various disciplines together to discuss matters relating adverse effects of chemicals and drugs on health of the people, domestic animals and wildlife.

The conference will also offer an opportunity to the scientists, teachers and students to interact with eminent toxicologists of India and abroad. There will be nine technical sessions with special focus on challenging issues related to environment, industry, occupational hazards, in-vitro food and drug toxicology and good laboratory practices (GLP). Health problems related to excessive pesticide use and metal-pesticide interactions will also be discussed.

The Society of Toxicology is a professional organisation of scientists from academic institutions, government, and industry representing a variety of toxicologists and is affiliated to the International Union of Toxicology (IUTOX). The Society of Toxicology presents several prestigious awards each year including the best young scientist award, best poster presentation award, best publication award in Toxicology International Journal, life-time achievement award and STOX gold medal. The three-day conference scheduled for October 16-18, is being attended by 200 delegates from different institutes of India and abroad, said Dr H.S. Sandhu, head, Department of Veterinary Pharmacology and Toxicology, GADVASU.

Heading: Science Club to hold meet to mark World Food Day - Indian Express
Content:
District and Session Judge-cum-Chairman of the District Legal Services Authority, G.K. Rai on Wednesday informed that a mega Lok Adalat was being organised at new judicial court complex over December 20 and 21 to clear the pending cases in different courts.

Giving details to the mediapersons, the District and Session Judge said that all the presiding officers at Ludhiana will preside over the benches to ensure that all pending cases were disposed off. He said the project was called as Samadhan - 2008, to be held in all the districts of Punjab and Haryana as well as UT Chandigarh, with a target to decide two lakh cases.

Elaborating further, the Justice Rai informed that in this Lok Adalat, the pending cases in various courts relating to civil suits, MACT cases, matrimonial disputes, traffic challans and cancellation of FIRs and all type of criminal compoundable cases would be settled with mutual consent of both parties. He urged the people to bring their cases in the special Lok Adalat for the immediate and final settlement.

Justice Rai said that the case settled in lok adalats could not be challenged in any higher court and the decision given was considered permanent. The process of lok adalats not only provided speedy justice to the litigants, but also helped in reducing the pendency of cases in the courts, he added.

Heading: New technique for hair transplantation - Indian Express
Content:
PAU Science Club in association with different departments of university will organise a function at Jacob hall on October 16 to mark the World Food Day, said a release issued by the Dean, Post-graduate Studies-cum-Chairperson, PAU Science Club.

Dr Manjit Singh Kang, vice-chancellor, PAU, will be the chief guest on the occasion. The secretary of the club, Dr B.S. Sohal informed that post-graduate students of Department of Food Science and Technology, Food and Nutrition, Microbiology, Plant Pathology, Plant Breeding and Genetics, Agronomy, Processing and Food Engineering will deliberate on the theme "Food security" highlighting the role of their respective departments.

He said that the Department of Food and Nutrition would hold a quiz on World Food Day wherein students from different city schools will participate. An exhibition of posters relating to different aspects of World Food Day will also be arranged on the occasion.

Heading: Olympic heroes honoured by Punjab government - Indian Express
Content:
A.K. Clinics in the city today introduced Follicular Extraction Technique of offering hair transplant by stitchless technique.

Talking to the mediapersons, Dr Aman Dua revealed that FUE hair transplant is the latest and more preferred method of restoring hair all over the world. She elaborated that the genetic and hormonal factors are the most common causes of male pattern bladness ( Androgenetic Alopecia) in men.

"This can lead to hair loss in front of the head but some hair at the back side are present, permanent hair donor area from where hair are extracted."

Heading: Grounded! - Indian Express
Content:
Star sportspersons, who brought laurels to the nation, were honoured by the Punjab government at a function organised at Burlton Park Hockey stadium where sports equipments were also distributed to as many as 14,000 athletes. Pugilist Vijender Singh, who won bronze at the Beijing

Olympics was given Rs 11 lakh, bronze medal winning wrestler Sushil Kumar and boxing quarter-finalist Jitender Kumar were handed over Rs five lakh each by Sukhbir Badal, President of the ruling Shiromani Akali Dal( SAD). Chief national boxing coach Gurbax Singh Sandhu was also given cash award of Rs 11 lakh. Sukhbir promised that the state would give handsome cash awards along with government jobs to medal winners in the Olympics, Asian Games and Commonwealth Games. He further said that two new astro-turfs would also be laid at the Jalandhar and Talwandi Sabo and seven six-a-side astro-turfs would be put in place to promote hockey in the state. Later on while talking to reporters, Sukhbir revealed that very soon a comprehensive Sports Policy would be announced for development of all sports in the state. Following the launch of the hockey league, a kabaddi World Cup would be held where overseas teams would be seen in action. Sports Minister Gulzar Singh Ranike and Padma Shree

Pargat Singh, Director Sports Department, Punjab, were also present on the occasion.

Heading: ‘Teens held with fake currency part of a group’ - Indian Express
Content:
Sacked Jet employees stage protest, say were promised job security only a week back

The spot outside the Chakala factory of a bottled water manufacturing company is a popular spot for agitations, but the crowds on Wednesday were not the usual suspects. Instead of angry political activists, one saw scores of well groomed men and women in uniforms: employees of Jet Airways, the country's largest private airline, taking to the streets in protest against their termination.

As the news of the lay-off spread, even employees already past their probation period came down to pledge their support. Many among them were actually roommates who had come to Mumbai in search of a career and took to the skies riding on India's aviation boom, which is now history.
