"I don't come from a super rich family. I come for an extremely middle-class family and my parents were very happy when I had announced that I had become an air hostess," said Reshma Pathan, who had been with Jet for a year.

"I come from Ahmedabad and really take pains to pay high rents and repay my loans. What will I do now?" Pathan asked.

They were from all over the country — Ahmedabad, Baroda, Bangalore, Kolkata. And what irked them the most was the way their jobs were terminated.

"Usually we receive a call six hours before our flights. So when I called the roster department when I did not receive any calls, I was told that I have been terminated as my services were not required anymore," said Rekha Iyengar, who quit her job at Kingfisher in Bangalore to join Jet in Mumbai. "I was about to sign my probation papers in just a day or two but now it's all gone."

Many crew members also claim that they were promised job security by none other the chairman Naresh Goyal only a week ago and now they've been given the pink slip. "Only last week Naresh Goyal told us that our jobs were secure and three days later even had a meeting with senior crew members who repeated the same assurance... And yesterday, when I called my roster office, they told me that my job has been terminated," said a crew member who did not wish to be named.

What also bothers them is the fact that they had chosen aviation as their career of choice while rejecting other jobs. "I used to work at a call centre and quit that place to join Jet as a flight steward, but now am without a job," said Mitesh Bhatt. "Don't you think those guys back at the call centre or at the travel company where my friend worked earlier will be laughing at us?"

Crew members also alleged that Jet did not even compensate them on fair grounds. "All they did was to return our deposits of Rs 55,000 along with salary till October 15, which we were entitled to, and then they say it's on humanitarian ground," said crew members in chorus.

Meanwhile, at a press conference at Jet's corporate headquarters at Marol, CEO Wolfgang Prock Schauer announced job cuts to the tune of 1900 across all departments including pilots and management. "The situation has become severe and globally markets have gone down. Therefore, we've started releasing employees who've been on probation and not confirmed," he said.

Heading: Slump hits MMRDA, no takers for Wadala plots - Indian Express
Content:
They came from Nepal, Bihar; cops looking for others, say seizure only tip of the iceberg

A day after two teenagers were caught trying to exchange fake currency at Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus (CST), investigators believe that the Rs 1 lakh worth fake currency notes seized from the duo could only be the tip of the iceberg.

Investigators say that both boys, who are now at the Dongri remand home after being remanded to "safe custody", are originally from Nepal and had come to the city about three days ago, carrying a large number of fake currency notes in denominations of Rs 1,000 and Rs 500. According to the police, they had a specific brief to circulate the notes.

"Eight people, including these boys, had come to Mumbai early this week," said A K Sharma, commissioner, Mumbai Railway Police. "Of these eight, some hail from border villages in Bihar on the Indo-Nepal border while the rest are from Nepal. The group also included the father of one of these teenagers, who fled the city a day before these two were caught," Sharma said.

The CST railway police had on Tuesday apprehended two teenagers for trying to circulate fake currency and recovered fake currency worth over Rs 1 lakh from them. The boys initially tried to mislead the police by giving Muslim names and also the wrong address. During the course of investigation, it was revealed that both the boys hailed from a village in Nepal, very close to the Indo-Nepal border.

Talking on the group's modus operandi, Sharma said: "People who assign them the job of exchanging fake money usually keep their house or some valuable items as a guarantee. The gang members have to return half the money after exchanging the fake notes in the Indian market and then take their possession back. So, the business is quite lucrative for these people who are very poor." The police are still verifying how much fake currency the gang has already circulated in the market.

"The boys had crossed the border using a bicycle as the border is porous there. They boarded a bus from Ghoresan village in Bihar for Muzaffarpur and from there the eight took a train to Mumbai, arriving at Kurla terminus," said Dilip Mane, senior police inspector of the CST railway police station, who is investigating the case.

"They had come to the city early this week. After coming to Kurla, they took a local train for Sion and from there they reached Dharavi where their relatives stay. Since the relatives refused to give them shelter, all eight stayed on the footpath for a couple of days," Mane said.

Interestingly, other members of the gang fled the spot when the two boys were arrested by the police. "We have named a few people and the probe is on," added Sharma.

Heading: TIFR team studying if Indus Valley civilisation understood the stars - Indian Express
Content:
After the poor response for its plots at Bandra-Kurla Complex (BKC), this time the Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA) has hit an all time low with two of its plots at Wadala not finding a single taker.

The two plots located opposite the IMAX Adlabs multiplex at Wadala are a 7,029 sq mt commercial space at a reserve price of Rs 240 crore and a 4,340 sq mt plot meant for malls and multiplexes, priced at Rs 135 crore. On Wednesday bids for both plots were to be opened at a scheduled meeting at the MMRDA building in Bandra. However, in the absence of any bidders, the meeting was never held.

The auctioning of the two plots are part of Phase One of the MMRDA's plans to develop the region in the vicinity of the Wadala Truck Terminus into a commercial district like Nariman Point or BKC. The project is to be carried out in four phases. This is the second time that the both plots abutting a 2000 sq mt garden have failed to elicit any response. MMRDA sources state that an earlier meeting on September 23, meant for the opening of bids, had to be postponed to Wednesday for the same reason.

The no-show at the auction was predicted in the realty circles. Riding high on a four-year boom, developers were heavily into land acquisition until the realty slump pulled the plug on all their projects.

"Share prices of real estate companies have come down by 80-90 per cent. Builders who have been bidding aggressively and went overboard with their offers are in a tight spot. Today less than 20 per cent of land transaction is being carried out in the market as no one is in a mood to or will dare to purchase land at this stage," said Mahesh Mudda, chairman of the Builders Association of India.

As an indicator of the state of things to come, in March this year, two of the five plots put on the block in BKC had found no bidder. Even the winning bidders in case of the other three were not issued plot allotment letters until recently as they had asked the MMRDA to make an allowance in its three-month payment period and extend it till the end of the year.

MMRDA additional commissioner Milind Mhaiskar said that they have decided to hold on to the plot for another three to four months. "The realty slump was bound to affect our auction. On Wednesday, the plan for the masterplan for Wadala Truck Terminus was approved. This would include a 28-hectare monorail and metro depot and several residential complexes in the area. In Wadala, accessibility was a problem but now that will be resolved and we expect better response next time," Mhaiskar.

Heading: MMRDA plans truck terminals in Navi Mumbai, Thane to decongest city roads - Indian Express
Content:
Archaeo-astronomical research project also seeks to fill gaps between Vedic period and Harappa civilisation

In a first, a team of four from the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR) has undertaken an archaeo-astronomical project that will study India's ancient Indus Valley Civilisation sites from a purely astronomical perspective.

Having just visited Dholavira in Kutch, Gujarat, to see if there were any indications of the use of astronomy by earlier civilizations, the team will also try to fill in the gaps between the Vedic period and the Harappan civilization.

Dholavira is the third largest archaeological site in India, and the fifth largest in the subcontinent.

"We are exploring possible astronomical roots in these areas. For example, astronomy would be required in order to calculate the farming and cultivation routines, and this would require detailed and continuous observations," says professor Mayank Vahia, who is a professor in the department of astronomy and astrophysics at TIFR.

The research project is funded by the Tata Trust and the Centre for Basic Sciences (CBS). Having been launched in January 2006, the project is a collaborative effort with the University of Washington, Seattle; Institute of Mathematical Sciences, Chennai; and the Indus Research Centre in Chennai.

Vahia says that most people are not aware of the subtleties of the astronomical system, and, if tapped into, it can open a completely new window to the prehistoric world, tracing ancestors by using astronomy as a window. "Some of the streets have been aligned in certain ways so as to suggest that some astronomical calculations may have been used for the geographical layout," says Vahia, also pointing out that the Harappan culture was one of the most advanced at the time.

The team also plans to do a cultural simulation to see how the mentalities of the civilisation evolved, research that will also help fill in the gaps in the archaeological data. "They must have used some amount of astronomy when it came to seasons and crops. The simulations will help us see how astronomy grew and evolved along with the civilization," says Kavita Gangal, a project assistant with the team.

Another area of research the team is venturing into is to decipher scripts found at the Dholavira site, comparing them with other sites of the Indus Valley Civilization. "The texts are very brief, and we have not found any large passages, which makes it more challenging to decipher these scripts," says research scholar and team-member Nisha Yadav.

The team is also hoping to find astronomical references in Vedic literature using the Sanskrit language. "Most of the Sanskrit literature has myths about cosmic bodies and studying these in the Puranas and the Vedas can help us come up with facts for the archaeo-astronomy project," said Bhagyashree Tarde, project assistant and the Sanskrit expert on the team.

Heading: A day after, residents thank firemen, police - Indian Express
Content:
In A bid to decongest city streets from heavy vehicles, the Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority would soon begin its search for plots in Navi Mumbai and Thane to build truck terminals.

According to Ratnakar Gaikwad, Metropolitan Commissioner, this idea was discussed at a recent meeting of the Unified Mumbai Metropolitan Transport Authority (UMMTA), the apex body working on the overall congestion policy for the city.

"It was discussed to locate land in areas like Navi Mumbai and Thane for truck terminals with more parking spaces to make city truck-free and reduce congestion," said Gaikwad. He added that the trucks could be allowed in the city in non-peak hours from midnight to 7am.

Meanwhile, the highly delayed plan for state-of-the-art truck terminal and an Inter State Bus Terminus (ISBT) at Wadala was finally given a go ahead by the Chief Minster Vilasrao Deshmukh, who heads the MMRDA. "Idea is to decongest areas like Masjid Bunder, Wadi Bunder, Karnak Bunder, where thousands of trucks are parked causing traffic jams through the holistic development of the Wadala Truck Terminal," said Milind Mhaiskar, Additional Metropolitan Commissioner, MMRDA.

Along with the WTT, the plan for the much awaited ISBT also got a nudge from Deshmukh that would facilitate much-needed inter-state connectivity for both private and state transport buses operators. "The tentative designs were presented before the authority prepared by consultants and a go ahead was given. The tendering process is expected to start within 45 days for the construction of both WTT and ISBT on Public-Private Partnership model for a concession period of 10 years," Mhaiskar said.

He added that the concessionaire, that bags the contract to construct and operate the truck terminal and bus terminus, would be charging fees from bus and truck operators using the space for parking vehicles, loading-offloading goods etc.

Around 60 boarding bays will be provided at 45 degree angles for easy manoeuvering with a separate area is proposed for idle bus parking. The truck terminus would have a centralised facility for the transport of goods by road. According to Mhaiskar, around 4,000 buses and trucks are expected to be housed in the nearly 30-hectare plot. It will be designed to have host offices and godowns of transport companies, easy loading and unloading facilities and other facilities like restaurants, etc.

Heading: After 2 yrs, teachers’ representatives to attend MU Senate meet - Indian Express
Content:
Fire brigade came within 15 minutes after the fire broke out; police indeed braved all the odds to help us, say residents

A day after fire broke out in the 100-year-old Johari Mansion on Kalbadevi Road, cooling operations by the Fire Brigade and the police continued full-fledged on Wednesday.

The fire which broke out on Tuesday killed 50-year-old Laxminarayan Baheti and his three-year-old granddaughter Maitri and injured four others. A day after the tragedy, Ramesh Baheti (28), whose family lost two members, applauded the fire brigade's and police's efforts of carrying out a remarkable job. His sentiments were echoed by other residents who claimed that the fire personnel and the police indeed braved all the odds to help them out.

"The fire brigade came within 15 minutes after the fire broke out. We did not expect such prompt service," said one of the shopkeepers, Shiv Tapadia. The building will be slowly opened to the shopkeepers who can gather their belongings.

The fire brigade sent 12 fire engines from Dadar, Fort, Colaba, Byculla and Sewri along with three tankers and an ambulance to tackle the situation. "Needless to say, it was a mayhem, but we took control of the situation by cordoning off the entire area. We stopped traffic coming from Pydhonie Road and Kalbadevi Main Road," said officer-in-charge from Colaba fire brigade, P D Prabhu. According to the fire officials, the fire first broke out in the first floor and immediately spread in the building, damaging the nearby Vrindavan residential building too.

Chief Fire Officer A V Sawant said that main problem faced by the firemen was to control the fire which was spreading fast in a short span of time. "The area is highly congested. Also, Johri Mansion is a wooden structure which is highly inflammable. Since it is an old structure, they had not taken enough fire safety measures. Due to all these factors the fire spread fast and became unmanageable," said Sawant. "As the mansion is in a commercial hub, it had numerous shops selling textiles, mattresses, yarns, furniture etc. All these things easily catch fire. It was difficult to douse the fire because of the presence of these inflammable goods," Prabhu added.

Shopkeepers also clarified that the mansion was a purely commercial hub where no illegal activities took place as reported by certain sections of the media. "This is just a textile and yarn market. It is not a centre for any kind of illegal activities. Such allegations are purely baseless," said shopkeeper Chandra Prakash Tiwari. Fire officials state that investigations will continue for the next ten days and only then can they come to any logical conclusion on what triggered the fire.

Monica Baheti, who flung her child to crowd instinctively in a bid to save her, is currently recuperating at the Bombay Hospital. "Monica got the maximum burns. The doctors will be soon operating on her," said D P Ghatania, a family friend.

Ramesh Baheti said, "I have lost the ones who meant the most to me—my daughter and father. My wife too is recuperating and I am very scared for her." But despite this tragedy, he wants to go back to his house. "This tragedy will not deter me to go back to the same place. It is like my ancestral home and will always hold a special place in my heart," said Ramesh.

His uncle Kishore Baheti agreed with him and said, "We request the authorities to repair the building at the earliest. We want to go back to our homes. Even at the face of this tragedy, everybody helped each other. So we don't fear going back to the place," he said.

Heading: Neeraj Grover murder trial likely to begin today - Indian Express
Content:
After two years, the University of Mumbai's Senate meeting on October 22 will have about two dozen representatives from the teaching community. While only four members of the teachers constituency have been attending the meeting in the last two years, this year it will be attended by 22 teachers' representatives who are considered to be an 'important vocal group'.

"This vocal group had been missing since past two years due to which several important issues were not discussed in the Senate meetings. In fact, the meetings used to be quite short as hardly any real issues were discussed," said Madhu Paranjape, one of the elected senate members and joint-secretary of the Bombay University and College Teachers' Union (BUCTU).

In July 2006, the chancellor of the university had set aside the elections of 17 teachers of the senate on the ground that the university had made illegal changes in the voters list on the eve of the polls in September 2005. On the chancellor's directions, the State appointed a one-member committee headed by Pratima Umarji to probe into the procedural failures on the part of the university that led to setting aside of the elections. In October 2007, the Division Bench of the Bombay High Court had pulled up the university for not conducting the elections. Later re-elections were held in January which were not considered valid after the High Court pointed out that electoral roll had not been updated. The elections were then held in July in which BUCTU won 14 out of 17 seats.

President of the BUCTU, C Sadasivan, said, "We will be raising issues like delay in results, syllabus, fee hike, teachers' appointment, pension, etc." Paranjape added, "Teachers are capable of raising issues that are most relevant to them and the students. They are able to point out lacunae in issues regarding harassment, syllabus, results and others better than any one else. In the past too, BUCTU has been raising several issues through out the year. However, the impact will be more at the senate meeting."

Heading: Cops foil robbery attempt, say motive was to use money to get friend released - Indian Express
Content:
The trial in the sensational murder of senior executive of Synergy-Adlabs Neeraj Grover, in which Kannada actress Mariah Monica Susairaj and her boyfriend and Naval officer Emile Jerome are main accused, is expected to begin in the Sessions Court on Thursday.

The prosecution is likely to submit draft charges to the court against Susairaj and Jerome, along with a list of witnesses which it will be examining to prove their case of murder and destruction of evidence against the two accused.

Jerome's lawyer Raja Thakur said, "Even before the trial begins, Jerome wants an English translated version of the chargesheet as he cannot understand Marathi and he wants to understand what evidence the police has collected." Thakhur added: "Jerome is likely to give me an application to move before the Cochin Naval Command (CNC) saying that as a serving Naval officer he can only be court-martialled in a military court and that a civilian court does not have the authority to try him."

Jerome, along with Susairaj, is charged with murdering Grover at Susairaj's Malad residence on May 8. According to the police, the duo is alleged to have chopped Grover's body into several pieces and disposed it of in the jungles of Manor. They have been in jail since their arrests on May 21. While Jerome was arrested from his Naval station in Cochin, Susairaj was arrested here.

Susairaj has given a confessional statement stating that it was Jerome who stabbed Neeraj to death and later chopped his body into pieces, and she acted on his behest and her role in destruction of the evidence is limited. She has also moved the Bombay High Court seeking bail, which will come up for hearing on October 18. Jerome, on the other hand, has not yet applied for bail.

Heading: Nair family suicide was planned days ahead, suspect police - Indian Express
Content:
The Mulund police who arrested three members of a gang when they were preparing to loot a jewellery shop, late Tuesday night, suspect that the gang was planning to use the money to get one of their accomplices released from jail.

"On Tuesday evening we received a tip-off that a jewellery shop on J N Road may be robbed. When we reached the spot we spotted five youths who were alighting from two motorcycles at the parking lot on Zaver Road. We nabbed them just as they were about to move towards the shop," said police sub-inspector Sanjay Sable, the investigating officer in the case.

The police recovered a revolver, four live rounds and a couple of choppers from the accused- Murthy Thevar, Ramkumar Konar and Satish Kumar Devendra. "Thevar revealed that his brother Raja has been jailed for his role in a robbery and is unable to get himself released. There is a possibility that the gang would have utilised the money from the robbery for his release," said police sub-inspector S V Bhosale who was a part of the team that made the arrest.

The police are also checking the criminal history of the gang. "Such robberies are conducted late in the evening when the jewellery shops are preparing to close. Before shutting down the shop all the jewellery and the cash are kept in a safe. That's when these robbers planned to barge into the shop and threaten the owners to part with the valuables," said Bhosale.

Heading: MMRDA grants extra FSI to buildings at BKC’s G block - Indian Express
Content:
Officers of the Kasturba Marg police station now have reason to believe that the Nair siblings had planned the suicide a couple of days before they took the extreme step. The police reached the possibility, based on the statement given by Sarita Chavan, a maid servant who was working for the Nair family for the past 8 months.

Police Inspector Mitesh Karle from the Kasturba Marg police station, who is the investigating officer in the case said, "When we were taking the statements of everyone acquainted to the family, we also came across a maid servant who had been working at the house of the Nair family. According to her statement, the Nair siblings on October 9 told her not to come the next day. The suicide note written by Suchitra Nair was dated October 10. Hence, it gives reason to believe that the siblings had probably planned it a day or two in advance."

The maid also told the police that while she worked with the Nair family, she did not ever witness the family arguing or discussing anything among themselves. "The maid told us that the family did not talk much among themselves and whenever they did, they used to do it in their mother tongue because of which Sarita could never figure out the general mood of the family members," said Karle.

Karle further said that a lot of books, on a variety of subjects, in English were found from the family's residence but nothing that may be called luxurious.

Another officer said on conditions of anonymity, "From what we have gathered so far, they had probably taken loans from many banks. However, the fact that they were borrowing heavily had probably ruined their credit and in the recent past, a bank had also rejected their loan application. At this stage it would not be prudent to disclose any more details as we are still enquiring further with various banks and financial institutions about how the family availed of loans despite the fact that they had no visible means of income."

Heading: Monorail from BKC to Bandra rly station gets MMRDA’s nod - Indian Express
Content:
The skyline of the city's still developing business district at Bandra-Kurla Complex could grow even taller, as the Special Planning Authority for the area-the Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA) has decided to give an opportunity to its G-Block occupants to use additional floor space index (FSI), on payment of a premium. FSI is the ratio of construction permitted to the size of the plot.

The state government that had in May raised the FSI from two to four on the 178-hectare G-block in BKC has now given a go ahead for institutions to utilise the remaining FSI as per a scheme of payment. According to Ratnakar Gaikwad, Metropolitan Commissioner, MMRDA, the interested parties would be allowed to utilise the FSI by paying 1.5 times of the existing ready reckoner rates of the government that stand at Rs 65,000 per sq metre. "The decision means that corporates, which have already consumed the FSI of two, can build more commercial space if they want. They will have to purchase the additional FSI at 1.5 times the ready reckoner rates prescribed by MMRDA, which comes to around Rs 97,000 per sq meters," Gaikwad said. According to Gaikwad, if all the buildings in this area go in for redevelopment, the MMRDA is expected to earn a whopping Rs 13,000 crore.

Among the projects in G-block that will benefit from this move is the commercial complex and the convention centre of Reliance Industries Ltd that is on a 18.5 acre plot. G-block is at the heart of the finance centre, which also has Citibank, NABARD, ICICI Bank, the Bharat Diamond Bourse, IL&FS, Jet Airways, among others.

Gaikwad added that the corporates and other occupants who want to use the extra FSI would have to pay the MMRDA by March 31, 2009. "They have to pay by the end of this financial year to avail this scheme and whether they want to demolish the existing building. Reconstructing now or later is entirely at their discretion," Gaikwad added. Meanwhile, for those who cannot afford to pay the entire amount in one go, the MMRDA has offered an installment-scheme. "The interested parties can pay the amount in five annual installments with an interest charge of 10 per cent annually," the commissioner added.

The market observers feel that most buildings are likely to go in for this scheme even though the scenario is pretty weak currently things can change two years down the line.

Heading: MGL to set up second supply network terminal at Mahape - Indian Express
Content:
The highest body of the Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA) on Wednesday cleared the proposal for a nine km monorail connecting Bandra-Kurla complex and Bandra railway station.

This project will address the growing demands of a better transportation service in the business district. The monorail route would cover Kalanagar-Diamond Bourse-Bandra station (East) at an estimated cost of around Rs 1,125 crore. Ratnakar Gaikwad, Metropolitan Commissioner, said, "The approval is a major thrust and will cater to BKC's needs of transportation." Once the project starts, the number of commuters, during peak hours, is expected to go up by at least 40,000.

Interestingly, for the first time a financial company has shown interest in funding an infrastructure project. "IDFC has expressed willingness to fund the nine km corridor. Now the pattern to be adopted for implementation of the project would be studied by the MMRDA and then the tendering process would begin," Gaikwad added.

The project would be carried out in two phases. The first stretch from Kala Nagar to Bharat Diamond Bourse is expected to be completed in 18 months of getting a go-ahead while the second phase would be from Bharat Diamond Bourse to Bandra station (east). MMRDA aims to complete the project in three years. Meanwhile, the decision on the first route of monorail in the city is expected to come on Thursday after the Empowered Committee headed by the Chief Secretary takes a call on the financial bids of the sole bidder. According to Milind Mhaiskar, Additional Metropolitan Commissioner, the BKC monorail route is less complicated than the first monorail which goes through congested stretches from Jacob Circle to Chembur via Wadala. "It's a hindrance-free route, simpler than the first one. A second project always has the benefit of experience," Mhaiskar said.

Heading: A monument in Stone - Indian Express
Content:
Availability of Piped Natural Gas (PNG) and Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) in the Mumbai Metropolitan is set to improve in the coming year, as Mahanagar Gas Limited (MGL) is constructing a second city gate station at Mahape in Navi Mumbai.

Currently MGL is providing its services to 3.66 lakh PNG customers and 131 CNG outlets through its single network originating from its city gate station at Wadala. P K Gupta, managing director of MGL, said that the work at the site for the second supply terminal has already commenced and it is expected to become operational by June 2009.

The LNG terminal at Mahape is strategically located to source the Liquid Natural Gas coming in from the LNG port at Dahej, Hajira and Dhabol and also the gas from KG basin. "With the second city gate station we would have two networks and the problem of low pressure can be eliminated as one system takes over the other system which is down," said Gupta.

Once the second city gate station comes into operation, MGL intends to reach out to satellite towns of Kalyan-Dombivli, Ambernath, Badlapur, Khargar, Taloja, Panvel and Roha in Thane and Raigad district.

Gupta said that the demand survey, design and expansion plans for the above mentioned regions have been completed and statutory approvals have also been obtained.

MGL set its foot in Thane in the year 2005 and it has already laid 201.85 km of pipe line catering to 30,434 PNG consumers.

In Thane there are 4945 PNG consumers who are registered and are yet to get their connection .

Eight CNG outlets in Thane cater to the 21,241 vehicles in Thane that have been converted to CNG.

"Currently we have a PNG customer base of 4 lakh for PNG against our capacity to cater to 12 lakh PNG customers. Demand for CNG is 55 per cent of the capacity. There is scope for more additions to the PNG customer base and CNG vehicles," said Gupta. He added that the achievemnet was despite supply deficit conditions and the results will be better once the supply increases.

Heading: Anxious fans wait for Big B’s reply on blog - Indian Express
Content:
Mumbai's aerial landscape will soon offer a view of the world's largest stone monument — the Global Pagoda — which is nearing completion. A replica of the Shwedagon Pagoda in Yangon, Myanmar, one of the most famous and revered Pagodas in the world, the Global Pagoda will have a lot to boast about when it is thrown open to the public later this year. Apart from being the largest stone monument, it is also the largest dome ever built without any supporting pillars.

Built with sandstone from Jodhpur, the construction has involved two sets of workers. While one set works on site in Gorai where the Pagoda is built, another set works in Pindwara, Rajasthan, cutting and dressing the stone so that it arrives at the site in ready-to-fix blocks.

"We have nearly completed the stone work, and by November it should all be done since we are planning a one-day course in December," says R K Aggrawal, administration in charge at the site. "The stones are such that they inter-lock with each other once they are placed, which makes the structure extremely firm," he adds.

The dome, being hollow unlike its counterpart, the Shwedagon Pagoda, allows 8000 people to be seated and meditate within. The centre of the dome will have an elevated, circular stage, which will act as a turntable, completing a rotation in approximately half-an-hour.

"This is done so that everyone present can see Acharya S N Goenka, who is behind this project, as he is conducting the Vipassana," says Aggrawal. The size of the dome is twice as large as the Gol Gumbaz dome in Bijapur, which used to be the largest hollow dome in the world.

"The entire construction is done in a way that allows Buddha's teachings to come through. It goes from a broad base to a needle at the top. Starting with an octagonal construction, then a hexagon, a circle, a cylinder and a crystal symbolising a needle at the very top of the entire structure," says M M Khandhar, an engineer and mediatator associated with the project. The centre of the dome has a large flower-shaped motif plated in real gold.

Genuine relics of Buddha, bones donated by the Mahabodhi society have been enshrined in the Global Pagoda. The site will also have two smaller Pagodas beside it. "Though these smaller Pagodas have no real functional purpose, they will be used to display information about Buddha and about other meditation courses etc," says Khandhar.

There will also be a meditation centre, where Buddha's teachings will be disseminated and ten-day courses will be made available to those interested. "The Burmese initially modelled their pagodas after the Shanti Stupa as a means of expressing their gratitude since it was from India that the Buddha set out. Now we are showing the Burmese gratitude for bringing his teachings back to us," Khandhar adds.

Heading: BMC to clarify on additional expenses incurred in civic polls last year - Indian Express

Unable to repay a trade debt to a fellow businessman, a 46- year-old man from Navi Mumbai murdered the lender at the deceased's office at Kalamboli. Pradeep Modi (46), a businessman dealing in steel came all the way from Goregaon in Mumbai to the office of Kishor Garodiya at Kalamboli to recover the dues that arose out of business transactions.

According to the investigating officer, police inspector J D Tambe, Modi had been relentlessly trying to recover his dues from Garodiya for the last four months. Modi turned up at Garodiya's office located on the first floor of Steel Chambers at Kalamboli, in order to recover Rs 40 lakh.

Garodiya had a kitchen knife and a hammer with him in the office. "The fact that he had come prepared with the weapon to murder indicates that he had pre-planned the crime and it was not in the heat of the moment," said inspector Tambe.

A long argument over the payment of dues ensued between the two inside the office. There was a third person inside the office as well. At 4 pm, Garodiya chose to end the argument by clubbing Modi with the hammer and then stabbing him with the kitchen knife.

Four hours later at 8:25 pm Garodiya walked into the Kalamboli police station and informed police sub-inspector Dattarray Khade (39) that he had murdered a person and the body was lying in his office. Garodiya has been remanded to police custody till October 22. According to Kalamboli police, Garodiya who is a resident of the posh NRI complex at Seawoods, Nerul, does not have any previous criminal records.

"Through interrogation we would try to find out what he did in the hours after committing the crime till the time of surrender. We are also trying to ascertain if he had any other accomplice in the murder," added inspector Tambe.

Heading: 60-year-old man dies in police custody - Indian Express
Content:
The election held last year to elect 247 corporators to the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation has now come under the scanner of the state Election Commission. While the total expenditure for the election was over Rs 19.09 crore, the civic body had spent additional Rs 4.38 on every voter during the civic election. Not satisfied with the reasoning of civic officials, the Election Commission has now sought immediate clarification from the BMC regarding the additional expenses.

According to the commission, the BMC has spent more money than what had actually been sanctioned for the election.

A letter dispatched to BMC on October 10 has asked the election department to explain about these expenses. While the civic administration has already given a clarification earlier, the election department says it has not been satisfied with their reasoning.

"It is informed that the rise in price of election equipment and stationery has led to additional expenditure in 2007, but during 2002 election, the expenditure was mere 0.17 paise on every voter taking the total expenses to over Rs 13 crore only. For setting up of voting centres, expenditure on every voter is Rs 7.06 more than what the commission had sanctioned for," the letter stated. "However, this election, the expenditure looks more," it added.

The commission has sought 'immediate clarification' from the BMC regarding the issue. Civic officials said that the clarification will be sent soon.

"While the reasons for the additional expenditure have already been sent, we will examine the expenditure on the points raised by the commission," said Joint Municipal Commissioner (election) S S Shinde.

P K Nair gets Satyajit Ray Memorial Award for archiving cinematic gems

In the Sixties, P K Nair made a trip to Kolhapur to meet a grocery shop owner. The latter had prints of Baburao Painter's films made in the 1920s. These films of the silent era are a significant part of India's cinematic heritage and were untraceable for years. Nair failed to convince the shop owner, who was asking for a hefty price, to hand over the black-and-white reels. However, some years later the shop owner's son, impressed by Nair's zeal to preserve cinematic works, handed over Painter's films to the National Film Archive of India (NFAI) for free.

This former NFAI director's dogged pursuance in collecting and preserving films earned him 'the Henry Langlois of India' tag. Langlois, a Frenchman, was a pioneer in film preservation and restoration. On Thursday, Nair's three-decade-long work it will earn him the Satyajit Ray Memorial Award. At the inaugural function of the 7th Third Eye Asian Film Festival, Nair will be honoured along with South Korean director Park Swang Su. This award was conferred on Aruna Vasudev last year and Prof Satish Bahadur in 2006.

Collecting film photographs and magazines was childhood hobby of Nair. But only after facing disillusionment while working in the Mumbai film industry that he took up archiving seriously. He moved to Pune in March 1961 to help build resources for the Film and Television Institute of India (FTII). Four years later, he found himself collecting and restoring films for the newly-built NFAI. "By then, nearly 70 per cent of the films made before 1950 were damaged or lost," he recalls.

The NFAI started with only 124 films. By the time he retired in 1991, it has grown into a veritable treasure of 12,000 Indian as well as foreign films. Collecting these works, took him place like Chor Bazar, defunct studios and film laboratories abroad. Sometimes people were forthcoming like Dadasaheb Phalke's family. They gave away remnants of seven of his films. "Of them, only Kaliya Mardan was intact," Nair says.

This avid collector is also credited for taking film appreciation courses beyond the boundaries of academic institutions. He held workshops at film societies across India. He also helped set up film circulation libraries, introducing film-buffs to the masters of world cinema.

Though a lot of attention is paid to the preservation of films now, Nair is not in favour the use of digital technology.

"The digital technologies should be used only for restoration. Celluloid works best when it comes to preservation," he says.

Heading: Double bonanza - Indian Express
Content:
Mister Behram and Other Plays puts the spotlight on Gieve Patel, the dramatist

Decades have passed since the talented cast and crew of Princes, Savaksa and Mister Behram took a bow. Their stage run might come to a halt, but their life on the shelf has just begun. The three plays, written by Gieve Patel, were back in the reckoning when the compilation Mister Behram and Other Plays hit bookstands recently.

Now, with the book out—it was released recently at Crossword, Kemps Corner— Patel hopes his plays will enjoy the spotlight again. "The plays are now available to theatre enthusiasts. Some group might stage them again," he says. The three plays are the only ones he wrote. And the Parsi community remained his constant inspiration. "If we takes a close look at a small group and write intimately about it, the writing acquires a universal character," he says, a Parsi himself.

When he writes his next play, Mumbai will seep into the Parsi story, predicts Patel. But he can't predict when he would get down to writing it. "I have the material for it for some time now but don't know when I would start working on the play." After Mister Behram in 1987, Patel hasn't gone back to writing plays. "I'm a slow writer. Each one of them took seven-eight years. Writing a play might have lasted two years, but preparations for them look longer," he admits. The book contains photographs of the productions taken by Madhu Gadkari and old interviews of Patel on his plays.

Apart from the rich use of spoken language as a basic instrument of

theatre, what made Patel's plays memorable was the association of Mumbai theatre's who's who. Pearl Padamsee directed Princes in March 1970 and Alyque Padamsee played the lead role apart from designing its sets and lights. Nearly 12 years later, Pearl directed Patel's second play Savaksa which opened in 1982. Mister Behram, which premiered at the Bombay Arts Festival in 1987 was directed by Toni Patel.

Theatre had this 68-year-old doctor-artist fascinated since his school days. This became a passion while studying at St Xavier's College. But itfound the right direction and guidance only when he started assisting the legendary Ebrahim Alkazi. "Though I mostly worked backstage,

I learnt a lot from him," Patel says. But the characters of his plays are something he has pick up from the people around him. "I have fictionalised their stories and blended them in my dramas," says Patel.

While the plays have come in long intervals, this medical practitioner has been consistent in expressing himself on the canvas. Poetry too takes up some of his creative hours and the poetry workshop in Rishi Valley School has been keeping his January schedule full for a decade. "For the last two years, I have stopped practising medicine. It's mostly painting that keeps me occupied while writing remains quite sporadic."

Heading: The dark knight - Indian Express
Content:
It will be twins for socialite Ramona Narang and Bruno Rodella

Socialite Ramona Narang, who tied the knot with businessman Bruno Rodella in February last year, will soon have the stork visiting. She confirmed the news from her Singapore home and said that she was overjoyed twice over for she is expecting twins—a boy and a girl. "I began to cry when I found out about the twins; I was so overwhelmed!" she said.

Mumbai's quintessential Powder Puff girl, Ramona is happy to give the parties a miss till the babies come. "There are days when nausea keeps me in bed all day long and I just have to sleep through it. But I do pamper myself, indulge in my favourite foods and rest a lot," she said.

The expectant mother isn't sporting a prominent bump yet but has her shopping list ready. She is, however, yet to decide where she will head with her shopping bags. "A bigger, better and child-friendly house tops my list and I have been busy

looking," she smiled.

What also keeps her busy is her workout schedule. "My appetite has gone up and I have put on seven kilos over the last four months. I want to be a healthy mother but not an overweight one," she elaborates. Her diet currently comprises light Japanese and Thai meals "as Indian food feels heavy". Narang is however, glad that she has had no cravings so far, "so no bingeing on chocolates or spicy food".

Narang has settled well in Singapore and travels to Hong Kong and Thailand pretty often. She has even made a new set of friends in Singapore. But she misses the ones back in

India. "Some of them were here for the F1 race and we had a great time," she smiles.

The glam girl is expected to be in Mumbai with her family for her delivery in March next year and plans to have her baby shower in Mumbai as well as Delhi for she has friends in both cities. "I want to be with my family for the last three months of my pregnancy. There is no place like home, after all," she adds.

Till then, Bruno is doing everything possible to make his expecting wife comfortable. "He's around as much as possible so he can be part of the experience and we do everything together—it feels like we're both pregnant," she laughs.

SHOP TILL YOU DROP: This is one thing every body has a voracious appetite for. And the best part on karva chauth you have a licence to splurge. Clothes, shoes, accessories, stores have some swell bargains at hand. At Zevar, Sector 22, there's an assured gift with every purchase. Instead of gold, go for silver at Silver Haze. At Harri Hyperstore, Sector 26, and Tango, Sector 35, discounts are on cosmetic and skin-care products. Chief, Sector 19, promises a wallet with every purchase of Rs 1,000. At Catwalk, women's wear has a 25 per cent off while at Landmark, Panchkula, you can win gifts worth lakhs. Buy a purse from Virus Store, Sector 22, and you'll get a digital stress buster!

TIME-PASS: How to kill a long day? You can watch a movie. Of course, it's Himesh Reshammiya's Karzzzz. For non-movie buffs, the Vanity Fair at Whispering Willows should be the place to be seen at. Parade Ground, Sector 17, has CII's fair and there's Tamil Nadu's cultural extravaganza Poompuhar-2008. For cricket fans, the test match between India and Australia at PCA stadium, Mohali, should be a great option.

Fast and feast!

Heading: Aamir plus - Indian Express
Content:
Shatrughan Sinha's daughter is showstopper for a menswear line

It's a menswear collection that explores the element of androgyny, but Sonakshi Sinha, daughter of yesteryear actors Shatrughan Sinha and Poonam, thinks it is just right for her ramp debut. "My role is to embody that element of femininity in the male psyche," says the 20-year-old, who will model for Kolkata-based designers Dev 'r' Nil for their Lakme Fashion Week show in Mumbai on October 22.

Sinha, who has known the designers for about three years, have often helped them backstage. "We have been saying that she should consider modelling. This time when we asked her to walk for us, she agreed," says Nil, adding, "Since this is our first menswear collection, we wanted the right personality to project the theme. She fits the bill splendidly with her height and strong personality."

Sinha, in fact, has worked hard on her look. "The concept requires me to look toned and fit so I have been gymming regularly and have lost a lot of weight," she shrugs.

Even though this will be Sinha's first stint in the limelight, she is unfazed. "I have been groomed since I was born, thanks to both my parents. It is not something that I have had to work for," says Sinha, who has just graduated in design from the SNDT Women's University, Mumbai, and hopes to launch her own designer label in a few years' time.

Film offers, says Sinha, have been coming in for a while, but she'd rather let her parents do the choosing. "I won't be allowed to do anything and everything. Thus, I have left the decision to them. I know whatever they decide will be the best for me."Good girl.

Heading: Subhash Sarovar to be developed as a tourist spot - Indian Express
Content:
Keeping faithfully to his code of casual chic, Aamir Khan cut quite a dashing figure at the launch of Tata Sky's new interactive feature, Tata Sky +, at the Grand Hyatt, Santa Cruz, on October 14. The handsome actor, who is Tata Sky's brand ambassador and the star of the much talked about 'Ardhnarishwar' Tata Sky ad, declared that life is indeed "jingalala" for him now that Tata Sky has launched its latest feature. "The new feature ensures that TV fits into my hectic life, by allowing me to record my favourite programmes and watch them at leisure," the Khan said. But that's just brand loyalty, isn't it Aamir?

Showstopper Aamir of course, who still retains those boyish good looks at 40+.

Heading: Mamata weighs Cong option - Indian Express
Content:
The next time you plan to visit the neglected lake near Beliaghata, you might just have to pay an entry charge.

Subhash Sarovar — the lake in Beliaghata that has long been an object of neglect is all set to be revived. In a first of its kind joint venture between the Kolkata Improvement Trust (KIT) and West Bengal Tourism Development Corporation (WBTDC), the lake area will be converted into a tourist destination.

"We have decided to develop the area as it can be a major tourist attraction," said TVN Rao, Managing Director, WBTDC. He added that the city needed more destinations for water sports like speed boats and paragliding. The centre has also allotted a sum of about 5 crores for the project, he said.

The lake under KIT will be developed by the WBTDC in a public private partnership.

Of the allotted sum, about Rs 144 lakhs will be spent on landscaping of the area and construction of a children's park. The area will have shelters for tourists with gardens and benches.

WBTDC also plans to market the place as a destination for picnics and fishing. "We have plans to make 30 decks for anglers, bedsides a felicitation centre and an open air performance centre. Once we complete the infrastructure, the space will be leased out to a private party," said Rao. The ticket counters will be located at the entry gate along with other offices.

"We have received the proposal from WBTDC and hope that work can be started early next year," said Ashok Chattopadhyay, officer on special duty, KIT. Officials at WBTDC informed that this was the first time that the company had taken up the development of a lake in Kolkata. The price of tickets and other modalities are currently being worked on.

Heading: Tatas gone, but who will own the land now? - Indian Express
Content:
Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee's recent visits to Delhi and parleys with top Congress leaders have triggered possibilities of a new equation in the state's politics. Banerjee's increasing proximity to senior Congress leaders is being viewed as a prelude to an electoral understanding between the two parties for the forthcoming Lok Sabha polls.

During her latest visit to Delhi, Banerjee had met Congress president Sonia Gandhi. Officially, it was described as a discussion over the Singur issue, but sources in the Pradesh Congress and the Trinamool said both parties are likely to forge an electoral alliance and a seat-sharing agreement in Bengal.

When asked about frequent meetings of Banerjee with Congress leaders like Prime Minister Manmohan Singh and Sonia Gandhi, Dinesh Dwivedi, a senior TMC leader based in Delhi, said: "Till now, our policy has been to maintain equal distance with the Congress and the BJP. But the reason that we opposed the Congress was because they had an alliance with the CPM." He added, "That hurdle (CPM) is not there now. It seems that the Congress understood the real face of the CPM."

Dwivedi, a Rajya Sabha member, said: "Banerjee's Delhi visit also aimed at dispelling the anti-industry image of the party, as well as underlining the fact that Ratan Tata had become the mouth piece of the CPM."

Trinamool sources said Samajwadi Party leader Amar Singh is playing a key role in bringing the two parties together. He visited the state a number of times recently and even shared the dais with Mamata Banerjee during her Singur protest. Senior Trinamool leaders said an electoral alliance with the Congress was a logical conclusion considering the recent developments. "The CPM and the Congress have split. Though nothing has been finalised now, we can certainly move ahead with the Congress," said a party leader.

The two sides are working on several equations. Considering the better position of the Congress in Malda, Murshidabad and districts like North and South Dinajpur, the Trinamool is willing to adjust seats in these areas. The two parties are focusing on seat adjustment rather than a merger. The only mantra is to ensure a one-to-one contest with the Left candidates. 

The Trinamool is also banking on the Muslim population, who had voted for the party in the last panchayat polls.  "A considerable section of the Muslims is with us, be it because of the land for industry issues or Rizwanur Rehman's case. If we now opt for the BJP, they will not remain with us. Therefore, secular Congress is a better choice," said a senior party leader.

Trinamool leaders said unlike the panchayat polls, division of votes will emerge as an important factor in the LS elections. "We do not want anti-Left votes to be divided in the state. Even though our popularity is growing in rural Bengal, the division of vote is a critical issue we may face this time," said a leader. Lower-ranking workers of the party have already asked Banerjee to go for a tie-up with the Congress at the grassroot level.

Heading: Hills tense over GJM’s new diktat - Indian Express
Content:
Even after the Tata Motors decided to pull out its Nano plant from Singur, the land in question not only faces an uncertain future, but there is also little possibility of it being returned to the farmers.

The state government has already announced that though the Tatas have decided to quit, the government will not abandon its plan of utilising the land for "some other industrial projects". In the government's scheme of things, returning the land to the farmers does not seem to be a priority, said a senior official of the Commerce and Industries department.

The status of the land, meanwhile, remains legally encumbered. Between September and December 2006, as many as 11 public interest litigations (PIL) have been filed in the Calcutta High Court, challenging the land acquisition process at Singur. After a series of hearing, the High Court had observed on January 18 that the land acquisition process for setting up the small car project by the Tata Motors was "legally valid".

Following this, seven petitioners had filed special leave petitions (SLP) in the Supreme Court challenging the verdict passed by the Calcutta High Court. Now, the case is pending before a bench of the Supreme Court. Tata Motors had also filed an application for participating in the legal battle in the Supreme Court. The case is likely to come up for hearing in October-November.

On July 21, 2006, the district magistrate had issued a notification for acquiring 997.11 acres at Singur. Finally, land was acquired by the state government on October 4, 2006. The district magistrate had taken possession of the said land, which stood vested under the Land Acquisition Act with the state government.

According to the affidavit filed by the West Bengal Industrial Development Corporation (WBIDC) in the Supreme Court, 265 acres have already been leased out to 50 vendors for setting up ancillary units. Even after the pullout, 645.67 acres are still in the possession of Tata Motors. The concerned land could not be used by any party other than the Tata Motors until the lease deed between WBIDC and Tata is repealed. The same applies to the remaining 265 acres which have been leased out to the vendors.

Heading: 2 more die due to dengue; KMC clueless about fresh cases - Indian Express
Content:
The Gorkha Janamukti Morcha's (GJM) programme to change signboards at government offices and public utilities from "Government of West Bengal" to "Gorkhaland" from October 17 has generated fresh tension in the Hills.

According to GJM leaders, the people, including government officials, will voluntarily accept the transition. The district administration, however, is keeping a silent watch over the prevailing situation.

State Home Secretary Asok Mohan Chakrabarti, at a meeting on Monday in Siliguri, advised the administration against any crackdown should the GJM activists attempt to change or deface government signboards.

Darjeeling District Magistrate Surendra Gupta maintained if government servants were to participate in this, it would be much easier to penalise them than the GJM activists.

"It will make my job easier because as government employees, they will have no excuse. The home secretary has made it clear that changing signboards to Gorkhaland is totally illegal," Gupta said.

GJM Secretary Roshan Giri, however, said: "Most officials in the district administration support us. Our party members will not change the signboards. We have asked the officials to do it in their respective offices. This also extends to offices of the Darjeeling Gorkha Hill Council and commercial establishments such as hotels and shops."

On Wednesday, the home secretary told mediapersons in Kolkata that the state government does not want to take police action against the GJM's "non-cooperation movement" in order to maintain a favourable atmosphere for the next round of tripartite talks scheduled for November in Delhi.

"The government is worried about the situation in the Hills," Chakrabarti said. A counter movement is brewing in the foothills of Darjeeling in favour of the Sixth Schedule by the Adivasi Vikas Parishad, he added.

Roshan Giri of GJM, however, refuted AVP's stand, saying the CPM was instigating a section of the Dooars-based tribals against the GJM. "Our movement aims at showing that we are different from West Bengal, and we're sure it won't hamper the ongoing talks," he said.

Heading: Vendors want their money refunded - Indian Express
Content:
At a time when deaths owing to several vector-borne diseases, including dengue, malignant malaria and Japanese Encephalitis (JE), are on the rise in the city, the health department of the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) is divided over the contents of reports confirming JE and dengue deaths.

Instead of taking preventive measures, Subodh Dey, Member Mayor in Council (MMiC), Health, and Debdwaipayan Chattopadhyay, Chief Medical and Health Officer, are at loggerheads over the report of the School of Tropical Medicine (STM) on JE.

Chattopadhay had written to the director of National Vector-borne Disease Control Programme for scrutinising the report of STM, mentioning that there is no paddy field and piggery within six kilometers of the residence of Pralay Choudhury, who had died of JE.

On Wednesday, Dey visited the residence of Choudhury, and said there are several piggeries and paddy fields near his residence, which are the breeding ground of JE. There is a private slaughter house nearby and many people keep their pigs in their houses, he said.

While the MMiC may be trying to prove the CMHO wrong, he does not seem to be taking an interest in the recent developments of vector-borne diseases in the city. In fact, the civic body does not even have information about recent dengue deaths and fresh cases.

On Tuesday, two deaths due to dengue were reported. Sandip Chanda (20) died of dengue at a private nursing home in north Kolkata and Himadri Adhikari (34), a resident of Budge Budge, died in a private nursing home in south Kolkata.

Ishika Saha, a resident of Beliaghata, was admitted to the B R Singh Hospital three days ago after being diagnosed as suffering from dengue. "The KMC does not coordinate with the hospitals. The health department cannot even say how many dengue cases have been reported in the city," said Jhuma Das, Councillor, ward 34.

When asked about the situation, Subodh Dey said on Wednesday that the civic body will set up a malaria clinic in ward 126, where Choudhury died of JE. "The number of health workers will be increased in the vector-prone wards," added a senior health official.

Heading: 11-year-old boy’s body recovered from pond - Indian Express
Content:
With the Tatas gradually dismantling their machinery at Singur, most vendors have decided to move the West Bengal Industrial Development Corporation (WBIDC) to get their investment refunded.

Around 21 companies manufacturing ancillary parts had taken land on lease from the WBIDC to set up their establishments in the vendor park, adjacent to the small car factory.

"We had leased seven acres from the WBIDC and 95 per cent of our work had been done. We will write to the corporation stating that we would like to return the land and get a refund for the same," said Udayan Banerjee, ED, Sharda Motor Industries.

Till date, none of the vendor companies have received any official word from the Tatas about their relocation to Sanand in Gujarat where the Nano car factory will be set up.

Many vendor companies, including Rucha, Mayur Industries and Endurance, said before taking any step they are waiting for the meeting with Tata Motors authorities to be held at the Taj Mahal hotel in Mumbai on October 16.

Sources said the vendors' meet will begin with the Tata authorities addressing the Nano car vendors at 10:30 am. This will be followed by an open meeting with vendors from all companies.

"We will move the WBIDC. But we are waiting for directives from the Tatas on Thursday," said a source from Endurance Technologies Pvt Ltd.

Mayur Enterprise, which had leased 1.8 acres land at Singur and was supposed to supply sunwisers and bellows for the small car, plans to write a letter to the corporation expressing its willingness to return the leased plot.

"Ideally we would like to get a refund. We will be writing to the WBIDC on Friday," said Rajesh Gupta, managing director of Mayur Enterprise.

Subrata Gupta, MD, WBIDC said refund was possible if vendors wanted to return the land.

"I have not yet received any such request. But if a vendor wants to return the land, it is possible," he said.

Heading: Job cut by Jet: 21 hit in Kolkata - Indian Express
Content:
There was tension in Agarpara on Wednesday after the body of an 11-year-old boy was found in a pond. Locals alleged that Abhijoy Mullick was killed by his father and stepmother and later thrown into the pond.

Following the incident, infuriated locals gathered at the Mullick residence and agitated against his death. Police have, meanwhile, initiated a suo motu case.

"Though no complaint has been lodged, we have initiated a suo motu case to check how the boy died. We are waiting for the postmortem report," said Belghoria police station inspector-in-charge Shyamal Ghosh. He added that the body did not have any external mark of injury.

Police said Abhijoy had gone out to play with his friends on Tuesday morning but did not return home. After a search, his father Sanjoy Mullick filed a missing diary at the Belghoria police station.

When the police officers came to Sanjoy's house to inquire, they were accompanied by angry locals who alleged that the boy used to be tortured by his parents. The boy's father had remarried after his first wife died in 2004.

The police then started a search for Abhijoy. Questioning his friends, police learnt that he was last seen playing near a pond. A rescue team finally fished out his body late in the night.

On Wednesday, some locals alleged that after his mother's death, Abhijoy had inherited land, on which Sanjoy had started constructing houses and was planning to start a real estate business.

"The boy's maternal uncles were asking him not to sign on documents but his stepmother wanted the property. It was a planned murder to get his property," alleged a local.

The locals staged an agitation in the area to protest against the boy's death which continued for an hour. Later, a huge contingent of police intervened and controlled the mob.

Police, however, said only the autopsy report would reveal whether the boy was killed or not. "So far we have not found any evidence that he was killed. Apparently it seems that he had drowned," said an investigating officer.

Girl commits suicide
A teenager allegedly committed suicide at Patharpratima in Diamond Harbour after her father could not afford to buy her a new saree for Lakshmi Puja. Jogamaya Gayen (15), a Class IX student of Gobindarampur High School, had requested her father to buy her a new saree for Lakshmi Puja. Sukesh Gayen, her father, who works as an agricultural labourer, scolded her after he failed to fulfil her wishes. An upset Jogamaya took her life by consuming poison. Her body has been sent for postmortem.

Heading: Dasgupta warns against investing in foreign banks - Indian Express
Content:
With Jet Airways announcing a second set of job cuts, about 21 cabin crew — who were based in Kolkata — will also be out of employment very soon, CITU leader Pranab Chakraborty said.

The move came a day after Jet's crucial strategic alliance with Kingfisher Airways.

"For the last two days I have been de-rostered and have not been allotted any flight. My base manager informed that I am one of the people who will soon be receiving their termination letters," said Rudra Ghurung, a flight attendant with Jet Airways.

This time Jet has announced a total of 600 job cuts throughout India. Last month too Jet had sacked 1,200 employees, mainly ground staff, including 71 employees from India.

Jet Airways employees will be participating in a rally on October 16 at the Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport.

MP Amitabh Nandy, meanwhile, called this job cut illegal and said they may stop Jet flights from going out of Kolkata.

Heading: BESU students prepare vision plan for civic improvement - Indian Express
Content:
State Finance Minister Asim Dasgupta on Wednesday advised people not to deposit money in foreign banks or foreign insurance companies considering the crash in the share market.

Dasgupta was of the view that the private banks which have tie-ups with foreign banks were also not safe for investment purposes.

On the prevailing situation of the share market, Dasgupta said foreign banks were responsible for the setback in the market. People should deposit money in nationalised banks and insurance companies, advised Dasgupta.

Dasgupta also felt that the steps taken by the Union finance ministry as well as the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) were not sufficient to revive the economy. The ministry should have slashed the interest rates of nationalised banks on loans given to industries, trading and agriculture sectors, he added.

The minister also claimed that the price rise would not have taken place if the interest rates were slashed by the Union finance ministry.

Dasgupta demanded that the Centre slash the price of petrol and diesel, as well as other petroleum products, as the price of crude oil has fallen in the international market.

Such measures could strengthen the economy, he added.

After the crash in the share market, the RBI had taken steps to increase the inflow of money in the market. Reacting to it, Dasgupta said it is not advisable to take such a step at this stage.

Heading: Thief lynched by mob - Indian Express
Content:
The students of the Bengal Engineering and Science University (BESU) have submitted a vision plan, "Plan for Development of KMC Area by 2025", to bring the city at par with international standards.

The KMC had requested BESU to conduct the study in 2006 for a spatial plan to improve the core infrastructure of the city like drainage, water pipelines, traffic and transport.

The Rs 17 lakh vision plan emphasizes on the improvement of traffic and transport in the city by increasing the inner city mobility and accessibility. The civic body has been suggested by BESU to construct more mass transit that can be used for public transport.

"The study reveals that some places in the city, including Salt Lake, are planned for individual vehicle transit. There is no scope for public transport. According to the study, the civic body has to prepare an action plan to make more use of public transport and plan new roads accordingly," said Dipankar Ganguly, director general, town planning department, KMC.

The study also stresses on improving water transport. A senior civic official said: "For improving water transport, the canals and the rivers need to have proper navigation. But, the city canals have not been desilted since ages. In this condition, improving water transport is very difficult in the city unless desiltation of canals starts."

It also suggests that the civic body should prepare an action plan on water supply.

The study says that although the generation of water is satisfactory in the city, the distribution of water must improve.

Heading: State government to recruit teachers without resolving PTTI crisis - Indian Express
Content:
Angry residents of a locality in South 24-Parganas lynched a member of a gang of thieves, who had killed a resident while allegedly trying to steal livestock late on Tuesday. District police officers said the twin killings took place a little after 11 pm in Kumropara in the Raidighi police station area.

Raidighi Officer-in-Charge Ratan Chakraborty said the thieves had tried to steal goats from the farm of one Babulal Bhandari, who also runs a fishery and guards the farm himself. Upon spotting the miscreants, the 65-year-old raised an alarm for help. It was then that one of the thieves hit him on the head with a weapon, killing him.

"But the locals had already been alerted. The miscreants didn't have enough time to escape and one of them was caught by the people who beat him to death. The rest managed to escape under the cover of darkness. As such, the gang has no criminal record but we have received reports in the recent past that they have been involved in several cases of theft and robbery," Chakraborty said.

Police said they were working on some leads to apprehend the other members of the gang, although no arrests have been made as yet.

Heading: Post retirement: Sourav unlikely for Ranji Trophy - Indian Express
Content:
Caught in the crisis of the Primary Teachers Training Institutes (PTTIs) in the state, in which the fate of nearly 75,000 students hangs in balance, the school education department is keen on recruiting primary teachers in schools without resolving the issue.

"We have been waiting for the court order for the last few years. Now our prime objective is to appoint primary teachers in state schools," said School Education Minister Partha De.

The minister said the government will come out with an advertisement and will appoint teachers subsequently.

On the issue of thousands of students caught in the crisis, the minister said the government is ready to return their fees and the department has sought an appointment with the Central government and the National Council for Teachers Education (NCTE) on the issue.

The Calcutta High Court verdict on October 1 declared the certificates awarded by the 122 PTTIs in the state functioning without the approval of the NCTE to be invalid.

The office of the Chief Minister, meanwhile, invited a delegation of the students of the PTTIs protesting at Metro Channel to submit their memorandum of demands today. Leader of the Opposition Partha Chatterjee said the state government will have to arrange for the recognition of the degrees of all students of the PTTIs in the state that have been de-recognised by a recent ruling of the Calcutta High Court.

Alleging that members of the ruling party have made money by giving permission to illegal PTTIs, Chatterjee urged the state government to punish the people responsible for the mess and bail out the students involved in the crisis.

Addressing a gathering of students of the primary teachers training institutes at Metro Channel, the TMC leader suggested that a delegation of the students should meet the Governor, Gopalkrishna Gandhi, and explain the issue to him. "I will bring this up on the first day of the Assembly session. As students you should be united and carry on the democratic protests," he told the delegation.

Heading: Favourites surge ahead in Asian junior meet - Indian Express
Content:
CAB's efforts notwithstanding, Sourav Ganguly is unlikely to play for Bengal after his retirement from international cricket. Though the state association is still harbouring hopes that the former India captain will come to assist Bengal should they finish atop in the Plate Group of the Ranji Trophy and get a chance to rub shoulders with the Elites from the quarter-final stage onwards, chief selector Sambaran Banerjee is not too sure.

"I will definitely request him once he returns after the Test series, but I tell you, it's very difficult to motivate for a lower level once you are through with international cricket," Banerjee told the The Indian Express. "This is specially true for a player of his stature," he added.

The question is, how best can Sourav's expertise be utilised for Bengal cricket after his retirement? Bengal cricket fraternity feels that the CAB should give him a patient hearing and listen to his plans that will help Bengal cricket prosper .

A story is also doing the rounds that Sourav might take to cricket administration after he hangs up his boots.

Sourav's family has had been into cricket administration for many years. His father Chandi Ganguly was a former CAB office bearer and headed the board of trustees. His brother Snehasish was a CAB assistant secretary during Prasun Mukherjee's regime. Will Sourav toe the line?

Grapevine has it that a section of the BCCI wants Sourav in the Bengal cricket administration, simply to put pressure on Jagmohan Dalmiya. Sourav had earlier voiced his displeasure over Dalmiya's functioning. However, there is no confirmation from any quarter.

A former BCCI official, who preferred anonymity, felt that Sourav would hardly make an impact if he comes to cricket politics. "Sports administration is a different ball game altogether. A good player doesn't always make a good administrator," he told this daily.

Former Bengal captain Gopal Bose concurs. "I don't think cricket administration is his cup of tea, simply because an administrator has to depend on his confidants to run the show. He should take to expert commentary and column writing that are his forte," Bose said.

National selector Raja Venkat, on the other hand, feels that the CAB, under its present dispensation will "hardly do anything" to use Sourav's experience and quality.

Sourav's spat with CAB president Dalmiya is well documented. But the fact is, Sourav has time and again said that he had nothing against Dalmiya but was not satisfied with the way some of his associates behaved. Dalmiya, too, has never said a word against the southpaw.

For the best interests of Bengal cricket, the two must join hands.

Heading: Book Wise? - Indian Express
Content:
In veterans' event, Dilip Kumar posts comfortable win

Top seed Vishal Passi, third seed Shaikh Abdullah, Md Azhar and second seed Abhishek Alla — moved to the semi finals of the boys event in the second edition of the Asian Under-14 Tennis Tournament that is being played at the courts of the Bengal Tennis Association (BTA). The tournament is being held under the sanction of the All India Tennis Association (AITA) and the Asian Tennis Federation (ATF).

In the girls' matches the semi-finals, the line-up is top seed Amrita Mukherjee, fourth seed C Sai Samitha, Simran Kaur Sethi and fifth seed Rimpledeep Kaur. Simran ousted the eighth seed Roma Chandiran 3-6, 6-4, 6-4.
