Poverty degenerates and does so without leaving any scope for sympathy. Adiga's narrator Balram Halwai's story is a sad, almost tragic one, of how the victim becomes the victimiser because he has no second choice. We admire Balram, even knowing he is a criminal. But we don't withdraw in pity and fear because there is only thus far we can approach him in the first place. Yet he speaks to us, by dictating letters to Wen Jiabao who plans to visit India to learn about entrepreneurship — letters about the India in darkness visible. Adiga's nuanced and sometimes blunt details are every bit necessary for the story; they are not meant to create "atmosphere" and "effect". It is these details and Balram's story that make the book dramatic, and also an indictment of society for failing its citizens. Everybody is guilty and a thin line separates the law-abiding but desperate man from temptation and capitulation. But while everybody is a thief not everyone is the white tiger — the survivor who lives to tell the tale.

Adiga's triumph is not only in capturing that India which hasn't changed since the Nehruvian era, an India Adiga studied on his travels, but also in making the generic appear particular and vice versa, not therefore as the whole hog but as an amalgamation of most of the subterranean territory the Balram Halwais inhabit.

Now that he's won the Booker, the fourth debutant novelist to do so, and over the likes of Amitav Ghosh and Sebastian Barry, people will trash the award or multiply for him the 700 per cent rise in sales the shortlisted books had seen recently. Readerly common sense says the Book will outlast the Booker. And one must necessarily pay little attention to such awards and yet have the nose to recognise the good book from the bad. What matters is not what the Booker says about the bright book of life but what the reader finds in it.

sudeep.paul@expressindia.com

Heading: PM expresses ‘concern’ over situation in Sri Lanka - Indian Express
Content:
With her flowing, hot-pink suit, jangly silver bangles and perky voice, Bhumika Chaturvedi, 24, doesn't fit the stereotype of a thuggish, heard-it-all-before debt collector. But lately, she has had no problem making American debtors cry.

For the past three years, Chaturvedi has been a top collection agent at her call centre, phoning hundreds of Americans every day and politely asking them to pay up. As the US financial crisis plunges Americans into debt, her business is one of the fastest growing sectors in Indian outsourcing. It is also one of the few sectors that is aggressively hiring.

Sitting in a narrow cubicle, her head-set switched on, Chaturvedi listens every night to increasingly disturbing tales of woe from the other side of the globe.

"My mortgage payments are just too high, honey. I just can't make the payment this month," a weeping woman with a Southern accent recently told her in response to a call for a $200 credit card payment. "I'm sure y'all heard about the credit crunch and gas prices.

"Ma'am, I am here to help you," Chaturvedi said. "Maybe you could make a small payment, $100 or $50, anything that you can."

Few places in India absorb and imitate American culture as much as call centres, where ambitious young Indians with fake American accents spend hours calling people in Indiana or Maine to help navigate software glitches, plan vacations or sell products. The subculture of call centres tends to foster a cult of America, an over-the-top fantasy where hopes and dreams are easily accomplished by people who live in a brand-name wonderland of high-paying jobs, big houses and luxury getaways.

But collection agents at this particular call centre in Gurgaon are starting to see the flip side of that vision: a country hobbled by debt and filled with people scared of losing their jobs, their houses and their cars. "Lately, 25-year-old Americans are telling me that they are declaring themselves bankrupt. We have to have so much empathy and patience " said Chaturvedi, raising her eyebrows in shock.

"It's like people are totally drowning," said Omkar Gadgil, 24, who goes by the alias Richard Rudy and was a math major in college. He is brainy and considered the office expert on the intricacies of debt collection. "There has just been years of overspending and now: the crash."

In the past, debt-saddled customers were often annoyed by Chaturvedi's calls from the open-air office at Aegis BPO Services. But now they seem depressed, defeated. Even the men sob into the phone, several agents said.

Under the pseudonym Carol Miller, Chaturvedi's ability to deftly work around the standard line, "The cheque is in the mail," is now being challenged by clients throwing out new responses: "How do you expect me to pay? This is the worst crisis since the Great Depression."

Talking to so many anguished Americans has taught these agents an important lesson: Live within your means. Agents with credit cards are vowing to pay them off every month, even during the upcoming holiday shopping season, when malls feature neon signs advertising flat-screen TVs and air conditioners.

Managers of this call centre say they have recently added a special seminar on the economic crisis, with PowerPoint slides that graph the financial mess as well as updates on other events that could affect the ability of US debtors to pay their bills, including natural disasters such as Hurricane Ike. The presentation is intended to enable agents to bond with their clients, and possibly deflect their excuses.

Since the crisis began, agents have seen call times shoot up dramatically because late payers often want to talk more. More callers have moved. More phones have been disconnected. Clients have started bargaining with agents for discounts on their debts "as if they were haggling at an Indian vegetable market," said Rhoit Chug, assistant vice president of training for Aegis. India handles about $16 billion, or about 5 per cent, of delinquent American accounts. More complicated health insurance bills and mortgage payments are still largely handled inside the United States, industry executives say.

But the debt collection business will continue to grow as debt rises and companies look to cut costs, industry experts said. Aegis, which handles nearly a fourth of debt collection outsourced from the United States, is undergoing a rapid expansion. The company is erecting a second office building for 5,000 employees, many of them to be hired over the next few years. Most employees are college-educated, but earn around Rs 2 lakh per year, less than a fourth of what their American counterparts make.

Inside the Aegis call centre, there is a clean, colourful cafeteria with round tables and darts to relieve stress. Because New Delhi is nearly 10 hours ahead of the eastern United States, there is an espresso machine and candy counter to keep the young workers awake.

Aparup Sengupta, global chief executive officer and managing director of Aegis, encourages his debt collectors to use a "hospitable Indian touch," meaning less arm-twisting and more emotional therapy.

"This businesses is a performing art," said Sengupta. "We are part therapists because the core of the issue is that every human being wants to be honorable in life.

We don't just push someone into a bad situation. We try to create a real solution."

Decorating the office are dozens of yellow smiley faces with the words, "Happy People. Happy Customers. Happy Investors," along with other posters that read: "Connect and Collect."

"How is the car running?" asked Parul Malhotra, 25, who goes by the alias Michelle Jones.

"It's a real piece of junk," the customer shot back, his voice registering more depression than anger. "It was in the shop. The electric's all messed up. And I have no money now. Plus, we have an illness in the family."

"Times are hard. I wish for everyone a speedy recovery," said Malhotra, trying to sound as cheerful as possible. After a pause, she got back to business: "But let's try to work out a payment."

Heading: Kanimozhi letter to father, says she’s ready to resign - Indian Express
Content:
Under severe pressure from key UPA allies in Tamil Nadu, Prime Minister Manmohan Singh on Wednesday expressed "serious concern" at the "escalating hostilities" in Sri Lanka and said there was no military solution to the problem. Instead, he called for a political settlement which would respect the human rights of the ethnic Tamil minorities.

In reaction, Sri Lanka assured that the recent developments in its northern part, including the escalation in fighting against the LTTE, was a "temporary phase" which will end after security forces attain victory over the rebels and should not be considered as an offensive against ethnic Tamil civilians. A senior Sri Lankan foreign ministry official said the government has already made it clear that it will endeavour to address the justifiable concerns of India.

Asked if he has spoken to Sri Lankan President Mahinda Rajpaksa, Singh said India has conveyed its views, as National Security Adviser M K Narayanan summoned Sri Lanka's Deputy High Commissioner last week.

"We always believe that the situation in Sri Lanka does not call for military victory. It calls for negotiated political settlement which respects the unity and the integrity of Sri Lanka and at the same time respects the essential human rights of minorities, particularly Tamil minorities," said Singh.

Heading: Rival faction serves notice on Kerala MP - Indian Express
Content:
A day after a multi-party meeting decided to issue a two-week ultimatum to the Centre to ensure a ceasefire in Sri Lanka, Rajya Sabha member K Kanimozhi called on her father and DMK president M Karunanidhi and handed over a letter expressing her willingness to resign from the post on October 29, the date on which the deadline ends.

Though initial reports suggested that she had submitted her 'post dated resignation', senior DMK leaders said it was a letter "citing her willingness to step down as per the decision taken during the meeting"; Tuesday's resolution indicated that the decision to resign if the ceasefire was not implemented was applicable only to LS members. Asked if it was a resignation letter, a DMK leader said: "She cannot take such a decision on her own."

In an 'all-party meeting' convened by Chief Minister Karunanidhi on Tuesday— the meeting was boycotted by most Opposition parties—it was decided that the Centre would be given an ultimatum to ensure a ceasefire in Sri Lanka, where a conflict is claiming "several innocent lives including that of children" every day. The resolutions adopted during the meeting also included demands to protect the rights of Lankan Tamils; cease all military assistance to the Lankan Government; allow supply of food and medicines to the affected Tamil families and stop killing of Tamil fishermen by the Lankan Navy.

If these demands were not met within the coming fortnight, all 'elected members' from Tamil Nadu would tender their resignations from the Parliament, it was announced after the meeting. However, the Opposition boycott was largely symbolic as their strength is limited to two MDMK members in the LS and seven AIADMK members in the Upper House.

The clarification, replacing a virtual ultimatum of two weeks with a definite October 29 deadline, has added the pressure on the Centre to take some positive steps. Congress, leading the Government at the Centre, and MDMK, toeing the AIADMK line that the all-party meeting was merely an eye wash, are both caught in the middle by the DMK ultimatum. "All Congress MPs have accepted the decision to stand by the Tamilians in this issue," said a leader. MDMK, with two members in the present Lok Sabha, is yet to announce its decision.

"Our decision is prompted by the sufferings undergone by the innocent Tamil families, who are caught in the middle of an intense conflict between the Government army and LTTE. Many are getting killed and there is no food or medicine available to the survivors. But as a state, Tamil Nadu can only appeal to the Centre to intervene to ensure a political solution," said DMK spokesperson T K S Elangovan.

But according to DMK's critics, the whole issue is a way of counter attacking the latest charge of favouritism against Karunanidhi, who was reportedly planning to make Kanimozhi a Minister in the Central Cabinet.

Meanwhile, the Tamil film industry, expressing solidarity with the Lankan Tamils and fishermen from the state, is organising a protest rally at the fishing hub of Rameswaram on Sunday, apart from a three-day suspension of all film related activities from October 18.

Heading: Tatas to set up first defence aerospace hub near Hyderabad - Indian Express
Content:
Factional feud in the state unit of the CPI(M) is far from over. MP S Ajayakumar, a prominent leader of the faction led by V S Achuthanandan, has been served with a show-cause notice by the rival faction of Pinarayi Vijayan.

Ajayakumar, who represents Ottapalam constituency, was slapped with the notice by the CPI(M) Ottapalam area committee, to which he belongs. During the last party election, the official faction had removed him from all party bodies. Later, he was included in the Ottapalam area committee at the behest of the Politburo.

The party has chargesheeted Ajayakumar mainly for not consulting the party on exhausting the MP's Local Area Development Fund and his failure to attend the area committee meetings. Sources close to Ajayakumar said the rival faction wanted to spoil his chances of fighting another Lok Sabha polls.

"The area committee had never given any suggestion on spending the MP fund. The committee meetings were always held when he was away in New Delhi," sources said.

A CPI(M) leader from Kannur and a party MLA from Palakkad were reportedly behind issuing the show-cause notice.

Heading: EC split, NC stand on early polls ‘welcome’ - Indian Express
Content:
In an apparent face-saver in the wake of the recent communal violence in Orissa and Karnataka, the UPA Government is all set to introduce the Communal Violence (Prevention, Control and Rehabilitation of Victims) Bill, 2005, in Parliament during the session starting Friday. However, except for a few minor changes, the Bill has no major deviation from its original draft.

Ever since its introduction in November 2005, the Bill has been surrounded by controversy and debate. With various NGOs and pressure groups demanding inclusion or modification of certain clauses, the passage of the Bill has been delayed. Prominent demands include bringing state chief ministers under the purview of the Act, empowering the Centre to deploy forces in disturbed areas without the consent of the state Government and replacing the concept of "relief" with "compensation".

However, other than effecting some minor changes proposed by the Standing Committee, the Home Ministry is learnt to have decided to bring in the Bill in "more or less its original form". While it realises that a stormy Parliament session could make its passage difficult, the Government is keen to bring it up so as to appear to have done something to check the escalation of communal incidents in the country.

Introduced in the Rajya Sabha in 2005, the Bill essentially seeks to provide for declaration of certain areas as communally disturbed areas by the state governments, lays down measures for prevention of acts leading to communal violence, enhances the quantum of punishments and makes provisions for speedy investigation and trial of offences through special courts.

In addition, the Bill also proposes institutional arrangements for relief and rehabilitation measures for victims of communal violence and seeks to make provisions for compensation to them along with granting of special powers to the Centre in certain cases. The Bill also seeks the setting up of a National Communal Disturbance Relief and Rehabilitation Council, State Communal Disturbance Relief and Rehabilitation Council and District Communal Disturbance Relief and Rehabilitation Council.

Heading: Traders from J-K, PoK form joint body - Indian Express
Content:
While no one in the Election Commission is willing to officially speak on the timing of the polls in Jammu and Kashmir, the divide within the panel leading to the delay in taking a decision reportedly lies between the Chief Election Commissioner on one side and the two Election Commissioners on the other.

The EC deliberations on Tuesday largely centred around the likely voter turnout in the event of an early election in the state.

CEC N Gopalaswami was said to be in favour of deferring the elections while the other two Election Commissioners reportedly didn't quite agree with him.Gopalaswami was said to have been guided by responses of various political parties that have met the election panel over the past few weeks.

The EC's main fear apparently is that a poor turnout in an atmosphere charged after the recent Amarnath dispute could sully the elections.

Speaking to The Indian Express on Wednesday, Gopalaswami said he had taken heart from the National Conference's "change of stand" to favouring elections in J&K, indicating that early polls in the state were still not ruled out. "National Conference president Omar Abdullah's statement is a positive development," Gopalaswami said.

The two Election Commissioners (Navin Chawla and S Y Quraishi) are said to be in favour of holding elections before the end of President's rule (January 9). One way suggested by them is to conduct the polls after the just-announced elections in five states are over; or to have the first phase after polling ends in Chhatisgarh (by the end of November) in the colder parts of the state first, and the Valley subsequently.

The advantage, say those arguing for early polls, is that a forum for political activity will emerge and help counter the Hurriyat's stepped-up campaign of "alienation". And it's not just the two Election Commissioners who back early polls; the security establishment as well as independent Kashmir-watchers in India have been arguing the same.

Another argument against delaying elections is that by then winter will set in, making it difficult for the EC to get support of local staff for the polls. The EC, in fact, is taking account of the Urdu-knowing staff it can marshal, and one factor in deciding poll dates may be the number of such officials it can muster from states like Punjab, Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar.

Apart from the NC, the People's Democratic Party of Mufti Mohd Syed had also argued against early elections when it met the poll panel on September 8.

During its representation to the EC then, the NC had stressed on "initiating a dialogue with the Valley", and said that "an early election would mean a referendum on the regional and religious divide in the state."

Heading: Can make moving around difficult: Maya gets Congress warning - Indian Express
Content:
The Jammu and Kashmir traders along with traders of PoK have formed a joint Chamber of Commerce to strengthen the trade and business relations between, Jammu, Kashmir and PoK. Named as Federation of Jammu and Kashmir Chambers of Commerce, the newly formed trade body will be headed by Zulfikar Abasi, who heads the PoK trade delegation that is now in Kashmir.

The announcement was made a day before PoK trade delegation leaves for Muzuffarabad. "The president ship of the new federation will be shared by the federations of J-K and PoK on yearly rotation basis," Abasi said. He said on October 21, cross LoC trade will begin between Srinagar and Muzuffarabad. "Fifteen trucks carrying load of 14.5 tons will be allowed to cross the LoC on that day,' he said.

Heading: A terrorist in their midst - Indian Express
Content:
As Mayawati took on Sonia Gandhi in Lucknow, here the Congress launched the second phase of its attack on the Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister. It threatened after Mayawati attempted to prevent a Sonia rally in Rae Bareli, its workers could stop the Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister from moving around in the country.

"The Congress is an organisation which is present in every village of the country... Leave alone the Congress president, if she (Mayawati) threatens even a Congress worker and does not rein in her dictatorial style and continues her vendetta politics, she would find it difficult to roam around in the country. The Congress workers will prevent her Bharat bhraman," Congress spokesman Manish Tewari said.

He added that the Uttar Pradesh Congress had prepared a detailed agitation programme against the Mayawati Government.

The Congress also criticised Mayawati again for her "intransigence" in stalling four projects in Rae Bareli, "dictated by her desire for political revenge".

"The entire political paradigm of Mayawati is based on fear, revenge and corruption. Her corruption is legendary, as is evident from the monuments she has built from Lucknow to Delhi," Tewari said.

The Congress leader reminded Mayawati that such politics and clashes with the Centre time and again were neither good for the people of the state nor for the federal constitution of the country.

"She should stop dreaming of becoming a PM. Instead, she should focus on discharging her responsibility of Chief Minister of UP first," said Tewari.

Heading: High Court reprieve for mother-daughter duo - Indian Express
Content:
For a man who occupied a place on Interpol's 'most wanted' list, Subrata Bayen alias Fateh Ali lived a remarkably quiet life in his four-storey mansion in Kolkata's posh Palm Avenue, a short walk from Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee's residence. But there were signs that all was not well at house number 9/3 in the weeks leading up to Bayen's arrest by the Special Task Force (STF) on Monday. According to police sources, the dreaded Bangladeshi criminal may have come to know that the police were hot on his trail, as he had been in a desperate hurry to sell off his home - in fact, add the sources, he was even willing to go for a 'distress sale', raising suspicion among some prospective buyers. The question that loomed among many was why the owner was trying to sell the property at less than half the price it was worth.

On Tuesday, the house that Bayen had lived in for 18 months remained sealed, with neighbours still incredulous that the quiet man who had lived among them with his wife and two children was a notorious gangster who was wanted for several terrorist activities. "They did not talk much with us. I have only seen the man once," said Laxmi Ghatal, a resident of 5B Palm Avenue, the house bang opposite to Bayen's. Another neighbour, Putul Majumdar claimed that the family led a luxurious life: "The wife wore a lot of gold ornaments and moved around in cars. However, no one knew so much about the man who had constructed it and what he did."

Others added that Bayen had bought the land and employed a local contractor Amir Khan - who is wanted for questioning by the police — to build the house. "The family began living here about a year-and-a-half ago, but they rarely came out," said Arshad Shahid, another neighbour.

According to police sources, Bayen had sent back his wife and children back to Bangladesh. Locals added that several brokers and prospective buyers had been visiting the house. "But for some reasons, Bayen was not able to find the right price," said an official of the STF of Kolkata police. "He had probably found out that it was not safe for him to continue residing in the area."

Jhunu Ganguly, a 40 year old resident of 5E Palm Avenue claimed that there was word going around that the house was up for sale at Rs 40 lakh. "This is less than half the price that such a property here would be worth," said Ganguly.

Bayen's residence also throws up questions about how such a notorious criminal, against whom a Red Corner Notice had been issued by the Interpol, managed not only to buy a property in a respectable locality, but also to live there without being detected for so long. These revelations have also put the role of the Intelligence Branch of the police here under the scanner.

Although the Deputy High Commissioner of Bangladesh in Kolkata did not want to comment on the matter, a senior officer at the High Commission said that since India and Bangladesh do not have an extradition treaty, the Indian police directly contacted the Dhaka Police and Bangladesh Rifles. "Criminals are often pushed back through the border," said the officer.

The man whom the Kolkata Police are referring to as a "big catch" has had a long and 'illustrious' criminal career that has transcended international borders for years.

Rajiv Kumar, the officer-in-charge of the Special Task Force ( STF) said that Bayen alias Fateh Ali was the founder of the "Seven Star Gang" (the name was derived from the number of members) of Barisal in Bangladesh that had terrorised the entire district for more than a decade. The police have gathered that this gang was involved in anti-national activities, leading to Subrata Bayen being branded a terrorist by the Bangladeshi Government.

Bayen was sixth in the list of criminals handed over to the BSF by BDR at a flag meeting on August 24 this year. A Red Corner Notice was issued by the Interpol in Bayen's name and he was wanted in several cases of extortion and murder, including his most daring crime — the grenade attack on a rally of Awami League leader and former Bangladesh prime minister Sheikh Hasina that killed 24 people. Police sources also said one of the most important allies of Bayen, Mollah Masud, was still operating from India.

To the Dhaka police, he is Trimoti Subrata Bayen, wanted in cases related to terrorism, illegal possession of arms and murder. Bayen carried a cash reward of one lakh rupees on his head and at least 17 cases of murder and extortion had been registered against him in Ramana police station alone.

Subrata Bayen, however, had a humble beginning. He was born to a middle-class father Bipul Bayen in Sutapur in Barisal. He was born a Christian but he changed religion after his second marriage and adopted the name Fateh Ali, said police sources.

His first mentor was a local criminal of Barisal, Tikka, and it wasn't long before Bayen began to rise in the ranks of the gang. He eventually broke away from Tikka and set up the Seven Star Gang in Mugbazar area of Barisal. The outfit 'specialised' in extortion and murder. During the 10-year period in which it operated, Bayen's gang was responsible for the murders of at least 15 traders, said police sources in Kolkata, adding that one of the gang members, Tanvir-ul Islam, is still lodged in a Bengal jail after he was caught some years ago.

Subrata, by now known as Fateh Ali, was caught by Bangladeshi police in 1997 and stayed in prison for two years. Police sources said that Subrata had established business relations in several districts of the state. He decided to permanently stay in India in 2004 after a major crackdown from the Bangladeshi government. He stayed in Teghoria and Dum Dum area as well, said police sources. "This man stayed and operated from several places in Bengal. We are still looking into his details as well," added STF officer-in-charge Rajiv Kumar.

Heading: Flood task force averts 43 cases of illegal trafficking - Indian Express
Content:
The Bombay High Court on Wednesday pulled up the sessions judge who awarded death sentence to the mother-daughter duo in the Dr Deepak Mahajan murder case, saying the judge recorded the evidence like a "tape-recorder" without any interruption and hence, it was not a fair trial.

Holding that the sessions judge was a silent spectator, a division bench of Justice Bilal Nazki and Justice Ashutosh Kumbhakoni stated, "This is a fit case to exercise jurisdiction under section 311 of CrPC" for calling witnesses and examining evidence. The court proposed to direct that certain witnesses who are important be called to the trial court for cross-examination, especially one Rahul Bhosale who was present for part of the crime.

The prosecution and defence will produce the list of witnesses to be called after which the court will frame the list on Thursday and give a deadline for the process.

Leena Devasthali (51) and Deepti Devasthali (27) were convicted by the Pune sessions court last year on charges of murdering Mahajan, a Pune-based orthopaedic surgeon, and given capital punishment.

Citing inaction on the part of the sessions judge and a "whipped up" prosecution case, the High Court observed that "It is most crucial and pertinent that the judge did not ask even a single question as a court question to any of the witnesses." "Recording of the entire oral evidence led by the prosecution unmistakably and crystal clearly demonstrates that the judge has played no role at all to find out the truth and veracity of any of the witnesses," the court said. The court likened the judge's conduct to a "tape-recorder".

The court also opined that the judge should have at least appointed an amicus curie to find out the truth as the accused did not engage a lawyer and conducted their defence themselves. "When one reads examination-in-chief, especially of those witnesses who were not crossed by both accused, even with inquisitiveness, one feels putting at least a few questions, to each of these witnesses in order to ascertain the veracity of their evidence," the judgement observed.

During arguments for confirmation of the sentence, defence advocate Shirish Gupte had argued that this was a mistrial. He also pointed out that the accused always had the impression that the judge was biased and therefore had filed a transfer application before the Supreme Court which was pending, but the judge did not stop the proceedings.

The High Court has now held that whatever shortcomings in the trial, as alleged, will be removed as there should not be an impression that the court has pre-judged the issue.

According to police, Devasthalis, hailing from Mumbai, first sent a letter to Mahajan, on a fake letterhead of one Omkar Charitable Trust sometime in June 2006, requesting him to join as chief orthopaedic surgeon at the hospital the trust was setting up. They were related to him, but used different names in the letter. They also set up a detective agency called 'Bluebird' in Pune and hired two persons.

Dr Mahajan was lured to a hotel room in Pune on June 30, 2006, and he was overpowered with the help of these two employees of detective agency and was administered an anaesthetic drug. Police claimed that the duo then called Mahajan's family and demanded a ransom of Rs 25 lakh. Unfortunately, Mahajan died because of high does of anesthetic. On July 2, his body was cut into pieces which were disposed of at different places.

Of the 46 witnesses, the prosecution had examined only 21. The accused were convicted on December 27, 2007.

Heading: Nepalese flood camp houses 12,000 Indians - Indian Express
Content:
While the state Government agencies are finding it difficult to locate 3,611 people who are reportedly missing since floods ravaged the state, the task force, set up by the state's Social Welfare Department, has managed to avert 43 cases of illegal trafficking in the districts that were worst hit.

The Social Welfare Department had constituted a 400-person task force, comprising NGOs and volunteers. They were deployed at bus stands, railway stations and relief camps. Speaking to The Indian Express, Social Welfare Department Principal Secretary Vijay Prakash said: "We have been coordinating with the Bihar Livelihood Project, a voluntary group that monitors the task force and compiles data pertaining to missing persons." He added that illegal trafficking becomes easy during floods due to the prevailing chaos and displacement of a large number of people. He said: "The police in Madhepura, Saharsa, Supaul, Purnea and Araria were extra vigilant and thereby prevented illegal trafficking."

With several people, including teenaged girls, being separated from their families, there has been a widespread apprehension of illegal trafficking. The task force members rescued 43 girls, some of whom had been taken to transit points and four of them to red light areas of Muzaffarpur and Sitamarhi. No trafficker, however, could be arrested.

Prakash admitted that tracing missing people is a daunting task. "We do not have a data on the number of people who have been reunited with their families," he said. The task force has so far united four people with their families at Supaul and Madhepura.

Disaster Management Additional Secretary Pratyay Amrit said: "Some people might be staying with their relatives in other cities."He said Safal Solutions Private Limited, a Hyderabad-based firm, is compiling the data of missing persons from all the 326 camps and the final list will be sent to respective district police.Most missing people are from Kumarkhand and Murliganj in Madhepura and Chhatapur in Supaul.

Heading: Rebel fears grow for BJP, Congress - Indian Express
Content:
More than 12,000 Indians, who had entered Nepal seeking relief after the Kosi floods destroyed their houses, are still living in camps in Sunsari district of Himalayan nation, authorities said.

Chief District Administrator Durga Prasad Bhandari said that over 12,000 flood affected Indians are living inside the camps in Inaruwa, Singiya, Laukahi and Haripur while many others had returned. "We have decided to repatriate these Indian families to their home country after providing them with necessary humanitarian assistance," he said. Fifty-five flood displaced families from India have already been sent to their homes, the official said.

Heading: MP denies Cong charges of scuttling rally - Indian Express
Content:
With the upcoming Assembly elections in the state, the ruling BJP and the Opposition Congress are facing intense pressure from aspirants for party tickets, leading to speculation about the possibility of both parties facing rebellion from within.

Both the BJP an the Congress have been engaged in an exercise to shortlist their candidates to contest the 90 seats in the state Assembly, but a clear picture is yet to emerge because of an almost ten-fold increase in the number of aspirants from both parties.

The number of aspirants for BJP tickets swelled, particularly after its senior leaders dropped hints that the party could deny tickets to a number of its sitting legislators, including ministers, in order to beat the anti-incumbency factor. Talk about the BJP adopting the 'Modi formula" of bringing in new faces to replace its "unpopular legislators" has left many leaders in a dilemma. Worried over the possibility of sabotage during the elections, the BJP is working out strategies to deal with any such situation, with party president Rajnath Singh recently visiting the state capital to guide their leaders about the need for intra-party discipline.

On the other hand, with almost a thousand aspirants vying for party tickets, infighting is at its peak within the Congress, as its leaders are lobbying to get the maximum number of tickets for their supporters. However, State Congress working president Satya Narayan Sharma told The Indian Express that the party has narrowed down its candidates for 50 constituencies. "Winning prospects is the only criteria for tickets," he said.

Meanwhile, the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) and Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) are keeping a keen eye on the developments within the BJP and Congress so as to poach rebels from the mainstream parties.

Although the BSP has already released its list of candidates for all 90 seats, state president Dauram Ratnakar has indicated that the party is open to replacing any of them in the event of the BSP winning over a suitable candidate. "A large number of BJP and Congress leaders are in touch with us", said Ratnakar. The NCP, on the other hand, has no other option other than to rope in rebels from the Congress, which is apparently not willing to forge any state-level alliance with Sharad Pawar's party. State NCP president Novil Kumar Verma openly stated that his party would field its candidates in about 40 seats if the Congress-NCP poll alliance did not materialise. "Our doors are open for Congress rebels," he added.

For Date Line stories, visit www.expressindia.com/dateline

Heading: Ensure safety of Fuchs, daughter: German consulate - Indian Express
Content:
The Madhya Pradesh Government on Wednesday countered the Congress's accusation that the ruling BJP had denied Sonia Gandhi permission to hold a rally, saying the party had just been asked to reschedule the function.

"The AICC chairperson was only asked to reschedule the rally from October 19 to any date after October 21 because the Lal Parade ground is booked for an official function," government spokesman Kailash Vijayvargiya said on Wednesday. In any case, she could have held the rally at Jamboree ground, a much bigger venue in Bhel area, he said.

MPCC president Suresh Pachauri had on Tuesday alleged that the local administration, under the influence of the ruling party, did not allow the rally to take place. The Congress' allegation followed the face off between the AICC chairperson and UP Chief Minister Mayawati.

Vijayvargiya said Sonia was welcome to hold a rally anywhere in the state and his Government would extend all possible cooperation.

Heading: 10 injured in Raman Singh’s birthday bash stampede - Indian Express
Content:
Even as the German consulate in Mumbai appealed to the Goa Government not to compromise with the security of Fadela Fuchs and her daughter, the elder son of Goa minister Atanasio Monserratte was at large for the second day after he was charged with raping the minor girl.

"I would be most grateful if you could ensure that criminal investigation is pursued vigorously and that the safety of Fuchs and her daughter not compromised," Consul General Walter Stechel said in a letter to the Goa Chief Secretary.

"We have not been able to arrest him till now. The search is still on," a senior police officer said, a day after Rohit(21) was booked in connection with the case. Meanwhile, the state police have claimed that the victim was not cooperating in the probe. "The police approached the girl with a woman activist and counsellor but she refused to cooperate. She has also refused medical examination," said a senior police official.

Advocate Aires Rodrigues, counsel for Fadela Fuchs said the girl's refusal for medical examination or deposition before the police does not hamper the case. He, however, said the girl's testimony is important to make the case more strong as every part of evidence is vital.

Monserratte, the Education Minister, is said to have told CM Digambar Kamat at a meeting of Cabinet members at the latter's residence that he had no faith in the police and asked for an impartial inquiry. into the incident.

Heading: Two shopkeepers held for Kanpur blast - Indian Express
Content:
At least 10 people, including eight children, were injured in a stampede during a dinner hosted at a public function organised to celebrate the 57th birthday of Chhattisgarh Chief Minister Raman Singh at Rajnandgaon, about 90 kilometers from here, on Wednesday night. BJP sources said the incident took place when people rushed for dinner. Local party workers were managing the dinner arrangements for more than 20,000 people.

Those present at the function, organised at the new Krishi Upaj Mandi ground, confirmed about the rush that left 10 people injured. All the injured were taken to the local government hospital. All the injured children are in the group of five to 15 years, while two other injured have been identified as Krishna (40) and Parvati Bai (65). Chief Minister Raman Singh visited the injured at the hospital.

Heading: Gay sex: HC asks Centre to give scientific proof - Indian Express
Content:
With the arrest of two shopkeepers, the Kanpur police on Wednesday claimed to have solved Tuesday night's blast case in Purani Sharab Gaddi area. The blast was caused by the accidental explosion of firecrackers kept in a bag on a cycle, the police said.

The arrested persons — Kamal Sahu and Mohammad Atiq — were part of a racket involved in making and selling illegal firecrackers.

The police is searching for their three accomplices, identified as Ayaz, Raju and Illiyas.

The explosion took place near Sahu's shop Gupta General Store. While inspecting the shop late on Tuesday night, the police found large quantity of illegal firecrackers.

The police presented Atiq and Sahu before the media where Sahu said: "Each packet contained 25 pieces of firecrackers, which had exploded and lead to commotion and panic in the area." Sahu said the firecrackers were manufactured at Sarsaul by Ayaz, Raju and Illiyas. "Atiq used to sell these firecrackers to small shopowners," said Sahu, adding that he had been selling these crackers for the last 10 years.

Narrating the events leading to the blast, Atiq said: "Ayaz came to my Colonelganj residence in the evening with the crackers in a bag and we left for Sahu's shop on a cycle." Atiq said he asked Sahu to get a glass of water, while Ayaz stood near the cycle.

"Suddenly, the cycle fell and the firecrackers kept in the bag exploded from the impact," Atiq said.

He said Ayaz too received injuries in the blast, but ran away. "When I saw Ayaz escaping, I too ran away," he added.

Superintendent of Police (Kanpur West) Dayanand Mishra said a case has been registered against Atiq and Sahu on charges of disturbing the law and order situation, creating panic among people, sale and supply of illegal firecrackers and possession of explosives.

Heading: CJI suggests retirement for ‘ineffective’ judicial officers - Indian Express
Content:
The Delhi High Court on Wednesday told the Centre to come up with scientific proof showing that decriminalisation of homosexual love will cause the spread of HIV/AIDS virus, rather than banking on religious texts.

Additional Solicitor General P P Malhotra was stopped short of quoting from an article referring to the Bible on gay sex. "We should not accept religious literature instead of scientific reports," a Bench, headed by Chief Justice A P Shah, said. "These are not scientific reports. These articles quoting the Bible are propaganda. Your arguments should be based on scientific reports. Show us scientific reports which justify criminalisation of such acts (gay sex)," the Bench observed.

The Bench, also comprising Justice S Muralidhar, asked the Government to place before it reports of the World Health Organisation on the issue of health hazards arising out of criminalisation of gay sex.

"We are not taking it (religious literature). We will be going by your report submitted by the National AIDS Control Organisation (NACO). We would rely on the NACO report. You can counter it by some scientific report. Show us what World Health Organisation says on the issue. We can rely on those scientific reports," the Bench said.

The NACO, in its affidavit filed on behalf of Union Health Ministry, had said that gay sex among consenting adults should be decriminalised.

Heading: SC pulls up Centre for delay in bringing broadcasting Bill - Indian Express
Content:
In yet another step aimed at cleansing the judiciary, Chief Justice of India K G Balakrishnan has suggested compulsory retirement for all those judicial officers who are found ineligible or ineffective. Extending the Fundamental Rules as applicable to Government employees, the CJI, in a recent letter written to all high courts, has suggested, "A judicial officer who is unfit, ineffective, incompetent or has doubtful integrity may be retired from service even before his continued utility is assessed in terms of directions of the court."

The CJI wrote: "Such a measure could be taken after reviewing the service records of judicial officers when they attain the age of 50 and 55 years with a view to weed out those with doubtful integrity."

"Pre-mature retirement is not a stigma and no civil consequences follow such requirement," he said, adding that review of judicial officers' service records, character rolls, quality of judgments and other relevant material at the age of 50 and 55 years will be in addition to the assessment being carried out at the age of 58 years.

The suggestion is timely as the judiciary is facing corruption charges at all levels, be it PF scam or Justice Soumitra Sen's case.

The CJI said Rule 56 (j) of Fundamental Rules enables the 'appropriate authority' to retire any Government servant, if it is in the public interest to do so, and the officer has attained the age of 50 years, if he/she had entered the service before attaining the age of 35 years, or has attained the age of 55 years in others cases.

Heading: Tribals see conspiracy in notice to Salwa Judum leader before elections - Indian Express
Content:
After being pulled up for its "dilly-dally" attitude for the past two years in passing a Bill for regulating TV content, the Centre on Wednesday told the Supreme Court that it would soon come out with an interim code or regulations, which will have to be adhered to by all channels till the Bill is passed.

Appearing for the Union Government, Additional Solicitor General Gopal Subramanium submitted this before a bench headed by Justice B N Aggarwal.

"The Government does not want to introduce it? Why are you dilly-dallying for the past two years? Does it involve any kind of votebank politics?" questioned the bench, also comprising Justices G S Singhvi and Aftab Alam.

Putting forth the Government's view that it is equally worried over the growing content of violence and vulgarity on television, the ASG said the Centre was in the process of consulting various stakeholders to facilitate the tabling of the Bill. He said the opinion of states, Union Territories and the various media houses was being elicited so as to arrive at an acceptable solution.

While the bench agreed that "today television is the most powerful instrument in the world capable of influencing the minds of the people", the judges differed in their approach to tackle the rising content of obscenity and violence being telecast on channels.

"Is there one day in a year when a family can sit together and watch a programme?" Justice Singhvi questioned the Centre's counsel as the judge observed: "Everyday, there's been an assault on their basic values."

On the other hand, Justice Alam said, "It's a very delicate issue. What people should watch I personally feel that I should not be a guardian. But it has to be addressed."

The remarks were part of the hearing on a PIL by NGO Common Cause, seeking strict regulations to check obscenity and violence on TV channels.

The bench granted the Government three weeks to submit its views on the fate of the proposed broadcasting Bill.

Heading: Cabinet to decide today on law - Indian Express
Content:
At a time when 'Salwa Judum' leaders are planning to contest the upcoming Assembly polls in South Bastar, the state Government has issued showcause notice to a prominent anti-Naxalite campaign leader, asking why disciplinary action should not be taken against him for not attending to his duties as a teacher in a school run by the Tribal Welfare Department.

Swayam Mukka, a teacher in a school being run by the department, is among the frontline leaders of 'Salwa Judum', ever since the anti-Naxalite campaign was launched in South Bastar in June 2005 to isolate the Maoist rebels and to create awareness among the masses against the Naxalite menace. Like Mukka, a number of other school teachers of Konta and Bijapur regions are closely associated with the movement.

The state Government, which has been extending support to 'Salwa Judum' terming it as a spontaneous movement by the locals against bloodshed and violence in the tribal region, had encouraged these Government employees to actively participate themselves in the movement during the last three years.

As the Assembly elections reached near, Salwa Judum activists began organising meetings at places where the people felt that local leaders of the anti-Naxalite campaign should contest the upcoming Assembly polls from Konta (ST), Bijapur (ST) and Dantewara (ST) constituencies in South Bastar so that the movement could get further boost. The perception among the 'Salwa Judum' cadres was that presence of its leaders in the Assembly would take their fight against Naxalites to a much higher level.

Even as the efforts to field 'Salwa Judum' leaders in the polls gained momentum, the tribal welfare department suddenly woke up to the fact that Swayam Mukka was not attending to the duties as a government school teacher. He has been asked to report for duty within ten days or face action.

Mukka told The Indian Express that he had received a notice from his department asking why action should not be taken against him for making "political statements" at 'Salwa Judum' meetings and not attending to his duties. " The department knows of my association with Salwa Judum for the last three years", he added.

About the possibility of his jumping into the poll fray for the Konta reserved seat, Mukka said he was considering it as the people active in Salwa Judum want him to contest the elections. Salwa Judum cadres, however, see it as an attempt to browbeat their leaders from going ahead with their plans to contest the elections. "It appears that the region's established leadership in both the BJP, Congress as well as the Communist Party of India (CPI) were trying to prevent new faces from coming to the front", they said.

Dantewara Assembly constituency is being represented by Congress leader Mahendra Karma, also the leader of the Opposition in the Assembly. Now a prominent leader of the Salwa Judum, his conflict with local 'Salwa Judum' leaders apparently began after the senior tribal leader started lobbying to field his son Chabindra Karma from Bijapur (ST) constituency, which falls in the area where anti-Naxalite campaign was active. Konta (ST) seat is being represented by Kawasi Lakma (Congress) while Rajendra Pambhoi (Congress) is the legislator from Bijapur (ST) constituency.

The BJP, which made considerable gains in the tribal Bastar region in the 2003 polls but could not make a dent in South Bastar, is now trying to wrest the seat from the Congress. Hence, both the parties don't want any new faces that have emerged through the 'Salwa Judum' movement.

Heading: Watchdog for distance education before Cabinet - Indian Express
Content:
With sharp differences continuing to persist between the Union ministries of Home Affair (MHA) and Health on the issue of repealing Section 377 of the Indian Penal Code, which bans sexual relations among people of the same gender, the Union Cabinet is expected to take a call on the subject on Thursday. Sources in the MHA said that the ministry has decided to let the Cabinet decide on the issue.

The Delhi High Court is already hearing a PIL challenging the legality of Section 377, with the petitioner asserting that Section 377 was being used to harass homosexuals.

"It was decided to place the issue before the Cabinet so that differences among various ministries can be ironed out. As of now, except for Health Minister Anbumani Ramadoss and, to some extent, Labour Minister Oscar Fernandes, nobody in the Central Government wants the law to be done away with," said a senior functionary of the Law and Justice Ministry.

A few days ago, Ramadoss had written to Prime Minister Manmohan Singh, highlighting the need to drop Section 377 on the ground that it was impending India's fight against HIV. On the other hand, the MHA had asked the Delhi High Court not to consider Ramadoss's views on legalising gay sex among consenting adults. It said Section 377 was the will of Parliament and the people.

The MHA feels that there is nothing wrong with the law since a majority of Indians are opposed to homosexuality. It says consultations with various groups, including religious leaders, on the issue have strengthened its claim that any move to tinker with the law could be fraught with danger.

Heading: Former Union minister’s kin claims to be N D Tiwari’s son - Indian Express
Content:
The distance education sector is all set to get a new and independent regulator in the form of a 19-member Distance Education Council (DEC). The legislation for the constitution of DEC, which will monitor and regulate the standards of open learning across the country, will come up for Cabinet approval on Thursday.

While a DEC already exists under the Indira Gandhi National Open University (IGNOU), the new regulator will be a statutory body independent of the central university.

Besides monitoring courses conducted via satellite-based channels and Internet courses, the new DEC is proposed to keep a close watch on all open learning institutes, including the regular institutes that offer correspondence courses. The new DEC will also be empowered to check fake institutions or institutions imparting sub-standard education.

De-linking of DEC from IGNOU had been a long-pending demand by universities offering Distance Education Programmes (DEPs), as they felt that the university, which itself was conducting such courses, should not prescribe norms for them.

Heading: Idea Exchange: BJP slams Home Minsiter - Indian Express
Content:
Andhra Pradesh Governor N D Tiwari is in the thick of a legal battle by a 29-year-old grandson of a former Union minister claiming to be his son, a version rubbished by the veteran Congress leader.

Rohit Shekhar, grandson of former Union Minister Sher Singh, said in the lawsuit in the Delhi High Court that he was born out of a relationship between Tiwari and his mother Ujjwala Singh, who is also associated with Congress Party. Efforts to get reaction from Raj Bhawan in Hyderabad proved futile.

When contacted Ujjwala said Rohit had to approach the High Court after Tiwari refused to accept him as his son. "I belong to a respectable family. My father was a former Union Minister. It needs guts to reveal such information in the open court but I stand by my son Rohit as his rights are being denied by Tiwari," Ujjwala, told PTI over telephone.

She said the court on April had issued notice to Tiwari who has denied the claim. She said the octogenarian leader has admitted his association with her but denied having any relationship.

Heading: Nano gets concessions, stamp duty exemption - Indian Express
Content:
The BJP has slammed Union Home Minister Shivraj Patil for his statement — made at The Indian Express Idea Exchange programme on Tuesday — that confessions before police as admissible evidence in court would not be acceptable to the UPA Government.

"The Government can strengthen the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act but ARC proposal to treat confession before police as evidence is not acceptable," Patil had said.

On Wednesday, BJP spokesman Ravi Shankar Prasad: "Home Minister Shivraj Patil has said that the Government would consider strengthening anti-terror law but any suggestion to make confession as admissible evidence would not be acceptable.

He needs to be reminded that the said provision in POTA was held to be legally valid by the Supreme Court and the very conviction of the assailants of the late Rajiv Gandhi was made possible by confessions of accused under the TADA. In so many other laws in India itself there are strong provisions of presumptions against the accused establishing their crime and the onus is on the accused to disprove it."

Patil had also said the Government was opposed to suggestions to shift the burden of proof from the prosecution to the defence.

Citing Section 304B of the Indian Penal Code (dowry death) and Section 138B of the Customs Act 1962, Prasad said: "Strong laws against dowry, dangerous drugs and the Customs putting the onus on the accused is permissible but similar strong provisions in case of fight against terror is not acceptable, is what the Home Minister is saying and this is being said in spite of the fact that the police and security forces are discovering the conspiracy and linkage in the entire country of the terror attack based upon the statements of the accused. This is a conclusive proof that the UPA Government is soft on terror."

Heading: Nano supporters prevent Tatas from shifting machines out of Singur factory - Indian Express
Content:
The Gujarat Government has given certain concessions to Tata Motors in the sale of land for the Nano car project that is being set up near Sanand in Ahmedabad district. At its weekly meeting held here on Wednesday, the Cabinet fixed the cost of 1,100 acres of land at Rs 400.65 crore. The land rate was calculated at Rs 900 per sq metre. There was no official press briefing on the decision, but later, the Government issued a one-page statement saying that the land cost for the Nano project was fixed as per the existing rules. Sources in the Chief Minister's Office (CMO) said the Government has decided to give some concessions to the company.

Sources added that it was decided that the company will be given a two-year moratorium wherein the company will not have to pay any installment for the land to the Government. However, it would have to pay an 8 per cent interest during this period.

The Government has exempted Tata Motors from paying 5 per cent stamp duty on the land transaction. The exemption of stamp duty on the total land cost will benefit the company by Rs 20 crore, the sources said. The company will make staggered payment in eight equal installments in as many years, with 8 per cent interest. In case it fails to pay regular installments, it will have to pay compound interest rates.

A senior CMO official said the Government has turned down the company's demand of converting the land from new tenure to old tenure. But the Government has agreed to waive off the conversion tax of Rs 6 per sq metre, which is usually charged for converting agricultural land into non-agricultural one.

Heading: Rae Bareli coach factory: Railways ready with Plan B - Indian Express
Content:
Supporters of the Save Nano Committee (SNC) prevented the employees of a private company, engaged by Tata Motors, from shifting some heavy machinery from the Singur plant on Tuesday.

A police officer said around noon, nearly 20 SNC members intercepted five trucks, in which a pay-loader machine and a few generator sets were being taken out of the factory through gate number five. The vehicles belonged to the company that the Tatas had engaged to dismantle the machines and shift to other places.

The employees of the company, who were in the vehicles, requested the SNC members to let them go but they refused to budge. The protesters, who sat outside the factory gate, demanded that Ratan Tata should reconsider his decision to pull out from Singur.

After a few minutes, the trucks were taken back to the project area, as the SMC supporters blocked the factory gate for several hours.

A senior police officer said the Singur police went to the spot to pacify the protesters, but their request to withdraw the blockade was turned down by the SNC supporters.

SNC convener Sadai Koley said: "We want to make it clear that the Tatas will not be allowed to shift machines from the project area. We will allow only the entry of machines and not the exit.

The Tatas will have to come back because almost 90 per cent work on the project is over."

He further said, "We also requested those who were shifting the machines today to support our movement for holding back Tatas in Singur."

Heading: IBSA to draw up mechanism to respond to financial crisis - Indian Express
Content:
With litigation over land allotment for the Rae Bareli rail coach factory threatening to push the Rs 1,550 crore project way behind schedule, the Railway Ministry is considering using the newly-enacted The Railway (Amendment) Act, 2008 to acquire the same 189 hectares of land whose sale deal was cancelled by the Mayawati Government.

Cleared during the last Parliament session, the Act empowers the Railways to acquire land for special projects. "It was enacted to deal with situations where state governments hinder the setting up of projects of national importance by not providing the required land," a senior Railway Ministry official said.

Even as the Railways are confident of securing a favourable decision from the Allahabad High Court in the case, which comes up for hearing on October 22, the possibility of acquiring the said land under the Act is being readied as Plan B. "Since negotiations with the state Government was already on, the use of the Act was not considered earlier. However, nothing prevents the Railways from acquiring land under this Act, if required," the official added.

As far as the ongoing litigation is concerned, the ministry is building up its case on the argument that the UP Government's decision to sell off 189 hectares of land in Rae Bareli to the Indian Railways came after protracted negotiations were carried out for almost a year during which both the parties mutually negotiated the terms of the land deal. "In July this year the UP Government decided to sell the land to the Railways. The sum of Rs 9 crore, determined as the cost of the land by the state authorities themselves, was paid to the UP Government in August. The possession of the land was handed over to the Railways in September," a ministry official said.

"The purpose for buying the land was always known and there was no malafide intention on the part of the Railways. The price of the land was paid to the UP Government, the mutation in revenue records was carried out and the possession was handed over to the Railways. This kind of a transaction is irreversible," said an official.

The ministry is also building up its case over the argument that the land is infertile and can't be of any use for agricultural purposes. "In fact, efforts to try out farming on the land were made by a local agriculture centre, but it did not yield any result," a source said.

Announced in the Supplementary Demand for Grants in 2007, the foundation stone for this factory was laid by Sonia Gandhi in February this year. The Railways plan to procure 840 coaches annually from this factory for a 10-year period, starting 2010-11. The plan also include getting air-conditioned double-decker coaches manufactured at this unit with the ministry eyeing procurement of at least 20 double-decker trains, having 24 coaches each, by 2021 from this factory.

Heading: Maya strikes back, plans ‘grand rally’ in Sonia bastion - Indian Express
Content:
As the international financial crisis looms large over economies across the world, the three IBSA countries — India, Brazil and South Africa — have agreed to call a meeting of their finance ministers and the governors' of central banks, and set up a "coordination" mechanism to jointly "respond" to the crisis.

Prime Minister Manmohan Singh, in his opening remarks at the IBSA summit, emphasised the key role that IBSA countries had on the international front. "We need more than ever before a renewed effort to reform the institutions of international governance, whether it is the United Nations or the G-8. We need to work purposefully towards the conclusion of the Doha Round of trade talks in a manner that promotes development and inclusive growth. The increase in energy and food prices and the challenge of terrorism threaten our developmental efforts," he said.

Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva said that the US and Europe should take immediate action to ensure that the crisis does not "reach the developing countries that did not participate in this financial casino."

"This call is urgent," he said, adding that the US and the EU had not acted for the last 10 months since the sub-prime crisis broke out and it was only in the last fortnight that they had realized the gravity of the crisis.

"The leaders stressed the need for a new international initiative to bring about structural reforms in the world's financial system. The new initiative must take into account the fact that ethics must also apply to the economy; that the crisis would not be overcome with palliative measures and that the solutions adopted must be global and ensure the full participation of developing countries," their joint statement, named as the Delhi declaration, said.

"The reform must be undertaken so as to incorporate stronger systems of multinational consultations and surveillance as an integral part. This new system must be designed to be as inclusive as possible and must be transparent," it said.

"The explosion of new financial instruments, unaccompanied by credible and systemic regulation, has resulted amongst others in a major crisis of confidence for which those responsible should be held accountable and liable. Developing countries are not immune to this and many would be very seriously affected," the declaration added.

Heading: Maya-opic - Indian Express
Content:
BSP supremo Mayawati on Wednesday announced a maharally in Rae Bareli to counter Congress president and UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi's latest roadshow and statement that "she is ready to go to jail for her karmabhumi".

Mayawati released an eight-page explanation clarifying the reasons for withdrawal of the land which her own government had allotted four months ago for the Central Government project of a rail coach factory in Rae Bareli.

Mayawati also deputed her Principal Secretary Mr Netram to conduct an inquiry into the issue and submit the findings within the next three days. "Based on the inquiry report, the matter will be put up before the Cabinet for any further decision", Mayawati said addressing a hurriedly called press conference at her official residence here.

In her clarification Mayawati blamed not only Sonia Gandhi and Rahul Gandhi but also Samajwadi party (SP) chief Mulayam Singh Yadav for limiting their development activities to Rae Bareli, Amethi and Saifai while neglecting the rest of the state.

"Why a factory in Rae Bareli where so many factories already exist? Why not a factory in Bundelkhand or in eastern UP? If the Central Government plans something for these areas, the government would gladly give land for the projects".

Referring to the agitation in Rae Bareli, Mayawati labelled Sonia's interaction with farmers a "political gimmick". Calling attention to two railway projects proposed in 2006 for Rae Bareli and Lalu Prasad Yadav's constituency Chhapra, the BSP chief said "While work has started a long time back in Lalu's constituency, in Rae Bareli the Congress wanted to go for bhumi pujan now — just before the Lok Sabha elections only to garner votes".

Mayawati reeled off statistics to back her claim: Rae Bareli has got 20 factories, of which nine are running and eleven have closed down and due to this 92 acres of land has been wasted. Similarly, in Amethi sixteen factories were put up, of which nine are running and seven have closed down and 862 acres of land has gone waste. "How many people have got jobs from these units?", she asked and added that the coach factory too would have given jobs to merely four to five thousand people.

Denying Congress allegations that she was blocking development efforts, she instead accused the Congress of always meting out step motherly treatment to the state and causing impediments in various developmental schemes. Mayawati named various such schemes pending with the Central Government, including her demand of an Rs 80,000 crore special package for the state.

She also reacted to Sonia Gandhi's statement — "Who can stop me from coming to my home" — and said her government did not restrict anyone's entry anywhere. "If I had to stop them I would not have let them enter my home town Badalpur and hold a rally there and also my government would have successfully stopped Congress leaders' entry into Rae Bareli and would not have let her hold a road show."

Heading: In voting booth, race may play a bigger role - Indian Express
Content:
• Your editorial 'One-UP?' showcases the bankruptcy of leadership in our national polity. Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Mayawati's actions in cancelling the land allotted for a rail coach factory on the eve of its bhoomi pujan, and denying permission to Congress President Sonia Gandhi to hold a rally, is an outrageous act of petulance.

It also brings into question Mayawati's suitability to rule India's largest state, let alone be prime minister of India. Is she being surrounded by advisors who tell her only what she wants to hear?

— Prasad Malladi

Nidadavole

• Mayawati's strategy to stymie Sonia Gandhi only shows her hauteur, hubris and sense of insecurity. This does not mean that the Congress is whiter than white. But what is worse in this contrived cancellation of allotment of land is that Mayawati has sacrificed the interests of the common man at the altar of her political ambitions. Arbitrariness and misuse of political power undermine all that democracy stands for.

— Satwant Kaur

Mahilpur

Best education

• This refers to the Jaithirth Rao's article 'A new class theory'. Rao does injustice to the UGC when he blames it for all that ails higher education in India. The actual culprits are the politicians, who — with the exception of the left — have been steadfastly refusing to increase the budget allocation for education. Rao cannot disregard the fact that, in India, the best and the brightest students come out of national institutions "guided" by the UGC. Rao also sticks to the dogma of private enterprise being superior to public enterprise, an argument that does not apply to the field of education. Even in the US, education is mostly funded by the state, or by non-profit trusts. It will be enlightening to know how many Nobel laureates have graduated from state run institutions in comparison to those from private ones.

— K. Raghu

Ahmedabad

Strong on terror

• This is with reference to the news report 'Modi refuses to speak at NIC, hands speech text slamming UPA on terror'. It is on terrorism that the opposition NDA has a clear cut edge over the ruling UPA. The Congress must seize the initiative and make anti-terrorism its own platform, while at the same time ensuring that minorities are not unfairly targeted.

— Deepak Chikramane

Mumbai

Green energy

• It is unfortunate that while most developed countries are concentrating on solar and other forms of renewable energy, New Delhi is "committed" to buying costly as well as hazardous nuclear power.

— Hansraj Bhat

Mumbai

Heading: On eve of last debate, McCain going, going... - Indian Express
Content:
With less than three weeks until Election Day, a big question is looming over the campaign for the White House, and it has nothing to do with the economic crisis or the caustic exchanges between Barack Obama and John McCain over character and credentials. It is race.

Obama and McCain almost never talk directly about it. In some cases, like the condemnation of the Republican ticket issued last weekend by Representative John Lewis, the topic has come up openly: Lewis invoked George Wallace, the noted segregationist, in rebuking McCain as tolerating political rallies marked by crowds yelling insults at Obama.

But more often, it is found only in sentiments that are whispered, internalised or masked by discussions of culture or religion, and therefore hard to capture fully in polling.

Political strategists once assumed that polls might well overstate support for black candidates, since white voters might be reluctant to admit racially tinged sentiments to a pollster. Newer research has cast doubt on that assumption. Either way, the situation is confounding aides on both sides, who like everyone else are waiting to see what role race will play in the privacy of the voting booth.

Harold Ickes, a Democrat who was the Rev Jesse Jackson's senior advisor when he ran for President, said when he looked at polls, he routinely shaved off a point or two from Obama's number to account for hidden racial prejudices.

"If he were white, this would be a blowout," Ickes said. "I think the country has come a long, long, long way since the 1960s. I think everybody would agree with that. But if you talk to people in certain states, they will say there are impulses that do not benefit Barack Obama because of the color of his skin."

Saul Anuzis, the Republican chairman in Michigan, said he had become accustomed to whispered asides from voters suggesting they would not vote for Obama because he is black. "We honestly don't know how big an issue it is," Anuzis said.

And if Obama is losing support simply because he is black, that is not a one-sided equation. A crucial part of Obama's theory for winning the election is turning out blacks in places like Florida and North Carolina, a state that Obama's advisors view as in play because of the significant African-American population.

Heading: Black still a colour for the colourblind generation - Indian Express
Content:
N Y TIMES-CBS NEWS

Obama 53-McCain 39

The McCain campaign's recent sharp personal attacks on Obama appear to have backfired and tarnished his more than their intended target, the latest New York Times/CBS News poll has found.

After several weeks in which the McCain campaign unleashed a series of strong political attacks on Obama, trying to tie him to a former 1960s radical, the poll found that more voters see McCain as waging a negative campaign than Obama. Six in 10 voters surveyed said that McCain had spent more time attacking Obama than explaining what he would do as President; by about the same number said Obama had spent more time explaining than attacking.

The poll found that if the election were held today, 53 per cent of those determined to be probable voters said they would vote for Obama and 39 per cent said they would vote for McCain. Voters who said their opinions of Obama had changed recently were twice as likely to say they had grown more favorable. And voters who said that their views of McCain had changed were three times more likely to say that they had worsened.

LA TIMES-BLOOMBERG

Obama 50-McCain 41

With fear about the economy driving voters his way, Barack Obama has broadened his lead over John McCain and strengthened his hold on key groups both presidential candidates are courting, a Los Angeles Times/ Bloomberg poll has found.

Three weeks before election day, Obama leads McCain 50 per cent to 41 among voters likely to cast ballots November 4. In September, the Illinois Democrat had a 49 per cent to 45 lead.

In the weeks between the two surveys, the nation's financial system teetered toward collapse, and the poll shows the effect of that upheaval on voters. Only 10% now feel the country is heading in the right direction — the lowest figure since the poll began asking the question in 1991. Eighty-four per cent said the country was on the wrong track.

Nearly 7 in 10 cited the economy as the most important issue for the presidential candidates to solve — from 4 in 10 in September — and Obama was the clear beneficiary. Voters saw him as more trustworthy than McCain on the economy and better able to handle a financial crisis.

Heading: China land reforms in limbo after Govt push - Indian Express
Content:
William Osborne, a sophomore political science major and member of the currently all-white University of Kentucky chapter of FarmHouse, an international fraternity, is naturally soft-spoken. But when asked if he had heard people say that they would not vote for Barack Obama because he is black, his voice dropped to a barely perceptible level.

"I might have heard something like that," he said. Asked if what he had heard was hard to talk about, Osborne stopped talking altogether and simply nodded, looking miserable.

Throughout this campaign season, many commentators and politicians have proclaimed today's youth to be a colourblind generation in which racial prejudice has receded and diversity is embraced. But in two days of interviews here and north of the Ohio River in Cincinnati, most young people acknowledged that race was still a powerful if subtle factor among their peers.

At the University of Cincinnati, Anthony Galarza, a graduate student in urban planning, said he had heard off-color jokes about an Obama presidency that suggested the White House would become "more ghetto" with "barbecues on the front lawn".

"I would think on a college campus we would be a little more liberal," said Galarza, 29. "To hear it so openly talked about, it's disturbing... I don't think anyone who is colourblind would make a comment like that."

The significance of race as a powerful factor among the young is supported by statistical data. Most polls show that Obama is far more popular among younger voters than John McCain. But in exit polls conducted by Edison/Mitofsky this year, younger Democratic primary voters were no less likely to say that race had been an important factor in their vote than people 30 and older.

And in two states — Georgia and Illinois — young voters were actually more likely than older ones to say that race had been important.

Heading: Drunk man attempts to ‘hijack’ plane - Indian Express
Content:
A funny thing happened on the way to the Third Plenary Session of the 17th Central Committee, where China's Communist Party leaders were expected to enact a bold land reform programme allowing farmers to buy, sell or lease their fields eventually.

In recent weeks, coverage of reform issues was stepped up in the official media. And President Hu Jintao made a high-profile trip to rural Anhui province, during which the state media quoted him telling farmers that they would be able to transfer their land rights.

Yet by the time the closed-door national meeting had wrapped up Sunday, the issue all but disappeared. It wasn't mentioned in the final communique from the 368-member decision-making body.

At stake is a system of ownership restrictions that hinder China's 740 million farmers from making more productive use of their plots.

"I'm very disappointed that land reform wasn't even mentioned in the communique," said Hu Xingdou, an economics professor with the Beijing Institute of Technology.

Land reform here have foundered for decades in part because the issue encapsulates many of modern China's fundamental contradictions. In spite of a roaring market economy, leaders of this nominally Communist country still maintain a collective land ownership system.

Hu and Premier Wen Jiabao spent much of their careers in the countryside, understand the farmers' plight and want to make changes, said a Communist Party member. But this is a social problem, he added, and intent isn't enough.

In a statement on Sunday, China's state news agency announced that the Central Committee passed a package of rural policies and discussed the global financial crisis. But it made no mention of land reform.

It also aims to double rural incomes by 2020. Annual per capita disposable income for those living in the countryside was $720 during the first half of 2008.

Sui Yuyou, a farmer from Shandong province, said he's pleased with the government's focus on rural issues. But if rural incomes were higher, he might not need to spend time in Beijing, where his family can earn as much in a month waiting tables as they earn in a year back in their village.

Heading: 5 soldiers, 52 Tigers killed in Lanka - Indian Express
Content:
A drunk passenger, who claimed to have a bomb tried to hijack a Russian-bound Turkish Airlines plane on Wednesday, but fellow passengers soon overpowered him, officials said.
