No wonder then that Aussie cricket's chief villain over the last summer finds himself with an unlikely and heroic moniker of 'Hottie'.

Heading: No hurdle too high for Gayathri - Indian Express
Content:
VirdhawaL Khade lived up to his billing on Wednesday, winning a gold and two silver medals and, in the process, sinking a games' record at the Commonwealth Youth Games here.

India's top swimmer first won a silver medal in the 200m freestyle with a timing of 1:49.86, and followed it up with gold in 50m butterfly with a new event record of 24.25s. He then wrapped up a rewarding day in the pool by rallying India to a second-place finish behind Australia in the 4X100m freestyle relay at the Balewadi swim-centre here.

Swimming the final leg of the relay, Khade stopped the clock at 3:33.20, putting the team — Aaron D'Souza, NA Sandeep, Ashwin Menon being the other three — ahead of the South Africans.

Commenting on his Day One success, Khade said, "I am happy with the gold medal but since I am taking part in five other events, I'm looking forward to successfully finishing the others with wins as well."

In the 200m freestyle, he was leading for the first 50m before Aussie Ryan Napolean caught up with him on the turn. The Indian then seemed to slacken his pace, and had to be content with a silver.

"I am not at all disappointed with the silver medal. I do not know what went wrong but then I gave my 100 percent and am sure that I will make it better the next time. I must also say that the competition was tough." Cheered on by a raucous crowd, the 16-year-old sure set the pool ablaze, and is likely to draw the crowds by the hordes in coming days as India gets accustomed to its own swimming sensation.

Commenting on his preparations for the 2010 Commonwealth games, Khade added, "This is almost the end of the season and I am planning to take a short break before starting with the preparations for the next season."

Heading: One aim: Uganda’s lifting bronze had some outside help - Indian Express
Content:
Gayathri Govindhraj surprised many on Tuesday when she came up with her best performance to secure a silver in the 100m hurdles event at the Commonwealth Youth Games at the Shiv Chhatrapati athletics stadium in Balewadi. A day later, however, it seemed quite normal when she added a 4x100m gold relay to her kitty.

Talking to The Indian Express after the medal ceremony, Gayathri stated her effort was doubly sweet as many of her fellow competitors had given her no chance of making an impression. "But all my coaches were sure I would do well," said the versatile athlete from Chennai, who has now turned her focus on Thursday's triple jump.

"At the start of my athletics career, I was a junior national triathlete, but my coach Dr. P Nagarajan advised me concentrate on the track and field events," said Gayathri, who first did just fitness exercises for three years. Blessed with strong legs, her coaches have advised her to concentrate on both jumping and hurdling. "They said if you train well for the triple, you'd well in the hurdles also."

Lack of proper competition in the national meets is one of the problems the 5-foot 9-inch tall girl is now facing. "The Barbados, who won the event on Tuesday, helped me to clock my best time-ever of 14 secs. But the crowd was also was very supportive," she added.

Heading: Split wide open: Anand, Kramnik draw again - Indian Express
Content:
This was a medal that came after a common cause brought together people of different nationalities. Charles Seekaya's first medal for his country, a bronze in the 62 kg category of men's weightlifting, brought smiles to the faces of the entire Ugandan contingent. But it was only made possible thanks to Suresh Pai, the weightlifting coach of Fiji and the Ugandan national olympic committee.

When it was required, the Indian origin Pai would arrange funds himself. At other times, he would travel to the remotest village in Uganda to conduct camps for kids.

"We are very grateful to him," said Salim Musoke, president of the weightlifting federation of Uganda.

Seekaya lifted a total of 215 kgs in the clean and jerk and snatch categories of the event to win bronze. In the process, he created a new record for the Commonwealth Youth Games with a 120 kg lift in the jerk.

The bronze was made even more special considering the turmoil the sport finds itself in back home. "The weightlifting scene in Uganda is not bright. Our athletes have had to deal with a lot of hardship before coming here. We do not receive proper funding from the government, and so facilities are a big problem," Musoke said.

The performance of Uganda's weightlifting contingent at the Beijing Olympics is proof of the sad state of affairs. Kivumbi Mubarak Musoke, the only lifter representing the country, was reduced to being a spectator after the games technical committee disqualified him for being overweight.

"It is a grand feeling for me. I am very happy with my performance as I had been training vigorously for the past one and a half years. Everyone at home will be ecstatic about my achievement," said Seekaya.

The squad will now look forward to the performance of Millykaitesi, the woman weightlifter in the 53 kg.

Heading: DCB stops defence lawyer from meeting client in courtroom - Indian Express
Content:
Prosecutors in an Italian court Thursday asked the key middleman in the IAF's VVIP chopper deal whether the initials 'AP' in an alleged "budget sheet" for bribes to politicians referred to Ahmed Patel, the political secretary of UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi.

The middleman, Guido Haschke, who has consistently denied bribing Indian officials or politicians, replied that he did not know who or what 'AP' stood for.

As first reported by The Indian Express, Italian prosecutors had last month produced a handwritten document they alleged was a "budget" drawn up by two middlemen — Haschke and Christian Michel — which purportedly lists initials of Indian politicians and designations of bureaucrats and IAF officers who allegedly had to be "handled" to fix the Rs 3,546 crore deal.

The alleged "budget sheet" detailed how kickbacks of 51 million euros would be divided and under the heading "POL" — Haschke has claimed this referred to Indian politicians — there is a reference to "AP" against which "3 million euro" has been listed.

Another amount of 15/16 million euros was listed against "FAM" which is said to be "Family". Haschke has claimed the note was dictated to him by British consultant Michel during one of their meetings in 2008.

On Thursday, Italian prosecutor Eugenio Fusco asked Haschke during a court hearing in Busto Arsizio near Milan whether "AP" in the note was a reference to Ahmed Patel.

In his reply, the middlemen said he did not know what AP meant when he wrote it down. Haschke also denied any bribes were paid for the contract and said that the "budget sheet" was just an imaginary note drawn up and was never acted upon.

He also said the budget sheet was merely bragging by Michel about his Indian contacts and that Haschke tried to disassociate himself from the Briton.

Strongly denying any wrongdoing in the deal, Haschke also claimed to Indian interrogators in the court that no bribes were paid for the contract and that the money he received from AgustaWestland - in excess of 24 million euros - is justified as fees for engineering consultations.

Italian prosecutors also produced another note in court Thursday - a March 2008 fax by Michel to Peter Hulett, said to be the then head of region, govt sales at AgustaWestland's India office. The fax said that among the politicians who would use the choppers once acquired by India would be UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi and her senior advisors, including Ahmed Patel.

However, Sonia is not entitled to use government helicopters. She can use VIP aircraft only when she flies with the PM, President or ministers who are officially entitled to the aircraft. This fax by the British middleman has also been shared by the Italian side with the CBI team that is in Busto Arsizio for the hearing.

Michel has been elusive and no investigative agency has been able to reach him.

Haschke, who is facing a case in Italy for being part of a conspiracy to bribe Indian officials to ensure the AW 101 chopper was picked by the IAF, faced several questions from the Indian side and denied any irregularity.

But the Indian side did not ask Haschke to explain what AP, FAM or any of the other acronyms in the note - "DS", "JS AIR", "AFA", "DG Acquisition", CVC" etc - referred to, source said.

The middleman, who was quizzed about his association with former Air Chief S P Tyagi - named as an accused in the CBI case in the deal - denied that any money had been paid to the retired Indian officer. Haschke, sources said, admitted that he was in regular touch with three cousins of Tyagi who have also been named in the case.

In response to a question from the Indian side, Haschke said he was not aware if any money was paid to S P Tyagi.

The UPA government had come under pressure in connection with the alleged kickbacks last month after The Indian Express report on the budget sheet of the middlemen. The opposition BJP had demanded the government reveal what or who "AP" and "FAM" stand for. The party also said that it wants a detailed discussion in Parliament on "alleged payments to persons close to the ruling establishment" in connection with the controversial chopper deal and has accused the government of "running away from discussions".

The discussion did not take place as the Parliament session was abruptly called off midway.

Heading: Is this seasoned socialist a potential Nano nemesis? - Indian Express
Content:
The designated Metropolitan Court, hearing the Ahmedabad blasts case, witnessed some heated scenes on Thursday when 16 accused, including Mufti Mohammad Abu Bashir and Abaas Samaeja, were produced before it at the end of their remand period.

The situation turned hostile when advocate Hashim Qureshi, representing accused Javed Ansari, tried to talk to him in the court room. He was stopped by an Ahmedabad City Detection of Crime Branch (DCB) policeman and rudely told to back off.

Qureshi took exception to this and said it was his right to speak to his client.

"Javed Ansari is a patient of tuberculosis and I wanted to talk to him to ascertain that he was being provided proper treatment by the DCB. In fact, the court had also given a ruling that he be given proper treatment. There was no need for the policeman to get aggressive," Qureshi said, adding that an advocate is an officer of the court.

Later, Metropolitan Magistrate G M Patel told Qureshi that he should have taken permission of the court before meeting his client.

Qureshi, meanwhile, moved an application before the court stating that the behaviour by the policeman was not befitting the kind that should be practiced inside a courtroom.

The court posted the matter for hearing on Friday, when the DCB is likely to demand further remand of all the 16 accused.

Heading: Fatal friendship: 27-year-old killed by his girlfriend’s uncle - Indian Express
Content:
H K Thakar, who has filed a PIL against Tata's project, is a disciple of Madhu Limaye

Who is H K Thakar who moved a Public Interest Litigation in the Gujarat High Court challenging the allotment of land for Tata's Nano car project? Many advocates practising in the High Court were seen asking each other on Wednesday about the political background of Thakar from the Rashtriya Kisan Dal (RKD).

The 64-year-old is an old socialist, and the general secretary of the state unit of the Samajwadi Party (SP). He is one of the closest persons to SP supremo Mulayam Singh Yadav, as both of them have worked with socialist ideologue late Madhu Limaye.

Thakar came in contact with Limaye in 1965 when the latter came to address students in the Gujarat College here. With a zeal for social reform, Thakar holding Ganga jal in his hands along with several other students, took oath in the presence of Limaye that he would never do power politics and always do his best for the uplift of the poor and the needy. He had also sworn not to contest polls, but work as a watchdog of the people.

Forty-three years down the line, Thakar has kept the promises made before the veteran socialist. When his party fielded candidates from several constituencies in 2002 and 2007 assembly elections in the state, he himself did not contest. Incidentally, his party could not win a single seat.

After graduating as mechanical engineer in 1968, Thakar set up a factory in the Wadhavan industrial estate in his native district of Surendranagar. The factory is defunct now and he survives on income from agriculture. He owns a large tract of agriculture land in Halvad village. When the state government raised tariff for farm power in 2003, his RKD was the first to oppose it.

His colleague Manoj Patodia fought against it for two years and also staged a sit-in agitation in Gandhinagar. Thakar also presented a document with 110 grievances of farmers to the Agriculture department at that time, which was termed as kisan dastavej (farmers' document). He also fought for reducing interest on farm loans from 14 per cent to 7 per cent by nationalised banks as also the cooperative banks in the state.

Talking about the Nano land controversy, he said he was not against the project, but against the grabbing of farmers' land for agricultural purposes and then passing it off to an industrialist at throwaway prices. He says the land was taken on a lease of 99 years in 1902 by the then British government in India for agricultural purposes. The lease period expired in 2002.

"Honestly, it should have been returned to the descendants of the original owners of the land. But in its official records, the government is showing the land as its own," he says. "This is illegal and cannot be accepted," he adds, affirming that he would fight to get justice for poor farmers.

When pointed out that the government has charged the Tatas Rs1,100 per square metre, which is the prevailing market rate in the area and hence his charge of selling it at a very cheap rate did not hold water, he said the money should not to go to the government but to the real owners of the land.

"The government is not the owner. It has illegally grabbed the land and selling it to the country's biggest corporate house in violation of all rules," he said.

His state party president Surendra Yadav said the government could not acquire the land for private parties. Not only in Sanand, the government made a similar mistake in Jamnagar also where it acquired farmlands and sold it out to Reliance for setting up a petroleum refinery.

"While the land in Jamnagar was acquired at a very cheap rate from farmers, it was sold to Reliance at a very high rate. Ideally, the farmers should have been paid at the rate at which Reliance was sold the land," said Yadav, adding the land acquisition policy was causing unrest among the farmers in the state.

Heading: Junior artiste’s real-life spear act was unintentional, say police - Indian Express
Content:
Accused was against his niece's friendship with the victim

27-year-old man was killed late on Wednesday allegedly by three persons for continuing his friendship with a girl.

According to the police, the victim, Hiren Patel from Ranip, was a friend of the niece of the prime accused, Harshad Patel.

The incident took place near Hiren's residence at Sumero Society in Ranip around 11 pm on Wednesday. Harshad (45) along with his two other accomplices, Kalpesh Thakore (22) and Raksh Patel (35), allegedly attacked Hiren with sharp-edged weapons, injuring him on head and neck. Hiren's brother, Dhaval and others intervened, following which the accused fled from the crime scene. Hiren was rushed to V S Hospital, where he succumbed to his injuries on Thursday.

Preliminary investigations revealed that Harshad was against his niece, Nimisha's friendship with Hiren and had warned her of severe consequences earlier.

Despite this, the two continued their relationship for the past two years. Nimisha even used to visit Hiren's house frequently, the police said.

"It seems that the accused killed Hiren because of his friendship with Nimisha. Based on a complaint filed by Dhaval, we have registered a case of murder. While Kalpesh and Rakesh have been arrested, Harshad, who is presently undergoing medical treatment, will be arrested soon," said K B Jhala, Sabarmati police inspector.

He added: "Meanwhile, Harshad has filed a counter complaint accusing Hiren, Dhaval and their friends of assaulting him. We are investigating both the complaints."

In a separate case, the owner of a petrol pump on the Ahmedabad-Gandhinagar highway, was robbed of cash to the tune of Rs 51,100 and his Innova car allegedly by three unidentified persons late on Wednesday. The incident took place near Kolas Tekri area in Sabarmati, when Santosh Agrawal (57) was returning to his home. The trio, who were on a motorcycle, overtook Agrawal's vehicle and asked him to stop.

"When Agrawal stopped the car to inquire into the matter, one of the three accused pounced on him. Thereafter, they started beating him up and escaped with his cash and car," Sabarmati police sub inspector, B P Jadeja said.

Heading: Twin tragedy: Love birds end life on Chandi Padva - Indian Express
Content:
Both Manu and Sajid lost their cool after latter's car hit the unit's horses

You are not likely to find this in the Ramayan: An angry soldier of Ravana's cavalry, galloping back from battle on horseback, and spearing a man to death, at the parking lot.

The incident occurred on Tuesday night when Manu Gulshan Sindhi, a junior artiste in the NDTV serial 'Ramayan' was racing down the road with a few dozen other costumed horsemen from the sets of Sagar Studio, where the serial is being shot.

Eager to find space for their tired steeds, the men were reportedly hurtling down the road when a car appeared came in their way and Sindhi and his horse crashed into it.

Eyewitnesses said there were about 40 horses galloping out of the set, and they were to move on the road inside the premises that connects the studio with the Ajwa Road, used for parking.

"Once the shot got over, there were some 40 horses racing out of the set at about 50 kmph. Cars and motorcycles were parked on the same road, as there is no other parking facility in the studio. The driver of the car, 35-year-old Sajid Saiyyad, perhaps may not have known that the horses would come charging at him,'' said Mohammed Zakir Sulaiman, a horse riding trainer for actors in the TV serial.

Panigate Police Inspector, M D Jadeja said both Sindhi and Saiyyad lost their cool after the horse hit the car.

"Manu must have thrust the spear he was carrying into Saiyyad's chest accidentally. It got stuck between his chest and neck," said Jadeja.

He added that it didn't look like Sindhi intended to kill Saiyyad.

"They knew each other and shared no enmity. It must have been a spur of the moment act," he said.

Manager of Sagar Studio, Raju Shukla said he was not present during the shoot as he had some engagements in the city.

"But, what I have gathered from the security guards is that Saiyyad started his Indica without realising that some 40 horses were coming his way," he said.

Heading: Over 42 cases of food poisoning on day of festival - Indian Express
Content:
Consumed poison at Dumas beach; girl yet to be identified

A couple committed suicide by consuming poison at the Dumas beach on Wednesday night while the entire city was celebrating the festival of Chandi Padva. The body of the youth was later identified with the help of his driving license, while the girl is yet to be identified. A bottle of poison has been recovered from the spot.

According to the police, Ramesh Laskhari, a resident of Dumas, found the bodies of the couple lying on Dumas beach on Thursday morning. He immediately informed the police, following which Umra police officers rushed to the spot and commenced investigations.

The youth has been identified as Bharat Dhameliya (22), a resident of Gautam Park Society in Punagam in Surat. The police also recovered a pocket diary, motorcycle keys and mobile phone from Bharat's pocket. The police made a phone call to one of the numbers mentioned in Bharat's diary and informed his cousin Sanjay about the incident. Sanjay rushed to the spot and identified Bharat's body. Investigations are on to identify the girl, the police said.

Sanjay revealed that Bharat hailed from Palitana taluka of Bhavnagar district and had been living in Surat for the last four years. He was worked in a diamond manufacturing unit at Kapodara and stayed alone in a rented house at Punagam. Sanjay, however, said that he did not know the girl.

Umra police inspector RS Patel said: "We have taken photos of the girl and sent our team to the factory where Bharat was working as well as to his residential society for her identification. We suspect that both were in love with each other and might have faced some difficulty, which drove them to take the extreme step. The approximate age of the girl is 20 years. We have sent our teams to different places for identification of the girl."

The bodies have been sent to New Civil Hospital for a post mortem.

Heading: 5-year-old girl still critical after rape - Indian Express
Content:
More than 42 cases of food poisoning were reported from the Katargam area of the city on Chandi Padva festival on Wednesday. Over 40 people, including minors, were admitted to Prannath hospital and three other hospitals in Katargam, after they complained of vomiting and loose motions.

The victims were employees of Pramukh Gems, a diamond firm in Surat, which had organised a get together at the community hall in Katargam on Wednesday evening to mark the Chandi Padva festival. The employees and their families celebrated the festival by eating gharis, rabdi, farsan and other sweets.

According to sources, the number of people who turned up for the function was much more than expected, as a result of which the organisers ran out of rabdi. The firm owner Vallabh Gadhia then sent his staff to bring more rabdi from Chhapra Pendawala, a sweet shop in Varachha.

More than 60 people had the rabdi and went home after the conclusion of the function. Later, however, some people who had the rabdi brought from Varachha complained of vomiting and loose motions and were admitted to nearby hospitals.

Sources from the Surat Municipal Corporation said that over 40 people suffered from food poisoning and were treated in four hospitals including Prannath hospital, Puja Hospital, Hans Hospital and Kalrav Hospital.

While a majority of patients were discharged on Thursday afternoon, around 17 patients are still undergoing treatment in the hospitals.

Katargam police officers rushed to the hospitals after learning about the incident. Surat Municipal Corporation Deputy Health Commissioner, Dr I C Patel, said: "We sent our teams to the sweet shop in Varachha and collected rabdi samples from the shop as well as from the community hall in Katargam. We will carry out various tests and if the shop owner is found guilty, we will take strict action against him and cancel his license. We are waiting for the lab test report."

Heading: Ford Foundation looks for new generation of social justice leaders - Indian Express
Content:
A five-year-old girl is fighting for life at the SSG Hospital after being kidnapped and raped by an unidentified person a couple of days ago at Ankleshwar in Bharuch district. This is the third rape incident in the district in a fortnight, wherein a minor has been victimised.

Police said that a case of kidnap and rape has been registered against an unidentified person. "The condition of the girl has been reported to be critical," said Investigating Officer A D Srivastav.

Based on description of the accused given by the girl, the police have released a sketch of the suspect. The accused is said to be around 30-year-old and five-feet tall and is said to have been wearing a yellow wristband on the right hand .

The girl, however, could not give much information about the incident as she was in a state of shock, the police said. "We suspect that the accused is a small-time labourer. An extensive combing operation is being carried out," Srivastav added.

The incident was reported on Tuesday when a local, Sabir Uniya, found the girl, with wounds, lying abandoned on a roadside. He took her to the Ankleshwar GIDC police station. Later, a medical check up of the girl confirmed rape. After giving her first aid at a local hospital, she was referred to the SSG Hospital for further treatment.

The girl, a resident of Bholav village in Bharuch district, has been living with her maternal uncle in Ankleshwar for the last 10 days. According to the police, after the girl lost her father a month ago and her mother eloped with another man, her uncle brought her to his house.

Heading: Raizuddin remanded to police custody till October 23 - Indian Express
Content:
The Ford Foundation International Fellowships Programme (IFP) on Thursday invited applications for its 2009 programme.

The programme seeks to build a new generation of social justice leaders in India and abroad by offering opportunities for quality higher education. The deadline for submitting applications is November 15, 2008.

Forty candidates will be selected following an intensive search and selection process for a Master's degree at a university abroad or in India. The applicant must be an Indian or a permanent resident of India, living in Gujarat, Bihar, Chhatisgarh, Jammu and Kashmir, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Orissa, Uttar Pradesh or Uttarakhand.

The applicant must also be a graduate with at least three years' work experience relevant to his field of study. The eligible fields of study include social science, arts and humanities. Graduates belonging to Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe Other Backward Classes, religious minorities as well as women and the physically challenged, are encouraged to apply.

"The programme is specially designed to support candidates from groups that have historically lacked access to higher education," said Vivek Mansukhani, Director, Ford Foundation International Fellowships. "There is an increasing need for sound education for committed people who would normally not have access to quality and focused education. IFP is making a long-term investment to fill this gap," he said.

The programme became active in India seven years ago, and will last only till 2010. Till now, 240 students have received the fellowship in India, while 160 completed their fellowship. About 75 per cent of the 160 alumni are back in India to serve the country.

The programme started in Gujarat three years ago. Till now, 15 candidates have been selected from the state and 10 have completed their fellowship. "We want to create opportunities for real social and economic change through a network of grassroots workers," said Mansukhan.

Arjun Rathva, an IFP alumnus from Gujarat said: "The course helped me understand education from the perspective of development. It will be very useful in my work as a resident director at the Adivasi Academy in Tejgadh, Vadodara, and as a teacher at the SMCR Arts College, Pavitjetpur, Gujarat University."

Through the Ford Foundation International Fellowships Programme, Rathva completed his Master's of Arts in Development and Education Studies from the University of Leeds, United Kingdom.

The application forms are available at www.ifpsa.org.

Heading: Lalu promises better rail services for Saurashtra - Indian Express
Content:
The designated Metropolitan Court hearing the Ahmedabad blasts case, on Thursday, remanded accused Raizuddin Nasir to police custody till October 23.

The Ahmedabad City Detection of Crime Branch (DCB) had sought the custody of Nasir in the Raipur Chakla blast case, which is registered with the Khadia police station.

Nasir, who was in judicial custody in Belgaum, Karnataka, was brought to Ahmedabad on September 24. The DCB is investigating the role Nasir played in the conspiracy of the July 26 blasts.

A DCB official said: "Nasir had gone to Pakistan to take training in terrorist operations. He has extensive links with the Laskar-e-Toiba and had attended the training camp held in Wagamon in Kerala."

Heading: Government approves gauge conversion of Bhuj-Naliya section - Indian Express
Content:
Union Railway Minister Lalu Prasad Yadav on Thursday promised to provide better rail service for Saurashtra region and indicated at setting up rail network connecting the coastal towns of Gujarat.

While inaugurating the Veraval-Somnath broad gauge line, Lalu said the railway authorities were seriously considering setting up railway network to cover coastal town of the state.

He said that Dwarka would be developed as model station at a cost of Rs 2 crore and promised a train from Okha to Rameshwaram in Tamil Nadu.

The broad gauge line inaugurated on Thursday is part of the larger, Rajkot-Somnath line, which is 190 km long and has been constructed at the cost of Rs 29.6 crore.

On his two-day visit to Gujarat, Lalu had reached Dwarka on Wednesday morning in a special train alongwith his wife Rabri Devi, son Tejpalsinh and daughters Laxmi and Aparna.

Before reaching Somnath on Wednesday night, he spent time with mediapersons at Jamnagar, where he claimed that rail service is improving and competing well with airline services. People who earlier preferred to travel in planes, are now turning to trains thus, increasing the profits in railways. He said that the railway department is expected to make a profit of around Rs 1 lakh crore this year.

Heading: Many skeletons tumble out of studio cupboard after killing - Indian Express
Content:
The government on Thursday gave its approval for taking up gauge conversion of the 101.24 km long Bhuj-Naliya section with further extension of 24.65 km up to Vayor at an estimated cost of Rs 318.24 crore.

The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) approved the funding pattern of the project —Rs 238.24 crore through budgetary support and Rs 80 crore to be given by cement industries in the area.

The existing metre gauge link Bhuj-Naliya was constructed in late 1980s on strategic consideration. After completion of gauge conversion of Gandhidham-Bhuj section, this metre gauge section has become isolated and is closed for traffic at present.

Gauge conversion of Bhuj-Naliya section will tap the freight traffic of this rich mineral belt and cement industries of Kutch district of Gujarat.

Besides, the conversion of this metre gauge section into broad gauge will enable the section to connect border areas of Gujarat with rest of the country.

Heading: Education in tribal belt is still a grey area in  Gujarat - Indian Express
Content:
Skeletons in the closet of Sagar Studio have started tumbling out after the killing of driver Sajid Saiyyad by junior artist Manu Ghulam Sindhi on Wednesday evening.

The temporary staff are crying foul that they are not paid regularly and are threatened that they would be sacked if their demands persist. Furthermore, the studio has to deal with problems of parking and water supply .

On Wednesday, junior artist Sindhi, a resident of Tarsali, stabbed Saiyyad with a spear. The management of Sagar Studios claims that Saiyyad worked there for only 13 days. But his brother, Naushad, who also works there as a driver, said Saiyyad had been working there for the past one year.

Around 20 drivers attending Saiyyad's funeral at a graveyard near Sardar Estate were fuming with rage against the authorities of Sagar Studio.

"They don't pay salaries for 4-5 months at a stretch. When somebody wants to quit, they tell them to go away and say that it's very easy to get a replacement," said a driver present at Saiyyad's funeral. He rather sneered when asked about the compensation Saiyyad's family would get.

"I don't know what led to the brawl, but my brother was frustrated about non-payment of salary for months," said Naushad.

Saiyyad's father Mohammed Sheikh had migrated to Sayajipura from Bihar in the 70s. He worked as a farm labourer, while Saiyyad and his three brothers learnt driving.

After the death of Sheikh, Saiyyad has taken charge of the family. His two children are students of a Gujarati medium school in Sayajipura.

On the other hand, manager of Sagar Studio Rajiv Shukla said there was no irregularity in payment of salary, nor was there a parking problem.

But, he admitted that there is no water supply in the studio.

A security guard, however, said: "The accident wouldn't have happened if there was a proper parking place that was located at a distance from the set where NDTV's 'Ramayan' was being shot."

Meanwhile, many junior artists, extras and drivers who either belong to Sayajipura or Vadodara are camping at Saiyyad's house trying to figure out how to offer help to the bereaved family.

"He died in a studio that is like our temple. This is the place to start in Vadodara for those who want a career in the film industry. The least that the management could have done was visit Saiyyad's family. But they did not do so," said Pradip Parmer, who is acting as Ravana's soldier in NDTV's Ramayana.

Heading: Heroes and the heroine - Indian Express
Content:
In a letter written to the principal secretary, Law and Judiciary, the prosecution has stated that  soon an appeal will be filed before the Supreme Court challenging the discharge of inter- state gangster Brijesh Singh.

Singh, a prime accused in the 1992 J J hospital shootout case was let off by the special TADA court last month after the court observed that there was no evidence directly against him.

Special public prosecutor Rohini Salian has written a letter to the principal secretary of the law and judiciary department of the state recommending filing of an appeal challenging Singh's discharge.In the letter, the prosecution has claimed that under the provisions of TADA, the Supreme Court had recently held that the confession of other accused can be used as substantial evidence.

On September 12, 1992, around 24 persons including Singh had allegedly barged into the state-run JJ Hospital. and opened fire on Shailesh Haldankar, a member of the Arun Gawli gang who was admitted in the hospital.

Heading: FACE TO FACE with Vatsal Sheth - Indian Express
Content:
Preity Zinta lets her hair down but not her guard

She is dressed casually in a six-pocketer and a sleeveless shirt, with her hair carelessly tied back. While most heroines dread being seen in public without caked faces, Zinta hasn't bothered with lip gloss. Her throat is hoarse from giving interviews for six hours straight yet she plunges into our half-hour marathon with the energy of a teenager. "The names of all my forthcoming movies begin with 'H' (Samir Karnik's Heroes, Deepa Mehta's Heaven on Earth and Jahnu Baruah's Har Pall); so excuse me if I sound confused," she warns.

Heroes, which releases alongside EMI, Fashion and Roadside Romeo on October 24, has patriotic undertones but Zinta is confident that it stands apart from what has been seen before. "I hate movies with long lectures and I wouldn't have taken it up if it were run-of-the-mill stuff," she assures, adding that she is glad the name of the movie was changed from Mera Bharat Mahan to Heroes. "It was too dramatic. I once saw a poster that read 'Mera Bharat Mahan', with 'Banana Padega' written much smaller in the next line," she laughs.

Heroes is a film about two youngsters (Sohail Khan and Vatsal Sheth) who undertake a road trip and meet people en route who change their perspective on the country. The cast includes Sunny and Bobby Deol, Mithun Chakraborty and Dino Morea, and Zinta is paired with Salman Khan. It's a role, she says, that's close to her own persona. "Kuljeet Kaur is a simple rural Punjabi girl who helps her husband in the farms yet can weather all storms and be the son of the house when the need arises," she explains in her newly acquired Punjabi accent.

So does she always take up roles 'close to her personality'? "Well, sometimes I pick roles that are close to my heart; sometimes I pick roles close to my friends and sometimes I pick the ones close to my bank balance," she laughs. "Heaven on Earth is close to my heart."

In Heaven on Earth, Zinta plays Chand, a Punjabi girl who marries an NRI and is subjected to domestic violence. "Deepa has taken real-life incidents and woven them into the story; the film is extremely moving," she says. Upon the suggestion that it sounds similar to Provoked, the Aishwarya Rai Bachchan-starrer, she snaps back, "There is no similarity in the two films except that both Aishwarya and I play Punjabi girls. You have to see the film to know."

But Har Pall will mark Zinta's return to commercial cinema after The Last Lear and Heaven on Earth.

The actress, who is also the only woman to own an IPL team, is looking forward to the next season of the game. Despite the disappointing results, she is excited. "The media has been unfair with me. I admit that when I ventured into it I hardly knew anything about the game but the fours and the sixes. But I have learnt now — I know how to lose with a smile, which is hard. But you know what? The most important are still the fours and sixes."

Heading: Very filmy - Indian Express
Content:
What's on your iPod?
The songs from my movie Heroes—which will release soon—especially the track Badmash Launde.

What's your DVD pick?
It would have to be Andaz Apna Apna all the way.

Your favourite romantic scene in a movie?
I think all the romantic scenes featuring Shah Rukh Khan and Kajol are wonderful. I particularly like the scene from Dilwale Dulhaniya Le Jayenge where he tells her that she's going to marry a guy she's never met.

Which actress you would love to go on a date with and why?
I would love to go on a date with Preity Zinta because she's a fantastic person and drop-dead gorgeous. I had a great time working with her on Heroes.

Which dialogue have you mouthed in front of the mirror the most?
I've never mouthed a dialogue in front of the mirror. I only peep in to check my hair.

Who inspired you to become an actor?
Honestly, I never planned to be an actor, so there was no inspiration. Besides, I'm not the kind of person who'd really look at other people to enhance my own performance.

The worst film you ever watched?
I can't think of a single one. I've loved every movie I've watched.

Which film you wish you could be a part of?
I'd have loved to play James Bond in the movie series.

What makes you an actor?
Honesty; that is very important. If you're an honest person, it reflects on the screen.

Quiz: From which film is this line: Apun ka naam hai Heera, apun ne sabko cheera.
Don't know (Correct answer: Gunda)

Heading: Don again - Indian Express
Content:
On record
Shah Rukh Khan has a fan following in Germany too. And that's official now. A collection of four exclusive and indepth interviews, releases today in Germany. The producers, Monica and Gareth Jones, say that it has been recorded especially for the non-Asian Bollywood market in Germany as "SRK's films, dubbed into German and released on TV and DVD, have found great success there". The DVD features interviews with Farah Khan, Karan Johar, Bollywood author Mushtaq Shiekh and the King Khan himself.

Local flavour
For those who've been wondering where Rani Mukerji has vanished, we'd like to let them know the actress is marooned in small village in Punjab. The actress, who is shooting with Shahid Kapoor for an untitled project, has been filling up time between the shoots by bingeing on locally-made chhole bhature. We just hope she's running in the mustard fields to work those calories off.

Auto mode
Himesh Reshammiya has surely worked hard on his bod to impress his auto-wallah fan following. So it didn't surprise us when he organised a special Karzzzz curtain-raiser concert to ensure their support for the forthcoming release. What irony then, that when the host Mona Singh went up to a 'fan' and asked him which movie will Himesh be seen in next, the auto-wallah said Tandoori Nights.

Anxiety pangs
Model-turned-actress Mughda Godse is losing some serious sleep as the release date of her debut film Fashion is coming close. The gorgeous lady apparently chopped off her hair recently, and that too in the middle of the night. Mughda's excuse? "I've been really nervous of late. I know it doesn't explain my action, but well..."

Heading: Centre not mentally strong to tackle terrorism, says Rajnath - Indian Express
Content:
Jaaved Jafferi's back but with a Rajnikant hangover

As animated in person as he is on screen, Jaaved Jafferi can effortlessly grab your attention even in a crowded pub. Even as our photographer waits for a photo session, he is busy posing for photographs with fans outside Firangi Paani, where we have a lunch date with the actor.

Diversity has always been his forte — an actor, a dancer, a mimicry artist and a singer — and this is what made him a natural choice for lending his voice to the villain in the animation movie Roadside Romeo. "I have lent my voice to Charlie Anna, the don of stray dogs. Anna is still stuck in the 1970s and thinks he's Rajnikant, which is where the fun begins," he smiles. Jafferi was approached by the director, Jugal Hansraj, and he instantly took up the role for he thought Charlie Anna made for an interesting character. "I like to do character roles for these leave an impression on the audience's mind," he says, "Look at Johnny Depp; he will always be remembered as Jack Sparrow. Similarly, I am still remembered as Abdul Cutpiece of Timex Timepass."

Hansraj has also utilised Jaffrey's crooning skills alongside Saif Ali Khan in a rap number. "This is my third film with Saif after Ta Ra Rum Pum and Salaam Namaste and he's so much fun. We just brought the same energy into the song," he explains. Despite the success of his iconic track Mumbhai from Bombay Boys, Jafferi does not consider himself a singer: "I don't have the skills to be a professional singer but I can express my feelings through words and music in my own style, which is what probably works for me."

Jafferi may briefly disappear from films, but he has always remained faithful to television through Boogie Woogie, the first reality dance show in India. "We don't sensationalise the show like the others on air currently; we are original. And the reason for our success is the fact that to be on our show, the participants don't have to look good. They are real people with real skills," says the judge.

The actor has also been invited on the judges' panel to Russia for the Golden Minbar Islamic Festival, a platform for movies that deal with Islam on day-to-day basis.

The 45-year-old has more projects underway — Loot with Govinda and Mithun Chakraborty, Daddy Kool, Dhamaal 2, Hello Darling and Chai Garam. But the film he is looking forward to the most is Paying Guest. "I play a normal guy in it, which is challenge of sorts." Or an irony of sorts.

Heading: ‘Modi will be party’s star campaigner in forthcoming elections’ - Indian Express
Content:
BJP chief congratulates Modi for bringing Nano project to Gujarat

Launching a scathing attack on the Congress-led UPA Government, BJP national president Rajnath Singh on Thursday accused the Centre of failing on all fronts, be it security, economy or society.

Addressing the media here, Rajnath said that terrorism and internal security issues will top the BJP's election agenda in the forthcoming general elections.

"There is not only a lack of stern will power to tackle the menace of terrorism, but I suspect that they do not have the right bent of mind for tackling terror," Rajnath said.

He added: "It is surprising that while Pakistan, the country which harboured and assisted terrorists for so long, is now mooting a national consensus on terrorism in India. The agenda of the National Integration Council did not even mention the word terrorism anywhere. When Narendra Modi and Vasundhara Raje voiced their disagreement, they used the word extremism."

Claiming that the Centre cannot differentiate between Muslims and terrorists, Rajnath said that he failed to understand as to why the government was not trying to reach a national consensus on terrorism. "With many of the UPA allies calling SIMI a cultural organisation and demanding citizenship for Bangladeshi infiltrators, it is apparent that the government is not serious about terrorism," he added.

He demanded a joint strategy involving the state police forces, fast track courts and 30 days' remand limit for terror accused.

Rajnath further said that the country has also been victimised by economic and cultural terrorism. "Fake currencies are now finding their ways even to the nationalised banks and the Union Government is raising questions on the very existence of Lord Ram," he added.

He slammed the Centre for failing to protect India from the impacts of the global recession by saying this is a result of economic mismanagement of the government.

Rajnath did not lose out on the opportunity to shower praise on Modi for bringing Tata's Nano car plant to Gujarat from West Bengal. "While Gujarat has created a model of development, I congratulate Modi for getting this prestigious project to Gujarat," he said.

He added: "For Gujarat, it is a proud moment as the next Prime Minister will be contesting from Gandhinagar. We would like to assure the country that we will not only pull the Indian economy out of this vicious bearish cycle, but also infuse a new life in the entire system."

Heading: Finance tech-city project waiting to be GIFT-wrapped - Indian Express
Content:
'As far as his moving to Delhi is concerned, it depends on what he wants...'

With the Election Commission announcing the dates for assembly polls in five states and the Lok Sabha elections inching closer, electioneering is gaining momentum across the country. BJP national president Rajnath Singh, who was in Ahmedabad to attend a party programme in connection with the biennial party expansion drive, talks to Newsline about his party's strategy for the forthcoming elections.

* Newsline: What is your party's take on whether Narendra Modi will move to Delhi?
Rajnath Singh: Narendra Modi is the Chief Minister of a state. Naturally, a CM has a national role as well. He will have a very important role to play in the forthcoming elections. As far as his moving to Delhi is concerned, it also depends on what he wants.

* NL: With dates for assembly elections in five states being declared, how is the party planning to take Modi's help for campaigning?
RS: He will be one of our star campaigners and will travel extensively for campaigning.

* NL: With so much thrust on development, how do you think the 'Gujarat Model' will work in other states?
RS: In terms of development, Gujarat has definitely created a successful model of its own and I give the credit for it to Narendrabhai. In other states, they have their unique characteristics and the developmental works are being done by negotiating local peculiarities. We'll continue to do the same.

* NL: You lauded Modi for bringing the Nano project to Gujarat. More than development, is the project becoming a symbol of political one-upmanship?
RS: It is the West Bengal Government who made a political issue of it. In Gujarat, this was brought in for the state's development.

* NL: While Modi has taken a very tough stand on terrorism, we saw the biggest serial blasts in the last one year happening in Gujarat. Also, there have been frequent cases of fake currency rackets surfacing here. Is this not a failure?
RS: You cannot call these failures. Look at the way it has been tackled here. Modi has done a great job. An event can take place anywhere. But what matters is how the administration handles it.

* NL: So much is being said about the Bajrang Dal and other similar groups, and some political parties have even demanded ban on them. But in Gujarat, we have seen them completely sidelined and almost silenced once the pitch of development picked up. Does this mean that these outfits become redundant as the focus shifts to development?
RS: They have not been engaged in anything destructive here. The issue is being politicised.

* NL: Recently, we saw Om Prakash Chautala's Indian National Lok Dal joining the NDA. Are there more parties coming NDA fold?
RS: NDA is in the expansion mode. We are also talking to some other parties and soon we'll have some other parties joining the Alliance.

* NL: Going by this, do we construe that even the BJP is not looking at the singular majority in Parliament anymore and has accepted the reality of coalition politics?
RS: Yes, sort of… But the BJP will in any case emerge as the single largest party in the next general election. May be we'll cross the 98-seat mark as well.

Heading: Card fraudster runs out of credit, lands in police net - Indian Express
Content:
As Nano gets red carpet, govt yet to acquire land for state's own much-hyped venture

The Narendra Modi government may have succeeded in getting 1,100 acres of land for the Tata's Nano car plant to be set up near Sanand in Ahmedabad district. But the government, it seems, has been struggling to acquire additional land from farmers for the much-hyped Gujarat International Finance Tech-City (GIFT) project proposed near Gandhinagar.

The difficulty the government is facing in acquiring private land from farmers threatens to delay the Rs 50,000-crore GIFT project to be benchmarked as "a global financial hub".

The project is envisaged to come up on about 1,000 acres near Shahpur village on the periphery of Gandhinagar. The government has already allotted 500 acres under its possession for the project, and now is in the process of allotting it another 250 acres of land. The project, which was announced over a year ago, still requires over 200 acres of land which is owned by farmers in the vicinity.

In its apparent bid to avoid any Singur-like controversy, the government has decided to purchase land from farmers on a piecemeal basis. Accordingly, the GIFT authorities recently invited offers from farmers to initially purchase only 11 acres of land from them.

At a meeting convened by GIFT officials in Gandhinagar last week, the farmers were reported to have quoted their land price at a whopping Rs 3,000 to Rs 4,000 per sq metre.

"We were taken aback when the peasants started bidding. They quoted exorbitant rates than expected. We are trying to persuade the land owners to sell their land at a lower rate," a GIFT official told Newsline on Thursday.

The official conceded that the agriculture land around Gandhinagar is much costlier than the one located in Sanand.

Although the government struggles to acquire additional land for the GIFT project, GUDC's Managing Director Srinivas Katikithala claims that the work on the Rs 4,000-crore infrastructure component of the project was expected to begin by the year end. "The land acquisition process is on, and we hope to commence work on the project shortly," he said.

The project is a joint venture between the Gujarat Urban Development Company (GUDC) and the Infrastructure Leasing and Financial Services (IL&FS) – a Mumbai-based leading infrastructure consultancy firm.

The East China Architectural Design and Research Institute (ECARDI), a China Government-owned firm credited with the design and construction of 80 per cent of the buildings in Shanghai, has been engaged to prepare detailed structural designs for several skyscrapers to come up at the sprawling GIFT site. One of the skyscrapers envisaged under the project will be more than 80-storey high, while another 50 high-rise buildings will have 50 storeys each.

Heading: Pitroda exhorts youth to think out of the box - Indian Express
Content:
Manish bribed some bank employees and mall officials to part with the details of credit cards of customers

The Ahmedabad City Detection of Crime Branch (DCB) arrested a credit card fraudster wanted in at least 23 cases from near Geeta Mandir Bus Stop on Thursday.

The accused has been identified as Manish Kakadia alias Vishal (26), a resident of Amika Nagar of Katar Gam in Surat and a native of Jaltarang Park of Nava Naroda area in Ahmedabad.

According to DCB officials, Kakadia used to bribe some officials of banks and shopping mall outlets to provide him with the details of credit cards of customers.

According to the DCB, through this racket, Kakadia has 'earned'

Rs 35 lakh. The DCB has handed over Kakadia to the Satellite police for further investigation.

Kakadia's name as the mastermind of the racket came to light following the arrest of two of his accomplices — Usmanbin Abdulla and Sonia Chhabda — by the Satellite police recently.

"Kakadia has accomplices in various cities like Mumbai, Delhi, Hyderabad and Chennai. They used to operate under the guise of a firm providing air-tickets. He would book tickets on Internet using the credit card details of other people and sell it at a lesser price," said a DCB official.

To misguide the banks and police, Kakadia used to lodge a complaint with the concerned bank of a particular credit card that some other person has used his card and so its services should be stopped. Interestingly, he would lodge the complaint only after the ticket has been used.

The police recovered two diaries from him, which contain details of stolen credit cards. A laptop, four cellphones, eight SIM cards and an ATM card were also recovered from him.

Heading: Surendranagar village, a pool of national-level swimmers - Indian Express
Content:
At the Bhaikaka Bhawan in Ahmedabad, they hung on to every word Sam Pitroda, chairman of the National Knowledge Commission (NKC), uttered. At times, his one-hour long speech evoked collective nods of agreement, while at times his anecdotes triggered repeated rounds of applause.

The response of 400 college students, who sat on chairs and more than 200, who plonked themselves on stairs — to Pitroda's lecture on the potential of knowledge —proved that his words had struck a chord with them.

And what they really took a liking to was Pitroda saying, "Don't listen to your parents and teachers. If they think you are doing something wrong, it means you must be doing something right. There is world of difference in what they experienced while growing up and what you are going through now."

Speaking about India's young workforce, Pitroda said: "We need good carpenters, good welders, good scientists and good engineers. India has almost 550 million people under the age of 35 who have the potential to provide workforce to the whole world."

Quoting from his life, he said that he was a son of a carpenter who had studied only till fourth standard. But he became successful only because of the knowledge he gained through education.

He said: "We have a population of over a billion, but only 350 universities. Our teachers don't do research and those who do, don't teach… but it is very important to share knowledge."

He added that by 2015, the country would need 1,500 universities, which would help to educate 20 per cent of population instead of a mere eight per cent.

Pitroda said that based on NKC's recommendations, the government had begun planning on a National Knowledge Network that will connect 5,000 colleges and research institutions across the country through a dedicated 10 gigabyte network. The total cost of the project is Rs 4,000 crore.

He said there was a need to de-regulate the higher education sector and forge public private partnerships to increase the quantity and the quality of institutions.

On NKC's recommendation that English be taught across the country right from Class I, he said that in today's world, English was the language of 'business'.

He said, "Our recommendations do not say that English be taught in place of our mother tongue or the national language. We have just said that it should be introduced at the primary stage because, at an early stage children pick up languages quickly."

Heading: Una SEZ: ‘Define boundaries in public view’ - Indian Express
Content:
Even without proper infrastructure, Pratappura kids hone their skills in the old Chandrasar Lake

A village in the interiors of Surendranagar district with a population of around 1,000 has been producing several state and national-level swimmers for nearly three decades. The feat assumes significance as children hone their swimming skills at the very old Chandrasar Lake, which is a habitat of reptiles like the turtle.

Under the guidance of Karsanbhai Patel, principal of a primary government school, children of Pratappura village come to the lake for practice twice a day. There are no modern facilities, which are otherwise available to the kids elsewhere preparing for professional swimming.

The village, nearly 150 kilometres from Ahmedabad, is popular in the district as a place where children learn to swim even before they learn to read and write.

Patel, a native of Pratappura village, said: "I was posted here in 1978. And as swimming is my hobby, I started swimming in the lake in 1979 due to the absence of a pool in the vicinity. After seeing me, some of the children of the village joined me and I taught them to swim."

Twenty-nine years down the line, the lake has now become 'an institute' in itself. Children trained under him have not only participated in various district, state and national level competitions; many of them have also won different championships. Ghanshyam Matariya, Ila Nakia, Mukesh Ingrodia, Dipak Chauhan and Gayatri Detroja are some of the names, which have won medals .

According to Patel, over 250 children from the village have participated in state-level competitions, while more than 45 have contested in national-level competitions.

Patel has been training them in various forms of swimming like free-style, backstroke, and breast-stroke among others, according to their ability. Everyday, two separate groups of girls and boys — wearing swimming costumes bought from donations gathered from various people — attend training classes.

In spite of such a huge potential, the village continues to struggle to get a proper swimming pool, which can help the kids to excel to a higher level.

"I have made a number of representations to the district officials and the local politicians to get a swimming pool near the village, so that the kids can be trained in a better way," said Himmatlal Badresia, a local who has represented the village in a number of swimming competitions.

"There was one pool in Surendranagar which is now defunct. We tried a lot to get it restarted, but nothing has happened so far," he added.

Kamlesh Nanavati, an international referee for the water sports and a known name in Gujarat, said, "The children of Pratappura village have got a lot of endurance, but they have to be properly trained. The government should take some initiative in this regard."

Heading: hluwalia’s bail rejected; remand extended till Oct 20 - Indian Express
Content:
Residents of Gagret block in Una district today demanded constitution of a committee of revenue officers to carry out demarcation of the land that would be acquired for the proposed SEZ in Gagret. The villagers of the area who fear to be displaced by the SEZ demanded to know the actual area that would be acquired and

demanded that the boundary of the land be defined in public view.

Over 500 residents of Gagret Block gathered at Banera village of Una district and raised several questions before District Revenue Officer Karam Singh about authenticity of the records and figures being projected by the SEZ promoter, Skil Infrastructure. Una Deputy Commissioner Padam Singh Chauhan said, "The DRO had gone to the spot to conduct an inquiry into the apprehensions expressed by people regarding the area to be acquired. I would get the report late in the evening, after which we would take a decision."

The Centre had, in principle, approved setting up of the SEZ in Una last month.

President of Matribhumi Sangharsh Samiti Dulambh Singh said Skil Infrastructure has misled the government and locals by quoting a very small number of families that would be affected. "At the moment, majority of the people falling in the SEZ area are not aware of the upcoming situation," he said.

The DRO has assured, said Dulambh, that a committee for this purpose would be constituted within a week and would include retired tehslidar, kanungo and patwaris of the area and representatives of the people's agitation against the SEZ. However, the DRO did not respond to any calls when The Indian Express tried to contact him.

The SEZ would come up on 3,230 hectares and the processing area required would be over 1,130 hectares. "The original map of the SEZ site submitted to the government shows that most fertile land of the area would be lapped up. Several families and their sources of income would be affected," claimed Ghuman Singh of Himalaya Niti Abhiyan.

Heading: Police predict low turnout as hosts play Kangaroos - Indian Express
Content:
The Special Court today rejected the bail application of IAS officer Subhash Ahluwalia and remanded him to police custody till October 20. Special Judge J.L. Gupta has specified in the order that the accused, who is facing charges of disproportionate assets, be produced before the court on the date when the case would be put up for further orders. With this now the total number of days for Ahluwalia's police remand has increased to 13.

Ahluwalia's lawyers today filed an application in the court according to which the condition of the IAS officer is reported to be deteriorating, after which he was put on artificial respiration.

However, the court said a bail application cannot be accepted only on medical grounds, especially when all required medical facilities are being made available to the accused.

The order further says that Ahluwalia is required by the police and Vigilance Bureau for further investigation, which was only possible if Ahluwalia remains in police custody.

The court also directed for producing the entire medical record of the accused before the court on October 20 and directed the police to ensure that every medical facility required by the accused be made available to him.

Heading: CHB auction a damp squib - Indian Express
Content:
Only 25% tickets sold till Wednesday night

As india gear up to take on bitter rival Australia in the second Test match of the Border-Gavaskar Trophy-2008, at the Punjab Cricket Association (PCA) stadium on Friday, the Punjab police foresee it as a low-key affair following a drop in the sale of tickets.

While a senior police officer predicts a gathering of not more than 10,000 spectators, PCA honorary treasurer GS Walia hopes the stadium would be half full and 50 per cent of tickets will be sold just before the match begins. The PCA has a seating capacity of 35,000 but till late Wednesday, barely 25 per cent of the total tickets had been sold.

One of the best equipped stadia in the country was put under tight security on Thursday and 700 personnel were deployed under three-tier security arrangements, said Mohali SSP Jatinder Singh Aulakh.

While the outer security ring will look after law and order management at various checkpoints, traffic routes and parking spots, the perimetre security ring just outside the stadium will man and patrol the channels and frisking. The inner security ring will be deployed at strategic points within the stadium for effective ground management during the match.

The road in front of the stadium and three others will remain closed for traffic from 8 am on Friday and only pedestrians will be allowed access till 6 pm for the next five days.

The stadium and its 2.5 km radius, meanwhile, have been divided into eight sectors with a gazetted officer in-charge of each sector.

The VVIPs, including both the teams, the Chief Minister, ministers and high court judges, will be allowed entry from Gate Number 1 after taking the direct road from Chandigarh. The MLAs and other VIPs could enter from Gate 1-C after coming from the side of Hotel Majestic. Except those entitled entry from Gate Number 1, other entrants will have to park their vehicles outside the stadium in the allotted lots.

Heading: Rain pain: trees uprooted, roads blocked - Indian Express
Content:
Call it the impact of global recession or the liquidity crunch in the market, the Chandigarh Housing Board (CHB) auction for commercial sites today turned out to be a complete failure. This has forced the board to consider giving up auctioning the properties and rent them out instead.

Thursday was another blow to the CHB commercial auction after 2005, where it had received a similar response.

Out of total 31 sites identified in Chandigarh and Manimajra for the auction on leasehold basis by the Property Allotment Committee of the Chandigarh Housing Board, only five went under the hammer.

Participants at the auction could hardly touch double digit. This, despite the fact that the sites are auctioned at a very marginal difference between the reserve price and the highest bid.

The five built-up booths — three at Manimajra and two in Sector 51 — were sold for a total amount of Rs 1.55 crore against the reserve price of Rs 1.43 crore. The three sites were auctioned with the maximum difference of Rs 6.10 lakh in the reserve price and the final bid. There were no takers for the rest 26 sites, which included lucrative options like corner booth and bay shop with basement.

The average price fetched was around Rs 1.42 lakh per sq. yard. The highest bid of Rs 26.10 lakh was for Booth No. 16 at Manimajra, 30.50 per cent over and above the reserve price of Rs 20 lakh. The rate worked out to around Rs 1.73 lakh per sq. yard in this case. 

Among the other booths sold in Manimajra, Booth No. 19 fetched Rs 32.30 lakh (reserve price Rs 29.50 lakh) and Booth No. 21 got Rs 30.80 (reserve price Rs 29.50 lakh).

In Sector 51, Booth No. 7 and Booth No. 10 were sold for Rs 32.90 lakh each against the reserve price of Rs 32 lakh. The rest of the booths were withdrawn from the auction due to lack of sufficient bidders.  

Market experts claim that beside the liquidity crunch, inflation and the stock market crash have hit the real estate sector hard, resulting in the poor response to the CHB auction for commercial sites.

A senior CHB official said this was a very poor response from the buyer's market.

Heading: Season of allergies is here again - Indian Express
Content:
Heavy storm lashed Chandigarh in the early hours on Thursday and left many trees and electricity wires uprooted. This was the second consecutive day when strong winds, accompanied by rain, swept through the city.

The maximum temperature on Thursday was around three degrees below normal. The temperature dipped by around 2.4 degrees since Wednesday, while the minimum temperature went down by 3.2 degrees.

The residents could feel the chill early in the morning and many predicted an early onset of winters. Towards afternoon, however, the clouds cleared.

Chatar Singh, director of Meteorological department, said the velocity of the wind reduced from 76 km per hour on Wednesday to 65 km per hour on Thursday. The weather would clear up soon, he added.

The destruction caused by the storm, meanwhile, was evident all across the city. Numerous uprooted trees gave way to blocked roads, in turn leading to disruption of traffic movement. In certain sectors, electricity supply was also disrupted for some time.

The storm also disrupted preparations for karva chauth. The stalls, which were being thronged by people till late in the night, had to pack up due to the weather. Everybody, meanwhile, had their fingers crossed for the match between India and Australia.

Heading: Helpless father seeks justice for bedridden son - Indian Express
Content:
As summers make way for winters, asthma, cold, cough, respiratory ailments and eye allergies dominate the mild illnesses that have gripped the city residents.

According to doctors, as much as 20 to 25 per cent load in the OPDs daily is of patients suffering from one of these common allergies, typically attributed to the changing season.

Dr Sandeep Chatwal of the Omni Hospital, who on an average is examining one-fourth of these OPD patients suffering from chest congestion to mild fever, says simple precautions like wearing the right kind of clothes and eating the right food can go a long way in keeping these infections at bay.

"Since the temperature dips sharply in the mornings and evenings, it is important, especially for the children, to keep the chest properly covered. The chances of catching cold or flu are very high if the adjustment is not made as per the changing temperature during the day," says Dr Chatwal.

Avoid ice in the fluids and say goodbye to air-conditioners in this season, says the doctor who feels that these two modifications would contain the incidents of sore throat, headache, sneezing and mild fever.

The changing season is also acting as a trigger for aggravating asthma allergy in the city. Remarks a PGI doctor: "In any case, Chandigarh has a high incidence of asthma with more than 40,000 residents suffering from the allergy. We see a large number of cases in the months of September and October as well as in March and April due to the presence of pollen in the air. It becomes extremely important for the patients to take the precautions."

"The rate of asthma in children is especially high in Chandigarh and the numbers are rising each year. This is in line with other developed nations where, due to cleanliness, other infections are low but allergies like asthma are high," added the doctor. The use of inhalers, as recommended by the doctors, is essential to avoid asthma attacks this season.

While throat and chest are the susceptible to catching easy infections, eyes in this season too need protection and care. Dr Rajan Chugh, attached with the Fortis Hospital in Mohali, says the prolonged rainy season has in fact increased the number of eye flu or conjunctivitis cases visiting the OPDs.

"We continue to see patients complaining of eye flu even as the season for this infection is traditionally over. But with an extended monsoon this year, the cases are coming in," says the doctor. "Pollen, dust, smoke, which also play with the respiratory system, are the irritants for the eyes as well. With these, patients are complaining of redness and frequent rubbing of eyes," says Dr Chugh.

Heading: Woman alleges police inaction after lodging complaint against husband - Indian Express
Content:
For KN Vohra, a 69-year-old resident of Sector 9 here, the wait for justice has been endless. Despite being physically challenged, Vohra has been running from pillar to post seeking justice for his only son Navneet, 40, who was rendered bedridden after an accident on September 12.

Navneet, a shopkeeper in Industrial Area, was seriously injured after a speeding maxi cab (CH03A0053) hit the two-wheeler he was driving at the Sector 9-16 roundabout.

The Panchkula police, who were duly given the cab's registration number, have made no headway in the case as yet.

The reason: Officers say that the records related to the case were damaged in a fire in Chandigarh and tracing the cab will not be possible now.

"Navneet is my only son. Both my daughters are married. My wife is old and does not keep well. After the accident on September 12, the cab driver stood at the spot for 10 minutes as a mute spectator. Later, he fled the spot," Vohra said.

He added that Navneet was very serious when he was rushed to the PGI and he remained on ventilator for more than two weeks.

"His ribs were severely damaged. There was hardly any improvement in his condition and we were advised to take him back home. He has to be, however, taken to the PGI every week, besides, his dressing has to be changed daily. My son is spending every day and night in pain," Vohra added.

"Seeing my son's condition, I decided to fight for justice. But seeing the attitude of the police, I have lost all hope. Despite several rounds of the police station, the accused is free," he said, adding that he is running the house with his meager pension.

Talking to Newsline, Panchkula Superintendent of Police (SP) Sandeep Khirwar said: "The family can meet me and if any records are missing, leading to the delay in solving the case, we will try to arrange for them from some other sources and get the matter solved at the earliest."

Heading: Special committee constituted to handle Industrial Area’s development project - Indian Express
Content:
Sushma, a 31-year-old resident of Sector 26, Panchkula, has alleged that the police have turned a blind eye to her complaints against her estranged husband who was harrasing her.

She said, her husband Hari Chaudhary (50) who is a resident of the same sector had threatened her with dire consequences if she did not vacate the flat where she is staying at present.

She said Hari had been torturing her for the past two years and he came to her flat on Monday night and told her to vacate the flat, failing which, she and her children would have to face the consequences.

"I was married to Hari Chaudhary in 1999, only to find that he was already married and had children from his first wife.

I, however, compromised for the sake of my two children, Niket (8) and Kavya (4). He started manhandling and torturing me two years ago, after which, I left him to stay with my children in a flat nearby," said Sushma.

"I have lost my only source of income and have no other place to stay.

But, as the police are taking no action, I feel very insecure. Also, I cannot leave my children alone as there are chances that he might harm them too," she added.

Sushma's father, meanwhile, demanded police protection for his daughter as she was facing a life threat.

Talking to Newsline, a police officer, on condition of anonymity, said: "We have registered the complaint of both the sides and are investigating the matter."

Heading: Airlines to pay up Rs 5,000 for harassing customer - Indian Express
Content:
UT Administrator General SF Rodrigues (Retd) today handed over the Industrial Area's infrastructure development project to a special committee constituted at the Raj Bhawan today.

UT Home Secretary Ram Niwas has been appointed as the chairman of the committee, which will design a roadmap for strengthening and modernising the infrastructure of the Industrial Area.

Expressing his concern over the delay, Rodrigues withdrew the work from the UT Municipal Corporation, as it was a non-starter, despite the availability of sufficient funds and resources provided to the body.

General Rodrigues, while presiding over the meeting, which was attended by the UT Advisor, Home Secretary, Finance Secretary, MC Commissioner and heads of the concerned departments, asked the officials to revamp the system of their respective departments and make the various components of this project workable within the scheduled time.

"There is no dearth of funds and the need is to change our attitudes and remove procedural bottlenecks, to upgrade facilities for the stakeholders," Rodrigues said.

He also stressed upon the need of a clear concept on the development of the Industrial Area, with a focus on water supply, sewerage and other functional requirements.

He said that as the deadline for the conversion had already expired on September 18, a project team, under the chairmanship of the home secretary with members of the CII, PHDCC, Beopar Mandal and other such organisations had been constituted to assess the state of conversion and draw up a plan to resume plots not being used and to take a holistic view of their upgrade.

He further emphasised upon promoting and adopting the concept of 'green building' in the city.

Heading: Nokia to replace defective mobile set - Indian Express
Content:
The District Consumer Forum has directed Jet Airways to pay Rs 5,000 for causing 'mental harassment' to a customer who missed attending the last rites of his father owing to a delay in the fight.

Dr Mahesh Hukmani, a resident of Sector 19, had booked a flight from Chandigarh to Jaipur on February 4, 2008.

He was asked to report at the airport two hours

before the departure slated at 5.20 pm.

The flight, however, did not depart and he reached Delhi at 8.20, but by that time he had already missed the connecting flight to Jaipur.

The complainant alleged that he then had to take a taxi, which cost him Rs 3,500. By the time he arrived, he had already missed the mandatory rituals of his late father, which were to be held on the morning of February 5.

Jet Airways, in its reply, pleaded that the delay had occurred due to a technical snag detected by the pilot. In order to avoid any untoward incident, the flight was checked by the engineers, which took around 40 minutes.

The forum found that the airline had not placed any document or report about the technical snag. It, however, stated that the delay being for one hour and forty minutes was too small, for which, a report was not required. The forum stated that no evidence was submitted to suggest the taxi charges between Delhi and Jaipur is Rs 3,500.

Heading: Victim’s kin alleges threat to life, demands security - Indian Express
Content:
The District Consumer Forum has directed mobile manufacturer Nokia to replace a mobile set with a new one after it was found to be defective. In case, the mobile cannot be replaced, the forum asked the company to refund an amount of Rs 21,980.

The complainant, Mandep Kumar, a resident of Manimajra, purchased a Nokia N-73 (M) mobile handset from Sector 22 for Rs 21,980 in 2007.

He alleged that the mobile set started giving problem within two days of its purchase. He approached the dealer for rectification, who returned the same after 10 days with an assurance that the set would function properly.

The complainant alleged that it worked only for some hours only to result in the same problem again.

He then visited the Nokia Care Centre with a request to replace the handset as it was in the warranty period. The handset was again kept by the centre and after about a month, the same was given back to him.

The same problem recurred and he was then assured that the set would be replaced.

However, they failed to refund him the money or replace the handset.

The counsel for Nokia failed to file a reply.

The forum found that the mobile set was defective, which was proved by job sheets. The forum said the defect occurred well within the warranty period, therefore, the whole amount should be refunded to the complainant.

Heading: IG orders crackdown on drug peddlers - Indian Express
Content:
QUARKCITY ENGINEER'S MURDER: Complainant demands that accused should not be allowed to meet relatives

With the trial proceedings in the murder of QuarkCity engineer Sukhwinderjit Singh in advanced stage, Sukhwinderjit's younger brother Gurvinderjit Singh, who is a complainant, has alleged threat from one of the two accused facing trial and has demanded security.

In an application moved before Mohali Additional Session Judge S K Garg, Gurvinderjit stated that on the last date of hearing, one of the suspects, Himmat Singh alias Brandy, threatened him and his father Inderjit Singh, with dire consequences.

"He told me that he will eliminate my family," he said, while recollecting that Brandy and his relatives had threatened him a when they had deposed before the trial court.
