Gurvinderjit pointed out that the accused were not restricted to move around inside the court premises in a casual manner and met their relatives and acquaintances.

The complainant has sought directions to the superintendent of Central Jail, Patiala, where the accused are lodged, and Mohali police to keep the accused under proper restraint while they are produced in court.

He demanded that the accused should not be allowed to meet anybody without the prior permission of the court.

Sukhwinderjit's wife Neki Nalwa and her alleged paramour Brandy, were lodged in the Patiala Central Jail on charges of murder ever since Sukhwinderjit was shot dead when he was strolling with Neki near their residence in Mohali on December 4, 2005.

While the Punjab Police had recommended a speedy trial by referring the case to a fast-track court, the trial proceedings before the court of Additional Sessions Judge in Ropar, were stalled for almost five months, following a

stay procured by Brandy from the Supreme Court on June 29, 2006.

The trial proceedings had resumed on November 20, 2006, after the apex court had dismissed "as withdrawn" Brandy's special leave petition (SLP), wherein he had sought stay on the trial proceedings at the Ropar Additional Session Judge's court.

During the resumed trial proceedings before the Mohali court, almost 40 of the total 63 witnesses, including the complainant, his father and eyewitnesses, were examined. Sources said the process is on to examine the remaining witnesses, which include the representatives of concerned banks, mobile phone companies and an Amritsar resident, whose gun was allegedly used in the crime.

The next date of hearing before the trial court is October 23.

Heading: Inter-state gang held in Mohali with cache of weapons - Indian Express
Content:
Inspector General of Police SK Jain today issued instructions to the operations cell, crime branch, special cell and the police stations across the city, to crackdown on the drug peddlers and break the alleged nexus between them and the police.

The department had suspended two of its Station House Officers (SHOs) in the last week, for their alleged nexus with drug peddlers and for concealing information about a policeman involved in the same. Senior Superintendent of Police S S Srivastava, today confirmed that instructions had been issued to the various cells and the police officers.

The Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB), meanwhile, issued notices to the six police officers who were named by Raju, a drug peddler, to join the investigations. Raju was arrested with 110 grams of cocaine and 5 kilograms of charas in his possession three months ago and had alleged that he used to bribe the police officers to run his business.

He had disclosed the names of six police officers during interrogation, who were then suspended. The suspended officers include Sub Inspector Harinder Singh Sekhon, posted with Special Crime Investigation Cell, Sector 24, Head Constables Baljit Singh, Sukhjinder, Kuldeep Singh Bichithar Singh, and Mohan Singh.

Heading: Fresh case of dengue in Ambala, toll rises to 3 - Indian Express
Content:
An inter-state gang of robbers was busted in Mohali with the arrest of its ring leader among nine gangsters, Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Jatinder Singh Aulakh claimed on Thursday.

He added that a Tata-207 mini-truck loaded with "deadly" weapons, including swords, iron rods and batons, was recovered from the criminals, belonging to the bangala tribe. During preliminary interrogation, the robbers have confessed committing at least 15 daring robberies, from where they decamped with a booty of Rs 1 crore in the last one month, Aulakh said.

The gang included Zuri, Rakesh from Kurali, Raju alias Raja, Raj Kumar alias Raja, Vishal, Rajan, Ravi alias Seem, Raj Kumar, all from Morinda, and Avtar Singh alias Taari of Mullanpur Sodhian village near Kurali were planning to make another deadly strike in this part of the region, when a district police party surrounded them near Bhukri village in Kharar on Wednesday night.

"No sooner our police officers asked gangsters to surrender, they panicked and tried to escape but our force from across the district managed to catch them with weapons," said the SSP.

Preliminary police interrogation revealed that the gangsters were active in different cities of Punjab, Haryana and Himachal Pradesh, where they used to target iron, steel and electronic stores. The gangsters confided that they used to sell robbed material to junk dealers in the Balongi area at minimal prices.

The district police have procured five-day remand of the gangsters, who were put to sustained interrogation for ascertaining their modus operandi, links and other strikes.

Heading: Cash-at-judge’s-door case: Nirmal Singh granted bail - Indian Express
Content:
A fresh case of dengue was detected from Kotwali Sarai on Thursday. The disease has already claimed the life of a young woman on October 9 from the same area.

The victim this time has been identified as one 12-year-old boy, Nitin, who was rushed to the Civil Hospital from where he was referred to the PGI in Chandigarh later owing to his serious condition.

The victim's family members stated the condition of the boy to be 'critical'. The residents of the locality have been alleging that the disease has spread due to unhygienic conditions prevailing in their colony. They complained that repeated requests made to municipal council president Harish Sasan and executive officer had fallen on deaf ears. Both of them have been passing the buck, denying responsibility for the same.

Earlier, the deputy commissioner had also visited the affected area after the death of Monica but no tangible results were seen thereafter.

When contacted, principal medical officer Dr OP Arya said that the disease was spreading due to stagnant water accumulated in water coolers but the residents claimed they had stopped using coolers over a fortnight ago. The case of Nitin is the third incident of dengue that has been reported from the city.

Nirmala, a resident of Hira Colony was detected with dengue and was referred to the PGI, whom the doctors had refused to admit when her family members took her there for treatment for the second time.

Heading: Despite promotion no revision in pay, UT principals blame ‘indifferent’ Education dept - Indian Express
Content:
The co-accused in the cash-at-judge's-door case, Nirmal Singh, was granted bail by the CBI court on Thursday. The court has asked him to furnish bail bonds of Rs 50,000.

Nirmal Singh was arrested on August 20, when he surrendered after his name featured in the scam.

The defence counsel pleaded that Nirmal Singh has no involvement in the case and he doesn't know the persons who have been framed. The bail was granted on the grounds that it will take some time for the CBI to file a chargesheet in the case, so there is no reason for him to be behind bars.

The public prosecutor though argued that as the bail plea of prime accused Ravinder Singh is to be heard on October 18, Nirmal Singh's release should be postponed.

Other accused in the case — former Haryana Additional Advocate General Sanjeev Bansal, property dealer Rajiv Gupta and munshi Parkash Ram — have already been granted bail earlier this week.

The scandal came to light after a packet containing Rs15 lakh was delivered at the residence of High Court Judge Nirmaljit Kaur in Sector 11 on August 13.

Thereafter, both the property dealer — Rajiv Gupta and Nirmal Singh — presented the sale deed to police on August 14, 2008 and claimed that the money was to be used for sale deed of some property and was erroneously delivered at the judge's residence. However, the CBI had claimed that the both the accused had given the sale deed to create a false alibi to cover up the offence of bribing a judge.

Heading: MCM controversy: guilty students to undertake community service - Indian Express
Content:
Despite being promoted as principals and headmasters, many seem to be drawing the same salary as of a lecturer or a master.

According to sources, cases of more than 30 principals and headmasters posted in different schools in the city have not been cleared in the Departmental Promotion Committee (DPC).

Even a year after they took charge, they are still waiting for the correct grades to be implemented. Baljinder Singh, Government Senior Secondary School, Maloya, Rajinder Kaur, Government Model Senior Secondary School, Sector 40, Tripta

of Government Senior Secondary School, Karsan are among the principals whose pay scales are still that of a lecturer.

"We have been suffering due to the inefficiency of the department. They have not put up my case in the DPC even a year after I took charge as principal. My salary remains that of a lecturer," says a disheartened principal.

The masters posted as headmasters against vacant posts in government schools include Sukhpal Kaur, Government High School, Sector 41, Piara Singh, Government High School, Daria, Prem Kumari, Government High School, Karsan, Surinder Chadha, Government Senior Secondary School, Kaimbwala, Saroj Bhasin, Government Model High School, Sector 24, among others.

Some of the aggrieved staff has even retired, waiting for their case to be cleared in the DPC.

As a result of this, the pension they are getting is that of a master despite the fact that they retired as headmaster. Surjit Singh and Mewa Singh, retired as principal and headmaster of Government Senior Secondary School, Sector 38 (West) and Government Model High School, Sector 26, respectively but they draw the pensions of a lecturer and a master.

"The department is denying us our right by not revising our pay scales. The sadder part is that we have not been promoted, just posted. Promotion requires clearing the names in the DPC, which the department has not bothered to do even months after I assumed charge," says a headmaster.

"It seems like they just wanted to fill up vacant posts. Our career is also at stake but the department is indifferent to that as well," rued another.

Clarifying his stand, Samwartak Singh, Director Public Instructions (Schools) said, "I am aware of these cases and it will be taken care of. The department is taking into consideration the deputation, promotion and seniority angle and only after thorough assessment will a decision be taken."

Heading: World Food Day: ‘Food security should be priority’ - Indian Express
Content:
The joint Committee formed by Director Higher Education (DHE) Raji P Shrivastava to look into the case of a MCM DAV College student alleging manhandling and misbehaviour by some girls from the college submitted its report on Thursday.

The joint action committee comprised of the DHE, Jagdish Arora, Registrar, Education (Colleges) and Dr Puneet Bedi, Principal, MCM DAV College.

After hearing both sides of the complainant as well as college authorities, the committee found two girls, Ritu and Jyoti, guilty of assaulting Priyanka Singh, a student of BA Part III.

"After studying the representation of both the Administration and the college authorities, misbehaviour by the two girls has been proven beyond doubt," reads the report.

The girls have been asked by the committee to undertake community service.

The committee has also asked the guilty students to tender a written apology to Priyanka and furnish an undertaking to the principal that they will not indulge in any kind of misbehaviour in the future and that they will not cause any harm to any individual in the college or otherwise."

Any deviation from this undertaking will lead to appropriate punishment and the entries would be made in their character certificates," the report says.

"Ritu and Jyoti will spend 10 hours each doing community service on a project to be monitored by the DHE herself. The location will be kept confidential in order to protect their identity. The aim of this direction is not punitive. It must be seen as a positive step towards channelising their free time towards a good cause and adding a new dimension to their personalities. Somewhere, it will give them scope for reflection and a chance to make a contribution to society," states the report.

The committee has also asked the college to take measures to improve the atmosphere in the campus.

According to the report, a series of confidence-enhancing measures are required to be drawn up and implemented. The principal will also put up an advisory on the notice board emphasising the security and dignity of thestudents and others on the campus and in it's immediate vicinity.

Any student/individual indulging in unlawful acts or those that lower the dignity of others on campus, will be severely punished.

The advisory must mention the punishment as well, the report says.

The committee has also asked the college to set up a reliable mechanism for grievance redressal so that students who come from non-influential backgrounds do not feel insecure.

"The principal must review security measures within the college and in the immediate vicinity of the college in consultation with the local police. The college cannot disown responsibility for incidents involving its students that occur in it's vicinity," recommends the committee.

It may be recalled that Priyanka Singh had accused the girls of physically assaulting her as a fallout of the student council elections that were held in September. The complainant had approached the DHE as she was unhappy with the way the college had handled her complaint.

Heading: PGI to impart medical education, treatment guidelines to hospital in Bhutan - Indian Express
Content:
In a bid to inculcate good food habits and hygiene among school students, Health Aid Medicare, an NGO, organised a lecture on 'Health and Food Safety' on the occasion of World Food Day at MRA Senior Secondary School on Thursday. Complying with CBSE guidelines, the NGO emphasised the importance of food safety and quality, proper food handling, hand washing and maintaining personal hygiene.

"Around 1.03 crore people die due to the lack of sanitation in our country. 7.8 lakh or around 7.5 percent of the total deaths are related to unclean drinking water and the lack of hygiene. Diarrhoeal diseases cause 4.02 lakh deaths, while malnutrition accounts for 2.17 lakh deaths. Intestinal nematode infection and water-borne diseases like malaria, dengue and encephalitis cause 19,000 deaths. Besides this, health hazards due to increasing consumption of junk food and product adulteration cannot be measured in figures," said Dr Anju Gupta, a counsellor with the NGO.

School Doctor Namita taught students proper handwashing techniques. Principal S Sawant also spoke on the occasion.

On the other hand, more than 150 vocational studies students took part in the celebrations to mark the World Food Day at Jan Shikshan Sansthan, Sector 23. R Kumar from the Food and Nutrition Board highlighted the significance of the day and delivered a talk on the management of common nutritional diseases. Dr Kanchan Monga gave a talk on the world food security, the challenges of climate change and bio-energy.

Arjun Kamboj highlighted the measures required for ensuring food security for the growing population. "India is expected to have the world's largest population by the year 2040 or even earlier. It is of extreme importance that focus be laid on food security in our country," he said.

Heading: Southern Spice - Indian Express
Content:
The Telemedicine project of the Post Graduate Institute of Medical Education and Research (PGIMER) was connected with the Jigme Dorji Wangchuck National Referral Hospital (JDWNRH), Thimphu in Bhutan, on Thursday as part of its project to connect with the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) nations.

The PGI, through this programme, has been connected with Bhutan for imparting medical education and assisting in the treatment of patients by rendering medical advice. Sources at the PGI said it is the first institute in the country, to be connected with another.

Professor K K Talwar, Director, PGIMER and Dr N Tenzin, Medical Director, JDWNRH, held discussions regarding the new facility on Thursday.

"The service will be provided by Telecommunication India Ltd (TCIL), New Delhi by MPLS through BSNL. This is for the first time that international connectivity will be used for the exchange of medical advice on both sides on a regular basis," said Dr Meenu Singh, coordinator for SAARC Telemedicine Network, at PGI.

The programme has been launched under the SAARC Telemedicine Network, an endeavour of the Ministry f External Affairs (MEA).

Union Minister Pranab Mukherjee had earlier announced that international connectivity would be established at the PGI, a few months ago.

"Bhutan is the first SAARC country to be connected under the project. The link with Sri Lanka will be established next. Subsequently, all the SAARC nations will be covered through telemedicine at the PGI," Dr Singh added.

Heading: Art Me`lange - Indian Express
Content:
With a slice of Tamil Nadu camping in the city, expect a cultural feast

A maternal uncle of mine once passed on to me a lesson for life while we were digging into a plate of piping hot Momos somewhere in East Delhi, many years back. "If you want to know a place, start with its food," he had said. It's worked well for me so far. Which is perhaps why I let the whiff of sambhar guide my way the moment I enter Leisure Valley in Sector 10 that's currently hosting Poompuhar, a cultural extravaganza from the state of Tamil Nadu till October 19. Tucked away in the farthest corner, right off the stage is Ram Prasad Restaurant. For those of you who have been to the Tamil Nadu House in Delhi's Chanakyapuri will be familiar with the name and its USP. For those who are not, it's one of those quaint places you get authentic flavours without regional twists! "It's for the first time we are in Chandigarh too," remarked one of the managers at the food stall which brings in a potpourri of south Indian namkeens and a live cooking counter. But if your South Indian namkeen vocabulary ends at just the crispy 'Murruku', you need to sample traditional treats here. There's the 'Thirumelveli Halwa', 'Athirasam' (quite like our gud but made from palm tree juice and ginger), a Chikki look-alike from Kovilpatti, Banana chips from Nagercoil, Seedai and Thatai, both savouries. Since many may be alien to the tastes, they are generous with tasting sessions! And while you are there tuck into authentic South Indian dishes that bring in the best of both vegetarian and non-vegetarian fare. There's traditional Chicken Chettinand, Madurai Idli, Uthapam, Mutton Varuval, Chicken Fry, Fish Fry...a lip-smacking treat indeed. And it's all pocket-friendly -- prices start as low as Rs 30 to Rs 60 for a dish.

Speaking of all things tasty, also present with their kitty of milk products is the Tamil Nadu Co-operative Milk Producers' Federation with their brand 'Aavin'. Here you can stock up on the South Indian Khoya (they call it Khova) priced at Rs 50 for 250 gms. But if you really want to sample an authentic sweet, then do try the 'Mysorepak' (Rs 45 for 250 gms). "We have also brought along ghee and our specialty badam milk powder along with UHT milk that can be kept without refrigeration for 120 days," mentioned Jai Prakash, assistant general manager (marketing) with the Federation.

And what's a state visit without its handlooms. At Poompuhar, there's a special stall by Co-optex that brings in handloom sarees. There are sarees in Kancheepuram silk, Arni silk, Salem silk, Coimbatore cotton et al. "It's festive time and you'll find art silk and printed silk sarees as well," informed manager R Jebaraj at the venue. Also finding place are carpets, bedcovers and cotton shirts for men. Down the line is the handicrafts exhibit with life-size sculptures of Ganesha in granite, wood and stone along with Thanjavur paintings, another speciality of Tamil Nadu. "Diwali is not too far and that's why we brought in Ganesha idols," spoke manager Hemalata listing out the fabrics, both in cotton and in silk and some with embroidery too. The highlight here are also the three-piece unstitched cotton suits which come complete with dupattas. For the rest, plan a visit.

Heading: A check in time... - Indian Express
Content:
The Creators display their expressions of the known & the unknown

Individuals they are and that is what their works display. Eight artists of the group The Creators, share a common love for art and individuality, the reason why hours spent together bring out only the best in them. They bring to town an exhibition of their expression carved in wood, oil, pastels and mix media. HS Purewal paints life's happiness and liveliness in bright reds. Be it the spiritual monks or the women of Rajasthan, or his wife looking up at the moon, beauty lies everywhere. BC Prasad explores the contemporary life and makes subtle comments on the life as he sees it, be it the cramped locals or terrorism. The unconscious finds a form on the canvas of Raj Gopal Sharma. A dream-like atmosphere rules the canvas as there are no concrete forms or movement. Portraits and florals are what Ram Binod enjoys the most. Familiar faces, those of his daughter, mother and wife, his favourite scenes -- landscapes of florals, exhibit his closeness to the freedom that nature gives him. KN Anand gives a wooden shape in sheesham to his perception of Ganesha, Trinity, Rhythm, Nandi et al. Jujhar Singh exhibits miniature murals and paintings of nature blended with geometrics. Sanjay Dhawan creates Earth, Horizon, Universe and Moon Phase in oil and Dalvinder Singh paints cityscapes of Chandigarh.

On at Government Museum and Art Gallery till October 19.<./i>

Heading: Fast Forward - Indian Express
Content:
Green couture
Accentuating nature's paradise, Gardenscapes brings in arty garden accessories
IT is impossible to compete with nature's bounty, but we sure can complement it in our own innovative ways. Bringing in artefacts for your garden is Gardenscape that's put up an exhibition at Dhillon Farms, a ten-minute drive from PGI. Decorative pieces in stone, wood and iron, pots, lights, water features, lamp posts...there's a lot to choose from. "These have been designed in rainbow stone and brought from Rajasthan," tells Geeta, a landscape designer and the brain behind the venture, as she takes us through the collection -- a turtle family, picnic table, bird baths, tulsi pots, traditional chaki water features. The window boxes, perfect for plants and pillar structures, hurricane lamps from Zen Spaces are ideal for evening parties, adds Simi, her partner. Also worth a dekko here are bar stools in the shape of water drums and mushroom sets. Nestled in a corner is furniture brought in by Shorabh from Malerkotla, which exudes an irresistible old-world charm.
Sheveta Bhatia

Present Perfect
THERE'S nothing that woos a woman more than diamonds. And what better than today to let her know she's special. Karva Chauth brings with it a lot of fasting and then festive feasting. "It's a day when a wife chooses to do something as unique as skipping meals and even water. So she deserves a special gift too," Niti Sidhu, owner of the chic jewellery store Maia in Sector 10 points out aptly. With a special spread of hand-crafted diamond rings, earrings, pendants, bracelets and necklaces set amidst semi-precious stones, and encased in white and yellow gold, there's plenty to choose from. "Diamonds are no longer seen as just big budget buys. They are perfect for occasion --based giftings too," tells Niti as we eye the contemporary designs on the shelves bringing in the best of diamonds. "There's going to be an extensive use of colour, at least, when we talk of jewellery trends this season," mentions Sidhu. For the unaware, Maia is a flagship brand of Mumbai-based company Suresh Brothers which has been in the business of diamonds and jewellery since 1910. And with a special lounge designed by Sidhu, you can plonk yourself on the sofa and take your pick!

Lucky Sip
COCA-COLA India today felicitated the mega prize winner of the 'Coca-Cola Jodi Banao Lakhon Kamao' consumer initiative, organized across the three states of Punjab, Haryana (except districts of Gurgaon & Faridabad) and Himachal Pradesh. Rohit Ohri, a lucky winner from Bhatinda won a brand new Chevrolet Spark car as the mega prize. Expressing his happiness on bagging the car, Ohri said, "I am delighted at winning a Chevrolet Spark car. I have grown up drinking Coca-Cola and enjoy it as much as I did during my childhood days. It's great to see the company organize such an exciting initiative to make consumers like me feel special."

Heading: NHAI, contractor taken to task - Indian Express
Content:
Shatrughan Sinha's daughter is showstopper for a men's wear line

It's a men's wear collection that explores the element of androgyny, but Sonakshi Sinha, daughter of yesteryear actors Shatrughan Sinha and Poonam, thinks it is just right for her ramp debut. "My role is to embody that element of femininity in the male psyche," says the 20-year-old, who will model for Kolkata-based designers Dev 'r' Nil for their Lakme Fashion Week show in Mumbai on October 22.

Sinha, in fact, has worked hard on her look. "The concept requires me to look toned and fit so I have been gymming regularly and have lost a lot of weight," she shrugs.

Even though this will be Sinha's first stint in the limelight, she is unfazed. "I have been groomed since I was born, thanks to both my parents. It is not something that I have had to work for," says Sinha, who has just graduated in design from the SNDT Women's University, Mumbai, and hopes to launch her own designer label in a few years' time.

Film offers, says Sinha, have been coming in for a while, but she'd rather let her parents do the choosing.

Heading: Security beefed up for President’s visit - Indian Express
Content:
Refusing to entertain any lame excuse for the delay in the construction of the Murthal and Gannaur flyovers, the High Court today took the National Highway Authorities and the contractor company to task.

Justice Uma Nath said the contractor will be taken in custody and the investigation would be handed over to CBI. National Highway Authorities will be directed to give the contract to some other company, he added.

The division bench comprising Justice Uma Nath and Justice Daya Chaudhary sought for the tender details of the company. Questioning the contractor's capabilities, Justice Nath said if the Panipat flyover could be completed in two and a half years, why not these.

The Judge came down heavily on the contractor for the delay in the construction of two flyovers. The cost of each brick of your house would be assessed, the Judge said.

Justice Nath also took strong exception to the "objectionable" expressions used by NHAI and the contractor in its application. We will pass strictures against the authorities who have drafted this application, said Justice Nath.

The counsel for the contractor company submitted the delay was not solely caused by them. The contract to the previous contractor was given in 2004 and M/s Valecha Limited was given the contract on July 7, 2007.

The counsel for Valecha contractor demanded the penalty of Rs 50 lakh rupees should be allowed to be deposited in the shape of bank guarantee.

It might be recalled that a penalty of Rs 50 lakh was slapped on Valecha company for not completing the construction within the stipulated time.

However, the Court dismissed it saying no alternatives were available. They were also asked to give complete details of escalation costs put on the state exchequer.

The counsel for Valecha company further claimed that the previous contractor had completed only 31 per cent of construction, whereas the company had completed an additional 46 per cent of work on the flyovers. The Court said it will find out as to whether the work completed is 46 percent or not.

Meanwhile, senior advocate M L Sarin, who is appointed amicus curiae in the case said from May till September, the contractor completed only 1 per cent of construction. "This is criminal negligence on the contractor's part," he said.

Heading: Hi-tech dairies to promote milk production in Haryana - Indian Express
Content:
With President Pratibha Patil visiting the city tomorrow, the security has been beefed up. Keeping in view a threatening e-mail, the District Administration has deployed additional force apart from the District Police. "More than 2,500 officers from Haryana Armed Police (HAP), Haryana Commando and CID have been deployed,'' said A.K. Dhull, Inspector General Police of Hisar Range.

Talking to The Indian Express, Superintendent of Police (SP) Anil Kumar said all the entry points have been sealed and no one will be allowed without a security check up.

Bomb disposal, dog squad, anti-riot vehicle, fire tender, ambulances and quick action police force have also been deployed.

The delegates and audience have been asked not to bring bags and mobile phones, he said.

"We are fully prepared as far as security arrangement is concerned,'' he added. Though the arrangements have been made for the security, but traffic has become a serious concern for the officials organising the function.

Heading: ‘State attracts maximum investments in North’ - Indian Express
Content:
In order to enhance milk production, the state is aiming to set up hi-tech diaries. The Centre has increased the financial allocation to the state for the purpose. The provision for the self-finance schemes has also been revised with the government proposing Rs 600 lakh for its implementation.

Milk production in the state is 54.70 lakh metric tonnes out of which 80 per cent is contributed by buffaloes.

The state is second to Punjab with 640 grams per head per day. The number of buffaloes in the state has also increased to 60 lakh and is increasing at the rate of three per cent annually.

"This data is according to the livestock census of 2003 and the number has improved after that," said a senior officer.

The state is also home to Murrah buffaloes, one of the best in the world. Other states, too are procuring breeding stock from Haryana. The government is making all efforts to improve and multiply the genetic stock of buffaloes in the rural areas.

The state has vast potential for generating self employment in animal husbandry and dairy sector. Establishment of dairy units of 3, 5, 10, 20 milch animals can alone generate substantial employment. One person can be employed full time by keeping 2-3 milch animals.

The state has also upgraded its infrastructure of veterinary institutions catering to the needs of the livestock owners to provide round-the-clock service at their doorstep. The strategic location of the state provides an opportunity to upgrade its existing well-organised milk marketing system. "Easy loans are also provided to the farmers and women entrepreneurs for setting up of dairies," said an officer.

Heading: Amritsar farmers angry, want acquired land back - Indian Express
Content:
Beating Punjab and other neighbouring states, Haryana has attracted maximum investments in the Northern region this year. According to the latest study by ASSOCHAM Eco Pulse (AEP) for the first six months of the current year Haryana attracted private investments worth Rs 50,595 crore. Incidentally, Haryana also tops the country in per capita investment.

The National Capital Region (NCR), which attracted investments of Rs 38,237 crore, stood second in the Northern region. Punjab was relegated to the third position with investments worth Rs 19,418 crore, while UP stood fourth with Rs 13, 343 crore.

Talking to The Indian Express, Rajiv Arora, Managing Director, Haryana State Industrial Infrastructure Corporation (HSIIDC), said the credit should be given to investor -friendly industrial policy of the present state government.

"Despite being a small state, Haryana has managed to do well as compared to its neighbours. We are coming up with many new industries across the state and not just the NCR region. HSIIDC's efforts have started bearing rich dividends,'' said Rajiv Arora.

Overall, North zone slipped to fourth position, with the East grabbing the number one slot for luring private investors. The AEP "regional investment announcements" for the Jan-June 2008 states out of the total investment announcements made by the private domestic companies, the northern region attracted Rs 1.23 lakh crore against Rs 2.23 lakh crore by the east. The southern and the western region had a capital outlay of Rs 1.76 lakh crore and Rs 1.74 lakh crore for the first six months of the year.

Despite its abundant potential, UP lacked in adequate infrastructure and did not attract much investment. Himachal Pradesh, Chandigarh and Uttarakhand attracted very little investment plans worth Rs 1,150 crore, Rs 667 crore and Rs 495 crore respectively, according to the AEP study.

Heading: Festival bonanza for state jailbirds - Indian Express
Content:
Land released to private builders by successive governments in Punjab, including the controversial 32 acres exempted by the Congress which led to the expulsion of Amarinder Singh from the state Assembly, has driven farmers up the wall.

About 1,000 persons, whose land was acquired by the government and handed over to the Amritsar Improvement Trust some time ago, are now demanding it back.

Their land, nearly 160 acres, was part of the original 275 acres acquired by the government, out of which 87 acres were once released by the Badal government and then another 32 acres by the Congress, both to private developers.

Announcing the formation of the Amritsar Farmers' Action Committee, a group of farmers today said they wanted to draw the attention of the public to the fact that successive governments have made the original scheme unviable by providing undue benefits to the colonisers. The committee threatened an agitation in case the government turned a deaf ear to their pleas.

Rajiv Randhawa, a spokesperson for the committee, claimed that the acquired land could be released in case the award for compensation was rejected by the farmers. He said, "Parkash Singh Badal had once released land to farmers after it was acquired. Several farmers had not accepted the compensation for the 1,300 acres acquired in Rajpura in 1994, and in 1998, many were given their land back."

Addressing newspersons here today, the committee members said if the land could be released to colonisers, then why not to poor farmers. "Eighty-seven acres exempted on one side of the project and 32 acres in the middle have rendered the acquisition process initiated by the Improvement Trust meaningless," he said.

The farmers in Amritsar were getting a meagre Rs 15 lakh per acre in an area where the market rates were several times higher, he added.

Heading: No laser show, aerial display of fireworks this Diwali - Indian Express
Content:
As a Guruta Gaddi Diwas gift, the Punjab government has announced to redeem three to nine months of term of all jail inmates.

"About 155 prisoners from all across the state will be released on October 20 and a special function will be organised at Ropar sub-jail, which will be upgraded to district jail, on that day," said Jails and Tourism Minister Hira Singh Gabria.

He said the waiver would be three months for those prisoners who have been sentenced to two and a half years to five years, six months for those sentenced to five to 10 years and nine months for the imprisonment of 10 years and above.

Gabria said that to inculcate moral values in prisoners, they have planned to send 'katha vachaks' to jails to deliver religious discourses. "We have painted couplets from Geeta and Guru Granth Sahib and of Kabir on the jail walls. Religious books are also kept in the small libraries of jails," he said, adding that Rs 200 crore were being spent on jail reforms.

Heading: Flight booked to carry holy books - Indian Express
Content:
Going back on its proposal to hold a laser show on Diwali, the Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (SGPC) has decided to hold an aerial display of fireworks.

The decision has been taken keeping in view the astronomical cost of the laser show and the demand of the people, who throng the shrine to witness the display of firecrackers.

Jaswinder Singh Advocate, member of a committee constituted by the SGPC in this regard, said crackers would be burst this time, but due attention would be given to the environmental concerns. "After holding discussions with various experts, the SGPC had decided to hold an aerial show, which is less polluting than the ground crackers, including bombs, 'phuljaris' and 'anars'," he said.

"Laser show is not an alternative to fireworks, as in it various shapes are created on a curtain, while firecrackers come with sounds and lights, which thrill the public," he said.

He said a laser show held during the 400th Parkash Utsav celebrations in 2004 had cost between Rs 20 and 25 lakh.

Nazar Singh, Executive Engineer, Punjab Pollution Control Board (PPCB), termed this decision of the SGPC as "unfortunate". Dr Balwinder Singh, a conservationist, said firecrackers emitted gases that could be detrimental to the gold of the Golden Temple.

Heading: Himachal moots environment fund - Indian Express
Content:
It was a routine Air India flight from London to New Delhi, but the 330-seater aircraft carried only 500 copies of scriptures of the Guru Granth Sahib and 32 sewadars.

The copies of the holy book were brought with due respect, placed on 300 seats. The flight, AI-112, arrived at Indira Gandhi International Airport at 2:30 am and was taken to a special bay to offload the holy books carefully, keeping the maryada in mind. "The books were carried by sewadars on their heads," an airline official said. Special arrangements were also made by the Customs and Immigration Departments for necessary checks. Checking was conducted in the aircraft itself, the official said. "It was just like a chartered flight because the entire plane was booked by the members of a local gurdwara committee," he said. The management of Gurdwara Mai Bhago in central Delhi's Karol Bagh brought these copies here after spending about 80,000 pounds (around Rs 64 lakh) by booking all seats of the flight.

Sikhs consider Guru Granth Sahib as their Guru, so it could not be stacked. "Hence, we booked the whole flight and kept one or two holy books on one seat depending upon their size," one of the sewardars said.

The copies, which were collected over a period of eight months from across the UK, were brought here as they were in bad shape and published a long time ago. Some of the pages of the holy book were torn due to their continuous use, said another member of the gurdwara committee.

The copies would be kept at Gurdwara Mai Bhago before being sent to Gurdwara Khushalpur, near Paonta Sahib, for specific rites. "This process will take another six months," he said. These sewadars will soon be off to the US and some European countries to collect more copies for such rituals.

Heading: Hem & Haw - Indian Express
Content:
CLIMATE MEET:Dhumal also proposes voluntary eco cess on all vehicle users

In a significant step towards environmental sustainability and making Himachal Pradesh a carbon neutral state, Chief Minister Prem Kumar Dhumal today proposed setting up an environmental fund, a first-of-its-kind initiative to deal with the effects of climate change in the hills. To give his proposal a practical shape, Dhumal also mooted an idea of levying environment cess on all vehicle users, but added that he would like the citizens to make this proposal a voluntary initiative. The money raised as such would be utilised only towards environmental protection measures to reduce the impact of global warming.

"I will be happy if citizens voluntarily decide to contribute, say about Rs 100 per month, towards the environmental fund as cost of damage caused to the environment in terms of carbon dioxide emissions," said Dhumal.

At a workshop organised by the state's department of environment and scientific technologies, the Chief Minister spoke about the need of collective efforts involving citizens and government agencies to meet the challenges posed by climate change and global warming.

On the government side, beside a series of initiatives already taken to preserve the forest wealth and prevent environmental pollution, Dhumal decided to introduce a concept of compulsory environmental audit by all departments. "Every department's future plan should invariably take into account environmental impacts of the development measures. A beginning should be made to conduct an environmental audit of their programmes and recast strategies to adjust to the needs of environmental impacts," he said.

The two major initiatives proposed by Dhumal received an endorsement from Prof N.H. Ravindra Nath, a noted scientist on climate change from Indian Institute Sciences. "Himachal can show the way to the nation in effectively meeting the challenges on climate change. The state is at an advantage of becoming the country's first carbon neutral state," he announced.

Arvind Bhatia and Navin Chopra, directors from Assure Corporate Solutions, who also made presentations, identified key sectors such as hydel, renewable energy, transport, cement, forestry, as areas for earning carbon credits.

The compact fluorescent lamp (CFL) scheme will earn the state nearly Rs 100 crore carbon credits, said Arvind Bhatia. Minister for Forest and Environment J.P. Nadda, who set out the agenda for the workshop, spoke about the state's initiative in the forestry sector and project of biocarbon credits introduced with World Bank funding.

Heading: World of Difference - Indian Express
Content:
The second day at the Wills Lifestyle India Fashion Week (WIFW) kicked off on a dull note. Perking up the sombre mood was designer duo Pankaj and Nidhi's eclectic collection cranking out tangerine jumpsuits, capes with cutwork and baggy pants gathered below the knee.

The only international designer in the WIFW, New York-based Vivienne Tam seemed intent to dispel the fears of a choppy market by infusing red. Her collection, 35 garments in vivid red, lilac, pink and black drew heavily from Indian cutwork and used Indian fabric taffeta. The show opened with her classic red peony dress in a striking silhouette and moved onto trench coats, chic tuxedos paired with a white print peony dress. "They're fun bordering on practicality. And yes, red is my favourite colour," said Tam post the show trussed in a red peony print dress. Though there's nothing concrete, Tam who is on her second visit to India, plans to open a store in India.

Meanwhile, at the Delhi Fashion Week, 11.11 by CellDsgn, a new avant garde label by Smita Singh Rathore and Himanshu Saini has been the best show by a debutante so far. Chiselled pants, tapering at the end, crushed uppers with knotted collars and backs, shorts and dresses in linen marked the collection. Watch out for this duo.

Earlier, on day two at DFW it was white dreams for Tarun Tahiliani's "Strong Complete Woman" sans embellishments. While there was no Shilpa Shetty to brighten up the collection, Tahiliani gave a spin-off to Indian kurtas with his clever draping. On the ramp were jersey trousers replacing the salwar with ivory shirts and a demure white layered frock trussed at the waist with a gold belt. "The collection is for the strong Indian woman rooted in her culture and yet is ironically western." Though the designer has not lowered the prices of his collection, he has pared down the palette and embellishments.

Heading: Grounded Jet Airways staff on the warpath - Indian Express
Content:
When the hammer comes down at the Sotheby's Contemporary Art Evening Auction in London today, it will bring together Damien Hirst's heart-shaped canvas with butterflies and household gloss and his Indian counterpart Subodh Gupta's pots and pans on canvas. Ravinder Reddy's head of Vasundra will share space with Andy Warhol's Skulls and Anish Kapoor's untitled pigment on fibreglass will come together with American artist Tom Friedman's untitled cardboard and monofilament. For traditionalists, who are still unsure about deviating from the regular format of keeping Indian art separate from world art on an auction platform, the evening signifies a move that is a tad uncommon but for Sotheby's it is part of the auction house's agenda to bring art from across the world together. "This gives connoisseurs an opportunity to see the best of contemporary world art," states Maithili Parekh, deputy director, Sotheby's, as she runs through the list of artworks that will be on auction.

The number of Indian artworks may be limited to a handful, but the inclusion, according to Parekh, will promote global reach of Indian art and will ensure that avid collectors, who are otherwise unfamiliar with art from the subcontinent, will get introduced to it. "Those who may not closely follow Indian art will get to see work by some prominent artists," notes Parekh. The price comparison? While Warhol's Skulls has the highest estimate price between Rs 42 crore and Rs 58.8 crore, among the Indian artwork Gupta's canvas, priced between Rs 2.5 crore and 3.3 crore, tops the list. Modern Indian artists, meanwhile, will have to wait for a bit before they find mention in an auction catalogue with their western counterparts. "We might consider that option," smiles Parekh. For now, the focus is on contemporary.

Heading: Ticket politics: Success in last civic polls to decide fate of Congress MLAs - Indian Express
Content:
Jaaved Jafferi's back but with a Rajnikant hangover

As animated in person as he is on screen, Jaaved Jafferi can effortlessly grab your attention even in a crowded pub. Even as our photographer waits for a photo session, he is busy posing for photographs with fans outside Firangi Paani, where we have a lunch date with the actor.

Diversity has always been his forte — an actor, a dancer, a mimicry artist and a singer — and this is what made him a natural choice for lending his voice to the villain in the animation movie Roadside Romeo. "I have lent my voice to Charlie Anna, the don of stray dogs. Anna is still stuck in the 1970s and thinks he's Rajnikant, which is where the fun begins," he smiles. Jafferi was approached by the director, Jugal Hansraj, and he instantly took up the role for he thought Charlie Anna made for an interesting character. "I like to do character roles for these leave an impression on the audience's mind," he says, "Look at Johnny Depp; he will always be remembered as Jack Sparrow. Similarly, I am still remembered as Abdul Cutpiece of Timex Timepass."

Hansraj has also utilised Jaffrey's crooning skills alongside Saif Ali Khan in a rap number. "This is my third film with Saif after Ta Ra Rum Pum and Salaam Namaste and he's so much fun. We just brought the same energy into the song," he explains. Despite the success of his iconic track Mumbhai from Bombay Boys, Jafferi does not consider himself a singer: "I don't have the skills to be a professional singer but I can express my feelings through words and music in my own style, which is what probably works for me."

Jafferi may briefly disappear from films, but he has always remained faithful to television through Boogie Woogie, the first reality dance show in India. "We don't sensationalise the show like the others on air currently; we are original. And the reason for our success is the fact that to be on our show, the participants don't have to look good. They are real people with real skills," says the judge.

The actor has also been invited on the judges' panel to Russia for the Golden Minbar Islamic Festival, a platform for movies that deal with Islam on day-to-day basis.

The 45-year-old has more projects underway — Loot with Govinda and Mithun Chakraborty, Daddy Kool, Dhamaal 2, Hello Darling and Chai Garam. But the film he is looking forward to the most is Paying Guest. "I play a normal guy in it, which is challenge of sorts." Or an irony of sorts.

Heading: Hawala racket busted, ED says operators confessed to Rs 200-cr deals - Indian Express
Content:
The poor performance of Congress candidates in the municipal polls of 2007 will now reflect on the allotment of tickets for the Assembly elections. Party sources said when Sonia Gandhi and Congress Election Committee would sit for reallocation of tickets for 47 MLAs on October 20, the performance of candidates under them during the civic polls would be taken into account.

Many of the 47 MLAs had lost all MCD seats under them. "There are clear orders that the sitting MLAs should not be reconsidered for ticket if all Congress candidates under them lost the people's mandate during the MCD polls," said a senior Congress leader.

One of the bigwigs who shared this fate is Ram Babu Sharma, former Delhi Pradesh Congress Committee president. All four MCD candidates who contested from Sharma's constituency of Rohtas Nagar lost the elections.

Sharma's example is closely followed by Hastsal MLA Mukesh Sharma, another heavyweight in the Congress camp. No councillor under Sharma had managed to win the MCD polls.

Three candidates under Congress MLA Narender Nath, who heads the Trans Yamuna Development Board's constituency Shahdara, lost the 2007 polls. Naseeb Singh, who is Parliamentary Secretary to the Chief Minister, too, faced a similar fate with just a single candidate under him winning the polls.

In several cases, even the relatives of sitting MLAs had failed to impress voters. For example, the younger brother of Congress MLA from Patparganj Amrish Gautam and the nephew of Congress MLA from Nangloi Dr Vijendra Singh were among the candidates who lost.

The other big names under whom at least three candidates were defeated include Meera Bhardwaj from Mandawali (east Delhi), Bhisham Sharma from Gonda, Surender Kumar from Bawana and Mateen Ahmed from Seelampur. The screening committee will also take into account the margin of victory of the winning candidates in the MCD elections.

Delimitation spells trouble
Apart from the civic link, another factor is going to spell trouble for at least six sitting MLAs. There is a delimitation tussle between Tarwinder Marwah and Tajdar Babbar, whose constituencies have been merged into Jungpura; Dr Kiran Walia and Health Minister Yoganand Shastri, whose constituencies Hauz Khas and Malviya Nagar have been merged; and north Delhi MLAs Rajesh Jain and Shadi Ram, who are both fighting for the Sadar Bazaar seat.

Heading: Court unites boy with natural parents, puts ‘welfare’ above ‘emotion’ - Indian Express
Content:
The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has unearthed a big hawala racket being run from Chandni Chowk and Ashok Vihar. Rs 4 crore in cash and some incriminating documents have been seized from the hawala operators who are likely to be charged under the Foreign Exchange Management Act.

Such a big seizure by the directorate comes after a long gap.

Officials said they had identified four people behind the racket. The four have reportedly confessed to indulging in transactions to the tune of Rs 200 crore.

The ED is now in the process of informing the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence about the network as the hawala operators were also reportedly working with several businessmen. The ED officials have also recovered fake currency notes in the denomination of Rs 100.

The Delhi Police and the Intelligence Bureau were informed of the seizure of fake Indian currency notes, though the amounts are reportedly not very large.

The ED officials said the chain was operated between Dubai, Hong Kong, Nepal and India. They claimed to have seized documents showing payments between local exporters or importers.

This, the officials said, indicated that local exporters and importers were using the services of these hawala dealers.

The officials added that there were indications that Chennai might be the hub of this network. Further investigations are on.

Heading: Upset foster parents will appeal higher up - Indian Express
Content:
A city court on Thursday ruled that the true welfare of a child rests with his biological parents, thereby closing the recent custody battle over a one-year-old boy whose natural parents had given him away last September because the child was born out of wedlock.

Metropolitan Magistrate Naveen Arora however noted that law was not oblivious to the emotional demands of the foster parents — who had nursed him for a year — but said the claim of his natural parents was stronger. The boy also had the right to the "love and affection" of his real parents.

The boy's parents had sought his custody last week, stating they were now married and therefore would not be hounded by the "social stigma" of raising a child outside marriage. They had also told the court that the boy had been given to his foster parents on a "temporary" understanding.

Trouble began when the foster parents refused to hand over the baby, pleading they had adopted the child. They had also challenged the authority of this court to decide on custody.

The magistrate however questioned the validity of the alleged adoption, observing it did not conform to relevant laws.

The magistrate said: "At this stage, what is to be considered is the welfare of the child and not the emotion and right of the parties... (the boy's welfare) would be better served if he lives with the natural parents." He also said there was nothing to show that the child would suffer adversely if his custody was handed over to his biological parents.

The magistrate noted it was imperative to solve the matter immediately rather than allowing it to be juggled in different courts of law. He was referring to the foster parents' wish that the case be transferred to a 'guardianship' court. Magistrate Arora said: "This might take years and the delay might have an adverse effect on the child and his childhood causing irreparable loss in his grooming and personality..."

Heading: Dip in mercury, strong winds blow away heat, is winter here? - Indian Express
Content:
It was a distraught moment for the infant's foster parents at the city court on Thursday after the magistrate ruled the boy would be put in the care of his natural guardians.

Soon after the judgment, a police officer picked up the crying child from the familiar lap of his 'mother' and gently placed him in the eager arms of his real mother. The foster father could be seen assisting his wife out of the courtroom since she had almost collapsed while listening to the decision.

Her final submission to the magistrate — that the child would die without her — had been set aside with the observation: "You need not worry. The child will be fine in a few days."

Their relatives, who had crammed the court on judgment day, protested before the magistrate saying it was not "morally right to deprive the present custodians of the child's company", even pointing out that he had been abandoned by his biological parents soon after birth.

The foster parents' counsel Nitin Sharma reacted sharply to the verdict, stating the magistrate had overstepped his authority to decide on the child's custody. He said such cases are the exclusive domain of a guardianship court or a district judge.

Sharma said: "We shall move the sessions court against this order. A magistrate cannot decide on custody. Moreover, the original petition moved by the biological parents was about the child's confinement. There was no need for this court to adjudge the custody angle."

Chairperson of the Delhi Commission for Child Rights, Amod Kanth, told Newsline: "It is not just the custody of the child that is important. There are equally important considerations like care, protection, development and rehabilitation that need to be addressed when deciding such issues."

The retired IPS officer, however, said he would first like to go through the order before forming an opinion.

Advocate Ashok Aggarwal said the foster parents were legally competent to file a petition in a guardianship court for the final judicial decision.

Heading: Delhi, UP cops in row over murder case jurisdiction - Indian Express
Content:
A nip in the air, mildly warm mornings and pleasant evenings — looks like it's the onset of winter already in the Capital. While the last few days saw a dip in the temperature, Thursday had been cloudy since morning. Strong winds blowing in the afternoon added a further chill to the air.

At 30.7 degrees Celsius, the maximum temperature remained three degrees below normal on Thursday, while the minimum touched a low of 21.2 degrees.

The meteorological department attributes the plummeting mercury to a western disturbance across the north-western parts of the country, a common phenomenon when monsoon recedes. "As monsoon withdraws, a western disturbance develops, which is responsible for the dip in temperatures," said an official.

"There has been a good snowfall in hilly areas, besides rains here and there. This is contributing to the dip," he said.

The maximum touched 32.7 degrees, one notch below normal, on Wednesday.

The minimum temperature over the past few days, however, hasn't gone below the normal of 19 degrees, though the department predicts a dip over the next few days.

"Partly cloudy sky with a possibility of rain or thunderstorms is predicted for the next few days," said an official at the Safdarjung Met office.

Heading: Blast suspects sent to police custody till Oct 27 - Indian Express
Content:
The UP Police and Delhi Police are at loggerheads over the jurisdiction of a murder case in Harsh Vihar area of Northeast Delhi on the Delhi-UP border. A murder case was finally registered at the Harsh Vihar Police Station after the Sub-Divisional Magistrate and senior police officers intervened.

Police said that at 6.30 pm on Wednesday, three assailants entered the house of one Birju (24). He was dragged 150 feet from his residence in Pratap Nagar (Delhi jurisdiction) and brought to the Railway Line in Loni (Uttar Pradesh jurisdiction). He was then beaten up and stabbed in his private parts.

"Birju, in retaliation also stabbed back one of the assailants, Bunty. When a crowd started gathering at the spot, two of the accused Gautam and Ganesh fled. Bunty, however, could not flee because of his injury. An onlooker called the PCR," a senior police officer said.

Delhi Police officers reached the spot and rushed the injured to Guru Teg Bahadur Hospital, where Birju was declared dead on arrival, while Bunty's condition is said to be critical.

Delhi Police then contacted their counterparts in UP for registering a murder case as the murder had taken place in Loni. UP Police, however, refused to register the case, claiming the crime had been initiated in an area under Delhi jurisdiction. The SDM was later called in and a case was finally registered at the Harsh Vihar Police Station on Thursday.

Two of the accused are yet to be arrested, while the third has been charged with murder.

Heading: Gurgaon waste to be dumped at Bandhwadi, treated at Faridabad - Indian Express
Content:
A city court on Thursday allowed further custodial interrogation of the five suspected terrorists accused of carrying out the Delhi serial blasts, noting that more time was required for enabling the investigating agency to collect more evidence.

Remanding all the accused in police custody till October 27, Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Sanjeev Jain said, "Fair investigation is the mandate of law. Keeping in view the dynamics of the case and the factual matrix, police remand is absolutely necessary."

The court sent accused Mohammed Saif, Zeeshan Ahmad, Mohammed Shakeel, Zia-ur-Rehman and Saquib Nissar to police custody in a fresh FIR against them in connection with Connaught Place blast.

Earlier, Additional Public Prosecutor Rajiv Mohan had sought police custody of the five accused in the fresh FIR, submitting that the accused had been formally arrested in the case relating to the September 13 blasts.

He said their custody was required to investigate whether the blast at Connaught Place was part of a larger conspiracy or a different terror plan.

The counsel for the accused, on the other hand, opposed the police remand plea, saying that the accused had already faced custodial interrogation for the last 26 days.

The September 13 serial blasts — which rocked Connaught Place, Gaffar Market in Karol Bagh and M-Block Market in Greater Kailash— left 25 people dead and several others injured.

Heading: JNU turns to street plays to create gender awareness - Indian Express
Content:
Provinding relief for residents of DLF City who have to contend with the daily nuisance of a stinking garbage dump in their neighbourhood, a detailed plan for solid waste management was laid out at a recent meeting held between top municipal corporation officials and the chief secretary of Haryana.

As proposed by the civic bodies here, the treated waste would initially be dumped at the proposed site at Bandhwadi; it would later be shifted to the mining pits at Moftabad in Faridabad district.

Once the proposed site is acquired by the Haryana Urban Development Authority (HUDA), municipal corporations of Faridabad and Gurgaon would install the waste management plant within the estimated deadline of nine months, said a senior government official.

The Municipal Corporation of Gurgaon (MCG) has been also been directed to clear the roadsides of garbage and construction debris within a month.

National Building Construction Corporation (NBCC), a government-owned body, has been appointed as consultant for the project. Corporation officials say that once treated, only 15 per cent of the total garbage would be left as inert material, which would be odourless. The new plant will have a daily processing capacity of 1,000 tonne of garbage and would cater to the needs of both Gurgaon and Faridabad. The expenditure would be borne by the Municipal Corporation of Faridabad (MCF), said Rajesh Khullar, Commissioner, MCF.

The plant would also ensure the final garbage does not pose a health risk for villagers living around the new dumping site at Bandhwadi.

The MCG has also proposed to set up 10 dustbin-cum-segregation centres, costing around Rs 1 crore. It also proposes to raise funds through selling advertising space on these dustbins.

Commissioner, MCG, Rajiv Sharma said: "We plan to make the plant operational for the next 30 years, free of charges. Since MCF is going to incur the cost with NBCC, the only cost we would have to bear is that of transportation."

In case the civic agencies fail to deliver the promised quantity of garbage, there could be a penalty imposed on them.

Heading: Encroachment of land: FIR against Dadri SDM, others - Indian Express
Content:
The Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) has decided to use the medium of street plays for spreading gender awareness on campus.

Despite being known as one of the safest campuses for women, the university's Gender Sensitisation Committee against Sexual Harassment (GSCASH) believes that sexual harassment lurks beneath the pretty picture and needs to be addressed in a "more interesting manner".

Dr Mondira Dutta, chairperson of GSCASH, said sexual harassment is not only about eve-teasing but also about defaming somebody, as happens when couples break up.

The plays will focus on the various manners in which sexual harassment can happen on campus and how to deal with it.

Strting Friday, a single play will be repeated twice a day in areas students frequent. This is particularly aimed at new students coming from various backgrounds and regions of the country.

Dutta said that though JNU is a place where both sexes are almost equal, changes in attitudes do not occur overnight. "When students from various backgrounds join JNU, they come with some common stereotypes like viewing a girl who smokes as 'bad'. Street plays will be the best method to tackle that," Dutta said.

After every show, a discussion on sexual harassment will follow, in which students will be able to have their questions answered.

Student representative Sarada Vishwanathan says GSCASH has been getting numerous complaints of sexual harassment, mostly from estranged couples. "Instead of going through lengthy processes of inquiry, we thought it is better to spread awareness," she said.

The play Jaane do Yaar will be enacted on Friday, Saturday and Sunday. It has a nine actors, all students of the university. Dutta said preparations for the play started last month. "We may not provide every solution through the play but may be viewers will go home and ponder upon certain aspects of sexual harassment that they do not usually think about," Dutta said.

Heading: Sri Lanka to hold crafts exhibit at Dilli Haat - Indian Express
Content:
The Noida police have registered an FIR against Dadri SDM Himanshu Gautam, Colonel S P Sharma (Retd) and son Ajay Kumar Sharma, tehsildar Ashok Kumar More, Behlolpur Kanungo Mangeram, lekhpal Amit Kumar and 50 unknown persons, after receiving directions from Allahabad High Court in a case of land encroachment.

A senior police officer said the land was sold to Sharma's wife in 1984 by one Jawahar, allegedly on the basis of fake documents. "The land belonged to Mahesh Kumar of Behlolpur," the officer said. On August 28, 2006, Kumar approached Gautam and complained about the encroachment. "The police were told to look into the matter," the officer said.

On July 5, 2007, Mahesh approached the High Court, alleging that Sharma and his family were continuously harassing him. "Mahesh said Sharma, along with 50 'soldiers', gheraoed his land where his brothers and nephew were tilling the fields and beaten them up," the police said, quoting the FIR lodged in the Sector-58 police station. Mahesh alleged that Sharma had used his position and in connivance with a few officials of the administration prepared forged documents in his wife's name.

On July 18 this year, the High Court directed the chief judicial magistrate to take action against the offenders. "Acting on directions of the CJM, we have registered an FIR under Section 156 (3) of the CrPC against the officials named by the complainant," said Ramsen Singh, Sector-58 station house officer.

Heading: DCE: students’ fest promises to be a musical extravaganza - Indian Express
Content:
The National Crafts Council of Sri Lanka is going to hold a crafts exhibition, "Shilpa Sri Lanka", at the Dilli Haat between October 22 and November 3.

The exhibition is being organised in association with the development commissioner (handicrafts), Government of India, and the Sri Lanka High Commission in India to mark 60 years of diplomatic relations between India and Sri Lanka.

The event will be inaugurated by Union Minister of Textiles Shankarsinh Vaghela, S B Navinna, Sri Lankan Minister of Rural Industries and Self Employment Promotion, and Milinda Moragoda, Sri Lankan Minister of Tourism.

Around 30 skilled artists from Sri Lanka will come together with their Indian counterparts to showcase their skills at the Dilli Haat.

Sri Lanka High Commissioner C R Jayasinghe said: "Through this event craftsmen from both countries will get to learn from each other. We are looking forward to a similar process of Indian artisans going to Sri Lanka. It would be great if something could be worked out."

P G Ratnayaka, consultant, National Crafts Council, Sri Lanka, said: "Six master craftsmen will give a live demonstration of their expertise. These artisans have won awards nationally and internationally. Some are even recipients of the Presidential award. There will be dance performances by traditional troupes on four days at this exhibition."

Heading: Family protests police ‘inaction’ in murder case - Indian Express
Content:
The Delhi College of Engineering is organising its annual music festival, Ecko 2008 on Friday.

The day long festival will see participation from close to over 600 students from colleges across Delhi. The participants will compete in four categories: Indian solo (Consonance), Western solo (Glissando), Indian band (Choral) and Western band (Treble).

The competition is expected to be riveting in the last two categories. "The judges have already reviewed demo tapes by various bands for the Indian and Western band competition and have short-listed five from each category," Rishabh Singhi, a fourth year civil engineering student responsible for organising the festival, said.

Heading: NSIT tech fest gets under way - Indian Express
Content:
The family members and relatives of a 19-year-old youth who was allegedly murdered on Wednesday in Ganga Vihar area blocked traffic on the Sheetla Mata Road near Sector 14 here protesting police inaction in the case.

The deceased Virender was found hanging from the ceiling of his house in Ganga Vihar where he lived in a rented accommodation. The police had filed a case of suicide based on preliminary investigations, but later charged five persons with his murder, mainly his neighbours, after his family protested. His family alleged that Virender, a daily wager, was supposed to receive his payment from the accused, but instead they charged him with theft.

Family members also alleged the police were being complacent and had not made any arrests yet, with the accused still absconding.

The family sat with Virender's body and blocked the road for 45 minutes.

Heading: Boy ‘stolen’ from Gurgaon hospital - Indian Express
Content:
The 25th edition of the annual three-day technical and business fest, Innovision 2008, began on Thursday at the Netaji Subhash Institute of Technology (NSIT).

A number of teams from various colleges participated in numerous competitions and games.

One of the competitions, 'Carnage' involved teams creating their own remote-controlled cars saw many innovative ideas, with basic four-wheeled machines being created out of items like notebook covers and pens. Another quirky event was 'Complicato', where participants were required to devise a complicated answer to a simple problem. The task given to the participating teams was to blow out a lit candle.

Teams devised levers and adjusted wires to create twelve-step procedures to blow out a candle. Apoorv Kansal, a participant said, "It's really not simple. We are using a water balloon, levers and a fan to blow out the candle, and have to make sure the angles, distance, etc, are just right."

Heading: In-house affair - Indian Express
Content:
Jaaved Jafferi's back but with a Rajnikant hangover

As animated in person as he is on screen, Jaaved Jafferi can effortlessly grab your attention even in a crowded pub. Even as our photographer waits for a photo session, he is busy posing for photographs with fans outside Firangi Paani, where we have a lunch date with the actor.

Diversity has always been his forte — an actor, a dancer, a mimicry artist and a singer — and this is what made him a natural choice for lending his voice to the villain in the animation movie Roadside Romeo. "I have lent my voice to Charlie Anna, the don of stray dogs. Anna is still stuck in the 1970s and thinks he's Rajnikant, which is where the fun begins," he smiles. Jafferi was approached by the director, Jugal Hansraj, and he instantly took up the role for he thought Charlie Anna made for an interesting character. "I like to do character roles for these leave an impression on the audience's mind," he says, "Look at Johnny Depp; he will always be remembered as Jack Sparrow. Similarly, I am still remembered as Abdul Cutpiece of Timex Timepass."

Hansraj has also utilised Jaffrey's crooning skills alongside Saif Ali Khan in a rap number. "This is my third film with Saif after Ta Ra Rum Pum and Salaam Namaste and he's so much fun. We just brought the same energy into the song," he explains. Despite the success of his iconic track Mumbhai from Bombay Boys, Jafferi does not consider himself a singer: "I don't have the skills to be a professional singer but I can express my feelings through words and music in my own style, which is what probably works for me."

Jafferi may briefly disappear from films, but he has always remained faithful to television through Boogie Woogie, the first reality dance show in India. "We don't sensationalise the show like the others on air currently; we are original. And the reason for our success is the fact that to be on our show, the participants don't have to look good. They are real people with real skills," says the judge.

The actor has also been invited on the judges' panel to Russia for the Golden Minbar Islamic Festival, a platform for movies that deal with Islam on day-to-day basis.

The 45-year-old has more projects underway — Loot with Govinda and Mithun Chakraborty, Daddy Kool, Dhamaal 2, Hello Darling and Chai Garam. But the film he is looking forward to the most is Paying Guest. "I play a normal guy in it, which is challenge of sorts." Or an irony of sorts.

Heading: Honey for the  society bee - Indian Express
Content:
Curators and critics interchange spaces but so do gallery owners and artists these days

Wearing many hats is common in the art world what with artists doubling as curators and curators often filling the space of critics. The latest trend has artists turning gallery owners while gallery owners are trying their hand at art.

Recently we have seen quite a few of the latter and some of the former. Priyasri Patodia's eponymous Worli gallery displayed a video work that she created for a group show. Tradition Art, Juhu, opened by Bina Aziz and Zarine Khan, last week, also showcases Aziz's paintings.

Samina Lokhandwala whose gallery Sam's Art Hub launched with a show featuring her work along with Geeta Tambe is another instance of the same kind. Painter Ghayathri Desai, who lived in the UK for years,

returned to Mumbai recently to open her gallery, DD Neroy Gallery near Opera House. The space is currently hosting her solo, Sadhana: A Tribute to Gauri Shankar.

"One may argue that there are galleries opening almost every fortnight all over the city but still there is not enough space for many artists to show. That is why I decided to open a gallery of my own. I have already had to solo shows at the Museum Gallery so, having my show at my gallery is not really an issue for me," says Desai.

However, she insists her own leanings as a spiritual artist does not influence her choice of artists for shows at the gallery. Yet, most of the shows have a spiritual bent, whether it is the group exhibition of artists painting Buddha or the upcoming show that focuses on Lord Krishna and Buddha. "Since I am an artist, I'm able to understand the art better and empathise with the plight of artists better," says Desai.

Patodia, however, feels there needs to be a distance between her role as a gallerist and work as an artist. Many in Body—One in Mind, the show in which she debuted as an artist, was really an experimental attempt and does not indicate the gallery owner is considering embarking on it full-time. "Showing with Enith Perez and Srinivas Mangipudi was fun, an experiment where we explored the

desires for comfort and happiness. I'm sure I can explore my interest in video art and installation further. Now, my commitment to the gallery is the priority," says Patodia.

For Lokhandwala, opening an art gallery was always a dream. The family pressure had her work as a lawyer. Now, she has dedicated the later half of her professional life to running her gallery. "I want to make the space interactive with lectures and workshops for children. It is true that it's hard to get noticed as an artist if one has not had 'formal' training. In many ways, my gallery caters to art that is different," says Lokhandwala, who is also exploring Dubai as a new venue for art.

Heading: Two much - Indian Express
Content:
IKNEW times were bad but didn't realise just how desperate we would get. The American economy is obviously playing havoc in the lives of the Bombay Page-Three Perennials.

Uncle Sam unfortunately can't stop the Sensex from plunging and we can't but watch in horror at the rupee fall. A handbag today costs Rs 35,000 more thanks to the exchange rate.

I almost fell off my bed during a conversation with Anuj Hegde. He is a page-three agent and is scouting around to help get socialites get paid for their

appearances at glamorous lesser known events. Events and companies that can't afford to pay the newspapers, want their event to be talked about. They don't have the contacts and certainly can't afford a film star. This was his brief.

Anuj with a little help from his friends set out to star his company 'Wannabe! Anything for Money' you can't fault him for saying it as it is even though it may lack imagination and sound a bit crass. But, then again, nothing about the whole deal sounded the least bit tasteful.

I was so appalled at the things he was suggesting but yet intrigued when I learnt of his success rate. I couldn't think of anything more horrific than dressing up for the love of money going to places where you don't recognise or care about the hosts, get photographed and the horror of seeing yourself every day in the papers. Absolutely ghastly, I tartly offered.

I had to try to keep him interested as I didn't want to him to know that I was really only interested in the people, rather the wannabes who had agreed. He

insisted that he had a great thing going and it was at this point that I threw up my orange juice and almonds.

He had made categories of people according to their rates. This was getting unbelievable. This man had done mathematics on page-three? Some were even getting a free meal. If the celebrity needs to appear in another city, depending on her status, Anuj is solely responsible in determining whether she goes with the herd or up in premier, Mercedes or Maruti. Colour preferences can be met if she lets him decide what she whould wear. Indian designers are doing great business and in fact are the only people not affected by the great American recession. Like I said, Gaultier just got costlier; there's no conversion when you buy Ashish Soni.

Now this was my mandate; I'd rather be a bar dancer. At least there's dignity in the job. This sounded like publicity prostitution. It offended my sensibilities. This was no labour of love. This was cheap narcissism. I had had enough and needed to end the conversation. I was no longer interested in the names. I could pretty much figure out who must've jumped at the opportunity.

I told him in no uncertain terms that I was definitely not a client. He tersely replied and he tried repeatedly to cut in while I was blabbering. He wasn't interested in me as client; he had called for telephone numbers. I had none.

Heading: Western Rly thump CRMD - Indian Express
Content:
Aravind Adiga dedicated his Man Booker-winning The White Tiger to the people of Delhi. The city's authors respond

William Dalrymple
It's no longer surprising that an Indian author has won the Booker prize. What is commendable about Adiga's win is that this is an author who lives and works in India unlike Amitav Ghosh who is predominantly based in New York and their works tend to be very different in terms of their view point, but equally valid.
Dalrymple is the author of several books, including White Mughals.

Advaita Kala
I'm a huge fan of the book. It captures India's underbelly with strong, dark humour. It's a literary novel, yet, not pretentious.
Kala is the author of best selling
Almost Single

Amitabha Bagchi
