It's great news for Adiga and great news for all Indian writers. But I must admit; I wished Amitav Ghosh had won, he is one of my formative influences.
Bagchi is the author of Above Average

Heading: Aashim’s team still on top - Indian Express
Content:
Western Railway ran roughshod over Central Railway Mumbai Division (CRMD), trouncing them 7-1 in a Group A match of the MFL Elite Division League at the RCF Sports Complex in Chembur on Thursday. Meanwhile, in a Group B match between Pifa Colaba Youngstars and MS Police, the game was brought to a halt due to bad light with Pifa leading 3-2. The remaining ten minutes of the game will be played at 8 am on Friday.

The goals for Western Railway came from Ravikanth Naidu (30th minute), Binoop MK (35th minute), Vijesh Vijayan (41st minute), Anil Pawar (75th and 78th minute) and Deven Premi (77th and 81st minute). The consolation goal for CRMD was scored by Asif Jamal (39th minute).

The first 30 minutes of the game were played on equal terms though, with Jamal threatening to score on a few occasions. However once their opponent's forward line got working, the CRMD defence succumbed under the onslaught and let in goals at regular intervals.

The Pifa Colaba-MS Police match was well contested, but the latter were let down by some goalkeeping errors from Shailesh Naik, who had been brought in to replace their regular custodian. Pankaj Deshmukh scored for the policemen early in the game, when his intended cross entered the goal, beating Mohd Afaque Khan all ends up. Rashid Sheikh equalized for Pifa Colaba in the 33rd minute. Santosh Telang then put the policemen back in the lead in the 42nd minute. However goals by the hardworking Nagesh Swamy in the 61st minute and Raza Rizvi in the 67th minute put the Pifa Colaba lads ahead, till the match was brought to an abrupt end.

The Budweiser man-of-the match for Western Railway was Anil Pawar. His team has played four matches to date and have 10 points, while CRMD have completed their league fixtures garnering just two points.

Heading: Milford canters away with Udhagmandalam Cup - Indian Express
Content:
Aashim Mongia's team continued their impressive run on Day Two of the ISAF Nations Cup as they won nine out of the 11 events on Thursday. Pre-tournament favourites Mahesh Ramachandran's team are in second place with seven wins out of 10 events.

Ayesha Lobo's team stayed bottom with just one win from eight events.

Results
Aashim Mongia's Team (Won 9 out of 11)-82%; Mahesh Ramchandran's Team (Won 7 out of 10)-70%; Farokh Tarapore's Team (Won 7 out of 10)-70%; Niel Semple's Team (Won 2 out of 9)-22%; Nitin Mongia's Team (Won 5 out of 9)-56%; Ayesha Lobo's Team (Won 1 out of 8)-13%; Pallavi Naik's Team (Won 2 out of 9)-22%.

Heading: ‘IM kingpin misled recruits on his financial status’ - Indian Express
Content:
Favourite Milford proved too good for his rivals as he claimed the Udhagmandalam Cup, the feature event of the Mysore Races held on Thursday. The four-year-old chestnut gelding, trained by M Eshwar and ridden by KPG Appu, beat Super Woman by more than a length in this race for horses rated 60 and above.

Results with Mumbai dividends
1. The Kanyakumari Plate (Category 25 and below; 4 year old and over) Distance 1200 metres: Simply Fetching (Mr HV Vidya Shankar) 60.5 G Vijay 1, Commandperformance 57.5 Shoban Babu 2, Amazing Flora 59.5 A Velu 3, Tough Love 50 KPG Appu 4, Road To Romance 58.5 Rajesh Babu 5. Won By: 3, 2 3/4, Neck, Shorthead. Time: 1:15.31 seconds. Heading: Grover murder: Defence seeks details of mobile numbers mentioned in chargesheet - Indian Express
Content:
Indian Mujahideen kingpin Riyaz Bhatkal, now on the run, may have miscalculated when he misled his young terror recruits into believing that his insufficient means meant the group would have to use methods including kidnapping to raise funds for their operations.

"The others being interrogated were shocked when we told them the truth," said Joint Commissioner of Police (Crime) Rakesh Maria. "We even took one of the arrested men all the way to Mangalore to show him the posh flat belonging to Bhatkal." Maria said the arrested IM members were "cooperating" with the investigations.

During interrogation, it has emerged that the conspiracy to kidnap a jeweller and a builder from Pune was hatched by Bhatkal to raise terror funds. He had told the others that his means were meagre and that he even spent nights at local mosques.

Maria said investigations showed the group had an amount of Rs 26 lakh in bank accounts, apart from the Rs 11 lakh seized from Mangalore, where Bhatkal had operated as a civil contractor. "Bhatkal also has a posh house at Mangalore and his followers were absolutely unaware of this."

According to Maria, almost all the arrested professionals donated a part of their salaries to Bhatkal in the belief that it would contribute to their cause. "All this while, Bhatkal had plans to use his own money to buy and develop properties in Mangalore," said Maria. "Bhatkal seems very committed to his cause but at the same time, is also very worldly wise and had his own agenda to develop properties while duping his men about his 'poverty' and instructing them to conduct kidnappings to raise money for their operations," he said.

On the men arrested for the conspiracy to kidnapping, Maria said, "They had carried out their surveillance in a Santro car and were supposed to steal a car for the actual kidnapping. Anik, who had been given the injections and the sedatives for subduing the kidnap victims, had tried the injections on Majeed and Akbar, rendering them unconscious for a period of 3-4 hours."

Prominent among those arrested are Mohammed Mansoor Asghar Peerbhoy (31), a computer engineer who worked for a multinational at an annual salary of Rs 19 lakh, and Mubin alias Salman Kadar Shaikh (24), a computer science graduate. Peerbhoy and Mubin took briefs on the content of the terror emails from Riyaz Bhatkal and his brother Iqbal before they drafted and converted them into PDF formats.

The idea of sending the e-mails was also to claim credit for the terror blasts, which those arrested have allegedly told investigators was Bhatkal's way of getting more attention and thus more funds from people with similar intentions.

Heading: Taxi, auto strike cripples city of fast life - Indian Express
Content:
The defence lawyer of Emile Jerome, who along with Kannada actress Mariah Monica Susairaj is accused of killing Synergy-Adlabs' senior executive Neeraj Grover, on Thursday moved an

application before the court seeking details of the mobile numbers mentioned in the chargesheet.

Defence lawyer Ishwariprasad Bagaria moved the application stating that the prosecution should give details about the four mobile numbers which were mentioned in the chargesheet claiming that Susairaj, a co-accused in the case, made calls to these numbers before her arrest.

Public Prosecutor R V Kini opposed the application stating that he was not relying on the telephone numbers to prove their case against the two accused. He, however, said that he would file a detailed reply on November 3, the next date of hearing.

According to the police, Grover was allegedly stabbed to death on May 7 by Mariah and Emile, who later chopped his body into pieces and disposed it of in the jungles of Manor in Thane district.

Heading: Train to CM’s hometown will take shorter route, less time - Indian Express
Content:
Though not all city taxi drivers joined the one-day strike called by the Sharad Rao-led autorickshaw and taxi union on Thursday, office-goers and other commuters were hit owing to acute shortage of feeder transportation systems to and from railway stations. A L Quadros's Mumbai Taxi Men union, the biggest taxi union in the city, did not fully support the strike, but with over a third of the 55,000 taxis and 1.04 lakh autorickshaws missing from the roads, commuters were a harried lot.

The Rao-led taxi and autorickshaw union had called a one-day strike to press their demands for increase in the fare. The union also demanded exemption of toll tax for taxis and barring fleet taxis from the city.

Both Rao and Quadros had also pressed for cancelling the order regarding scrapping of taxis which are more than 25 years old. "They have given us an assurance that there will be some relaxation in professional and other taxes," said Quadros, who met Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh on Thursday.

"The taxi men did put forth the demand before the government and the issue was discussed in the meeting. But as of now, no decision has been taken," said Ramanath Jha, principal secretary, transport department.

The strike also saw two unions locking horns with each other. "Some 300 taxis were damaged by men from Rao's union," claimed Quadros. When contacted, Rao said the allegations were baseless. But the sufferers were the common people. "Why should we suffer every time? The buses were overcrowded as that was the only option apart from trains. Plus the heat is unbearable," fumed Punit Karnik, a media executive who takes a cab to office and back.

The BEST, meanwhile, operated on new routes, which gave some relief to commuters. "We ran 100 percent of our services on account of the strike. We also operated on new routes today to ferry people to residential colonies where our buses do not ply otherwise," said a spokesperson for the BEST. "The city was much calmer today as the movement of traffic was swifter than usual," said Harish Baijal, DCP (Traffic).

Heading: Acknowledge marriage or demand talaq: Abu Salem to Monica - Indian Express
Content:
Gauge conversion will reduce Mumbai-Latur travel time by 5 hrs

Reaching Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh's constituency from Mumbai is set to get easier with the conversion of the Osmanabad-Kurduwadi line into broad gauge. Also, the present circuitous Mumbai-Latur route will be changed and trains from Latur to Mumbai Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus (CST) will now run on the much shorter route via Kurduwadi, Daund and Pune.

The distance from Mumbai CST to Latur will now reduce from 744 kms to 529 kms, saving travelling time by about 5 hours — from 15 hours to 10 hours. The distance from CST to Osmanabad will reduce from 825 kms to 449 kms, almost by half, and the journey will take 7 hours less. Consequently, fares will be cut too.

K K Sharma, chief administrative officer (construction), said, "Presently the train from Mumbai CST to Latur and Osmanabad takes a circuitous route via Igatpuri, Manmad, Aurangabad, Parbhani and Parli."

The first passenger train on the route will be flagged off on October 19. Deshmukh, Union ministers Shivraj Patil, Sharad Pawar, Shushil Kumar Shinde and Narain J Rathwa will attend the function.

"As Latur is the constituency of the Chief Minister, this project was well supported by the state government. To resolve the hurdles, the Chief Minister paid personal interest through periodic meetings of state and railway officers. Prompt action was taken for early transfer of land, the entire requirement of ballast was met by state government free of cost too," said an official of the Central Railway.

Heading: Work on second line of Metro rail to start in January: MMRDA - Indian Express
Content:
While actor Monica Bedi got entry into the reality show Bigg Boss for the second time, extradited gangster Abu Salem said he was "perplexed with her liaison with other men in the show."

Salem on Thursday sent a fresh notice to Bedi saying that he is "mentally tortured and deeply hurt" whenever she denies that she was ever married to Salem. Salem in the notice claimed that they got married in a Los Angeles mosque in November 2000.

Since Bedi is one of the most spoken about candidates in the show, Salem has shown his disgruntle stating that if "Monica wants to go ahead with her own life, she's is free to demand for Talaq."

Bedi, in several interviews to the media after her exit from the reality show, had said that she had known Salem for many years, but never married him.

Salem in the notice claimed that his anguish had been "multiplied manifold" since he was unable to communicate with Bedi due to his imprisonment. Salem has been lodged at Arthur Road Jail ever since his deportation from Portugal in November 2005. There are several murder and terrorism cases pending against him.

Salem in his earlier notice too had made a mention of his displeasure with Bedi for her continuous statements to the media. In interviews to the media, she had said that she was "single" and not married to Salem.

On a romantic note, Salem in his initial notice had mentioned how he found "peace, solace and comfort while reading Bedi's letters and cards sent to him on (their) marriage anniversaries in prison".

But this time, Salem "warned" Bedi that if she fails to publicly acknowledge that she's married to Salem, he will be forced to resort to legal action against her.

Heading: This Diwali, BMC to gift laptops to its corporators - Indian Express
Content:
The work on the second line of the metro rail that's to run between Charkop and Mankhurd via Bandra would start from January, the Metropolitan Commissioner announced on Thursday.

"The Request for Proposals (RfP) from seven shortlisted consortia would come in by December and we expect the work to start by January on the Charkop-Bandra-Mankhurd corridor," said Ratnakar Gaikwad, Metropolitan Commissioner, Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA). The seven consortia in the fray for the second metro rail corridor project in the city are GE India-L&T-CA-IDPL, Tata Power-Mitsubishi-Tata Realty's Pioneer Infrastructure, GVK-Bombardier-YTL, IL&FS-Soma Constructions-Punj Lloyd, Essar-Alstom, Reliance Infra-SNC Lavalin and Reliance Industries Ltd-Siemens-Gammon India.

Meanwhile, as many as 14,000 families that would be displaced due to the construction of the car depot land at Charkop would be rehabilitated on the same plot, measuring around 50 hectares. The decision was taken by Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh at a meeting of the Democratic Front's elected representatives held at the MMRDA headquarters.

"The chief minister cleared the issue of the rehabilitation of the nearly 14,000 families that would be displaced they will now be rehabilitated on the same land where the car depot will be constructed," Gaikwad said after the meeting.

According to sources, the second metro rail corridor is expected to cost Rs 6,192 crore including a viability gap fund of nearly Rs 1,600 crore. "From Charkop, the metro rail would pass via Link Road and Linking Road, and then run parallel to the Western Railway line till Bandra. Then, it would cross the Western Express Highway.

After this, it would pass along the main road of Bandra-Kurla Complex —with a stop at MMRDA's headquarters— and pass through Lal Bahadur Shastri Marg at Kurla to reach Mankhurd via HD Barve Road.

Heading: State locks horns with Rlys over prime Bandra plot - Indian Express
Content:
But that's not all as state govt has agreed to increase their honorarium to Rs 10,000

This Diwali, the corporators of the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) are set to get hi-tech and rich. The civic administration plans to give each of its 227 elected representatives a Sony Vaio laptop as a Diwali gift.

Meanwhile, the state government has also agreed to increase the honorarium from existing Rs 5,000 to Rs 10,000.

BMC's standing committee chairman Ravindra Waikar said that the proposal for the laptops will soon be tabled in the committee.

"But we wish to give the laptops to all corporators as a Diwali gift and hope to hand it over to them before the festival," he said.

The laptops of Sony Vaio cost Rs 53,000 each and the civic body has a total provision of Rs 1.2 crore. After the five-year term ends, the corporators will be required to return the machine back to the civic body. Mayor Shubha Raul had last year demanded laptop saying it will be helpful in coordination and administration in this age of Information Technology.

On a demand made by the corporators for raising the honorarium, the state government has given its approval. Waikar said that on Wednesday the Urban Development Department had agreed to raise the honorarium to Rs 10,000.

"A notification in this regard will be received soon and accordingly the monthly honorarium will be raised," he said.

Presently, elected representatives are entitled to Rs 5,000 honoraium which includes cost for stationery, conveyance and other expenditure. Corporators had complained that the amount is too less for monthly expenditure due to the heavy workload.

Heading: Four Lakdawala aides arrested for extortion - Indian Express
Content:
In what could be the reason for imminent clash between the state government and the Indian Railways, Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh on Thursday instructed the Mumbai District Collector (suburban) Vishwas Patil to examine the documents of the 11-hectare prime land at Bandra, which the railways claims to be theirs.

The state government has now claimed to be the owner of the land. Incidentally, a month ago, the state urban development had given a Floor Space Index (FSI) of 4 to the railways for the plot. The state government had given an FSI of 2 for the same land, but increased it later after a request made by the railways. TC Benjamin, the secretary, state urban development department, was unavailable for comment.

"A major portion of the land that belongs to the state government is huge. We're examining the documents. If the land is sold by anyone, we will take a legal action against the concerned authorities," said Patil. "According to the land records, the land belongs to a housing society and there are other claimants as well," he said.

Accodring to sources, the land which is near to the Bandra station is considered as a prime location and the railways has plans to use the land commercially. The railways is expected to earn more than Rs 2000 crore from the same plot, sources said.

Sources also said that the Mumbai Rail Vikas Corporation (MRVC)— the nodal agency responsible for the implementation of the rail projects under the Mumbai Urban Transport Project (MUTP) — would use the money for funding of the MUTP phase II projects. This could well put the funding of the MUTP phase II in limbo, sources added.

When contacted, PC Sehgal, managing director of the MVRC said, "I was not present at the meeting when the decision was taken. I cannot comment on it."

Heading: Water crisis rocks BMC meet, Cong walks out - Indian Express
Content:
The Anti-Extortion Cell of the Crime Branch has arrested four alleged aides of Ejaz Lakdawala who had attempted to extort Rs 10 lakh from a city-based builder. The accused, which include two of Lakdawala's brothers-in-law, had threatened to kill the builder if he refused to pay.

According to the police, the builder had been receiving threats from one 'Azgharbhai', who claimed to be a close aide of notorious don Lakdawala, and had complained to the Crime Branch. The accused Imtiaz Salim Mohammed Qureshi (37) alias Azgharbhai had directed the builder to furnish an 'advance' of Rs 1.5 lakh on October 1. However, the officials laid a trap and nabbed Qureshi and Ravi Kumar Sitaram Saha (24) red-handed while accepting the money.

According to Joint Commissioner of Police (Crime) Rakesh Maria, during interrogation the duo revealed that Harish Nanikram Thadani (37) and Bhagwan Hiranand Thadani (36), who are related to Lakdawala, were also involved in the extortion threats. The police arrested them on October 14 and they have been remanded to police custody till October 21.

The police also said that the accused have also confessed to having issued threats to 8-10 builders

Bhagwan Thadani had also been involved in a 2005 case when, acting on Lakdawala's instructions, he and his aides had shot a shopkeeper in Versova after he had refused to comply with their extortion demands. However, the police had arrested Thadani and recovered Rs 4.4 lakh from him.

Heading: MHADA to demolish two floors of Johri Mansion - Indian Express
Content:
Oppn attacks Sena-ruled administration for failing to plug loopholes in supply system

A high drama erupted during Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation's (BMC) standing committee meeting on Thursday as Congress leaders walked out of the committee.

Just last week corporators had raised a storm over water crisis prevailing in the city and Thursday's standing committee meeting met with a similar fate.

Corporators blamed the BMC for failing to plug the loopholes in the supply and distribution system and said that the rising number of buildings in the city are adding to the water problem.

After a heated debate, Congress leaders walked out of the standing committee and the meeting was adjourned. The city's present water shortage amounts to nearly 1,000 MLD (million litres a day).

Congress leader, Rajhans Singh said, "Last week all corporators united and brought up the issue. Despite last week's adjournment, the civic body has not woken to the crisis. M-ward corporators had to go on a strike last week to prove their point. However, their condition is still the same."

The discussion took an ugly twist when Congress leaders started blaming the Shiv Sena-ruled BMC for not taking up the issue seriously despite numerous discussions.

"Water distribution is very haphazard with some wards getting proper supply while others not getting enough. We blame the Shiv Sena ruled BMC for this. If someone is in power, they should take their work seriously," said Vinod Shekhar, another Congress leader.

Corporators blamed the rising number of high-rises for the lopsided supply of water in the city. Congress corporator Waquarunissa said, "All the upcoming high-rises across the city can easily pump water even to the highest floor but slum areas are constantly neglected. Somewhere water mafias are playing truant. We request the civic body to curb this water problem as soon as possible."

The standing committee chairman, Ravindra Waikar, echoed the same thought. "As more and more high-rises come up more and more water is taken away. The slums are the hardest hit. The state government should stop authorizing new buildings," said Waikar.

To address the problem of water distribution in the city, corporators suggested appointment of a distribution-network consultant who will look into the matter.

"Considering the fact, that some wards get uninterrupted water supply while others do not, we need to have distribution-network consultants who will take care of water distribution in each ward," said BJP corporator, Shirshat.

Additional municipal commissioner, Anil Diggikar assured that they will immediately take stock of the situation. "A lot of issues have come into the fore. The city should get 1960 MLD of water but around 340 MLD of water is wasted due to leakages. Also some wards don't get water because pressure points in their areas are low." said Diggikar. He added, "However, people should immediately report to us about the leakages and pressure points and we will take care of the situation in that ward immediately."

Hydraulic engineer M M Kamble gave assurances as well. "I have asked my officials to conduct surveys throughout the city. We will fix any leaking pipes within days," said Kamble.

Heading: Korean director honoured as film festival kicks off - Indian Express
Content:
Two days after a fire gutted the 100-year-old wooden Johri Mansion, killing a man and his three-year-old grandchild, the Mumbai Fire Brigade has instructed MHADA to demolish the fourth and fifth floor of the building and repair it later to maintain the stability of the structure.

The four-storey building on Kalbadevi Road caught fire on Tuesday, allegedly due to a short circuit on the first floor. The fourth and fifth floor were the worst affected due to the fire.

"Parts of the top two floors have fallen apart and many portions that are hanging need to be demolished. A lot of portion has fallen on the third floor, putting load on it. Adequate safety measures need to be taken immediately," said deputy chief fire officer P Karguppikar. He further said, "For the stability of the building it is necessary to repair the damaged parts. Part of the fourth and fifth floors have collapsed and the staircase of the third floor is totally damaged, they will have to be demolished and resurrected."

He added that the remaining floors, from the third floor onwards, are in a stable condition. The fire department has also given instructions to support the structure as a precautionary measure.

The fire department is investigating the exact cause of the fire. The fire is said to have started in the lower floors of the building and soon the upper floors came under its grip. Cloth material, cotton mattresses and furniture which was stored on the fifth floor of the building caught fire and huge flames erupted destructing the top floors.

According to fire officials, the fire fighting operation was difficult to carry out as the staircase had collapsed. "The fire was combated with aerial ladders from the back of the building as there was no way to go inside," Karguppikar said. The cooling operations are expected to be completed by Friday.

Heading: Discharge of Brijesh Singh to be challenged in court - Indian Express
Content:
The seventh Asian Film Festival kicked off on Thursday night, promising cine lovers in the city a week of internationally acclaimed cinema from around Asia.

The festival will be held from October 16 to 23. It will showcase 80 films from around 20 countries. A number of special screenings, including a tribute to filmmaker Satyajit Ray and noted playwright Vijay Tendulkar will be on display.

Korean director Park Kwang Su, who is known for his politically- charged films, was presented with the Asian Film Culture Award. The award is given to an Indian and an Asian on alternate years. Filmakers Mrinal Sen and Adoor Gopalakrishnan have won the award in the past. "I am too young to be receiving this award. I will work harder now," quipped Kwang Su.

The Satyajit Ray Memorial Award was given to P K Nair, the former director of the National Film Archive. "I am greatly honoured. Mainly because the award is named after such a great filmmaker," said Nair.

"We cannot and must not underestimate our audiences. We have to make films in local languages, and reach out to more people," he added. "Maharashtra is the place where film as an art was instituted. There needs to be much more money put into this by the state government. The efforts of more people outside the realm of focus should be recognised by the state," said Kumar Ketkar, editor of Loksatta.

"Asian films have found it difficult to enter the mainstream world of cinema. Now we have had an overwhelming response from around Asia,"said Kiran Shantaram, Chairman, Asian Film Foundation. "I inaugurated the festival in 2002 and I am happy to see it each year," said Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh, who inaugurated the function.

Heading: Marathas drop demand for political reservation - Indian Express
Content:
Jaaved Jafferi's back but with a Rajnikant hangover

As animated in person as he is on screen, Jaaved Jafferi can effortlessly grab your attention even in a crowded pub. Even as our photographer waits for a photo session, he is busy posing for photographs with fans outside Firangi Paani, where we have a lunch date with the actor.

Diversity has always been his forte — an actor, a dancer, a mimicry artist and a singer — and this is what made him a natural choice for lending his voice to the villain in the animation movie Roadside Romeo. "I have lent my voice to Charlie Anna, the don of stray dogs. Anna is still stuck in the 1970s and thinks he's Rajnikant, which is where the fun begins," he smiles. Jafferi was approached by the director, Jugal Hansraj, and he instantly took up the role for he thought Charlie Anna made for an interesting character. "I like to do character roles for these leave an impression on the audience's mind," he says, "Look at Johnny Depp; he will always be remembered as Jack Sparrow. Similarly, I am still remembered as Abdul Cutpiece of Timex Timepass."

Hansraj has also utilised Jaffrey's crooning skills alongside Saif Ali Khan in a rap number. "This is my third film with Saif after Ta Ra Rum Pum and Salaam Namaste and he's so much fun. We just brought the same energy into the song," he explains. Despite the success of his iconic track Mumbhai from Bombay Boys, Jafferi does not consider himself a singer: "I don't have the skills to be a professional singer but I can express my feelings through words and music in my own style, which is what probably works for me."

Jafferi may briefly disappear from films, but he has always remained faithful to television through Boogie Woogie, the first reality dance show in India. "We don't sensationalise the show like the others on air currently; we are original. And the reason for our success is the fact that to be on our show, the participants don't have to look good. They are real people with real skills," says the judge.

The actor has also been invited on the judges' panel to Russia for the Golden Minbar Islamic Festival, a platform for movies that deal with Islam on day-to-day basis.

The 45-year-old has more projects underway — Loot with Govinda and Mithun Chakraborty, Daddy Kool, Dhamaal 2, Hello Darling and Chai Garam. But the film he is looking forward to the most is Paying Guest. "I play a normal guy in it, which is challenge of sorts." Or an irony of sorts.

Heading: Whiff of Pune link to Hyderabad blasts - Indian Express
Content:
CHANGE OF TACK: Panel says quota in education and jobs will do, wants special OBC category for community

In an interesting turn to the issue of reservation for the Maratha community, the coordination committee of Maratha organisations on Thursday declared that it would not demand political reservation as Marathas already have a strong representation in state politics. This has come with most OBC leaders opposing any shrinking of their existing quota on account of a new entrant.

"We don't want reservation in politics. But our demand for reservation in education and government jobs still stands," said Purushottam Khedekar, executive president of the Maratha coordination committee, an umbrealla of nine Maratha organisations.

Khedekar said that there should be a special OBC quota for Marathas. "We don't want to disturb the present 19 per cent quota of OBC. The government should consider a separate 30 per cent quota for Marathas that would take the total reservation to 82 per cent," he said.

"We will meet the Chief Minister with the new demands and appeal to him to pass a bill in the winter session of the Assembly," said Rajendra Kondhare, convener of the committee. He claimed that the committee had met all party leaders on the issue and had been assured their support.

Party leaders are playing it safe and say they won't mind reservations to Marathas based on economic grounds, though they wanted a special OBC quota for the community. But OBC leaders in most parties opposed the idea of including the Maratha community in the present 19 per cent quota for OBCs.

"The BJP is of the opinion that Marathas should be given reservation on economic grounds and we will put forth our view if ever the state government calls for an all-party meeting on the issue," said Vinod Tawade, state BJP spokesman.

Shiv Sena leader Diwakar Rawate also supported reservation for Marathas on economic grounds. Republican Party of India MP Ramdas Athawale agreed: "Many people in the community are economically backward and their demand for reservation is valid. But they should not be included in the present OBC quota as there would be clash between other castes and Marathas."

BRP-Bahujan Mahasangh leader Prakash Ambedkar, grandson of Babasaheb Ambedkar, too called for a special OBC quota for Marathas and felt they should think of contesting polls as a separate forum.

"The Mandal Commission has spelt out 11 criteria for a caste to be given reserved status. Reservation should be given on that basis," said Ratnakar Mahajan, executive chairman of the state Planning Commission.

But the end word may be that no party can afford to take a stand that will offend the Maratha community as it constitutes 32 per cent of the state's population. The Congress and NCP have already welcomed reservation for the Marathas.

"No party will oppose reservation to the Maratha community. The state government had already constituted the Bapat committee to look into the issue. One should ask for the report of this committee," said political scientist Suhas Palshikar.

WANT SOME, FORGO SOME
Who's demanding:
The coordination committee of Maratha organisations, which includes Maratha Seva Sangh, Sambhaji Brigade, Akhil Bharatiya Maratha Mahasangh, Shivsangram, Chhava, Chhava Yuva, Bharatiya Maratha Mahasangh and Maharashtrian Maratha Mahasanghthey can do without: Political reservation; they say they have enough leaders in state politics already

What they want:
* A special OBC quota for Marathas
* Reservation in jobs and education
* Reservation on the basis of economic status, which is low in the community at large

Other OBC leaders say:
No shrinking of quota for existing OBCs; let there be a special OBC quota for Marathas

Heading: Zebra crossings getting better, use them or face action - Indian Express
Content:
Two Mujahideen arrested from city suspected to have planted the explosives

Two of the Indian Mujahideen (IM) men arrested from Pune are believed to have triggered last year's Hyderabad blasts. A Hyderabad police team that interrogated the suspects believes that Mohammed Akbar Ismail Choudhary and Anique Shafique Sayyed, both of Kondhwa, had planted the explosives that killed 42 persons, including one from Pune.

"We have interrogated the suspects in Mumbai. We have not yet visited Pune. Investigations are still on," Hyderabad police commissioner B Prasada Rao told The Indian Express, refusing to discuss the details.

Choudhary was allegedly the driver of the IM media wing headed by Pune techie Mohammed Mansoor Peerbhoy. Anique was a partner in Acme Computer Institute in Pune Camp along with Majid Sheikh, also of Kondhwa.

When this reporter visited Choudhary's house, the family refused to speak. Choudhary lived at Manisha Complex in Mithanagar in Kondhwa while Anique was a resident of Bhagyoday Nagar, also in Kondhwa.

It is now understood that Choudhary, Anique, Majid and other IM members in Pune used to conduct meetings at the H-302 flat in Ashoka Mews, the alleged "control room" of the terror outfit, and at Acme Computer Institute near Qureshi Masjid in Camp.

Investigators say Choudhary and Anique had visited Hyderabad in July 2007. Travelling by bus, they performed a recce and zeroed in on three spots for planting the bombs. They also transported bombs from Mangalore to Hyderabad in buses.

They had taken a flat on rent at Habsiguda in Hyderabad with the help of a local citizen who is a relative of another IM member, Farooq Shamshuddin Tarkash, again of Kondhwa. They paid Rs 12,000 to the flat owner in advance and then joined a computer institute at Ameerpet, an exposure that helped Anique when he started Acme in Pune.

On August 25, Riyaz joined them. He planted a bomb at Gokul Chat Bhandar, Choudhary planted one at Dilsukhnagar and Anique planted explosives at Lumbini Park during the laser show, investigators said. The bomb at Dilsukhnagar did not explode because of a faulty circuit.

Investigators now say the conspiracy to carry out blasts in the country may have been devised in Pune in 2006 by masterminds Riyaz Bhatkal and his brother Iqbal. Police are probing Bhatkal's association with LeT and other terror outfits from Pakistan and Bangladesh.

Heading: Civic body set to start BRTS work on Airport-Balewadi stretch - Indian Express
Content:
The civic administration has promised to rectify the defects in its zebra crossings. Once that is done, it expects pedestrians to use them; it has vowed strict action against jaywalkers.

"There are defects in zebra crossings at various places. We will study crossings throughout the city and remove all defects," Municipal Commissioner Praveensinh Pardeshi said.

Among the steps being contemplated are activation of a push-button signal that will make it easier for senior citizens to cross major junctions; establishment of pedestrian refuges; and separate signals at major zebra crossings on roads being developed under Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM).

Once all the moves are in place, the civic body will crack down on any offence. Pardeshi said the police would be asked to take action against those violating signals at zebra crossings.

Civic activist Prashant Inamdar of Pedestrian First, who is coordinating with the Pune Municipal Corporation, agreed that the plan to penalise traffic offenders is justified, but insisted that all zebra crossings should first be made safe and usable.

Pardeshi said the civic administration would also take strict action against those encroaching on bicycle tracks and forcing bicycles onto roads. It also plans to shift some bus stops of the public utility PMPML from wherever they are choking the traffic flow, Pardeshi added.
